meta.method: Ghidra 12 decompile-first spec + blind asm-only re-derivation + adjudication on structural disagreement
meta.udp_header_note: UDP-S2C:*/UDP-C2S:* keys share the Fireway UDP framing documented in UDP-S2C:0x03 semantics: 8-byte header, hdr0 bits 0-10 size, bit 11 (0x800) = ENCODED (the server constant NO_ENCODE_FLAG names this bit backwards), bits 12-19 seq; hdr1 checksum; body coded with EncodebyArray. Grammars exclude the header and the opcode byte.

live_verification.campaign: 13 group passes (chat_mail_gm, combat_skill, destructive, item_inventory, login_character, party, premium_cash, pvp_arena, quest_cards_misc, shop_storage, social_friend, trade, world_movement_npc) against the running server_live baseline (worktree commit 5f35880) and the patched EN 2008 client WindSlayer_patched.exe. Each test either injected an S2C packet (wsdev.py send/sendspec) and observed the client (screenshot + read-only memory probe), or drove the client UI and captured the resulting C2S bytes.

specs.name: LoginRequest
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x70E6F4], TCP 7022; loaded directly from the global before every Add/Send)

locations.role: S2C 0x5A (key exchange) handler entry; the login send is the tail of this handler
reads i32 key from S2C 0x5A, then SetCodeKey at 0x44D7F8
Sleep(1000) before building the packet (receive critical section app+0x368 still held)
login dialog: strcpy of the account-ID edit text (UI ctrl 0x1c) into player+0x48
login dialog: strcpy of the password edit text (UI ctrl 0x1e) into player+0x101
ConnectToGameServer after the empty-field checks and the channel status==3 check

specs.grammar:
str[41] account_id
str[21] password

fields.name: account_id
fields.meaning: Login account ID typed in the login dialog, NUL-terminated. Exactly 0x29 bytes are copied from a 185-byte buffer.
fields.dest_or_source: app[+0x4CC] (player/account struct) +0x48; filled by strcpy at 0x448160 from UI edit ctrl 0x1c

fields.name: password
fields.meaning: Plaintext password, NUL-terminated. Exactly 0x15 bytes are copied from a 48-byte buffer.
fields.dest_or_source: app[+0x4CC] +0x101; filled by strcpy at 0x448184 from UI edit ctrl 0x1e

specs.semantics: Account login on the game socket. The server sends S2C 0x5A (i32 code key) as the first packet after connect. The client's 0x5A handler: (1) calls SetCodeKey(key); (2) initializes the object at app+0x700 (FUN_0045ae40); (3) computes the MD5 hex of the account-ID string into app+0xD0A. The second %s in that sprintf is a zeroed 64-byte stack buffer, so the key is NOT hashed. (4) strncmp's the hex against player+0x131 (32 bytes) and sets player+0x218 = 1 if they differ, else 0. (5) Sleeps 1000 ms. (6) Sends opcode 0x01 + 41 bytes of account ID + 21 bytes of password. Nothing else is Added: no ResetBuffer, no helper Adds, no branches between the first Add and Send. The hash and the key are not sent.
specs.trigger: Automatic: runs every time S2C 0x5A is received on the game socket. Normally this happens once, right after the user presses login in the channel/login dialog and ConnectToGameServer succeeds.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x02 login result: u8 result (1 = success, followed by the account/character list; other codes show an error dialog and the client closes the socket).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Before connecting, the login dialog (FUN_00446300) requires non-empty account and password (strlen checks at 0x4481A9 and 0x4481C9) and a channel status of 3 at 0x448211. The strcpy's are unbounded and do not clear the rest of the buffer. So (a) an account ID of 41+ chars is sent with no NUL terminator, and (b) bytes after the NUL can be leftovers from an earlier, longer entry in the same session. The server must split each field at the first NUL. Because of the Sleep(1000) inside the receive critical section, the login arrives about 1 s after 0x5A, and no other S2C packet is processed meanwhile. Every extra S2C 0x5A makes the client re-send the login (the server already ignores a mid-flow 0x01). The Send argument is always 1 (encode mode; it is not part of the body).
specs.references: Matches the live capture (0x01 payload = 62 bytes), protocol.md ('CHAR[41] username, CHAR[21] password') and windslayer_server.py _handle_login (payload[0:41], payload[41:62]). Correction to protocol.md: it says the 0x5A handler 'computes MD5 of username+key'. The asm shows sprintf("%s%s", account_id, <zeroed 64-byte buffer>), so it is MD5(account_id) only. The key is not mixed in, and the hash is used only locally (player+0x218 flag). PySlayer has no client_packets parser for 0x01.
open_questions: Meaning of player+0x218 (set when MD5(account_id) != player+0x131); it may mark a changed or new account for saved-login UI. It is not on the wire.
The max length of edit controls 0x1c/0x1e was not checked. If it is 40/20 or less, the NUL is always inside the field.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of the Send(int) argument (always 1 here); it is not part of the body.
Whether Fireway's Send clears the accumulated buffer (assumed, since every client send site is Add...Send with no ResetBuffer).

specs.name: WhisperChat

locations.role: "/message " (compares 6) and "/whisper " (compares 9) -> prefix_len=6 in BOTH cases (client bug)
first-switch case 2: validate and parse the target name into game_state+0x4B0 (17 bytes zeroed, then strncpy of 1..16 chars)
chat-mode override: [g_ui_root+0x44]==1 with no prefix -> type=2, msg_len=(u8)length, msg=whole text, target=previous game_state+0x4B0
after the send: look the target up in UI window 0x6E (whisper list) and add it via FUN_00444950 if absent

specs.grammar:
str[17] target_name
u8 msg_len
bytes[msg_len] message

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: Recipient character name, 1..16 chars, NUL-padded to 17 (always NUL-terminated on the normal path). On the whisper-tab path (no /w prefix) it is the previously stored target and can be all zeros if none was ever set.
fields.dest_or_source: game_state+0x4B0 (0x70EEB0): zeroed at 0x445256, filled by strncpy at 0x445300 from the name token after the /w prefix

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Byte count of the message that follows (no NUL counted). Explicit /w: input_length - space_index - 1. Whisper-tab mode: low byte of the full input length.

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Whisper text (EUC-KR/ASCII), not NUL-terminated on the wire.
fields.dest_or_source: EBX = input text + space_index + 1 (explicit /w), or the whole input buffer (whisper-tab mode)

specs.semantics: Private message to one character. After Send the client makes sure the target is in its whisper-history list (UI window 0x6E, FUN_00444950) and sets the chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]=1, so later plain lines also go as whispers to game_state+0x4B0. The client does not echo the message locally. The echo comes from the server (S2C 0x09).
specs.trigger: The user types "/w name message" (also "/W", "/ㅈ ", "/message ", "/whisper ") and presses Enter, or types a plain line while the chat mode is whisper ([g_ui_root+0x44]==1). Chat macros and the UI 0x294 path reach the same code.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x09 (handler around 0x4511D9) to the sender: u8 result (0x66 "can not be found.", 0x67 "is rejecting whispers.", 0x65 or a channel number = delivered), then str[17] target, and on success u8 len + text shown as "<To: %s> %s". S2C 0x0A (0x451383) to the recipient: u8, str[17] sender, u8 len, text shown as "<From: %s> %s". The 0x09/0x0A layouts were only skimmed; confirm them with the S2C specs.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Common chat gates first: length>=1; Curse_Engine_Clean ("No cursing please"); manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40; [scene+0xF00]==6. Whisper gates: length > prefix_len, else "/w player_name message"; manner [scene+0xEE0] > -20, else "You can't whisper to others due to your low manner point."; the name ends at the first space within 16 chars, else "Character name must be within 16 characters." or the usage message; at least one byte after the space; target != own name (scene+0x206), else "You can't  send a message to yourself.". Whispers have NO 700 ms anti-spam check (normal and party chat do). QUIRK 1: "/message " and "/whisper " set prefix_len=6, so the name is parsed from index 6 ("/whisper bob hi" -> name "er"). QUIRK 2 (LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION, C35, chat_mail_gm#13): whisper mode with no stored target sends an all-zero 17-byte name but msg_len AND the message ARE present - observed payload 00 x17, 02, "hi" (20 B), not msg_len = 0 as previously documented. The server must still drop a whisper whose target name is empty. QUIRK 3: the whisper-tab path can send an all-zero target name if no target was stored. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.
specs.references: PySlayer has no C2S 0x02 parser but has S2C opcode_0x0A 'Whisper' (u8 1, name17, u8 len, text), which matches the EN 0x0A read order seen here. windslayer_server.py has no 0x02 dispatch branch.
open_questions: Full S2C 0x09 layout (the result codes other than 0x65/0x66/0x67, and whether a channel u32/u8 follows) was not traced here.
Which UI element sets [g_ui_root+0x44]=1 besides a successful /w (for example a chat-tab button). This decides how often the empty-target whisper-tab case can happen.
blind_open_questions: Exact S2C the recipient receives (0x0A per PySlayer) not verified in the EN binary in this pass.
Default value of chat mode ui_root+0x44 at login is unknown.

spec_errata.old: empty-target whisper said to carry msg_len 0
spec_errata.new: the name is zeroed but msg_len and the text are present

spec_errata.old: curse filter mentioned without its substring behaviour
spec_errata.new: substring filter; a blocked word means zero packets

specs.name: NormalChat
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x70E6F4], TCP 7022). Every Add and the Send at 0x445C66-0x445CA7 load ECX from [0x70E6F4].

locations.role: strncmp(text,"/\xA4\xB1 ",4) (EUC-KR jamo for the a key). Sets type=3, prefix_len=4 and [g_ui_root+0x44]=5 (0x4450D9)
No recognized prefix: type=3 and prefix_len=0. The chat mode is unchanged
First switch case 3. Exact "/a \0" or "/\xA4\xB1 \0" shows "/p message to all" and returns 3 (0x44590D). Otherwise sprintf_s(buf61 @esp+0x38, 0x3D, "%s", text+prefix_len) at 0x4458C8
[esp+0x18] = strlen(buf61). strcpy buf61 back over the start of the text buffer (0x4458F0). EBX=[esp+0x20]=text (0x445902/0x445906)

Type 3 routing by chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]: mode 0 -> 0x445A67 (JZ 0x44544D); mode>5 or negative -> 0x445A67 (JA 0x445459); else table 0x445E68: 1->0x445936 whisper, 2->0x44594C party, 3->0x445A67, 4->0x4459D7 friends, 5->0x445A54
Mode 5: type=3 and [esp+0x18] = low byte of the length ARGUMENT [esp+0x21C], which is strlen of the ORIGINAL text in all callers
Modes 0/3/>5: EBX=[esp+0x20] (text). The length stays strlen(buf61)
Final switch case 3 (table 0x445E7C/idx 0x445E90). Anti-spam: diff < 0x2BC jumps to 0x445BFA "Do not Spam." (timer refreshed, no send). Otherwise [this+0x3E8]=now (0x445C72)
Add(char* EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]): exactly msg_len raw bytes
Send(1) on g_sock_game, then refreshes chat UI windows 9/10 (FUN_004838c0) and returns 0
Caller: chat macro slot this+0xE88+i*0x25 (12 slots), len=strlen
Caller: 64-byte stack copy of UI control 0x294 text (sprintf_s 0x40), sets [g_ui_root+0x44]=5 at 0x44AE50, len=strlen

specs.grammar:
u8 msg_len
bytes[msg_len] message

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Chat modes 0, 3 or anything >5: strlen of the prefix-stripped text, <= 60. Chat mode 5 ("All" tab, forced by a "/a " or "/ㅁ " prefix and by the 0x294 caller): low byte of strlen of the ORIGINAL input including the prefix. The two values are equal for a plain line of <= 60 bytes with no prefix.
fields.dest_or_source: stack byte [esp+0x18], set at 0x4458E2 (strlen) or 0x445A61 (mode 5, from arg2)

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Chat text (ASCII/EUC-KR), no NUL terminator on the wire in the normal case. In mode 5 with a prefix, the buffer holds the stripped text, then its NUL, then the rest of the original input, so the real message ends at the first 0x00. Example: "/a hi" -> 03 05 68 69 00 68 69.
fields.dest_or_source: EBX = the caller's text buffer after the in-place strcpy of the sprintf_s(61) result

specs.semantics: Public (area/all) chat line. The client strips a "/a " or "/\xA4\xB1 " prefix (and switches chat mode to 5) or takes the line as is, runs sprintf_s(61,"%s",text+prefix_len), copies the result back over the input, then routes by chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]. Mode 1 becomes whisper opcode 0x02 (send site 0x445ADD), mode 2 becomes party 0x6A (0x445BD9), and mode 4 becomes the friends path (0x445BE4, not this send site). Modes 0, 3, >5 and 5 reach this send, with the length rules above. After the 700 ms anti-spam check the client sends u8 len + raw bytes, then refreshes chat windows 9/10. There is no local echo; the line appears only when the server broadcasts S2C 0x16. Lines starting with '/' that are not client commands (for example "/heart") are sent as ordinary chat. Live capture "hi" -> 03 02 68 69 matches.
specs.trigger: The player presses Enter in the chat box (FUN_004449b0). Also a chat macro hotkey (FUN_0043db00, GetAsyncKeyState, 12 slots of 37 B at this+0xE88) and UI list control 0x294 in FUN_00446300 (0x44AE75, forces mode 5). Chat-tab buttons in FUN_00446300 set the mode: 0x448A9E=1, 0x448B04=2 (after a party check), 0x448B64=4, 0x448BC5=5.
specs.expected_response: Server broadcast S2C 0x16 (handler 0x451AF0). It reads str[17] name first (0x451B0D), then u8 len (0x451B24), then str[len] into a 61-byte stack buffer (0x451B64). It then checks text[0]=='/' for emotes like "/heart" and formats "%s : %s" (0x451CEA). The client waits for nothing specific.
specs.gates_and_hazards: length arg > 0. Curse_Engine_Clean passes, else "No cursing please" (return -1). Manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40, else "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point." [scene+0xF00]==6, else a silent return. A GM ([scene+0x970]+0x12==1) matching a GM command sends a GM opcode (e.g. 0x06) instead. An exact "/a " or "/ㅁ " shows "/p message to all" and returns 3, so the IME text is kept. Anti-spam: a line within 700 ms of the last chat shows "Do not Spam." and refreshes the timer. The strstr for EUC-KR B0 AD C1 F8 C2 AF toggles game_state+0x404 locally with no wire effect. Client-side hazard: sprintf_s(61) at 0x4458C8 does NOT truncate (real CRT sprintf_s). A stripped text over 60 bytes calls the CRT invalid-parameter handler, likely a client abort. Server hazards: in mode 5, msg_len can include a 0x00 and leftover bytes, so cut at the first NUL. An S2C 0x16 with len > 61 overflows the receiver's stack buffer. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire grammar, u8 msg_len + bytes[msg_len] with opcode 0x03, and the asm confirms it. 0x445C7D Add(u8 [esp+0x10]=3), 0x445C8A Add(u8 [esp+0x18]), 0x445C99 Add(EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]), 0x445CA7 Send(1), all on [0x70E6F4]. Both length rules are correct: mode 5 (0x445A54/0x445A61) uses the low byte of arg2 [esp+0x21C], and all three callers pass strlen of the original text (0x4449DD, 0x43DBDB, 0x44AE6F); otherwise strlen of the case-3 result is used (0x4458E2). A's example "/a hi" -> 03 05 68 69 00 68 69 is right, because the "/a " prefix always forces mode 5 (0x4450AC). On mode routing, B was complete (0, 3 and >5 all keep strlen: JZ 0x44544D, JA 0x445459, table 0x445E68 entry 3 -> 0x445A67), while A's "0/3" left out >5. On the 60-byte cap, A was right: 0x48A8CF is real sprintf_s (-> __vsprintf_s_l) and does not truncate, so B's "truncated to 60" is wrong. The chat-tab writers of [g_ui_root+0x44] are 0x448A9E (1), 0x448B04 (2), 0x448B64 (4), 0x448BC5 (5) and 0x44AE50 (5); no writer of 0 or 3 was found. Both analysts were right that our server's 0x16 echo is misaligned: windslayer_server.py _handle_chat builds u8 0x01 + name17 + len + text, but the EN handler's first read (0x451B0D) is char[17], so the leading 0x01 must be removed. PySlayer parse_0x03 (payload[1]=len, text follows) agrees with this spec. Our server's NUL-split parse happens to cope with the mode-5 tail.
open_questions: Initial value of chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44] after login (0 vs 5). It does not change the wire format, only whether msg_len counts the original length (they differ only for prefixed or >60-byte lines).
Is a custom CRT invalid-parameter handler installed? None was found, so a >60-byte stripped line probably aborts the client before sending.

spec_errata.new: substring filter; a blocked word means zero packets

specs.name: InputState_ToRoomHost

locations.role: mode != 0 and host flag == 0: jump to 0x42362D, skipping the snapshot build
return (skipping the input reset) if local player scene+0x970 is NULL
send if local entity +0x98 == 3, or scene+0xF08 == 0, or (scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C) > 9000 (unsigned, JBE at 0x42367C)
Add u8 0x03 via CALL EDI (EDI=[0x4A40FC] at 0x423688)
SendTo(str scene+0xF38, port = movzx word scene+0xF48 + 0x2710, reset=1) via CALL [0x4A410C]
post-tick input reset (also runs when nothing was sent)
S2C 0x2F sets scene+0xF08=0 and (0x450B93) scene+0xF0C = current tick
receiver increments scene+0xF08 for each accepted room snapshot 0x07/0x08/0x09

specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 input_a
u8 input_b

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Local player uid (account_id).

fields.name: input_a
fields.meaning:
(action*10 + dir) & 0xFF.
- dir = scene+0x254: 8 = none, 2/6 = horizontal direction.
- action = scene+0x255: 0 none, 1-5 attack/skill keys, 6 dash, 7 skill cast (sticky).
See UDP-C2S:0x4237FD/0x03 for the full key mapping.

fields.name: input_b
fields.meaning: (skill_variant*10 + status_code) & 0xFF, where skill_variant = scene+0x256 (1..11) and status_code = scene+0x257 (0..5, recomputed each tick).

specs.semantics:
Input/keep-alive datagram from a non-host room participant to the room's UDP host. This is the only UDP traffic a non-host client produces in room maps; no snapshot is built.

Destination: IP string scene+0xF38 (host_ip from S2C 0x2F; SendTo uses inet_addr with gethostbyname fallback). The port is (u16 scene+0xF48 room_no + 10000) & 0xFFFF, passed through htons. scene+0xF48 is also written by the room-join UI at 0x44931C..0x44B031.

Conditions:
- scene+0xF90 != NULL.
- scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6.
- mode [scene+0xF88]+0x70 != 0 (arena/team-battle maps; the map XML mode attribute).
- scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in EN).
- scene+0x970 != NULL.
- At least one of:
  - (a) local entity +0x98 == 3 (player-type entity, as created by room/player spawn packets). The datagram is then sent EVERY tick (at most every 30 ms).
  - (b) scene+0xF08 == 0: no room snapshot 0x07/0x08/0x09 accepted since S2C 0x2F reset it, so it is sent every tick until the host answers.
  - (c) scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C > 9000 ms: keep-alive. F20 is the previous tick's time; F0C is stamped on each send and by S2C 0x2F.

Input bytes are cleared at the end of every tick even when nothing is sent (dir=8; action/variant=0 unless action==7).

On the host side FUN_00423850 uses the datagram's source ip:port to register the peer (entity+0x6A/+0x80, +0x14EA=1) and stores the input digits in entity+0x8B3..0x8B6.

Framing: 8-byte Fireway header (len|0x800|seq<<12; shared per-socket seq at CSNSocket+0x13A8, wrapping 255->0) plus the EncodebyArray checksum/XOR (cencmsg.encode_by_array). reset=1.
specs.trigger: FrameMove tick in a room map (mode != 0) after S2C 0x2F provided host_ip/room_no, subject to the state/F08/9 s conditions above.
specs.expected_response: The room host must send UDP snapshots to the client's g_sock_map, i.e. the source address of this datagram, normally port 42907. Accepted opcodes are 0x07/0x08/0x09 (mode 1 only; header+records, the same layout as 0x04). They must carry map_code == the client's map+0x1B8. Each accepted snapshot increments scene+0xF08, which drops the 0x03 rate to the 9 s keep-alive unless the local entity is +0x98==3. HP/MP datagrams 0x06/0x0B/0x0A/0x10 are also accepted.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- No EN 2008 client can be the host (scene+0xF24 is never set), and every client binds 42907, not room_no+10000. A private server supporting arenas must therefore itself listen on UDP host_ip:(room_no+10000) and act as the host.
- host_ip must be NUL-terminated within 16 bytes. An unresolvable name makes inet_addr and gethostbyname fail; sendto then targets 255.255.255.255 without SO_BROADCAST, and the send fails silently.
- room_no + 10000 is truncated to 16 bits.
- If the local entity is +0x98==3, the flood is continuous (~33/s) regardless of host replies.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x2F: host_ip (scene+0xF38) and room_no (scene+0xF48) are described as 'Non-host peers later send UDP to this IP on port room_no+10000 (FUN_00423260 @0x4236E8)'. PROTOCOL.md C2S 0x0D: 'Not sent in P2P room mode ([map]+0x70 == 1)'. The receiver's host-registration logic is FUN_00423850 at 0x423850-0x423A04.
open_questions: Whether the original service ran a UDP room host/relay on host_ip:(room_no+10000), and which address it replied to. The client accepts snapshots from any source address.
Whether the original host sent 0x07/0x08/0x09 to the recvfrom source port or to the TCP-reported p2p_udp_port (42907). These differ only behind NAT.
blind_open_questions: Scene+0xF24 is never set nonzero anywhere in EN 2008 .text (raw disp32 scan found only the 0 write at 0x411FC3). So who acted as host at host_ip:room_no+10000 (a dedicated battle process, or a host client from another build) cannot be settled statically.
What the original host sent back besides 0x07/0x08/0x09 snapshots, for example the UDP 0x06/0x0A/0x0B/0x10/0x11 cases, was not traced.

specs.name: InputState_Loopback

locations.role: FUN_0042ac00 (keyboard sampling, run only when scene+0xF00 is 4 or 6) writes scene+0x254/0x255 before the builder runs
FUN_0042cf20 recomputes scene+0x257 (clears it at 0x42D0CA, sets 1..5 at 0x42EFDE-0x42F3C0) before the builder runs
after the 0x04 loopback: CMP scene+0xF24,0; the 0x03 block runs only for non-hosts
Add u8 0x03 via CALL EDI (EDI=[0x4A40FC] loaded at 0x423798)
Add u8 (byte scene+0x255 * 10 via IMUL CL) + byte scene+0x254
SendTo("127.0.0.1", port=[scene+0x244], reset=1) via CALL EBP (EBP=[0x4A410C] from 0x423779)
post-send: if scene+0x255 != 7 then scene+0x255=0 and +0x256=0; scene+0x254=8 always
receiver FUN_00423850 (from FUN_00458640 case 3) decodes the input bytes

specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 input_a
u8 input_b

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Local player uid (account_id from S2C 0x02). The receiver looks up the entity with +0x84 == uid and +0x98 in {1,3}.

fields.name: input_a
fields.meaning:
(action*10 + dir) & 0xFF, computed with 8-bit IMUL.
- dir = scene+0x254. 8 = no horizontal input (reset every tick). FUN_0042ac00 sets 2 when only key app+0xDE0 is held and 6 when only key app+0xDE4 is held; dash also uses 2/6.
- action = scene+0x255:
  - 0 = none
  - 1 = key app+0xDF4 (gated by FUN_0041ca50 ammo/MP)
  - 2 = key app+0xDF0
  - 3 = key app+0xDE8
  - 4 = key app+0xDEC
  - 5 = key app+0xDF8 (gated)
  - 6 = double-tap dash (FUN_00426c50(0x50))
  - 7 = skill cast, set by the S2C skill-use confirmation; sticky until acknowledged.
The receiver writes action = a/10 to entity+0x8B4 and dir = a%10 to entity+0x8B3, and sets +0x15DC=1 if a != 8.

fields.name: input_b
fields.meaning:
(skill_variant*10 + status_code) & 0xFF.
- skill_variant = scene+0x256 (1..11 for action 7; cleared with 0x255).
- status_code = scene+0x257 (0..5): a local-player effect class recomputed each tick by FUN_0042cf20, e.g. 1 for effect ids 0x192-0x19C, 2 for 0x8C6-0x8D0 / 0x908-0x912, 3 for 0x934-0x93E, 4 for 0xA10-0xA1A, 5 for 0x9D9-0x9E3. The builder never resets it.
The receiver writes b/10 to entity+0x8B5 and b%10 to entity+0x8B6.

specs.semantics:
The local player's input state, sent to the client's own socket every tick in normal maps, right after the 0x04 loopback snapshot (seq = snapshot seq + 1).

Destination: 127.0.0.1 : scene+0x244 (= 42907).

Conditions:
- scene+0xF90 != NULL and scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6.
- mode [scene+0xF88]+0x70 == 0.
- scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in EN).
- The local player pointer scene+0x970 is NOT checked on this path, so it is also sent at character select.

After the send, dir resets to 8. Action and variant reset to 0 unless action == 7, which stays until a received snapshot shows the local entity with action code 0x17..0x21 (FUN_00458640 0x458CAx clears scene+0x255/0x256).

Receiver: FUN_00458640 case 3 -> FUN_00423850(uid, a, b, src_ip, src_port). It finds the entity with uid match and +0x98 in {1,3}, stores the decoded digits in +0x8B3..+0x8B6 and +0x88 = scene+0xF1C. When the receiver is a host (never in EN) it also records src_ip/src_port in entity+0x6A/+0x80 and sets +0x14EA=1. If the receiver is in room phase 2, or phase 1 with F1C < 5100, actions 1/5/7 and input_b are zeroed.

Framing: 8-byte Fireway header (len|0x800|seq<<12; seq is the shared per-socket counter at CSNSocket+0x13A8, wrapping 255->0) plus the EncodebyArray checksum. The payload is XORed with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]. reset=1.
specs.trigger: Every FrameMove tick in map mode 0 (after the 0x04 loopback at 0x423787).
specs.expected_response: None. It is consumed locally by FUN_00458640 case 3.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Loopback only. Do not bind UDP 42907 on the client PC.
- In the local field the player entity is usually +0x98==4, so the self-receive lookup (which needs +0x98 in {1,3}) usually finds nothing and the datagram is a no-op. It still consumes a sequence number.
- Byte math is modulo 256, but the maximum 7*10+8 = 78 and 11*10+5 = 115 fit.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C skill-use confirmation notes 'scene+0x255=7 and scene+0x256=variant ... go out on the UDP P2P state as action*10+dir'. FUN_0042ac00 input writes at 0x42B045-0x42B22A. FUN_0042cf20 +0x257 writes at 0x42D0CA, 0x42EFDE-0x42F105 and 0x42F2D8-0x42F3C0.
open_questions: Which of dir 2/6 is left and which is right. The key bindings app+0xDE0/0xDE4 are not resolved to named keys.
Exact meaning of the scene+0x257 status classes 1..5 (buff/effect families).
blind_open_questions: Exact key bindings behind game_state+0xDE0/0xDE4/0xDE8/0xDEC and the ranges read at FUN_0042ac00 +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20 (which keys give action 1-5) were not traced.

Whether a normal-field local player is ever state 1 or 3 in the original server flow (PROTOCOL.md notes FUN_00444100 creates state 4, which FUN_00423850 ignores) decides whether this loopback actually drives movement in the field.

specs.name: StatPointAllocate (STR)

locations.role: dispatch: window 1 (status window) control switch (ctrl-0xA, table 0x44BB50); ctrl 10 -> 0x4483D8

specs.grammar: u8 stat_index

fields.name: stat_index
fields.meaning: Which stat gets +1. At this site it is always 0 (STR, the first + button). Sites 0x4484CC send 1/2/3.

specs.semantics: Spends one stat point on STR. The client itself sends only the index. Checking remaining points and applying the change is left to the server.
specs.trigger: Click on control 10 of UI window 1 (character status window, the STR + button). This is FUN_00446300's default click path (param_4 not 1..4, ctrl != 0).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x14 stat update (u32 uid, u8 stat_type, u16 new_value), per PySlayer add_stats(). No 'waiting' modal is shown.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Blocked client-side when [[this+0x4D8]+0x70]==1 (arena/play-room map flag): the chat line 'Not allowed in arena.' is shown and nothing is sent. The client does NOT check remaining stat points here, so the server must validate them.
specs.references: PySlayer game_server.py opcode 0x4 setStats: payload[1] 0=str,1=dex,2=int,3=tol, answered with opcode_14(uid,type,value). Our windslayer_server.py _handle_set_stats reads payload[0] correctly but replies 0x14 with a hardcoded value 4 and does no bookkeeping.
open_questions: Whether the server must also send an updated remaining-stat-points value (0x14 only carries one stat) is not determined from this site.
blind_open_questions: Which S2C opcode the original server used to confirm the allocation (our server uses 0x14 uid+type+u16, unverified).
Stat names for index 0..3 (probably STR/DEX/INT/SPR in window order, not proven statically).

specs.name: StatPointAllocate (DEX/INT/TOL)

locations.role: dispatch: window 1 ctrl table 0x44BB50: ctrl 12 -> 0x44842B, ctrl 14 -> 0x44844F, ctrl 16 -> 0x448473
gate (ctrl 12): [[this+0x4D8]+0x70]==1 -> 'Not allowed in arena.' (same check at 0x448459 and 0x44847D)
Add(u8) opcode 0x04 for ctrl 12, then PUSH 1
Add(u8) opcode 0x04 for ctrl 14, then PUSH 2
Add(u8) opcode 0x04 for ctrl 16, then PUSH 3

specs.grammar: u8 stat_index

fields.name: stat_index
fields.meaning: 1 = DEX (ctrl 12), 2 = INT (ctrl 14), 3 = TOL/VIT (ctrl 16). Index 0 (STR) is sent from site 0x44840E.

specs.semantics: Spends one stat point on DEX, INT or TOL. Same packet as 0x44840E/0x04, just a different index.
specs.trigger: Click on the +DEX/+INT/+TOL buttons (controls 12/14/16) of window 1, the character status window.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x14 (u32 uid, u8 stat_type, u16 value), per PySlayer.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Arena/play-room map flag [[this+0x4D8]+0x70]==1 blocks the send and shows 'Not allowed in arena.'. There is no client check of remaining points.
specs.references: PySlayer setStats (0=str,1=dex,2=int,3=tol). Our _handle_set_stats reads payload[0] but fakes the reply value (4). The stat order matches the 0x0E character-create stat fields (+0x296..+0x29C).
blind_open_questions: Confirmation S2C opcode and its payload.
Human names of stats 1..3.

specs.name: HostWorldSnapshot_Unicast (dead code)

locations.role: the snapshot is built when mode==0, or when mode!=0 and host flag scene+0xF24 != 0
mode==0 && host!=0 -> 0x423715 (mode!=0 && host!=0 also reaches 0x423715 via 0x423644)
per entity in scene+0xC: +0x98 == 3 or 1, and byte +0x14EA != 0 (peer registered)
SendTo(str entity+0x6A, port=u32 entity+0x80, reset=0): the same buffer goes to each peer
the only write to scene+0xF24 in the image (0, CGameMain ctor), which makes this path unreachable

fields.name: header
fields.meaning:
Bits:
- 0-8: 0 (mode != 1).
- 9-17: count of entities with +0x98==3, or +0x98==4 && +0xE64>=3.
- 18-31: map_code = map+0x1B8.

fields.name: rec_a
fields.meaning:
Bits:
- 0-11: trunc(posX*0.5).
- 12-22: trunc(posY*0.5).
- 23: facing (0 if +0x8BD==2).
- 24-29: action-1, or 0x16+skill variant.
- 30/31: attack event flags.
Same as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04.

fields.name: rec_b
fields.meaning:
Bits:
- 0: entity+0x8E0 & 1.
- 1-25: uid & 0x1FFFFFF.
- 26-31: stale.

specs.semantics:
Host-side fan-out of the world snapshot to every registered P2P peer. Peer addresses were learned from the source address of their 0x03 datagrams (FUN_00423850).

Destination: for each scene-list entity with +0x98 in {3,1} and +0x14EA != 0, the IP string at entity+0x6A and the port at u32 entity+0x80. SendTo is called with reset=0 so the same payload goes to every peer; ResetBuffer runs after the loop. If no peer qualifies, the built snapshot is simply discarded.

Conditions: host flag scene+0xF24 != 0 and mode != 1 (mode 1 uses opcodes 7/8/9 instead). No 0x03 is sent in host mode.

DEAD CODE in EN 2008: scene+0xF24 is written only as 0 (0x411FC3), confirmed by a .text scan for disp 0xF24.

Framing: as for all g_sock_map sends. Each per-peer SendTo gets its own seq (the counter increments per call), so the header and XOR differ per peer even though the plaintext is identical.
specs.trigger: Unreachable in EN 2008 (would be every FrameMove tick with host flag set).
specs.expected_response: None (peers consume it in FUN_00458640 case 4).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Dead code. Documented only so a server author is not confused by the SendTo site. A server never receives this datagram from an EN client.
specs.references: Raw IAT xref census: 0x4A410C is referenced only at 0x4236F7, 0x42371C and 0x42377B. PROTOCOL.md pvp_arena dead-code C2S 0x93/0x94/0x95 entries record the same F24 finding.
blind_open_questions: Whether some unanalyzed path (a struct copy, or code outside .text) sets scene+0xF24. None was found statically.
Map modes other than 0/1 were not seen in the corpus; the opcode choice for them (0x04) is taken straight from the code.

specs.name: WorldSnapshot_Loopback

locations.role: render loop FUN_0040db20 calls vtable+0x18 (FUN_0042b260, FrameMove) at most once per 30 ms, inside CS game_state+0x368 (entered at 0x40DD03)
FUN_0042b260 returns unless scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6
CALL FUN_00423260 with ESI=scene. Afterwards 0x42B4F4 sets scene+0xF20 = game_state+0x364 (tick ms)
return if scene+0xF90 (UDP socket) is NULL
mode=[[scene+0xF88]+0x70]. The snapshot is built if mode==0, or if mode!=0 and host flag scene+0xF24!=0
Add u8 opcode. PUSH 4 at 0x4232B2 when mode!=1; 7/9/8 by scene+0xF04 when mode==1
header bits 0-8 cleared (the timer is only set when mode==1 && F04==1, 0x4232CD-0x42331A)
count loop (mode!=1 filter): entity+0x98==3, or +0x98==4 && +0xE64>=3; increments header bits 9-17
Add(char* scene+0xEEC, 4) via CALL EBX (EBX=[0x4A40EC] loaded at 0x4233D2)
record loop over scene+0xC list (node[0]=next, node[2]=entity), same filter as the count loop
Add(char* scene+0xEF0, 8) per record via CALL EBX
mode==0: host flag==0 -> 0x42376D (loopback). host!=0 -> peer unicast 0x423715 (dead)
SendTo("127.0.0.1" (0x6F3270), port=[scene+0x244], reset=1) via CALL EBP (EBP=[0x4A410C] loaded at 0x423779)
receiver: reads the header into scene+0xEEC, drops the datagram if (hdr>>18) != map+0x1B8, reads count records of 8 bytes into scene+0xEF0

specs.length: 4 + 8*N, where N = header count. At most 254 records fit, because Fireway Add refuses to grow the buffer past 0x7F7 bytes. A 13 + 8*N byte datagram on the wire.

fields.name: header
fields.meaning: Snapshot header, assembled in scene+0xEEC and sent as 4 raw bytes (little-endian).

fields.name: header.round_timer_s
fields.meaning: Always 0 at this site, because mode==0. The builder only fills it when mode==1 && scene+0xF04==1: trunc(u32 scene+0xF1C ms * 0.001) & 0x1FF.

fields.name: header.count
fields.meaning: Number of records that follow (9-bit counter, wraps at 512). Counts scene-list entities with +0x98==3 (player-type entity) or with +0x98==4 and +0xE64 >= 3 (unsigned; +0xE64 = gamedef category, >=3 is an AI monster).

fields.name: header.map_code
fields.meaning: Loaded map code = AA*100+BB parsed from stageAA_BB.hmi (FUN_00407190 0x40752D). Only the low 14 bits survive. Receivers discard the datagram when it differs from their own map+0x1B8.

fields.name: rec_a
fields.meaning: Per-entity position/action word, built in scene+0xEF0.

fields.name: rec_a.x_half
fields.meaning: trunc(posX * 0.5) & 0xFFF. FISTP with RC=chop; DAT_6F8AE0 = 0.5. The receiver stores x*2 in entity+0x15A4.

fields.name: rec_a.y_half
fields.meaning: trunc(posY * 0.5) & 0x7FF. The receiver stores y*2 in entity+0x15A8.

fields.name: rec_a.facing
fields.meaning: 0 if entity+0x8BD == 2, else 1. The receiver sets entity+0x15B0 = 2 (bit clear) or 6 (bit set).

fields.name: rec_a.action_code
fields.meaning: (entity+0x904 action - 1) & 0x3F, e.g. idle 8 -> 7. If byte entity+0x8FE (skill variant) is 1..11, the value is replaced by 0x16+variant (0x17..0x21; switch at 0x423568, jump table 0x423824). A receiver whose local entity shows code 0x17..0x21 clears its own scene+0x255/0x256 (skill-cast acknowledgement).

fields.name: rec_a.event_flag_30
fields.meaning: Set if action(+0x904) is 1, 2, 4, 0xE, 0xF or 0x11 and byte +0x8D9 != 0, or if action is 3 or 0x17 and byte +0x8D1 == 1. Tests the raw action, not the overridden code. The receiver fires attack/hit effects and sounds when bit 30 or 31 is set.

fields.name: rec_a.event_flag_31
fields.meaning: Set if action is 3 or 0x17 and byte +0x8D1 == 2.

fields.name: rec_b
fields.meaning: Per-entity identity word, built in scene+0xEF4.

fields.name: rec_b.anim_toggle
fields.meaning: entity+0x8E0 & 1. When this bit changes, the receiver resets the entity's animation timer +0x15AC and stores the bit in +0x15B2.

fields.name: rec_b.uid
fields.meaning: Entity uid & 0x1FFFFFF. The receiver matches (rec_b>>1)&0x1FFFFFF against entity+0x84 for entities with +0x98 > 2.

fields.name: rec_b.stale
fields.meaning: Never written by the builder. They carry whatever scene+0xEF4 held: the last record built or received (the receiver copies into the same scratch), and at first uninitialised heap from CGameMain new(0xFA0). Must be ignored.

specs.semantics:
Per-tick world snapshot. In normal (non-room) maps the client sends it to its own UDP socket, so the client acts as its own simulation host.

Destination: 127.0.0.1 : u32 scene+0x244. That port is only ever written as 42907 (0x4400D9, 0x459BAB, 0x476526), which is the client's own g_sock_map bind. The datagram never leaves the machine.

Conditions, all required:
- scene+0xF90 != NULL.
- scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6. This includes character select (F00=5) and in-world.
- mode = [scene+0xF88]+0x70 == 0. The map XML 'mode' attribute is parsed by FUN_00407190 at 0x4076E7; values >1 are stored minus 2.
- Host flag scene+0xF24 == 0. This is always true in EN 2008: the only write is 0 in the CGameMain ctor at 0x411FC3, confirmed by a .text scan.

Rate: once per FrameMove, at most every 30 ms (~33 Hz). It is followed in the same tick by the 0x03 loopback (seq+1).

Records are emitted in scene-list order. The emit filter is identical to the count filter in this mode, so the count matches the records unless more than 254 qualify: extra Adds then fail silently and the header count is too high.

Receiver (FUN_00458640 case 4, accepted only when its mode != 1): drops the datagram if map_code differs, otherwise applies each record to the entity with the matching uid. See the field meanings.

Framing: 8-byte Fireway header. dword0 = (len+8)&0x7FF | 0x800 | seq<<12, where seq is the per-socket counter CSNSocket+0x13A8 shared by all g_sock_map sends, pre-incremented and wrapping 255->0. dword1 = EncodebyArray checksum. The payload is XORed with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] (static table; cencmsg.encode_by_array). reset=1 clears the buffer after the send.
specs.trigger: Every FrameMove tick (FUN_0042b260 -> FUN_00423260) while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6 and the map mode is 0.
specs.expected_response: None from any server. The client's own receive path (FUN_00458640 case 4) consumes it.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Loopback only. A server or tool on the same PC must not bind UDP 42907, or the client's socket creation fails.
- If scene+0x244 were still 0 (never observed after login), sendto goes to port 0 and fails silently.
- The stale bits 26-31 of rec_b must be masked.
- Positions are truncated to even coordinates, X in 0..8190 and Y in 0..4094. Negative or larger coordinates wrap modulo the field width.
specs.references: Fireway SendTo(str) 0x10003C60: inet_addr with gethostbyname fallback, SetHeader, EncodebyArray, sendto(len+8), and reset when arg3 != 0. Constants: 0x6F8AE0 = 0.5, 0x6F8A90 = 0.001, 0x6F8A98 = 2^32, 0x6F3270 = "127.0.0.1". The receiver-side decode in FUN_00458640 (0x458763-0x458D45) confirms every bit position. No server involvement is needed; the private server correctly never binds 42907.
open_questions: Direction convention of entity+0x15B0 values 2/6 (left/right) set from the facing bit is not verified.
Exact semantic names of entity+0x8D1/+0x8D9 (attack-phase flags) and +0x8E0 (animation restart toggle) are inferred from receiver behaviour.
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of entity +0x8D1, +0x8D9 and +0x8E0 (hit-stage and toggle flags) was not traced beyond the bit packing.
Whether scene+0xEF4 is zeroed at allocation, which decides bits 26-31 of the first entry ever sent, was not found. Receivers ignore those bits.

specs.name: KeepAlive

locations.function: FUN_00446300 (back to server select / close game socket)

specs.semantics: Periodic heartbeat that keeps the game connection alive. The payload is empty and the client expects nothing back.
specs.trigger: Win32 timer id 6, repeating every 240000 ms (4 min). The S2C 0x03 (enter world / map info) handler arms it and re-arms it (resetting the interval) on every 0x03, i.e. on every map load. It is killed on logout-to-server-select and on app cleanup.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate beyond the timer being active (sent inside the app critical section, whatever the UI state). Do NOT reply with S2C 0x05: per project notes that resets in-game state and kicks the client. The server may use the absence of 0x05 for more than about 4 minutes (plus slack) as an idle/dead-connection signal.
specs.references: Our server _dispatch: 0x05 consumed with no reply ('client heartbeat ~4 min'), which matches the 240000 ms timer. PySlayer has no C2S 0x05 parser.

specs.name: GmMannerPointAdjust

locations.role: chat-command parser entry (__thiscall, this=game_state 0x70EA00, args: text ptr, strlen)
caller: chat box IME submit (passes CIME text +0x104, strlen)
caller: chat macro hotkeys (12 slots, text at this+0xE88+i*0x25)
caller: UI message 0x294 path (sprintf of FUN_00483120()+0x50)

specs.grammar:
u8 gm_subcmd
str[17] target_name
i32 manner_delta

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: GM command selector, constant 0x0A = /manner

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: target character name: first whitespace-delimited token after "/manner " (sscanf %s into a zeroed 17-byte stack buffer [esp+0x24]), NUL padded

fields.name: manner_delta
fields.meaning: manner points to add/subtract (signed); must be non-zero or nothing is sent

specs.semantics: GM chat command "/manner <name> <points>" typed into chat (or a chat macro). Asks the server to change the named character's manner points by the signed amount (manner points are the value at scene+0xEE0 that blocks chat/whisper/trade/room use when low). Client does nothing locally besides clearing the chat input (function returns 0).
specs.trigger: GM (local entity word +0x12 == 1) submits chat text starting with "/manner " and longer than 8 chars, with a non-empty name token and a non-zero integer second token.
specs.expected_response: None awaited; fire-and-forget. No client-side follow-up state.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates in order: strlen>=1; ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text) must pass (else "No cursing please"); scene+0xEE0 (own manner points) > -40 (else "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point."); scene+0xF00 == 6 (else return, nothing sent); word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1 (GM flag of local player entity, filled by the u16 read at 0x44F08D in S2C 0x07) else the text goes to normal chat parsing at 0x445063; strlen > 8. Hazards: name token > 16 chars overflows the 17-byte stack buffer; the i32 local [esp+0x20] is NOT initialized on this path, so if the second token is not a number sscanf leaves stack garbage and it is sent if non-zero. Offset of the second sscanf assumes exactly one space after the name.
specs.references: No C2S 0x06 parser in PySlayer (client_packets has only 03,0B,0C,0D,0F,15,1A,2B,2C,7E) and no GM-command references there. Our server's _dispatch (windslayer_server.py ~602-655) has no 0x06 branch. "/manner " string at 0x6F7BF8 is only referenced by this function.
open_questions: Server-side semantics (whether delta is added or set, and any reply packet) are not observable in the client.
Exact meaning of scene+0xF00 == 6 (assumed in-world field scene).
blind_open_questions: Server-side meaning of manner_points (absolute set vs delta) cannot be derived from the client.
Whether the server answers with any S2C (e.g. notice) is unknown.

specs.name: GmSimpleCommand (/update, /shadow, /stop N, /kick N)

locations.role: REPE CMPSB 10 bytes vs "/\xBE\xF7\xB5\xA5\xC0\xCC\xC6\xAE\0" (CP949 "/업데이트" = /update, exact match incl. NUL)
/stop path: Add(u8 0x06), Add(u8 0x07) at 0x445006, PUSH atol(text+5), JMP 0x444C81
/kick path: Add(u8 0x06), Add(u8 0x0C) at 0x44504F, PUSH atol(text+5), JMP 0x444C81
shared Add via ESI = PTR_Add_004a40fc (Add(uchar)) of the pushed value

specs.length: 1 byte for /업데이트 (06 00) and /shadow (06 02); 2 bytes for /stop (06 07 NN) and /kick (06 0C NN)

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: 0x00 = "/업데이트" (update; exact 9-char CP949 string), 0x02 = "/shadow" (prefix match, 7 chars; likely GM invisibility), 0x07 = "/stop" (prefix 5; string table neighbours are the maintenance-shutdown messages), 0x0C = "/kick" (prefix 5)

fields.name: arg
fields.meaning: only for /stop and /kick: atol(text+5) truncated to its low 8 bits (Add(uchar) via ESI=[0x4A40FC]); e.g. "/stop 3" -> 03, "/kick 300" -> 0x2C

specs.semantics: GM one-shot commands sharing one Send. /업데이트 sends 06 00 (server-side update/reload; exact meaning unknown). /shadow sends 06 02 (probably toggle GM hidden/shadow mode). /stop N sends 06 07 N (probably schedule server maintenance shutdown; S2C 0x3A prints "[Announcement] Server will be down in 3 minutes for the maintenance."). /kick N sends 06 0C N (numeric u8 argument only - not a name). The client does nothing else; chat input is cleared.
specs.trigger: GM submits chat text: exactly "/업데이트"; or text beginning "/shadow" (no length check); or beginning "/stop" with strlen > 5; or beginning "/kick" with strlen > 5. Check order in the GM branch: /manner, /업데이트, /not(ice), /proom, /shadow, /reset, /go, /stop, /kick.
specs.expected_response: None awaited by the client. Possibly related S2C 0x3A (maintenance announcement) for /stop - unverified.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same gates as the whole GM branch: strlen>=1, Curse_Engine_Clean pass, scene+0xEE0 > -40, scene+0xF00 == 6, word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1 (else normal chat). /stop and /kick: argument silently truncated to 8 bits; non-numeric text gives 0. Prefix matching means e.g. "/stopwatch" or "/shadowy" is captured as a GM command and never sent as chat. /업데이트 needs the exact CP949 bytes (typeable only through a Korean IME or a macro).
specs.references: No PySlayer or server coverage. Strings: "/shadow" 0x6F771C, "/stop" 0x6F5770, "/kick" 0x6F527C, "/업데이트" 0x6F572C, all also listed in the message-string pointer table around 0x70BA48..0x70BC44 (neighbour strings used only as naming hints).
open_questions: Server meaning of sub-ops 0x00 (/업데이트) and 0x0C (/kick with u8 argument - channel? index?) is not derivable from the client.
Whether the /stop u8 is minutes until shutdown (S2C 0x3A text hardcodes 3 minutes).
blind_open_questions: Server meaning of sub 0x00 (update/reload?) and sub 0x02 (/shadow = GM invisibility toggle?) is inferred from command names only.
Why /kick carries only a u8 (atol truncated) - possibly kick-all by channel/server index; cannot be derived client-side.

specs.name: GmNotice
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x70E6F4], TCP 7022) - every Add and the Send at 0x444CB9..0x444CFD load ECX from [0x70E6F4]

locations.role: EBX = param_3 (text length; every caller passes strlen of the text), EBP = param_2 (chat text pointer) at 0x444AAF
TEST EBX,EBX / JLE exit: length must be > 0
Curse_Engine_Clean(text): if it fails, shows 'No cursing please' and returns -1 (nothing sent)
[[this+0x4CC]+0xEE0] > -40 (manner) or shows the low-manner message and returns -1
word [[[this+0x4CC]+0x970]+0x12] == 1 (GM flag); otherwise jumps to the non-GM path at 0x445063
REPE CMPSB with 10 bytes against '/업데이트'+NUL (0x6F572C) fails -> 0x444C9C
strncmp(text, '/notice ' @0x6F5720, 4): only the 4 bytes '/not' are compared
CMP EBX,4 / JBE 0x445D18 at 0x444CB3: length must be > 4
Send(1) on g_sock_game, then JMP 0x445D18 (XOR EAX,EAX -> return 0)
caller: chat input submit (IME result string at [0x70E708]+0x104, len = strlen). A return of 0 leads to CIME::ResetResultString, which clears the chat input
caller: macro text slot (this+0xE88+i*0x25, 37-byte slots, so strlen <= 36)
caller: text built by sprintf_s into a 0x40-byte buffer (strlen <= 63)

specs.grammar:
u8 gm_subcmd
u8 text_len
bytes[text_len] notice_text
specs.length: 2 + (L - 4), where L = strlen of the typed line (the caller-supplied length). Total body with the opcode is L - 1 bytes.

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: GM command selector, constant 0x01 = notice/announcement. Related sites in the same function: 0x0A = /manner (site #15, 0x444C22), 0x00 = /업데이트 'update' (site #16, 0x444C7F)

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: (L - 4) & 0xFF, the number of text bytes that follow
fields.dest_or_source: MOVZX EAX,BL; SUB AL,4; PUSH EAX (EBX = caller-supplied strlen)

fields.name: notice_text
fields.meaning: The raw line starting at byte index 4, with no NUL terminator and possibly CP949 multibyte text. Only '/not' is checked and exactly 4 bytes are skipped, so '/notice hello' sends 'ice hello' (9 bytes), '/not hello' sends ' hello' (leading space kept) and '/nothello' sends 'hello'
fields.dest_or_source: ADD EBX,-4; PUSH EBX (N); ADD EBP,4; PUSH EBP (src = text+4)

specs.semantics: A GM asks for a server-wide announcement. The client sends [06 01 len text...] and returns 0, which makes the chat-submit caller clear the input line. The client shows nothing locally. The server should broadcast the text as a system notice. The client has an '[Announcement] ' string at 0x6F5710 for display, but this spec does not identify which S2C packet carries it.
specs.trigger: A GM (flag word ==1 at [[scene+0x970]+0x12]) submits a chat or macro line whose first 4 bytes are '/not' and whose length is > 4. The /manner and /업데이트 checks come first.
specs.expected_response: None awaited. The server presumably broadcasts an announcement S2C to all players (opcode not determined here).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates, in order: L > 0 (signed); Curse_Engine_Clean(text) passes, so the notice text itself is profanity-filtered (on failure 'No cursing please' and nothing is sent); manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40; [scene+0xF00] == 6; GM word [[scene+0x970]+0x12] == 1; not '/manner ' (8-byte strncmp); not exactly '/업데이트' (10-byte compare including NUL); strncmp(text,'/notice ',4)==0; L > 4 (unsigned JBE). Server hazards: (1) payload keeps the 'ice ' leftover when the full '/notice ' is typed, so strip it if wanted; (2) the prefix is u8 but the appended count is the full L-4. If L-4 >= 256 the prefix would wrap and a server trusting it would desync. Macro callers (L<=36) and the sprintf caller (L<=63) cannot reach that. The IME chat buffer limit was not measured, so a server should read the rest of the packet body rather than trust text_len.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: No real dispute on the wire format. Analyst A (decomp+asm) and Analyst B (asm only) gave the same grammar (u8 sub-command 0x01, u8 length (L-4), then L-4 raw bytes from text+4), the same socket (g_sock_game) and the same gates. The signatures 'u8 u8 bytes[text_len]' and 'u8 u8 bytes[msg_len]' differ only in names. The asm confirms both: 0x444CA4 strncmp(EBP,"/notice ",4); 0x444CB0 CMP EBX,4 / 0x444CB3 JBE; 0x444CC5 PUSH 6 / 0x444CC7 Add(u8); 0x444CCF PUSH 1 / 0x444CD1 Add(u8); 0x444CD9 MOVZX EAX,BL, 0x444CDC SUB AL,4, 0x444CDF Add(u8); 0x444CE7 ADD EBX,-4, 0x444CEA PUSH EBX, 0x444CEB ADD EBP,4, 0x444CEE PUSH EBP, 0x444CEF Add(char*,N) via IAT 0x4A40EC; 0x444CFD Send(1) with ECX=[0x70E6F4]. Their examples also agree: A's '/nothello'->'hello' and B's '/not hello'->' hello' both follow from the 4-byte compare and 4-byte skip. A left the sub-command, length and text Adds out of locations; B listed them. I also resolved B's open question on the length wrap as far as statics allow: EBX is the caller's strlen (0x4449DD, 0x43DBDB, 0x44AE6F), the macro and sprintf callers are bounded at 36 and 63, and only the IME chat buffer bound is still unknown. Other references: the 0x06 opcode is a GM command family in this function (06 0A <17-byte name> i32 = /manner at site #15; 06 00 = /업데이트 at site #16; 06 01 = notice). PySlayer has no client_packets parser for 0x06, and our server (windslayer_server.py) has no handling of C2S 0x06.
open_questions: Maximum length of the IME chat buffer ([0x70E708]+0x104), which decides whether text_len can wrap past 255 for typed input. Macro and sprintf callers cannot.
Whether the original server stripped the 'ice ' leftover or GMs typed '/not <text>'. The 4-byte compare of an 8-byte literal looks like a leftover from a Korean command string.
Which S2C opcode the server used to broadcast the announcement (the '[Announcement] ' prefix at 0x6F5710).

specs.name: GmDeletePlayRoom (/proom)

locations.role: strtok(text," ") x3: command, room number, optional points
if points token > 0: show "Points to deduct must be less than 0." and send nothing

specs.grammar:
u8 gm_subcmd
u32 gm_uid
u16 room_no
i32 manner_points

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: constant 0x0B = /proom

fields.name: gm_uid
fields.meaning: the sending GM's own character uid

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: play room number: atol(2nd token) truncated to 16 bits (MOVZX EBX,AX)

fields.name: manner_points
fields.meaning: manner points to deduct from the room owner, always <= 0; 0 when the third token is absent
fields.dest_or_source: ESI: 0 if 3rd strtok is NULL, else _atol(3rd token) (must be <= 0)

specs.semantics: GM command "/proom <room#> [<points<=0>]". Most likely asks the server to delete a play room (P-key Play&Chat Room) with an inappropriate name and optionally deduct manner points from its creator; the adjacent message strings are "The room has deleted due to inappropriate room name..." and "Your manner point has reduced due to creating a room with inappropriate room name.". Client sends and clears input.
specs.trigger: GM submits chat text starting "/proom " with strlen > 7, and third token absent or <= 0.
specs.expected_response: None awaited by the sender. Room members/owner probably get the room-deleted / manner-reduced messages from the server (S2C not identified here).
specs.gates_and_hazards: GM-branch gates (strlen>=1, Curse_Engine_Clean, scene+0xEE0 > -40, scene+0xF00 == 6, local entity word +0x12 == 1). Positive points -> dialog "Points to deduct must be less than 0." (color 0xFFFD4C87), nothing sent. Crash hazard: "/proom " followed only by spaces makes the 2nd strtok return NULL and _atol(NULL) is called unchecked. strtok writes NULs into the chat buffer in place. room_no silently truncated to 16 bits.
specs.references: No PySlayer/server coverage. Memory note: scene+0x220 is the local-player uid used by the registration gate, consistent with this field being the sender uid.
open_questions: Semantic of the command (delete room + penalty) is inferred from neighbouring strings in the message table, not from code.
Why the client sends its own uid (server could know it from the session) - possibly for GM audit logging.
blind_open_questions: Exact server semantics of room_no + points (penalize room owner vs all members) unknown.
Whether this is the game_state object (0x70EA00) is inferred from +0x4CC matching the scene-pointer offset; the uid source offset (+0x220) matches the documented local-player uid either way.

specs.name: GmReset
specs.grammar:
u8 gm_subcmd
str[129] target
str[3] reset_arg

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: constant 0x03 = /reset

fields.name: target
fields.meaning: first token after "/reset " (character or account name), NUL padded; must be non-empty
fields.dest_or_source: stack buffer [esp+0x78] (0x81 bytes, zeroed by memset)

fields.name: reset_arg
fields.meaning: second token (at most 2 chars + NUL), NUL padded; must be non-empty

specs.semantics: GM command "/reset <target> <xx>": asks the server to reset something for the target identified by a 129-byte name/ID string, qualified by a 2-character code. Exact reset semantics cannot be determined from the client. Client only clears the chat input.
specs.trigger: GM submits chat text starting "/reset " with strlen > 7 and two non-empty whitespace-delimited tokens.
specs.gates_and_hazards: GM-branch gates (strlen>=1, Curse_Engine_Clean, scene+0xEE0 > -40, scene+0xF00 == 6, local entity word +0x12 == 1). Either token empty -> nothing sent. Stack overflow hazards: second token longer than 2 chars overflows the 3-byte buffer into adjacent locals ([esp+0x14] text ptr copy, [esp+0x1c] saved this) - not used afterwards on this path, but a long token can corrupt more; first token > 128 chars overflows its buffer. Second-token offset assumes exactly one space between tokens.
specs.references: No PySlayer/server coverage. "/reset " at 0x6F5C70; no nearby string clarifies its meaning.
open_questions: What is being reset and what the 2-character code encodes (possibly a stat/skill/type code).
Whether target is a character name or an account ID (129-byte width suggests account/ID string rather than the 17-byte character name used elsewhere).
blind_open_questions: Meaning/valid values of the 2-char reset_arg code are not in the client.
Whether target is a character name or account id (129-byte width is larger than the 17-byte name used elsewhere).

specs.name: GmCommandGo

locations.role: chat line parser (this = game_state, param_2 = text, param_3 = length). Called from 0x4449E1 (FUN_004449b0, typed chat on Enter), 0x43DBDF (FUN_0043db00, chat macro slots) and 0x44AE75 (FUN_00446300, UI control 0x294)
gate: [scene+0xF00]==6 (CGameMain in-world scene type, set at 0x411F98)
GM gate: word [[scene+0x970]+0x12]==1 (the local player entity's GM flag)
sscanf(text+4,"%s",buf17) into a 17-byte zeroed stack buffer at [esp+0x24]

specs.grammar:
u8 gm_subcmd
str[17] target_name

fields.name: gm_subcmd
fields.meaning: GM subcommand selector, always 0x08 for /go. Other /-commands in the same function use opcode 0x06 with different subcodes (see batch notes).

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: Name of the character the GM wants to go to: the first whitespace-separated token after "/go ". NUL-padded in a 17-byte zeroed buffer.
fields.dest_or_source: sscanf %s token from the chat input, stack buffer [esp+0x24]

specs.semantics: GM chat command "/go <charname>". Asks the server to move the GM to the named character. The client sends it and does nothing else: no local UI change and no wait for a reply.
specs.trigger: A GM types "/go <name>" in the chat box (or it comes from a chat macro or the UI 0x294 path) and presses Enter.
specs.expected_response: None awaited. A server would presumably answer with the normal map-change/teleport sequence (0x08, 0x03, 0x07, ...), but the sender code does not show this.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Checks run in order before the send. (1) length >= 1. (2) ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text), else "No cursing please". (3) manner points int [scene+0xEE0] > -40, else "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point.". (4) [scene+0xF00]==6, else the function returns silently. (5) u16 [[scene+0x970]+0x12]==1 (GM), else the text is handled as normal chat. (6) The input does not match an earlier GM prefix ("/manner ", "/업데이트", "/notice ", "/proom ", "/shadow", "/reset "). (7) strncmp "/go " matches, total length > 4, and the token is not empty. HAZARD: sscanf %s has no bound. A token of 17+ chars overflows the 17-byte stack buffer, and the 17 bytes sent are then NOT NUL-terminated. The server must bound the name to 17 bytes and not assume a terminator.
specs.references: PySlayer has no C2S 0x06 parser. windslayer_server.py _dispatch has no 0x06 branch. The 0x06 opcode byte, the 0x08 subcode and the Add(char*,17) are confirmed in the asm at 0x444F9D-0x444FC6.
open_questions: Exact server-side meaning of /go: teleport the GM to the target, or summon the target? The client string gives no hint, and no S2C reply is tied to it in the sender.
What the server sends back when the target is offline or unknown.
blind_open_questions: What the server must reply with for /go (teleport via map-change replay?) is not visible in the client send path.
Meaning of scene+0xF00==6 (appears to be a scene/connection state; values 2,4,5,6 are written elsewhere) - required for ANY chat to be sent.

specs.name: HostRoomSnapshot_Phase0 (dead code)

locations.role: header timer bits only when F04==1 (so 0 here)
mode==1 count loop: counts only entities with +0x98 == 3
record loop uses the wider filter (+0x98==3, or +0x98==4 && +0xE64>=3)
receiver: opcode 7 (mode 1 only) -> FUN_00428090(scene,0) if F04 != 0

specs.length: 4 + 8*N_emitted. N_emitted can exceed the header count, see semantics.

fields.name: header
fields.meaning:
Bits:
- 0-8: 0 (the timer is only set in phase 1).
- 9-17: count of entities with +0x98==3.
- 18-31: map_code = map+0x1B8.

fields.name: rec_a
fields.meaning: Same layout as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04 rec_a.

fields.name: rec_b
fields.meaning: Same layout as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04 rec_b.

specs.semantics:
Room (map mode 1) snapshot from the P2P host while the round phase scene+0xF04 == 0 (waiting). Opcode 7 tells receivers to enter phase 0. The layout matches 0x04.

Difference from 0x04: the header count includes only +0x98==3 entities, but records are emitted for +0x98==3 and for +0x98==4 with +0xE64>=3. Any AI monster in the room adds uncounted trailing records, which the receiver ignores.

Destination: each registered peer (entity+0x6A ip string : entity+0x80 port), reset=0 per peer, then ResetBuffer.

DEAD CODE in EN 2008 (host flag scene+0xF24 is never nonzero).

Framing: shared per-socket seq (+1 per peer send), header len|0x800|seq<<12, EncodebyArray.
specs.trigger: Unreachable (host flag set, map mode 1, F04==0).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Dead code. However, a server acting as room host MUST send exactly this layout (opcode 7, 8 or 9 + header + records) to EN clients in mode-1 maps: FUN_00458640 accepts 7/8/9 only when its own map mode == 1 and ignores 0x04 there.
specs.references: Receiver FUN_00458640 0x458740-0x458BFA for opcodes 7/8/9 (phase switching, countdown messages, clock).
open_questions: Whether round phase 0 = waiting/lobby (inferred from the receiver calling FUN_00428090(scene,0)); not verified.
blind_open_questions: Whether the original battle host used this client code (host flag set by a variant build) or a separate server that sent the same datagrams.

specs.name: HostRoomSnapshot_Phase1 (dead code)

locations.role: mode==1 and scene+0xF04 not in {0,2}: PUSH 8
mode==1 && F04==1: header bits 0-8 = trunc(u32 scene+0xF1C * 0.001) & 0x1FF
receiver: opcode 8 -> phase 1 (team alive recount, HP/MP refill, 'The battle is starting.' at timer 0), countdown texts for timer 1..4, 'Fight!' at 5, clock = scene+0xF37*60 - timer

fields.name: header
fields.meaning:
Bits:
- 0-8: round_timer_s = trunc(scene+0xF1C ms / 1000) & 0x1FF, only when F04==1; 0 for F04 >= 3.
- 9-17: count of entities with +0x98==3.
- 18-31: map_code.

fields.name: rec_a
fields.meaning: Same layout as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04 rec_a.

fields.name: rec_b
fields.meaning: Same layout as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04 rec_b.

specs.semantics:
Room snapshot from the host while the round is running (scene+0xF04 == 1, or any value other than 0/2). The header timer carries the elapsed round seconds. Receivers show the start countdown for seconds 1..5 and derive the remaining-time clock from time_limit_min*60 - timer.

The count covers only player entities (+0x98==3), while the record filter also emits AI monsters.

Destination: registered peers (entity+0x6A : entity+0x80), reset=0, then ResetBuffer.

DEAD CODE in EN 2008 (host flag never set).

Framing: shared per-socket seq, 0x800 flag, EncodebyArray.
specs.trigger: Unreachable (host flag set, map mode 1, F04 != 0 and != 2).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Dead code. A server emulating the room host must supply the elapsed-seconds timer in bits 0-8 of 0x08 (9-bit, max 511 s). The receiver shows round-start messages whenever the timer value changes.
specs.references: Receiver countdown strings: 'The round will start in N seconds.', 'Fight!', 'The battle is starting.' (FUN_00458640 0x4589xx-0x458B5F).
open_questions: Exact meaning of scene+0xF1C (round-phase elapsed ms is assumed; FUN_0042c450 copies it to scene+0x24C).
blind_open_questions: Which code advances scene+0xF1C in arena mode: FUN_00417e10 adds 30 per frame, but FUN_0042b260 calls it only in the mode-0 branch; FUN_00412360 also calls it. Not traced.
Behaviour when F04 is 3 or higher (still opcode 8, timer 0) was not seen in practice.

specs.name: HostRoomSnapshot_Phase2 (dead code)

locations.role: receiver: opcode 9 -> FUN_00428090(scene,2) if F04 != 2 (round-end evaluation)

fields.name: header
fields.meaning:
Bits:
- 0-8: 0 (the timer is only set when F04==1).
- 9-17: count of entities with +0x98==3.
- 18-31: map_code.

fields.name: rec_a
fields.meaning: Same layout as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04 rec_a.

fields.name: rec_b
fields.meaning: Same layout as UDP-C2S:0x423787/0x04 rec_b.

specs.semantics:
Room snapshot from the host after the round has ended (scene+0xF04 == 2). Receivers switch to phase 2 through FUN_00428090(scene,2).

The layout, count/filter mismatch and destinations are the same as for 0x07/0x08.

DEAD CODE in EN 2008 (host flag scene+0xF24 is never set).

Framing: shared per-socket seq, 0x800 flag, EncodebyArray.
specs.trigger: Unreachable (host flag set, map mode 1, F04==2).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Dead code. A server acting as room host that sends opcode 9 makes the client run its round-end evaluation, whose host-only branches are also dead because F24==0.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md dead-code C2S 0x93/0x95 (FUN_00428090 mode 2) documents the round-end host logic that this phase would trigger.
blind_open_questions: Round-state transitions on the host (who sets F04 1 -> 2 -> 0 when F24 != 0) were not traced beyond FUN_00428090's callers in the UDP receive path.

specs.name: NpcShopBuy

locations.role: handler for window 0x10 (purchase amount dialog), button 2
dialog 0x10 [+0x40] != 0x1C selects the NPC shop path at 0x46A325
FUN_00466A30(win=0xD NPC shop): [S+0x20]=record+0 item id; [S+0x14]=window 0xD pointer
FUN_00467680(def, handler, type, item, qty, victy price def+0x1E8, npc=1), EAX=gold price def+0x1E0
JMP to the shared Send tail 0x469D97

specs.grammar:
u16 item_id
u16 qty
u16 npc_id

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item id selected in NPC shop window 0xD

fields.name: qty
fields.meaning: quantity: typed amount (1..999 type 0, 1..99 type 2) or 1 for other types

fields.name: npc_id
fields.meaning: shop NPC index/id stored in NPC shop window 0xD at +0x11C (FUN_004665E0 uses it with RosterLookupByIndex)

specs.semantics: Buys an item from the open NPC shop.
specs.trigger: NPC shop window 0xD, select an item, then OK (button 2) in the 'What is your purchase amount?' dialog 0x10
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x18 (u64 gold, u32 winnie, u16 item, u16 count), as our server does
specs.gates_and_hazards: Shop window 0xD must exist, and the selected record must have def+0x1F0==0. For types 0 and 2 there is a qty range re-prompt. FUN_00467680 checks 'You are short of gold.', 'You are short of Victy.' and bag slots, and for skill books (type 3) level/class/already-learned. The dialog is closed via FUN_00446300 before the Adds.
specs.references: PySlayer parse_0x0B reads u16 item, u16 count, u8 undef; the u8 is really the low byte of npc_id. windslayer_server.py _handle_buy_item parses item and count correctly and ignores npc_id. This third field is u16 in EN (Add(ushort) at 0x46A4F4).
open_questions: Exact meaning of window 0xD +0x11C (NPC roster index vs. NPC template id)
blind_open_questions: Confirm that shop window 0xD's +0x11C always holds the shop NPC's content index (it is set for NPC dialog ids other than 0x1A7/0x298/0x299/0x29A).

specs.name: NpcShopSell

locations.role: inventory window 9 button 0xC opens sell dialog 0xF ('What is  your sales amount?' for stackables, 'Are you sure to sell the items?' for types 1/3)
handler for window 0xF; button 2 goes to 0x46A535
FUN_00466980(handler,&S+0x60, win=9) copies the selected inventory slot record

specs.grammar:
u16 item_id
u16 qty
u8 socket_count
repeat(socket_count) { u16 socket_stone_id }
u16 item_extra

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item id of the selected inventory slot

fields.name: qty
fields.meaning: quantity to sell: typed (1..999 type 0, 1..99 type 2) or 1 for other types
fields.dest_or_source: ESI (movzx of _atol(edit 5 of window 0xF), or 1 set at 0x46A53E)

fields.name: socket_count
fields.meaning: number of leading non-zero socket words at record+0x02..+0x0B (max 5); sent for every item type

fields.name: socket_stone_id
fields.meaning: socketed elemental stone ids

fields.name: item_extra
fields.meaning: record+0x0C

specs.semantics: Sells a bag item to the open NPC shop. The full descriptor (id, sockets, extra) identifies which copy is being sold. After Send, the client closes the dialog (FUN_00489960(0,0) at 0x46A686).
specs.trigger: With an NPC shop open: select a bag item, click Sell (button 0xC), then OK (button 2) in dialog 0xF
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x19 (u64 gold, u16 item, u16 count, u8 n, n x u16, u16 trailer), as our server does
specs.gates_and_hazards: Record must exist with def+0x1F0==0. Stackables: qty != 0, <=999 / <=99 (else '999  is maximum number.' / '99  is maximum number.'), and owned (FUN_004679C0, 'You've exceeded the amount you have.').
specs.references: PySlayer parse_0x0C reads u16 item, u8 count, u16 undef; its sample 0c 5400 0100 00 0000 actually matches this EN layout: item 84, qty u16 1, socket_count 0, extra 0. windslayer_server.py _handle_sell_item reads count as u8 payload[2], so quantities of 256 or more come out wrong. It also ignores the socket list and extra.
open_questions: item_extra meaning

specs.name: PlayerMoveState

locations.role: caller: per 30 ms logic tick, only when scene+0xF00==6 and [0x70EED8]+0x70==0
S2C 0x1B handler, which decodes the same 8-byte state block for remote players (relay counterpart)

fields.name: realtime_delta_ms
fields.meaning: Real-time (timeGetTime) milliseconds covering the last 10 sends. A counter at scene+0x978 goes up by 1 per send; when it reaches 10 at send time this is now minus scene+0x974 and the counter resets. Otherwise it is 0, including the first packet. Probably a speed-hack check.

fields.name: map_code
fields.dest_or_source: [[0x70EED8]+0x1B8], low 16 bits of the map object's u32
fields.meaning: Current map code (map loader FUN_00407190 @0x40752D computes a + b*100 from the map file name, e.g. 101). The capture shows 0x0065 = 101.

fields.name: logic_elapsed_ms
fields.meaning: Logic-clock ms since the last 0x0D send. scene+0xF1C goes up by 30 each logic frame (0x417E23), so the value is a multiple of 30 (capture: 30). scene+0x24C is set to scene+0xF1C after each send (0x42CEA6).

fields.name: state_lo
fields.meaning: Packed input/state bits. Bits 0-1: player+0x8B3 (01 = value 2, left; 10 = value 6, right; 00 = other, 8 = none). Bits 2-4: player+0x8B4&7 (vertical/jump input; 4 = Up). Bits 5-8: player+0x8B5&0xF. Bits 9-11: player+0x8B6&7. Bits 12-15: player+0x94C&0xF (action_event). Bits 16-19: player+0x950&0xF (interact_event). Bits 20-21: player+0x8D0 (01 = 2, 10 = 6, 00 = other). Bits 22-31 are never written and hold stale scratch bytes (scene+0xEF8 is reused as the parse buffer by the S2C 0x1B/0x2A handlers), so they are garbage.

fields.name: state_hi
fields.meaning: Bits 0-11: player+0x958&0xFFF (a timer; 600 is set on the target at 0x417CFF). Bits 12-31 are stale garbage.

fields.name: event_source_uid
fields.meaning: UID of the entity tied to the action event (e.g. the item-hit path writes the thrower's uid into the victim's +0xD80 at 0x417CF9). Present only if player+0x94C != 0.

fields.name: f64_1338
fields.meaning: Action parameter double (x-like). Unknown meaning; compared against in FUN_00413920. Present only if 0x8B6==4 and 0x94C is 9 or 7.

fields.name: f64_1340
fields.meaning: Action parameter double (y-like), same condition as f64_1338.

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: UID of the entity this player interacted with (0x417CED: the other entity's +0x84). Present only if player+0x950 != 0.

fields.name: pos_x
fields.meaning: Local player world X. Sent ONLY inside the interact_event block. Ordinary movement packets carry no position.

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: Local player world Y (interact_event block only).

fields.name: target_dx
fields.meaning: target.x - self.x (computed at 0x417D09).

fields.name: target_dy
fields.meaning: target.y - self.y (computed at 0x417D1B).

fields.name: flag_8db
fields.meaning: Copied from target+0x8DA in the item-hit path (0x417D2D). Meaning unknown.

fields.name: flag_8e7
fields.meaning: Flag: 0 in the item-hit path (0x417D35), 1 in other paths (0x416A20). Meaning unknown.

fields.name: timer_dac
fields.meaning: A per-entity counter that goes up by 30 per frame (0x416450) and is handed between entities on contact. Meaning unknown.

fields.name: target_action_event
fields.meaning: The target's +0x94C (action event) captured at interaction time (0x417D4D).

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Only when interact_event == 0xC (thrown-item/projectile hit, item word from the record checked against 0xA31..0xA3B at 0x417B16). The item id that hit.

specs.semantics: The local player's input/state sync. The client sends its current input bytes and event state plus the logic time elapsed since the last send; remote clients simulate the movement from these. Position is included only in the interaction-event block. No state is changed from the server side. On the client, after sending, scene+0x24C = scene+0xF1C; the previous-input snapshot (player+0x8B7..0x8BA = 0x8B3..0x8B6) is updated every tick whether or not a packet is sent. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C12, world_movement_npc#00/#01 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): (a) For the LOCAL player a bad (IP-octet) seed in the spawn record does NOT produce a ~28-packet stream: the client resets +0x8B3/+0x8B4/+0x8B5/+0x904 from real input immediately, and only +0x8B6 = 1 survives ~1.5 s after a map-change 0x07 (7 non-idle sends). After a spawn the client emits a burst of about 5 idle 0x0D, so a server sanity check should allow <= 5, not <= 2. The idle-default rule still matters for the REMOTE records in S2C 0x04/0x05/0x07 and for 0x1A. (b) A basic melee swing is lo bits 2-4 (+0x8B4) = 1 with +0x904 = 4 - NOT an action_event: +0x94C stays 0 for a plain attack, so the 22-byte event_source_uid form is never produced by one. +0x8B4 values: 0 idle, 1 basic attack, 3 jump, 4 down/portal/drop-through. Bits 20-21 (+0x8D0) and hi bits 0-11 (+0x958) are live during jumps. (c) The interact tail for interact_event 0xC is confirmed at 45 bytes: u32 target_uid, f64 pos_x, f64 pos_y, f64 dx, f64 dy, bool, bool, u32 timer, u8 action_event (= 9), u16 item_id.
specs.trigger: Checked every 30 ms logic tick from FUN_0042b260 (possibly several times per rendered frame during catch-up), when scene+0xF00 == 6 (in world), [0x70EED8]+0x70 == 0 (not a P2P room), and player (scene+0x970) != 0. (1) Sends at once if any of player+0x8B3..0x8B6 changed since the last tick, or player+0x950 != 0, or player+0x94C != 0 (also sets scene+0x250 = 1). (2) Otherwise nothing if logic_elapsed < 210 ms. (3) If not idle (idle means 0x904 == 8, 0x8B3 == 8, and 0x8B4, 0x8B5, 0x8B6 all 0), sets scene+0x250 = 1 and sends about every 210 ms. (4) If idle and scene+0x250 != 0, clears it and sends one final packet. (5) If idle otherwise, sends only when logic_elapsed >= 15000 (keepalive).
specs.expected_response: Nothing to the sender. It must NOT be echoed back: echoing desynced the cipher, per memory. For multiplayer the server should relay to other players on the map as S2C 0x1B (handler 0x4523F9: u32 uid, u32, bytes[8] state, if(ae) u32, if(vb==4 && ae in {9,7}) f64 f64, if(ie) f64 f64). The 0x1B conditional tail is NOT the same as 0x0D's, so the relay must re-encode rather than copy the bytes.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Variable length: the server must parse the conditional tails using bits of the packet itself. The client tests the full ints (player+0x94C, +0x950, byte +0x8B6), but the packet carries only 4/4/3 bits of them. The equivalence holds only if those values fit (all observed writers use values <= 0xD). The upper 10 bits of state_lo and upper 20 bits of state_hi are stale garbage and must be ignored (capture: 53 40 / 60 64 75). Not sent in P2P room mode ([map]+0x70 == 1), which appears to use a UDP path instead (FUN_0042c450, not traced).
specs.references: Capture '00 00 00 00 65 00 1E 00 00 00 00 02 40 53 00 60 64 75' decodes exactly: realtime_delta 0, map 101, elapsed 30, state_lo 0x53400200 (0x8B6=1, other fields 0, garbage high bits), state_hi 0x75646000 (0x958&0xFFF = 0), 18 bytes, no tails. PySlayer parse_0D agrees on offsets (payload[5:7] u16 'sub_opcode' = map code; payload[7:9] == 0xD2 = elapsed 210; keycode payload[0x0B] = first state byte). Our server's _handle_world_sync docstring wrongly says the payload 'begins with two f64 world coords': positions appear only in the interact_event tail. The memory atlas note calling 0x0D a 'heartbeat' is wrong (it is S2C 0x0D in sub_handler_3, a different message).
open_questions: Exact meaning of player+0x8B4/0x8B5/0x8B6/0x8D0 values and of action_event (0x94C, values 1..13 seen) and interact_event (0x950, values 1, 9, 0xB, 0xC seen).
Meaning of f64_1338/f64_1340, flag_8db, flag_8e7, timer_dac; appears related to item/PvP contact mechanics.
Meaning of the second u32 in the S2C 0x1B relay (probably logic_elapsed_ms) and whether the relay should carry the 0x0D realtime_delta.
Whether scene+0xF1C can be resynced by the server (FUN_0042c360 writes it at 0x42C3BF), which would affect logic_elapsed.

Which action actually produces the 22-byte event_source_uid tail? Live (world_movement_npc#00) proved +0x94C stays 0 for a basic attack, so the tail must come from skills or grabs; the 45-byte interact-0xC tail is already confirmed.
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of 8b5 (4-bit), 8b6 (3-bit), 8b4 codes 1/5/6, and the hit_type/hit_reaction enumerations.
Is state_b low 12 bits (player+0x958) really damage? It is 250/50/attack-minus-defense in FUN_00416380 but the server should not trust it.
Meaning of unk_dac, target_flag_8da and unk_8d4 (only when hit_type==12).
Unit of scene+0xf1c clock assumed ms (caller steps it in 30s).

spec_errata.old: IP-octet seed said to cause a ~28-packet stream; a basic attack said to set the action_event (ae) nibble
spec_errata.new: local state is reset from input immediately (<= 5 idle sends); a basic attack is +0x8B4 = 1 with +0x94C = 0

spec_errata.old: no open question about the ae tail
spec_errata.new: open question added for the unresolved 22-byte form
