specs.semantics: Creates a character from the look choices and distributed stats in the creation window. After Send the client shows the 'Waiting for the server to response.' modal (0x449390).
specs.trigger: Character-creation window 0x13, control 3 (create/OK). Window 0x13 opens from char-select window 0x12 ctrl 1, which is refused at 5 characters: 'No more characters can be created.'.
specs.expected_response: Not traced in EN. Our server replies S2C 0x02 (refreshed char list) and it works.
specs.gates_and_hazards: All stat points must be spent (+0x294==0). FUN_0043DF40 name check: empty -> 'Enter your name.'; spaces, apostrophe or backslash, reserved words (gamemaster, yahoo, wind, windmaster, windy, winsle, master, avocade, administrator, hamelin), or a Curse_Engine_Clean hit -> 'Invalid name. Please try another name.'.
specs.references: Our windslayer_server.py _handle_create_character parses the same 35 bytes (5*u16, name[17], 4*u16) and labels them class, face, top, bottom, shoes, str, dex, int, spr. The layout matches, but 'class' is wrong: +0x3C0 is appearance slot 10 (1..4 / 101..104 by gender). PySlayer ignores opcode 14. Rendering FUN_0047DB10 @0x480FE0 pushes +0x3AC..+0x3C6 as a 14-slot look array.
open_questions: Human names for look slots 1/5/6/9/10 (hair/face/top/bottom/shoes) are not proven; hs/face101 etc. suggest 101-based values are the female variants.
Where gender flag [+0x130] comes from (account data vs a UI toggle) is not traced.
blind_open_questions: Real meaning of the five appearance u16s (hair/face/top/bottom/shoes?).
Mapping of stat_0..3 to STR/DEX/INT/SPR.
Which S2C opcode(s) the original server used for success/failure.

specs.name: EquipItem

locations.role: EquipItem: ECX=item def, EAX=game_state, args u16 item_id, ptr to 12-byte option record (u16 stones[5] + u16 extra)
Add(u8) stone_count (loop 0x44C420 counts leading non-zero words, max 5)
caller: quick-slot hotkey with Type 1 item, record = game_state+0x10DE+slot*12, throttled 1000 ms via game_state+0x11C0[slot]
caller: inventory window 9 activation of Type 1 item, record = UI slot record +0x02

fields.name: item_id
fields.dest_or_source: stack arg 1: quick-slot id game_state+0x10BE[slot] or inventory UI record +0x00
fields.meaning: Item-table idx of the Type 1 equipment piece to equip

fields.name: stone_count
fields.dest_or_source: computed: number of leading non-zero u16 in record[0..4] (stops at first zero, max 5)
fields.meaning: Number of socketed stones/options that follow (quick-slot registry calls these 'QuickSlotStone%d%d')

fields.name: stone_id
fields.dest_or_source: record[i] (record = game_state+0x10DE+slot*12 or UI slot record +0x02)
fields.meaning: Socketed stone/option item id i. Words after the first zero are never sent.

fields.name: extra_option
fields.meaning: Unknown 6th per-item option word. It is not saved to the registry with the quick slots. S2C 0x1D echoes it.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to equip the bag item <item_id> with its stone list. Sending changes no client state. The equip is applied when the server sends S2C 0x1D (u32 uid, u16 item, u8 n, u16[n], u16; handler 0x45298C writes equip grid entity+0x13C/+0x16E and recomposes the sprite). The bag entry is removed by a bag-remove packet (our server uses S2C 0x23). Live capture matches: double-clicking Wooden Stick 179 sent 'B3 00 00 00 00' = item 179, stone_count 0, extra 0.
specs.trigger: Double-clicking/activating an equipment item in the inventory window (window 9) with no NPC-shop/storage/stall context active. Also pressing a quick-slot hotkey (or HUD quick-slot button) that holds an equipment item, at most once per 1000 ms per slot.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x1D equip (same body layout prefixed by u32 uid) plus a bag removal (0x23). Also error chat on failure (server-defined).
specs.gates_and_hazards: All client-side, each showing a message and not sending on failure. scene+0x970 local entity non-null (silent). def+0x1D4 gender: ==1 requires scene+0x130 != 0 and ==2 requires scene+0x130 == 0, else 'You can not equip other gender's item.'. scene+0x979 (level byte) >= def+0x1D8 (Lv), else 'You need higher level'. entity+0x904 not in {1,4,0xE,0xF} and < 0x18, entity+0x15B4 not in {1,4,0xE,0xF} and < 0x18, and scene+0x258 (pending skill) == 0, else 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.'. def+0x168+entity.class(+0x110)*4 (Job[class]) != 0 or def+0x168 (Job[0]) != 0, else 'You can't equip other class items.'. Hazard: an unanswered C2S 0x15 skill leaves scene+0x258 set and blocks this packet permanently. The quick-slot path updates its 1000 ms timestamp even when a gate rejects.
specs.references: This is the only 0x0F send site in the client. Our server's _handle_equip_item reads only u16 item_id and ignores stone_count/stones/extra. That is safe for parsing but loses stone data, and its 0x1D reply does not echo stones. The docstring 'u16 item [, u8, u16]' is correct only for stone_count == 0. PySlayer parse_0F has the same n==0-only layout and wrongly asserts payload[0]==0x0D. It matches the captured 5-byte payload.
open_questions: Meaning of the 6th option word (record+10 / extra_option) - maybe refine/enchant level or durability.
Whether unequip uses a different C2S opcode (not in this batch).
Identity of entity+0x904 / +0x15B4 state values 1,4,0xE,0xF,>=0x18 (attack/skill animation states).
blind_open_questions: What the 6 option words mean (enchant/card/union stats?) and whether the server must check them against the bag copy.
game_data+0x130 polarity (non-zero seems to mean male, given gamedef Gender 1=male, 2=female).

specs.semantics: Asks the server to unequip an equipped item and return it to the bag. The client changes nothing locally and waits for the server. The body layout matches C2S 0x0F EquipItem (0x44C2C0) exactly, only the opcode differs.
specs.trigger: The player double-clicks an equipped item in the Equipment window (window id 7), or drags it from the Equipment window onto the Inventory window (9). Both reach 0x44BD10 -> 0x46CAD0 with window 7. The source slot/control index must be 3..27.
specs.expected_response: Most likely S2C 0x1E (handler 0x454090, shared with 0x24): u32 uid, u16 item_id, u8 n, n x u16 enchant, u16 enchant_last. It calls 0x4269A0 to clear the entity's equip slot (+0x13C / +0x16E), recomposes the sprite (0x426D50) and, for the local player (uid == scene+0x220) with opcode 0x1E and bag capacity byte scene+0x3A9 <= 45, puts the item back in the bag with its attribute words. Our server's own notes also call 0x1E the remove/unequip opcode.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks, in order: (1) slot index - 3 <= 0x18; (2) bag capacity byte char+0x361 (char = ctx+0x18 = scene+0x48) <= 45 AND at least one empty word in bag[0..cap) at char+0x380 (0x424D60), otherwise a modal notice 'You have no more slots for the item.' (0x489DA0) and no packet; (3) 0x466DF0 and 0x466E10 abort (no message) when ctx+0 == 0x259 and ctx+0x20 or ctx+0x1C is set (a special UI mode, probably a personal shop); (4) 0x466980 finds the selected Equipment record and its catalog entry; (5) the local player entity (char+0x928) has action state +0x904 not in {1,4,14,15} and < 24, the same for +0x15B4 (4 = attacking), and word scene+0x258 == 0; otherwise chat notice 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.' (0x4817D0) and no packet; (6) catalog type +0x154 == 1 (equipment), otherwise nothing. No local pending state: double-clicking again before the server answers sends another 0x11, so the server must check the item is still equipped.
specs.references: Captured C2S 0x0F equip 'B3 00 00 00 00' (u16 179, u8 n=0, u16 0) confirms this shared shape (builder 0x44C2C0 uses the same loop, reading from rec+2). PySlayer parse_0F reads a fixed u16,u8,u16 and ignores the n-word loop; PySlayer has no 0x11 parser. Our server: _dispatch has no inbound 0x11. Its _build_en_opcode_1D_equip docstring states '0x1E is the REMOVE/unequip opcode', which matches the expected response. Do not confuse this with the server-notes '0x11 + account_id' UDP broadcast on the map/tertiary socket: that is a different message on a different socket.
open_questions: What differs between S2C 0x1E and 0x24 in handler 0x454090 beyond the 0x1E-only bag re-add branch (0x45424F); is 0x24 unequip-and-destroy or a remote-player variant?
Meaning of the 6 attribute words (enchant/option).
blind_open_questions: Exact S2C sequence the client expects after 0x11 (equipment-slot clear plus bag add). Not visible at this site.
FUN_00466980 reads the item from the Equipment window's selected index [win+0xEC], not from the ECX slot argument. Presumably they are the same after the click, but this is not proven.
Meaning of item_attr (record+0x0C).
What ctx mode 0x259 is (FUN_00466df0/FUN_00466e10 block unequip in it).

specs.name: LanAddressProbeBroadcast

locations.role: S2C 0x02 login-result case entry; the broadcast runs only in the result==1 branch
EnterCriticalSection(game_state+0x368). The whole handler runs under the lock that FrameMove also holds, so it cannot interleave with the per-tick UDP builder
SetBroadCast(1) via CALL EDI (EDI=[0x4A40E0] loaded at 0x44DFC2) = setsockopt(SOL_SOCKET, SO_BROADCAST)
SendTo(ulong ip=0xFFFFFFFF (PUSH -1), port=0xA79B, reset=1) via IAT 0x4A40DC. This is the only reference to 0x4A40DC in the image
receiver FUN_00458640 case 0x11: copies the datagram's source IP string to scene+0x224 and sets scene+0x244=42907
Fireway CSNSocket::SendTo(ulong,uint,int): SetHeader + EncodebyArray + sendto(len+8). The ip is stored raw into sin_addr and the port goes through htons

specs.grammar: u32 account_id
specs.length: 4 (payload after the opcode). The datagram is 13 bytes on the wire: 8-byte Fireway header + opcode + u32.

fields.name: account_id
fields.meaning: Local account/player uid. It was read earlier in the same S2C 0x02 packet into scene+0x220. Receivers do not check it: case 0x11 only requires its own scene+0x220 != 0 and discards the value.

specs.semantics:
A one-shot LAN broadcast the client sends right after a successful login. Its purpose is to learn the client's own IP address. The client's socket is bound to 0.0.0.0:42907, so it normally receives its own broadcast, as does every other client on the LAN. FUN_00458640 case 0x11 then zeroes scene+0x224..0x233, copies the recvfrom source IP string into scene+0x224 (p2p_ip) and sets scene+0x244=42907. Both values are later sent to the game server in the TCP enter-world request (p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port).

Destination: 255.255.255.255:42907 (sin_addr=0xFFFFFFFF, htons(0xA79B)). SO_BROADCAST is switched on just before this send and off right after it.

Framing (common to all g_sock_map sends): the socket was created by CreateSockets at 0x4402DB as Create(port 0xA79B, type 2=UDP, encode=true, header=true). NoEncode is not imported by the exe, so the encode flag always applies. Each SendTo emits exactly one datagram of 8 + payload_len bytes, where the payload is opcode + fields.
- Header dword0 (SetHeader 0x10002150): bits 0-10 = (payload_len+8) & 0x7FF; bit 11 (0x800) = 1; bits 12-19 = seq; bits 20-31 = 0.
- Sequence: the counter at CSNSocket+0x13A8 starts at 0 (Init / Initial_Socket), is incremented before every SendTo on this socket, and wraps 255 -> 0. The first datagram therefore has seq 1. One counter is shared by every UDP kind (this broadcast, the loopback 0x04/0x03, and 0x03 to the room host).
- Header dword1 plus payload come from CEncMsg::EncodebyArray (0x10006B20), which is identical to cencmsg.encode_by_array. With T = the Fireway table at 0x1000B138 (low byte of each 4-byte entry): chk = (T[seq] + sum(plain[i] & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF, and every payload byte ^= T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF].
- The client's TCP Send uses the same header and cipher code.
- A third SendTo argument of 1 zeroes the 0x7F8-byte payload buffer after the send.
specs.trigger: S2C 0x02 (login result) with result==1, after the character list and transfer status are parsed. It runs once per successful login.
specs.expected_response: None. No server or peer reply is expected. The only effect is on receivers of the broadcast (normally the sender itself), whose case 0x11 handler records the source IP.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates:
- Sent only in the result==1 path of S2C 0x02, and always sent there.
- The receiver ignores 0x11 until scene+0x220 != 0.

Hazards:
- The u32 is not compared with the receiver's own uid. A 0x11 broadcast from another client on the same LAN overwrites scene+0x224 with that client's IP (last writer wins).
- If broadcast delivery or loopback fails, scene+0x224 keeps its previous value, which may be empty.
- A server process on the client machine must not bind UDP 42907. The client's own bind at CreateSockets 0x4402DB would fail and the socket-creation error path runs.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x02 (login result) already mentions this broadcast. PROTOCOL.md C2S enter-world fields p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port (scene+0x224 / +0x244) are what this datagram feeds. In server/windslayer_server.py, UDPMapServer (a logger/decoder for this datagram) is defined but deliberately not started in main(): the comment notes that binding 42907 breaks the client. No server action is needed. Fireway SendTo(ulong) body 0x10003E38-0x10003F4F: htons(port), raw ip into sin_addr, sendto(sock, buf, len+8, 0, &sa, 16), and reset if arg3 != 0.
open_questions: Whether the original server-side infrastructure ever listened for this broadcast. It cannot cross routers, so it is most likely a pure self-discovery trick.
On Windows hosts with several interfaces, which source IP recvfrom reports for the looped-back broadcast. This decides the p2p_ip value.
blind_open_questions: Nothing in the static code reads scene+0x224 for the UDP sends traced here. Which subsystem uses the discovered local IP (e.g. the host/room TCP packets 0x93/0x95) was not traced.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to delete one character from the account. The client sends the selected character's 17-byte name and the 21-byte confirmation password/SS#, shows 'Waiting for the server to response.', and then always calls FUN_004295a0(this+0x700).
specs.trigger: On the character select screen (window 0x12), the Delete button (control 2) needs character count != 0 and a selected character in idle pose (+0x15A8==0x214, +0x904==8). FUN_00464480 then opens password dialog 0x201 owned by 0x235. Confirming that dialog raises window 0x235 / control 2, which builds and sends this packet. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x1F [u8 result]. The handler at 0x45285A first closes message window 0x16. Results: 1 = success (FUN_00422b90 removes the character whose uid is [this+0x3F8]+0x84 and clears the selection), 2 = 'Server process is running. Please try again in a few minutes (DB)', 3 = 'You can't delete a character created within 24 hours.', 12 = 'Invalid password. Please check your password again.'. Results 4..11 do nothing. S2C 0x1F [u8 result] closes the waiting box. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: character count != 0, and a selected char entity with +0x15A8==0x214 and +0x904==8. If the entity check fails, no packet goes out and it jumps to 0x44ABC2. Hazard: if window 0x201 is missing or has fewer than 5 controls, the client calls Add(NULL,0x15). Whether Fireway handles NULL is unknown (possible client crash), but the normal flow always has the dialog. Leaves a modal waiting box that needs S2C 0x1F to clear.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer client_packets. windslayer_server.py has no C2S 0x12 handler (its 0x12 references are the S2C ground-item drop builder, a different direction). Field widths agree with other char-select packets: 0x2B carries name[17] at its tail.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to drop (throw on the ground) `amount` of an inventory item. The item is identified by its id plus its option words, the same item-reference encoding used by 0x0F equip, 0x0C sell and S2C 0x23. The client changes nothing locally before sending. It waits for the server to update the bag.
specs.trigger: Drag an item from the inventory window (dialog 9) onto the ground (FUN_0046c420 target 0), which calls FUN_00466b60(ctx,9). That opens the amount popup 0x18 ("Not allowed in play room/arena" checks, count pre-filled, edit disabled when count==1). Clicking OK sends event 2 on dialog 0x18.
specs.expected_response: Not determined statically. Most likely S2C 0x23 (bag remove: u16 id, u16 count, u8 n, u16[n], u16 opt6; handler 0x46DD4B) plus a ground-item spawn.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No send when: scene+0x4D8->+0x70 == 1 (arena/play room, message shown); dialog 0x18 rec+0x40 != 9 (goes to the 0x14 path when it is 7); nothing selected in the window (rec+0xEC == 0) or item_id == 0 or no item template; template+0x1F0 != 0 (cash item); amount == 0; template+0x154 == 0 (consumable) and amount > 999 ("999  is maximum number."); template+0x154 == 2 (misc) and amount > 99 ("99  is maximum number."); FUN_004679c0 fails ("You've exceeded the amount you have."). The amount is truncated to 16 bits BEFORE the max checks, so typing 65537 sends 1. The server must re-validate ownership and count.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer. Not in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. The item-reference layout {u16 id, u8 n, u16[n], u16} matches the real 0x0F capture 'B3 00 00 00 00' and PySlayer parse_0x0C/0x0F (u8 + u16 after the id).

Meaning of opt6 (record +0x0C) is unknown.
blind_open_questions: What is slot record +0x0C (the trailing u16)? It could be a 6th option, a refine level or a flag.
Item def +0x1F0 must be 0 to drop. Server notes call +0x1F0 'Kind', but if that were true equipment could never be dropped or traded, so it is more likely a no-drop/bound flag.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to cast skill <skill_id>. The client has already checked cost, cooldown and state locally and sends nothing else (no target). Right after Send it sets scene+0x258 (u16 pending/casting skill) = skill_id. That field locks out further casts (gate at 0x44C0E1) and also equip/unequip (FUN_0044c2c0 gate 0x44C3B3 and the 0x11 path), until the server clears it. For ids 0x0A31..0x0A3B (Booby Trap Lv1-10 and Puppet, 0x0A3B) the client adds its own integer X/Y. S2C 0x3B reads a matching u16,u16 pair for the same id range (0x452E2B).
specs.trigger: Pressing a quick-slot hotkey (game_state+0xE38[0..7], page byte game_state+0x10BC, 2x8 slots; HUD quick-slot buttons send WM_KEYDOWN for the same keys via FUN_0044bd10). Also activating a skill icon in the skill window (window 5) or an inventory entry whose def Type == 3. Quick-slot path requires scene+0xF00 == 6 (field mode), no item-stall session, no trade modal, and game_state+0xD84 == 0.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x25 (handler 0x452D69, local path 0x453412 -> 0x453D7F) clears scene+0x258 and starts the cooldown (FUN_00426cc0 with def+0x1EC and game_state+0x364). S2C 0x5F (0 bytes, handler 0x457794) only clears scene+0x258, so it works as a reject/cancel. Other players are told via S2C 0x3B (u16 id, u32 caster uid, [u16 x, u16 y for 0x0A31..0x0A3B], ...). HP/MP cost updates go via S2C 0x28/0x44.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Branch taken only when def+0x154 (Type) == 3. Gates, in order: def+0x1DC > 0 (signed); scene+0x970 local entity non-null; scene+0x258 == 0 (no pending skill); scene+0x255 != 7 (S2C 0x25 sets 7 for some buff-skill ranges); entity+0x15B4 in {6, 8, 0xC} (8 = idle; attacking/jumping blocked). If def+0x168 (Job[0] traveler flag) == 0 and entity+0x112 == 0: shows 'You can't use the skill with elementary traveler weapon.' and does not send. entity+0xA0 (cur MP) must be >= |def+0x15C| (MP column, stored negative), else 'MP low.'. For ids 0x124..0x12E or 0x8DC..0x8E6 only, entity+0x9C (cur HP) must be > |def+0x158|, else 'Not enough HP.'. Cooldown: def+0x1EC (CT ms) + last_use_tick <= game_state+0x364 (now), unsigned, else silently nothing. HAZARD: if the server never answers with S2C 0x25 or 0x5F, scene+0x258 stays set. The player can then never cast another skill and gets 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.' on every equip attempt. No ResetBuffer: the packet starts with the Add(0x15) in this function (callers add nothing before).
specs.references: PySlayer parse_15 reads only u16 and ignores the trailing booby-trap X/Y. Its game_server handles Type 3 by sending a buff packet plus HP/MP deltas. Our windslayer_server.py dispatches 0x15 to _handle_use_item, which returns early for any type != 0. Skills get no 0x25/0x5F reply, which triggers the scene+0x258 lock described in gates. It only reads u16, so the 6-byte booby-trap variant parses harmlessly. The item DB confirms the id ranges: 0xA31-0xA3A 'Booby Trap' (Plants an invisible bomb on the field), 0xA3B 'Puppet', 0x124-0x12D Attack Boost, 0x12E Defense Boost, 0x8DC-0x8E5 Heaven Strike (HP -47/MP -47), 0x8E6 Aura of Advance. Note: the client's HP-cost range is inclusive of 0x12E and 0x8E6, one past each skill family.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to accept (take) the quest shown in the NPC quest dialog. The client does NOT add the quest locally: after sending it closes the dialog window (FUN_00446300(win,0,1,0,1)) and the NPC quest-list window 0x236, clears quest_mgr+0 and +0x1C, and waits for S2C 0x26 (u16 quest_id), whose handler places the id into the first empty of 3 slots at chardata+0x256 (chardata = local player entity+0x48), zeroes the ready flag at chardata+0x25F+slot, grants the quest's start items (quest+0xC94 ids / +0xD34 counts, up to 10) via FUN_00440920 and refreshes the quest window. Note the 0x26 handler only uses a slot if quest reward gold (+0xDE8) < 0, or it has required items (+0xD0C != 0), or a required count (+0xDF8 != 0); otherwise it calls FUN_004264a0 instead (talk-only quest).
specs.trigger: UI event type 2 on a quest dialog window whose record has a non-zero +0x120 (quest id), i.e. confirming/accepting the quest offer dialog opened by clicking a quest NPC. Any window receiving event 2 goes through FUN_00477210; it is a no-op unless rec+0x120 != 0.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x26 u16 quest_id (quest accepted, added to log; handler @0x4775D9). Real capture: server replied 0x26 + 0x18 and the client showed the quest as Accepted.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Preconditions checked client-side in order: (1) a window record with id == window id exists in ui_root+0x5C0; (2) rec+0x120 (quest id) != 0; (3) quest table (app+0x4DC) has an entry at index quest_id-1; (4) not all 3 active slots chardata+0x256/0x258/0x25A are non-zero, else MessageBox 'You can only take 3 quests at a time...' (0x4772C6) and no send; (5) FUN_00426040(player, quest_id, inventories chardata+0x5F6/+0x650/+0x760/+0x7BA/+0x380/+0x3DA, counts +0x361..+0x363) inventory-space check for items granted on accept, else MessageBox 'There isn't empty space in the inventory.' (0x477365) and no send; the dialog + window 0x236 are closed in both the send and the no-space cases. The client does NOT check whether the quest is already held or already completed - server must validate (duplicate/replayed ids). Hazard: the completion/in-progress dialogs opened by FUN_00477af0 also carry the quest id in rec+0x120, so if such a dialog raises event type 2 the client would send 0x16 for a quest it already holds or just turned in; server should ignore 0x16 for held/done quests rather than treating it as turn-in.
specs.references: Matches live capture (quest 26 -> 0x16 '1A 00'). PySlayer game_server.py: opcode 22 'AcceptQuest' (no-op). Our server windslayer_server.py _dispatch handles 0x16 in _handle_accept_quest: parses u16 quest_id correctly and sends 0x26 grant; BUT it also treats 0x16 at the end NPC as TURN-IN - the binary shows turn-in is a separate C2S 0x17 (send site 0x477F3E), so that branch is based on a wrong assumption.

specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x70E6F4], via quest_mgr+0x14 = [EBX+0x14], set in FUN_00477040 @0x477054)

locations.role: NPC quest interaction: scans the 3 active slots, checks completion requirements, sends turn-in

specs.grammar: u16 quest_id

fields.name: quest_id
fields.meaning: Id of the held quest being turned in at its completion NPC
fields.dest_or_source: MOVZX word [chardata + 0x256 + slot*2] (chardata = [quest_mgr+0x18] = local player entity+0x48; slot = first of 0..2 whose quest passes all checks).

specs.semantics: Asks the server to complete (turn in) a held quest at its end NPC. Sent at most once per NPC click: after the send it leaves the slot loop, remembers the NPC content index in quest_mgr+0x1C and opens the quest's completion dialog (window id quest+0xDDC, with rec+0x11C=npc idx, rec+0x120=quest id) via FUN_00477f70. No local state change; the client waits for S2C 0x27 (u16 quest_id) whose handler clears the slot and progress byte, adds quest gold (+0xDE8, signed; 'Gave %u Gold.' / 'You've received %u Gold.') to the u64 at chardata+0x228, removes required items (+0xD0C ids / +0xDAC counts, up to 10) 'Gave %u item(%s).', grants reward items (+0xCBC ids / +0xD5C counts, up to 20) and refreshes the quest window/NPC list.
specs.trigger: Left-click/interact on an NPC whose roster entry +0x638 != 0 (quest NPC) when the player holds a quest whose end NPC (quest+0xE0C) equals the NPC's content index (entity+0xE60) and all requirements are met.
specs.gates_and_hazards: FUN_004447d0 gates: npc entity non-null; FUN_0048a2a0()==0; not (app+0xD7C or app+0xD78 set while app+0xD5C == 0x259); FUN_00468fa0()==0; RosterLookupByIndex(npc+0xE60) non-null with +0x638 != 0. FUN_00477af0 per slot (chardata+0x256, 3 u16): quest id != 0 and in quest table; quest+0xE0C == npc+0xE60; if reward gold quest+0xDE8 < 0 then u64 money chardata+0x228 must be >= |gold|; if required count quest+0xDF8 != 0 then progress byte chardata+0x25C+slot >= it; for each of up to 10 required items (quest+0xD0C, count +0xDAC) by item-def+0x154 type: 0 -> sum of matching u16 counts in bag ids player+0x63E/counts +0x698 (n=player+0x3AA) must cover the count, 1 -> FUN_00424df0 must be non-zero (equipped), 2 -> sum of byte counts in bag ids player+0x7A8/counts +0x802 (n=player+0x3AB); then FUN_00426270 reward-space check, else MessageBox 'There isn't empty space in the inventory.' (0x477DDB), no send, dialog +0xDD8 shown instead. The ready-to-complete flag (chardata+0x25F+slot, set by S2C 0x59) is NOT consulted. If the NPC is the START npc (quest+0xE08) of a held quest, only the in-progress dialog (+0xDD8) is opened. Server must re-validate requirements; the client trusts its own inventory/progress mirror. Note the completion dialog carries quest id in rec+0x120, which could make FUN_00477210 emit a stray 0x16 if that dialog raises event type 2.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer. Our server has no 0x17 branch ('Unhandled opcode'); instead _handle_accept_quest assumes turn-in arrives as 0x16 at the end NPC - the binary shows the real turn-in request is this 0x17. Server already has _send_quest_complete (S2C 0x27 u16), which matches the client's 0x27 reader (GetDataFromPacket ushort @0x47786E).
open_questions: Whether the server is expected to send any failure reply when requirements disagree server-side; none is visible in the client.
Exact semantics of FUN_00424df0 (type-1 requirement, assumed equipped-item check) and FUN_00426270 (assumed reward inventory-space simulation).
blind_open_questions: The meaning of quest_record+0xDF8 as a kill/progress requirement and of player_data+0x25C+slot as the per-slot progress byte (set by S2C 0x59) comes from usage, not from a named source.
It is unconfirmed whether the original server also expected 0x16 here in some flows. Statically, this site is the only turn-in send.

specs.grammar:
str[17] room_title
u8 max_users
u8 round_time_min
str[5] password
u16 map_id
u8 room_type

fields.name: room_title
fields.meaning: Room name: exactly 17 raw bytes copied from the edit-control text buffer (control+0xD1). NUL-terminated text; bytes after the NUL are whatever the edit buffer holds and are not guaranteed to be zero.
fields.dest_or_source: arena: window 0x2B edit ctrl 9; play room: window 0x479 edit ctrl 8

fields.name: max_users
fields.meaning: Low byte of atol() of the selected dropdown caption. The dropdown has 10 options. Probably max players, based on the room-list record having maxuser/curuser at +0x14/+0x15; not proven.
fields.dest_or_source: arena: window 0x2B ctrl 6 caption; play room: window 0x479 ctrl 6 caption

fields.name: round_time_min
fields.meaning: Arena: low byte of atol() of a 2-option dropdown caption (meaning unknown). Play room: always 1. LIVE-VERIFIED (C23, pvp_arena#05): this is the arena create dialog's "Time" dropdown = the round time in MINUTES, and the client only offers 3 or 5; play-room creation hardcodes 1. It is the source of scene+0xF37, which S2C 0x2F echoes back.
fields.dest_or_source: arena: window 0x2B ctrl 7 caption; play room: constant 1

fields.name: password
fields.meaning: Room password text: exactly 5 raw bytes from the edit-control text buffer. Empty text = first byte 0 = no password. A 5-character password has no terminating NUL inside these 5 bytes.
fields.dest_or_source: arena: window 0x2B edit ctrl 0xA; play room: window 0x479 edit ctrl 9

fields.name: map_id
fields.meaning: Arena map 0x2649/0x264A/0x264B/0x264C (9801..9804), chosen by matching ctrl 8's caption against option controls 0x1D..0x20; defaults to 0x2649 if nothing matches. Play room: always 0x26AF (9903).
fields.dest_or_source: arena: dword [ESP+0x10] (low 16 bits); play room: constant

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: Arena: 0/1/2/3, chosen by matching ctrl 0xF's caption against option controls 0x21..0x24 (3 = novice-only room). Play room: always 4. FUN_00444700 treats game+0xF70 == 4 as 'in play room'.

specs.semantics: Creates an arena room (window 0x2B, from the F-key ARENA list) or a Play&Chat room (window 0x479, from the P-key list). Both variants build the same 27-byte body in the same order and share the Send at 0x449384. After sending, the client opens the modal 'Waiting for the server to response.', which only a server reply can close.
specs.trigger: Control 3 ('Create') in the arena create-room dialog (window 0x2B) or in the play-room create dialog (window 0x479).
specs.expected_response: A reply is required to close the 'Waiting for the server to response.' modal. The most likely candidate is the room-enter result (S2C 0x2F reads game+0xF70/+0xF48); not verified. On failure, S2C 0xA2 has 'The number of the play rooms are excessive...'. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x34 RoomJoinResult (or S2C 0x2F on a successful enter, 0x30/0xA2 on a create failure).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Arena: FUN_00444400 blocks when manner < -20, already in arena or play room, in flea market, level < 5, in party play (window 0x75 state 1), waiting for battlefield, not standing still, hunting, stall open, or in cash shop. Play room: FUN_00444590 (same checks minus the level-5 rule). A title that fails Curse_Engine_Clean shows 'No cursing please' and nothing is sent. Title length and emptiness are not checked. If an edit control is missing, FUN_0048A030 returns NULL, and Curse_Engine_Clean and Add(char*,N) dereference it (crash). Novice-only rooms (type 3) cannot have a password, but that is enforced in the password UI, not on this send path. Text fields are raw edit buffers, so a server must stop at the first NUL and ignore trailing bytes. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C23, pvp_arena#05): both variants are 27 B and match the grammar field for field. max_users comes from a dropdown of {2,4,6,...,20}, so clamp it to 2..20 (design F3.3's 2..16 is wrong). The map dropdown order is 9801 "Popola Arena", 9802 "Marble Mount." (EN wording, not "Ohaengsan"), 9803 "Amakusa", 9804 "Balderan". room_type 3's EN caption is "For Beginners". round_time_min is only ever 3 or 5 from the arena dialog and 1 from the play-room dialog. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x34 (or 0x2F/0x30/0xA2 on failure).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on every Add call, its width and its order: u8 0x18, 17-byte title, u8, u8, 5-byte password, u16, u8 (27 bytes). The asm confirms this at 0x449969-0x4499ED (arena) and 0x44B30A-0x44B386 (play room); both jump to 0x44937C -> Send(1) @0x449384. Stack offsets check out: CSNSocket::Add is thiscall and pops its own arguments, so [ESP+0x1C]/[ESP+0x24]/[ESP+0x10]/[ESP+0x18] are read at the same ESP where they were stored. The only disagreement is whether the 5-byte password is typed bytes[5] (A) or str[5] (B). Both describe the same 5 raw bytes. The source is FUN_0048A030 (CALL FUN_00483120; ADD EAX,0xD1), the same edit-control text accessor that supplies the 17-byte title, which both analysts typed as str. The password is user-typed, NUL-terminated text, so B's str[5] is the correct DSL type. Wire length is identical either way. Neither our server (no 0x18 branch in _dispatch) nor PySlayer (no C2S parser) handles it. PySlayer's S2C 0x33 room entry (name[17], u16 room no, u8 maxuser, u8 curuser, ...) supports the max_users name.

[RESOLVED by live verification pvp_arena#05, 2026-09-17] Live: yes - it is the maximum player count, taken from a dropdown of {2,4,6,...,20}, so the server should clamp 2..20. Original question: "Whether max_users is really the maximum player count."

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: Room type of the selected row: 0 = level-restricted, 1/2 = normal, 3 = novice-only (4 = play room in the play-room list)

specs.semantics: Joins the room currently selected in the arena room list, when that room has no password. A password-protected room opens dialog 0x4A instead, which sends 0x1C from another site. The client remembers the room number and type in [this+0x4CC]+0xF48/+0xF70 and shows a blocking 'Waiting for the server to response.' modal.
specs.trigger: Click on one of the room-row controls 10..19 in window 0x2A (ARENA room list opened with F, which sends C2S 0x2C).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x34 join result (handler 0x455C21: 'Your level is not appropriate.', 'Invalid room #.', 'The room is full...'). The waiting modal must be cleared by the server's reply. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x34 RoomJoinResult (or S2C 0x2F + 0x2E when the join succeeds).
specs.gates_and_hazards: FUN_00444400: manner < -19 -> 'You can't use play room, battlefield, or arena...'. Arena/play-room map flag -> silent fail. Flea market -> refused. Level < 5 -> 'Level 5 or above is allowed to join.'. Party window 0x75 state != 1 -> 'Unable to do during the party play.'. Window 0x17B open -> 'already subscribed'. Motion != 8 -> 'Only able during stop motion.'. FUN_00418A90 -> 'Not during hunting/battle.'. Item stall 0x259 or cash shop 0x1CF open -> refused. FUN_00468FA0 must be 0. Room type 3 with a class-changed player ([[this+0x4CC]+0x970]+0x110 != 0) -> 'Only novice can enter a [novice-only room].'. Non-class-changed player and type != 3 -> 'A novice can only enter [Novice only room].'. If [rec+0x18]==0 (type 0), player level must be within [room_level(+0x16)-2 (min 1), room_level+1 (max 99)], else 'To enter Lv.%u room...'. Without a server reply the client stays stuck on the waiting modal. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x34.
specs.references: PySlayer client_packets/parse_0x1A.py reads u16 + u8 (example '1a 01 00 01'). Our server's _dispatch treats 0x1A as 'mob query - consumed' (wrong name, no reply). The play-room list (window 0x478 ctrl 10..19) sends the same 0x1A layout from a different send site.

(dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x34 RoomJoinResult (or S2C 0x2F + 0x2E when the join succeeds).

Its slice payload[1:2] reads only 1 byte for the u16, a bug. game_server.py handles 0x1A right after the 0x2C room-list flow, with a commented-out opcode_34 reply, which agrees this is a room join. Our windslayer_server.py consumes 0x1A as 'mob/target query' with no reply, which is wrong. The arena list (window 0x2A, another send site) sends the same 0x1A shape.

specs.semantics: Asks to join a password-locked room (arena or Play&Chat) after the user types its password. The client sends the room number and category it saved when the lock prompt opened, plus 5 bytes of password. It then shows a modal 'Waiting for the server to response.' box (message window 0x16) and waits for the server.
specs.trigger: The password dialog (window 0x4A) opens when the user picks a locked room (record+0x20 != 0) from the arena list (window 0x2A) or the Play&Chat list (window 0x478). It also reopens when S2C 0x34 returns result 3. Pressing OK (control 2) sends this packet. Cancel (control 4) only closes the dialog.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x34 [u8 result][u8 category] on failure. It closes/replaces the waiting box. Results: 1 'Incorrect password.', 2 'Invalid room #.', 3 reopen password dialog 0x4A, 4 'The room is full' (sets the cached row's cur_users = max for room_no == +0xF48), 5 close the waiting box and clear/refresh the room list (play-room list if category==4, else arena list), 6 'Your level is not appropriate.', 7 'Only novice can enter a [novice-only room].', 8 'A novice can only enter [Novice only room].'. The success reply (actually entering the room) was not traced in this batch. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x34 RoomJoinResult (result 3 = wrong password).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate at the send itself. Gates run when the dialog opens: FUN_00444400 for arena (manner point >= -19, not in flea market, level >= 5, not in party play, not already queued for battle, standing still (+0x904==8), not hunting, no item stall, not in cash shop), or FUN_00444590 for play rooms (same checks without the level gate). The arena list also checks novice status and level range. Hazard: the client waits on a modal box, so the server must always reply (for example with 0x34) or the UI stays stuck. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x34.
specs.references: PySlayer has no parser for 0x1C. Its S2C opcode_34 / opcode_A1 builders match the room record layout the client stores (name[17], u16 +0x12, u8 +0x14 max, u8 +0x15 cur, u8 +0x16, u8 +0x17 type, [u16 +0x22], bool +0x20 locked). windslayer_server.py _dispatch does not handle 0x1C (falls into 'Unhandled opcode'). The C2S create-room packet 0x18 (window 0x479) also sends a 5-byte password, which agrees with str[5].
open_questions: Which S2C packet confirms a successful room join / room entry (0x34 only covers failures) was not traced here.
Max length of the password edit box: 4 chars + NUL, or 5 chars with no NUL, is unknown. Only 5 bytes go on the wire either way.
blind_open_questions: Is the dialog 0x4A password edit box limited to 4 characters? The 5-byte copy suggests so, but the control's max length was not checked.
Which S2C opcode confirms a successful room entry (0x34 only handles errors)?
The exact meaning of room_kind values other than 3 (novice-only) and 4 (Play&Chat room), e.g. 0 for arena rooms entered by number.

specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x70E6F4], via quest_mgr+0x14 = [EBX+0x14], set in FUN_00477040 @0x477054)

locations.role: quest window UI event handler (EAX=window id, arg1=quest_mgr, arg2=control id, arg3=event type, arg4)
caller: UI dispatcher default path (control id != 0), only if app+0xD30 != 0 and FUN_00469090 did not consume the event
Add(ushort) quest_id = low word of selected list row +0xC
builds quest-window (id 6) list rows: 0x24-byte row, +8 byte in_progress flag (1 only for rows from active slots chardata+0x256), +0xC quest id

fields.name: quest_id
fields.meaning: Id of the in-progress quest selected in the quest window list
fields.dest_or_source: MOVZX word [row+0xC]; row = FUN_00459fd0(list @ window6+0xAC, index = [window6+0xEC]-1), window6 = FUN_004830f0(ui_root, 6). row+0xC was filled by FUN_00478380 from the active quest slot word chardata+0x256+2*slot (chardata = local player entity+0x48).

specs.semantics: Asks the server to abandon (give up) the currently selected in-progress quest. The client does not modify its quest state when sending; it waits for S2C 0x38 (u16 quest_id), whose handler zeroes the matching slot word at chardata+0x256.. and its progress byte at chardata+0x25C+slot, then refreshes the quest window (FUN_00478380) and the NPC quest list (FUN_004786d0(quest_mgr+0x1C)). Name inferred from that effect plus the 3-quest-limit message text ('...complete or abandon one of the quests already taken').
specs.trigger: UI event (any event type) on window id 0x29 with control id 2 (a button associated with the quest window, id 6), while a row of the 'in progress' tab (tab control 0x18) is selected.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x38 u16 quest_id (quest removed from active log; handler @0x4777E0).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Checks in order: quest_mgr+8 (ui root) != 0; window id == 0x29 and control id == 2; FUN_00444700(app) returns 0 - if app+0x4D8+0x70 == 1 it shows 'Not allowed in play room.' (player+0xF70 == 4) or 'Not allowed in arena.' and does not send; window 6 record exists; its selection index +0xEC != 0; selected row exists; row+8 (in_progress flag byte) != 0 - rows from the available/completed tabs have flag 0 so nothing is sent. No confirmation dialog in this code path (a confirmation may be the 0x29 window itself). Server must validate that the quest is actually held.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer client_packets (no parse_0x1E) nor game_server.py. Our server has no 0x1E branch (falls to 'Unhandled opcode'). Memory note reference_combat_model lists 0x1E among 'INBOUND' opcodes but that concerned S2C; this C2S 0x1E is quest abandon. S2C 0x38 (quest removal) must not be confused with C2S 0x38 (handled as basic attack by our server).
open_questions: Identity of window 0x29 (quest window button panel vs. an abandon-confirmation box) and control 2 label - defined in UI data files, not in the exe.
FUN_004773c0 does not check event type for the 0x29/control-2 path, so it may fire on more than one event kind per click; server should tolerate duplicates.
blind_open_questions: That window id 0x29 is the 'Abandon Quest / Would you like to discard this quest?' confirmation, and control 2 its Yes button, is inferred from UI strings. No code reference opens window 0x29 (the UI is data-driven). The wire format does not depend on this.

The dispatcher parameter p2 is read as the control id from the WM_LBUTTONUP hit test in FUN_00487DB0 (msg=[+0x30] window, p2=[+0x34]). This is consistent with, but not proven by, the other cases in FUN_004773C0 (window 6 tabs 0x17..0x19, window 0x236 controls 1..5).

specs.name: GroundItemPickupRequest

locations.role: calls it on WM_SYSKEYDOWN (0x104) for VK_MENU/VK_F10
creates the 0x40-byte ground-item node (from S2C 0x12); uid stored at node+0x12
the response that marks the item picked and adds it to the bag

specs.grammar: u16 ground_item_uid

fields.name: ground_item_uid
fields.dest_or_source: ground-item node +0x12 (word). Node comes from the list at scene(*0x70EECC)+0x1C. FUN_00423a10 wrote the value (param_6) when S2C 0x12 spawned the item.
fields.meaning: instance id of the ground item (dropped loot) to pick up. The same id is matched by S2C 0x13 (FUN_00440e50 compares node+0x12).

specs.semantics: The player asks to pick up one ground item. The client does all range, ownership and bag-space checks first. It sends at most one 0x1F per key event: the first item in the scene ground-item list that passes all checks. The client does not change the item locally. It waits for S2C 0x13 to set node+0x16=2, set node+0x1C=picker, and, when the picker is the local uid, add the item to the bag and print "you've received %s. (Count:%u)".
specs.trigger: Pickup key held during any key-down message. The key is the bound slot at game_state+0xDFC, copied from COption+0x68 (registry "Key3", default 'W' 0x57) by FUN_00475710. FUN_0043d5c0 runs from MsgProc on WM_KEYDOWN when the UI did not consume the key and chat does not have focus (g_ui_root+8==0, g_ui_root+0x30==0). It also runs on WM_SYSKEYDOWN with Alt/F10. It then calls GetAsyncKeyState(pickup key).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x13 (handler 0x4518D0): u16 ground_item_uid, u16 count, u32 picker_uid. Broadcast it to everyone on the map so other clients mark the item taken. If validation fails there is no known error reply; the client simply keeps the item on the ground.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates, in order: (1) scene+0xF00 == 6 (in-game). (2) NOT (game_state+0xD7C != 0 && game_state+0xD5C == 0x259). (3) FUN_00468fa0() == 0: UI window 0x28C/modal state is not 3. (4) app+0x9E == 0 (device not lost) and app+0x9D != 0 (app active). (5) The pickup key is down. (6) scene != 0 and scene+0x970 (local player entity) != 0. Per item in the scene+0x1C linked list: skip null nodes and nodes with state byte +0x16 == 2 (already picked). Range: (player u16@+0x15A4 - node.x u16@+0x0E)^2 + (player u16@+0x15A8 - node.y u16@+0x10)^2 < 625 (unsigned). Ownership: node+0x1C owner == 0, or == scene+0x220 (local uid), or node+0x24 + 15000 < scene+0xF1C (15 s loot protection). Otherwise the item is flagged as not owned. Bag space by node+0x18 category (from item def +0x154): 0 = capacity byte scene+0x3AA <= 45 and FUN_00424c80 (qty node+0x14 <= 999; a same-id stack at ids scene+0x63E / counts scene+0x698 with count+qty < 1000, or an empty slot). 1 = capacity scene+0x3A9 <= 45 and an empty slot in scene+0x3C8 (equipment, no stacking). 2 = capacity scene+0x3AB <= 45 and FUN_00424d00 (qty <= 99; a stack at ids +0x7A8 / byte counts +0x802 below 100, or an empty slot). Any other category is never sent. If nothing is sent: an owned in-range item with no bag space and game_state+0x3DC != 0 shows "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory." and clears +0x3DC (MsgProc sets it back to 1 on WM_KEYUP). Otherwise, if some in-range item was not owned, it shows "You don't have ownership of this item." HAZARDS: holding the key auto-repeats WM_KEYDOWN, so the client can send 0x1F for the same uid many times before 0x13 arrives. The server must be idempotent: grant once, ignore uids already picked. The uid is only 16 bits on the wire (node+0x12 is a u16), so ground uids must fit in u16.
specs.references: PySlayer: no C2S parser for 0x1F. Our server: this is the "pickup-request opcode still unidentified" noted near windslayer_server.py:1925. Ground drops (0x12) are deferred because of it. DISCREPANCY in our _build_opcode_13 (line ~1724): it packs the second u16 as the item id, but FUN_00440e50 uses that value (param_4) as the COUNT, both for the bag add (e.g. MOVZX EAX,[ESP+0x64] at 0x440EEB) and for the "(Count:%u)" text. The item id comes from the ground node (node+0x00). Our GROUND_ITEM_UID_BASE 0x00200000 truncates to 0x0000 on the wire, so it is unsafe as a u16 uid.
open_questions: Exact meaning of item category 2 (stack max 99, ids at scene+0x7A8, byte counts at +0x802): quest/material bag?
Whether node+0x24 (drop timestamp) comes from the S2C 0x12 wire or is stamped from the client clock (it feeds FUN_00423a10 param_9)
What game_state+0xD7C / +0xD5C==0x259 represent (some action/cutscene state that blocks pickup)
blind_open_questions: The meaning of the gate [game_state+0xD5C]==0x259 with [game_state+0xD7C]!=0. It sits inside the embedded SubHandler1 object and is probably some trade/shop mode.
Whether ground-item +0x24 and scene+0xF1C are both millisecond ticks. The +0x3A98 (15000) constant suggests they are.

specs.grammar: str[17] requester_name

fields.name: requester_name
fields.meaning: name of the player who asked to trade, echoed back (NUL padded)
fields.dest_or_source: label text of dialog 0x70 control 1, which S2C 0x45 set from its str[17] name

specs.semantics: Accepts an incoming trade request. The requester sends C2S 0x20 (u32 target uid), and the server shows the target a popup via S2C 0x45 (requester name). Clicking OK on that popup sends this packet with the requester's name so the server can open the trade for both players.
specs.trigger: Event 3 (OK/accept button) on popup dialog 0x70, which S2C 0x45 opened.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x46 (str[17] partner name; opens trade window 0x4E and resets its buttons) or S2C 0x47 u8 status (6 = "Trading.", 4 = "The player is rejecting trade.").
specs.gates_and_hazards: No preconditions beyond the dialog event. Hazard: the copy is an unbounded strcpy from the label (up to 0x81 bytes) into a 17-byte stack buffer. The S2C 0x45 name must be NUL-terminated within 16 chars, or the client overflows the stack. If control 1 is missing, strcpy reads from NULL and the client crashes. No decline packet is built in this function.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer or our server. S2C 0x45/0x46/0x47 handlers in SubHandler1 (0x46CF40) confirm the flow.
open_questions: That event 3 is 'accept' (not 'decline') is inferred: it is the only packet dialog 0x70 produces, and the S2C 0x46 trade-open follows it. How a decline is reported (if at all) was not found.
blind_open_questions: Naming is inferred from neighbouring trade handlers. No UI string for dialog 0x70 was found in the exe (it is probably in UI resources), so it could in theory be a similar name-based request prompt (e.g. party).
Does declining send anything? Not from FUN_00469090; it may be handled generically in FUN_00446300 or just close the dialog.

specs.semantics: Adds a stackable item from the bag to the local trade offer. The item is the one selected in inventory window 9; the quantity comes from the trade quantity dialog 0x74.
specs.trigger: Clicking OK (button 2) in dialog 0x74, the trade quantity prompt
specs.expected_response: Most likely S2C 0x4B (trade slot add: u16 item, u16 count, u32 owner uid, u8 n, n x u16, u16 extra). It puts the item into the own or partner trade list depending on the uid.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to put a non-stacking item (catalog type 1) from the player's bag into their own offer in the open player-to-player trade window. The client does NOT move the item locally. It sends the packet and waits for the server's echo.
specs.trigger: The player drags an item from the Inventory window (UI window id 9) and drops it on the Trade window (window id 0x4E) while a trade is open. Stacking items (catalog type 0 or 2) do not send from here: they open the quantity dialog (UI 0x74, default value = rec+0x0E), and on OK FUN_00469090 sends the same opcode from send site #66 (Send at 0x469D9C, Adds at 0x469F27..0x469F4F) as: u16 item_id, u16 entered_qty, u8 0, u16 0.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x4B TradeItemAdded (SubHandler1, 0x46E542): u16 item_id, u16 qty, u32 owner_uid, u8 n, n x u16 enchant, u16 enchant_last. Send it to BOTH traders. When owner_uid == local uid (char+0x1D8 = scene+0x220), the client takes the item out of its bag (0x467140) and adds it to its own trade grid (0x489A80, window 0x4E). Otherwise it appends the item to the partner-offer list (win+0xBC). If the partner has no room, send S2C 0x4D ('There are no more spaces in the other player's item slot.').
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks, in order: (1) source window 9 and destination window 0x4E; (2) FUN_00489090 returns non-zero for Trade window sub-controls 3 and 2 (their +0x1C state; probably the trade is not yet locked or confirmed); (3) the Trade window exists and its own-offer count [win+0xB8] < 12, otherwise a modal notice 'There are no more spaces in trade slot' (0x489DA0) and no packet; (4) 0x466980 finds the dragged bag record and its catalog entry; (5) catalog+0x1F0 == 0, otherwise the drop is silently ignored (a no-trade flag; 0x465290 greys these items out during a trade); (6) catalog type +0x154: 1 = send now; 0 or 2 = quantity dialog; any other type = nothing. Hazards: the client keeps no pending state, so repeated drags of the same item send duplicate 0x22s. The server must check ownership, the 12-slot limit, the no-trade flag and that a trade session is active. The receiver must zero-fill enchant words >= enchant_count. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.
specs.references: Our server: _dispatch (windslayer_server.py ~line 602) has no inbound 0x22 handler. Outbound 0x22 in our server is S2C SetLevel, a different direction and meaning. PySlayer: no client_packets parser for 0x22. The trailing layout (u8 n, n x u16, u16) is the same as C2S 0x0F equip (builder 0x44C2C0, captured payload 'B3 00 00 00 00') and C2S 0x11, and it mirrors S2C 0x4B, which reads exactly these fields plus a u32 owner uid after qty.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to cancel the current trade. It is sent when the player clicks the X close button (control 2, text 'End') or the 'Cancel' button (control 4) in the trade offer window 0x4E 'Exchange', or the same two buttons in the final window 0x291 'Confirm Exchange'. Before sending, the client disables controls 2 and 4 of that window so the click can't repeat. The window stays open until the server answers. There is no body. The positive buttons are control 3 in each window: 'OK' in 0x4E sends 0x23 + u64 gold, and 'Trade' in 0x291 sends 0x25 + gold + items. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#04, trade#12): the EN captions differ from the KR lng strings quoted in the references - window 0x4E is captioned "TRADE" (not "Exchange") and window 0x291 is "Comfirming Trade" [sic] with list headers "Items to Send" / "Items to Receive" and ctrl 3 labelled "Trade".
specs.trigger: Clicking X/End (control 2) or Cancel (control 4) in trade window 0x4E or 0x291
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x49 'Trade has been canceled.' (handler 0x46E465). It closes windows 0x4E and 0x291 with FUN_00483430(win,1,1) and returns the items staged in the window's +0xAC/+0xB0 list to the bag. The server should send 0x49 to both players. The client does not block waiting for it.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only gate: the UI root [ctx+0xC] must be non-null (0x4690BC). There are no trade-state checks. If the server never replies, controls 2 and 4 stay disabled and the window can't be closed. Only S2C 0x46 (trade open, 0x46DFA9) enables them again (EDI=1 at 0x46DFEE). A server must not treat 0x24 as a confirm or lock: those are 0x23 and 0x25. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, trade#05/#06): live proof - after the first Cancel click both Cancel and the caption X are disabled and produce ZERO packets, so the TRADE window cannot be closed at all until the server answers. RECOVERY: send S2C 0x49 (it closes 0x4E/0x291 and returns the staged items). The server must always answer 0x24.
specs.references: ADDITIONAL CHECK: the UI layout file hs/windslayer.hui (read-only decode with the asset cipher K=[E9,DE,E0], output written only to the scratchpad) names the buttons. Its text ids resolve through hs/UILngKo.lng. Window 78 (0x4E), title 845 'Exchange': control 2 = text 491 'End', a 16x16 type-9 close button at 292,9; control 3 = text 330 'OK'; control 4 = text 331 'Cancel'. Window 657 (0x291), title 4750 'Confirm Exchange': control 2 = 'End' (X); control 3 = text 8048 'Trade'; control 4 = 'Cancel'. OTHER SOURCES: not in PySlayer client_packets and not handled in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. Related S2C handlers in SubHandler1: 0x46 opens 0x4E and enables controls 2/3/4 on both windows; 0x47 is a status message ('Trading.' / 'The player is rejecting trade.'); 0x48 (u32 uid, u64 gold) marks one side as locked and moves both players to 0x291 once both have locked; 0x49 is cancel; 0x4A is complete.
open_questions: Whether the server should also send 0x49 to the player who cancelled or only to the partner. The client handles 0x49 the same either way, so sending it to both is safe.

specs.semantics: Final accept of a player-to-player trade. After both sides lock (S2C 0x48 for self and for the partner), the client opens the confirmation window 0x291. Pressing OK disables the button and sends the whole deal as this client sees it: its own gold and item list, then the partner's gold and item list. Each item is id, quantity, a variable-length option list, and word +0x0C.
specs.trigger: Event 3 (OK button) on dialog 0x291. S2C 0x48 opens that window once button 3 of trade window 0x4E is disabled (own lock) and ctx+0x24 == 1 (partner locked).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x4A (trade completed) or S2C 0x49 ("Trade has been canceled."). Pairing comes from the handler strings; the payloads were not followed here.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs ctx+0x0C != 0. Button 3 is disabled BEFORE the dialog null-check, so if FUN_004830f0(0x291) returns null nothing is sent but the button stays disabled. The gold values are round-tripped through text with _strtoi64. A null text pointer from FUN_0048a050 would make _strtoi64 hit its invalid-parameter path. Counts are u8; the own trade grid is capped at 12 slots. Events 2/4 on the same dialog send C2S 0x24 (zero payload) instead. SERVER HAZARD: our server's _dispatch (windslayer_server.py:644) treats inbound 0x25 as UseSkill/attack (_handle_attack). A trade-confirm packet would be misparsed as a hit list. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C25, trade#13): the misparse does NOT stop at the first list - the attack parser read past my_item_count and produced one bogus target per offered item on BOTH sides (2 bogus targets from a 1+1 deal), so the exploit surface is every item id in either list, not just the sender's.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A gave u64 my_gold, u8 count, items{u16 id, u16 amount, u8 n, n*u16, u16}, u64 partner_gold, u8 count, items{same}. Analyst B did not report this key, because the path reaches the shared Send at 0x469BA8 only through JZ 0x469BA3 @0x46AB27 or JMP 0x469BA3 @0x46ABD0. The asm confirms A in every detail. 0x46A99C PUSH 0x25 -> Add(uchar). 0x46A9AD FUN_0048a050(EDX=0x1D) -> FUN_0048b6ac (_strtoi64 base 10) -> PUSH EDX, PUSH EAX -> Add(u64) [0x4A40C4] @0x46A9C0. Count loop over [dlg+0xB0] -> Add(uchar) @0x46A9FD. For each node with data: Add(ushort) [data] @0x46AA3A, Add(ushort) [data+0xE] @0x46AA44, option count (<5, stop at zero) Add(uchar) @0x46AA6D, Add(ushort) loop @0x46AA8D, Add(ushort) [data+0xC] @0x46AAA8. Then EDX=0x1E -> u64 @0x46AADE, list [dlg+0xC0] with the same pattern @0x46AB15..0x46ABB8, then Send(1). Own/partner list identity comes from S2C 0x48 @0x46E184: uid == self marks dialog 0x4E list +0xB0; otherwise gold goes to label 0x1F, ctx+0x24 = 1 and list +0xC0 is marked. The lists are copied to dialog 0x291 +0xAC/+0xBC containers (heads +0xB0/+0xC0) at 0x46E2A7/0x46E2EF. The dialog id was decoded from the table: 0x291 -> 0x46A95C. Not in PySlayer. Our server has an inbound 0x25 handler with a DIFFERENT meaning (skill/attack hit list). The only literal PUSH 0x25 + Add(uchar) opcode site in the corpus is this one, so the server's 0x25-as-attack assumption should be re-checked.

Payload layouts of S2C 0x49 and 0x4A were not traced in this task.
Is there a register-supplied 0x25 send elsewhere (skill use) that our server's _handle_attack corresponds to? No literal one was found.

specs.semantics: Takes an item back out of the player's own trade offer. The client has already put the item back in its bag (0x467200: type 1 into the first empty bag slot, type 0 via 0x423B70 into the consumable bag, type 2 via 0x423E70 into the etc bag), refreshed the Inventory UI (0x465290) and removed the offer node. The packet tells the server so it can update the trade and notify the partner.
specs.trigger: The player drags an item out of their own side of the Trade window (window 0x4E) and drops it on the Inventory window (9) or on empty space (destination 0).
specs.expected_response: No reply to the sender is needed: its UI is already updated. Send S2C 0x4C (u8 slot_index; handler 0x46E729) to the trading PARTNER only; it removes node #index (0-based, 0x45A000) from the partner-offer list (win+0xBC). Do NOT send 0x4C to the sender: it would delete an entry from the sender's view of the partner's offer.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks: source 0x4E and destination 9 or 0; Trade window sub-controls 3 and 2 both non-zero (0x489090); a catalog entry exists for the dragged item id at ui_root+0x14 (0x404210 on [scene+0xF84]); the Trade window exists. For each own-offer node, it matches when node word+0x00 == dragged id AND the 12 bytes at node+0x02 equal ui_root+0x16 (0x427390). On a match, 0x467200(type, ctx, item_id, qty) must return non-zero before the packet is sent. HAZARDS: (1) if 0x467200 fails (bag full: type-1 bag capacity byte char+0x361 > 45 or no empty slot), the node is STILL unlinked and freed but no packet goes out, so the item disappears from the client's trade UI while the server still holds it as offered (desync). (2) The loop does not stop after a match. Several identical offers (same id and attributes) are all removed, one 0x26 each, and the index counter keeps counting removed nodes, so every later packet's trade_slot_index is based on the list as it was BEFORE any removal. A server that removes by index should process them against the original order, or match by item_id plus attributes.
specs.references: Our server: no inbound 0x26 in _dispatch. S2C 0x26 in our server is the quest GRANT, the opposite direction and unrelated. PySlayer: no 0x26 client parser. The body mirrors S2C 0x4B's item layout plus a slot index; S2C 0x4C carries only that index to the partner.

specs.name: PartyBreak

locations.role: window 0x50 (player context menu) control switch, table 0x44BC2C: ctrl 5 -> 0x44A4C0
gate FUN_00444700 (arena / play room -> message, abort)
FUN_004837C0(window 0x17B) == 3 -> FUN_00444750 always returns 1 -> abort ('Not able to do it, during waiting to join the battle field.')
FUN_004830F0(0x50): context menu window must exist, saved at [ESP+0x14]
loop over party slot windows 0x75..0x78: count nonzero slot uids in EBX
CMP slot uid [slot+0x134] with target uid [win0x50+0x134]; JZ 0x44A549
same slot-uid test labels window 0x50 ctrl 5 'Break Party' (otherwise 'Make Party')

specs.semantics: Bare opcode, no body. It is sent by the context-menu button (window 0x50 ctrl 5) when the right-clicked player's uid matches one of the party slot windows 0x75..0x78. The same test in FUN_0044C4B0 labels the button 'Break Party'. No uid or name is sent, so the server must work out the party from the sender's session. It means leave or disband the sender's own party, not kick the clicked player. If there is no match, the same button sends 0x27 + u32 target uid (invite), or shows 'The party is full' when 4 slots are filled.
specs.trigger: Player context menu window 0x50, control 5 ('Break Party'), on a player who is already in one of your party slots.
specs.expected_response: No 'Waiting for the server' modal on this path. The server should update or clear the party slot windows (reply opcode not traced here).
specs.gates_and_hazards: FUN_00444700: blocked in arena or play room ('Not allowed in arena.' / 'Not allowed in play room.'). Blocked while window 0x17B (battlefield standby) is in state 3. Window 0x50 must exist. The 'party full' check is not reached on this path. Edge case: slot windows with uid 0 are still compared, so a target uid of 0 would match an empty existing slot.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on every byte. The packet is the opcode 0x29 alone: Add(u8 0x29) at 0x44A551 goes straight to JMP 0x4484C4, which is MOV ECX,[g_sock_game]; PUSH 1; CALL Send. There is no Add between the opcode and Send. A wrote the empty grammar as ""; B wrote "stop". Those are only two spellings of a zero-length body, and the wire meaning is the same. Since no Add follows the opcode, the correct grammar for this C2S packet is empty (length 0). "stop" is meant for a read path that ends early and does not apply to a send. B's extra VA 0x44C8BE ('Break Party' caption) is correct and is included. Not handled by our server (no 0x29 branch in _dispatch). PySlayer has no C2S parser for it.
open_questions: Whether the server treats 0x29 as leaving the party or disbanding it (the client sends no data to tell them apart).

specs.name: CharacterInfoRequest

locations.role: FUN_004830F0(0x50): context menu window must exist
FUN_004189F0(uid=[win0x50+0x134], scene [game+0x4CC]) looks up the target entity
entity found -> fills info window 0x72 locally, no packet; entity not found -> JZ 0x44A339
S2C 0x52 reads a 17-byte name first and later opens window 0x72 (0x45700D), so it is the likely reply

specs.grammar: str[17] target_name

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: Character name of the context-menu target. The buffer is zeroed first and then strcpy'd, so it is NUL-padded to 17 bytes.
fields.dest_or_source: window 0x50 control 2 caption (the target name, also used in 'You requested <%s> to join the party.')

specs.semantics: Asks the server for another player's profile when that player is not loaded in the client's current field. If FUN_004189F0 finds the entity locally, the client fills info window 0x72 from local data and sends nothing. Otherwise it sends the target's name.
specs.trigger: Player context menu window 0x50, control 3 (info), on a player not present in the current field (e.g., opened from a list or chat name). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C52, social_friend#07, trade#15, login_character#18): right-click alone opens the player popup window 0x50 (no double-click needed). EN entry order top to bottom: Char. Info / Trade / Make Party / Whisper / Add as Friend / Converse / Copy Name / Praise / Report (ctrl 3..11).
specs.expected_response: Most likely S2C 0x52 (reads str[17] name, then data, and opens window 0x72 at 0x45700D). No wait modal on the client side.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Window 0x50 must exist. If control 2 is missing, ECX = 0 and the strcpy reads from NULL (crash). The strcpy is unbounded into a 17-byte stack buffer, so a caption longer than 16 characters overflows the stack; normal names fit. No arena, party or battle gates on this path.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A did not report this key; analyst B did, and the asm confirms B. Window 0x50 ctrl 3 resolves through jump table 0x44BC2C to 0x44A01C (read from the binary). On the not-found branch 0x44A339, a 17-byte buffer at [ESP+0x40] is zeroed (four dwords at +0x40/+0x44/+0x48/+0x4C plus one byte at +0x50), the ctrl-2 caption is strcpy'd into it (0x44A370 loop), and the code does PUSH 0x2A; JMP 0x44A650. There: CALL Add(u8) (thiscall, pops its argument), PUSH 0x11, LEA ECX,[ESP+0x44] (= frame+0x40, the same buffer), PUSH ECX, CALL Add(char*,17) @0x44A669, then JMP 0x4484C4 -> Send(1). The found branch (0x44A050-0x44A336) contains no Add or Send. Body: str[17] target_name, 17 bytes. Not handled by our server or PySlayer.
open_questions: Confirm that S2C 0x52 is the reply to 0x2A (its first field, a 17-byte name, and its opening window 0x72 strongly suggest it).

locations.role: gates: scene+0xF00==5, app+0x3F8 != 0, [app+0x3F8]+0x15A4 > 0x30C, UI window 0x16 check
call FUN_004410d0, which loads per-character registry settings (HKCU\Software\Hamelin\WindSlayer\<name>) into COption at app+0x4E8 via FUN_00474820 @0x441169
reads RefuseWisper->+0x18, RefuseExchange->+0x1C, RefuseParty->+0x20, RefuseFriend->+0x24, RefuseTalk->+0x28 (DWORDs; 0 if missing)
dialog 'Waiting for the server to response.'
UDP/P2P handler case 0x11: copies the datagram source IP into scene+0x224 and sets scene+0x244 = 0xA79B
S2C 0x03 handler calls KillTimer(2), which ends the wait

specs.grammar:
u8 refuse_whisper
u8 refuse_exchange
u8 refuse_party
u8 refuse_talk
u8 refuse_friend
str[16] p2p_ip
u32 p2p_udp_port

fields.name: refuse_whisper
fields.dest_or_source: low byte of app+0x500 (0x70EF00) = COption+0x18, registry 'RefuseWisper'
fields.meaning: Player option: block whispers (0/1).

fields.name: refuse_exchange
