fields.meaning: Player option: block friend requests.

fields.name: p2p_ip
fields.meaning: The client's own IPv4 dotted string for peer-to-peer (UDP) rooms, learned from its UDP 0x11 datagram's source address (FUN_00458640 case 0x11). NUL-padded. Captures show '127.0.0.1' and '10.5.0.2'. Could be empty/stale if no echo was received.

fields.name: p2p_udp_port
fields.meaning: Client UDP P2P port. The client only ever assigns the constant 0xA79B = 42907 (0x4400D9, 0x459BAB, 0x476526). It is used as the SendTo port in FUN_00423260.

fields.name: char_name
fields.meaning: Name of the character entering the world (also used as the registry subkey). NUL-padded.

specs.semantics: Request to enter the game world with the selected character. It also reports the player's refuse-* social options and P2P UDP endpoint. On the client, app+0x3F8 (selected character) is cleared so the request fires once; a 5.5 s TIMER_RECEIVELOADED starts and a wait dialog is shown.
specs.trigger: Character-select screen (scene+0xF00 == 5). A character is clicked (0x44CA84 sets app+0x3F8 = entity, entity+0x8B4 = 4). Once that entity's int X (+0x15A4) exceeds 780 (0x30C) (likely the walk-off after Start), and UI window id 0x16 is absent or its +0x3C == 1, the packet is built on the next logic tick. The UI branches on entity+0x110 only copy text between controls of window 0x2B and do not change the bytes.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x03 (in-game state; its handler at 0x44E38F kills timer 2 and closes windows 0x16/0x13), then S2C 0x07 local-player spawn (PySlayer and our server also send 0x0A welcome chat; ours also sends 0x28/0x44 HP/MP).
specs.gates_and_hazards: If scene+0x224 was never filled, p2p_ip is zeros, so the server must not require it. What happens when TIMER_RECEIVELOADED (id 2, 5500 ms) fires with no S2C 0x03 was not traced (memory notes a ~35 s loading loop re-arming). The branch with entity+0x110 != 0 dereferences a NULL text pointer if window 0x2B is missing (client-side crash only).
specs.references: Capture (42 bytes) '00 00 00 00 00 | 31 32 37 2E 30 2E 30 2E 31 00*7 | 9B A7 00 00 | 54 65 73 74 48 65 72 6F 00...' matches: 5 refuse flags, 16-byte IP, u32 42907, 17-byte name. This CORRECTS memory protocol.md, which calls it a 'client version string' plus a 'WORD 0xA79B magic key', and our server's docstring ('[5-13] ip', '[21-22] 0xA79B magic'). The real layout is str[16] at 5..20 and u32 port at 21..24. Our server reads name = payload[25:42], which is correct. PySlayer parse_2B reads the IP from body[6:0x15], consistent.
open_questions: TIMER_RECEIVELOADED (id 2) expiry handler not located: does it resend 0x2B or abort?
Identity of UI window 0x16 (its +0x3C must be 1) and meaning of entity+0x110 on the select screen.
Whether the original server used p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port to broker P2P arena rooms (FUN_00458640 UDP protocol).
blind_open_questions: What does timer id 2 do on expiry (disconnect/error)? WM_TIMER handler not located in this pass.
Exact origin of the scene+0x224 IP (local NIC, server-reported, or DirectPlay address) and whether a server needs it for P2P relaying.

specs.name: ArenaRoomListOpen

locations.role: outer switch on arg3 (action); table 0x44B848 = [0x4466DF, 0x446A9E, 0x4463FF, 0x4463FF], so actions 3 and 4 go to the open branch at 0x4463FF
FUN_004837C0(id) returns [win+0x3C] (1 if the window is not registered); if it equals the action, jump to 0x446AB4 and send nothing
inner switch: idx byte 0x44B878[id-1], ptr table 0x44B858; id 0x2A maps to 0x44643A
FUN_00489580(0x2A): sub-control state change, UI only. It runs BEFORE the gate
gate: CMP [[this+0x4D8]+0x70],1 / JZ 0x44B830 (epilogue): no packet and the window is not shown
ECX=[0x70E6F4]; PUSH 0x2C; CALL [0x4A40FC] Add(uchar): the opcode, and the only Add
PUSH 1; CALL [0x4A4108] Send on g_sock_game, then JMP 0x4466BF, which reaches FUN_004835B0 (show window)
hotkey poller: slot 10 window id [this+0x10B0] (set to 0x2A by the constructor at 0x4298CB) -> FUN_00483800 toggle (action 3 if state==1 or window missing, else 1)
internal UI button case that also toggles window 0x2A via FUN_00483800

specs.semantics: Asks the server for the arena room list. The body is the opcode byte only; no Add follows the opcode. FUN_00446300 is the UI window-state setter (thiscall, this=[g_ui_root+0x59C]=game_state; arg1=window id, arg3=new state: 1 hide, 3 show, 4 show+focus). When window 0x2A (ARENA room list) moves to state 3 or 4 from another state and the map-mode gate passes, the client sends this packet and then shows the window. It does not wait for a reply.
specs.trigger: F key (hotkey slot 10), an internal UI button (0x44AA62), or any FUN_00446300(0x2A, *, 3|4, ...) call. Live capture: F -> 0x2C with 0 bytes.
specs.expected_response: Nothing is awaited. The list is filled by S2C 0x33 (handler 0x4555E6: frees the arena room list at game_state+0x440, refreshes window 0x2A via FUN_004838C0, closes window 0x16, then falls through into the 0x32 parser at 0x45565E, which reads a u8 room count and loops over entries) and/or S2C 0x32 (append entries). PySlayer answers with 0x33.
specs.gates_and_hazards: (1) Not sent if FUN_004837C0(0x2A) already equals the requested state. A 3<->4 transition sends it again. (2) Not sent, and the window stays hidden, if [[game_state+0x4D8]+0x70]==1. That field is the map's 'mode' XML attribute, loaded in FUN_00407190 at 0x4076E7 (values >1 have 2 subtracted); this is the arena/play-room map ('Not allowed in arena.'). (3) FUN_00489580(0x2A) runs even when the gate blocks. (4) No ResetBuffer before the Add; the code relies on Send leaving the buffer empty. (5) Our server's _handle_room_query reads payload[0] as a 'code'. EN sends no code byte, so the server gets 0 and sends no list.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A (decomp+asm) and B (asm only) agree on every wire fact: opcode-only body, g_sock_game, gates 3/4 + state-differs + map-mode==1. The dispute is only notation: A grammar "" vs B "stop". The asm has exactly one Add: ECX=[0x70E6F4] at 0x446464, PUSH 0x2C / CALL [0x4A40FC] at 0x44646A-0x44646C, then PUSH 1 / CALL [0x4A4108] Send at 0x446478-0x44647A. There are no calls between the Add and Send, and no Adds earlier on the path (0x4463FF -> 0x44643A -> 0x446447 -> 0x44645B). The canonical grammar is therefore empty (zero fields); 'stop' is a read-path terminator and describes no wire bytes. On details: B is right that FUN_00489580 runs before the gate (0x44643C precedes 0x446451). A's response analysis is verified: the 0x33 handler at 0x4555E6 frees +0x440, refreshes window 0x2A and falls through to the 0x32 parser at 0x45565E. Other references: matches the live capture (F -> 0x2C, 0 bytes). Disagrees with PySlayer parse_0x2C (KR adds a u8 code). Our server: consumed but misparsed, and its 'sent once at spawn' comment is wrong for this site.
open_questions: Byte layout of the S2C 0x33/0x32 room entries is outside this batch.
Whether any other send site outside this batch emits 0x2C.

specs.name: ArenaRoomListClose

locations.role: close switch on id-9: idx byte 0x44B8F8, ptr table 0x44B8E8 = [0x446E36, 0x446748, 0x446724, 0x4466C5]; only id 0x2A maps to 0x446748
CALL [0x4A40FC] Add(uchar): the opcode, and the only Add
S2C 0x08 (and 0x5E/0xA3/0xA4, which share the block from 0x450867) map-load path: unconditional FUN_00483430(0x2A, EBX=1, EBX=1), with EBX set at 0x4508FC

specs.semantics: Tells the server the ARENA room list window (0x2A) was closed, presumably so it stops room-list updates. It is the close counterpart of C2S 0x2C. The body is the opcode byte only. It is sent when window 0x2A moves to state 1 from a non-1 state; the window is then hidden.
specs.trigger: F key while the list is open, the window's close button, the internal toggle at 0x44AA62, or a forced close while the list is open: in the S2C 0x08/0x5E/0xA3/0xA4 map-load block at 0x450A05, or in the S2C 0x2F handler at 0x450BD0. Live capture: closing the F ARENA list -> 0x2D with 0 bytes.
specs.expected_response: none (the server must not reply; the server notes say a reply froze the client)
specs.gates_and_hazards: The only condition is FUN_004837C0(0x2A) != 1; the close path has no map-mode gate. Windows start in state 1 (0x48255E), so an auto-close only emits 0x2D if the arena list is currently open. If the player has the F list open when a map change (S2C 0x08) or S2C 0x2F arrives, the server receives an unsolicited 0x2D and must simply consume it.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree on the wire (opcode-only; PUSH 0x2D at 0x446748, JMP to the shared tail at 0x446A7F, Add at 0x446A85, Send(1) at 0x446A93 on [0x70E6F4]) and on the close-switch routing (decoded tables: id 0x2A -> byte 1 -> 0x446748; no other id maps there). The canonical grammar is empty (""), not "stop". The substantive difference is trigger coverage. B is right and A missed that the S2C 0x08 map-load block also force-closes window 0x2A: 0x4508FC sets EBX=1, every path from 0x4508AC reaches 0x450A01 PUSH EBX / PUSH EBX / PUSH 0x2A / CALL FUN_00483430 at 0x450A05, and FUN_00483430 calls FUN_00446300(id,0,arg2=1,0,1). That block is also entered for S2C 0x5E, 0xA3 and 0xA4 (they fall into 0x4508AC). Both correctly cite the 0x2F close at 0x450BD0. B's open question is resolved: windows start in state 1 (FUN_004824D0 at 0x48255E), so these auto-closes do NOT emit 0x2D on every map load, only when the arena list is open. Other references: matches the live capture (close F list -> 0x2D). Our server (line 655) consumes 0x2D but labels it 'scene-finalize / map-ready ack'. Consuming is correct; the label is wrong for this site.
open_questions: If the server really sees 0x2D after every map load without the F list open, another C2S 0x2D producer must exist outside this batch (e.g. a register-supplied opcode). This site alone cannot explain it, given the initial window state of 1.

specs.name: DeathReviveRequest

locations.role: control id == 0 -> ignore (the only check before per-window dispatch)
S2C 0x3E: local entity ([game+0x4CC]+0x970)+0x94C = 0xD, FUN_00483430(0x79,4,1) shows window 0x79
the only other writer of +0x94C = 0xD, next to the dying flag +0x1388 = 1 and level-based exp-penalty math (table 0x6F0EAC), so state 0xD = dead
S2C 0x08 map load hides window 0x79 when not in arena

specs.semantics: Bare opcode, no body. It is sent when any control on window 0x79 is clicked. S2C 0x3E opens that window and puts the local player into motion state 0xD. State 0xD is the death state: FUN_0041A230 sets it together with the dying flag and the exp-loss calculation. So window 0x79 is the death dialog and 0x2E asks the server to revive or return the player. The handler never checks which control was clicked, so every button sends the same packet.
specs.trigger: Clicking any nonzero control on window 0x79 (the death dialog opened by S2C 0x3E).
specs.expected_response: Probably a map (re)load: S2C 0x08 hides window 0x79 outside arenas, then the spawn/enter sequence. Not verified for EN. This is a different packet from the S2C 0x2E map/channel enter. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, combat_skill#21): the client sends this the moment the death dialog's only button is clicked and closes the dialog itself, so the server MUST answer with the revive sequence (HP via S2C 0x28/0x44 plus the map-enter sequence S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07) - otherwise the player stays dead with no UI and no way to retry.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No client-side gate beyond control id != 0. The handler ignores the control id, so a multi-button dialog cannot tell the server which choice was made. Window 0x79 stays open until the server sends something that hides it (S2C 0x08 outside arena), so the player can click repeatedly and send duplicates.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the body is empty. Add(u8 0x2E) at 0x44A67C goes directly to JMP 0x4484C4 and Send(1), with no other Add. A's grammar "" and B's "stop" both mean zero bytes. The correct grammar is empty (length 0). On naming: A's 'revive request' is supported by more evidence than B's generic 'Window79Confirm'. The value S2C 0x3E writes (+0x94C = 0xD) is also written by FUN_0041A230 @0x41A283, right next to the dying flag (+0x1388 = 1) and the per-level exp-penalty code, so 0x79 is the death dialog. A's cross-reference 'PySlayer answers respawn with S2C 0x2E' is for the other direction and a newer KR build; do not assume a server reply opcode from it. Our server has no C2S 0x2E branch in _dispatch.
open_questions: Whether the server should revive in place or send the player to town. The client sends no choice.
Which S2C sequence the original server sent in reply (0x08 map reload is the most likely, since it hides window 0x79).

spec_errata.old: expected_response was "probably a map (re)load, not verified"
spec_errata.new: the server must answer or the player is stuck dead

spec_errata.old: medium
spec_errata.new: high (byte-exact live capture: 0-byte payload from window 0x79)

specs.name: MessengerFriendListRequest
specs.socket: game: CSNSocket* at CMessenger(app[+0x4E4])+0x74. FUN_0046f860 copies g_sock_game [0x70E6F4] there (0x46F934), so it is the same TCP 7022 socket.

locations.role: S2C 0x03 handler entry (character/world info + map load); the send is at its tail
calls FUN_0046f860(messenger), which resets messenger state and sets messenger+0x74 = g_sock_game
MOV [messenger+0x74], g_sock_game; only if messenger+0x70 (ui root), messenger+0x68 (app) and g_sock_game are all non-null
S2C 0x0B friend-list handler on the same messenger object (likely reply)

specs.semantics: Opcode-only request from the messenger (friend list) subsystem. Earlier in the same S2C 0x03 handler, FUN_0046f860 re-initializes CMessenger: it clears the friend-list state and copies the local name from player+0x48+0x1BE and fields +0x1D8/+0x1CF. At the end of the handler, after the map is loaded, the UI is refreshed and timers 6 (240000 ms) and 0xB (7000 ms) are armed, the client sends a bare 0x2F on the messenger's socket (the game socket). Nothing is Added before or after the opcode. The only other Add(0x2F) in the binary is this one. It is fire-and-forget: the client does not wait for a reply before continuing to the 0x63 send.
specs.trigger: Automatic, at the end of every S2C 0x03 (world/map info) handler, i.e. after each map load, both on entering the world and on map change. Always immediately followed by C2S 0x63.
specs.expected_response: Probably S2C 0x0B friend list, handled in SubHandler3 on the messenger object and read through messenger+0x74: u8 unk (messenger+0xD1), u8 count, repeat(count){ str[17] name, u8 unk, u32 unk, u8 state }. The client does not require a reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sent only if [app+0x4E4]+0x74 != 0, i.e. FUN_0046f860 found a UI root, an app pointer and g_sock_game. app+0x4E4 itself is dereferenced without a null check here and at 0x44E52F, so it must exist (allocated at app init). Because this runs on every 0x03, a server that answers 0x2F with a friend list resends that list on every map change.
specs.references: The live capture shows 0x2F with 0 bytes sent right after a map loads, which agrees. windslayer_server.py _dispatch consumes 0x2F with the log 'arena query — ignoring'. That label is WRONG: the packet comes from CMessenger (friend list), not the arena. The arena room list is C2S 0x2C/0x2D. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x2F.py is an unrelated S2C 0x2F (the same number means something else in the other direction); PySlayer has no C2S 0x2F parser. Our server comment 'no heartbeats arrived after 0x2F+0x63' matches the send order.
open_questions: Name is inferred from the owning object (CMessenger, whose S2C handlers 0x0B-0x10/0x60-0x62/0x78/0x7A-0x7E carry friend-list, 1:1 chat and mentor strings); no UI string names 0x2F directly. Friend list vs. full messenger sync (friends + mentor) is not proven.
Whether the original server answered with 0x0B, and whether other messenger packets (e.g. 0x7B mentor info) also followed, is unknown.
blind_open_questions: Confirm that S2C 0x0B is the reply the server should send (the client does not wait for or require one; no reply appears harmless in live play).
Exact meanings of the u8/u32/u8 fields in each S2C 0x0B friend entry.

specs.name: FriendAddRequest

locations.role: checks the gates, builds and sends; ECX=name pointer, stack arg=target uid, ESI=messenger

locations.function: FUN_00446300 (UI event dispatcher), window 0x50 player popup, button 7
locations.role: caller: name = popup element 2 text (+0x50), u32 = window 0x50 +0x134 (clicked entity's uid, copied from entity+0x84 at 0x44C7D7)
caller: name = dialog 0x179 element 5 edit text (FUN_0048a030), u32 pushed as 0 at 0x472F8E; requires strlen >= 1

specs.grammar:
u32 target_uid
str[17] target_name

fields.name: target_uid
fields.dest_or_source: stack arg ([ESP+0x90]): the popup window 0x50 +0x134 (uid from entity+0x84) when using the player right-click menu; 0 when the name was typed into the add-friend dialog 0x179
fields.meaning: character uid of the player to befriend, or 0 when unknown (the server must then resolve by name)

fields.name: target_name
fields.dest_or_source: ECX/EDI name pointer: popup text buffer (+0x50) or edit box text; exactly 17 bytes copied
fields.meaning: character name of the player to befriend, NUL-terminated. Bytes after the NUL are whatever the UI buffer held, so they may not be zero

specs.semantics: Asks the server to send a friend request to another character. After sending, the client prints "Requesting <name> to be a friend" (0xFF00C800) in the system chat. It does not add the friend locally.
specs.trigger: Player right-click popup (window 0x50) button 7 'add friend', or messenger window 0x176 button 8, which opens the name-entry dialog 0x179; its OK button sends
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x0C (friend add result, handler 0x470A37): u8 result; if result is 1 or 0x0B: str[17] name, u8 channel, u32 friend_uid, u8 state, then the entry is added to the list with "<name> has been registered in your friend list."; otherwise: str[17] name and an error dialog chosen by code (2 not online, 3 refused, 4 friend function off, 5 target list full, 6 already in list, 7 your list full, 0x15 generic error). The target receives S2C 0x0D (u32 requester_id, str[17] requester_name), which opens dialog 0x17C, and answers with C2S 0x31 {u32 id, str[17] name, u8 accept} (FUN_004701e0).
specs.gates_and_hazards: messenger+0x74 socket not NULL and name pointer not NULL; name must differ from own name (messenger+0x7C, strcmp), otherwise "You can't register yourself."; name must not already be in the friend list (FUN_00472180), otherwise "The player is already registered as friend."; friend count (messenger+0xD0) must not equal max slots (messenger+0xD1, from S2C 0x0B), otherwise "Can't be add.\r\n\r\nVisit Frenaiga." In the popup path the messenger (main+0x4E4) must exist. The dialog-0x179 path rejects an empty name with "Please enter a character name."
specs.references: Not in PySlayer, memory notes or our server (no 0x30 branch in _dispatch). Partner packets in the same class: C2S 0x31 answer (FUN_004701e0), S2C 0x0B/0x0C/0x0D/0x0E friend handlers in SubHandler3 0x4708C0.
open_questions: Unconfirmed whether the original server used target_uid or target_name as the key (uid is 0 for the typed-name path, so name lookup must be supported).
The text of button 7 in window 0x50 was not tied to a string; 'add friend' is inferred from the called function and its messages.
blind_open_questions: Does the server key on target_id or target_name? The dialog path always sends id 0, so the name must be enough.
Max length of the dialog edit control is unknown; a 17+ character name would leave no NUL inside the 17 bytes.
The S2C 0x0C/0x0D pairing as the response is inferred from handler strings, not traced from this send.

specs.name: FriendRequestReply

locations.role: builder (ESI=CMessenger; stack args: requester_id, name ptr, accept flag)
S2C 0x0D: opens dialog 0x17c, stores the u32 at dialog+0x134, writes the name into control 2

specs.grammar:
u32 requester_id
str[17] requester_name
u8 accept

fields.name: requester_id
fields.meaning: Id of the player who sent the friend request. It echoes the u32 from S2C 0x0D.
fields.dest_or_source: dialog 0x17c +0x134 (stored by the S2C 0x0D handler at 0x470D00)

fields.name: requester_name
fields.meaning: Requester's character name, NUL-padded. It is copied from the text buffer of control 2 of dialog 0x17c, which FUN_004838c0 memsets 0x81 bytes and then strcpy's from S2C 0x0D's name.

fields.name: accept
fields.meaning: 1 = accept the friend request (button 4). 0 = refuse (button 5) or close (button 6).
fields.dest_or_source: constant pushed by the caller (1 at 0x4730C1, 0 at 0x4730EC)

specs.semantics: The player answers a 'Request of Friend Addition' popup (dialog 0x17c) that the server opened with S2C 0x0D (u32 requester_id, str[17] requester_name). It tells the server whether the player accepts becoming friends with the requester.
specs.trigger: Clicking button 4 (accept) or button 5/6 (refuse/close) of dialog 0x17c ('Request of Friend Addition').
specs.expected_response: Inferred, not proven: S2C 0x0C to the original requester, either result 1/0x0B + friend entry (str[17] name, u8 channel, u32 id, u8 status) meaning 'has been registered in your friend list', or result 3 + str[17] name meaning 'has refused to register you as a friend'. The accepting player probably also gets S2C 0x0C result 1 with the requester's entry.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only sent when param_3 (button) is 4..6, FUN_004830f0 finds dialog 0x17c, CMessenger socket != NULL, and control 2 of dialog 0x17c exists (a NULL name pointer means no send). No local state change in the builder.
specs.references: The companion C2S 0x30 (FUN_0046fe30: u32 + str[17] target) sends the original request. S2C 0x0C result strings in SubHandler3 give the meaning. EN lng 2721 'Request#of#Friend#Addition', 2724 'Comment#on#Addition#Request'. PySlayer has no C2S parser. Our server has no handler.
open_questions: Is requester_id a character id, an account id or a session id? The client only echoes it (the C2S 0x30 request sends 0 in that slot from the 0x179 dialog).
Does button 6 really mean close/X? Buttons 5 and 6 both send accept=0; the exact UI roles are not verified.
blind_open_questions: What the u32 means (requester char id vs. a request serial): the client just sends back whatever S2C 0x0D gave it.
Which of controls 5/6 is 'No' and which is the close [X]; both send accept=0.

specs.name: FriendDelete
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game via CMessenger+0x74; messenger+0x74 is loaded from [0x70E6F4] at 0x46F86A and stored at 0x46F934 by FUN_0046f860 on S2C 0x03; ECX=[ESI+0x74] before every Add/Send in the builder)

locations.role: Builder with a custom calling convention: ESI = CMessenger ([game_state+0x4E4]), EDI = friend name pointer, [ESP+4] = friend_id (u32), RET 4. Gate: [ESI+0x74] != NULL (0x46FFE3) and EDI != NULL (0x46FFE7); otherwise it returns without sending.
MOV EAX,[ESP+4] / PUSH EAX / CALL [0x4A40F0] Add(unsigned int): u32 friend_id
PUSH 0x11 / PUSH EDI / CALL [0x4A40EC] Add(char*,17): exactly 17 name bytes

Tail call. MOV [ESP+4],1 at 0x470010 overwrites the caller's argument slot with 1, then JMP [0x4A4108] runs CSNSocket::Send(1) on ECX=[ESI+0x74]. Send's RET 4 returns straight to the caller at 0x473042 and pops the slot. This is the only JMP into any Fireway IAT slot in the binary.

locations.function: FUN_00472900 (messenger UI handler), window 0x17A case at 0x472FEB, button param_3==2
locations.role: Only caller. 0x472FFF: FUN_004830f0(ui_root=[messenger+0x70], id 0x17A) gets the dialog, saved at [ESP+0xC]. 0x473015: FUN_00483120(window 0x17A, control 4) gets the control; EDI = control+0x50 (text buffer), or 0 if the control is missing. If the dialog is NULL it jumps to 0x473364 ('Please select a character name. ') and sends nothing. Otherwise it pushes [dialog+0x134], sets ESI=EBX=messenger and calls the builder. Afterwards (0x473042-0x473062) it sets [ui_root+0x5A4]=1 and calls FUN_00446300(0x17A,0,1,0,1) to close the dialog, even if the builder skipped the send.

locations.function: FUN_00472900, window 0x176 (friend list) button 9 (jump table 0x473724 index 2)
locations.role: Prepares the confirm dialog. If window 0x176 +0xEC (selected row, 1-based) == 0: 'Please select a character name. ' and dialog 0x17A is closed (0x472B08 -> 0x473055). Otherwise FUN_00459fd0(list window+0xAC, index-1) returns the friend node (EDI).
The only code that writes dialog 0x17A +0x134: [dialog+0x134] = friend_node+0x18 (friend_id from S2C 0x0B/0x0C)
FUN_004838c0(window EAX=0x17A, control 4, EDI=friend_node): memsets control+0x50 to 0 for 0x81 bytes, then strcpy's friend_node+0x00 (name) into it
Generic route: FUN_00472900([game_state+0x4E4] messenger, window id, button id) when FUN_004773c0 does not consume the event
Handler for the response S2C 0x0E FriendDeleteResult

specs.grammar:
u32 friend_id
str[17] friend_name

fields.name: friend_id
fields.dest_or_source: Dialog 0x17A +0x134. Written at 0x472B46 from friend_node+0x18, the friend_id the server sent in S2C 0x0B (friend list) or 0x0C (friend added).
fields.meaning: Server id of the friend to remove, echoed exactly as the server gave it. The same field is used by C2S 0x33 chat invite and matched by S2C 0x60 status updates.

fields.name: friend_name
fields.dest_or_source: Text buffer (+0x50) of control 4 of dialog 0x17A. FUN_004838c0 at 0x472B56 zeroes 0x81 bytes, then copies friend_node+0x00 (the 17-byte name from S2C 0x0B/0x0C, stored in a zeroed 0x28-byte node).
fields.meaning: Character name of the friend to remove, NUL-terminated and zero-padded to 17 bytes. Stale bytes are not possible on the normal path because the buffer is memset first.

specs.semantics: Asks the server to remove a friend from the player's friend list. The client changes nothing locally when it sends: the list node, the count (messenger+0xD0) and the '(count/capacity)' label only change when S2C 0x0E arrives. The body is fixed at 22 bytes: 0x32, u32 friend_id (LE), 17 name bytes. There is no ResetBuffer call; the packet is built with Add calls and flushed with Send(1), like the other messenger sends (0x30/0x31/0x33/0x34/0x5C). Flow: the player selects a row in the friend list window 0x176 and clicks button 9. The UI script opens confirm dialog 0x17A; the code copies the selected node's friend_id into dialog+0x134 and its name into control 4. Clicking button 2 (OK) of dialog 0x17A sends this packet and closes the dialog.
specs.trigger: Friend list window 0x176 ('My Friends'): select a friend, click button 9 (Delete). Then click button 2 (OK/Yes) in confirm dialog 0x17A, which probably uses UILng 8001 'Would you like to delete the character from your Friend List?' and 8002 'Name of Friend's' (inferred). This is the only trigger: FUN_0046ffe0 has one caller (0x47303D), and window id 0x17A appears only in FUN_00472900.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x0E FriendDeleteResult (handler 0x470D35): u8 success, str[17] name. If success != 0: popup '<name> is deleted from friend list.', then FUN_004721e0 unlinks every friend node whose name exactly matches (strcmp) and redraws window 0x176 and the (count/capacity) label. If success == 0: popup 'Deleting <name> from your friend list failed. Please again in a few minutes.' The server should echo friend_name byte-exactly, because removal is by name, not by friend_id.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Send-time gates, in order: (1) dialog 0x17A must be found in the ui_root+0x5C0 window list; otherwise 'Please select a character name. ' and no send. (2) messenger+0x74 must be non-NULL; it is NULL until the first S2C 0x03. (3) Control 4 of dialog 0x17A must exist (EDI != NULL). If (2) or (3) fails, nothing is sent and there is no message, but the dialog still closes. Nothing checks that friend_id is non-zero or that the name is still in the list. Open-time gates (button 9 of 0x176): a row must be selected (+0xEC != 0), otherwise the message is shown and 0x17A is closed. HAZARD: if FUN_00459fd0 returns NULL or dialog 0x17A is not found, +0x134 and control 4 are not refreshed, so OK would send whatever an earlier use left there. The code does not reset them. In the mentor tab (FUN_00470270 else-branch), buttons 8 and 9 of window 0x176 are put in state 3 (FUN_00489320(0x176,9,3)), which probably disables them, so deletion should only be reachable from the friend tab.
specs.references: PROTOCOL.md S2C 0x0B/0x0C (friend_id source) and S2C 0x0E (FriendDeleteResult: 'Reply to C2S 0x32 (delete friend: u32 friend_id, str[17] name), sent from the delete-confirm dialog 0x17A'), which matches this derivation. Sibling messenger sends in the same class with the same register convention: 0x46FF17/0x30 FriendAddRequest, 0x470224/0x31, 0x470084/0x33, 0x47025F/0x34, 0x46FFD8/0x5C (FUN_0046ff70, the function right before, ESI/EDI convention). Missing from protocol_spec.json because the Ghidra scout only annotated plain CALL [0x4A4108] sites and this one is a tail JMP. PySlayer: server_packets/__init__.py imports opcode_0x32 inside try/except but the file does not exist; there is no C2S parser. Our server (windslayer_server.py, wsproto.py) has no 0x32 handling and no friend system. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C43, social_friend#06): captured live byte for byte - payload 21 B "02 00 00 00 42 6F 62 00*14" = u32 friend_id (2) followed by str[17] "Bob", exactly the grammar above. (This spec was missing from the earlier protocol_spec.json snapshot that the verification matrix was written against; it is present and correct in this corpus.)
open_questions: Whether the original server keyed the deletion on friend_id or friend_name (the client sends both; the S2C 0x0E reply removes by name only).

The mapping of window 0x17A and button 9 to UILng strings 8001/8002 ('delete from Friend List') is inferred from lng ordering (0x17C->8006, 0x17D->8007) and the S2C 0x0E strings, not from a parsed UI definition file.
Whether FUN_00489320 state 3 really disables button 9 in the mentor tab. If not, a selected mentor record (+0x18/+0x00) would be sent in the same 0x32 layout.
Whether the other 0x17A buttons (cancel/close) are handled only by the UI script: FUN_00472900 ignores every param_3 except 2 for window 0x17A.
blind_open_questions: How dialog 0x17A becomes visible is data-driven. No .text or .data immediate references window id 0x17A outside FUN_00472900 (the other 0x17A imm32 hits are branch displacements). The inference comes from FUN_00446300 opening the control's link window before dispatch, plus the no-selection path immediately hiding 0x17A. The confirm dialog's text is not in the exe strings.

The earlier handlers in the FUN_00446300 generic chain (FUN_00469090 when main+0xD64 is set, FUN_004773c0 when main+0xD30 is set) are assumed to return 0 for window 0x17A ctrl 2, so FUN_00472900 is reached. Not traced in full.
The server-side meaning of friend_id (character DB id vs session id) is whatever the server put in S2C 0x0B/0x0C. The client sends both id and name, and the reply removal is by name only.

spec_errata.old: spec reported missing by the matrix / no live capture
spec_errata.new: present and live-confirmed at 21 bytes

specs.name: MessengerChatInvite

locations.role: builds and sends; ECX=name pointer, stack arg=target uid, EDI=messenger
caller: name = popup element 2 text (+0x50), u32 = window 0x50 +0x134 (clicked entity uid)

caller: selected friend record (FUN_00459fd0); name = record+0x00, u32 = record+0x18; refuses if record+0x20 == 1 ("is not on line.") or if the room window 0x177 is open with 10 or more members (+0xC8)
caller: name = dialog 0x178 element 4 edit text (+0xD1), u32 pushed as 0

specs.grammar:
u32 target_uid
str[17] target_name

fields.name: target_uid
fields.dest_or_source: stack arg ([ESP+0x94]): popup window 0x50 +0x134 (entity uid), friend_record+0x18 (friend uid), or 0 when typed in dialog 0x178
fields.meaning: character uid of the player being invited, or 0 when only the name is known

fields.name: target_name
fields.dest_or_source: ECX/ESI name pointer (popup text, friend record name, or edit box); exactly 17 bytes copied
fields.meaning: character name of the player being invited to the messenger chat room (NUL-terminated)

specs.semantics: Invites a player into the messenger conversation (chat room window 0x177). After sending, the client prints "Inviting <name> for a conversation.": inside the chat room window (FUN_00472430, color 0xFF00A2A2) if window 0x177 is open, otherwise in the system chat (0xFF00C800). The room id is not sent, so the server must track which room (if any) the inviter is in.
specs.trigger: Player right-click popup (window 0x50) button 8; messenger window 0x176 button 7 with a friend selected; or, with no friend selected, the chat room flow opens the name dialog 0x178, whose OK button sends
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x0F to the inviter (handler 0x470E31): u8 result; if 1: u32 room_id (stored in messenger+0xCC), u8 member_count, repeat(member_count) str[17] member_name, then the chat room window 0x177 opens; otherwise str[17] name and an error by code (2, 3 refused personal chat, 4 rejecting chat, 5 room full, 6 in conversation with another player, 8 not online). The invitee receives S2C 0x10 (u32 id, str[17] inviter_name), which opens dialog 0x17D only if its messenger+0xCC == 0, and answers with C2S 0x34 {u32 id, u8 accept} (FUN_00470230).
specs.gates_and_hazards: messenger+0x74 not NULL and name pointer not NULL (the only checks in FUN_00470030). Callers: the friend-list path blocks offline friends (state 1) and rooms with 10 or more members ("You cannot invite more players.\r\nThe chatting room is full."). The dialog-0x178 path only checks that the edit element exists, NOT that the text is non-empty, so a 17-byte all-zero name can be sent. There is no self-invite check.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer, memory notes or our server (the 0x33 in windslayer_server.py is an unrelated S2C arena note in _handle_room_query). Companion C2S 0x34 answer at FUN_00470230; S2C 0x0F/0x10/0x61/0x62 room handlers in SubHandler3.
open_questions: Unconfirmed whether the u32 in S2C 0x10 (echoed back in C2S 0x34) is the room id or the inviter id.
The exact message for S2C 0x0F code 2 is at DAT_006F4CD0 and was not decoded.
blind_open_questions: Is S2C 0x0F/0x10 the response pair? This is inferred from the handler strings and window ids, not traced.
Is target_id 0 (dialog path) resolved server-side by name? Is the friend id the same as entity uid?
Max edit-control length for dialog 0x178 is unknown.

specs.name: ChatInviteReply

locations.role: builder (ESI=CMessenger; stack args: inviter_id, accept flag)
caller: dialog 0x17d button 4, accept = EDI = 1 (set at 0x472928)
S2C 0x10: opens dialog 0x17d (only if CMessenger+0xcc==0) and stores the u32 at dialog+0x134

specs.grammar:
u32 inviter_id
u8 accept

fields.name: inviter_id
fields.meaning: Id of the player who invited this player to a messenger conversation. It echoes the u32 from S2C 0x10.
fields.dest_or_source: dialog 0x17d +0x134 (stored by the S2C 0x10 handler at 0x4711E5)

fields.name: accept
fields.meaning: 1 = accept the conversation invite (button 4). 0 = refuse (button 5) or close (button 6).

specs.semantics: The player answers a 'Request to Conversate' popup (dialog 0x17d) that the server opened with S2C 0x10 (u32 inviter_id, str[17] inviter_name). On accept the server should put the player into the inviter's messenger chat room.
specs.trigger: Clicking button 4 (accept) or button 5/6 (refuse/close) of dialog 0x17d ('Request to Conversate').
specs.expected_response: Inferred: on accept, S2C 0x0F with u8 result=1, u32 room_id (stored at CMessenger+0xcc), u8 member_count, then repeat(member_count) str[17] member_name, sent to the joiner (opens window 0x177) and probably to the other members. On refuse, S2C 0x0F to the inviter with result=3 + str[17] name ('has refused to have a personal chat').
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only sent when param_3 (button) is 4..6, dialog 0x17d is found, and CMessenger socket != NULL. The S2C 0x10 invite is silently dropped (no dialog) when the client is already in a room (CMessenger+0xcc != 0).
specs.references: The companion C2S 0x33 (FUN_00470030: u32 friend_id + str[17] name, prints 'Inviting <name> for a conversation.') sends the invite. S2C 0x0F results: 2 = ?, 3 = refused personal chat, 4 = rejecting chatting, 5 = room full, 6 = in conversation with another player, 8 = not online. EN lng 2729 'Ruquest#to#Conversate'. PySlayer has no C2S parser. Our server has no handler.
open_questions: Is inviter_id a character id or a server session id? The client only echoes it; C2S 0x33 fills it from the friend entry +0x18 (the u32 id the server gave in S2C 0x0B/0x0C).
Does the inviter also receive S2C 0x0F result=1 with the full member list, or a different join notice?
blind_open_questions: Whether the u32 is the inviter's character id or a server room id; the client just echoes the S2C 0x10 value.
The accept response format (S2C 0x0F) is taken from a quick look at the handler and is not fully specified here.

specs.name: MessengerRoomChat
specs.socket: game (CMessenger+0x74, which FUN_0046f860 copies from g_sock_game [0x70E6F4] while handling S2C 0x03 at 0x44E52F; the constructor FUN_0046f670 sets it to 0)

locations.role: builder: checks, adds the opcode, length and text, then calls Send
caller: the Enter/IME result in the messenger chat window 0x177 (reached from FUN_00487db0 at 0x488E8E when window 0x177 is open and CIME::IsStringResult is true)
caller: chat-macro hotkey (12 key slots at +0xe58, macro text slots of 0x25 bytes at +0xe88) while the focused window is 0x177
S2C 0x61: the matching room-chat broadcast the client displays

specs.grammar:
u8 text_len
str[text_len] text
specs.length: 1 + text_len (text_len = strlen(text) & 0xFF; no NUL is sent)

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: Length of the chat text in bytes. It is the low byte of the strlen the caller passes (param_2); Add(uchar) pushes EBX, so only BL is sent.
fields.dest_or_source: caller's strlen of the text. From FUN_00444a30 it is strlen(CIME+0x104). From FUN_0043db00 it is strlen of the macro slot (player+0xe88+idx*0x25, at most 36).

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Chat text for the messenger chat room. Exactly text_len raw bytes with no terminator (Add(char*,N) with N = movzx BL at 0x470177).
fields.dest_or_source: CIME result string (DAT_0070e708+0x104) or the macro text slot

specs.semantics: Sends one line of chat into the messenger/friend conversation room the player is currently in (room id held at CMessenger+0xcc). The client does NOT show its own line locally. It waits for the server's S2C 0x61 relay, which prints "<name> : " and "  text" in window 0x177. The line is colored 0xffc766a6 when the name equals the player's own name (CMessenger+0x7c), otherwise 0xff3277cc.
specs.trigger: The player presses Enter with text in the messenger chat window (UI 0x177, 'Messenger Window'), or presses a chat-macro hotkey while window 0x177 is the focused window (g_ui_root+8 == 0x177) and that window's state (+0x3c) != 1. Otherwise the macro goes to normal chat through FUN_00444a90.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x61 to every member of the room, the sender included: str[17] sender_name, u8 len, str[len] text. It is only processed while CMessenger+0xcc (room_id) != 0.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No send when: CMessenger socket (+0x74) is NULL, the text pointer is NULL, or CMessenger+0xcc (room_id, set by S2C 0x0F result=1) == 0. Also no send when ENGINE.DLL Curse_Engine_Clean(text) returns false; the client then prints 'No cursing please' (color 0xfffdf34c) to the chat log. After the IME path the client calls CIME::ResetResultString and memsets player+0x14d8 (0x3d bytes). HAZARD for the relay: the S2C 0x61 handler reads len bytes into a 64-byte stack buffer and then sprintf_s("  %s") into a 0x3d (61) byte buffer. The server must relay len <= 58, otherwise sprintf_s hits the invalid-parameter handler (client abort), and len >= 64 also leaves the text unterminated.
specs.references: Same shape as the normal chat C2S 0x03 capture ("02 68 69" = u8 len + text), but scoped to the messenger room. PySlayer has no C2S parser for 0x35. Our server's _dispatch has no 0x35 branch. The UI string 2675 'Messenger Window' names window 0x177.
open_questions: What maximum length does the IME impose on the 0x177 input box? The client-side buffer at player+0x14d8 is 0x3d bytes, which suggests <= 60 chars, but this was not verified.
Does the server echo S2C 0x61 back to the sender? The client never echoes locally, so it must, or the sender never sees their own line.
blind_open_questions: Curse_Engine_Clean(char*) may rewrite the buffer in place before the bytes are added; it is not clear whether the wire text is the original or the filtered one.
Longest possible IME result string: the input buffer app+0x14D8 is 0x3D bytes, which suggests at most 60 characters, but this was not verified from the IME side.
It is not confirmed that the server sends S2C 0x61 back to the sender as well as the other members (the client never adds its own line locally at the send site).

specs.name: MessengerChatRoomLeave
specs.socket: game. The socket is CMessenger+0x74, a cached copy of g_sock_game [0x70E6F4]. It is loaded at 0x46F86A and stored at 0x46F934 in FUN_0046f860, which the S2C 0x03 handler calls at 0x44E52F.

locations.role: Window-state switch 0x4463F8 (table 0x44B848), state param [EBP+0x10]==1 (hide/close). FUN_004837c0 checks the current state and skips everything if it is already 1.
Window id check: EBX==0x177 jumps to 0x446925.
Walks the g_ui_root window list (+0x5C0) for id 0x177. If it is missing, the function returns at 0x4727CA and nothing is sent.
Frees the window's two linked lists (+0xB0/+0xB4/+0xB8 and +0xC0/+0xC4/+0xC8). EBX is reloaded from the arg at 0x472857.

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Tells the server that the local player left the messenger chatting room. The packet is only the opcode. When window 0x177 (the chatting-room window) changes to state 1 (hidden), the client frees that window's two local lists: chat lines at +0xB0 and participants at +0xC0, whose count at +0xC8 is checked against 10 in 'The chatting room is full'. It then zeroes CMessenger+0xCC, the room id that S2C 0x0F wrote at 0x470E60 when result==1, and sends 0x36. No room id goes on the wire, so the server has to track which room the session is in. Once +0xCC is 0, the client ignores the S2C room messages 0x61 and 0x62, which check +0xCC!=0 at 0x47132D and 0x47121A.
specs.trigger: Any close or hide of window 0x177 (FUN_00446300(0x177, ctrl, state=1, ...)) while it is not already hidden, for example when the user closes the chat room window.
specs.expected_response: None. The client does not wait for a reply and clears its room state before sending. The server may want to tell the other room members; which S2C does that was not traced.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No send if window 0x177 does not exist. No send if CMessenger+0x74 is NULL (S2C 0x03 not handled yet). No ResetBuffer before the Add. The packet is sent even if the player never joined a room, because only the window's visibility matters. The server must accept 0x36 from a player who is in no room.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts found the same wire format: the opcode byte only, built by FUN_00472790 with Add(u8 0x36) at 0x4728DA and Send(1) at 0x4728E5 on CMessenger+0x74. The only disagreement was notation: A wrote the grammar as '(empty - opcode byte only)' and B wrote 'stop'. The asm shows no other Add between the window lookup and Send, and no ResetBuffer or AddToHead. The caller path is confirmed: state switch table 0x44B848 entry 1 is 0x4466DF, then EBX==0x177 leads to 0x446925 and the call at 0x446930. Both are right on content. B's 'stop' is used because it is valid DSL for a zero-byte body. A's extra detail is also verified: S2C 0x0F stores a u32 room id at +0xCC (0x470E58/0x470E60), and this packet zeroes it. The packet is not in PySlayer client_packets, the windslayer_server.py _dispatch, or the captures.
open_questions: Which S2C (if any) a server should broadcast to the remaining room members on leave; 0x61/0x62 are room-gated handlers but were not decoded here.

specs.grammar: u8 status

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: The player's own messenger presence status. Control 0x17 sends 0 (default after login, most likely 'Online'). Control 0x18 sends 3 and control 0x19 sends 2 (by UI string order 2666 Online / 2667 Away / 2668 Busy, these are most likely 3=Away and 2=Busy).
fields.dest_or_source: EDI, which the caller computes from the clicked control id in messenger window 0x176 (0x17->0, 0x18->3, 0x19->2); also stored in CMessenger+0x9c

specs.semantics: The player picks a new presence status from the 'Status Change' dropdown in the messenger (friend list) window. The client sets the dropdown label (control 10) to the chosen option's text, stores the value in CMessenger+0x9c, and sends it only if it differs from the previous value. The server should save it and tell the player's friends (the friend-list entry status byte at +0x20 is carried by S2C 0x0B/0x0C/0x60).
specs.trigger: Clicking option control 0x17, 0x18 or 0x19 of window 0x176 (messenger / friend list, 'Status Change'). UI dispatch goes through FUN_00446300 into FUN_00472900(CMessenger, 0x176, ctrl).
specs.expected_response: Nothing is required by the sender. The client has already updated its UI and state. The server most likely pushes S2C 0x60 (u32 friend_id, str[17] name, u8 channel, u8 status) to online friends.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No send if the new status equals CMessenger+0x9c. The value is stored before the socket NULL check, so with a NULL socket the change is remembered but never sent. CMessenger+0x9c is reset to 0 each time S2C 0x03 is handled, so after each (re)entry the client believes it is status 0.
specs.references: PySlayer has no C2S parser. Our server has no 0x37 handler (a comment in windslayer_server.py about 0x37 refers to an unrelated sound id). EN UILngKo.lng: 2663 'Status#Change', 2666 'Online', 2668 'Busy'; KR lng 2666 온라인 (Online), 2667 자리비움 (Away), 2668 다른용무중 (Busy). S2C 0x60 treats friend status 0 as 'has logged in. (Friend)' and 4 as 'logged in (Friend, Channel %d)'; 1 = offline (see FUN_00470270 and the 'not on line' checks).
open_questions: Which of controls 0x17/0x18/0x19 maps to which label (Online/Away/Busy)? The UI layout resource was not decoded. Wire values 0/3/2 are certain; the names are inferred from string order.
Does the server reject friend requests or chat invites when status is 2 or 3 (S2C 0x0C code 4 / 0x0F code 4 'is rejecting chatting' may instead come from the RefuseFriend/RefuseTalk options)?
blind_open_questions: Meaning of status values 0/2/3: the captions of controls 0x17/0x18/0x19 are in UI data, not the exe. Likely something like normal / reject-chat / friend-function-off, but unconfirmed.
Value 1 is never sent from this site; it may be a server-only 'offline' state (friend entries use +0x20 == 1 for 'not on line').

specs.name: BattlefieldInfoRequest

ECX=[this+0xDDC]-[this+0x3EC]; CMP 0x7D0; JC 0x4466C5: skips the send if the unsigned difference is < 2000, but the window still opens
ECX=[0x70E6F4]; PUSH 0x38; CALL [0x4A40FC] Add(uchar): the opcode, and the only Add
[this+0xDDC] = [this+0x364] (tick) - [this+0x410] (baseline, set from timeGetTime in FUN_0042C360 at 0x42C377)
hotkey slot 11 window id [this+0x10B4] (=0x14, set at 0x4298D5) -> FUN_00483800 toggle
S2C 0x63 (u16 + u8) writes '%s(%u/12)' and '<n> Players' into window 0x14: the likely reply

specs.semantics: Opening the Battlefield window (UI window 0x14) asks the server for battlefield status. The body is the opcode byte only. Closing window 0x14 sends nothing: in the close-branch switch at 0x44671D, id 0x14 maps to the no-op 0x4466C5. This is NOT a basic attack.
specs.trigger: T key (hotkey slot 11), an internal UI button (0x44AA83), or any FUN_00446300(0x14, *, 3|4, ...) call. Live capture: T -> 0x38 with 0 bytes.
specs.expected_response: Nothing is awaited. Probably S2C 0x63 (handler 0x4577A8: u16 player count + u8 value, rendered into window 0x14). This is inferred because that handler is the one that fills window 0x14's text.
specs.gates_and_hazards: (1) Not sent if window 0x14 is already in the requested state. (2) Map-mode gate [[game_state+0x4D8]+0x70]==1 blocks both the packet and the window. (3) Timer gate: sent only if (u32)([game_state+0xDDC] - [game_state+0x3EC]) >= 2000. +0xDDC is the ms elapsed since the FUN_0042C360 clock baseline. +0x3EC is written only by the constructor (0x42993C), so this is effectively 'at least 2 s since the clock reset', not a per-send cooldown. If blocked, the window opens without a packet. (4) SERVER HAZARD: windslayer_server.py dispatches 0x38 to _handle_melee (basic attack), so every T press damages a nearby monster. It must be remapped.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree on the wire (opcode-only), socket, gates and throttle. The disputes are grammar notation ("" vs "stop") and the reply (A: likely S2C 0x63; B: undetermined). The asm has one Add: PUSH 0x38 / CALL [0x4A40FC] at 0x446618-0x44661A, then PUSH 1 / CALL [0x4A4108] at 0x446626-0x446628, with ECX=[0x70E6F4] at 0x446612 and 0x446620, and no other Add on the path 0x446447 -> 0x44645B -> 0x4465F1 -> 0x4465FA. The canonical grammar is empty. On the throttle both were partly right and their readings compose: B correctly found the +0xDDC writer (FUN_0042B260 at 0x42B281); A correctly tied the baseline to FUN_0042C360 (+0x410 at 0x42C377). A raw scan finds a single reference to 0x70EDEC (the constructor at 0x42993C), confirming +0x3EC is never updated. A's reply inference is supported: the S2C 0x63 handler at 0x4577A8 reads u16+u8 and writes into window 0x14 (FUN_004838C0 with EAX=0x14 at 0x457811/0x457843). Other references: matches the live capture (T -> 0x38). Contradicts our server's 'BASIC ATTACK' handling (line 648/1635); memory reference_combat_model.md already says the EN basic attack sends no packet.
open_questions: Confirm dynamically that S2C 0x63 is the intended reply.

specs.name: BattlefieldSummonReady

locations.role: when waiting count == 12, sets game_state+0x1200=5 and SetTimer(10, 1000 ms) at 0x4579EA

specs.semantics: Sent when the 5-second 'You will be summoned to the battle field' countdown ends, after the Death Match / Battlefield waiting list reached 12/12. It tells the server the client is ready to be moved into the battlefield. The payload is empty. Right before sending, the client kills timer 10 and changes the countdown text to "Waiting for the server to response."
specs.trigger: S2C 0x20 arrives with its first u8 (players waiting) == 12, and (game_state+0x4D8)->+0x70 != 1 (otherwise the whole 0x20 packet is ignored). The handler shows "%s\r\n(%u/%u)" 'Standing by' (count/12), sets game_state+0x1200 = 5, shows "5sec. You will be summoned to the battle \r\nfield in." and starts timer 10 (1000 ms). Each tick: while +0x1200 > 1 it decrements and redraws "%u"+"sec. You will be summoned...". At the tick where +0x1200 <= 1 it sends 0x3A, about 5 s after the 12/12 packet.
specs.expected_response: Unknown from static analysis. The client shows "Waiting for the server to response.", so it expects a server-driven transition into the battlefield map (probably map-change 0x08 and the usual 0x03/0x07 replay), but the exact opcode was not traced. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with the battlefield enter sequence S2C 0x2F -> 0x2E, or S2C 0x20.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sent once per countdown (the timer is killed before sending). A new S2C 0x20 with count 12 restarts the countdown and triggers another 0x3A. The field game_state+0x1200 is a u32 countdown. Opening the Battlefield window (T key) sends C2S 0x38, which our server currently treats as a basic attack; that is a separate issue. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: the battlefield enter sequence (S2C 0x2F -> 0x2E) or S2C 0x20.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer. Not in our server's _dispatch. Related strings: "Death Match waiting list.", "Standing by", "Not able to do it,\r\nduring waiting to join the battle field.". S2C 0x3A ("Server will be down in 3 minutes") is an unrelated inbound opcode with the same number. Live capture (pvp_arena#11): after S2C 0x20 with waiting_count 12 opened the countdown box, the client sent C2S 0x3A with a 0-byte payload about 5 s later, all by itself, and the box text changed to "Waiting for the server to response." - byte-exact confirmation of the empty body.

specs.semantics: Asks to withdraw one equipment-type item (template+0x154 == 1) from the bank/storage window (dialog 0x1A7) into the inventory. The client sends the full item record: id, count 1, the non-zero option words, and word +0x0C. Non-equipment items take the 0x46A7AF branch instead. That branch opens the amount prompt (dialog 0x1A9) and sends nothing here. Its OK button sends 0x3D with the typed amount from another send path, which this spec does not cover.
specs.trigger: Event 0x25 on dialog 0x1A7. Two sources: slot controls 0x0C..0x24 in FUN_0046cad0 (probably double-click activation), or dragging a bank item onto the inventory window (dialog 9) in FUN_0046c420. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, shop_storage#25): EN button labels - the Bank window's "Search" button (EN translation) is ITEM withdraw (dialog 0x1A9) and "Withdrawal" is GOLD withdraw (dialog 0x1AB).
specs.expected_response: Not determined statically. Presumably a bank-remove plus inventory-add update from the server.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs ctx+0x0C (UI root) != 0 and a valid selected record (FUN_00466980 returns non-null, so item_id != 0 and a template is found). Also needs template+0x1F0 == 0 and template+0x154 == 1. Inventory room check: byte player+0x361 <= 0x2D and FUN_00424d60 finds a zero word among the first N slots at player+0x380. If either fails, it shows the MessageBox "You have no more slots for the item." and sends nothing. The amount is hard-wired to 1, so the server must not trust it for stackables (they never take this path anyway). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. specs.semantics: Sends the player's five privacy 'refuse' toggles so the server can block whisper, exchange, party, personal chat and friend requests. FUN_004741a0 copies pending +0x18..+0x28 into committed +0x2C..+0x3C and sends only if at least one value changed. It then writes the registry and clears the dirty flag.

The same five flags, in the same order, are sent at the start of C2S 0x2B enter-world (0x42F85F..0x42F8AD from game_state+0x500/+0x504/+0x508/+0x510/+0x50C), so the server gets the initial state there. (SubHandler3 0x4708C0).

specs.semantics: Sent when the Item Mall (cash shop) main window, control 0x1CF, receives notification 3. This is almost certainly its close/exit button. The client first hides all Item Mall sub-windows (FUN_0045cc20). It then reports the net result of the session's item moves between two lists of 28-byte cash-item records. List 1 is account cash storage (main+0x700+0x28), filled by S2C 0x6A and appended to by S2C 0x6C purchases and 0x79 gifts. List 2 is the character's cash-item inventory (main+0x700+0x4), filled at login by S2C 0x6F entries with flag==0. S2C 0x6A (mall open) snapshots both lists (+0x48 and +0x58). While the window is open the player moves records between the lists: storage->character via control 0x1FC notification 0xCA, which checks per-category slot limits ('You have no more slots for the item.') and duplicates ('The item is already in your inventory. You can't store it any more.'); character->storage via control 0x1FD notification 0xC9. On close the client sends each list's additions compared to its snapshot, keyed by record+0x00 (u32 serial). Removals are never sent explicitly. The server should treat each list-A serial as 'now in storage' (moved off the character, or a no-op for items bought or gifted this session) and each list-B serial as 'now on character' (moved out of storage). Record layout as the client uses it: +0x00 u32 serial, +0x04 u16 item id, +0x06 u8 kind (0/1/2), +0x08 u16, +0x0A u16, +0x1A u8 (3 = event item). Only the serial goes on the wire.
specs.trigger: The player closes the Item Mall window (control 0x1CF, notification 3). The windows hide even if the socket is null.
specs.expected_response: None awaited: no waiting dialog and no state change that depends on a reply. The temporary vectors are freed right after Send.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Built only if [main+0x700+0x20] != NULL. FUN_0045ae40 sets it during the S2C 0x5A key/login-start handler. SubHandler4 also ignores mall packets unless +0x14 and +0x18 are set there. The opcode Add is inside the null-check, so nothing is appended to the buffer when the socket is null. The snapshots +0x48/+0x58 are rebuilt ONLY by S2C 0x6A, and neither the snapshots nor the live lists are updated after this send. If the window is reopened without a fresh 0x6A and closed again, the same serials are re-sent, so the server must make applying them idempotent. Items bought (0x6C) or gifted (0x79) during the session appear in list A even though they never left storage. A deletion (0x6E) removes a record only from the live storage list, so it produces no serial; only the flag reports it. Counts are i32 while the elements are u32; element pointers are never NULL, so the counts always equal the number of u32 entries that follow.
specs.references: PySlayer has no C2S 0x42 parser. PySlayer's server_packets/opcode_0x42.py is an unrelated S2C builder for the KR build (u32,u32,u16), and S2C 0x42 is not C2S 0x42. Not handled by our windslayer_server.py _dispatch (no 0x42 branch). The Item Mall meaning comes from strings used in FUN_0045f2e0/SubHandler4: 'Item is added to your wish-list.', 'You have no more slots for the item.', 'You failed to delete the item.', 'You are short of cash.', 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash...'.
open_questions: Notification 3 on control 0x1CF is inferred to be the close/exit button, because it hides all mall windows; there is no UI layout file to confirm it
What the server is supposed to do with storage_deleted_flag (possibly a resync hint); it is only set by S2C 0x6E and cleared by 0x6A
Which C2S request opens the mall and makes the server send S2C 0x6A (not in this batch). The correctness of the diff depends on 0x6A being sent on every open.

Which window shows which list (0x1FC vs 0x1FD) does not affect the wire format. List A = account storage (+0x28, from 0x6A) and list B = character cash items (+0x4, from 0x6F flag 0) are inferred from the slot-limit and 'already in your inventory' checks on the storage->character move.
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of the u32 record key (item serial / box slot id) and of the other 24 bytes of the S2C 0x6A record.
How mall+0x04 (the to-inventory vector) gets its initial contents. S2C 0x6A only snapshots it into +0x58 and does not fill it from the packet.
Which S2C packet(s) the server should send back after 0x42.
Which widget sub-control 3 of window 0x1CF is (probably the close/X or OK button).

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Tells the server to delete all stored messenger messages, the 126-byte records that S2C 0x78 adds to the CMessenger+0x34 list. Closing the received-messages window 0x3FE with ctrl 2 or ctrl 9 opens the confirmation box. Pressing OK there (message box 0x16, ctrl 2, owner 0x3FE, phase 6) sends the bare opcode. The client then clears everything locally: the HUD window 3 ctrl 8 indicator goes to state 3, window 0x3FE is hidden, the message list is freed and the count label is refreshed. No message ids are sent.
specs.trigger: Close the messenger messages window (0x3FE ctrl 2 or 9), then press OK in the 'All the messages will be deleted...' confirmation.
specs.expected_response: None. The client clears its list without waiting for a reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs game phase [[scene+0x4CC]+0xF00]==6 and the message-box owner to be 0x3FE. If CMessenger+0x74 is NULL, neither the send nor the local clear happens. The server should drop the stored messages, or they will come back on the next S2C 0x78. C2S 0x44 has nothing to do with S2C 0x44 (setMP).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree on everything that matters: a bare opcode from FUN_00472900 (Add u8 0x44 at 0x472955, Send at 0x47295F), gated on dlg==0x16, ctrl==0x64 and a non-NULL socket, with the only real caller at 0x446EB0. The disagreement was notation only ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm confirms there is no other Add. The caller code at 0x446E5D-0x446EB0 checks phase 6 (SUB 3/SUB 2/SUB 1), ctrl 2 and owner 0x3FE, then does PUSH 0x64; PUSH EDX(=0x16); PUSH [scene+0x4E4]. EDX survives FUN_004832b0, which does not touch EDX. A is right that the UI clear is inside the socket-non-NULL branch, because the JZ at 0x47294D skips to 0x473707. The 0x3FE switch table decoded from the binary maps ctrl 2 and ctrl 9 to the confirm prompt at 0x47324E. The other caller FUN_0044bd10 only passes (0x176,7). The generic dispatch at 0x44B7E1 passes the real ctrl id, which would have to be 100 on window 0x16. 'stop' is used as the zero-byte DSL form. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.
open_questions: Whether the server should delete messages permanently or only mark them read (client treats them as gone).

specs.socket: game (g_sock_game 0x70E6F4, cached at [app+0x700+0x20] by init FUN_0045AE40)

specs.semantics: Asks the server to re-send the account's Wind Cash / mileage balance. The body is just the opcode byte. It is built with Add(u8 0x46) at 0x463D7E and Send(1) at 0x463D89, and nothing else is added (no helper or caller adds to the buffer). The object is the cash-shop (item mall) controller at app+0x700: +0x18 = UI root, +0x20 = game socket, +0x588 = cash, +0x58C = mileage.
specs.trigger: UI event: window 0x1CF (cash shop / item mall; its handler uses the wish-list strings) receives control 0xA8. The FUN_0045f2e0 switch was checked against tables 0x461564/0x461538 and 0x4615C0/0x461598: (0x1CF, 0xA8) goes to 0x45F3F1, and 0x1CF is the only window id that reaches that switch. It only sends if [app+0x700+0x5AC] != 0. That flag is set to 1 when the player presses control 5 in the same window. Control 5 closes windows 0x1F7-0x1FA, minimizes the client (PostMessage WM_SYSCOMMAND SC_MINIMIZE) and opens http://windslayer.kr.games.yahoo.com/item/item_filling.html, which is the cash top-up page. So this is the 'refresh balance after topping up' action.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x70 (SubHandler4 @0x4624DE): u32 wind_cash -> [app+0x700+0x588], u32 mileage -> [+0x58C], u8 first_purchase_bonus (non-zero shows the 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash. 500 mileage...' dialog). The client then calls FUN_0045C700 to refresh the display and clears the +0x5AC flag.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sent only while [app+0x700+0x5AC] != 0. The flag starts at 0 (FUN_0045AE40 at session init), is set only by the charge-cash button (control 5), and is cleared only by S2C 0x70. Until a 0x70 arrives, every control-0xA8 event sends another 0x46. If the player never presses charge-cash, control 0xA8 does nothing. There are no dialogs and no 'waiting' UI. Pressing charge-cash minimizes the game window and opens a dead Yahoo KR URL in the browser.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer (no parse_0x46 and no S2C 0x70 builder). Not handled by windslayer_server.py _dispatch (it falls through to 'Unhandled opcode'). There are no memory notes on the cash shop. S2C 0x70 layout was taken from the handler asm at 0x4624DE-0x462541.

specs.semantics: Send the selected cash item as a gift to another character, with an optional message. Paid from the sender's cash.

It opens password dialog 0x201, which sends C2S 0x51 (site #50: str[21] password + u32 0x1F9). The server replies S2C 0x80 {u8 1, u32 0x1F9}, and FUN_0045E0D0 opens gift dialog 0x1F9. Pressing Send (param_3 4) there sends this.

(plus the '50% bonus mileage' line if mileage rose), 0x0E='You are short of cash.', 0x02='The character doesn't exist.', 0x14='You can't send a player an item of the other gender.', 0x0C='You can't send a gift to your character', else='You failed to send a gift.'; if 1: u32 cash ->+0x588, u32 mileage ->+0x58C

After sending, the dialog closes and a 'Waiting for the server to response.' box shows, so the server must answer with 0x71. Hazards: message_len is strlen truncated to u8 (256+ chars would wrap). MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x72 CashItemUsed (echoing the real cash_item_serial).

Dialog button must be 2 (OK) and window 0x3F4 must exist. Skill-type items already registered show 'The item is already registered. Please check your skill list.' and send nothing. After sending, the modal waiting box stays until the server replies, so the client appears stuck if the server ignores 0x48. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x72.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A reported send site 0x460A72 carrying opcode 0x48 as 'u16 item_id' (2 bytes after the opcode). Analyst B did not report this key because it only followed the linear 0x49 path into the shared Send. Analyst A is correct. The asm shows case 0x3F4 of the dialog switch (raw jump table 0x4617B4/0x4617E0 resolves dialog 0x3F4 to 0x460DE6). At 0x460DE6 it checks SUB EAX,2 / JNZ, then FUN_004830f0 with a NULL check. Then 0x460E03 MOV ECX,[EBX+0x20]; 0x460E06 PUSH 0x48; 0x460E08 CALL [0x4A40FC] Add(uchar). Then 0x460E0E MOVZX EAX, word [ESI+0x134]; 0x460E18 PUSH EAX; 0x460E19 CALL [0x4A40F4] Add(ushort). Then 0x460E1F JMP 0x460A6D, which does MOV ECX,[EBX+0x20]; PUSH 1; 0x460A72 CALL [0x4A4108] Send. So the full packet is 48 + u16. The decompiler agrees (case 0x3f4: Add 'H', Add *(ushort*)(iVar9+0x134), goto LAB_00460a6d). The same Send VA also carries 0x49 (u8 0x49 + 17-byte string via 0x460A55-0x460A67), which is a separate key. Not handled by PySlayer client parsers (no parse_0x48) or by windslayer_server.py.

Whether [ctx+0x720] is exactly the same CSNSocket as g_sock_game [0x70E6F4]. It is very likely, but no direct assignment was found in the corpus.

The server cannot tell the skill-registration variant (opener param_5==2) from a normal use, because the wire bytes are identical. It has to work that out from the item type.

specs.semantics: Apply a Stat Reset cash item. Dialog 0x3FA shows the four current stats and the number of points the item can reset (window+0x40). Buttons 3/4/5/6 decrement the displayed str/dex/int/tol value (never below 0) while total removed < item points and update the remaining counter (ctrl 11); nothing is sent for those. Button 0xC (confirm) sends 0x4A with the item id and the per-stat number of points removed, if any points were removed, then shows a modal waiting box. Removed points presumably return to the free stat-point pool server-side.
specs.trigger: Using a Stat Reset item (0xC8E/0xC8F/0xCA2/0xCA3) opens dialog 0x3FA; player decrements stats and presses confirm (param_3 == 0xC).
specs.expected_response: Likely S2C 0x76 (SubHandler4 0x462848): u32 uid; u16 x4 stats written to entity +0xE6,+0xE8,+0xEA,+0xEC; HP/MP bars refreshed; later closes box 0x16 and reads u32 + u16 -> FUN_00464380 (item count update). Not fully verified. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x76 StatRedistributeResult (18-byte form to the requester).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Not sent if total displayed == total current (nothing removed). Deltas are u8 (value mod 256) but bounded by item points (<=20). The client never checks base/minimum stats beyond >=0, nor that deltas sum to exactly the item's points (only <=), so the server must validate: sum(deltas) <= points of item_id, each resulting stat >= class minimum, and the player owns item_id. Opener requires item points (param_4) != 0. Modal waiting box stays until the server replies. No ResetBuffer before Adds. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C13, premium_cash#21): the client's own cap is the u16 quantity at +0x08 of the 28-byte cash record delivered by S2C 0x6F, not the item def's Cash_V. The server must validate sum(removed) <= record.quantity (and treat Cash_V only as the value stamped into quantity when the record is created). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, live): this send puts up the modal "Waiting for the server to response." box (dialog 0x16), which has NO OK button and stays up until the matching reply arrives - the client is soft-locked behind it. The server MUST answer: S2C 0x76.
specs.references: Stat order/names from 0x07 read order (+0xE6,+0xE8,+0xEA,+0xEC) and PySlayer opcode_0x07.py (str 힘, dex 민첩, int 지혜, tol 근성); our server calls the 4th 'spr'. Item names from server/data/en/items_en.json. Not in PySlayer parsers; not handled by windslayer_server.py.

specs.semantics: Received-gift popup 0x3EF (shown for each gift record from S2C 0x6D whose item is giftable or a WS Gift Card 0xCFF..0xD04) lets the player type a thank-you note. specs.semantics: Asks the server to deliver a written note to another character (works for offline friends too, per the item description), using up one note item. After sending, the client closes the note window and shows a modal 'Waiting for the server to response.' dialog.

Success: item count -1 (FUN_00464380), controls 7 and 9 cleared, window 0x3FD closed, 'You successfully sent the message.' Other values: 'Failed to send the message .' fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item definition id of the megaphone being used: 3377 Super Megaphone x13, 3378 x5, 3379 x1 (whole world); 3380 Megaphone x11, 3381 x1 (whole channel)
fields.dest_or_source: Megaphone window 0x3FF +0x40 (FUN_00483330), set when the item is used (FUN_00463d90 @0x463F76, from item_def+0x144 = definition index). Low 16 bits

specs.semantics: Asks the server to broadcast a megaphone message using a megaphone cash item from the inventory. The item id tells the server whether it is a Super Megaphone (whole world) or a normal Megaphone (whole channel). After sending, the client closes the megaphone window straight away and shows no waiting dialog, so it does not need a direct reply. The server should check that the player owns the item, use up one charge, broadcast the message, and update the item count.
specs.trigger: The player double-clicks a Megaphone or Super Megaphone item (ids 3377-3381), types in window 0x3FF (edit control 6) and clicks the send button (control 3).
specs.expected_response: No reply packet is required (window closes, no modal). The broadcast and item-count update presumably come in a separate S2C packet, but it was not found in this pass.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Client checks before sending: text is not empty ('Please enter the contents.'); Curse_Engine_Clean(text) passes ('No cursing \r\n\r\nplease.'); low 16 bits of window+0x40 are not 0 (otherwise it returns silently with no dialog). Opening window 0x3FF any other way leaves +0x40 at 0, so nothing is sent. Hazard: unbounded strcpy of the edit-control text into a 61-byte stack buffer. If the control allows 61 or more characters the text is not NUL-terminated inside the 61 bytes sent (and the stack overflows). No ResetBuffer is called; the buffer is assumed empty after the previous Send. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all.
specs.references: No match in PySlayer (no parse_0x4C). Not handled in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. The scout guess (0x48 + u16 + str) was wrong: the Add(0x48)+u16 at 0x460E06 belongs to window 0x3F4 and jumps to site #52's Send at 0x460A6D. Item names come from data/en/items_en.json and the PySlayer gamedef items table (Type 5 cash items).

Maximum length of edit control 6 in window 0x3FF (limits the real text to 60 characters or fewer?) is not verified.
blind_open_questions: What S2C packet (if any) confirms the megaphone and consumes the item: 0x72 item-use broadcast, a chat/announcement opcode, or something else?
Does Curse_Engine_Clean change the buffer in place (mask words) or only check it?
Meaning of the Send(int) argument (always 1 here).

specs.name: MentorRemove

locations.role: Friend window 0x176, ctrl 0x1C (switch 0x4729AA, verified from table 0x47374C/0x473724). If the CMessenger+0x14 list (head +0x18) has an entry, it opens window 0x200 and sets ctrl 4's text to entry+0x00 (name).
Generic dialog click dispatch: FUN_00472900(CMessenger, dlg=0x200, ctrl)
Window 0x200 lookup (FUN_004830f0). Ctrl 4 label text via FUN_0048a050 (control+0x50).
If the window is missing or the ctrl 4 text is empty, shows 'Please select a character name.' (0x473364) and sends nothing.
Calls FUN_00472260, which frees the CMessenger+0x14 list (+0x18/+0x1C/+0x20) and refreshes the friend UI via FUN_00470270. Then FUN_00446300(0x200,0,1,0,1) closes the window.
S2C 0x7A ('is registered as your mentor.') adds entries to that same CMessenger+0x14 list.

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Asks the server to dissolve the local player's mentor relationship. Friend window 0x176 button 0x1C opens confirm window 0x200 only if the client has a mentor entry in list CMessenger+0x14 (filled by S2C 0x7A), and shows that mentor's name in ctrl 4. Button 0x1B next to it is the register-mentor path, which requires a novice ('Only a novice can register a mentor.'). When OK (ctrl 2) is pressed and the name label is not empty, the client sends the bare opcode, frees its local mentor list at once, refreshes the friend window and closes window 0x200. No name or uid is sent, so the server works out the mentor from its own records.
specs.trigger: Friend/messenger window 0x176 button ctrl 0x1C, then OK (ctrl 2) in confirm window 0x200.
specs.expected_response: None. The client removes the mentor locally before any reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs window 0x200 to exist and its ctrl 4 label to be non-empty, otherwise the client shows 'Please select a character name.'. If window 0x200 exists but ctrl 4 does not, FUN_0048a050 returns NULL and the strlen loop at 0x473308 dereferences NULL, crashing the client. No send (and no local clear) if CMessenger+0x74 is NULL. The client drops the mentor whatever the server does, so if the server refuses it must send the mentor data again to resync.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: the bare opcode, with Add(u8 0x50) at 0x473322 and Send(1) at 0x47332D in FUN_00472900's dlg==0x200/ctrl==2 branch. The only difference is notation ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm shows no Add between the socket gate at 0x473315 and Send. The name read from ctrl 4 at 0x4732F9 is only used for the empty-string check and is never Added. Decoding switch table 0x47374C/0x473724 from the binary confirms ctrl 0x1C goes to 0x472D72 (the opener) and ctrl 0x1B to 0x472D12 (the novice-only register-mentor path). S2C 0x7A writing the list at LEA ESI,[EBX+0x14] (0x4716C4), and FUN_00472260 freeing +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20, are verified. A's confidence was medium only because window 0x200 has no text string. The control flow (mentor list present, then name shown, then list freed) supports 'remove mentor', so high confidence is justified for the wire format. B's NULL-dereference hazard is real, since FUN_0048a050 returns 0 when the control is missing. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.
open_questions: Whether list CMessenger+0x14 can also hold disciples (S2C 0x7A only showed mentor wording); the removal target semantics depend on server records.
Which S2C (e.g. 0x7C) the server should send to the former mentor was not traced.
