specs.socket: game (g_sock_game [0x70E6F4], copied into cash-shop manager ctx 0x70F100+0x20 by FUN_0045ae40 at login, 0x45AE40/0x45AE55)

locations.role: window-event case for dialog 0x201 (jump table 0x4615A0 area: 0x1CF-based table 0x461538/0x461564 entry 0x201 -> 0x46078D); param_3 (control id) - 2 == 0 -> 0x4607C2
FUN_0048a030: text (+0xD1) of edit control #5 of window 0x201 (password box, masked: FUN_00464480 sets control+0x24=1)
FUN_004830f0: find window 0x201 object (needed for +0x134); if NULL the send is skipped but the window still closes
opener: checks account flag [[gs+0x4CC]+0x218] (else 'no SS# in this ID...' box), opens window 0x201, sets window+0x134 = requested window id via FUN_00483270
caller passes 0x1A7 (NPC with UI id 0x1A7, e.g. NPC idx 97)
S2C 0x80 reply handler (u8 ok; if ok==1 u32 window_id)

specs.grammar:
str[21] password
u32 target_window_id

fields.name: password
fields.meaning: Password typed into edit control #5 of dialog 0x201 (masked edit). NUL-terminated; copied with an unbounded strcpy into a stack buffer at [esp+0x30] that is NOT zero-initialised on this path, so bytes after the NUL are stack garbage. Server must parse up to first NUL.

fields.name: target_window_id
fields.meaning: Id of the UI window/feature that requested password confirmation; echoed back by the server in S2C 0x80. Known values: 0x1F9 (cash-shop gift send), 0x1A7 (NPC service window, NPC UI id 423), 0x235 (NPC-target service window).

specs.semantics: Password re-confirmation gate. When the player opens a protected feature (cash-shop gift, some NPC service windows) the client first shows password dialog 0x201. Clicking OK (control id 2) sends 0x51 with the password and the id of the window that should open on success, then closes dialog 0x201 (no 'waiting' box). Control id 4 on this dialog only refocuses the edit box (FUN_00489960(0x201,5)).
specs.trigger: Dialog 0x201 OK button (window event param_3 == 2) after FUN_00464480 opened the dialog (gift purchase in cash shop, NPC UI 0x1A7, NPC-target 0x235 interaction).
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x80 (handler 0x44E2FE): u8 ok; if ok==1 { u32 window_id; if window_id==0x1F9 -> FUN_0045e0d0 (continue gift flow) else FUN_00483430(window_id,3,1) opens that window } else box 'Invalid password.\r\n\r\nPlease check your password again.' CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F. Target window ids seen live: 0x1A7 (bank), 0x1F9 (cash-shop purchase continuation) and 0x235 (character delete confirm). Always echo the id the client sent.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Opener requires account flag byte [[game_state+0x4CC]+0x218] != 0, otherwise shows 'no SS# in this ID...' and nothing is sent. Send is skipped if cash-shop ctx socket pointer (+0x20) is NULL (returns without closing) or window 0x201 object is not found (window still closed). No ResetBuffer before the Adds (relies on the prior Send having cleared the buffer). strcpy of the edit text into the stack buffer is unbounded (edit length limit not verified). Password field trailing bytes are uninitialised.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x80.py sends 0x80 with p8(1)+p32u(0x4CF), consistent with the (ok, window_id) reply shape. Our server (windslayer_server.py _build_opcode_80 ~line 1107) treats 0x80 as a 'CashShopBalance' (flag, value) - the client actually interprets the u32 as a window id to open (FUN_00483430(value,3,1)), so sending a balance there is semantically wrong. C2S 0x51 is not handled in _dispatch. Related send site #33 (0x44ABA4, opcode 0x12) also reads window 0x201 text.
open_questions: Exact meaning of the password (account password vs a secondary/SSN-bound password); only the failure string 'Invalid password' is known.
Maximum length enforced by edit control #5 of window 0x201 (buffer is 21 bytes, copy is unbounded).
Identity of windows 0x1A7 and 0x235 (NPC service windows; 0x1A7 is the UI id of NPC idx 97 'Mikomakisho', possibly storage).

specs.name: VillageTransfer

locations.role: gold check: u64 gold [[this+0x4CC]+0x270/+0x274] >= fee [win+0x134], else 'You are short of gold.'

specs.grammar:
u8 village_index

fields.name: village_index
fields.meaning: Destination village index 1..10 into the name table @0x70B8B4: 1 The Beginning of the Adventure, 2 Popola Village, 3 Ozzi Village, 4 Balderan, 5 Amakusa, 6 Mining Settlement, 7 Atajokuna, 8 Serien the City of Water, 9 Serien Underworld, 10 Underwater City RA (0 = 'Nearest Village')

fields.name: fee
fields.meaning: Gold fee the client computed and displayed. Base = table @0x70D07C[distance] (distance 1..: 1000,1940,2840,3700,4520,5300,6040,6740,7400,8020,...), where distance = |order[cur]-order[dest]| from order table @0x70D098 {0,1,2,3,4,5,5,6,7,8,9}. Distance 0 uses 1000. +1 when crossing index 5 (cur==5 && dest>5, or dest==5 && cur>5). Current village = the index whose value in table @0x70D04C {0,1,2,4,7,5,8,6,9,10,11} equals current map_id/100. If manner point [[this+0x4CC]+0xEE0] >= 500, fee = trunc(fee*0.9) (FPU chop mode). 0 means already there, and the dialog never opens
fields.dest_or_source: [window0x237+0x134] (u32 holding a u16), written by FUN_0043dc40

specs.semantics: Asks to teleport to another village for a gold fee. The client sends the destination index and the fee it computed itself. The server should recompute and check the fee and the gold. No waiting dialog is shown.
specs.trigger: In the village-transfer destination window 600 (0x258), picking a destination (controls 3..12) opens confirm window 0x237 with the name and fee. Pressing control 7 (confirm) sends this packet if the u64 gold is at least the fee.
specs.expected_response: Most likely S2C 0x81 (handler 0x4528F3): u8 ok. If ok==1 it is followed by u64 remaining gold, written to [[this+0x4CC]+0x270], and plays sound 0x29. Otherwise it shows 'Village transfer failed. Please try again in a few minutes.'. The server presumably then sends the normal map-change sequence (0x08, 0x03, 0x07, 0x0A, 0x28, 0x44, 0x1A...).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: window 0x237 must exist, and u64 gold >= fee (client-side, so the server must validate). Dialog-open gates in FUN_0043dc40: index <= 10, fee != 0 ('You can't move to where you already are.'). The fee is client-computed, so do not trust it. Note S2C 0x5D is unrelated (a disconnect notice).
specs.references: The scout's guess of 0x66 was wrong: 0x65/0x66 belong to window 0x290 (a different path that jumps to the shared send at 0x4484C4). No PySlayer parser for C2S 0x5D. windslayer_server.py does not handle 0x5D.

Which map/spawn packets the server must send after a successful transfer, and the destination map ids per village index (map_id/100 group from @0x70D04C), still need confirming against gamedef.
What opens window 600 (0x258): a teleport NPC or an item.

specs.name: ItemStallStopForEdit

locations.role: dialog 0x259 event switch (EDI-2, byte table 0x46C3CC, jump table 0x46C3B0). Decoded: event 0x1B -> 0x46B6A5; events 2/0x1A -> 0x46B6C1; 0x1C -> 0x46B705; 0x19 -> 0x46B485; 0x1E -> 0x46B86D; 0x32 -> 0x46B38A.
S2C 0x83 handler: u8 result; if 1, FUN_00467030 sets ctx+0x20 = 0 and ctx+0x1C = 1 and re-enables the stall controls

specs.semantics: Opcode byte only, no payload. Sent from the Item Stall (personal shop) window, dialog 0x259, while the stall is open (ctx+0x20 != 0). It asks the server to stop selling so the stall can be edited. Locally the client only clears ctx+0x1C before sending. The stall-open flag is cleared later by the S2C 0x83 result == 1 handler (FUN_00467030), which also sets edit mode ctx+0x1C = 1.
specs.trigger: Event 0x1B (a button on dialog 0x259) while ctx+0x20 != 0.
specs.expected_response: Probably S2C 0x83 u8 result (1 = back to edit mode). Inferred from what FUN_00467030 does and from the 0x5E/0x5F/0x60 <-> 0x82/0x83/0x84 numbering; not proven by a direct link.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs ctx+0x0C != 0 and ctx+0x20 != 0; otherwise nothing happens. ctx = owner+0xD5C: +0x00 active dialog id, +0x1C edit mode, +0x20 stall open (set by FUN_00466f20 on S2C 0x82 result 1). S2C 0x82 result 9 shows "Invalid information transaction..."; other non-1 results show "Item stall opening failed...".
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A reported a zero-payload 0x5F from dialog 0x259 event 0x1B. Analyst B missed it: the path reaches the shared Send only by JMP 0x469BA3 @0x46B6BC. The asm confirms A. At 0x46B6A5, CMP [EBX+0x20],ESI (ESI=0 since 0x4690B2 and untouched on the 0x1A7->0x46A92A->0x46B370 path) and JZ exit. 0x46B6AE MOV ECX,[EBX+0x14]. 0x46B6B1 PUSH 0x5F. 0x46B6B3 MOV [EBX+0x1C],0. 0x46B6B6 Add(uchar). JMP 0x469BA3 -> MOV ECX,[EBX+0x14], PUSH 1, Send @0x469BA8. No other Add runs between the opcode and Send. The event mapping was decoded from jump table 0x46C3B0/0x46C3CC in the PE, and the dialog mapping 0x259 -> 0x46B370 from table 0x46C294/0x46C2C4. Not in PySlayer or our server.
open_questions: The on-screen label of control 0x1B (Modify/Stop) is not in the exe strings.
The pairing with S2C 0x83 is inferred, not proven.

specs.name: ItemStallClose

locations.role: events 2 and 0x1A on dialog 0x259. If ctx+0x20 != 0, send 0x60; else FUN_00483430(0x259,1,1) closes the window with no packet.
automatic: shared S2C handler block 0x450867 (opcodes 0x08, 0x5E, 0xA3, 0xA4 per s2c_dispatch_map). If FUN_004837c0(0x259) != 1 and ctx+0x08 != 0, fires event 2 on 0x259.
automatic: if entity uid == local uid ([+0x4CC]+0x220), entity+0x15B4 != 8, ctx+0x00 == 0x259 with (ctx+0x20 or ctx+0x04) != 0, and ctx+0x08 != 0, fires event 2 on 0x259
S2C 0x84 handler: u8 result; 1 -> FUN_00483430(0x259,1,1) closes the stall window

specs.semantics: Opcode byte only, no payload. Closes an open Item Stall. The user sends it by closing the stall window (event 2) or pressing control 0x1A while the stall is open. The client also sends it by itself on the S2C 0x08/0x5E/0xA3/0xA4 handler path and from FUN_0042cf20 when the local player's state +0x15B4 is not 8. Locally the client only clears ctx+0x1C and does not clear ctx+0x20. If the stall is not open (ctx+0x20 == 0), the same events just close the window with no packet.
specs.trigger: User: event 2 or 0x1A on dialog 0x259 while ctx+0x20 != 0. Automatic: the OnReceive block at 0x450867 (S2C 0x08/0x5E/0xA3/0xA4), or FUN_0042cf20 @0x42F42F when the local player leaves state 8.
specs.expected_response: Probably S2C 0x84 u8 result (1 -> the client closes dialog 0x259). Inferred.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sent only while ctx+0x20 != 0 (and ctx+0x0C != 0). ctx+0x20 is not cleared on this path, so the FUN_0042cf20 trigger may fire again on later updates until the server reply closes the window or state changes. The server should treat repeated 0x60 as harmless and idempotent.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A reported a zero-payload 0x60 from dialog 0x259 events 2/0x1A, with automatic triggers. Analyst B missed it: the path reaches the shared Send only by JMP 0x469BA3 @0x46B6D4. The asm confirms A. 0x46B6C1 CMP [EBX+0x20],ESI (ESI=0). JZ 0x46B6D9 (close window, no send). 0x46B6C6 MOV ECX,[EBX+0x14]. PUSH 0x60. MOV [EBX+0x1C],0. Add(uchar) @0x46B6CE. JMP 0x469BA3 -> Send(1) @0x469BA8, with no further Adds. Jump-table decode: events 2 and 0x1A -> 0x46B6C1. The callers were verified in the asm: 0x42F424 PUSH 0x259 / ECX=2, and 0x450916 ECX=EBX+1=2 with EDX=0x259 pushed. The s2c_dispatch_map routes opcodes 0x08, 0x5E, 0xA3 and 0xA4 to handler 0x450867, which flows into 0x450919. The S2C 0x84 handler @0x46D1AD reads u8 and on 1 closes dialog 0x259. Our memory notes: +0x15B4 is 8 when idle and 4 when attacking. Not in PySlayer or our server.
open_questions: Does closing dialog 0x259 (FUN_00483430) run a callback that clears ctx+0x00/+0x08/+0x20? That decides whether the FUN_0042cf20 auto-close repeats.
The pairing with S2C 0x84 is inferred.
The return-value meaning of FUN_004837c0(0x259) in the @0x450901 check (== 1 skips) was not confirmed.

fields.name: stall_owner_uid
fields.dest_or_source: clicked entity +0x84 (uid) of a remote player (entity+0x98 == 3, uid != scene+0x220)
fields.meaning: Unique id of the player whose open item stall the user wants to browse

specs.semantics: Asks the server to open another player's item stall for browsing. The client changes no state on send. S2C 0x85 (handler 0x46CF9C) sets entity+0x14F4 = 1, entity+0x150E = u16, entity+0x14F5 = char[25] stall title. S2C 0x86 clears it with 'The shop is closed or adjusting.'. 0x61 is sent only while that flag is set.
specs.trigger: Left mouse button release (WM_LBUTTONUP 0x202) in field mode (scene+0xF00 == 6) over another player whose stall is open (entity+0xE2 == 0, entity+0x14F4 != 0). Screen anchor: sx = ent+0x15A4 - cam(game_state+0x1044) + 400 + edge_adj, sy = ent+0x15A8 - cam(+0x1048) + 0x102 + edge_adj. The hit counts when the mouse (game_state+0x3FC/+0x400) is within dist^2 < 0xA28 of (sx,sy), or inside the stall-sign box sx-0x67 < mx < sx+0x67 and sy-0x6E < my < sy-0x50. The first entity in list order that passes the hit test decides.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x87 (handler 0x46D1F9): u8 result. 1 = OK: u8 item_count, then if count > 0 u32 owner uid (to stall mgr game_state+0xD60), char[25] title, opens window 0x259, then per item u16, u16, u32, u8 n, u16[n], u16. 6 = 'Open stall is opened. Close the Open stall and try again.'. Any other value (or count 0) = 'The shop is closed or adjusting.'.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Target must be entity+0x98 == 3 with uid != scene+0x220 (not self) and entity+0xE2 == 0. Entities with +0xE2 != 0 are room/portal objects that open the 'Enter the arena?' / 'Would you enter the play room?' / 'Enter the cash shop?' (0x81) dialogs instead. Also: entity+0x14F4 != 0; FUN_00466df0(game_state+0xD5C) == 0 and FUN_00466e10 == 0 (no own stall / stall browse session active in stall manager id 0x259, flags +0xD7C/+0xD78); FUN_00468fa0 == 0 (no trade window 0x28C in state 3 / blocking modal). Hovering sets the cursor (ui_root+0x10 = 0x48). No pending lock, so repeated clicks resend.
specs.references: Not in windslayer_server.py _dispatch (would log 'Unhandled opcode 0x61'). PySlayer has no C2S parser for 0x61. Its server_packets/opcode_0x61.py is an unrelated S2C chat guess for the KR build (and S2C 0x61 in EN is a Packet_handler_3 opcode at 0x47132D, different meaning). UI strings confirm EN terminology 'Item stall' / 'Open stall'.

specs.name: CardDeckListRequest
specs.socket: game: CSNSocket* at app+0xDD0 = card-deck object (app+0xDC4)+0xC. FUN_0045a130 copies g_sock_game [0x70E6F4] there (0x45A141), so it is the same TCP 7022 socket.

locations.role: in the S2C 0x02 login-result==1 branch: FUN_0045a130(EAX=app+0xDC4) initializes the card-deck object
MOV [cardobj+0xC], g_sock_game (app+0xDD0); also +0x0 = app, +0x4 = ui root, +0x8 = player[+0xF84], +0x10 = player+0x48
card-deck object's S2C handlers: 0x8A deck list, 0x8B register-card result
sibling C2S 0x64 (u16 card id) register-card send on the same object

specs.semantics: Opcode-only request that asks the server for the card deck ('dictionary') contents. The send is unconditional and comes right after the messenger 0x2F send, at the very end of the S2C 0x03 handler. It goes through the card-deck object's socket pointer (app+0xDC4, the same object passed to SubHandler5). That object only handles S2C 0x8A: u8 count stored at (player+0x48)+0xE30, then u16 ids. It then refreshes the Card Deck UI ('%u / %u (%u%%)'). S2C 0x8B error code 2 says 'Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again.', which ties this data to the login/world-entry fetch. No other Adds; the only Add(0x63) in the binary is this one. Fire-and-forget.
specs.trigger: Automatic, at the end of every S2C 0x03 (world/map info) handler, i.e. after each map load, immediately after C2S 0x2F (or in its place when the messenger gate fails).
specs.expected_response: Probably S2C 0x8A card deck list: u8 count, repeat(count){ u16 card_id }. It is stored at player+0x48+0xE30/+0xE32 and handled in SubHandler5_ifelse. The client does not require a reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate. [app+0xDD0] is only set by FUN_0045a130 in the S2C 0x02 success path (result==1). If a server sends S2C 0x03 without a prior successful 0x02 on this connection, ECX may be NULL or stale and CSNSocket::Add would fault (crash). SubHandler5 ignores 0x8A/0x8B unless cardobj+0x0 (app) and +0x4 (ui) are non-null, which is also set in that 0x02 path.
specs.references: The live capture shows 0x63 with 0 bytes after a map load, which agrees. windslayer_server.py _dispatch answers C2S 0x63 by sending S2C 0x63 with an EMPTY body. That looks wrong: the client's S2C 0x63 handler (0x4577A8) is unrelated. It reads u16 + u8 and formats '%s(%u/%u)' / '%u Players' (a player-count display), so an empty body means reading past the end. The natural reply is S2C 0x8A. PySlayer has no C2S 0x63 parser; its server_packets list has no 0x8A either.
open_questions: Name and reply are inferred from the owning object (card-deck/dictionary object at app+0xDC4, its S2C 0x8A/0x8B handlers and strings); wire format (0 bytes) is certain, semantic name is medium confidence.

S2C 0x03 already reads a u8 into player+0xE78 (= player+0x48+0xE30, the card count slot) at 0x44E629; it is unclear whether 0x8A is still needed to fill the u16 id array or whether 0x03's byte is an unrelated field sharing that offset.
Whether the current server's empty S2C 0x63 reply causes visible side effects (a garbage player-count label) was not verified statically.

The identity of UI window 0x14 (it may be the T-key Battlefield / Death Match window; not confirmed).

specs.semantics: Asks the server to register a card item in the character's Card Deck (a collection book). Client flow: (1) inventory action case 0x65 in FUN_00469090 on a selected inventory item calls FUN_0045a3c0. That function checks that the item def has +0x154==2 and +0x14C!=0; otherwise it shows 'This item cannot be registered.'. It also scans the local deck list (byte count at charData+0xE30, u16 ids from +0xE32; charData = main+0x4CC+0x48); a duplicate shows 'This card is already registered . You can't register it again.'. If both checks pass, it stores the id in control 0x292 +0x134 and opens dialog 0x292. (2) When the user confirms dialog 0x292 (notification code 2), FUN_0045a4a0 sends [0x64][u16 card_item_id] and shows the modal 'Waiting for the server to response.'.
specs.trigger: The player uses the card-register action on a card item in the inventory (FUN_00469090 case 0x65), then confirms dialog control 0x292 (notification 2). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C47, quest_cards_misc#07): the user gesture behind FUN_00469090 case 0x65 is DRAGGING a card from the bag (Miscellanies tab) onto the Card Deck window (window 8, hotkey B) - neither a right-click nor a double-click is involved. The confirm dialog 0x292 then reads "Once the card is registered to the Card Deck, it cannot be returned back to your inventory."
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x8B (handled in SubHandler5 @0x45A520). Its grammar is: u8 result; if(result==1){ u8 new_count  u16 card_item_id }. On result 1 the client sets charData+0xE30=new_count and writes card_item_id at charData+0xE30+new_count*2, so new_count is the 1-based slot and equals the new total. This happens only if the item lookup and FUN_00467140(card_item_id,0,1) both succeed (probably consumes the card from the inventory). The client then refreshes the deck UI and prints 'Registered %s in the Card Deck.'. result 2 = 'Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again.', result 6 = 'Already registered.', anything else = 'Failure to register card. Please try again in a few minutes.'. The 0x8B handler first calls FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1), which probably dismisses the waiting box. S2C 0x8A (u8 count; repeat(count){u16 card_item_id}) replaces the whole deck list. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): the client is soft-locked behind the modal "Waiting for the server to response." (dialog 0x16, no OK button) until the server answers with S2C 0x8B CardDeckRegisterResult - this one box does have an OK button, so an unanswered 0x64 is not a soft-lock, but nothing is registered.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs [main+0xDC4+4] (g_ui_root copy) != 0, which FUN_0045a130 sets during the S2C 0x02 handler. FUN_00446300 only reaches this handler if [main+0xDC4] != 0 and the item-mall handler FUN_0045f2e0 returned 0. The socket pointer is not null-checked here. After sending, the client shows a blocking 'Waiting for the server to response.' message box. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C47, quest_cards_misc#07): the waiting box (dialog 0x16) HAS an OK button, so an unanswered 0x64 does NOT soft-lock the client - the player closes the box, nothing is registered and the card stays in the bag. (Drop "soft-locks" from the design-doc note.) control0x292+0x134 is not cleared after the send, so confirming the dialog again would re-send the same id. The duplicate check runs only against the client's local deck list, so the server must also reject duplicates (result 6).
specs.references: No C2S parser in PySlayer (its client_packets only cover 0x03,0x0B,0x0C,0x0D,0x0F,0x15,0x1A,0x2B,0x2C,0x7E). PySlayer has server builders opcode_0x8A/0x8B in __init__ (KR). Not handled by our windslayer_server.py _dispatch (no 0x64 branch). The UI strings in FUN_0045a3c0 and SubHandler5 confirm the Card Deck meaning.
open_questions: [RESOLVED by live verification quest_cards_misc#07, 2026-09-17] Live: notification 2 on control 0x292 is the OK button of the register confirmation dialog, reached by dragging a card from the bag onto the Card Deck window (window 8). Original question: "Exact meaning of notification code 2 on control 0x292 (assumed to be the OK/Yes button of the register confirmation dialog)"
Whether FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) at the start of the 0x8B handler is what closes the 'Waiting for the server to response.' box
What FUN_00467140(card_item_id,0,1) does in the 0x8B success path (likely removes one card from the inventory); whether the server must also send an inventory update
blind_open_questions: What button value 2 means in dialog 0x292 (probably OK/Yes). Inferred from FUN_00446300 re-dispatching with [ebp+0xC]=2 elsewhere; not traced to the widget code.
Whether the server must also re-send 0x8A after a successful 0x8B. The client updates its local deck array from 0x8B alone.

specs.socket: game (g_sock_game 0x70E6F4, cached at [app+0xD5C+0x14] by init FUN_00464ED0)

locations.role: taken when word [this+0x64]==0 or [this+0x66]==0; EAX still = window 0x293
start (control 0x17) in the Refining (0x28E) / Concoction (0x28D) window: FUN_004668f0 gets the selected product id, then skill checks

specs.grammar: u16 product_item_id

fields.name: product_item_id
fields.meaning: Item id of the recipe/product the player selected to make (Mineral Refining or Concoction). The item definition holds 8 material ids at +0x202 and quantities at +0x212. Def +0x224 == 2 means Mineral Refining; otherwise it is Concoction.
fields.dest_or_source: low word of [window 0x293 + 0x134], set at start by FUN_00483270 from the item selected in the recipe list ([ESP+0x14] filled by FUN_004668f0)

specs.semantics: Sent when the 5-second Mineral Refining or Concoction progress bar (window 0x293) finishes. It names the product to craft so the server can use up the materials and grant the item. It is built from the same per-frame check as 0x68 (window 0x293 state 3, elapsed > 5000 ms, window found) whenever the reinforcement slot words +0x64 and +0x66 are not both non-zero. Afterwards the client sets +0x60 = 0 and closes window 0x293 (FUN_00446300(0x293,0,1,0,1)); the busy flag this+0x2C is cleared by that window event.
specs.trigger: The player opens the Mineral Refining window (0x28E, near the smelter, interaction code 0x13C) or the Concoction window (0x28D, near the alchemy station, code 0x13B), selects a recipe and presses start (control 0x17). The skill-level checks FUN_00424c80/00424d00/00424d60 must pass by def type +0x154. After 5 s of progress in window 0x293 the client sends this.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x8D (SubHandler1 @0x46EA1C): u8 result, u16 product_item_id. result 1: the client removes the 8 materials (def +0x202 ids / +0x212 qty) and adds the product (FUN_00440920), then shows '<Mineral Refining|Concoction> Successful.'. result 0 or 0x11: materials are removed and it shows 'Failed.' (0x11 adds 'Out of empty slot in inventory'). 0x0F: 'Short of material item'. 0x10: 'The skill hasn't been learned yet.'. The result window 0x28F then opens with the product id.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Start gates: 'Out of item.' if the recipe list is empty ([this+0x54]==0), 'Choose item.' if nothing is selected, and skill-level checks. While this+0x2C is set, other item actions show 'Not allowed during concoction, mineral refining, or reinforcement.'. Hazard: whether 0x67 or 0x68 is sent depends on the reinforcement slot words, not on which window started. Stale non-zero +0x64/+0x66 would send 0x68 instead. The progress window closes without waiting for 0x8D. All timing is client-side.
specs.references: No PySlayer coverage for C2S 0x67 or S2C 0x8D. Not in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. Names come from strings 'Mineral Refining', 'Concoction', 'Too far for Mineral Refining. Go near the smelter.', 'Too far for Concoction. Go near the alchemy.'.
open_questions: Whether the server is expected to tell refining and concoction apart only by the product item's definition (+0x224). The packet has no mode field.
blind_open_questions: Window id of the Concoction list (anything other than 0x28E takes the 'Concoction' title); not needed for the wire format.

Whether the selected list row's u16 is the product id or a recipe id that equals the product item id. S2C 0x8D looks the same id up as an item record whose +0x202 holds the materials, so they are probably the same.

specs.socket: game: [this+0x14] where this = app+0xD5C (ECX set at 0x42F77D in FUN_0042cf20); +0x14 is loaded from g_sock_game [0x70E6F4] by FUN_00464ed0 at 0x464ED9/0x464EE3

fields.name: equip_item_id
fields.meaning: Item id of the equipment placed in the Reinforcement window (0x28C)
fields.dest_or_source: word [app+0xD5C+0x66], set at 0x468C54 from the placed item record +0x00

fields.meaning: The equipment record's 6 words at +0x02,+0x04,+0x06,+0x08,+0x0A,+0x0C, sent in that order. These are the enchant/option slots that match the {u16 item_id, 6 x u16} equipment layout. The placement check only needs one of the first five (+2..+0xA) to be zero; the 6th (+0xC) has no known meaning. S2C 0x8E success reads back exactly 6 u16s.
fields.dest_or_source: 0x38-byte item record copy = [[win0x28C+0xB0]+8] (the first node of the equipment list); ESI = rec+2, step 2, 6 iterations

specs.semantics: Reinforcement completion request. FUN_004684d0 runs every frame. When progress window 0x293 is in state 3 and more than 5000 ms have passed since [this+0x60], and both reinforcement slot words (+0x64 stone, +0x66 equipment) are non-zero, the client finds window 0x28C and the first node of its equipment list. It then sends 0x68: equipment id, stone id, and the 6 option words of the equipment record copy. The server decides the result. After Send, if [this+8]!=0, the client runs window 0x28C controls 3 and 4. The two slot-clear handlers in FUN_00469090 zero +0x64 (0x46BE08) and +0x66 (0x46BE35). Then, as on every other exit from this block, it resets the timer [this+0x60]=0 and closes window 0x293.
specs.trigger: The player places a reinforceable item and an elemental stone in the Reinforcement window (0x28C, near the smithy) and presses Reinforce (FUN_00469090 @0x46BD5C). The packet goes out on the first frame more than 5 s later.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x8E (SubHandler1 @0x46EC37): u8 result, u16, u16, then if result==1 { repeat(6) u16, u16 }. Result dialog is window 0x29B: 'Reinforcement Successful.' / 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.' / 'Reinforcement Failed.'. The client has already cleared the slots and closed the progress bar; the busy flag [this+0x2C] is cleared by the 0x8E handler.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Send-time gates: window 0x293 is in the UI list with [win+0x3C]==3; elapsed > 5000 ms (unsigned delta, converted to float); FUN_004830f0(0x293) != 0; word+0x64 != 0 and word+0x66 != 0; window 0x28C exists; its list head [+0xB0] and node data [node+8] are non-null. If any 0x28C lookup fails, NO packet is sent, but the timer is still reset and window 0x293 closed. [this+0x2C] busy then stays 1 until a 0x8E arrives, which a server will never send unprompted, so reinforce/refine stays locked. HAZARD: 0x67 and 0x68 share window 0x293 and timer +0x60. The opcode is chosen only by whether +0x64/+0x66 are non-zero, not by which button started the bar. Start-time gates (FUN_00469090 / FUN_00468b10): the stone must be present, the equipment must be present and reinforceable, and stone level <= equipment level. Opening the window zeroes +0x64/+0x66.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: There is no real disagreement. Both analysts described the same 16-byte wire format, u16 [this+0x66] equipment id, u16 [this+0x64] stone id, then six u16 words from the equipment record at +2..+0xC. A wrote it as repeat(6) and B as 8 flat u16s, which is why the 'structural signatures' differ. The asm confirms both: 0x46869D push 0x68 / 0x46869F Add(uchar); 0x4686A5 movzx eax,word[edi+0x66] + 0x4686AC ebx=[0x4A40F4] Add(ushort) + 0x4686B3 call ebx; 0x4686B5 movzx ecx,word[edi+0x64] + 0x4686BD call ebx; 0x4686BF add esi,2 (esi=[node+8] from 0x46868F); 0x4686C2 mov [esp+0xC],6; body 0x4686D0 movzx edx,word[esi] / 0x4686D7 call ebx / add esi,2 / dec counter / jnz 0x4686D0; 0x4686E8 Send(1). Equipment is added BEFORE stone, as both said. The node walk at 0x468669-0x46867A starts with ECX=0 and takes the index-0 (head) node at once. The canonical grammar uses repeat(6) because the code is a counted loop over contiguous record words; the bytes are identical to B's expansion. Minor corrections: the socket is [this+0x14] loaded from g_sock_game at 0x464ED9 (both right). A's post-send claim that controls 3 and 4 empty both slots fits the two slot-clear blocks at 0x46BE08 (+0x64=0) and 0x46BE35 (+0x66=0). The exact control-number-to-block mapping was not traced through FUN_00469090's switch. B's narrower claim ('control 4 clears the stone slot') is also not contradicted. The naive scout (Add8(0x68) only) was wrong. PySlayer has no C2S 0x68 parser. windslayer_server.py does not dispatch 0x68. The S2C 0x8E success path reads exactly 6 u16s (loop counter 6 at 0x46ECB5), which supports the 6-word block.
open_questions: Meaning of the 6th option word (record +0x0C): it is sent, but the client's 'has a free slot' check only covers +0x02..+0x0A.
Which of FUN_00469090 controls 3 and 4 maps to the +0x64 clear (0x46BE08) and which to the +0x66 clear (0x46BE35); not traced through the switch table.
Meaning of the two unlabeled u16s and the trailing u16 in S2C 0x8E (outside this C2S spec).

fields.name: gather_node_record_index
fields.meaning: 1-based index into the anim/content record container (app+0x4E0 = *0x70EEE0) of the herb or mineral node the player is gathering from. The node entity's +0xE60 value is copied into app+0x1540 by the proximity scan (within 0x32 of the local player on +0x15A4/+0x15A8). The container record has +0x644 = 1 for mineral, 2 for herb, and +0x640 = node grade. This is a content/type index, not a per-spawn uid.
fields.dest_or_source: [window 0x295 + 0x11C], set at gather start by FUN_0048a260 from FUN_00467b00 param_2 = [app+0x1540]

fields.meaning: Item id of the gathering tool used: garden shovel 0x8A7-0x8AA for Herb Gathering, shovel 0x8AB-0x8AE for Mining
fields.dest_or_source: low word of [window 0x295 + 0x134], set by FUN_00483270 at gather start (MOVZX of the used item id)

specs.semantics: Tells the server that the client's 5-second gathering (Mining or Herb Gathering) progress bar has finished, and for which node type and with which tool. Each frame the client first checks for craft progress window 0x293 in state 3; only if that is absent or not in state 3 does it check gather window 0x295. When window 0x295 is in state 3 and timeGetTime() - [app+0xD5C+0x5C] > 5000 ms (unsigned; the 5000.0 constant at 0x4A67AC was verified), the client sends this packet. It then sets +0x5C = 0 and closes window 0x295 with FUN_00483430(0x295,1,1). Any window-0x295 event also clears the busy flag [app+0xD84] (= this+0x28) via FUN_00446300 at 0x446A26. While the bar is running it only updates the gauge (FUN_004891e0) and sends nothing.
specs.trigger: Player uses a gathering tool item (item def +0x154 == 2) while standing near a herb node (interaction code 0x138) or mineral node (0x139), with the matching skill (0x56 Herb Gathering / 0x52 Mining), a tool of the right grade and enough level. The 5 s progress bar in window 0x295 must then finish.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x8F (SubHandler1 @0x46E90F): u8 result, u16 tool_item_id (client removes 1 of this item, even on failure); if result==1, u16 obtained_item_id is added with FUN_00440920. result 0x11 shows 'There isn't empty space in the inventory.', any other value shows 'Failed to obtian item.'. The handler clears the busy flag this+0x28.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: this+0x28 must be 0 to start (not already gathering). Tool id must be 0x8A7-0x8AE. The player's interaction code [[scene+0x928]+0x94] must be 0x138 (herb) or 0x139 (mining). The record at app+0x1540 must have +0x644 of 2 or 1. The skill must be known, FUN_00427310 must pass the tool-grade check, and the item level must be <= the player's level. At send time, if [win0x295+0x11C] == 0 the function returns without sending, without closing the window and without resetting the timer, so the progress window stays stuck. That should not happen because the start requires a non-zero record. The window closes right after sending, so the client does not wait for 0x8F to hide the bar. The timing is purely client-side.
specs.references: No PySlayer parser or builder for C2S 0x69 or S2C 0x8F. Not in windslayer_server.py _dispatch. Crafting and gathering strings confirm the system: 'Mining', 'Herb Gathering', 'You need a shovel to conduct mining...', 'Learn the Herb Gathering skill from Lona in Popola'.
open_questions: Does the server need a per-spawn node identity? The client only sends the content record index (+0xE60), so the server must pick the drop from the node type/grade.
Exact meaning of window state value 3 at +0x3C (probably visible/open).
blind_open_questions: Is entity+0xE60 a per-map object instance index or a template index? It is 1-based into the [main+0x4E0] list; the server must map it back to the same node.
What the u16 read after a successful 0x8F means (quantity or a second item id), because FUN_00440920 was not traced.

Chat-mode path: a plain line (type 3) first runs case 3: sprintf_s(buf61,0x3D,"%s",text+prefix_len) is copied back and EBX=text (0x445906)
Only for type 3 with [g_ui_root+0x44]!=0: mode switch table 0x445E68, where mode 2 goes to 0x44594C
Mode 2: sprintf_s(buf88 @esp+0x158, 0x58, "%s : %s", scene+0x206, EBX). type=0x6A (0x445996), [esp+0x18]=strlen (0x4459AB), strcpy back into EBX (0x4459C0)
Final switch (idx 0x445E90, table 0x445E7C): type 0x6A goes to 0x445B4C
Second party check FUN_004837c0(ctrl 0x75). ==1 jumps to 0x4454A3 (party error, no send)
Anti-spam: [this+0x364]-[this+0x3E8] < 0x2BC (unsigned) shows "Do not Spam.", refreshes +0x3E8 and skips the send. Otherwise +0x3E8 = now (0x445BA9)
Add(char* EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]): exactly text_len raw bytes
Send(1) on g_sock_game, then jumps to 0x445D18 (return 0)

specs.grammar:
u8 text_len
bytes[text_len] text

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: strlen of the client-formatted party line, with no NUL counted. It comes from an 88-byte sprintf_s buffer, so it is at most 87.
fields.dest_or_source: stack byte [esp+0x18], set at 0x44555B (prefix path) or 0x4459AB (party chat-mode path)

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: The client-built string "<own character name> : <message>" (format "%s : %s" at 0x6F7C30; name from scene+0x206). The client strips the "/p " or "/\xA4\xC4 " prefix first. No NUL terminator on the wire.
fields.dest_or_source: EBX = the caller's text buffer, overwritten in place by the formatted string

specs.semantics: Party chat line for the server to relay to party members. The sender name is embedded in the text by the client. Two client paths reach this send. (A) Prefix path: the input starts with "/p " (3 bytes) or "/\xA4\xC4 " (4 bytes). The client sets type 0x6A and chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44]=2, checks party membership, rejects an exact "/p " or "/ㅔ " with a usage popup, formats "%s : %s" (own name, text+prefix_len) into 88 bytes, copies it back over the input and refreshes chat UI windows 9/10. (B) Chat-mode path: a plain line while [g_ui_root+0x44]==2 (party tab or an earlier /p). The line is type 3, so it first goes through case 3 (sprintf_s(61,"%s") copy-back), then the mode switch reformats it as "%s : %s" and changes the type to 0x6A. Both paths then pass the second party check and the 700 ms anti-spam check, and send u8 len + raw bytes. There is no local echo. The function returns 0, so caller FUN_004449b0 resets the IME result and clears this+0x14D8.
specs.trigger: The player presses Enter in the chat box (FUN_004449b0, IME result string at [0x70E708]+0x104) on "/p message" or "/ㅔ message", or on any plain line while the chat mode is party (set by the party chat tab at 0x448B04 in FUN_00446300 or by an earlier /p). It can also come from a chat macro slot (FUN_0043db00) or the UI list control 0x294 (FUN_00446300 @0x44AE75) if their text starts with "/p ".
specs.expected_response: The client waits for nothing. The S2C opcode used to show relayed party chat was not identified. S2C 0x6A (sub-handler 4 @0x461BDA) reads u32,u32,i32+list and is not chat. The only other user of the "%s : %s" format is the S2C 0x16 normal-chat handler (0x451CEA).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates, in order: the length arg is > 0 (0x444AC2). Curse_Engine_Clean passes, else "No cursing please" and return -1. Manner [scene+0xEE0] > -40, else the low-manner popup. [scene+0xF00]==6, else a silent return. A GM ([scene+0x970]+0x12==1) goes through GM command parsing first. The party check FUN_004837c0(g_ui_root, 0x75) walks the control list at g_ui_root+0x5C0 and returns ctrl+0x3C, or 1 if the control is missing; ==1 means not in a party. This check runs twice on path A (0x445499, 0x445B53) and once on path B. An exact "/p " or "/ㅔ " shows "/p message to party" and returns 0x6A, so the IME text is kept. Anti-spam blocks a send within 700 ms of the last chat. Client-side hazards: sprintf_s at 0x48A8CF is the real CRT sprintf_s (via __vsprintf_s_l) and does NOT truncate. Output over 87 chars, or over 60 chars in case 3 on path B, calls the CRT invalid-parameter handler, likely terminating the client. The copy-back is an unbounded strcpy of up to 88 bytes into the caller's buffer. For a macro slot (37 B at this+0xE88+i*0x25) this overwrites the next slot(s). For the 0x294 caller it is a 64-byte stack buffer. Server note: the embedded "name : " is client-controlled and spoofable. Use the session character name instead. In theory, text_len can be 0 with EBX=[esp+0x20]=0 (0x4454F2 -> 0x445433 -> 0x445A67), sending "6A 00". That needs length arg <= prefix_len without matching the exact usage strings, which cannot happen because all 3 callers pass strlen. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C41, chat_mail_gm#00, party#06): a length-prefixed text field carries EXACTLY the prefixed number of bytes and NO trailing NUL - the client terminates the string itself. (The wsproto codec forced a NUL into the last byte of str[<length field>], which is only correct for a fixed str[N]; every length-prefixed text in the campaign had to be sent with len+1 or as raw hex to work around it. The grammar here is correct as written.) Live capture: "/p hi there" produced payload 13 + the raw 19-byte string "TestHero : hi there" with no NUL and no local echo. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C46, premium_cash#19, party#06): the client-side Curse_Engine filters the text BEFORE sending, so an unmodified client never delivers a blocked word - the server's own filter will never see one. The filter matches SUBSTRINGS: the literal "hello" is rejected because it contains "hell", the client shows "No cursing please" and sends NOTHING at all. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49, party#06): the "not in a party" refusal is a system-notice line in the floating overlay, not a modal popup.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire grammar, u8 len + bytes[len] with opcode 0x6A, and the asm confirms it. 0x445BAF Add(u8 [esp+0x10]), 0x445BBC Add(u8 [esp+0x18]), 0x445BCB Add(EBX, movzx [esp+0x18]), 0x445BD9 Send(1), all on [0x70E6F4]. The disagreement was only about preprocessing detail. B was right that the chat-mode-2 path first runs case 3 (0x445872, sprintf_s(61,"%s") copy-back): the jump table at 0x445DE8 sends type 3 to 0x445872, and only after that does 0x44545F use the mode table (0x445E68, mode 2 -> 0x44594C). A's "same formatting" left this step out. B was wrong to call that step truncation to 60: 0x48A8CF is sprintf_s -> __vsprintf_s_l with (buf,size,fmt,arg) and no _TRUNCATE count, so over-length input triggers the CRT invalid-parameter handler, as A said. Both were right about the party check (FUN_004837c0 returns ctrl 0x75's +0x3C, or 1 if absent), the usage popup and the 700 ms anti-spam. B's len-0 corner case matches the code but cannot be reached. Added here: the in-place copy-back overflow hazard for macro slots and the 0x294 list caller. Other references: no PySlayer parser for C2S 0x6A, and windslayer_server.py _dispatch has no 0x6A branch.
open_questions: Which S2C opcode the EN client uses to show a relayed party chat line (not found; S2C 0x6A is not chat).
Does ctrl 0x75 +0x3C == 1 mean 'no party'? The UI popup text strongly implies it, but the control's full semantics were not traced.
Is there a custom CRT invalid-parameter handler? None was found by name in functions.tsv, so an over-length sprintf_s probably terminates the client.

spec_errata.new: substring filter; a blocked word means zero packets

specs.name: FriendChatMessage
specs.socket: game. The CMessenger object's +0x74 socket pointer is loaded from g_sock_game [0x70E6F4] at 0x46F86A and stored at 0x46F934 in FUN_0046f860, which the S2C 0x03 handler calls at 0x44E52F.

locations.role: Builds the packet (ESI = CMessenger, the stack holds len and text): walks the friend list, Adds the entries, then Adds the text and prepends the count and the opcode
AddToHead(uchar 0x6B) opcode (prepended last, so it is the first byte)
Only caller: pushes the text pointer EBX and movzx byte [ESP+0x18] (len), with ESI = [main+0x4E4] messenger
strncmp against "/f " (0x6F3AB8) and _strnicmp against "/\xA4\xA9 " (0x6F3A94). Either one sets chat type 0x6B and ui_root+0x44 = 4
sprintf_s(buf, 0x58, "%s : %s", player_record+0x206, msg) for the /f path, then strlen into [ESP+0x18] at 0x445751. The sticky mode-4 path does the same at 0x445A0C/0x445A2F
Local echo FUN_00445f00(text, color 0xFF8EE085) before the messenger socket check and the send
S2C 0x91 receiver: u8 len, then char-buffer read of len bytes into an 88-byte zeroed buffer, printed with the same color 0xFF8EE085

specs.grammar:
u8 recipient_count
repeat(recipient_count) {
  u8 friend_channel
  u32 friend_id
}
u8 msg_len
str[msg_len] message

fields.name: recipient_count
fields.dest_or_source: Loop counter BL (copied to [ESP+0xC]), prepended with AddToHead(uchar) after the body is built, so it comes right after the opcode on the wire
fields.meaning: Number of (channel, id) recipient entries that follow. Always >= 1, because the packet is not sent when it is 0.

fields.name: friend_channel
fields.dest_or_source: friend_entry+0x14 (CMessenger CPList head at +0x08; entry pointer = node+0x08; filled by S2C 0x0B/0x0C/0x60)
fields.meaning: Channel byte of the friend. An entry is included only if entry+0x20 (presence) is 0 or 4 and this byte is non-zero.

fields.name: friend_id
fields.meaning: Friend's character id (the key S2C 0x60 matches on), naming the recipient

fields.name: msg_len
fields.dest_or_source: arg1 = movzx byte [ESP+0x18] in FUN_00444a90 = strlen of the sprintf_s result (0x445751 or 0x445A2F)
fields.meaning: Byte length of message. No NUL is counted or sent.

fields.name: message
fields.dest_or_source: arg2 = chat input buffer (EBX), overwritten with the formatted string
fields.meaning: Display line "<own char name> : <text>", built by the client from player_record+0x206 and the typed text. Exactly msg_len bytes, with no terminator. CP949 text.

specs.semantics: Friend chat. FUN_0046fd80 walks the CMessenger friend list (list head at messenger+0x08, next pointer at node+0, entry at node+8) in list order. For each non-null entry with presence [+0x20] of 0 or 4 and a non-zero channel byte [+0x14], it Adds u8 channel and u32 id and increments BL. If BL != 0 it Adds u8 len and the len text bytes, then AddToHead(count) and AddToHead(0x6B), so the wire order is 6B, count, entries, len, text. Then it calls Send(1). No ResetBuffer is called here; the socket buffer is assumed empty. The text already contains the sender's name. The client prints its own copy locally before this function runs, so the server must not echo it back to the sender.
specs.trigger: A chat line starting with "/f " (0x6F3AB8) or the Korean-IME form "/\xA4\xA9 " (0x6F3A94), or any plain chat line while sticky chat mode [g_ui_root+0x44] == 4 (set by an earlier /f).
specs.expected_response: The client waits for nothing. A server should relay S2C 0x91 {u8 len, str[len] text} (receiver at 0x457C01, same color 0xFF8EE085) to each listed recipient that is really online, and send nothing back to the sender.
specs.gates_and_hazards: FUN_00444a90 gates: Curse_Engine_Clean ("No cursing please") at 0x444AC9. Manner points [player_record+0xEE0] must be > -40 (CMP -0x28 / JG at 0x444AF9), otherwise "You can't chat with others due to your low manner point." A bare "/f " with no text shows the "/f message to friends" hint and sends nothing. Anti-spam: [main+0x364]-[main+0x3E8] < 700 shows "Do not Spam." (0x445BF2). The local echo happens at 0x445C28. Then [messenger+0x74] must be non-zero (0x445C33), i.e. S2C 0x03 has already initialized the messenger. FUN_0046fd80: an empty list returns before any Add (0x46FD8E). If entries exist but none qualify, BL stays 0 and nothing is Added or sent, even though the line was already echoed locally. Hazard (not reachable in practice): the entry Adds happen before the count test, so 256 qualifying friends would wrap BL to 0 and leave stale bytes in the socket buffer, and more than 256 would send a wrong count. Receivers copy len bytes into an 88-byte zeroed buffer (memset 0x57 plus a 0 byte), so a server relaying S2C 0x91 must keep len <= 87. sprintf_s uses a 0x58 buffer, so the client-built text is <= 87 bytes.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts derived the same wire layout: after the opcode come u8 count, then count x (u8 channel, u32 id), then u8 len, then len text bytes. The "structural signature" difference is only in typing and truncation. A typed the text as bytes[msg_len]; B typed it as str[text_len], and B's signature string simply dropped the final field. The asm at 0x46FDDB-0x46FE14 settles it. arg1 (EDI = [ESP+0x14]) is pushed once for Add(uchar) at 0x46FDE3, then pushed again as N together with arg2 ([ESP+0x18]) for Add(char*,N) at 0x46FDF2. After that come AddToHead(BL) at 0x46FE06, AddToHead(0x6B) at 0x46FE0D and Send(1) at 0x46FE14. There is no NUL and no other field, so both layouts are correct. Because the payload is client-formatted display text (sprintf_s "%s : %s" at 0x445734 and 0x445A0C, with strlen stored at 0x445751 and 0x445A2F), str[msg_len] (exactly len bytes, no terminator) is the right DSL type; on the wire it is identical to bytes[msg_len]. On the one factual point where they differ, A is right and B left it open: the delivery packet is S2C 0x91. Its handler at 0x457C01 reads u8 len (IAT 0x4A4094) and then len chars (IAT 0x4A4098) into an 88-byte buffer, and prints them with color 0xFF8EE085. That constant appears in only two places in the corpus: the /f local echo at 0x445C1B and 0x457C5C. A's manner-point gate is confirmed (CMP [rec+0xEE0],-0x28 / JG at 0x444AF9). Socket: CMessenger+0x74 = g_sock_game, loaded at 0x46F86A and stored at 0x46F934, as both analysts said. Other references: PySlayer has no C2S parse_0x6B (its S2C 0x6B is unrelated). Our server's _dispatch has no 0x6B branch. Not in the memory notes or the opcode atlas.
open_questions: Presence values: 1 = offline is confirmed by the 'not on line' check at 0x472A0A. 0 = same channel and 4 = other channel are inferred from the S2C 0x60/0x7A/0x7E handlers and not verified here.
Whether the original server trusted the client-supplied recipient list or checked it against its own friend table is unknown. A safe server should intersect it with the stored friend list.
It is not proven that friend_id (entry+0x18) shares the id space of entity uid (+0x84) or the character DB id.
Whether an over-long input (formatted line > 87 chars) is prevented by the edit-box limit, or instead reaches the sprintf_s invalid-parameter handler, was not checked.

specs.name: TrapTriggered
specs.socket: game (g_sock_game, used through its copy at scene+0xF94; CreateSockets writes scene+0xF94 = [0x70E6F4] at 0x44030B)

locations.function: FUN_0042b260 (30 ms fixed-step sim tick, no static callers = timer/WndProc path)
locations.role: caller gate: the whole simulation (incl. FUN_00416380) runs only when room_info(app+0x4D8 == scene+0xF88)+0x70 == 0 (non-PvP) and scene+0xF00 in {4,5,6}
call FUN_00416380(scene, entity): extra ticks for state-3 entities with +0x135C > 1
owner gate: room_info+0x70 == 1 OR owner uid(+0x84) == scene+0x220 (own character uid)
loop over 21 (0x15) effect slots at owner+0xE84, 0x18 bytes each
slot gates: skill_id(+0) != 0, remaining time i32(+0xC) > 0, 0xA31 <= skill_id <= 0xA3B, owner+0x950 == 0
CSpriteControl::GetColRect(rect, 0xE1, slot.x u16 @+6, slot.y u16 @+8, 0x1E, 2): trap hit box
scan scene entity list for the first eligible victim (see gates)
FUN_0041ce20(scene,&box,victim,0,0) victim box; rectangle overlap test 0x417C5B-0x417C99
owner+0x950 = 0xC (trap-catch state), cross-link owner/victim uids (+0xD78/+0xD80/+0xD64/+0xD60), victim+0x958 = 600
slot remaining time (+0xC) = 0 so the trap cannot fire again
send gate: scene+0xF24 == 0 (always true in this binary)
related: C2S 0x15 skill use appends u16 x/u16 y (+0x15A4/+0x15A8) only for skills 0xA31..0xA3B = trap placement
related: C2S 0x0D movement adds u16 owner+0x8D4 when local player +0x950 == 0xC

specs.grammar: u16 trap_skill_id

fields.name: trap_skill_id
fields.meaning: Skill id of the trap that fired, level-specific, always 0xA31..0xA3B (2609..2619, 11 levels of one trap skill). It is the u16 at +0 of the owner's effect slot.
fields.dest_or_source: word [slot+0x00], slot = owner_entity+0xE84+i*0x18 (i=0..20); the same value is also copied to owner+0x8D4

specs.semantics: Sent when a trap the player placed is set off. Every 30 ms tick the client walks the owner entity's 21 effect slots at +0xE84 (each 0x18 bytes: +0 u16 skill_id, +6 u16 x, +8 u16 y, +0xC i32 remaining ms, +0x14 u32 caster uid). For a slot whose skill is 0xA31..0xA3B and still has time left, it builds the hit box with GetColRect(sprite 0xE1, x, y, 0x1E, 2). It then finds the first entity in the scene list whose collision box (FUN_0041ce20) overlaps that box. On a hit the client locally: sets owner+0x950 = 0xC (a catch/grab state that FUN_00412360 turns into 9 on the next tick); links the two entities (owner+0xD78 = owner+0xD64 = victim uid, victim+0xD80 = victim+0xD60 = owner uid); sets victim+0x958 = 600; stores the victim-owner dx/dy in owner+0x1328/+0x1330; sets owner+0x8D4 = skill_id (FUN_00418ac0 uses it as the damage source, see the push 0xA31 at 0x418DC6); and zeroes the slot timer. It then sends [0x6C][u16 skill_id] on the game socket. The packet tells the server that this trap fired. Because it carries no victim uid, the server has to work out the victim itself, or get it from the grab block of the next C2S 0x0D.
specs.trigger: Automatic, from the fixed-step sim tick FUN_0042b260 -> FUN_00416380. Sent when a monster (or, in PvP, an enemy-team player) walks into a trap placed with a 0xA31..0xA3B skill (placed via C2S 0x15 with x,y). No user click is involved.
specs.expected_response: The client does not wait for any reply. A server should probably apply the trap's effect/damage to the caught entity and remove the consumed trap slot on the owner (for example via its effect-removal / skill-hit S2C). The client zeroes only the slot timer and never clears the slot itself.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Victim eligibility, evaluated in scene-list order with the first match used: victim != owner; and either (victim +0x98 == 3 AND room_info+0x70 == 1 AND victim team +0x14EB != owner team) or (owner +0x98 == 3 AND victim +0x98 == 4 AND victim +0xE64 (gamedef category) >= 3, i.e. an AI monster). The branch 'owner +0x98 == 4 AND victim uid == scene+0x220' can never match here because the owner is already required to be state 3. Also required: victim +0x904 (action) not in {0x14, 0x10, 0x16}; if victim +0xDF0 > 0 or action in {3, 0x17}, the victim must be state 4; the boxes must overlap; victim +0x94C == 0 (not already caught). At most one 0x6C per owner per tick, because owner+0x950 becomes nonzero. The caller only runs this function when room_info+0x70 == 0, so in practice the owner must be a state-3 entity whose uid == scene+0x220. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C28, combat_skill#22): there is NO reachability problem - in normal field play (scene+0xF00 == 6) the local player spawned by S2C 0x07 IS a state-3 entity and C2S 0x6C fires. Live facts to use instead: the trap slot needs +0xC > 0 and the client counts it down from the skill's Con (7020 ms), so a trap is live for about 7 s client-side; MP cost -16 per placement; one trap slot only (a re-cast replaces it). Victim eligibility has an unexplained extra condition: server-spawned 0x1A monsters (action_state 0, +0xDF0 = -20) were never caught, even at the trap's exact x,y, while client-revived monsters (action 0xC, +0xDF0 = 0) were caught instantly. Nothing on the client stops the same trap from being re-reported once the server refreshes the slot timer.
specs.references: No C2S parser in PySlayer (client_packets only has 0x03/0x0B/0x0C/0x0D/0x0F/0x15/0x1A/0x2B/0x2C/0x7E). windslayer_server.py _dispatch has no 0x6C branch (it falls through to the unknown-opcode log). The S2C 0x6C handler (0x462273, mileage/'50% bonus mileage') is unrelated because opcode numbers are direction-specific. Consistent with the in-binary C2S 0x15 trap placement at FUN_0044c090 (adds x,y only for 0xA31..0xA3B) and with the S2C 0x3C/0x43 handler checking 0xA31..0xA3B at 0x456714. The memory note 'alive state 3 remote / 4 local' agrees with the reachability concern above. Not seen in live captures, which is consistent with it being unreachable in field mode.
open_questions: [RESOLVED by live verification combat_skill#22, 2026-09-17] Live: the premise was wrong - in field mode (scene+0xF00 == 6) the local player spawned by S2C 0x07 is a state-3 entity with uid == scene+0x220, and 0x6C fires normally. Original question: "What is the exact game mode where the own character is a state-3 entity with uid == scene+0x220 and room_info+0x70 == 0? Presumably scene+0xF00 == 4 or 5 room modes. In field mode (0xF00 == 6) the local player is state 4, so the owner gate fails."
What should the server reply with? No response is awaited, and the S2C opcode that removes the trap slot or applies the trap hit is not determined here.
Which skill/class name goes with 0xA31..0xA3B? It is probably a Trapper skill ('Trapper' strings exist), but it is not tied to a name table.
What does victim+0x958 = 600 mean (hold/stun duration in ms?), and what does FUN_00411ee0 do to the victim?

Victim eligibility: server-spawned 0x1A monsters (action_state 0, +0xDF0 = -20) are never caught by a trap, while client-revived ones (action 0xC, +0xDF0 = 0) are caught instantly (combat_skill#22). Re-check the +0xDF0 / action compare near 0x417B80-0x417C52 (sign vs != 0) and FUN_0041ce20's collision box for action 0.
blind_open_questions: The victim is not on the wire. Does the real server work out the victim/damage from its own trap simulation, or was the victim reported by another packet (none seen in this function)?
Exact meaning of owner+0x950 (=0x0C) and target+0x958 (=600): trap cooldown and stun/hold duration are guesses.
Entity state byte +0x98 semantics (3 vs 4) conflict with the memory notes. That affects whether this packet can ever fire with the current server's local-player spawn.

specs.name: ComplimentPlayer

gate: param_3==10, socket non-NULL, target_id non-zero

u32 target_id
str[17] target_name

fields.name: target_id
fields.meaning: complimented player's id (window 0x435 user data +0x134 copied from popup window 0x50 +0x134); S2C 0x96 later matches this id against entity uid +0x84

fields.meaning: target character name; exactly 17 bytes copied straight from control 8's label buffer (+0x50), so bytes after the NUL may be stale/non-zero - read up to first NUL

specs.semantics: Gives a 'compliment' (raises manner points) to another player, from the Compliment window 0x435 opened via the player popup menu. Sent on the confirm button (control 10); the client does not close the window or change local state on this path.
specs.trigger: Confirm (control 10) in compliment window 0x435. specs.name: PlayerReport
specs.socket: game (CMessenger+0x74 = cached g_sock_game 0x70E6F4; NOT null-checked on this path, loaded at 0x47356C)

locations.role: Right-clicking another player sets popup dlg 0x50 +0x134 = entity+0x84 uid (per analyst B).
Popup 0x50 item 11 calls FUN_00473bb0(CMessenger, uid=[dlg0x50+0x134]) with the name from popup ctrl 2 in ECX.

Opens report window 0x434: +0x134 = target uid (FUN_00483270), ctrl 10 = name, ctrl 12 = fee label, +0x40 = fee (FUN_004832f0 at 0x473C8D). Category radios 0x15..0x1B are set to state 3. CMessenger+0xD8 is NOT reset.
Category radio ctrl 0x15..0x1B: CMessenger+0xD8 = ctrl-0x15; the label comes from string table 0x706888 (14-byte entries).
u64 gold [info+0x228/+0x22C] >= fee, else 'You are short of gold.'
Ctrl 10 edit text (+0xD1), strcpy'd into the zeroed 17-byte local [ESP+0x14]
Name validation (its strings: 'Enter your name.', 'No blank is allowed in Name.', 'Invalid name...')
Name == own name [info+0x1BE] (case-sensitive), else 'You can't report your own character.'
Ctrl 0x11 edit text, strcpy'd into [ESP+0x28] (1 byte + 0x70 bytes zeroed; 132 bytes to the cookie)
content_len = (u8)strlen. If 0, shows 'Please enter the contents.'

specs.grammar:
u32 target_uid
str[17] target_name
u32 report_fee
u8 category
u8 content_len
bytes[content_len] content

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: Uid of the reported player. It is carried from the right-click popup (dlg 0x50 +0x134) into report window 0x434 +0x134. The client does not validate it and it can be 0.

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: Reported character name from window 0x434 ctrl 10. It is strcpy'd into a 17-byte local that was zeroed first, so it is NUL-padded to 17 bytes. The user can edit it.

fields.name: report_fee
fields.meaning: Gold fee computed by the client when the window opens: v = u8 [[info+0x928]+0x99] (probably level); fee = (v%10==0 ? v/10 : v/10+1)*100. The client checks gold >= fee but does not deduct it.

fields.name: category
fields.meaning: Report reason 0..6: 0 Abuse, 1 Spamming, 2 Item Fraud, 3 Real Trading, 4 Assuming a GM, 5 Leakage Info, 6 Hacking Tools (string table 0x706888)
fields.dest_or_source: CMessenger+0xD8 (set to 0 at messenger init 0x46F976; updated only by radio clicks at 0x4733FB)

fields.name: content_len
fields.meaning: strlen(content) truncated to 8 bits; the client requires it to be non-zero (TEST AL,AL / JA at 0x473540)

fields.name: content
fields.meaning: Free-text report description, exactly content_len bytes, with no NUL terminator on the wire

specs.semantics: Files an abuse report against another player from report window 0x434, which is opened from the right-click player popup (item 11). The user picks a category radio, types a description and presses ctrl 0x1C. The client checks, in this order: u64 gold >= fee ('You are short of gold.'); the name passes FUN_0043df40; the name differs from the player's own name ('You can't report your own character.'); content_len != 0 ('Please enter the contents.'). It then builds the packet above, sends it and hides window 0x434. It does not deduct gold locally. On success, S2C 0x95 carries the new gold total.
specs.trigger: Report window 0x434 button ctrl 0x1C, reached through right-click on a player, then popup 0x50 item 11.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x95 (handler 0x471DA3): u8 result. result==1: u64 gold -> info+0x228, gold HUD refreshed (FUN_004659d0), message 'Reported successively.'. result==2: 'The character doesn't exist. Please check and try again.' (0x471C58). result==7: 'You can report a player only once a day.'. Any other value is ignored silently.
specs.gates_and_hazards: CMessenger+0x74 is used without a NULL check (0x47356C), so the client would crash if S2C 0x03 was never handled. CMessenger+0xD8 is not reset when the window reopens (FUN_00473bb0 only sets the radio visuals), so a report sent without clicking a category carries the previous report's category, or 0 after messenger init. The server should range-check 0..6. Both strcpy calls are unbounded: the name goes into 17 bytes and the content into 132 bytes before the stack cookie, limited only by the edit controls. FUN_0048a030 returning NULL (missing control) would crash in strcpy. content_len is strlen mod 256. The fee and name are client-supplied, so the server should recompute the fee from the player's level and resolve the target from target_uid (or the name).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B found identical fields in identical order: u32 uid, 17-byte name, u32 fee, u8 category, u8 len, len-byte content. The structural signatures differ only because B wrote the last field as 'str[content_len]', which the signature extractor dropped, while A wrote 'bytes[content_len]'. The asm settles the order and widths. Add(u8 0x6E) at 0x473579. Add(uint EDI=FUN_004832b0(0x434)) at 0x473585 through IAT 0x4A40F0. PUSH 0x11 and LEA ECX,[ESP+0x18] (the name at [ESP+0x14] after one push), then Add(char*,17) at 0x473591. MOV EDX,[ESP+0x10] (fee) and Add(uint) at 0x47359F. MOVZX EAX,byte [EBX+0xD8] and Add(uchar) at 0x4735AC. [ESP+0xC] and Add(uchar) at 0x4735B6. PUSH MOVZX [ESP+0xC] and LEA EAX,[ESP+0x2C] (content at [ESP+0x28] after one push), then Add(char*,len) at 0x4735C6. The content has no NUL and is not padded, so bytes[content_len] is the accurate DSL. On side details A is more correct than B: category +0xD8 is set to 0 at messenger init (0x46F976), so it is not uninitialised, only stale across reports; and the reply exists as S2C 0x95 (0x471DA3: u8 result, and on 1 a u64 gold into info+0x228), which B marked unknown. game_system is set to admin_gm because this is a GM moderation report, even though CMessenger builds it. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.
open_questions: Whether u8 [[info+0x928]+0x99] is the character level (strongly suggested by the fee formula and our server's SetLevel notes, not proven here).
Maximum text lengths enforced by window 0x434 edit controls 10 and 0x11 were not determined.
What the second argument 0 to FUN_0043df40 disables (e.g. the reserved-word list 'gamemaster', 'yahoo', ...), i.e. whether names containing those words can be reported.

Magic-number division: EDI = v/10000 (region slot), ESI = v%10000 (destination map id)

If v/10000 >= 1: region window DAT_00709298[v/10000] gets +0x134 = 0 and is closed. This runs whether or not the packet was sent
Using item 3430/3432/3434 (0xD66/0xD68/0xD6A) opens world map window 0x0A (unless its state is 3) and sets its +0x134 = item id

Confirms the encoding: region code == map_id/100 (table 0x70D04C) and destination control+0x28 == map_id%100

specs.grammar:
u16 item_id
i32 dest_map_id

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item definition id of the Region Warp Stone used: 3430 (x50), 3432 (x20) or 3434 (x10)
fields.dest_or_source: Window 0x471 +0x134. Copied from the region window, which got it from world map window 0x0A, which was set on item use (FUN_00463d90 @0x463F17). Low 16 bits

fields.name: dest_map_id
fields.meaning: Destination map id = region_code*100 + map suffix (e.g. 101). Region codes by region slot 0..9 (table 0x70B9AE): 1 The Beginning of the Adventure, 2 Popola Village, 4 Ozzi Village, 7 Balderan, 5 Amakusa, 8 Mining Settlement, 6 Atajokuna, 9 Serien the City of Water, 10 Serien Underworld, 11 Underwater City RA
fields.dest_or_source: (window 0x471 +0x40) % 10000. The +0x40 value was built at 0x44B6F3 as clicked control+0x28 (map_id%100) + (region_code[i] + 100*(i+1))*100

specs.semantics: Asks the server to teleport the player to the chosen map, using one charge of a Region Warp Stone. The client packs the region-window slot (v/10000) and the map id (v%10000) into one int, but only the map id goes on the wire. After OK the client clears the item id on that region window and closes it. It shows no waiting dialog.
specs.trigger: The player uses a Region Warp Stone, opens a region on the world map, clicks a destination (only allowed while the region window's +0x134 item id is not 0), then clicks OK (control 6) in confirmation window 0x471.
specs.expected_response: Most likely S2C 0x9A: u8 result; if ==1: u32 inventory_entry_id (item count -1); otherwise 'You are unable to transfer\r\nto the area.' The map change itself probably follows through the normal map-change packets (not verified).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No packet is sent if the u16 item_id is 0 or dest_map_id <= 0; the region window is still reset and closed when v/10000 >= 1. Region windows opened without a warp stone have +0x134 == 0, so confirmation window 0x471 never opens (0x44B6BB). The encoding assumes map suffix < 100; a control value >= 100 would change v/10000 and the map id. The server must validate that dest_map_id is a real, allowed destination.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer or in windslayer_server.py. The scout guess (0x70 + u16 + i32) matches. Region names come from pointer table 0x70B8B8. The region code tables at 0x70B9AE and 0x70D04C are identical, and DAT_00709298[i+1] == DAT_0070BA1C[i] (same window ids).
open_questions: Confirm that S2C 0x9A is the reply to C2S 0x70 (inferred from its error string).
Which packets perform the warp after success (probably the usual 0x08 + map replay)?
It is not verified that every region-window destination control's +0x28 is below 100 (FUN_0042c450 strongly suggests map_id%100).
blind_open_questions: Is destination_code exactly a map id (e.g. 101), or a location index the server maps to a map plus spawn point? control_data comes from UI resource control +0x28 values, which were not dumped.
Confirm S2C 0x9A is the reply to 0x70 (inferred from its failure string).
Which spawn coordinates should the server use for each destination?

specs.socket: game (CMessenger+0x74 = cached g_sock_game 0x70E6F4; NOT null-checked on this path, loaded at 0x47369C)

locations.role: The NPC dialog manager opens service window 0x47B (FUN_004835b0). Frenaiga is the NPC named in 'Can't be add. Visit Frenaiga.'
Generic dialog click dispatch: FUN_00472900(CMessenger, 0x47B, ctrl)
Dialog routing: dlg-0x435-0x46==0, i.e. dlg==0x47B, goes to 0x47363E. EDI is still 1 from 0x472928.
u64 gold [info+0x22C]:[info+0x228] >= 50000 (0xC350), else 'You are short of gold.'
Friend capacity byte [CMessenger+0xD1] < 50 (0x32), else 'You can't add more friends to your friend list.'
PUSH EDI(=1); JMP 0x4736FE (shared Send tail, which also serves C2S 0x6D)
Friend window 0x176 ctrl 8 (add friend): count [+0xD0] == capacity [+0xD1] shows 'Can't be add. Visit Frenaiga.'
S2C 0x9D reply handler: writes capacity to +0xD1 and gold to info+0x228

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Buys more friend-list slots at the Frenaiga NPC service window 0x47B. On OK (ctrl 2) the client checks gold >= 50,000 and friend capacity (CMessenger+0xD1) < 50, then sends the bare opcode. It does not deduct gold or raise capacity locally; the server must do both and report back with S2C 0x9D. No amount or slot count is sent, so the server decides the increment and the price. CMessenger+0xD0 is the current friend count and +0xD1 the capacity; S2C 0x0B fills capacity first.
specs.trigger: OK (ctrl 2) in the Frenaiga friend-slot expansion window 0x47B.
specs.expected_response: S2C 0x9D (handler 0x471F07): u8 result. result==1: u8 new_capacity -> CMessenger+0xD1, u64 gold -> info+0x228 (gold HUD refresh), message box 'You added him/her on your friend list...', and window 0x176 ctrl 0x13 label '(count/capacity)'. Otherwise: 'You failed to added him/her on your friend list.'
specs.gates_and_hazards: The client requires gold >= 50000 and capacity < 50; the server must check both again. CMessenger+0x74 is not NULL-checked on this path, so the client crashes if the messenger was never initialised (S2C 0x03). The 50000 check is only a minimum-gold gate; the actual cost comes from the server through the u64 gold in 0x9D.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the packet is the bare opcode: Add(u8 0x73) at 0x4736A1, then PUSH EDI(=1) and JMP to the shared Send at 0x4736FE/0x473701. The difference was notation only ('(empty...)' vs 'stop'). The asm shows no Add on this path between the capacity gate at 0x47367C and the Send tail. The shared tail at 0x4736FE only reloads ECX=[EBX+0x74] before Send, so the u32/str[17] Adds of the 0x6D branch (0x4736C9-0x4736F6) are not on the 0x73 path. The naive scout wrongly merged the two branches. EDI is still 1: it is set at 0x472928 and not written on the route 0x47292D -> 0x472DC1 -> 0x47320A -> 0x473615 -> 0x47363E. On the expected response A is right and B's 'not identified' is superseded: S2C 0x9D at 0x471F07 reads u8 result, then u8 into CMessenger+0xD1 (0x471F33/0x471F3A) and u64 into info+0x228 (0x471F56), and prints '(%u/%u)' from +0xD0/+0xD1. Not in PySlayer, our server or the captures.
open_questions: Slots gained per purchase and the real price are server-defined (not visible in the client).

The 0x9D success text is the generic 'You added him/her on your friend list' string; whether another S2C was intended for expansion is unknown, but 0x9D is the only handler that writes +0xD1 besides init/0x0B.

specs.semantics: Asks the server for the Play&Chat room list. The body is the opcode byte only. When window 0x478 moves to state 3 or 4 from another state and the map-mode gate passes, the client sends this packet, then updates sub-controls and shows the window. It does not wait for a reply.

specs.expected_response: Nothing is awaited. The list is filled by S2C 0xA1 (clear the list at +0x450, refresh window 0x478, then parse entries via the 0xA0 code at 0x455A9E) and/or S2C 0xA0 (append entries). This mirrors the arena 0x33/0x32 pair.

(3) Unlike the 0x2C path, the gate comes before FUN_00489580. (4) No ResetBuffer. (5) Our server does not handle it: it is logged as unhandled, which is harmless but leaves the list empty.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree on the wire (opcode-only), socket and gates. They differ on grammar notation ("" vs "stop") and game_system (A pvp_arena, B social_friend). The asm shows one Add: PUSH 0x74 / CALL [0x4A40FC] at 0x44669F-0x4466A1, then Send(1) at 0x4466AD-0x4466AF on [0x70E6F4], with only a gate between 0x446685 and the Add. The canonical grammar is empty. For game_system, pvp_arena (the room-lobby subsystem) is correct: the window uses the same map-mode gate as the arena list; its list handlers 0xA1/0xA0 (0x455A2A/0x455A9E) mirror the arena 0x33/0x32 pair and both close window 0x16; the shared S2C 0x08 block handles room errors (0xA3 'The room has deleted due to inappropriate room name'); and PySlayer KR folds this request into C2S 0x2C code 4. It is not a friend/social feature. Other references: matches the live capture (P -> 0x74). Not in PySlayer client_packets. Not handled in windslayer_server.py.

specs.gates_and_hazards: The only condition is FUN_004837C0(0x478) != 1; the close path has no map-mode gate. Windows start in state 1 (FUN_004824D0 at 0x48255E), so the S2C 0x2F auto-close emits 0x75 only if the user actually has the list open. The server may still receive an unsolicited 0x75 right after it sends 0x2F. The S2C 0x08 map-load block does not close 0x478; it closes 0x2A, 0x480, 0x4D, 0x47A, 0x47E and 0x4B.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree on the wire (opcode-only, no map gate on close). They differ on grammar notation ("" vs "stop") and game_system (pvp_arena vs social_friend). B also noted that this Send site emits a second opcode, 0x2D; A covered that in its own spec. The asm shows PUSH 0x75 at 0x446A7D, then the shared tail: ECX=[0x70E6F4] at 0x446A7F, CALL [0x4A40FC] at 0x446A85, PUSH 1 / CALL [0x4A4108] at 0x446A91-0x446A93. Only two entries reach the tail: fall-through from 0x446A7D (0x75) and JMP 0x446A7F from 0x44674A (0x2D, grep-verified). The canonical grammar is empty; game_system is pvp_arena for the same reasons as C2S 0x74. B's open question about the initial window state is resolved: FUN_004824D0 sets [win+0x3C]=1 at 0x48255E, so spurious 0x75s occur only if the window is open. Other references: matches the live capture (close P list -> 0x75). Not handled by our server; not in PySlayer.
open_questions: Whether any UI loader step changes [win+0x3C] of window 0x478 from its creation value of 1 before the user interacts (not observed statically).

What the feature does cannot be determined from code: the immediate value 0x4A4 appears only at 0x44B63E, and 0x4A3/0x4A4 are not referenced by any S2C handler or string.

specs.expected_response: Unknown. The client shows no wait modal and hides nothing, so the server reply (or another UI action) must close window 0x4A4.

Asm 0x44B661 CMP ECX,2 / JNZ; 0x44B66A MOV ECX,[g_sock_game]; PUSH 0x7C; CALL Add(u8); JMP 0x4484C4 -> Send(1). No other Add, so the correct grammar is empty (length 0). Jump tables verified from the binary: 0x4A3 -> 0x44B632 and 0x4A4 -> 0x44B661. A grep of the whole asm corpus for 0x4a3/0x4a4 finds only PUSH 0x4A4 @0x44B63E. Not in our server or PySlayer. fields.name: portal_line_index
fields.dest_or_source: return value of FUN_00406df0 (EAX to ESI), Add(ulong) 0x4A40A4
fields.meaning: 0-based position, among ALL entries of the current map's collision-line list ([scene+0xF88]+0x58, built layer by layer, sprite by sprite, line by line in FUN_00406170), of the first line with type 0, event != 0, y1 == trunc(posY) and x1 <= trunc(posX) <= x2. Sent only when that line's sprite 'event' attribute == 1 (portal). This is the 'portal_code' used by PySlayer/our portals.json (capture 0x17 = 23 on map 101).

specs.semantics: Asks the server to use the portal the local player is standing on. The client does not change map by itself; it relies on the server's change-map/spawn packets. The line's value_num attribute is fetched but NOT sent.
specs.trigger: Player presses Up while standing on a portal. The check runs every logic tick and requires: scene+0xF00 == 6; [0x70EED8]+0x70 == 0 (not a P2P room); player (scene+0x970) != 0; player+0x8B4 == 4 (Up input); player+0x904 == 8 or 0xC; and app+0x364 (now, ms) > app+0x470 + 2500 (2.5 s cooldown). When these gates pass, app+0x470 = now whether or not a packet goes out.
specs.expected_response: Server change-map sequence: S2C 0x08 (new map code) then S2C 0x07 re-spawn at the destination (PySlayer). Our server also sends 0x03/0x0A/0x28/0x44. The send site has no client-side wait dialog or timer. The reply is the mandatory map-enter sequence S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07 (-> 0x0A/0x28/0x44 -> 0x1A), live-captured for the 101 -> 102 portal. Do NOT answer with a bare 0x08: it destroys the local player and hangs the client on the loading overlay (C1).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Latent client bug: if no line matches, FUN_00406df0 returns 0 without writing the event out-param. The caller then tests an uninitialized stack slot ([ESP+0x14], also written at 0x42D145 with entity+0x15B4). If that stale value is 1, a spurious 0x7E with index 0 is sent. The server must validate (map, index) against its portal table and ignore unknown entries, as our server already does. Match requires the truncated Y to equal the line's y1 exactly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C17, world_movement_npc#04/#06, shop_storage#20): EN portal indices differ from the KR-derived portals.json. Live: 101 -> 102 = 23 (0x17), 102 -> 101 = 31 (0x1F) (portals.json also carries an unused 102_26), 102 -> 103 = 17 (0x11) - portals.json only has 102_14, which is why every map past 102 is unreachable on the EN client. Map 201 additionally has an event portal tile to 9701 (flea market) at (2600,1600) with no portals.json entry at all. The map-101 portal trigger is at world (~1412, 814) - the MIDDLE depth tier: Up moves one depth tier back, Down moves one tier forward and fires the portal. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C18, world_movement_npc#04): the 2.5 s cooldown holds for presses made INSIDE the window, but input made during the ~1.5 s map load is NOT dropped - a second Down press made then fires another 0x7E right after the cooldown expires (observed 3.06 s apart), bouncing the player back through the arrival portal. The server should ignore a 0x7E that arrives within ~3 s of a transfer (or while the arrival spawn still sits on the destination's reverse portal tile).
specs.references: Agrees with PySlayer parse_7E (up32u(payload[1:5]) = portal_code, looked up per current map) and our _handle_change_map (struct '<I', key f'{cur_map}_{portal_code}'). The capture '17 00 00 00' matches.
open_questions: Semantics of player+0x904 values 8 vs 0xC (both allowed for portal use).
Whether the real server also checked player position or line validity; the client provides only the index.
blind_open_questions: What is rec+0x28 (second out value, unused here)? Maybe a destination/portal code the server could cross-check.
What do other rec+0x24 values (not 1) mean? Other trigger types in the same list.

fields.name: server_index
