specs.semantics: Embedded battle-host (room server) logic. At round end (mode 2) it walks the scene entity list. For each remote player (entity+0x98==3) that has a team (+0x14EB!=0), has +0x15DC==0 (flag set to 1 in FUN_00423850 when the player acts; probably 'did something this round'), and is in a room with game type scene+0xF70<=3, it clears the pending team (+0x14EC=0). It then broadcasts {room, index, 1, uid, team, 0} to every child socket of the CSNSockMan. In practice this removes idle players from their team. The in-client analogue on the real game socket is S2C 0x35 (u32 uid, u8 team, u8 pending_team at 0x455E94), which the game server sends instead.
specs.trigger: FUN_00428090(scene, 2) (round-end evaluation) when scene+0xF24 (host/server-mode flag) != 0. Unreachable in the EN 2008 client: +0xF24 is only ever written as 0, and +0xF98 (CSNSockMan*) is only ever written as NULL. A raw byte scan of the .text section for disp32 0xF24/0xF98 writes confirms this.
specs.expected_response: none (fire-and-forget broadcast; this client has no receiver for this format)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: param_2==2 && scene+0xF24!=0 (0x428110/0x428116); entity non-null, +0x98==3, +0x14EB!=0 (0x428155-0x42816A); entity+0x15DC==0 (0x42819C); scene+0xF70<=3 (0x4281A9). Sent once per child socket in the list [[scene+0xF98]+8]+4, inside that socket's critical section (+0x12C08). DEAD CODE in the EN client. If ever reached, [NULL+8] would crash, because +0xF98 is never set. A private server for this client never receives this packet on port 7022. Do NOT treat it as a C2S 0x93 handler: S2C 0x93 on the game socket means 'item expired' and is unrelated.
specs.references: No match in PySlayer (no 0x93 C2S parser; no GetChildSocketPtr use) or in windslayer_server.py. The fields mirror S2C 0x35 (team change: uid, team, pending_team) handled at 0x455E94, which is what the game server actually sends to clients. The scout found only Add16/AddU32 and missed the Add(uchar) calls made through EDI=[0x4A40FC].
open_questions: What is the exact meaning of sub_op values 1 and 3? The EN client has no receiver for this host protocol, so they cannot be confirmed from the binary.
Is entity+0x1C really the index of the upstream connection (game/channel server) or a room slot? It is used as the GetChildSocketPtr index at 0x428586, which suggests a connection index.
Exact meaning of entity+0x15DC (set to 1 in FUN_00423850 when an action is taken, reset to 0 on round start at 0x4289AB).
blind_open_questions: Who the child sockets of room+0xF98 were meant to be (a dedicated battle-host server build reusing this code, relaying to the game server) cannot be settled statically; the field is never initialised in this client.
Meaning of entity+0x15DC (a player with a nonzero value is excluded; mode 1 clears it at 0x4289AB).

specs.semantics: Team auto-balance at round end (room_mode != 4). The host computes the imbalance: diff = to_blue - to_red - stay_red + stay_blue (based on +0x14EB/+0x14EC). It then walks the scene entity list backwards from the tail (scene+0x10, node+4 = prev) while |diff|>0. A Blue player is picked when diff>0, a Red player when diff<0. If |diff|>=2, the player is moved to the other team (team=pending=other), diff moves 2 toward 0, and the team counters scene+0xF61/+0xF62 are updated. If |diff|==1, pending is set to the player's own team, team becomes 0 if both teams exist (otherwise unchanged), and diff becomes 0. Each change is broadcast to every child socket as 0x93 sub 1.
specs.trigger: FUN_00428090(scene, 2) with scene+0xF24!=0, scene+0xF70!=4, |imbalance|>0 and a non-empty entity list. Unreachable in the EN 2008 client (+0xF24 is always 0; +0xF98 is always NULL).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: param_2==2 && scene+0xF24!=0; scene+0xF70!=4 (0x42860D); |diff|>0 (0x4286C6/0x4286ED); entity team==1 && diff>0 (0x42870F/0x428714) or team==2 && diff<0 (0x42878D/0x428796). There can be several packets per round end, one broadcast per moved player. DEAD CODE in the EN client.
specs.references: Wire format is identical to send site 0x428244 (10 bytes, sub_op 1). Client-facing analogue on the game socket: S2C 0x35 (u32 uid, u8 team, u8 pending_team). Not in PySlayer or windslayer_server.py. The scout's Add16/AddU32 missed the four u8 Adds made through EDI.

specs.semantics: This is room-server PvP scoreboard broadcast code compiled into the client, and it is dead here. After an entity's death is processed in a PvP room (room_info+0x70 == 1): team death counters are updated, alive counts are recomputed, and a round end is triggered if only one team is left. Then for each child connection of the socket manager, the per-entity lines for dirty entities are appended and the header [0x94][u16 room_id][u8 count][u8 f72][u8 f71][u8 f74][u8 f73] is prepended with AddToHead. The prepends run in reverse call order, so the final order is the one given in the grammar. The packet is sent only if at least one line was added. Dirty flags are then cleared. The body minus room_id and minus the per-entry +0x1C byte is exactly what the client's S2C 0x37 reads (u8 count, u8->F72, u8->F71, u8->F74, u8->F73, count x {u32 uid, u32 points, u8 ->+0x14EE, u8 ->+0x14ED}). This suggests the real game server turned room 0x94 into client 0x37. It is not a packet the EN client ever sends to our game server.
specs.trigger: None in the EN client. Room-server side, it fires on every entity death in a PvP room.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unreachable: all three call sites (0x414912, 0x414A19, 0x415679) require scene+0xF24 != 0, which is never written nonzero in this binary. The sim caller FUN_0042b260 only runs when room_info+0x70 == 0, while the broadcast needs room_info+0x70 == 1. scene+0xF98 is NULL, so the read at 0x41AB08 would crash. The function does not call ResetBuffer; it relies on each socket's buffer being empty (the previous Send). The per-entry +0x1C byte must not be forwarded to clients: S2C 0x37 has no such byte. Also note that S2C 0x37 stops reading an entry's remaining 6 bytes when the uid is unknown (0x456564), so a server building 0x37 from this data must only include uids the client has spawned.
specs.references: No 0x94 in PySlayer client_packets or windslayer_server.py. Cross-checked against the EN client S2C 0x37 handler at 0x456431 (field order F72, F71, F74, F73 and entry u32/u32/u8/u8 match, and the sprintf push order gives '[Blue F73 : F74 Red]'). The client's S2C 0x94 handler (0x471B61, u8 subcode switch) is unrelated. The companion FUN_00428090 sends 0x93/0x95 to the same child sockets.
open_questions: Is team 1 (+0x14EB == 1) really 'Blue'? This is inferred only from the '[Blue%d:%dRed]' argument order in S2C 0x37.
Kill/death naming of +0x14ED/+0x14EE is inferred from FUN_00418ac0 (HP==0 entity gets +0x14EE). It should be confirmed against the scoreboard UI (FUN_00443280).
Is scene+0xF48 the room number? Assumed from the S2C writers.

Whether [socket+0x11BE8] is really the Fireway send-buffer length (it is inside the 0x12C20-byte CSNSocket object).

specs.semantics: Battle-host round-end broadcast. The winner is decided as follows. If room_mode<5 and only one team still has living players (+0x98==3, HP>0), that team wins. Otherwise (room_mode>=5, both teams alive, or both wiped) the team kill counters decide: scene+0xF71 = Blue kills (incremented when a Red player dies), scene+0xF72 = Red kills. Greater count wins; equal is a tie. The builder updates the round counters, then for each child socket appends one 12-byte record per scene entity. Only if that socket's send-buffer length (+0x11BE8, confirmed in Fireway.dll Add/AddToHead) is non-zero does it prepend the 10-byte header plus the opcode and send. Afterwards round_no advances, or everything resets when round_no==scene+0xF36 (max rounds). On a real server the client-facing equivalent is S2C 0x36 (round ended) on the game socket.
specs.trigger: FUN_00428090(scene, 2) with scene+0xF24!=0. Unreachable in the EN 2008 client: scene+0xF24 is only ever written as 0 (CGameMain ctor 0x411FC3), and the CSNSockMan at +0xF98 only as NULL (0x440301).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: param_2==2 && scene+0xF24!=0. No filter on alive/team for records: every non-null node in scene+0xC gets a record. player_count is a u8 and wraps past 255 (the Fireway buffer limit is 0x7F7 bytes, about 169 records). Header is built with AddToHead, so the wire order is the reverse of the call order (opcode, room_mode, room_no, round_result, count, round_no, f5c, f5d, f5e, f5f). Note that at 0x4283F0 the asm overwrites the low byte of EBX (the entity pointer) with the team value; this is harmless because EBX is reloaded at 0x428358. DEAD CODE in the EN client. Do not confuse with S2C 0x95 on the game socket (player-report result at 0x471DA3).
specs.references: S2C 0x36 handler (0x456015) reads the same round counters (f60, f5b, f5c, f5d, f5e, f5f) and prints '%uRound ended. [Blue%d:%dRed]' with (f5b, f5c, f5e). This confirms f5c=Blue wins and f5e=Red wins. The sibling host message 0x94 (FUN_0041a230 send site #2) uses the same record layout without player_result. Not present in PySlayer or windslayer_server.py. The scout's 'AddU32 AddU32 AddToHead16' missed all u8 Adds (made through EDI=[0x4A40FC]) and the u8 AddToHead calls (EBX=[0x4A4104]).
open_questions: What is entity+0xB4, the bonus added to winners' score when room_mode>=5?
Exact list of room_mode (scene+0xF70) values and their names.
Is the recipient an upstream game/channel server (which then emits S2C 0x36 to players)? The design suggests so, but the recipient is not in this binary.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of entity+0xB4, the bonus added to winners' score in modes >= 5.
[sock+0x11BE8] is assumed to be the CSNSocket send-buffer length (inside Fireway.dll, not verified).
room+0xF71 and +0xF72 are assumed to be team kill scores (compared to break ties).

u16 room_id
u32 entity_uid

fields.name: room_id
fields.meaning: Room/battle number the simulation belongs to (scene+0xF48; in the client, S2C handlers such as 0x44931D/0x44A80D store a room number there)

fields.name: entity_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the entity whose timed effect ran out

fields.name: skill_id
fields.meaning: Skill/effect id of the removed slot. It is read before the array shift, so it is the expired slot's id.

specs.semantics: This is server-authoritative room simulation code compiled into the client, and it is dead here. When scene+0xF24 != 0 (a room host/server instance) in a PvP room, the effect slots on every player/monster are timed down. Once a slot's timer goes negative, the effect is removed, stats are recomputed, and [0x97][u16 room_id][u32 uid][u16 skill_id] is broadcast to every child connection of the socket manager (presumably the game servers that host the room's players). Opcode 0x97 is the plain/debuff-range variant; see the 0x99 spec for the other one. It is not a message the EN client can send to our game server. The client's own S2C 0x97 handler (0x471E71) reads u32 + i32, so it is a different message.
specs.trigger: None in the EN client. It would be the room-server sim tick on effect expiry in a PvP room.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unreachable for two independent reasons: (1) scene+0xF24 is never written nonzero anywhere in WindSlayer.exe (a byte scan finds only the init write 0x411FC3 and compares/reads); (2) FUN_0042b260 calls FUN_00417e10(scene,0) only when room_info+0x70 == 0, but the send path needs room_info+0x70 == 1. Even if both were forced, scene+0xF98 is NULL, so dereferencing [NULL+8] at 0x418207 would crash. Do not poke scene+0xF24 in memory.
specs.references: No counterpart in PySlayer client_packets or windslayer_server.py. The companion room-server code FUN_00428090 sends 0x93/0x95 on the same socket list and uses CSNSockMan::GetChildSocketPtr(scene+0xF98, entity+0x1C), which confirms that scene+0xF98 is a server-side socket manager. The layout does not match the client's S2C 0x97 (u32,i32) or 0x99 (u8 subcode) handlers.
open_questions: Which component was the real receiver: a game server relaying room events, or something else? What does it forward to clients (maybe an effect-removal S2C)?
Exact meaning of scene+0xF48 (room number assumed).
blind_open_questions: Whether the original room/game server used exactly this layout for its own 0x97/0x99. The EN client's S2C 0x97/0x99 handlers read different layouts, so do not emit this format to the client.
Meaning of definition flag def+0x1C8 (possibly 'show buff icon / notify').

specs.semantics: Same packet shape and trigger as 0x97 from the same Send site. The opcode is 0x99 when the expired effect's skill definition has +0x1C8 != 0 and the skill id is outside the harmful/DoT ranges that FUN_004257A0 lists, i.e. a beneficial buff with a flag set. The room server broadcasts it to all child connections. It is dead code in the EN client and does not match the client's S2C 0x99 handler (0x457FE1 reads a u8 subcode first).
specs.trigger: None in the EN client (room-server effect expiry in a PvP room).

specs.name: VersionCheckAndServerList

locations.role: handler block (primary switch, index table 0x4584B0 idx 0)
version rejected: SendMessageA(gs+0x3E0 launcher dlg, 0x401) -> window proc 0x476424 starts auto-update thread 0x475970
read str[notice_len] notice_text into heap buffer (len+1, zeroed)
call ParseChannelList(this, pkt, offset BY VALUE) - stdcall RET 0xC
version>=0xEA61: notice popup then FUN_0044d4b0 disconnect dialog
version==3: SetTimer(launcher dlg, 8, 300ms) -> enables/blinks Start button (WM_TIMER at 0x475FAA)
consumer: ConnectToGameServer uses stored channel IP, port hardcoded 7022 at 0x44080E

specs.length: 2 if version rejected; else 2+2+notice_len+1+SUM over servers(1 + (server_status!=1 ? 2 + 7*channel_entry_count : 0)) for a well-formed list (channel_no strictly ascending, 1..channel_slot_count)

fields.name: version_code
fields.meaning: Client-version gate. Accepted only if ==3 (normal: Start button enabled) or >=0xEA61 (60001: notice/refusal mode). Anything else: stop reading, launcher runs the auto-patcher (G_UpdateList.h from windslayer.globalgamecdn.com).

fields.name: notice_len
fields.meaning: Byte length of the notice text that follows (0 allowed)

fields.name: notice_text
fields.meaning: Launcher notice text (no NUL needed; buffer is zero-terminated by client). Shown in launcher dialog control 0x403; if version_code>=0xEA61 also shown in popup dialog 0x16 (strcpy into a 0x3E9-byte buffer)
fields.dest_or_source: heap buffer -> SetDlgItemTextA(gs+0x3E0, 0x403) at 0x44D74A; freed at 0x44D784

fields.name: server_count
fields.meaning: Number of world servers. UI shows only 4 (loop at 0x441528); record array is 0x80 bytes each from gs+0x1290 and runs into gs+0x1490 (selected server/channel bytes) at index 4 -> keep <=4

fields.name: server_status
fields.meaning: World status, stored zero-extended as u32. UI: <1 hidden, 1..2 greyed, 3 selectable, >3 hidden. Value 1 means no channel data follows for this server.

fields.name: channel_slot_count
fields.meaning: Number of channel slots for this server (loop bound). Slots are 12-byte records at gs+0x1294+i*0x80+j*12; only 10 fit before this byte itself (UI loop shows 10) -> keep <=10. Every slot 1..count not listed below is marked state 2 = '(inspection)' (maintenance)

fields.name: channel_entry_count
fields.meaning: Number of channel entries actually present on the wire

fields.name: channel_no
fields.meaning: 1-based channel number of the next entry. First one read unconditionally when channel_entry_count!=0 (even if channel_slot_count==0); subsequent ones read only after a matched entry while entries_read<channel_entry_count. Must be strictly ascending and <=channel_slot_count or the remaining entries are NOT consumed
fields.dest_or_source: temp (reuses stdcall arg slot); copied to slot byte gs+0x1298+i*0x80+(no-1)*12; slot state u32 set to 3

fields.name: user_count
fields.meaning: Channel population/load. UI colour = user_count/200: 0 green, 1 yellow, >=2 red

fields.name: game_server_ip
fields.meaning: Game server IPv4 for this channel, passed to CSNSocket::Connect(ip, 7022) at 0x440814. Our server sends host-order 0x7F000001 (LE bytes 01 00 00 7F) for 127.0.0.1 and that works

specs.semantics: Version-server (TCP 7011) reply. Global gate: whole OnReceive is skipped if [game_state+0x408]!=0. Reads version_code; if not 3 and <0xEA61 the launcher starts its HTTP auto-updater and nothing else is read. Otherwise reads the notice text and calls ParseChannelList, which fills the per-server/per-channel tables, closes the version socket (error 'Failed to close version server socket' aborts the UI refresh), copies the previously chosen server gs+0x1492 into gs+0x1490 if that server's status==3, and redraws the server/channel list ('Channel - N', 'Channel - N (inspection)', load colours). Then the notice goes to launcher control 0x403. version_code>=0xEA61: popup with the notice, immediately followed by FUN_0044d4b0(0) = 'Connection to Server got disconnected' + SetTimer(main hwnd,7,5000); Start is NOT enabled. version_code==3: SetTimer(launcher,8,300) which enables and blinks the Start button. Canonical well-formed wire per channel entry is simply u8 channel_no, u16 user_count, u32 ip (7 bytes) repeated channel_entry_count times.
specs.trigger: Immediately after the client connects to the version server (7011); server sends it once and the client closes the socket.
specs.expected_response: None on the version socket (client closes it). If version_code==3, the user picks a server/channel and presses Start -> ConnectToGameServer TCP to game_server_ip:7022, where the server must send 0x5A.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Top-of-dispatch gate [gs+0x408]!=0 drops the packet. Wrong version_code -> launcher tries to download patches from a dead CDN. server_count>4 overflows into gs+0x1490.. (selected server/channel); channel_slot_count>10 overwrites the slot_count/entry_count bytes and the next server record. Non-ascending or out-of-range channel_no silently leaves remaining entries unread (and slots marked 'inspection'). notice_text >1000 bytes overflows the popup buffer in the >=0xEA61 path (strcpy into 0x3E9 bytes). version_code>=0xEA61 path ends in a disconnect dialog + 5 s timer 7.
specs.references: Our VersionServer._build_version_body matches exactly: u16 3, u16 len, text, u8 1 server, u8 status 3, u8 slots 1, u8 entries 1, u8 ch 1, u16 0, u32 0x7F000001. protocol.md agrees (port in list ignored, 7022 hardcoded at 0x44080E). PySlayer (newer KR) differs: KR accepts version 4 (not 3) and its channel entry carries extra u32 port + u8; KR also uses msg 0x402 and loads main99_01.hmi - do not copy KR layout.
open_questions: Exact effect of timer 7 set by FUN_0044d4b0 in the >=0xEA61 path (likely client exit after 5 s) was not traced.
IP byte order relies on Fireway CSNSocket::Connect doing htonl (per our server comment / live success), not re-verified in Fireway.dll here.
Difference between server_status 0 (hidden) and 2 (greyed) in terms of server intent (e.g. offline vs full) is UI-only; no textual label found.
blind_open_questions: Byte order of channel_ip inside CSNSocket::Connect(ulong,uint) was not re-verified in Fireway.dll; the server notes' host-order claim is assumed.
FUN_00489DA0's return value decides whether FUN_0044D4B0 (disconnect message + timer 7) runs for version_result >= 60001; not traced.
What distinguishes server_status 2 from 1 beyond parsing (both display greyed).

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1=success. Failures (socket closed first): 2 'Server process is running...(DB)', 3 silent (no dialog), 4 'Connection already exists. Disconnecting existing connection', 5 'This ID is blocked due to excessive abuse...', 6 'The server is full', 7 '(HIO)', 8 '(HIS)', 9 '(READ)', 0x0A '(InternetQuery)', 0x0B 'Login process was corrupted (RETURN)', 0x0C 'Login process was corrupted', 0x0D 'disconnected, 24 hours logged in', 0x0E 'Server is under maintenance (LOGIN_FAIL_BY_SRVLOCK)', 0x0F 'ID, Password field can not be left blank', 0x10 'We cannot log you into your account at this time', 0x11 'Enter the correct password', 0x12 'You account need email confirmation', 0x13 'You account has been deleted'; 0 or >0x13: silent close

fields.name: account_id
fields.meaning: Account/local-player uid. Later local-player registration (0x422120) requires spawn entity+0x84 == this value; also broadcast in UDP 0x11

fields.name: cash_first_purchase_flag
fields.meaning: First byte of the cash/billing object; when nonzero SubHandler4 shows 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash. 500 mileage...' once and clears it. Send 0

fields.name: account_gender_flag
fields.meaning: Normalised to bool. Equip check 0x44C2C0: items with gender 1 require flag!=0, gender 2 require flag==0 ('You can not equip other gender's item')

fields.name: rank_3
fields.meaning: Ranking position #3 (same display rules)

fields.name: rank_change_3

fields.meaning: Appearance/costume ids, same u16[14] block as 0x07 (entity+0x120). All-zero renders an invisible character

fields.name: transfer_status
fields.meaning: Account-transfer UI state: 1 = text '<transfer_text>Applying' (reads 33 more bytes); 2 = 'requesting ID transfer.'; other: if scene+0x218==0 'Account transfer possible', else hides window 0x12 controls 5,6,7. Send 3 for none

fields.name: transfer_text
fields.meaning: Only when transfer_status==1: prefix text, sprintf_s('%s%s', text, 'Applying') into window 0x12 control 7

specs.semantics: Login result. result!=1: CSNSocket::Close(g_sock_game) then (for 2,4..0x13) a message dialog; nothing more is read. result==1: screen fade (~640 ms of Sleep), UI windows 0x16/0x73 reset, character-select map ./hs/main99_02.hmi loaded, scene+0xF00=5, scene+0xF68/0xF6C cleared; stores account_id, billing flag, gender flag, manner points; for each character allocates a 0x15F0 entity, reads the record, then sets posX f64 = 110*(i+1) (+0x15A4 int too), posY f64 = 300 (+0x15A8), alive(+0x98)=3, uid(+0x84)=30000000+i (0x1C9C380+i), +0x8D6=1, cur HP(+0x9C)=100, level(+0x99) from exp, +0x9A=99, registers it in the scene list (not as local player, alive!=4) and sets +0x8B4=4. Then reads transfer_status (+optional 33-byte text) and updates the transfer text. Finally scene+0xF18=0, resets three sub-systems (gs+0xD2C, gs+0xD5C, gs+0xDC4), stores the game server peer address at gs+0x14C8 and broadcasts UDP 0x11 + u32 account_id to 255.255.255.255:42907 on the map socket.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x01 login (after 0x5A). Also re-sent after character creation to refresh the list (our server does this).
specs.expected_response: Success: no TCP reply; client sends UDP broadcast (map socket) u8 0x11 + u32 account_id to port 42907. User then acts on the char-select screen (create character / enter world, e.g. C2S 0x2B). Failure: none (socket closed by client).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only the global [gs+0x408]!=0 drop; no in-world check - a success 0x02 received while in world tears the client back to character select (matches our server note). Any result!=1 (including unknown values) closes the game socket. Each success allocates new character entities. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C6, login_character#03/#05): the previous entities are NOT freed - they are appended, scene+0x14 is INCREMENTED (not reset) and uids restart at 30000000+i, so a second success 0x02 received at character select produces DUPLICATE uids and overlapping bodies (clicking then selects the older entity). SERVER RULE: never send a second success 0x02 while the client is at character select; announce a new character with S2C 0x1C instead. Level is derived client-side from total_exp; sending a level number in job_branch changes the displayed class name instead. Extra trailing bytes after the last read are ignored. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C38, login_character#23): the "hide window 0x12 controls 5, 6 and 7" done for transfer_status values other than 1/2 (when scene+0x218 != 0) is STICKY - a later 0x02 with status 1 or 2 only sets the control-7 text and does NOT make the controls visible again. The ID-transfer UI (and therefore C2S 0x65/0x66) is reachable only if the session's FIRST 0x02 carries status 1/2 (or scene+0x218 == 0).
specs.references: Our _build_login_success is wire-compatible (12-byte header, 75-byte records, u8 3, plus 16 ignored trailing bytes) but MISLABELS fields: the byte it calls 'level' is job_branch (entity+0x111; sending level=1 shows 2nd-job name e.g. 'Berserker'), the first u32 'look' is total_exp, the 6 u32 'fields' are 3 u32 ranks + 3 i32 rank changes, 'unknown_1' is the cash first-purchase flag, 'has_premium' is the gender flag, 'premium_flags' is manner points, the trailing byte 3 is transfer_status. It uses results 0x0B (short payload) and 0x11 (bad password) correctly. protocol.md error list is incomplete (see result field). PySlayer KR 0x02 differs: extra header bytes and per-char layout (bool, u8, u16 job, u32 exp, ...) with 0x2AD8-byte entities - do not copy. RegisterLocalPlayer uid gate (scene+0x220) agrees with project_local_player_spawn.md.

A second success 0x02 appends a second set of entities, increments scene+0x14 and restarts uids at 30000000+i, giving duplicate uids and overlapping characters. specs.length: 64 + (mentor_id!=0 ? 18 : 0) + 3*completed_quest_count + SUM_equip(5 + 2*option_count) + 4*consume_item_count + 3*etc_item_count. Minimum (all counts 0, mentor_id 0) = 64 bytes, matching the observed 64-byte 0x03 in the working map-change replay.

fields.name: channel_id
fields.meaning: Current channel/server number of the local character. Byte right after the 17-byte char name at scene+0x206; copied into friend manager +0x90 (used as 'same channel' value in mentor/friend login notices); compared against mentor_channel. PySlayer: 'must be >= 1'.

fields.name: map_code
fields.meaning: Map xml code (e.g. 101). Used ONLY to build './hs/stage%02u_%02u.hmi' (map_code/100, map_code%100) and load the map; NOT stored in the scene struct.

fields.name: game_clock_ms
fields.meaning: Synchronized game clock in milliseconds: logic tick adds 30 (0x1E) per frame (FUN_00417e10), compared with +15000 windows, *0.001 for seconds (FUN_00423260); copied to entity+0x88/+0x95C at registration. Also written by S2C 0x08 (u32 after map code).

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Gold. Displayed with '%I64u' in inventory; 'You are short of gold.' check; quest reward adds to it.

fields.name: exp_total
fields.meaning: Cumulative experience; exp bar '%u/%u' computed against cumulative curve table 0x6F0EB0 (FUN_00442aa0) using local entity level (+0x99).

fields.name: fame_points
fields.meaning: Fame/honor points; shown '%u' (UI text 0x20/0x10) and converted to rank 0..98 via threshold table 0x6F11D8 -> scene+0x96C and local entity +0x9A.

fields.name: winnie_points
fields.meaning: Shown as '%u' in UI text id 0x27. Name from PySlayer ('winnie'); not otherwise confirmed.

fields.name: battle_win
fields.meaning: Battlefield wins, '%u Win'

fields.name: battle_lose
fields.meaning: Battlefield losses, '%u Lose'

fields.name: battle_ko
fields.meaning: Battlefield KOs, '%u KO'

fields.name: battle_down
fields.meaning: Battlefield downs, '%u Down'

fields.name: mentor_id
fields.meaning: Mentor character id; 0 = no mentor (skips the sub-block). If non-zero a 0x28-byte entry is allocated: entry+0x18 = mentor_id (matched later by FUN_00470780 mentor login notices), entry+0x24 = 1, appended as head of friend-manager list +0x14.

fields.name: mentor_name
fields.meaning: Mentor character name (only if mentor_id != 0). Exactly 17 raw bytes (GetDataFromPacket char buffer N=0x11).

fields.name: mentor_channel
fields.meaning: Mentor online status/channel (only if mentor_id != 0). 0x66 ('f') = offline -> entry+0x14=0, entry+0x20 state=1; equal to channel_id -> state 0 (online same channel); any other value -> state 4 (online, other channel), stored as channel.

fields.name: unk_e78
fields.meaning: Unknown scene flag; no other scene-relative reader found in corpus (all other +0xE78 refs are entity-struct). PySlayer KR analog sends 10.

fields.name: active_quest_id[3]
fields.meaning: 3 active quest-log slots (0 = empty). All three non-zero => client refuses new quest accepts. Same array written by S2C 0x26 and cleared by 0x27/0x38.

fields.name: active_quest_progress[3]
fields.meaning: Per-slot progress counter for the active quests (same bytes S2C 0x59 writes). The following 3 'ready to complete' flags scene+0x2A7..0x2A9 are zeroed, not read.

fields.name: equip_tab_slots
fields.meaning: Equipment inventory tab capacity. Must be 1..45: item-add paths reject when >45 (0x2D) and 0 gives 'There isn't empty space in the inventory'.

fields.name: consume_tab_slots
fields.meaning: Consumable inventory tab capacity (<=45).

fields.name: etc_tab_slots
fields.meaning: Etc/material inventory tab capacity (<=45).

fields.name: completed_quest_count
fields.meaning: Number of completed-quest records. Arrays are 85 entries; NO bounds check (max 85).

fields.name: completed_quest_id
fields.meaning: Completed quest id (prerequisite lookups scan 85 slots, FUN_00477ff0).

fields.name: completed_quest_times
fields.meaning: Times that quest was completed (compared >= required count).

fields.name: equip_item_count
fields.meaning: Items in the equipment tab (array index = slot). NO bounds check, max 45.

fields.name: item_id (equip)
fields.meaning: Equipment item id for slot i.

fields.name: option_count
fields.meaning: Number of option u16s that follow for this equip item; NOT stored. Max 5 (a 6th lands on record+10 and is overwritten by item_extra; 7+ overflows into the next record).

fields.name: option_value
fields.meaning: Item option/enchant value j of the 12-byte equip record (same record layout S2C 0x66/0x67 read: u8 n, n*u16, u16).

fields.name: item_extra
fields.meaning: Last word of the 12-byte equip record; meaning unconfirmed (PySlayer writes id+10).

fields.name: consume_item_count
fields.meaning: Items in consumable tab. NO bounds check, max 45.

fields.name: item_id (consume)
fields.meaning: Consumable item id slot i.

fields.name: quantity (consume)
fields.meaning: Stack count (UI caps sums at 999). Companion u32 array scene+0x6F4 is neither read nor cleared here.

fields.name: etc_item_count
fields.meaning: Items in etc tab. NO bounds check, max 45.

fields.name: item_id (etc)
fields.meaning: Etc item id slot i.

fields.name: quantity (etc)
fields.meaning: Stack count (UI caps at 99).

specs.semantics: Full 'enter world / (re)load map' character-state packet on the game socket. Order of effects: FUN_0043d560 fade-out (blocks ~640 ms if this+0x357==0); this+0x1534=0; close UI windows 0x16 and 0x13; KillTimer(hwnd,2). Reads the fields above in order (scene = *(0x70EA00+0x4CC) = *0x70EECC). Between battle_down and mentor_id it resets the friend/mentor manager (FUN_0046f860). After the reads it memsets the unsent 4th item tab (scene+0x830 u16x45, +0x88A u8x45), refreshes inventory (gold) and storage UIs, windows 0x15/0x16/0x1A, quest window, stats UI; builds './hs/stage%02u_%02u.hmi' from map_code and loads it (on failure logs 'Could not load MAP. (%s)' and CONTINUES); FUN_0042c450 state reset (scene+0x24C=clock, etc.); FUN_00422f40 DESTROYS ALL ENTITIES including the local player (scene+0x970=0); FUN_004271e0 frees scene item lists; shows map name (truncated to 20 chars + '...') in UI text 4 and 0x17; FUN_00444100 spawns the map file's NPCs client-side with uids 33000000+n; resets many HUD buttons (FUN_00489320 on window 0xB); shows char name (scene+0x206) in text 0x4E; scene+0xF00 game mode = 7; SetTimer(6, 240000 ms) and SetTimer(0xB, 7000 ms); finally sends two zero-length C2S packets: 0x2F (on the friend manager's socket, only if it was initialised) and 0x63 (on [this+0xDD0]).
specs.trigger: Send in response to the client's C2S 0x2B enter-game request (initial world entry), and it can be re-sent on a map change (proven replay: 0x08, 0x03, 0x07, 0x0A, 0x28, 0x44, 0x1A). Must be followed by S2C 0x07 for the local player because 0x03 wipes every entity.
specs.expected_response: Client immediately sends C2S 0x2F (0 bytes, only if friend manager initialised) and C2S 0x63 (0 bytes) - matches live captures ('0x2F and 0x63 0 bytes sent right after a map loads'). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C1, world_movement_npc#18, party#14): MANDATORY MAP-ENTER SEQUENCE (live-verified): S2C 0x08 (map code) -> S2C 0x03 (character/world state) -> S2C 0x07 (player list containing the LOCAL player, uid == scene+0x220) -> S2C 0x0A/0x28/0x44 (HP/MP) -> S2C 0x1A per monster/NPC. 0x08 alone never completes a map change. 0x03 is step 2 of that sequence; it destroys every entity, so an 0x03 that is not followed by 0x07 leaves the client with no local player on the loading overlay.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No opcode-specific gate (only the generic OnReceive check this+0x408==0). No bounds checks on any list count: completed_quest_count >85, any item list >45, or option_count >5 corrupts adjacent client state (slot capacities, item records, next arrays). Tab capacities must be 1..45 (>45 makes every item add fail; 0 => 'There isn't empty space in the inventory' on quest accept). Item lists should be contiguous non-zero ids (UI loops stop at the first 0 id). Quest 'ready to complete' flags (scene+0x2A7..0x2A9) are zeroed and not sent; a server must re-send S2C 0x59 for quests that are ready. mentor_channel 0x66 = offline marker (100 is NOT special here, unlike the live mentor notice). If the friend manager's UI pointers are not set, FUN_0046f860 does not clear the mentor list, so a re-sent 0x03 with mentor_id!=0 can duplicate the mentor entry, and 0x2F is not sent. Destroys all entities including the local player: without a following 0x07 the player never exists (endless loading). A missing map file does not abort the handler. The fade-out uses Sleep on the network thread (~640 ms stall).
specs.references: Our server _build_pyslayer_opcode_03 (windslayer_server.py:1986, used at :684 enter-world and :1249 change-map) emits exactly this EN grammar for the empty case (64 B: mentor_id=0, 3+3 quest slots, capacities 35/35/35, four zero counts) - byte-layout correct. Label errors there: +0xF1C labelled 'x ?' is the game clock in ms (sent 1000); +0x278 labelled 'fame related' is cumulative EXP (sent 30000 - drives the exp bar); +0x27C is fame (sent 0). Item lists, completed quests, active-quest persistence and mentor are never populated -> 'partial'. PySlayer opcode_0x03.py targets the newer KR build and does NOT match EN: KR has an extra u8 bool before mentor id, uses ' ' (0x20) not 'f' as offline marker, 5 quest slots instead of 3, 48-byte item records and a trailing u32; the KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 3) confirms the divergence. PySlayer naming used for gold/fame/winnie/battle W-L-KO-Down/mentor/tab-slot counts/completed quests, and confirmed for gold, exp, fame, battle stats, quest arrays and tab capacities by independent client code (FUN_00442aa0, FUN_00442c90, FUN_00464f30, SubHandler2 0x26/0x27/0x38/0x59, FUN_00478380, FUN_00477ff0, FUN_00440920). Memory note project_local_player_spawn.md: 0x03 triggers hs/ sprite+NPC resource loading - consistent with FUN_00444100. Observed 0x03(64B) in the working map-change replay matches the minimum length.

specs.name: UdpPlayerInput

locations.role: ioctlsocket(FIONREAD), then recvfrom one datagram. inet_ntoa/ntohs give the source ip string and port (host order)
udp_header flag (+0x13B6) is set: memcpy into a zero-filled 0xFEE-byte stack buffer, then GetUDPHeader
Seq check. If last_seq(+0x13AC) >= 0xFF, last_seq = -1. seq == last_seq -> drop (SetLastError 0x130). Otherwise last_seq = seq, stored BEFORE decode
Bit 0x800 set: DecodebyArray 0x10006BC0 (checksum fail -> drop 0x12F; flag set on a non-encrypting socket -> drop 0x133). Bit clear: plaintext accepted, checksum ignored
UDPPacketManager(body=hdr+8, len=(hdr&0x7FF)-8, ip, port), which jumps to listener vtable+0x10 (0x6F8408[4] = 0x478850)
Thunk: FUN_00458640(ECX=body, owner=[listener+4]=0x70EA00, len, from_ip, from_port)
Gate: owner+0x408 != 0 -> return without reading or locking. This flag is set only by the main WndProc on WM_CLOSE (0x43E450)
EnterCriticalSection(owner+0x368). The lock is shared with the UI thread; the dispatcher runs on the Fireway socket thread
u8 opcode at offset 0 (IAT 0x4A4094); switch(opcode-3) with index table 0x459BF8 and jump table 0x459BD8
u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8) -> [esp0+0x10] (overwrites the saved body pointer)
CALL FUN_00423850. Registers: EAX=scene [owner+0x4CC], EDX=uid. Stack: input_a, input_b, from_ip, from_port (callee pops 0x10)
Walk scene+0xC entity list for an entity with +0x98 in {3,1} and +0x84 == uid. No match -> return
Host-only branches (scene+0xF24 != 0): suppress actions and record the peer ip/port at entity+0x6A/+0x80/+0x14EA. DEAD in EN: the only write to +0xF24 is 0 at 0x411FC3 (byte scan)
LeaveCriticalSection. One message per datagram; trailing bytes are ignored
Client sender, arena non-host: same 7-byte body to host_ip scene+0xF38 : room_no scene+0xF48 + 10000
Client sender, field mode non-host: same body to 127.0.0.1:[scene+0x244] (=42907, i.e. to itself), every tick after the 0x04 snapshot

specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 input_a
u8 input_b

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Player uid. Matched against entity+0x84 of scene entities whose state byte +0x98 is 3 (player) or 1 (spectator). Monsters (+0x98==4) and unknown uids are ignored. The local player (state 3, uid == scene+0x220) also matches.

fields.name: input_a
fields.meaning: Primary input, encoded action*10 + dir (u8 arithmetic). Ones digit -> entity+0x8B3 = input direction. The sender resets scene+0x254 to 8 every tick (8 = no direction); the key handler sets 2 or 6 (0x42B05E/0x42B045). Tens digit -> entity+0x8B4 = action state. 7 = skill cast (scene+0x255 is kept across ticks only when ==7, 0x4237FF); 4 = Up per the portal-trigger spec.
fields.dest_or_source: sender: scene+0x255*10 + scene+0x254 (0x4236A5); receiver: entity+0x8B4 (tens), entity+0x8B3 (ones)

fields.name: input_b
fields.meaning: Secondary input, encoded variant*10 + sub. Tens digit -> entity+0x8B5 = action sub/variant (scene+0x256 = skill variant). Ones digit -> entity+0x8B6 = sub-state (scene+0x257, values 0..5 written by FUN_0042cf20).
fields.dest_or_source: sender: scene+0x256*10 + scene+0x257 (0x4236BF); receiver: entity+0x8B5 (tens), entity+0x8B6 (ones)

specs.length: Body is 7 bytes including the opcode, so the datagram is 15 bytes and header size = 0x00F. Fixed length. If the datagram is short, the GetDataFromPacket bounds check fails: the target is left unchanged, 'Error occured in Fireway (0x10/0x16)' is logged, and parsing continues.
specs.semantics:
DATAGRAM FRAMING (Fireway CSNSocket UDP; applies to every UDP opcode on port 42907).

One datagram = 8-byte header + body.
- hdr0 (u32 LE):
  - bits 0-10 = size = 8 + body_len. The receiver trusts this, not the recvfrom length; the dispatcher gets len = size - 8.
  - bit 11 (0x800) = ENCODED flag. It is set by SetHeader when encryption is on and NoEncode is off. The server's NO_ENCODE_FLAG name for this bit is backwards.
  - bits 12-19 = seq (u8).
  - bits 20-31 = unused: the sender leaves them 0 and the receiver ignores them.
- hdr1 (u32 LE) = checksum, checked only when bit 11 is set.
- Encoding (EncodebyArray 0x10006B20 / DecodebyArray 0x10006BC0, static and key-independent; SetCodeKey is never called on this socket). T[i] = low byte of the dword at Fireway 0x1000B138 + 4*i (= cencmsg._STATIC_TABLE).
  - body[i] ^= T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]
  - checksum = (T[seq] + sum(plain[i] & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF
  - The decoder accepts when hdr1 - ((T[seq] + sum + T[seq+0x25]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq.
  - cencmsg.encode_by_array/decode_by_array implement exactly this.
- Sender (client SendTo 0x10003C60/0x10003DF0): pre-increments a per-socket seq (+0x13A8: 1..255, then 0), sets size and bit 11, encodes, and sends exactly size bytes.
- Receiver: GetUDPHeader drops a datagram only if its seq equals the last accepted seq on this socket (any source; initial last_seq = 0 from Init). Unlike TCP there is no ordering requirement, no size sanity check, and no socket close. A datagram with bit 11 clear is accepted as plaintext even though this socket encrypts.
- Dispatch: FUN_00458640 returns if owner+0x408 (WM_CLOSE flag) != 0. Otherwise it locks owner+0x368, reads u8 opcode at offset 0 and handles exactly one message per datagram.

OPCODE 0x03 (player input).
- Reads u32 uid, u8 input_a, u8 input_b. FUN_00423850 finds the player/spectator entity with that uid.
- Writes the decoded digits into entity+0x8B3..+0x8B6: dir, action, variant, sub. These are the same input slots that FUN_00412100 fills for remote players from the TCP movement queue; the entity update FUN_00413920 consumes them.
- Stamps entity+0x88 = scene+0xF1C (room clock, +30 per tick).
- Sets entity+0x15DC = 1 (activity flag) unless input_a == 8.
- No map-mode gate: accepted in field and arena modes.
- Scene bytes +0x254..+0x257 are read ONLY by the UDP sender FUN_00423260. In field mode the client sends this datagram to itself every tick (127.0.0.1:42907), so field-mode local-player keyboard input reaches the local entity only through this UDP loopback. In arena mode a non-host sends it to the room host instead (no loopback).
- EN-only dead code (host flag scene+0xF24 is never set):
  - During countdown (F04==1 && F1C<5100) or round end (F04==2), actions 1/5/7 are zeroed, and so are the input_b digits.
  - The first packet from each peer stores its source ip (str16 at entity+0x6A) and port (+0x80) and sets +0x14EA=1. The host then unicasts snapshots there (0x423759).
specs.trigger:
Generated by clients every logic tick in FUN_00423260, called from FUN_0042B260 when scene+0xF90 (map socket) != NULL.
- Field mode ([map]+0x70==0), non-host: loopback to 127.0.0.1:[scene+0x244] (0x4237FD).
- Arena mode ([map]+0x70==1), non-host: sent to host_ip:(room_no+10000) from S2C 0x2F. It goes every tick while the local entity +0x98==3; otherwise only while scene+0xF08==0 (no snapshot yet) or as a keepalive when scene+0xF20 - scene+0xF0C > 9000.
- A server or room host emulator would send it to the client's ip:42907 (p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port from C2S 0x2B).
specs.expected_response: None. The client sends no reply. In arena mode the host is expected to answer with snapshot datagrams 0x07/0x08/0x09 (not traced here).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates:
- owner+0x408 == 0 (the game is not closing).
- Header accepted: seq != last accepted seq; if bit 11 is set, the checksum must be valid.
- uid must match an entity with +0x98 in {1,3}.

Hazards:
- SEQ COLLISION: the dedupe is per socket, not per peer, and the client's own loopback datagrams (2 per tick in field mode: 0x04 then 0x03) land on the same socket. A server datagram whose seq equals the last accepted seq is dropped silently. The only trace is a log line 'Error occured in Fireway (304)'. Never use seq 0 for the first datagram after socket init. Resending with a different seq is safe because this message sets absolute state.
- If bit 11 is set with size field < 8, DecodebyArray loops over (size-8) treated as a huge unsigned count and the client crashes. With bit 11 clear, size < 8 just yields len < 0, opcode 0, no-op.
- A datagram longer than 4078 bytes overflows Fireway's stack buffer (memcpy uses recv length, 0x100041E8). Keep size <= 0x7FF.
- If the size field is larger than the bytes actually sent, the missing bytes read as 0.
- There is no source-address filter: any host can inject input for any player uid, including the receiver's own local player (overridden until the next loopback tick).
- FUN_00423850 dereferences scene+0xC without a NULL check. Safe in practice because the scene exists before the socket is created (0x4402E9).
- u8 packing overflows if action > 25.
- Blocking UDP loopback on 42907 (firewall, port already bound by a second client) removes field-mode local input.
specs.references:
- Byte-identical to the client's own UDP 0x03 sends at 0x4236F5/0x4237FD (Add u8 0x03, Add u32 [scene+0x220], Add u8 [+0x255]*10+[+0x254], Add u8 [+0x256]*10+[+0x257]).
- cencmsg.py encode_by_array/decode_by_array match Fireway 0x10006B20/0x10006BC0.
- PROTOCOL.md: S2C 0x07/0x05 name the same entity fields input_dir_8b3/action_state_8b4/action_sub_8b5/action_sub_8b6.
- Portal trigger spec: +0x8B4==4 means Up.
- C2S 0x93 spec: the idle check uses +0x15DC.
- windslayer_server.py has no UDP sender; its UDPMapServer class is never started, and it correctly notes that 42907 is the client's own bind.
open_questions: In arena mode a non-host client never loops 0x03 back to itself. Does the original room host (external, at host_ip:room_no+10000, since the in-client host flag is dead in EN) relay 0x03 to every client, or is movement purely snapshot-driven (0x07/0x08/0x09)? Not decidable statically.

Exact meaning of each digit value: dir codes besides 2/6/8, action codes besides 4 (Up) and 7 (skill), and the scene+0x257 sub-state (0..5). Consumers are in FUN_00413920/FUN_00412360 and were not fully traced.
entity+0x88 (last-input room-clock stamp) has no reader found other than the reset in FUN_00428090. Its purpose (idle timeout?) is unconfirmed.
blind_open_questions: Did the original arena relay/host on room_no+10000 forward C2S UDP 0x03 payloads to other clients as S2C UDP 0x03? This is inferred from port and uid-lookup design, not provable from the client alone.
Are entity+0x8B3..0x8B6 values set by UDP 0x03 honored on normal field maps (map mode 0), or overwritten each tick by the snapshot path FUN_00412100? The ordering was not traced.

specs.semantics: Other player(s) appear. Byte-identical format and per-record processing to 0x07 (new entity, alive=3, buffs applied, RegisterLocalPlayer links it into the scene entity list; remote non-party players are prepended via FUN_00459D30 when [[scene+0xF88]+0x70]==0, else appended), but after the loop the opcode check at 0x44F6FE fails so there is NO scene-state change (scene+0xF00 untouched) and no UI panel refresh. If a record's uid equals scene+0x220 it would still set scene+0x970 (local player) because the gate is uid-based.
specs.trigger: Server should send to clients already in a map when another player enters their map/view (one or more records). Not sent by our server today.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
No uid de-duplication (sending an already-present uid creates a second entity; server must send a despawn/leave first or only send new arrivals). Do not send the receiving client's own uid (it would re-register as local player and duplicate the character). skill_count>30 overflows entity skill array. Buff ids 0xA31..0xA3B carry 4 extra bytes. cur_hp=0 renders the remote player dead. Use idle defaults for the state-machine fields (action_state_904=8, anim_substate_8cf=8, direction_8bd=2, input_state_8b3=8, rest 0). No length checks in handler. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C2, world_movement_npc#12 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): the spawn position is used VERBATIM. A remote record spawned above the floor HANGS in mid-air (y 712 over floor y 912 for 3 s+) and only falls once a queued movement command runs. The "spawn above the floor and let gravity settle it" rule (design 1.5) holds ONLY for the local player. The server must send a floor-level pos_y, or follow the spawn with S2C 0x1B / 0x2A so the entity simulates. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C12a, world_movement_npc#01/#20): the four input/state bytes must carry the client's IDLE DEFAULTS (8, 0, 0, 0), never IP octets as PySlayer/our old builder did. For the LOCAL player the client overwrites them from real input within one tick, but a REMOTE record keeps whatever the server sent and renders/animates from it. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C48, shop_storage#09/#11, trade#16): with shop_open = 1 the client draws the stall TITLE but NO signboard sprite for sign ids 0, 1 or 0x168 on the S2C 0x04 vendor path (id 1 produced only a brief flash), so 0x168 is NOT a valid sign-sprite id. CONFLICT: on the S2C 0x05 ghost path sign sprite id 1 DID render a real sign plus an owner glow (trade#16), so the valid id set - and what distinguishes the two paths - is still unknown. Also live: an all-zero appearance block yields an INVISIBLE body (nameplate only).
LIVE: a vendor record needs non-zero appearance values or the body is invisible; with shop_open=1 and sign sprite 360 the signboard still does not draw (open question).
specs.references: windslayer_server.py has no S2C 0x04 builder (the 0x04 in _dispatch ~line 566 is the C2S stat-increase request). PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x04.py is the KR layout (17 appearance, 15 equips, 10x3 cash, IP bytes, trailing str[13]) and must not be reused; EN layout equals 0x07 above. KR Hex-Rays (doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 2045) also shares case 4/7 in one block.
open_questions: Which S2C opcode removes a remote player entity (needed alongside 0x04 to avoid duplicates) was not examined in this batch.
Same field-meaning uncertainties as 0x07 (state-machine fields, buff param units, room_id 0x81).
blind_open_questions: Intended server use of 0x04 vs 0x07 in the original EN server (e.g. other-player enter-view vs self spawn) is inferred only from the missing UI refresh
Same unknown tail-field meanings as 0x07

map-mode gate: [[owner+0x4D8]+0x70]==1 drops 0x04 (0x45874F); !=1 accepts only 0x04 (0x45875A). No NULL check on [owner+0x4D8]

mode!=1 -> jump straight to 0x458BFA (skips all arena UI/phase code)
now = timeGetTime() (one value for all records)
per-record read: GetDataFromPacket(char*,8) IAT 0x4A4098 into scene+0xEF0 (rec_lo) / +0xEF4 (rec_hi)

first sight (+0x15A0==0): snap +0x15A4/+0x15A8; if entity==scene+0xEE8 snap camera owner+0x488/+0x490(y-100), owner+0x1044/+0x1048

attack-phase rising edge (+0x15B1==0 and rec_lo&0xC0000000) -> FX switch 0x458F33 (tables 0x459C2C/0x459C1C)

SENDER: Add(char*,4) header scene+0xEEC (map_code<<18 | count<<9 | timer)
SENDER: Add(char*,8) per entity record scene+0xEF0
SENDER: SendTo("127.0.0.1", scene+0x244=42907, reset=1) when map_mode==0 and scene+0xF24==0 (loopback to itself)
listener vtable 0x6F8408 slot 4 -> FUN_00458640(ECX=body, owner, len, from_ip, from_port)
Fireway UDPBufferManager: header on (+0x13B6=1), len passed = (hdr0&0x7FF)-8

fields.name: map_mode
fields.meaning: [[game_state+0x4D8]+0x70] = [[0x70EED8]+0x70]; 0 normal field, 1 arena/team battle. 0x04 is only processed when != 1

fields.name: map_code
fields.meaning: [[0x70EED8]+0x1B8] = current map code (a + b*100 from ./hs/stageAA_BB.hmi, e.g. 101), compared as full u32 against hdr>>18

fields.name: hdr
fields.type: u32 (wire is 4 raw bytes read with GetDataFromPacket(char*,4) 0x4A4098; little-endian bitfield)
fields.meaning: Snapshot header bitfield. Stored raw into scene+0xEEC before any check

fields.name: hdr.timer
fields.meaning: Phase timer in seconds. For 0x04 it is only stored (sender always writes 0 outside arena phase 1)

fields.name: hdr.count
fields.meaning: Number of 8-byte entity records that follow (0..511; the 0x7FF Fireway size cap limits it to 254)
fields.dest_or_source: loop bound (re-read from scene+0xEEC each iteration @0x45959C)

fields.name: hdr.map_code
fields.meaning: Map code of the sender; must equal the receiver's current map code or the datagram is ignored after the header

fields.name: rec_lo
fields.meaning: Entity display state bitfield

fields.name: rec_lo.x_half
fields.meaning: X position / 2. Display X = 2*x_half. Sender: trunc(entity+0x11F8 * 0.5) (FPU chop mode) masked to 12 bits, so X must be 0..8190
fields.dest_or_source: entity+0x15A4 (first sight) and +0x1598 (last net X); motion segment dx

fields.name: rec_lo.y_half
fields.meaning: Y position / 2. Display Y = 2*y_half. Sender: trunc(entity+0x1288 * 0.5) masked to 11 bits, so Y must be 0..4094
fields.dest_or_source: entity+0x15A8 (first sight) and +0x159C; motion segment dy

fields.name: rec_lo.facing
fields.meaning: Facing: 0 -> 2, 1 -> 6 (sender: entity+0x8BD==2 -> 0, else 1)

fields.name: rec_lo.action_idx
fields.meaning: Action index = action-1. Sender: entity+0x904 - 1, overridden to 0x16+v when cast variant entity+0x8FE = v in 1..11 (so 0x17..0x21 = skill-cast variants). Known actions (idx+1): 8 idle, 4 attacking, 1/0xE/0xF attack family, 3/0x17 special with phase FX, 0x10 dead/down, 0x16 downed/revive

fields.name: rec_lo.attack_phase
fields.meaning: Attack/effect phase 0..3. Sender sets 1 for actions {1,2,4,0xE,0xF,0x11} when +0x8D9!=0, and 1 or 2 for actions 3/0x17 from +0x8D1. A 0 -> nonzero edge triggers hit FX

fields.name: rec_hi
fields.meaning: Entity id bitfield

fields.name: rec_hi.anim_toggle
fields.meaning: Animation-restart toggle (sender: entity+0x8E0 & 1, flipped by FUN_00413920/FUN_00428C90 when an action restarts). Any change zeroes the remote animation timer

fields.name: rec_hi.uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (25 bits). Must equal entity+0x84 exactly, so uids >= 2^25 can never be addressed

fields.name: rec_hi.unused
fields.meaning: Ignored by receiver; sender leaves stale bits here (send 0)

specs.semantics:
DATAGRAM FRAMING (all UDP on g_sock_map; Create(0xA79B, type=2, encode=1, header=1) @0x4402DB): same 8-byte Fireway header as TCP. hdr0 u32 = size (bits 0-10 = 8+body_len) | 0x800 (EncodebyArray flag) | seq<<12 (bits 12-19, bits 20-31 = 0); u32 checksum; body = opcode + grammar, XORed with the static table (cencmsg.py EncodebyArray, the same as TCP). Receive path: recvfrom @0x10004755 -> UDPBufferManager 0x10004180 (copies the datagram into a ~4 KB stack buffer) -> GetUDPHeader 0x10003A00 -> listener slot 4 0x478850 -> FUN_00458640(ECX=body, owner=game_state 0x70EA00, len=(hdr0&0x7FF)-8, from_ip, from_port). The length comes from the header, not from the datagram size. GetUDPHeader has no [8,0x7FF] range check. Seq rule: one per-socket last_seq (+0x13AC, set to 0 by the ctor and Init). If last_seq >= 255 it is first reset to -1. The datagram is dropped (error 0x130) iff seq == last_seq; otherwise last_seq = seq, and that happens BEFORE the checksum check. Flag 0x800 set: DecodebyArray, and a checksum failure drops it (0x12F). Flag clear: the body is accepted as plaintext. The client's own SendTo pre-increments a per-socket counter (+0x13A8), wrapping 255->0, so client datagrams carry seq 1..255,0,1.... The source address is never validated. Dispatcher: if owner+0x408 != 0 the datagram is silently dropped; otherwise EnterCriticalSection(owner+0x368), u8 opcode, switch.

OPCODE 0x04 (normal maps). Processed only when map_mode != 1. Steps: read the 4-byte header into scene+0xEEC; if hdr>>18 != current map code, stop. Then owner+0x1524 = timer, now = timeGetTime(), and for i in 0..count-1 read 8 bytes into scene+0xEF0 and walk the whole scene entity list (scene+0xC). For EVERY entity with +0x98 >= 3 (alive player or monster) and +0x84 == uid: (a) If +0x15A0 == 0 (never positioned), snap +0x15A4/+0x15A8 = (2x, 2y). If that entity is the camera target scene+0xEE8, also snap the camera (owner+0x488 = x, +0x490 = y-100 as f64, clear +0x474/+0x478/+0x4A8/+0x4AC/+0x498/+0x4A0, ints owner+0x1044/+0x1048). Otherwise, if now != +0x15A0 and (2x,2y) != (+0x1598,+0x159C), append a motion segment {from=+0x1598/+0x159C, delta, f64 duration=now-+0x15A0, f64 0} to entity+0x1588; FUN_0042AA10 then interpolates +0x15A4/+0x15A8. (b) +0x15B0 = facing (2/6). (c) If the entity is the local player (scene+0x970) and action_idx is 0x17..0x21 (a skill cast is echoed), clear the pending cast scene+0x255/+0x256. (d) Animation toggle: a change zeroes +0x15AC; store +0x15B2. (e) If the old +0x15B1 == 0 and attack_phase != 0, play FX by action_idx: idx 1/0x10 -> sound 2 plus effect {5,2,0,+/-10 by facing,0,x,y,0} queued on owner+0x430. idx 0x1F: class(+0x110)==2 and tier(+0x111)==2 -> FUN_0042B580(0xDA,0,0,x,y,1,7,facing). idx 0x1F/0x21 with class 6, tier 2: effect 0x114 (idx 0x1F; on non-arena maps it also queues effects 0x37/0x54 on the uid with sounds and an HP-gauge refresh) or 0x118 (idx 0x21). It is offset horizontally by trunc((+0x15AC-450)*mult)+100 against the facing, with mult 1.2 or 1.26..1.8 from FUN_00426C50(0x17C) returning 0x17C..0x185. (f) +0x15B1 = attack_phase. (g) If action_idx+1 != +0x15B4, call FUN_0042B860(owner, action, entity) for action-start FX. Action 0x10 clears the entity buff tables +0xE84/+0x107C and refreshes the stat panel, HP gauge and party bars. Then set +0x15AC: 0 unless the old action was 6, in which case new action 1 gives class(+0x112) 2/4 -> 120, 3 -> 210, 5/6 -> 270, else 150, and new action 4 gives +0x112==3 -> 180, 5/6 -> 200, else 1380. Then +0x15B4 = action. (h) Always: +0x15A0 = now, +0x1598 = 2x, +0x159C = 2y. Nothing is read after the last record. Records never create or remove entities.

WHO SENDS IT: in the EN client, FUN_00423260 builds 0x04 every game tick (called from FUN_0042B260 while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6) from all entities with +0x98==3, or +0x98==4 and +0xE64>=3. When map_mode==0 and scene+0xF24 (host) == 0, it SendTo's it to 127.0.0.1:scene+0x244 (its own port 42907) @0x423787, followed by a 0x03 datagram @0x4237FD. So in normal fields this handler is the client's own simulation-to-display bridge: f64 pos +0x11F8/+0x1288, +0x8BD, +0x904/+0x8FE and +0x8E0 are copied through the wire bitfields into +0x1598..+0x15B4, which the renderer FUN_00431960 draws.
specs.expected_response: None. No reply on UDP or TCP. A private server does NOT need to send 0x04: the client loops it back to itself every tick.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates: (1) owner+0x408 != 0 drops the datagram before the opcode. (2) map_mode == 1 drops 0x04. (3) There is no NULL check on [owner+0x4D8] or [owner+0x4CC] in this case (unlike 0x06/0x0A/0x0B/0x10). (4) hdr>>18 must equal the current map code, otherwise nothing after the header is used (scene+0xEEC is still overwritten). (5) An entity is updated only if it already exists with +0x98 >= 3 and a uid < 2^25.
Hazards: (a) The client already feeds itself 0x04 via loopback, so a server-sent 0x04 gets applied on top of it. Positions jitter between the two sources, and a server datagram whose seq equals the client's last loopback seq is dropped. (b) SERVER CONSTRAINTS IMPLIED BY THE LOOPBACK: entity uids (monsters too, and account_id for the local player) must be < 33,554,432 (2^25), and X must stay in 0..8190 and Y in 0..4094. Otherwise the display fields never match or wrap, and the entity renders frozen or at the wrong place. (c) Short datagram: GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) with offset+N > len does not copy or advance. It calls the g_sock_game listener OnError(0x17, opcode) (FUN_004788E0 logs 'Error occured in Fireway (23), WSA(4)', no disconnect) and the stale scene+0xEF0 record is re-applied for each missing record. (d) The count is not bounded by the length. (e) The first datagram on a fresh socket with seq 0 is dropped (last_seq starts at 0). (f) UDPBufferManager copies the datagram into a ~0xFF0-byte stack buffer with no length check. Keep datagrams <= 2047 bytes.
specs.length: Body = 1 + 4 + 8*count bytes (opcode included); UDP datagram = body + 8-byte Fireway header. Max 2047 total, so count <= 254.
specs.trigger: Every client game tick (FUN_0042B260 -> FUN_00423260) while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6 on a normal map; sent by the client to itself at 127.0.0.1:42907.
specs.references: Sender FUN_00423260 (0x4232B2 opcode, 0x4233D8 header, 0x423432-0x423609 record packing, 0x423616 Add 8, 0x423787 loopback). Fireway.dll SendTo 0x10003C60 (SetHeader 0x10002150 + EncodebyArray when +0x13B5=1 and +0x13B4=0; NoEncode is never called by the exe). Map code field is also used by C2S TCP map_code ([[0x70EED8]+0x1B8]) in PROTOCOL.md. PySlayer and windslayer_server have no UDP snapshot support (the server only has an abandoned fake-0x11 UDP experiment).
open_questions: Exact names of the action enum values (entity+0x904) beyond 8=idle, 4=attacking, 0x10=dead/down, 0x16=downed/revive; and precisely what +0x8D9/+0x8D1 (the attack_phase sources) represent.
Whether [0x70EED8] (map object) can be NULL when a datagram arrives before the first map load; case 0x04/0x07-0x09 dereference it without a check.
FUN_00426C50(0x17C,0) is assumed to return the caster's learned skill id in 0x17C..0x185 (skill level scaling); not traced.
blind_open_questions: Exact enumeration of action states (entity+0x904 / +0x15B4). Known from context: 0x10 = 'is down', 0x16 = dead/awaiting revive (arena), 6 = charge-like state that sets +0x15AC on 6->1/4, 0x18..0x22 = forced states from entity+0x8FE 1..11. FUN_0042b860 switch not fully decoded.
Meaning of rec_b bit 0 (entity+0x8E0) and of strike values 1 vs 2 (entity+0x8D9 / +0x8D1).
Whether a server-injected 0x04 can drive remote entities reliably while the client keeps looping back its own 0x04 each tick in field mode (needs runtime test).
Whether a record for the local player's own uid has visible side effects beyond +0x15xx fields and the input-byte clear.
Linkage of the tick sender FUN_0042B260 to the ~30 ms frame loop was not verified (no direct caller xref in corpus).

specs.semantics: Adds ONE other player to the current field. The client allocates a new 0x15F0-byte entity, zeroes it, sets alive=3 (remote), parses name, uid, manner points, room sign, GM flag, job, level, rank, gender, looks, stats, 16 equipment slots with options, 9 extra slots, buffs (added to the buff table through FUN_00424e20) and learned skills. It then calls RegisterLocalPlayer (0x422120), which adds the entity to the scene entity list at scene+0x8. With the normal field flag scene+0xF88->+0x70 == 0 the entity goes to the list head, otherwise the tail. RegisterLocalPlayer also marks party members (+0x13A0=1, recomputes party average level at scene+0x96D) and resets the motion fields to defaults. After that the handler reads the motion snapshot, position (f64 x,y), HP, MP and the last state bytes straight into the now-registered entity. This is the single-player version of 0x07/0x04 (handler 0x44EF72): no leading u8 count, no trailing +0x14F4 personal-shop sign block, and a buff entry is always exactly u16+i32 (0x07 adds 2 extra u16 for ids 0xA31..0xA3B). There is no finalize step (0x07's FUN_004400c0 etc. does not run).
specs.trigger: Server should send it to every client already in a field when another character enters that field or comes into view. The matching removal is most likely S2C 0x06 (handler 0x4507A1 reads one value, then FUN_00422b90 removes the entity). Do not send it to the entering player about themselves; use 0x07 for the initial field list.
specs.gates_and_hazards: 1) No duplicate check: sending 0x05 twice for the same uid creates two entities (ghosts). Remove the old one first (likely 0x06). 2) If uid == the receiver's own uid (scene+0x220) and scene+0xF24 == 0, RegisterLocalPlayer overwrites scene+0x970/+0xEE8 (local player pointer) with this alive=3 entity. That likely explains the in-game reset our server saw (windslayer_server.py comment at line 585). 3) skill_count has no bounds check: more than 30 writes past the +0x29A array into later entity fields (at most +0x498, still inside the 0x15F0 allocation, but it corrupts state). 4) Buff ids missing from the client table are dropped silently; buffs beyond 21 active slots are ignored. 5) Any motion field read before registration would be reset, but all of them are read after, so the packet values stay. Sending 0 for motion_id/input_dir differs from the client defaults (motion_id 8, input_dir 8, facing 2, attack_dir 8); it is safer to send those defaults. 6) cur_hp = 0 makes the player dead/untargetable. 7) room_no != 0 shows a clickable room sign; keep it 0 unless a room exists. gm_flag == 1 shows the 'Wind Master' nameplate. 8) The entity is added to the list partway through parsing, so a truncated packet leaves a registered entity with default motion/position. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C2, world_movement_npc#12 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): the spawn position is used VERBATIM. A remote record spawned above the floor HANGS in mid-air (y 712 over floor y 912 for 3 s+) and only falls once a queued movement command runs. The "spawn above the floor and let gravity settle it" rule (design 1.5) holds ONLY for the local player. The server must send a floor-level pos_y, or follow the spawn with S2C 0x1B / 0x2A so the entity simulates. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C12a, world_movement_npc#01/#20): the four input/state bytes must carry the client's IDLE DEFAULTS (8, 0, 0, 0), never IP octets as PySlayer/our old builder did. For the LOCAL player the client overwrites them from real input within one tick, but a REMOTE record keeps whatever the server sent and renders/animates from it. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C48, trade#16): on this single-player spawn path sign sprite id 1 DID render a real signboard plus an owner glow and an orange nameplate, unlike the S2C 0x04 vendor path where ids 0, 1 and 0x168 drew nothing - see the 0x85 open question.
specs.references: Matches the per-player block of EN 0x07 (_build_en_opcode_07 in windslayer_server.py ~line 2219) byte for byte, except 0x05 has no trailing +0x14F4 bool (drop the builder's last byte) and no count prefix. The memory note project_local_player_spawn.md calls +0xE2/+0xE1/+0xD0 'marriage/spouse'; the binary shows a room sign (arena/play room/battle), from the dialog strings in FUN_0044c4b0 and the sign drawing in FUN_004316b0. The same code shows +0x12/+0x14 are the GM flag and hidden flag, not guild as PySlayer guessed. The KR Hex-Rays case 5 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 3093) also creates a single alive=3 entity with no count, so the role matches, but the KR layout is much larger. PySlayer's server_packets/opcode_0x05.py 'Ingame Init' has a leading u8 count and KR layout, so it does NOT fit the EN client; sent to EN it would misparse. PySlayer/our server treat +0x8B3..+0x8B6 as IP octets; the client code uses them as motion input/state bytes. Captured 0x07 replay (369 bytes = 1 count + 368) agrees with this layout.

specs.semantics: Removes a player (any entity whose +0x84 == uid) from the current field: FUN_00422b90 unlinks the node, frees its buff/effect sub-lists (+0x1354, +0x158C, +0x1374, +0x1364), destroys (FUN_00422ea0) and frees it. While removing, each of its 21 buff slots (+0xE84, 0x18 bytes each) is passed to FUN_00425af0 which re-evaluates party/team aura buffs (skill ids 0x8E7-0x912, 0xAE3-0xAF8); if any was re-evaluated the function returns 1 and the handler refreshes the local stat panel (FUN_00443840), HP display (FUN_00443690) and party HP bars (FUN_0043d4e0). In scene mode 5 (post-login lobby) entities after the removed one are shifted left 110 px and their uid decremented. No reply.
specs.trigger: Server broadcasts to players on a field map when another player leaves that map (map change, logout, disconnect). Counterpart of 0x05 (single player spawn) / 0x04,0x07 (player list).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Removal does NOT clear scene+0x970 (local player ptr) or scene+0xEE8 (camera/target ptr): sending the local player's own uid leaves dangling pointers -> likely crash on next frame. Unknown uid is a silent no-op.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 6: reads u32 uid, calls remove (sub_442880), same three refresh calls when it returns nonzero, plus KR-only clear of a struct if uid matches a stored id. Not built by PySlayer. Our server never sends it (no multiplayer despawn yet).

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (matched against entity+0x84 in the scene+0xC list). If it is 0 or unknown, nothing more is read and nothing happens. On a short read the slot keeps the from_ip pointer that was stored there at entry, so the lookup fails.

fields.name: cur_hp
fields.meaning: New ABSOLUTE current HP, zero-extended. Not clamped to max HP (+0x110C). Written for any entity, remote or local.

fields.name: popup_value
fields.meaning: Floating number shown over the entity in HP popup slot 0 (immediate style 0). The slot is assigned, not added to. 0 = no popup. This is the slot the client's own FUN_00418ac0 fills (ADD at 0x419EEA) for ordinary computed hits.

specs.length: Body 9 bytes including the opcode (grammar 8) when the uid is found. The client consumes only 5 bytes if the uid is unknown/0, and 1 byte outside map mode 1. The wire datagram is 8-byte Fireway UDP header + 9 = 17 bytes (h0 length field 0x011).
specs.semantics:
HP sync with a damage number for arena/room maps. Execution order (asm 0x4595B9-0x4596B0):
1. Check the map object (owner+0x4D8 non-NULL) and map+0x70 == 1.
2. Read u32 uid and look it up with FUN_004189f0 (stop if NULL).
3. Read u16 cur_hp, then u16 popup_value.
4. Opcode 0x06: entity+0x1114 = popup_value.
5. entity+0x9C = cur_hp.
6. If uid == scene+0x220: local entity (scene+0x970, if non-NULL) +0x9C = cur_hp, and FUN_00443690 redraws the HP text and gauge (it is called even when scene+0x970 is NULL).
7. FUN_0042fd20(owner) runs. It needs scene and scene+0x970 non-NULL and walks every entity. For each non-zero slot +0x1114/+0x111C/+0x1124 whose byte +0x98 is >= 3, it mallocs a 0x20-byte record {[0]=kind, [1]=value, [2]=0 age, [3]=0x14, [4]=0x28, [5]=entity+0x15A4, [6]=entity+0x15A8, [7]=style 0/1/2}, pushes it onto owner+0x430 (FUN_00459df0) and zeroes the slot. The slot is zeroed even when +0x98 < 3. Kind in mode 1 is 0 if entity+0x14EB (team) equals the local player's +0x14EB, else 1; outside mode 1 it is 0 if +0x98 == 3, else 1.
Opcode 0x06 uses style 0, drawn immediately by FUN_00430aa0.
HP 0 does NOT change the alive state (+0x98); the snapshot datagrams carry that. The handler sends nothing and does not use the source ip/port. No code in the EN client emits UDP 0x06; the original sender was an external battle/relay host.

FRAMING (Fireway UDP; g_sock_map = Create(0xA79B, type 2, encode +0x13B5=1, header +0x13B6=1)):
- Datagram = u32 h0 (LE) + u32 h1 (checksum) + body. Exactly one message per datagram; the dispatcher parses one opcode and ignores trailing bytes.
- h0 bits 0-10 = total length including the 8-byte header (max 0x7FF). Bit 11 (0x800) = encoded. Bits 12-19 = seq.
- UDPBufferManager 0x10004180 zeroes a 0xFEE-byte stack buffer, copies the datagram in, calls GetUDPHeader, then hands the listener body = buf+8 and len = (h0 & 0x7FF) - 8. The length comes from the header, not from recvfrom, and reads past the real data return 0.
- GetUDPHeader seq rule: if last_seq (+0x13AC; 0 at construction, 0x100019A2/0x100019E6) is >= 0xFF, it becomes -1. Then seq == last_seq -> drop (err 0x130); otherwise last_seq = seq, set before decoding. last_seq is per socket and shared by every sender, including the client's own loopback datagrams.
- Bit 11 clear: body accepted as plaintext with NO checksum check.
- Bit 11 set: requires +0x13B5 != 0 and +0x13B4 == 0, else drop 0x133. +0x13B4 is set only by NoEncode, which the exe does not import. DecodebyArray XORs each body byte with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] and requires h1 - ((T[seq] + sum(plain_i & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq, else drop 0x12F. T = low byte of each dword in the table at 0x1000B138; this equals cencmsg.py encode_by_array.
- Every field read is CSNSocket::GetDataFromPacket (this = g_sock_game, used only for its error callback), little-endian. A short read leaves the destination untouched, does not advance, and logs through listener slot 6.

Example plaintext datagram (seq 1, uid 1, hp 500, popup 37): 11 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 01 00 00 00 F4 01 25 00.
specs.trigger: The arena authority (battle server or host at the S2C 0x2F address; not emitted by the EN client) applies ordinary damage to an entity in a map-mode-1 room.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Silently ignored unless owner+0x408 == 0, owner+0x4D8 != NULL and map+0x70 == 1. In normal field maps use the TCP HP packets.
- The uid must exist in scene+0xC. uid 0 always fails.
- Seq: never repeat the seq of the previously accepted datagram on this socket, which also includes the client's loopback traffic. The first datagram after socket creation must not use seq 0. Plaintext (bit 11 clear) is accepted, but the seq check still applies.
- h0 length must equal 8 + body length. Too short: reads fail and stale stack values get written. Too long: extra reads return 0.
- cur_hp is u16 and not clamped. HP 0 does not kill; send the state via snapshots.
- The popup is assigned, and each arrival flushes. A popup shows only if entity+0x98 >= 3 and the value is non-zero, and it needs scene+0x970 non-NULL (otherwise the slot stays pending).
- No source-address validation.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the wire bytes (u32, u16, u16), the stack slots ([esp+0x30] -> +0x9C, [esp+0x18] -> +0x1114) and the jump-table routing (re-decoded from the binary: idx[3]=2 -> 0x4595B9). The dispute was the grammar, and analyst A is right. The asm exits to 0x459BB5 BEFORE any field read when owner+0x4D8 is NULL or map+0x70 != 1 (0x4595C1/0x4595CB), and exits after the uid read when FUN_004189f0 returns NULL (0x4595FF), so the cur_hp/popup reads are conditional. The verified TCP spec encodes such client-state gates in the grammar (TCP 0x40 'if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) { stop }', TCP 0x20 'if(client_in_battlefield_map) { stop }'); B's flat grammar drops them.
B's claim that FUN_0042fd20 'also runs every tick' is wrong for this mode: FUN_0042b260 at 0x42B4BA CMP [map+0x70],0 / JNZ 0x42B4CC calls the flush only in mode 0 (A correct).
B is right, and A silent or imprecise, on these framing details: initial last_seq = 0 (Fireway ctor 0x100019A2 XOR EAX,EAX -> 0x100019E6), so seq 0 is dropped as the first datagram; the zeroed buffer is 0xFEE bytes (byte [buf]=0 plus memset(buf+1,0,0xFED) at 0x100041C4-0x100041D5); and the checksum mask is applied before seq is added (0x10006C41 AND 0x0FFFFFFF, 0x10006C47 SUB, 0x10006C4C CMP with the seq byte). A's formula is numerically equivalent for real lengths.
The kind/style decode of FUN_0042fd20 (0x42FD69-0x42FE5A, [7]=EBP=0) was verified. Local counterpart: FUN_00418ac0 0x419EEA. The server has no UDP sender for this opcode.
open_questions: Which process originally emitted UDP 0x06: a dedicated battle server at the S2C 0x2F host_ip:port+10000, or a host peer build not present in the EN client.
Exact digit sprite sets for popup kinds 0/1 in FUN_00430aa0 (not asm-verified).

specs.semantics: Enter-world / full player list. For each record the client allocates a new 0x15F0-byte entity (ctor 0x444390, memset 0), forces alive state +0x98=3, parses fields up to the skill list, applies buffs via FUN_00424E20, then calls RegisterLocalPlayer(0x422120) which: recomputes derived stats/max HP/MP (FUN_0041ACE0) from job/level/stats/equipment, if scene+0xF24==0 and uid==scene+0x220 sets scene+0x970 and scene+0xEE8 = entity (local player), otherwise updates party-average level, resets movement/state fields to defaults, computes screen coords from position (still 0.0 at this point), and links the entity into the scene entity list (append tail FUN_00459DF0 or prepend FUN_00459D30). The remaining fields (state machine, position, HP/MP, shop) are then read directly over those defaults. If RegisterLocalPlayer returns nonzero (entity carries a party-aura buff type) it refreshes character panel/HP bar/party HP (FUN_00443840, FUN_00443690, FUN_0043D4E0). After the loop, ONLY for opcode 0x07: FUN_004400C0(EDI=6) sets scene+0xF00=6 (in-world; if previous state was 5 it also sets ui_root+0x5A4=1 and calls FUN_00446300(0x15,0,1,0,1)); then refreshes stat window (FUN_00442510), equipment window from the 25 slots (FUN_00441A10), inventory window (FUN_00441C20), HP bar (FUN_00443690), MP bar (FUN_00443780), EXP bar (FUN_00442AA0), FUN_00443AC0, FUN_00443F90->FUN_00478380, scene+0xEE0 counter (FUN_00442C00), and clears this+0x1534 (render-block flag checked by FUN_0043E1A0). All refreshes no-op if scene+0x970 is NULL.
specs.trigger: Server sends on enter-world and after a map change, to the entering client, listing the client's own character (uid == login uid) plus other players present. Our server sends it after 0x03.
specs.expected_response: none from this handler LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C1): 0x07 is the final step of the mandatory map-enter sequence. MANDATORY MAP-ENTER SEQUENCE (live-verified): S2C 0x08 (map code) -> S2C 0x03 (character/world state) -> S2C 0x07 (player list containing the LOCAL player, uid == scene+0x220) -> S2C 0x0A/0x28/0x44 (HP/MP) -> S2C 0x1A per monster/NPC. 0x08 alone never completes a map change. Nothing is sent back by the client, but without this packet the client never leaves the loading overlay.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Local player is registered only if scene+0xF24==0 and uid==scene+0x220 (NOT gated on alive==4; alive is hard 3 for every record). No uid de-duplication: every record creates a new entity, so re-sending a uid already in the scene list duplicates it unless the list was cleared by a map load. skill_count is unbounded: >30 overwrites entity fields past +0x2D6. buff ids 0xA31..0xA3B consume 4 extra bytes (desync if server omits them). Max 21 buff slots; unknown skill ids ignored. cur_hp=0 makes the character appear dead (HP 0/max). gm_level==1 gives GM title and client GM commands; gm_hidden hides the entity. karma<-9 red name. rank_icon<99 draws an icon. Handler performs no length checks. Recommended idle defaults (RegisterLocalPlayer's): action_timer_end_954=0, state_flag_8d9=0, anim_substate_8cf=8, action_state_904=8, action_timer_e00=0, direction_8bd=2, vertical_velocity=0, input_state_8b3=8, 8b4..8b6=0, flags 0, timer_d94=0, combo_stage=0. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C2, world_movement_npc#12 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): the spawn position is used VERBATIM. A remote record spawned above the floor HANGS in mid-air (y 712 over floor y 912 for 3 s+) and only falls once a queued movement command runs. The "spawn above the floor and let gravity settle it" rule (design 1.5) holds ONLY for the local player. The server must send a floor-level pos_y, or follow the spawn with S2C 0x1B / 0x2A so the entity simulates. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C12a, world_movement_npc#01/#20): the four input/state bytes must carry the client's IDLE DEFAULTS (8, 0, 0, 0), never IP octets as PySlayer/our old builder did. For the LOCAL player the client overwrites them from real input within one tick, but a REMOTE record keeps whatever the server sent and renders/animates from it.
specs.references: Agrees byte-for-byte with project_local_player_spawn.md layout (368 B per record) and with windslayer_server.py _build_en_opcode_07 (~line 2219). Corrections: (1) memory claims the scene+0x970 registration requires alive==4; asm 0x422144..0x4221A8 shows alive==4 only selects timing defaults, the uid gate at 0x422196 runs for alive==3 too. (2) Server labels +0xE6/E8/EA/EC as 'equip-appearance/dye ids' and sends 0: they are the four base stats (FUN_00442510 stat window). (3) Server fills +0x8B3..+0x8B6 with client IP octets (PySlayer KR layout); in EN these are input/state bytes (default 8,0,0,0). (4) Server sends +0x954=32,+0x8CF=1,+0x904=0,+0xE00=501,+0x8BD=0 (PySlayer values) instead of idle defaults 0/8/8/0/2. (5) Server sends cur_hp/cur_mp=0 and patches with 0x28/0x44 afterwards; real values could go here. (6) The 9 u16 at +0x15C are equipment slots 16..24 (cash slots), not 'extra'. (7) Stale comment at server line ~689 says positions are i32; code correctly uses f64. PySlayer opcode_0x07.py targets KR (0x2AD8 entity, 17 appearance, 15 equips, 10x3 cash, positions before state, IP bytes, trailing str[13]) and does NOT match EN.
