specs.semantics:
Framing: see UDP-S2C:0x04. It is the same Fireway 8-byte header (size|0x800|seq<<12, checksum, static-table XOR body; plaintext with 0x800 clear is also accepted). A datagram is dropped iff its seq equals the last accepted seq on the socket. Length is taken from the header.

Arena ('P2P room', map_mode==1) snapshot for room phase 0 (waiting/intermission). Same wire grammar as 0x04, but accepted only when map_mode == 1. After the map-code check: (1) toggle the round-timer control in windows 4 and 0x17 based on the PRE-packet scene+0xF04 (==1: zero +0x18 of the 3rd child; else FUN_00489320(ui,4|0x17,3,3)); (2) scene+0xF08++ (snapshots received since S2C 0x2F); (3) if scene+0xF04 != 0: FUN_00428090(scene,0). For a non-host (scene+0xF24==0, always true in EN) this only sets scene+0xF04 = 0. Then FUN_00442EE0 (blue/red/spectator status text), FUN_00443280 (team-balance notice) and FUN_004307C0 (camera follows the local player if it has a team, else picks a player to spectate via FUN_004305B0); (4) if timer != owner+0x1524: countdown/Fight! messages for timer 1..5 and the clock text F37*60-timer in windows 0x480/4/0x17 control 3; (5) owner+0x1524 = timer, then the per-record loop exactly as described for 0x04 (snap/interpolate position, facing, cast-echo clear, anim toggle, attack FX, action change via FUN_0042B860, +0x15AC timers, +0x15A0/+0x1598/+0x159C). Arena-only additions inside the action-change block: new action 0x10 prints '[<name>]is down.' colored by team (+0x14EB 1 = 0xFF5D9DFF, 2 = 0xFFFF5D5D), plus 'Revival in 20 seconds.' for the local player when room type scene+0xF70 >= 5. In attack FX idx 0x1F the extra 0x37/0x54 effects are skipped in arena.

WHO SENDS IT: the arena room HOST (FUN_00423260 with scene+0xF24 != 0). Each tick it sends the opcode from its scene+0xF04 (0 -> 0x07, 2 -> 0x09, else 0x08) to every peer entity's +0x6A ip / +0x80 port, which it learned from that peer's UDP 0x03 hello (FUN_00423850). In the EN client scene+0xF24 is never set non-zero, so the host is external: host_ip:room_no+10000 from S2C TCP 0x2F. Non-host arena clients do NOT build snapshots. They only send 0x03 (u32 uid + two action/dir bytes) to that address every tick, so in arena maps the display state of ALL entities, the local player included, comes from these host datagrams.
specs.expected_response: None directly. The client keeps sending UDP 0x03 hellos/inputs to host_ip:(room_no+10000) every tick.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: owner+0x408 == 0; map_mode == 1 (no NULL check on [owner+0x4D8]); hdr>>18 == map code; records apply only to existing entities with +0x98 >= 3 and a matching 25-bit uid. Phase code runs only when scene+0xF04 != 0 (the transition), but scene+0xF08++, the UI toggle and the timer block run on every accepted arena snapshot. Hazards: the 9-bit timer caps at 511 s, so for round_time_min (F37) > 8 the clock can never reach 0. The same short-read and stale-record behaviour as 0x04 applies. A server emulating the host must make count equal the number of records (the in-client host code counts only +0x98==3 entities in arena but writes records for qualifying state-4 monsters too). Seq collisions with other datagrams drop packets.
specs.trigger: Arena host tick while the host's room phase scene+0xF04 == 0.
specs.references: FUN_00428090 phase setter (writes scene+0xF04 @0x428BA5). Host sender FUN_00423260 @0x4232AE/0x423759. S2C TCP 0x2F supplies host_ip/room_no/round_time_min (scene+0xF38/+0xF48/+0xF37) and resets scene+0xF08. Not implemented in the private server.
open_questions: Whether the local player's on-screen position in arena comes exclusively from host snapshots (renderer uses +0x15A4/+0x15A8), i.e. whether an arena without snapshot traffic freezes all sprites. Inferred from the non-host sender path; not traced through the renderer.
Exact semantic difference between phase 0 (0x07) and phase 2 (0x09) from the original host's point of view (intermission vs round result) - the EN client has no working host path to confirm.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of scene+0xF70 (arena sub-mode: >=5 round-based with revival, <=3 'The battle is starting.') and scene+0xF37 (round length minutes) sources (likely TCP arena setup packets).
Whether the S2C-0x2F battle address (port+10000) was a relay/host server that emitted 7/8/9 in the original service, or purely a peer host.

specs.semantics: Full map change. Reads map_code and scene clock, then: if UI window 0x259 is open and this+0xD64!=0 calls FUN_00469090(2, this+0xD5C, 0x259) (closes that window, possibly sending a 1-byte 0x60 on that subsystem's socket); builds the map path; fades the screen out (~640 ms blocking); remembers whether the OLD map had type +0x70==1 (PvP map) else closes window 0x79; closes window 0x236 and any active modal window; unloads and loads the map (on failure logs 'Could not load MAP. (%s)' but continues); FUN_0042c450 resets scene transition state; closes windows 0x2A, 0x480, 0x4D, 0x47A, 0x47E, 0x4B and a batch via FUN_00483470; sets the map-name label (map header +0x178, truncated to 20 chars + '...') on UI windows 4 and 0x17; destroys every entity (including the local player: scene+0x970=0, +0xEE8=0) and scene list +0x1C; if the old map was a PvP map clears scene+0xF6C/+0xF68 and refreshes the stat panel; spawns the new map's static NPCs from map data (FUN_00444100, uids from 33000000); sets scene mode to 7 (field) - if the previous mode was 5 it also runs UI transition FUN_00446300(0x15). The local player is NOT recreated.
specs.trigger: Server sends when the player changes map: response to C2S 0x7E portal, teleports, returning from dungeons/arena.
specs.expected_response: No direct Send in the block. Server must follow with 0x07 (player list containing the local player whose uid == scene+0x220) and re-send other players/monsters (0x1A) - live-tested sequence 0x08,0x03,0x07,0x0A,0x28,0x44,0x1A works. Possible incidental C2S window-close messages from forced UI closes (unverified). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C1, world_movement_npc#18): MANDATORY MAP-ENTER SEQUENCE (live-verified): S2C 0x08 (map code) -> S2C 0x03 (character/world state) -> S2C 0x07 (player list containing the LOCAL player, uid == scene+0x220) -> S2C 0x0A/0x28/0x44 (HP/MP) -> S2C 0x1A per monster/NPC. 0x08 alone never completes a map change. Injected on its own, 0x08 freed every entity, put the scene in mode 7 and left the client on the "Loading..." overlay indefinitely (still there at +33 s).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No precondition checks. map_code must exist in ./hs/ or the scene is left without a map (log only). All entities are destroyed - without a following 0x07 the player stays invisible/uncontrollable. The ~640 ms Sleep-based fade blocks the network handler thread. Static map NPCs use uids 33000000+ - server-assigned uids must not collide. Server notes: sending 0x08 during the enter-world sequence caused a re-map-load loop (mode 5 -> 7 transition). Trailing bytes after the 6 read bytes are ignored (handler returns via shared break 0x44D7AD). HAZARD (live, world_movement_npc#18): 0x08 ALONE HANGS THE CLIENT on the loading overlay until 0x03/0x07 arrive - every entity (including the local player) is freed, scene mode goes to 7 and nothing recovers on its own. RECOVERY: send the rest of the sequence (0x03 then 0x07); a client left in this state can only be fixed by a restart. Never use a bare 0x08 as a teleport.

EN has NO reason byte: the reasons became separate opcodes 0x5E (KR 1), 0xA3 (KR 3), 0xA4 (KR 4). Our server _handle_change_map sends u16 map + u32 uid + u32 0 (10 bytes): the first 6 bytes are correct (the u32 lands in the scene clock, not a uid), the trailing u32 is ignored. Docstring claim 'cmp cl,0x5e/0xa3/0xa4 compares the OPCODE' is correct.

specs.semantics:
Framing: identical to UDP-S2C:0x04 (Fireway 8-byte header, EncodebyArray or plaintext, drop iff seq == last accepted seq, len from header).

Arena snapshot for room phase 1 (round start countdown and fighting). Grammar identical to 0x04/0x07; accepted only when map_mode == 1 and the map code matches. Common arena steps: timer-control UI toggle by old scene+0xF04, scene+0xF08++. Phase transition (only if scene+0xF04 != 1): FUN_00428090(scene,1). For a non-host this does: if old F04 == 0, reset the round counters (F5B=1, F5C..F60, F71, F72 = 0); if scene+0xF08 > 1, reset every entity's HP/MP to max (+0x9C=+0x110C, +0xA0=+0x1110), clear buffs (+0xE84 0x1F8 bytes, +0x107C 0x90 bytes), recompute stats (FUN_0041ACE0) and possibly clear +0x14ED/+0x14EE/+0x14F0; recount living team members into F73/F74; F04 = 1. The handler then recounts F73 (team 1) / F74 (team 2) for entities with +0x98==3, team != 0, HP > 0. If this packet's timer == 0 it prints the start message (room type F70 >= 5: '<round#>Starting the Round.'; F70 <= 3: 'The battle is starting.') and 'The round will start in 5 seconds.'. The local player gets HP/MP = max, then HP/MP gauges, team status, team balance notice and camera target are refreshed, and the stat panel too if F08 > 1. Then the common countdown block (timer changes 1..5 -> messages/sound, clock F37*60-timer), owner+0x1524 = timer, and the per-record loop (see 0x04). The loop adds, for 0x08 only: when an entity's action changes away from 0x16 and F70 >= 5, restore that entity's HP/MP to max and refresh the gauges and team UI (round-mode respawn). The arena 'is down.'/'Revival in 20 seconds.' messages apply as in 0x07.

Sender: arena host FUN_00423260 when its scene+0xF04 is not 0 or 2, to each peer's learned UDP address (see 0x07). Its header timer is trunc(scene+0xF1C * 0.001), the only case where the timer is non-zero.
specs.expected_response: None. Clients continue to send UDP 0x03 input/hello datagrams to the host.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: owner+0x408 == 0; map_mode == 1; map code match; the transition block runs only when scene+0xF04 != 1. Hazards: (1) F70 == 4 with timer 0 prints an uninitialized 32-byte stack buffer (neither sprintf branch runs). (2) The phase-1 transition heals everyone and wipes buffs whenever F08 > 1, so flipping between 0x08 and another phase mid-round resets combat state. (3) 9-bit timer limit (511 s). (4) Short reads, stale records and seq-collision drops as for 0x04.
specs.trigger: Arena host tick while the host's scene+0xF04 == 1 (round running).
specs.references: FUN_00428090 phase-1 path (decomp lines ~388-470). Host sender FUN_00423260 @0x4232A6. S2C TCP 0x2F sets F37 (round minutes) and resets F08. Not in PySlayer or our server.

Whether the original host sent timer 0 exactly once at phase start (needed to get the start messages), or relied on the phase-transition packet always carrying timer 0.

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: 0x66 (102) = target not found, reading stops. 0x67 (103) = target is refusing whispers, reading stops. 0x65 (101) = delivered, printed with no channel tag. Any other value = delivered, printed as the target's channel number '[Channel-N]' (raw %u).

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: Whisper recipient name, NUL-padded (16 chars plus NUL). Used as %s.

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Byte length of the echoed whisper text. Only on the wire when status is not 0x66 or 0x67. The client does not range-check it.

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Echoed whisper text: exactly msg_len raw bytes with no NUL terminator on the wire. Read into a 61-byte buffer that was zeroed first, so the zero padding supplies the terminator.

specs.semantics:
The server's answer to the local player's whisper (C2S 0x02).
- status 0x66: formats '<target>can not be found.' and appends it to the chat log (FUN_00445f00, colour 0xFFFDF34C).
- status 0x67: formats '<target>is rejecting whispers.' and posts it as a system notice (FUN_004817d0 on g_ui_root, colour 0xFFFD4C87).
- Any other status: reads msg_len and the message, then appends '<To: target> msg' (status 0x65) or '<To: target[Channel-status]> msg' to the chat log in whisper colour 0xFFAAD0D8.
No game or scene state changes. Unlike KR, the EN client does not reset a whisper mode on 0x66.
specs.trigger: Send to the whisper sender after the server processes C2S 0x02 (u8 opcode 0x02, str[17] target, u8 len, bytes[len] msg; built at 0x445A88). Use 0x66 or 0x67 on failure. On success, echo the text with 0x65 (same channel) or the target's channel number. The recipient gets S2C 0x0A.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- No gates: the handler always runs.
- CRASH (confirmed): every output goes through _sprintf_s into an 88-byte (0x58) buffer at [S+0x418]. If the text does not fit, __vsprintf_s_l (0x48E71D) calls _invalid_parameter (0x48BA46). The client installs no handler ([0x70DB10] is only written with the encoded null at CRT init), so __invoke_watson (0x48B94A) terminates the process. Limits (strlen values, excluding NUL):
  - status 0x65: 7 + len(name) + len(msg) <= 87, so name + msg <= 80.
  - Channel form: 17 + len(name) + digits(status) + len(msg) <= 87, so name + digits + msg <= 70. Example: a 16-char name with a 3-digit status allows at most 51 message bytes.
  - The 0x66/0x67 lines are always short enough with a valid name.
- STACK OVERFLOW: msg_len is not checked against the 61-byte buffer at [S+0x4B4]. msg_len above 61 corrupts neighbouring locals, and 61 leaves no NUL. Keep msg_len <= 60, which also matches the client's own whisper limit.
- target_name must contain a NUL within its 17 bytes, or %s reads past it into adjacent stack and can push the line over the sprintf_s limit.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: The two analysts' wire formats are byte-identical. Both read u8 status, char[17] name, stop on 0x66/0x67, otherwise u8 msg_len and msg_len bytes of text. The only difference is notation: A wrote bytes[msg_len], B wrote str[msg_len]. B's structural signature is cut off after 'u8' because str[N] in the DSL means a fixed-width, NUL-padded field, and a variable-length str[] was not recognised. A's form is correct. Evidence: at 0x4512D5 the client loads MOVZX EDX,byte[S+0x88] (the msg_len read at 0x4512B6), pushes it as N at 0x4512ED, and calls GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) at 0x4512F6 into [S+0x4B4]. So exactly msg_len raw bytes are consumed with no terminator, and the terminator comes from the memset at 0x4512C8. Both analysts' early stops are right: 0x45121C and 0x45125C JMP to the 0x44D7AD break before any further read. Their length limits agree once B's '18+...<=88' (which counts the NUL) is converted to A's '<=70' form. Verified in addition: the C2S send at 0x445A88 is switch case 2 (index 0x445E90, jump table 0x445E7C), and sprintf_s overflow does terminate (no invalid-parameter handler installed).

Other references:
- PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 9 has the same order and codes (102/103/101, '<To: %s>', '<To: %s[%s-%u]>'). KR uses a 0x9C output buffer and 0x81 message buffer and resets a whisper mode on 102; EN does not.
- PySlayer has no opcode_0x09.py.
- Our server (windslayer_server.py) neither handles C2S whisper 0x02 nor sends S2C 0x09.
open_questions: Whether Fireway's GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) checks N against the remaining packet length (the check lives in Fireway.dll, not the EXE). A short packet could leave the pre-zeroed buffer partially filled or read stale bytes.
Which channel numbering the original server used (for example 1-based). Any value other than 0x65/0x66/0x67 is printed raw as %u.

u8 channel
str[17] sender_name
u8 msg_len
bytes[msg_len] message

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: 0x65 (101) = no channel tag ('<From: name> msg'). Any other value, including 0x66 and 0x67, is printed as the sender's channel number '<From: name[Channel-N]> msg'. It has no other effect.

fields.name: sender_name
fields.meaning: Whisper sender name, NUL-padded (16 chars plus NUL). strcpy'd into the whisper-partner dropdown (UI control 0x6E) if not already there.
fields.dest_or_source: stack char[17] [S+0x25C], then 17-byte heap node via FUN_00444950

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Byte length of the whisper text. Not range-checked.

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Whisper text: exactly msg_len raw bytes with no NUL on the wire. Read into a pre-zeroed 61-byte buffer.

specs.semantics:
An incoming whisper.
1. The client reads channel and sender_name.
2. It looks up sender_name in the whisper-partner list (UI control 0x6E). If it is missing, FUN_00444950 allocates a 17-byte copy and adds it to that list.
3. It reads msg_len and the message.
4. It appends '<From: sender> msg' (channel 0x65) or '<From: sender[Channel-N]> msg' to the chat log in colour 0xFFAAD0D8.
Nothing else changes: no game, scene or entity state. The EN client has no early-return gate here (KR has sub_4D2140).
specs.trigger: Deliver a C2S 0x02 whisper to its recipient. Our server also uses it as a system 'welcome' line after 0x07, on enter-world and on map-change replay.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- No gates: the handler always runs.
- CRASH (confirmed): _sprintf_s into an 88-byte buffer at [S+0x730]. On overflow, _invalid_parameter (0x48BA46) finds no installed handler and calls __invoke_watson (0x48B94A), which terminates the process. Limits (strlen values):
  - channel 0x65: 9 + len(name) + len(msg) <= 87, so name + msg <= 78.
  - Channel form: 19 + len(name) + digits(channel) + len(msg) <= 87, so name + digits + msg <= 68. Example: a 16-char name with a 3-digit channel allows at most 49 message bytes.
- STACK OVERFLOW: msg_len above 61 overruns the 61-byte buffer at [S+0x474], and 61 leaves no NUL. Keep msg_len <= 60.
- HEAP OVERFLOW: sender_name must have a NUL within its 17 bytes, because FUN_00444950 strcpy's it into a 17-byte heap block (0x444953/0x444971).
- Every distinct sender name, including a fake 'Server', stays in the whisper dropdown for the session.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: The two analysts' wire formats are byte-identical: u8 channel, char[17] sender, u8 msg_len, then msg_len bytes of text, with no branches affecting reads. A wrote the last field as bytes[msg_len] and B as str[msg_len]. B's structural signature is cut off after 'u8' because str[N] in the DSL means a fixed-width, NUL-padded field, and a variable-length str[] was not recognised. A's notation is correct. Evidence: MOVZX EAX,byte[S+0x8E] at 0x451477 (the value read at 0x451458) is pushed as N at 0x451489, and GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) at 0x451498 reads exactly N raw bytes into [S+0x474], which was pre-zeroed at 0x45146A. The whisper-list lookup and add between the name and msg_len reads (0x4513E2-0x451440) consumes no packet bytes; EDI is restored from [EBP+0xC] at 0x451440. Both analysts' length limits are equivalent: B's '20+...<=88' counts the NUL, A's '<=68' does not.

Other references:
- Our server (windslayer_server.py ~765 enter-world, ~1306 map change; not ~718/~1258 as A cited) sends u8 1 + 'Server' padded to 17 + u8 len + text. This renders '<From: Server[Channel-1]> Welcome to WindSlayer!', 48 chars against a limit of 87, so it is safe, and it adds 'Server' to the whisper list.
- PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x0A.py has the same layout (p8u(1), pstr(name,17), p8u(len), pstr(chat,len)).
- KR Hex-Rays case 0xA has the same order, with larger buffers (0x81 message, 0xA1 output) and an extra sub_4D2140 early return that EN lacks.
- The comment in our server that 0x0A 'may be the trigger that finalizes the in-game transition' is not supported: this handler only touches the chat log and whisper list.
open_questions: Whether Fireway's GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) bounds-checks N against the remaining packet length (the check is inside Fireway.dll, not visible in the EXE).

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Healed entity uid (entity+0x84). If it is 0 or unknown, nothing more is read.

fields.name: has_hp
fields.meaning: 1 byte; any non-zero means hp follows. With has_mp == 0 it also triggers effect/sound 0x37. Both bools are read before either u16.

fields.name: has_mp
fields.meaning: 1 byte; any non-zero means mp follows (after hp if present) and triggers effect 0x58 (on the local uid) and sound 0x58.

fields.name: hp
fields.meaning: Present iff has_hp != 0. New ABSOLUTE HP after healing, zero-extended, unclamped. Written to the target (remote or local); local copy and HUD updated when the target is local.

fields.name: mp
fields.meaning: Present iff has_mp != 0. New ABSOLUTE MP, zero-extended, unclamped (any entity; local copy + HUD if local).

specs.length: Body 7 + 2*(has_hp!=0) + 2*(has_mp!=0) bytes including the opcode (7, 9 or 11) when the uid is found (5 consumed if unknown, 1 outside mode 1). The datagram is 15/17/19 bytes with the 8-byte header.
specs.semantics:
Heal/restore in arena/room mode (asm 0x459856-0x459B43). UDP relay form of TCP S2C 0x40 (same wire layout), but it writes remote entity HP/MP and adds the revive-camera call. Execution order:
1. Map gate.
2. Read u32 uid; lookup (EDI; stop if NULL).
3. Read bool has_hp, then bool has_mp.
4. If has_hp:
   a. If the target is the local player (scene+0x220 == entity+0x84), scene+0x970 != NULL and its HP +0x9C <= 0 before the update, call FUN_004307c0(EDX=owner). If the local team byte +0x14EB != 0, it sets the camera/follow target scene+0xEE8 = local entity. Otherwise, if scene+0xEE8 is NULL or its team is 0, it calls FUN_004305b0(owner, 0x27).
   b. Read u16 hp; entity+0x9C = hp; if local, (scene+0x970)+0x9C = hp and FUN_00443690.
   c. If has_mp == 0: malloc a 0x20 record {[0]=0x0A, [1]=0x37, [2]=0, [3]=target uid, rest 0}, push it to owner+0x430 (FUN_00459df0), and Play_Sound(0x37, x=+0x15A4, y=+0x15A8, owner+0x1044, +0x1048, +0x104C, +0x1050, 0).
5. If has_mp:
   a. Read u16 mp; entity+0xA0 = mp; if local, (scene+0x970)+0xA0 = mp and FUN_00443780.
   b. Queue record {0x0A, 0x58, 0, uid = scene+0x220}. This is the LOCAL player's uid even for a remote target (client quirk).
   c. Play_Sound(0x58) at the target's position.
6. Always (even with both flags 0): queue record {0x0A, 0x54, 0, target uid} and Play_Sound(0x54) at the target.
Type-0x0A records are drawn by FUN_00430aa0 case 0x0A at the uid's entity. There are no damage numbers and no FUN_0042fd20/FUN_00430020 call. The alive state +0x98 is not changed.
No emitter in the EN client.

FRAMING: identical to UDP-S2C:0x06.
- 8-byte header: u32 h0 (bits 0-10 total length incl. header, bit 11 encoded, bits 12-19 seq) + u32 checksum; one message per datagram; listener len = (h0&0x7FF)-8.
- Seq equal to the per-socket last_seq (initial 0; reset to -1 once >= 0xFF) is dropped.
- Bit 11 clear = plaintext, no checksum. Bit 11 set = XOR T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] with checksum h1 - ((T[seq]+sum(plain&0x5F)+T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq (cencmsg.py encode_by_array).
- owner+0x408 != 0 drops all. LE reads; a short read leaves stale stack values and does not advance.

Example plaintext (seq 2, uid 1, HP 800, MP 300): 13 20 00 00 00 00 00 00 0A 01 00 00 00 01 01 20 03 2C 01.
specs.trigger: The arena authority reports that an entity was healed or used HP/MP recovery (potion or heal skill). This includes healing a dead local player (the camera refocuses).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Map mode 1 only (owner+0x4D8 != NULL, map+0x70 == 1). owner+0x408 busy drops the datagram. The uid must be in scene+0xC.
- Both bools come before either u16; do not interleave. Send the bools as 0/1 (the client tests byte != 0).
- h0 length must match the flags: if a flag is set but its u16 is missing, a stale stack value is written as HP/MP.
- Each datagram mallocs 1-3 effect records and plays 1-3 positional sounds (0x54 always, even with both flags 0), so do not send per tick.
- Effect 0x58 always attaches to the local player's sprite.
- Reviving via hp does not change alive state +0x98; send the snapshot state as well.
- HP/MP u16, unclamped.
- Seq rules as UDP 0x06.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the byte layout and the effect/sound flow, and the asm confirms it. Stack slots: has_hp [esp+0x18] (0x4598B2 LEA after 3 pushes), has_mp [esp+0x30], hp [esp+0x34] (0x459929), mp [esp+0x28] (0x459A0E). Branches: 0x4598DF (has_hp), 0x45996D/0x4599F2 (has_mp).
The dispute was the grammar, and analyst A is correct. The exits at 0x45985E/0x459868 (map gate, before any read) and 0x45989E (lookup NULL, before the bools) are part of the parse and must be stops. The verified TCP S2C 0x40 grammar in protocol_spec.json uses exactly 'u32 uid / if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) { stop } / bool has_hp / bool has_mp / if(has_hp != 0) { u16 hp } / if(has_mp != 0) { u16 mp }'; B's version drops the stops.
On FUN_004307c0 behaviour B is more precise: 0x4307E6-0x4307FC calls FUN_004305b0(owner,0x27) only when scene+0xEE8 is NULL or its team byte is 0, not merely 'may call'.
Effect record fields verified at 0x459994-0x4599AD / 0x459A71-0x459A8A / 0x459AE8-0x459B01. The 0x58 record uid is taken from [scene+0x220] at 0x459A55.
open_questions: Asset names for effect/sound ids 0x37, 0x54 and 0x58 (0x54/0x37 match the client's heal-skill visuals; 0x58 is inferred to be MP recovery).
Whether attaching effect 0x58 to the local uid is intentional or a client bug.

specs.name: FriendList
specs.socket: game (7022). Dispatched by OnReceive_MainTcpHandler (reads from g_sock_game) -> default chain -> SubHandler3 @0x4708C0 with param1 = CMessenger* (main+0x4E4). Reads use CMessenger+0x74 as the CSNSocket, which S2C 0x03 sets to g_sock_game.

locations.role: call into SubHandler3 (ECX=pkt, args: [main+0x4E4] messenger, opcode, offset, len)
FUN_0046fb00: free and clear the whole friend list (CPList at messenger+0x04, head +0x08, tail +0x0C, count +0x10)
FUN_00459df0: append node to friend list
FUN_00470270: redraw friend window 0x176, label "(%u/%u)" = count/capacity
S2C 0x03 handler calls FUN_0046f860, which clears this list and zeroes capacity (messenger+0xD0/+0xD1)

specs.grammar:
u8 friend_capacity
u8 friend_count
repeat(friend_count) {
  str[17] name
  u8 channel
  u32 friend_id
  u8 status
}

fields.name: friend_capacity
fields.meaning: Maximum friend-list slots. Shown as the second number in "(count/capacity)". Client blocks C2S 0x30 add-friend when count == capacity ("Can't be add. Visit Frenaiga."), and blocks the 0x73 buy-a-slot request when capacity >= 50.

fields.name: friend_count
fields.meaning: Number of entries that follow (loop counter, unsigned byte).

fields.name: name
fields.meaning: Friend character name (NUL-padded). The node is zeroed first (0x28 bytes), so a name using all 17 bytes is still terminated.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Channel the friend is on. S2C 0x60 overwrites the same field and prints it in "<%s> has logged in.(Friend, Channel %d)".

fields.name: friend_id
fields.meaning: Server id of the friend. The client sends it back in C2S 0x32 delete-friend (window 0x17A+0x134) and C2S 0x33 chat-invite. S2C 0x60 status updates only apply if their u32 matches this field.

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: Online status, zero-extended to u32. 1 = offline: drawn grayed, sorted after online friends, and a chat invite shows "is not on line.". 0 = online (0x60 prints "has logged in. (Friend)"). 4 = online on a channel (0x60 prints the channel number). Any other value is sorted as online.

specs.semantics: Replaces the whole friend list. The handler frees every existing node, stores the capacity at messenger+0xD1, then builds one zeroed 0x28-byte node per entry (name +0x00, channel +0x14, friend_id +0x18, status +0x20, +0x24=0) and appends it to the CPList at messenger+0x04. Last, FUN_00470270 copies the list count into messenger+0xD0, redraws friend window 0x176 (entries with status != 1 are added first, then status == 1) and sets the "(count/capacity)" label. No reply is sent. Returns 1 (handled). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50/C52, social_friend#00): EN labels - window 0x176 is captioned "My Friends" with the header "(count/capacity)"; its ctrl 7 is "Converse" (not "Invite") and tab 0x1A is labelled "Mento". The window is opened from HUD window 3 ctrl 2 (the bottom-right "Avatar" button, tooltip "Character Information"), which opens menu 0x1CE (Quick Slot, My Friends, Card Deck, Map, Quest, Skill, Equip, Bag, Status); item 2 "My Friends" toggles window 0x176.
specs.trigger: Send after S2C 0x03 (login/enter world and every map change). The 0x03 handler (0x44E52F -> FUN_0046f860) unconditionally clears the friend list, sets capacity and count to 0 and resets the chat room id. Without a later 0x0B the client shows an empty "(0/0)" list and cannot add friends.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 returns 0 (the packet is silently dropped by the rest of the chain) if messenger+0x68 (app) or messenger+0x70 (g_ui_root) is NULL. Both are set in the CMessenger constructor 0x46F670 at startup, so in practice this always passes. messenger+0x74 (the CSNSocket used as `this` for reads) stays NULL until the first S2C 0x03. Sending 0x0B before 0x03 calls GetDataFromPacket with this=NULL; whether that works depends on Fireway and is untested. Nothing checks friend_count against capacity. No de-duplication, but the list is cleared first.
specs.references: PySlayer has no S2C 0x0B (server_packets only imports it in a try/except and the file is missing). reference_opcode_atlas.md calls sub3 0x0B "BUY"; that is the C2S meaning (C2S 0x0B = buy item), and the S2C meaning is the friend list. Our server never sends S2C 0x0B. Strings: "(%u/%u)" @0x6F808C and "Can't be add.\r\n\r\nVisit Frenaiga." (FUN_0046fe30).
open_questions: Status values other than 0, 1 and 4 (e.g. 2 or 3) render as online. Their intended meaning is unknown.
Which C2S request (if any) made the original server send 0x0B, or whether it was pushed right after 0x03, cannot be determined statically.
blind_open_questions: What is mgr+0x68 (a SubHandler3 gate)? It is probably set when the messenger/UI is initialized.
Exact meaning of status values 2 and 3 (sprites 0x96/0x97).
Is friend_id a character db id or a session id? It must match the u32 the server later sends in S2C 0x60.

spec_errata.new: labels and the Avatar -> menu 0x1CE path recorded

specs.name: ArenaEntityMpUpdate_Popup0 (set MP + MP damage number)

locations.role: gate: owner+0x4D8 NULL -> exit; 0x4596C7 map+0x70 != 1 -> exit (no reads)
local uid only: MP text '%d/%d' (+0xA0 / +0x1110) and gauge refresh
always: flush MP popup slots +0x1118 and +0x1120 for every entity
slot +0x1118: if +0x98 >= 3, record kind 4 (same team) / 3 (enemy), [7]=0 (0x43015A); slot zeroed at 0x430162

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (entity+0x84). If it is 0 or unknown, nothing more is read.

fields.name: cur_mp
fields.meaning: New ABSOLUTE current MP, zero-extended, unclamped vs max MP +0x1110. Written for any entity; also to the local player with HUD refresh when local.

fields.name: popup_value
fields.meaning: Floating MP number (MP popup slot 0, style 0). Assigned. 0 = no popup.

specs.length: Body 9 bytes including the opcode when the uid is found (5 consumed if unknown, 1 outside mode 1). The datagram is 17 bytes with the 8-byte header.
specs.semantics:
MP twin of UDP 0x06 (asm 0x4596B5-0x4597AC). Execution order:
1. Map gate.
2. Read u32 uid; lookup (stop if NULL).
3. Read u16 cur_mp, then u16 popup_value.
4. entity+0x1118 = popup_value.
5. entity+0xA0 = cur_mp.
6. If uid == scene+0x220: local entity +0xA0 = cur_mp (if scene+0x970 non-NULL) and FUN_00443780 refreshes the MP UI.
7. FUN_00430020(owner) walks all scene entities (needs scene+0x970). Non-zero +0x1118 and +0x1120 with byte +0x98 >= 3 become 0x20-byte records on owner+0x430 {kind, value, 0, 0x14, 0x28, +0x15A4, +0x15A8, style 0}, then the slots are zeroed. Kind in mode 1 is 4 when +0x14EB equals the local player's team, else 3; outside mode 1 it is 4 if +0x98 == 3, else 3. FUN_00430020 never reads +0x1128.
In the client's own FUN_00418ac0, the MP slots are used when the hit is redirected to MP (ADD +0x1118 at 0x419ECF for ordinary hits).
No emitter in the EN client.

FRAMING: identical to UDP-S2C:0x06.
- 8-byte header: u32 h0 (bits 0-10 total length incl. header, bit 11 encoded, bits 12-19 seq) + u32 checksum; one message per datagram; listener len = (h0&0x7FF)-8.
- A seq equal to the per-socket last_seq (initial 0, reset to -1 once >= 0xFF) is dropped.
- Bit 11 clear = plaintext, no checksum. Bit 11 set = XOR T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] with checksum h1 - ((T[seq]+sum(plain&0x5F)+T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq.
- owner+0x408 != 0 drops all. LE reads; short reads leave stale values.
specs.trigger: The arena authority reports an entity's MP reduced by an ordinary hit (damage redirected to MP) in a map-mode-1 room.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- owner+0x408 == 0, owner+0x4D8 != NULL, map+0x70 == 1, uid present; otherwise ignored.
- Seq and length rules as UDP 0x06.
- The popup is assigned; a duplicate datagram re-shows it. It needs scene+0x970 non-NULL and entity+0x98 >= 3.
- MP is u16, unclamped.
- No source validation.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: The wire layout is undisputed (u32, u16, u16; stack slots [esp+0x30] -> +0xA0, [esp+0x18] -> +0x1118 via 0x459735 CMP AL,0xB / 0x459742). Grammar: analyst A is correct. The map-mode exits at 0x4596BD/0x4596C7 happen before any read, and the lookup-NULL exit at 0x4596FB happens before the u16 reads; this matches the verified TCP spec convention, which B's flat grammar ignores.
FUN_00430020 was verified: 0x4300CE kind 4 (same team) / 0x430136 kind 3; 0x43015A [EAX+0x1C]=EBP=0.
The per-tick flush exists only in map mode 0 (FUN_0042b260 0x42B4BA). Fireway framing corrections as in UDP-S2C:0x06: initial last_seq 0, per B.

specs.name: FriendAddResult

locations.role: failure path: read str[17] target_name into zeroed stack local
FUN_004817d0 green (0xFF00C800) notice "<name>has been registered in your friend list."
FUN_00489da0 popup with the formatted failure text

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 or 0x0B = added (same handling for both). Failures: 2 = "<name>is not on line."; 3 = "<name>has refused to register you as a friend."; 4 = "<name>has turned friend function off."; 5 = "<name>doesn't have a empty spot in friend list."; 6 = "<name>is already in your friend list."; 7 = "There are no empty slots in your friend list." (name ignored); 0x15 = "An error occurred while adding.<name>". Any other value shows a popup built from an uninitialized buffer.

fields.name: name
fields.meaning: (success) New friend's name. Also used in the "has been registered" notice.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: (success) Friend's channel, same as the 0x0B entry.

fields.name: friend_id
fields.meaning: (success) Friend id, same as the 0x0B entry. Used later by C2S 0x32 delete and 0x33 invite, and matched by S2C 0x60.

fields.name: status
fields.meaning: (success) Online status: 1 = offline, 0/4 = online (see 0x0B).

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: (failure) Name of the player the add attempt targeted. It fills <%s> in the popup text and must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes, because stack bytes after it are uninitialized.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x20] (17 bytes zeroed before the read)

specs.semantics: Result of a friend-add attempt. On success (1 or 0x0B) the client builds one friend node, appends it to the friend list without checking capacity or duplicates, redraws window 0x176 (count/capacity) and shows a green notice "<name>has been registered in your friend list.". On failure it formats the matching message into a 128-byte buffer and opens popup window 0x16 (FUN_00489da0). No packet is sent back. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49, social_friend#02): every FAILURE code renders as a MODAL POPUP; only result 1 / 0x0B produce the green floating notice.
specs.trigger: Reply to the requester after C2S 0x30 (add friend: u32 id-or-0, str[17] target name) resolves. For example, after the target answers the S2C 0x0D prompt with C2S 0x31. It can also go to the accepting side. 0x0B looks like a second success code, possibly for the accepter; the client does not tell them apart.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same SubHandler3 gate as 0x0B (messenger+0x68 and +0x70 non-NULL; messenger+0x74 socket is only set after S2C 0x03). HAZARD: result values 0, 8, 9, 0x0A, 0x0C-0x14 and >= 0x16 go to 0x470B72, which passes an uninitialized 128-byte stack buffer ([esp+0x40]) to the popup. The text is garbage and the strcpy into the 0x3E9-byte dialog buffer could over-read. Only send 1, 2-7, 0x0B or 0x15. On success the list count can go past capacity, and duplicate names are not checked. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#02): the 24-byte SUCCESS form (result 1 + str[17] name + u8 channel + u32 friend_id + u8 status) is accepted and renders correctly - the grammar here is right; the wsproto encoder was building the 18-byte failure layout for result 1. Failure codes render as MODAL POPUPS; only result 1 / 0x0B produce the green floating notice.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Our server's 0x0C is the C2S SELL handler, and it never sends S2C 0x0C. The atlas does not name S2C 0x0C. The client-side add flow is FUN_0046fe30 (C2S 0x30, "Requesting <name> to be a friend").
open_questions: What was the real server-side difference between result 1 and 0x0B? The client handles them the same.
Is result 7 (no empty slots in YOUR list) sent to the requester while 5 goes about the target? Presumed from the strings.
blind_open_questions: Semantic difference between result 1 and 0x0B: the client treats them identically. Perhaps one goes to the requester and one to the acceptor.
Meaning of the u32 in C2S 0x30. FUN_00472900 passes 0 from the add-friend window 0x179, and FUN_00446300 passes another value.

spec_errata.new: success = 24 B (live), failures are modal popups

spec_errata.old: failure text described as a popup without the notice/popup split
spec_errata.new: failures = modal popups, success = floating notice

specs.name: ArenaEntityHpUpdate_Popup1 (set HP + delayed damage number with effect/sound 1)

gate owner+0x4D8 != NULL and map+0x70 == 1, else exit with no reads
local uid only: HP text/gauge refresh
slot +0x111C -> popup record with [7]=1 (0x42FF1E), slot zeroed at 0x42FF2A
renderer: style 1 or 2 is not drawn while age [2] < 0x78; at age == 0x78, style 1 queues effect {type 6, id 1} at popup x/y and Play_Sound(1); the number is then drawn with age-0x78

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (entity+0x84). If it is 0 or unknown, nothing more is read.

fields.name: cur_hp
fields.meaning: New ABSOLUTE current HP, zero-extended, unclamped. Written for any entity; also to the local player with HUD refresh when uid is local.

specs.length: Body 9 bytes including the opcode when the uid is found (5 consumed if unknown, 1 outside mode 1). The datagram is 17 bytes with the 8-byte header.
specs.semantics:
Same code block as UDP 0x06 (0x4595B9). Only the popup slot differs: the opcode compare at 0x45964E routes the value to entity+0x111C. After the writes (entity+0x9C = cur_hp; local copy and FUN_00443690 when uid == scene+0x220), FUN_0042fd20(owner) flushes every entity's slots. +0x111C becomes a record with style [7]=1 and kind 0 (same team, +0x14EB) or 1 (enemy), provided byte +0x98 >= 3; the slot is then zeroed.
In FUN_00430aa0, a style 1 record waits until its age reaches 0x78. At exactly 0x78 it queues effect record {type 6, id 1} at the popup position and plays sound 1, then the number is drawn.
In the client's own damage code FUN_00418ac0 this slot is used (ADD at 0x419EAD) when the preset-damage stack arg ([esp+0x80]) is non-zero and the attack-kind arg ([esp+0x74]) != 4. In arena mode 1 (or when not host) that marks preset/skill-type HP damage.
No alive-state change. No emitter in the EN client.

- 8-byte header: u32 h0 (bits 0-10 total length incl. header, bit 11 encoded, bits 12-19 seq) + u32 checksum; one message per datagram; listener len = (h0&0x7FF)-8.
- Seq equal to the per-socket last_seq is dropped (initial 0; reset to -1 once >= 0xFF).
- Bit 11 clear = plaintext, no checksum. Bit 11 set = XOR T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] and h1 - ((T[seq]+sum(plain&0x5F)+T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq (cencmsg.py encode_by_array).

- Same gates as UDP 0x06: owner+0x408 == 0, owner+0x4D8 != NULL, map+0x70 == 1, uid present.
- Seq and length rules as UDP 0x06.
- The popup is assigned, not accumulated. Each delayed popup spawns an effect and plays sound 1, so do not spam.

specs.name: FriendRequestPrompt

locations.role: FUN_004838c0: set control 2 text of window 0x17C = requester_name
on button click: FUN_004701e0(window+0x134, control2 text, accept) -> C2S 0x31
C2S 0x31 send: u8 0x31, u32 request_id, str[17] name, u8 accept(1/0)

specs.grammar:
u32 request_id
str[17] requester_name

fields.name: request_id
fields.meaning: Id of the pending friend request, probably the requester's id. The client stores it and sends it back unchanged in C2S 0x31.

fields.name: requester_name
fields.meaning: Name of the player who wants to add you. Shown in dialog 0x17C control 2 and echoed in C2S 0x31. Must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes, because following stack bytes are uninitialized and the text is strcpy'd.

specs.semantics: Incoming friend request. Opens the Accept/Refuse dialog (window 0x17C), stores request_id in window+0x134 and puts the requester's name in control 2. The handler sends nothing itself. When the user clicks a button (FUN_00472900 control 4 = accept, 5/6 = refuse), the client sends C2S 0x31 = u32 request_id, str[17] name, u8 accept (1 or 0).
specs.trigger: Send to the target player when another player sends C2S 0x30 (add friend) naming them.
specs.expected_response: Deferred, user-driven: C2S 0x31 { u32 request_id, str[17] requester_name, u8 accept (1 = accept, 0 = refuse) }. The server should then send S2C 0x0C to the requester (success entry, or result 3 = refused) and presumably 0x0C success to the accepter.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same SubHandler3 gate. Pops a modal dialog every time. HISTORICAL HAZARD: old server snapshots (windslayer_server.snapshot.20260426*.py) echoed the 18-byte C2S movement 0x0D as S2C 0x0D. The client parsed that as this packet, read 3 bytes past the end and opened friend dialog 0x17C, which is consistent with the desync recorded in project_local_player_spawn.md. Never reuse S2C 0x0D for anything else.
specs.references: reference_opcode_atlas.md calls sub3 0x0D "heartbeat"; that is wrong for S2C, and C2S 0x0D is movement. PySlayer has no S2C 0x0D. S2C 0x10 has the same shape (u32 + str[17]) and opens window 0x17D as the chat-invite prompt (answered by C2S 0x34).
open_questions: Is request_id the requester's friend_id (character DB id) or a server-side transaction id? The client treats it as opaque.
blind_open_questions: What Fireway's char-buffer GetDataFromPacket does when fewer than 17 bytes remain (relevant to the old 18-byte echo, which has only 14 bytes left after the u32).

specs.name: MessengerChatRoomJoinResult

locations.role: SubHandler3 gate: [mgr+0x68] != 0 and [mgr+0x70] != 0, else nothing is read
handler block start (opcode comes in as arg [EBP+0xC] and is not read here)
member_count == 0 -> JBE 0x471FF6 (return 1; nothing else is read)
FUN_004830f0(0x177) == 0 -> return 1 without reading the names
FUN_0048b484(0x28) = operator new (malloc loop, memory NOT zeroed)
loop: read str[17] member_name into node+0x00 (IAT 0x4A4098, N=0x11)
FUN_00459df0 appends the node to the CPList at window+0xBC (head +0xC0, tail +0xC4, count +0xC8)
member_count > 2 -> return; otherwise sprintf '<%s> has entered.' using the last node name ([esp+0x1c])

FUN_00489da0(text,3,3,0,0) modal popup (0x80-byte text buffer at [esp+0x40])

fields.name: subtype
fields.meaning: 1 = joined/room formed (room id + member list follow). Failure popups: 2 = '<name>' + 'is in other channel. You can't have a personal chat.' (0x6F4CD0); 3 = 'has refused to have a personal chat.' (0x6F4BCC); 4 = 'is rejecting chatting.' (0x6F4D0C); 5 = 'You cannot invite more players. The chatting room is full.' (0x6F4AC4, name read but unused); 6 = ' is in conversation with other player right now.' (0x6F4B00); 8 = 'is not on line.' (0x6F4C3C) and the friend is marked offline. 0, 7 and 9+ go to 0x47113C and show a popup from an uninitialized 0x80-byte stack buffer.

fields.name: room_id
fields.meaning: (subtype 1) Messenger chat-room id. It is written to mgr+0xCC before member_count is checked, so it is stored even when member_count == 0. Nonzero means 'in a room': S2C 0x10 invites are ignored and C2S 0x35 room chat is allowed. Copied to window 0x177 +0x134 when the window opens.

fields.name: member_count
fields.meaning: (subtype 1) Number of 17-byte names that follow (movzx, 0..255). 0 = handler returns immediately (no window, no more reads). If it is 1 or 2, the client adds the room line '<last member_name> has entered.'

fields.name: member_name
fields.meaning: (subtype 1) Room member name. Exactly 17 bytes are copied into a new malloc'd 0x28-byte node that is NOT zeroed, which is appended to the window 0x177 member list (+0xBC) with no clearing or de-duplication. The name must be NUL-terminated within the 17 bytes.

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: (subtype != 1) Name of the invited/other player, printed as '<name>' in the popup; for subtype 8 it also selects the friend to mark offline and remove. Read into a zeroed 17-byte buffer with no extra terminator, so it must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (max 16 chars).

specs.semantics: Result of a messenger personal/group chat-room invite or join. Subtype 1: the client stores room_id at mgr+0xCC and reads member_count. If the count is 0 it returns. Otherwise it opens window 0x177 (FUN_00483430 0x177,3,1). If the window can't be fetched it returns without reading the names. Otherwise it sets window+0x134 = room_id, appends each name to the window member list, and calls FUN_00489960(0x177,9). If the count is at most 2 it also adds '<last name> has entered.' in color 0xFF00A2A2 via FUN_00472430. Any other subtype reads target_name and shows a modal popup through FUN_00489da0(text,3,3,0,0). Subtype 8 first calls FUN_004723c0, which sets the friend's status (+0x20) to 1 (offline) in the friend list headed at mgr+0x8. It does the same for the single head node at [mgr+0x18] if its name matches, removes and frees matching entries in the list headed at mgr+0x28, and refreshes the UI with FUN_00470270. The client sends nothing back.
specs.trigger: Server reply to C2S 0x33 (chat invite: u32, str[17] name): a failure subtype (2-6, 8), or subtype 1 once the room is formed. It is probably also sent to the invitee after it accepts an S2C 0x10 prompt with C2S 0x34, and to existing members when someone joins (count 1 -> 'has entered.'). Those last cases can't be proven statically.
specs.expected_response: none (afterwards the client may send C2S 0x35 room chat)
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 gate at 0x4708DE: [mgr+0x68] and [mgr+0x70] must be nonzero. S2C 0x03 (FUN_0046f860) resets mgr+0xCC. HAZARDS: subtype 0, 7 or 9+ passes the uninitialized 0x80-byte buffer [esp+0x40] to the popup (garbage text and a possible over-read), so only use 1-6 or 8. Subtype 1 with a count > 0 stores room_id even if window 0x177 can't be fetched. Member nodes are not zeroed and the list isn't cleared or de-duplicated, so every name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes, and resending the full list may duplicate rows. target_name/member_name with 17 non-NUL bytes makes sprintf %s read past the buffer.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A's grammar was 'u8 subtype; if 1 { u32 room_id; u8 member_count; if count==0 stop; repeat(count) str[17] } else str[17]'. Analyst B's was the same without the explicit stop. On the wire they are identical: with count 0, repeat(0) reads nothing, so both consume 1+4+1+17n or 1+17 bytes. A's explicit early exit matches the code exactly: 0x470E7A CMP byte [esp+0x13],0 / 0x470E7F JBE 0x471FF6, which does MOV EAX,1 and returns, so that form is kept. The field widths were verified in the asm: u8 via IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x470E3F and 0x470E74, u32 via 0x4A40C8 into [EBX+0xCC] at 0x470E60, and the 17-byte char reads (PUSH 0x11, IAT 0x4A4098) at 0x470EEF in the loop (0x470F03-0x470F11, movzx count, JL) and at 0x470FA6. The analysts also disagreed on details that don't affect the wire. (1) Node zeroing: A said not zeroed and was right. FUN_0048b484 is operator new (a _malloc/_callnewh loop) with no memset, and only 17 bytes are written, so B's 'zeroed node' is wrong. (2) Subtype 8 side effects: each analyst was partly right. The code at 0x4723C0-0x47242B marks the friend found by FUN_00472180 in the list headed at [mgr+8] (+0x20=1) and also compares only the head node of [mgr+0x18] and marks it (B saw this, A didn't). It then calls FUN_00472340, which removes and frees matching entries from the list headed at [mgr+0x28] and refreshes via FUN_00470270 (A saw this, B didn't). (3) Jump table 0x472148, dumped from the binary: 2->0x471068 (0x6F4CD0 'in other channel'), 3->0x470FC4 (refused), 4->0x471016 (rejecting), 5->0x471120 (room full; sprintf '%s' at 0x4A6318, then shared popup), 6->0x471116 (in conversation, jumps into 0x47101B), 7->0x47113C (default, uninitialized text), 8->0x4710BA (not on line). Both analysts had this mapping right. Neither PySlayer (its 0x0F is the C2S equip) nor our server covers this packet.

Subtype 5's popup does not use target_name at all (the field is read but unused). Original question: "Does the member list include the receiving player, and is subtype 1 sent to both inviter and invitee? The 'has entered' line for count <= 2 suggests self plus one other."
Whether closing or reopening window 0x177 (FUN_00446300 -> FUN_00472790) clears the member list at +0xBC. If not, repeated subtype-1 packets pile up duplicate rows.
Subtype 7 has no text in this client; was it unused by the original server?
What the list at mgr+0x18 is: only its head node is compared, so it may be a 'currently selected/whispered friend' slot rather than a full list.

spec_errata.old: whether the member list includes the receiver
spec_errata.new: it does; subtype 5 ignores target_name

specs.name: MessengerChatInvite

locations.role: call into sub3 from OnReceive_MainTcpHandler (this=[game_state+0x4E4] CMessenger, offset passed by value)
dialog 0x17D button handler: reads window+0x134 and calls FUN_00470230 (sends C2S 0x34)
C2S 0x34 builder: u8 0x34, u32 id, u8 accept
C2S 0x33 invite sender (u32 target_uid, str[17] target_name) that causes the server to emit this packet to the target

specs.grammar:
u32 inviter_id
str[17] inviter_name

fields.name: inviter_id
fields.meaning: Invitation id (most likely the inviter's character uid). The client doesn't read it; it stores it on the dialog and sends it back unchanged in C2S 0x34.

fields.name: inviter_name
fields.meaning: Name of the player sending the chat-room invite (NUL-terminated, max 16 chars). Shown in control #2 of dialog 0x17D.
fields.dest_or_source: local [esp+0x20] (zeroed first) -> FUN_004838C0(ctrl 2) text of window 0x17D

specs.semantics: Invite to a Messenger chat room (1:1 or group chat). Both fields are always read. Then, only if CMessenger+0xCC (current chat-room id) == 0, i.e. the player is not already in a chat room, the client opens dialog window 0x17D via FUN_00483430(0x17D,3,1). It stores inviter_id at window+0x134 and puts inviter_name into control 2. If the player is already in a room, the invite is silently dropped and handled returns 1. It is the chat-room counterpart of S2C 0x0D (friend request, dialog 0x17C, answered with C2S 0x31).
specs.trigger: Server sends it to the target when another player sends C2S 0x33 (invite to conversation: u32 target_uid or 0, str[17] target_name).
specs.expected_response: When the user closes dialog 0x17D, the client sends C2S 0x34 {u32 inviter_id echoed from window+0x134, u8 accept}. Button id 4 sends accept = EDI (1 on this path). Buttons 5 and 6 send accept = 0. No reply is sent if the invite was dropped because the player is already in a room.

CMessenger+0x74 (socket) is only set by FUN_0046F860, which the S2C 0x07 enter-world handler calls at 0x0044E52F, so send this only after 0x07. The invite is ignored with no reply if the player is already in a messenger room (+0xCC != 0), so a server must not block waiting for C2S 0x34.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not implemented in windslayer_server.py. reference_opcode_atlas.md lumps sub3 opcodes under unrelated names; the sub3 handlers are really the CMessenger subsystem (friends / chat room / mentor), as the vtable CMessenger in constructor FUN_0046F670 shows.

Dialog 0x17D body text comes from UI resources, not the exe. Exact wording is unverified.

specs.name: ArenaEntityMpSet (silent MP sync)

locations.role: gate: owner+0x4D8 NULL -> exit; 0x4597C3 map+0x70 != 1 -> exit (no reads)

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (entity+0x84). If it is 0 or unknown, nothing more is read.

fields.name: cur_mp
fields.meaning: New ABSOLUTE current MP, zero-extended, unclamped vs +0x1110.

specs.length: Body 7 bytes including the opcode (grammar 6) when the uid is found (5 consumed if unknown, 1 outside mode 1). The datagram is 15 bytes with the 8-byte header (h0 length field 0x00F).
specs.semantics:
Plain MP set with no visuals (asm 0x4597B1-0x459851).
1. Map gate.
2. Read u32 uid; lookup (stop if NULL).
3. Read u16 cur_mp; entity+0xA0 = cur_mp.
4. If uid == scene+0x220: local entity +0xA0 = cur_mp (if scene+0x970 non-NULL) and FUN_00443780 refreshes the MP UI.
There is no popup slot, and unlike 0x0B/0x0D/0x0F it does not call FUN_00430020, so pending MP popups are not flushed. Likely use: MP spend/regen sync.
No emitter in the EN client.

FRAMING: identical to UDP-S2C:0x06.
- 8-byte header: u32 h0 (bits 0-10 total length incl. header, bit 11 encoded, bits 12-19 seq) + u32 checksum; one message per datagram; listener len = (h0&0x7FF)-8.
- Seq equal to the per-socket last_seq (initial 0; reset to -1 once >= 0xFF) is dropped.
- Bit 11 clear = plaintext, no checksum. Bit 11 set = XOR T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF] with checksum h1 - ((T[seq]+sum(plain&0x5F)+T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF]) & 0x0FFFFFFF) == seq (cencmsg.py encode_by_array).
- owner+0x408 != 0 drops all. LE reads; short read leaves the stale value.

Example plaintext (seq 3, uid 1, mp 120): 0F 30 00 00 00 00 00 00 10 01 00 00 00 78 00.
specs.trigger: The arena authority reports a non-damage MP change (skill cost, regen, item) in a map-mode-1 room.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- owner+0x408 == 0, owner+0x4D8 != NULL, map+0x70 == 1, uid present; otherwise ignored.
- Seq/length rules as UDP 0x06. A short u16 read writes a stale stack value as MP.
- MP is u16, unclamped.
- No source validation.
specs.references:
ADJUDICATION: The wire layout is undisputed (u32 uid, u16 cur_mp; [esp+0x18] -> +0xA0 at 0x45981E). Grammar: analyst A is correct. The asm exits at 0x4597B9/0x4597C3 before reading anything outside map mode 1, and at 0x4597F7 after the uid when FUN_004189f0 returns NULL, so the u16 read is conditional. This matches the verified TCP spec gate convention; B's flat 'u32 uid / u16 cur_mp' omits it.
Both analysts correctly note: no FUN_00430020 call, and FUN_00443780 only on the local branch (JNZ exit at 0x459834).
Framing seq-init (0) and checksum-mask placement follow B, verified in Fireway.dll at 0x100019E6 and 0x10006C41-0x10006C4C.
open_questions: Which game events originally triggered 0x10 versus the popup variants (no sender in the EN client).

specs.name: GroundItemSpawn

locations.role: branch: CMP opcode(byte [esp+0x43]),0x12; JNZ -> 0x45183C (0x11 path reads the state byte)
CALL FUN_00423a10 = allocate 0x40-byte ground-item record and append it to the scene ground-item list (scene+0x18)
per-tick ground-item state machine (1 -> 3 after 800ms; 2 freed after 1000ms)
pickup key handler: distance/ownership gate, sends C2S 0x1F u16 ground_id

specs.grammar:
u8 entry_count
repeat(entry_count) {
  u16 item_id
  u16 quantity
  u16 x
  u16 y
  u16 ground_id
  u32 drop_time
  u32 owner_uid
  u32 source_uid
  u8 opt_count
  repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt_word }
  u16 opt_tail
  u8 state
}

fields.name: entry_count
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x5e], outer loop bound (0 = nothing happens)
fields.meaning: number of ground-item entries

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item template id; 1-based index into item-def vector [scene+0xF84]+8. 0 or out of range -> no record created (fields still consumed). itemdef+0x154 (category 0/1/2) copied to rec+0x18

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: stack count (the local/offline drop generator passes 1); no reader found in this pass

fields.name: x
fields.dest_or_source: stack esp+0x164 -> arg4 -> rec+0x0E (u16) and rec+0x30 (f64)
fields.meaning: world X pixel coordinate

fields.name: y
fields.dest_or_source: stack esp+0x19c -> arg5 -> rec+0x10 (u16) and rec+0x38 (f64)
fields.meaning: world Y pixel coordinate; client subtracts 10 when state==1 (or when scene+0xF24 != 0)

fields.name: ground_id
fields.dest_or_source: stack esp+0xe0 -> arg6 -> rec+0x12 (replaced by a local counter scene+0xF34 if scene+0xF24 != 0)
fields.meaning: ground-item instance id; the client echoes it in C2S 0x1F pickup and S2C 0x13 matches on it

fields.name: drop_time
fields.meaning: drop timestamp in the map clock scene+0xF1C (ms; set by S2C 0x03/0x08, +30 per client tick). Ownership lapses when drop_time + 15000 < scene+0xF1C

fields.name: owner_uid
fields.meaning: uid with loot rights; 0 = anyone may pick up. Otherwise only this uid can, until the 15 s window ends

fields.name: source_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the entity that dropped it (for example the killed monster). Only 0x12 uses it for positioning

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: number of item extension words that follow (must be <= 5; see hazards)

fields.name: opt_word
fields.dest_or_source: stack u16 buffer esp+0x218+2*i -> copied to rec+0x02+2*i
fields.meaning: item extension/option word i (same 12-byte block that equipment slots keep at +0x422+i*0xC; same u8 n + u16[n] + u16 pattern as S2C 0x1D)

fields.name: opt_tail
fields.meaning: 6th (last) extension word, always present

fields.name: state
fields.meaning: initial ground-item state: 0 = resting on ground, 1 = drop pop-in (y-10; after 800 ms becomes 3), 3 = falling/bounce physics then 0, 2 = being picked up (flies to rec+0x1C entity, freed after 1000 ms)

specs.semantics: For each entry the client builds a 0x40-byte ground-item record (FUN_00423a10) and appends it to the scene ground-item list (scene+0x18/0x1C). Record layout: +0 item_id, +2..+0xD six extension words, +0xE x, +0x10 y, +0x12 ground_id, +0x14 quantity, +0x16 state, +0x18 item category (itemdef+0x154: 0 = consume bag +0x3AA, 1 = equip bag +0x3A9, 2 = other bag +0x3AB), +0x1C owner_uid, +0x20 source_uid, +0x24 drop_time, +0x28 animation timer = 0, +0x30/+0x38 f64 x/y. Unlike 0x12, 0x11 always uses the wire x/y and takes the state byte from the wire, so it suits listing items already on the ground (state 0) or spawning drops at exact coordinates (state 1). Items are drawn and pickable only while scene+0xF00 == 6.
specs.trigger: Server sends it to show items already lying on a map (for example after the map-load sequence), or to spawn drops at explicit coordinates with a chosen initial state.
specs.expected_response: None immediately. Later, when the player presses the pickup key within about 25 px (dx^2+dy^2 < 625) of an item they may take, the client sends C2S 0x1F u16 ground_id (send site 0x43D7E8) and the server should answer with S2C 0x13.
specs.gates_and_hazards: STACK OVERFLOW: extension words go into a 12-byte stack buffer (esp+0x218..0x223). opt_count 6 is harmless because opt_tail overwrites slot 5; opt_count >= 7 writes past the buffer. Keep opt_count <= 5 (recommended: exactly 5). STALE DATA: the buffer is zeroed once per packet, not per entry, so an entry with a smaller opt_count inherits the previous entry's words; send a constant 5. An invalid item_id silently skips record creation without desyncing the reads. With state=1 the client subtracts 10 from y. With state=2 the item is freed after 1 s. Pickup gate in 0x43D5C0: state != 2, distance < 25 px, and owner_uid in {0, local uid} or drop_time+15000 < scene+0xF1C; otherwise the client shows "You don't have ownership of this item." A full bag shows "There isn't empty space in the inventory." LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C19, item_inventory#09): the map change (S2C 0x08 / 0x03) CLEARS the client ground-item list, so every ground item must be re-sent with S2C 0x11 on map entry. Container: scene+0x18 = {vtable 0x6F7F3C, head node, tail node, u32 count at +0x24}; node = {next, prev, record*}.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x11/0x12) reads the option block first and has fewer fields, so the layout differs; EN asm is authoritative. PySlayer has no S2C 0x11 builder. Our server does not send 0x11. Its comment at windslayer_server.py:170 agrees that 0x12 is a ground spawn, not a walk.
open_questions: No reader of rec+0x14 (quantity) was found in this pass, so the name 'quantity' is inferred from the offline generator passing 1.

[RESOLVED by live verification item_inventory#09, 2026-09-17] Live: YES - the ground list is cleared by the map change (0x08/0x03); the server must re-send 0x11 for the new map. Container scene+0x18 = {vtable 0x6F7F3C, head, tail, u32 count at +0x24}, node = {next, prev, record*}. Original question: "Whether the ground-item list is cleared on map change was not traced."
scene+0xF24 != 0 looks like a local/offline simulation mode (FUN_00413920 generates drops locally); exact meaning unconfirmed.
blind_open_questions: What sets and resets the client scene clock [scene+0xF1C] (FUN_00428090 writes it, possibly on map load)? This decides whether a server-chosen drop_time can ever enforce ownership.
What is [scene+0xF24]? When it is non-zero, drop_id is replaced by counter [scene+0xF34] and objects are mirrored into list scene+0x28 (replay/record mode?).
What do the 6 attr words mean (options, upgrade level, durability)? They are only copied as an opaque 12-byte block into the player's slot option array (+0x422+i*12) for category-1 items.
How are state values > 3 rendered? They are not handled by the update loops seen.

spec_errata.new: map change clears the list - re-send 0x11 on entry

spec_errata.new: cleared - re-send 0x11

specs.name: UdpLocalEndpointDiscovery

locations.role: Thunk into FUN_00458640 (ECX=body, owner=0x70EA00, len=(hdr&0x7FF)-8, from_ip, from_port)
owner+0x408 (WM_CLOSE) gate, then EnterCriticalSection(owner+0x368) @0x458688, then u8 opcode @0x4586AD; jump-table index 6 -> 0x459B45
Gate: scene [owner+0x4CC] != NULL and scene+0x220 (account_id/local uid) != 0; otherwise no read
u32 read (IAT 0x4A40C8) into stack [esp0+0x14]; never used afterwards
strcpy(scene+0x224, from_ip). from_ip is Fireway's inet_ntoa of the datagram SOURCE address (max 15 chars + NUL)
scene+0x244 = 0xA79B (42907), a constant; the source port is ignored
inet_ntoa(sin_addr) copied into a 16-byte buffer, ntohs(sin_port); both passed to UDPBufferManager

specs.grammar: u32 sender_account_id

fields.name: sender_account_id
fields.meaning: The broadcaster's account id / local uid (scene+0x220 on the sender). The receiver reads it and discards it: no comparison with its own uid.
fields.dest_or_source: sender: scene+0x220 (0x44DFE0); receiver: stack local only (unused)

specs.length: Body is 5 bytes including the opcode, so the datagram is 13 bytes and header size = 0x00D. Fixed length. A truncated body still works: the failed u32 read only logs, and the IP copy happens anyway.
specs.semantics:
Framing: same Fireway UDP framing as the UDP-S2C:0x03 spec. 8-byte header: u32 size|0x800(encoded)|seq<<12, then u32 by-array checksum. The seq must differ from the last accepted seq on the socket. Plaintext (bit 11 clear) is also accepted.

Purpose: local P2P endpoint self-discovery.
- Right after a successful login, the client broadcasts {0x11, account_id} to 255.255.255.255:42907 from its own socket, which is bound to 0.0.0.0:42907. The broadcast is delivered back to that socket.
- Handler steps:
  1. Checks that a scene exists and that account_id (scene+0x220) is set.
  2. Consumes the u32 and ignores it.
  3. Zeroes the 16-byte string scene+0x224 and copies in the datagram's SOURCE IPv4 dotted string, i.e. the client's own outgoing interface address as seen by the stack.
  4. Forces scene+0x244 = 42907.
- Uses of these values:
  - The client reports them to the game server as p2p_ip (str[16]) and p2p_udp_port (u32) in C2S 0x2B EnterWorldRequest.
  - FUN_00423260 uses scene+0x244 as the loopback SendTo port.
- No other code writes scene+0x224. The scene ctor memset (0x411FAE, +0x48..+0xEE7) leaves it all zeros until this datagram arrives. scene+0x244 is also set to 42907 at 0x4400D9 and 0x476526.
specs.trigger: The client itself: S2C login result==1 handler (0x44DFBC-0x44E012), once per successful login. Nothing on the server side needs to send it. It could also arrive from any other host broadcasting on the LAN (another client logging in) or from a deliberate unicast.
specs.expected_response: None. The learned endpoint is reported later in C2S 0x2B (key 0x42F904/0x2B, fields p2p_ip / p2p_udp_port).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Gates:
- owner+0x408 == 0.
- UDP header accepted (seq != last accepted seq; valid checksum if bit 11 is set).
- scene != NULL and scene+0x220 != 0. Before login the datagram is consumed with no effect.

Hazards:
- NO SENDER VALIDATION. Every 0x11 datagram from any source overwrites p2p_ip with that sender's address. A server unicasting 0x11 would set p2p_ip to the SERVER's IP, not the client's. Another client logging in on the same LAN rewrites this client's p2p_ip to the other machine's IP. The server should not send this opcode.
- If the broadcast loopback is blocked (firewall, no interface or broadcast route, port 42907 bind failure), p2p_ip stays empty (all zeros) in C2S 0x2B.
- The IP string always fits in 16 bytes because Fireway builds it with inet_ntoa, so the unbounded strcpy cannot overflow.
- Generic UDP framing hazards (see UDP-S2C:0x03): seq collision drop, crash on an encoded datagram with size < 8, overflow above 4078 bytes.
specs.references:
- PROTOCOL.md C2S 0x2B EnterWorldRequest: p2p_ip is 'learned from its UDP 0x11 datagram's source address'; captures show '127.0.0.1' and '10.5.0.2'.
- PROTOCOL.md S2C login result: the broadcast of 0x11 + account_id to 255.255.255.255:42907.
- windslayer_server.py _fake_map_server (disabled) once sent 20x UDP 0x11 + 64 zero bytes as a guessed 'map-server response' and saw UI errors. Statically, 0x11 only rewrites scene+0x224/+0x244, so it is not a map-server response.
- The server's UDPMapServer class is never started, and there is no UDP send path.
open_questions: The earlier live experiment (20 UDP 0x11 datagrams to 127.0.0.1:42907) was followed by 'cascading UI errors'. Static analysis of case 0x11 shows no UI side effects, so those symptoms were probably coincidental or caused by concurrent TCP experiments. Unverified.
Whether the original server actually used p2p_ip/p2p_udp_port from C2S 0x2B to broker arena P2P, or the room host at host_ip:room_no+10000 learned addresses from datagram sources instead.
blind_open_questions: Does Windows always deliver the client's own 255.255.255.255 broadcast back to its socket, for multi-NIC or VPN setups? If not, p2p_ip in C2S 0x2B stays empty.
The windslayer_server.py comment near line 841 attributes 'cascading UI errors' to a 20x UDP 0x11 experiment. This UDP handler has no UI calls, so the cause lies elsewhere (unverified).
Did the original server use C2S 0x2B p2p_ip for anything, such as NAT detection or arena host selection?

specs.name: GroundItemDrop

locations.role: branch on opcode == 0x12: no state byte read; position resolved from entities
FUN_004189f0(EDX=source_uid, scene): find entity by uid in scene+0xC list
neither entity found: use wire x/y
CALL FUN_00423a10 with state arg hard-coded to 1

specs.grammar:
u8 entry_count
repeat(entry_count) {
  u16 item_id
  u16 quantity
  u16 x
  u16 y
  u16 ground_id
  u32 drop_time
  u32 owner_uid
  u32 source_uid
  u8 opt_count
  repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt_word }
  u16 opt_tail
}

fields.name: entry_count
fields.meaning: number of dropped items

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item template id (1-based into [scene+0xF84]+8; invalid -> skipped)

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: stack count

fields.name: x
fields.dest_or_source: rec+0x0E / rec+0x30 f64, only if neither entity is found
fields.meaning: fallback world X

fields.name: y
fields.dest_or_source: rec+0x10 (minus 10) / rec+0x38, only if neither entity is found
fields.meaning: fallback world Y

fields.name: ground_id
fields.meaning: ground-item instance id (echoed by C2S 0x1F, matched by S2C 0x13)

fields.name: drop_time
fields.meaning: drop time in the scene+0xF1C map clock (ms); owner rights expire 15000 ms later

fields.name: owner_uid
fields.meaning: uid with loot priority (0 = anyone)

fields.name: source_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the dropping entity (for example the dead monster)

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: number of extension words (<= 5)

fields.name: opt_word
fields.meaning: item extension/option word

fields.name: opt_tail
fields.meaning: 6th extension word

specs.semantics: Same record creation as 0x11, with state forced to 1 (pop-in animation, then fall physics after 800 ms, then resting). Position: if an entity with uid == source_uid exists in the scene entity list (scene+0xC), the item appears at that entity's truncated (int)posX (+0x11F8) and posY (+0x1288); otherwise at the entity with uid == owner_uid; otherwise at the wire x/y. A uid of 0 never matches. y is then reduced by 10 (state == 1).
specs.trigger: A monster dies with loot, or an item is dropped onto the map. Broadcast to players on that map.
specs.expected_response: None immediately; later C2S 0x1F u16 ground_id pickup request, answered by S2C 0x13.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same stack overflow (opt_count >= 7) and stale-word hazards as 0x11. POSITION PITFALL: if the monster (source_uid) was already removed client-side and owner_uid is the killer, the item appears at the killer's feet, not the death spot. To force the wire x/y, set source_uid and owner_uid to 0 or non-existent uids (owner 0 = free-for-all), or use 0x11 with state=1. Positions are truncated to u16. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C19, item_inventory#09): the map change (S2C 0x08 / 0x03) CLEARS the client ground-item list, so every ground item must be re-sent with S2C 0x11 on map entry. Container: scene+0x18 = {vtable 0x6F7F3C, head node, tail node, u32 count at +0x24}; node = {next, prev, record*}.
specs.references: Our server's _build_opcode_12_drop (windslayer_server.py:1651) has the right widths (26 bytes for one entry with no options) but mislabels fields. It writes item, x, y, count, 0, ground_uid(u32), x(u32), 0(u32), 0, 0. The client reads item, quantity, x, y, ground_id, drop_time, owner_uid, source_uid. Result: quantity=x, x=y, y=1, ground_id=0, owner_uid=x. This explains the 'misaligned drop position' and 'un-pickable' notes at :1874. The builder is unused (drops go straight to the bag). The KR 0x11/0x12 layout differs.
open_questions: Whether FUN_004189f0 can match the local player (is the local entity in the scene+0xC list?). Probably yes, since RegisterLocalPlayer calls it, but not verified.
rec+0x14 quantity has no confirmed reader.
blind_open_questions: Same open questions as 0x11: the clock origin of [scene+0xF1C] and the meaning of [scene+0xF24] and the attr words.
Should the server send 0x12 before or after the monster's removal/death packet so that the source_uid lookup still finds the entity?

spec_errata.old: clearing of the ground list on map change untraced
spec_errata.new: map change clears the list - re-send 0x11 on entry

specs.name: GroundItemPickedUp

locations.role: CALL FUN_00440e50 (fastcall ECX=ground_id, EDX=picker_uid; stack: this, quantity)
find the ground record by rec+0x12, mark it picked, add to the local bag if picker is the local player, show message

specs.grammar:
u16 ground_id
u16 quantity
u32 picker_uid

fields.name: ground_id
fields.dest_or_source: stack esp+0x200 -> ECX -> compared with rec+0x12
fields.meaning: ground-item instance id from 0x11/0x12 (and C2S 0x1F)

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: count added to the bag (consume via FUN_00423b70, other via FUN_00423e70) and shown as '(Count:%u)'; not used for equipment

fields.name: picker_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the player who picked the item up

specs.semantics: The client scans the ground-item list (scene+0x1C) for the first record whose rec+0x12 == ground_id; if none, nothing happens. On a match it sets rec+0x16 = 2 (picked: flies toward the picker entity and is freed after 1000 ms), rec+0x28 = 0, and rec+0x1C = picker_uid. If picker_uid == local uid (scene+0x220) it adds the item by category rec+0x18. Category 0: FUN_00423b70 into the bag at +0x63E/+0x698/+0x6F4, capacity +0x3AA, with quantity. Category 1 (equipment): first empty slot in u16[+0x3C8] (capacity +0x3A9, must be <= 45); writes item_id and copies the 6 extension words to +0x422+slot*0xC. Category 2: FUN_00423e70 into +0x7A8, capacity +0x3AB, with quantity. On success it refreshes UI panes 7/8/9/0x28 and shows the center notice "you've received %s. (Count:%u)".
specs.trigger: Server reply to C2S 0x1F (u16 ground_id) once the pickup is validated; broadcast to everyone on the map so the item disappears for all.
specs.gates_and_hazards: If the local bag add fails (full, or equipment capacity > 45), no message is shown but the ground record is still marked picked and disappears, so the item is lost client-side. The server must check bag space before sending. Nothing happens for an unknown ground_id. Only the first record with a duplicate ground_id is affected, so keep ids unique per map.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x13.py sends u16, u16, u32 (same widths). KR Hex-Rays case 0x13 has a leading u8 result, so it is newer and differs. Our server's _build_opcode_13 (windslayer_server.py:1675) has the correct widths and order, but names the 2nd field 'item' when it is quantity. It is never called, and C2S 0x1F is not in _dispatch.
open_questions: Bag-slot synchronisation with any server-side inventory model is not covered by this packet (no slot index is sent; the client picks the first free slot).
blind_open_questions: Exact per-category inventory semantics of FUN_00423b70 / FUN_00423e70 (which bag tab each category is) were not traced.

specs.name: SetBaseStat
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 stat_index
u16 value

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: uid (entity+0x84) of the entity whose allocated base stat is set
fields.dest_or_source: stack [ESP+0xD4] (IAT 0x4A40C8); entity lookup key, compared to party frame +0x134 and scene+0x220

fields.name: stat_index
fields.meaning: 0=Strength (+0xE6), 1=Dexterity (+0xE8), 2=Intelligence (+0xEA, drives max MP), 3=Spirit (+0xEC, drives max HP). Values > 3 write nothing, but the derived-stat recalc and stat-window refresh still run

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: new ABSOLUTE allocated base-stat value (assignment, not a delta)

specs.semantics:
All three fields are always read first. entity = FUN_004189f0(scene, uid); if it is null, stop (break at 0x4547EF). Switch on stat_index (jump table 0x4585E4, verified: 0->0x45480A, 1->0x45481B, 2->0x45482C, 3->0x4548F0; >3 -> 0x45492D):
- Case 0: word +0xE6 = value.
- Case 1: word +0xE8 = value.
- Case 2: word +0xEA = value. If level +0x99 != 0, FUN_00427f40(0) recomputes max MP (+0x1110) and clamps cur MP (+0xA0) down to it. Then the party frames UI 0x75..0x78 are scanned; on the frame whose +0x134 == uid, if max MP != 0, text 2 = '%u/%u' (+0xA0, +0x1110) and bar 2 = ratio.
- Case 3: word +0xEC = value. FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recomputes max HP (+0x110C) and clamps cur HP (+0x9C) only if it exceeds the new max. If the low word of max HP != 0, FUN_0043d3f0(uid, (u16)max_hp, (u16)cur_hp) updates the party HP display.
All paths that found the entity then run FUN_0041ace0(scene, entity), which recomputes derived stats including the equipment bonuses +0xF0..+0xFC. If uid == scene+0x220 (the local player), FUN_00442510 redraws the stat window: 'Lv.%u', each stat as '%u' or '%u+%u' (base + bonus), and remaining stat points = total(level) - (E6+E8+EA+EC), where FUN_00440e10 total(L) = 9 + 4*min(L-1,28) + 5*max(0,L-29), or 0 if L > 99.
specs.trigger: Server reply to the client's stat-point allocation (C2S 0x04 in our server), or any server-side base-stat resync.
specs.gates_and_hazards: The entity must exist, otherwise the packet is consumed (7 bytes) and ignored. The value is absolute: our server's hard-coded value 4 overwrites the real stat. Remaining points are derived client-side from level minus the sum of the four stats, so wrong values also corrupt the displayed free points. The packet never writes cur HP/MP directly; it only clamps them down after the max recalculation, so using 0x14 as a 'monster HP' packet is wrong. Case 2 skips the MP recalc when level == 0. Case 3's party HP update tests only the low 16 bits of max HP.

locations.role: FUN_004189f0 entity lookup; null -> JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4547EF (after all reads)
case 2: word +0xEA = value (Intelligence); FUN_00427f40(0) at 0x454845; party MP bar
case 3: word +0xEC = value (Spirit); FUN_00427d40(scene,entity,0) at 0x454906; FUN_0043d3f0 at 0x454928
FUN_00442510 local stat window refresh if uid == scene+0x220

specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analysts A and B agree on the read sequence: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 at 0x45479F, [ESP+0xE0]-12 = [ESP+0xD4]), u8 stat_index (IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x4547BA, [ESP+0x88]-12 = [ESP+0x7C]), u16 value (IAT 0x4A4090 at 0x4547D2, [ESP+0x70]-12 = [ESP+0x64]). A appended `if(entity_by_uid(uid) == null) { stop }`. The asm shows the entity lookup (CALL 0x4189F0 at 0x4547E6) and its null break (JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4547EF) come after all three reads, and no later path reads the packet. The condition gates side effects only, so B's grammar `u32 uid / u8 stat_index / u16 value` is the correct canonical form, and A's trailing stop is redundant (wire-equivalent, but a mis-modelled structural branch). The switch targets were confirmed from the raw jump table 0x4585E4 (0x45480A, 0x45481B, 0x45482C, 0x4548F0). Both analysts are right that values > 3 write nothing but still reach FUN_0041ace0/FUN_00442510 via JA 0x45492D. B's remaining-points claim is confirmed by the FUN_00442510 decomp (FUN_00440e10() - EC - EA - E8 - E6). The stat names come from strings 0x6F3C58 Strength, 0x6F3C4C Dexterity, 0x6F3C3C Intelligence, 0x6F3C34 Spirit, referenced via table 0x701760..0x70176C. Cross-refs: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x14.py = p32u uid, p8u type, p16u value (matches EN). The KR Hex-Rays case 0x14 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 4222) reads a u32 plus four u16 deltas: a different build, not applicable to EN. windslayer_server.py _handle_set_stats (line 957) uses the correct layout but uid = account_id and a hard-coded value 4. The comments at lines 88 and 1817 calling 0x14 an HP/monster-HP packet contradict the binary.
open_questions: FUN_0043d3f0(uid, max_hp, cur_hp) is assumed to be a party/target HP display update; its UI target was not traced.
