specs.name: SystemMessage

locations.role: handler block; zeroes an 89-byte text buffer at esp+0x528
FUN_00445f00(this, text, color): append to chat log (wraps at 88 chars)
FUN_004737f0(this+0x4E4, text, color, msg_type) if this+0x4E4 != 0

specs.grammar:
u8 msg_type
u8 text_len
str[text_len] text

fields.name: msg_type
fields.meaning: 0 = color 0xFF00E4FF (light blue); 1 = 0xFFE4FF00 (yellow-green); 2 = notice: red 0xFFFF0000 if the text starts with "[Warni" (strncmp 6 against "[Warning]"), 0xFF00E4FF if it starts with "[Annou" ("[Announce]"), else green 0xFF00FF00; >= 3 = color taken from uninitialized stack esp+0x1cc (garbage)

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: number of text bytes that follow

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: message text (no NUL needed on the wire)

specs.semantics: Shows a colored system line in the chat log, with no sender prefix. If the secondary message list at this+0x4E4 exists, the line is also added there for msg_type 0..2 (FUN_004737f0 ignores type >= 3).
specs.trigger: Server/GM system notices, warnings and announcements.
specs.gates_and_hazards: STACK OVERFLOW: text is read into an 89-byte buffer; text_len > 89 overflows, and 89 leaves no NUL terminator. Keep text_len <= 88. msg_type >= 3 gives an uninitialized color (text may be invisible or random) and is not added to the secondary list. Use 0, 1 or 2.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x15 has types 0..6 with extra u8/string/u32 fields (guild match messages), so it is newer and does not apply to EN. PySlayer has only the C2S parse_0x15 (unrelated). Our server never sends S2C 0x15; its opcode 0x15 handling is the C2S UseItemOrSkill.
open_questions: Purpose of the secondary list object at this+0x4E4 (only filled when non-null).
blind_open_questions: What does window [this+0x4E4] display (lists +0x44 vs +0x54: a general vs notice tab)?

specs.name: ChatMessage

locations.role: if text[0]=='/': emote alias rewrite using table 0x70C6E0 (30 entries x 72 B: canonical + 5 aliases of 12 B)
FUN_004830f0(ui 0x294) emote list; match i -> emote_id = i + 0x118
FUN_00418a20(scene, name): find REMOTE entity (alive state 3) by name
speech bubble: copy 61 bytes of text to entity+0x1D, entity+0x8C = this+0x364

specs.grammar:
str[17] sender_name
u8 text_len
str[text_len] text

fields.name: sender_name
fields.meaning: speaker character name, NUL-padded (max 16 chars + NUL); used in the '%s : %s' line and to find the speaker entity by name

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: number of text bytes

fields.name: text
fields.dest_or_source: stack buffer esp+0x2c8 (61 bytes, pre-zeroed); later copied to entity+0x1D
fields.meaning: chat text

specs.semantics: Ordinary (say/map) chat. If text starts with '/', known emote aliases are rewritten to their canonical form (for example /love, /l -> /heart; /:) -> /pleased). If the result matches an entry of the emote UI list 0x294 (1-based index i), it is an emote: no chat-log line, and ANY scene player entity with that name - the LOCAL player included (live C34, chat_mail_gm#01: an echoed emote plays on the sender's own character) - gets entity+0x94 = 0x118+i with the timestamp in +0x90. Otherwise the client appends "name : text" (white) to the chat log, and a remote player entity (alive state 3) with that exact name gets a speech bubble (text copied to entity+0x1D, time to +0x8C).
specs.trigger: Server broadcast in response to C2S 0x03 chat (u8 len + text) from any player on the map.
specs.gates_and_hazards: STACK OVERFLOW: text goes into a 61-byte buffer; text_len > 61 overflows and 61 leaves no NUL. Keep text_len <= 60. sprintf_s into 0x58 bytes: a 16-char name + ' : ' + 60-char text = 79 fits, but a 17-byte name with no NUL runs into the following stack bytes and could exceed the buffer (sprintf_s invalid-parameter crash). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C34, chat_mail_gm#00/#01): bubbles and emotes attach to ANY scene player entity carrying that name, including the local player, so echoing a line back to its sender plays the emote (and presumably the bubble) on the sender's own character. Wire text_len EXCLUDES the terminating NUL - the client NUL-terminates by itself, and a raw text_len = 5 payload with no NUL printed correctly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C41, chat_mail_gm#00, party#06): a length-prefixed text field carries EXACTLY the prefixed number of bytes and NO trailing NUL - the client terminates the string itself. (The wsproto codec forced a NUL into the last byte of str[<length field>], which is only correct for a fixed str[N]; every length-prefixed text in the campaign had to be sent with len+1 or as raw hex to work around it. The grammar here is correct as written.)
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x16.py = pstr(name,17) + u8 len + text: exact match. KR Hex-Rays case 0x16 (u32 + strings) is newer and differs. OUR SERVER IS WRONG: _send_chat_line (windslayer_server.py:1486) and _handle_chat (:897) prepend an extra u8 count=1. The client then reads name = 0x01 + first 16 name bytes and text_len = name padding byte 0x00, so every server chat line shows as '\x01Name : ' with empty text. The code comment claiming 0x451AF0 reads a leading count is disproved by the asm (first read is the 17-byte char buffer at 0x451B0D). Fix: drop the leading count byte.
open_questions: The C2S 0x03 send path (FUN_00444a90, 'case 3') shows no local FUN_00445f00 call in the decompile, which suggests the server must echo 0x16 back to the sender for them to see their own line. Not fully traced.
The emote list UI 0x294 contents and the renderer for entity+0x94 emote ids were not traced.
blind_open_questions: What does UI list element 0x294 contain (presumably the emote names)? It decides which '/' commands become emotes (emote_id = index + 0x118).
Does the speaker's own balloon come from a local code path (this packet ignores state-4 entities)?

spec_errata.old: "the named remote player" (alive state 3 only)
spec_errata.new: any scene player entity with that name, local player included

spec_errata.old: bubbles/emotes only attach to remote (state 3) entities
spec_errata.new: they attach to any entity with that name, local included

spec_errata.old: no statement on NUL handling for str[text_len]
spec_errata.new: length-prefixed text carries no NUL (codec bug noted)

specs.name: SuppressDisconnectNotice

locations.role: handler block (whole body: one MOV then break)
reader of game_state+0x1528: socket-close callback shows 'Connection to Server got disconnected' + 5s close timer only if flag==0
reader: Fireway error 0x83 callback shows 'Transferring to server failed.' only if flag==0
reader: opcode 0x5D reason dialog skipped if flag!=0

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: Reads nothing. Sets game_state(0x70EA00)+0x1528 = 1 (absolute 0x70FF28). That flag means 'disconnect already handled'. While it is set, the client shows no disconnect dialog and does not start the 5-second WM_CLOSE timer: not on socket close (FUN_00478880), not on Fireway error 0x83 (FUN_004788e0) and not on a later 0x5D. In short: 'the server is about to drop you on purpose, don't show an error or close the game'. Every write to +0x1528 in the corpus sets it to 1. Nothing clears it, so the suppression lasts for the rest of the process.
specs.trigger: Send just before the server closes the game socket on purpose (e.g. a server/channel transfer or logout) so the client doesn't show 'Connection to Server got disconnected' and close itself 5 s later.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No preconditions. Hazard: the flag is never reset, so after one 0x17 the client silently ignores every later disconnect, including 0x5D kicks and real network drops. It will not show a dialog or close itself. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, quest_cards_misc#18): live-verified - after an empty 0x17 the following S2C 0x5D produced NO dialog and the client did NOT exit (still in world 10 s later, normal HUD). RECOVERY: nothing clears the latch except a full client restart, so a session that has received 0x17 can never be told about a disconnect again.
specs.references: Matches the KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x17: *(v3+13360)=1, same 'no payload, set flag' behaviour at the KR struct offset). Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py.
open_questions: Game_state initialisation wasn't checked to confirm +0x1528 starts at 0 (it's a static global, so it probably does). Whether a reconnect path clears it indirectly (e.g. a memset of game_state) wasn't traced.
The exact situations where the original server sent 0x17 are unknown. Logout and server transfer are guesses from what the flag does.
blind_open_questions: I did not find anything in this corpus that clears game_state+0x1528 (for example on reconnect or server select). If nothing clears it, the latch lasts for the whole process.

spec_errata.old: latch behaviour from static reading
spec_errata.new: live-confirmed; only a restart clears it

specs.name: GetItem (gold/Victy update + grant item)
specs.grammar:
u64 gold
u32 victy
u16 item_id
u16 count

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Inventory gold, total (not a change amount)
fields.dest_or_source: player_info+0x228; label window 9 child 0xB via FUN_004659d0 @0x46DE70

fields.name: victy
fields.meaning: 'Victy' currency total (checked by 'You are short of Victy.' in FUN_00467680). PySlayer and our server call it Winnie.
fields.dest_or_source: player_info+0x238; label window 9 child 0x27 via FUN_00465a30 @0x46DE9C (%u)

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item to grant (1-based catalog id); 0 = no item, currency update only

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number granted (type 0: u16 stacks up to 999; type 2: u8 stacks up to 99; type 1 equipment always adds exactly one slot)

locations.role: look up the item definition; switch on def+0x154: 0 FUN_00423b70 add, 1 FUN_00423ff0 add (options NULL -> zeros, capacity <= 45), 2 FUN_00423e70 add, 3 FUN_00426b80 learn skill, 4 FUN_004249e0 + FUN_00440bc0 class change

specs.semantics: Stores gold at player_info+0x228 and refreshes the inventory gold label. Stores Victy at player_info+0x238 and refreshes the Victy label (window 9 child 0x27). Then FUN_00440920 grants item_id x count. It looks up the definition in [scene+0xF84] (item_id 0 or out of range: nothing happens) and switches on its type: 0 adds to the u16-stack tab (player_info+0x5F6 ids / +0x650 counts, capacity +0x362); 1 puts one equipment slot at player_info+0x380 with a zero option block at +0x3DA (capacity +0x361, must be <= 45); 2 adds to the u8-stack tab +0x760/+0x7BA (capacity +0x363); 3 learns a skill (needs [scene+0x970]) and shows 'You've learned skill(%s).'; 4 checks and applies a class change ('... is your new class.'). If a type 0-2 add succeeds, shows 'you've received <name>. (Count:<count>)' and refreshes the inventory UI. Returns 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.
specs.trigger: Shop buy result (reply to C2S 0x0B), quest reward, monster drop pickup, and any gold/Victy change (item_id=0). Seen live: after C2S 0x16 quest accept the server sent 0x18 (16 B) and the client accepted it.
specs.gates_and_hazards: gold and Victy are absolute values and overwrite whatever the client had. No crash risks (fixed size). The add silently fails (no message) when the bag is full, count=0, the capacity byte > 45, or item_id is unknown. The currency updates still apply. Equipment ignores count (adds 1) but the message still prints count. Type 3 needs the skill structure at [scene+0x970].
specs.references: Matches PySlayer opcode_0x18 (p64u gold, p32u Winnie, p16u item, p16 count) and our server's _build_opcode_18 (16 B). The EN client names the u32 currency 'Victy'. [ctx+0x18] (player_info) = [ctx+0x10] (scene) + 0x48: FUN_00440920 reaches the same fields through [this+0x4CC]+0x3C8/+0x3A9/+0x63E/+0x7A8, and SubHandler1 through [ctx+0x18]+0x380/+0x361/+0x5F6/+0x760.
open_questions: What item types 0 and 2 are called in the UI (type 1 is equipment).
blind_open_questions: Category 4 (def+0x154 == 4) path via FUN_004249e0/FUN_00440bc0 was not traced; its meaning (avatar/cash item?) is unknown.
The absolute address of chardata (ctx+0x18) was not pinned. Offset correlation with FUN_00440920 suggests chardata = scene(*0x70EECC)+0x48, but this is unverified.

specs.name: SellItemResult
specs.grammar:
u64 gold
u16 item_id
u16 count
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }
u16 opt_extra

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Inventory gold after the sale; its label is refreshed right away
fields.dest_or_source: player_info+0x228; label window 9 child 0xB via FUN_004659d0 @0x46DC20

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item id that was sold, 1-based index into the item catalog [[ctx+0x10]+0xF84]

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number sold. Removed from type-0/type-2 stacks; ignored for equipment (type 1 always removes 1). Printed in 'Sold %u (%s).'
fields.dest_or_source: local [frame+0x14] (low word) -> FUN_00467140 arg3 (read as a word)

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: How many option words follow (0..5)

fields.name: opt
fields.meaning: Option words 0..opt_count-1 of the item's 12-byte option block. The array starts zeroed, so words not sent stay 0.

fields.name: opt_extra
fields.meaning: Word 5 of the 12-byte option block (always read after the loop)

locations.role: FUN_00404210: item definition from catalog by item_id (EAX=id, ESI=[[ctx+0x10]+0xF84])
FUN_00467140(type=def+0x154, item_id, &opts, count): remove from inventory

remove dispatcher: type0 -> FUN_00423b70(ECX=-count) on +0x5F6/+0x650/+0x6AC cap +0x362; type1 -> FUN_00423ff0(EAX=-1, opts compared) on +0x380/+0x3DA cap +0x361; type2 -> FUN_00423e70(EAX=-count) on +0x760/+0x7BA cap +0x363; type>=3 -> returns 0

specs.semantics: 1) Store gold at player_info+0x228 and refresh the inventory gold label. This happens even if the rest fails. 2) Read item_id and count, zero a local 12-byte option block (6 u16 words), read opt_count, then opt_count u16s into words 0.., then one u16 into word 5. 3) Look up the item definition by item_id; if none (item_id 0 or past the end of the catalog), stop quietly (returns 1). 4) Remove the item according to its type (def+0x154): type 0 subtracts count from u16 stacks (the whole thing fails if total owned < count); type 1 (equipment) removes the first slot whose id matches AND whose 12 stored option bytes equal the packet's block exactly, then shifts later slots down; type 2 subtracts count from u8 stacks; any other type fails. 5) Only if removal worked: show system chat 'Sold <count> (<item name>).' and refresh the inventory UI. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.
specs.trigger: The server's reply to a shop sell request (C2S 0x0C in our server). The gold field lets the server credit the sale price.
specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH HAZARD: the opts array is 6 words on the stack and opt_count is never checked. opt_count >= 6 writes past word 4 (word 5 is later overwritten by opt_extra) into other locals; opt_count >= 63 reaches the /GS cookie at [frame+0xB0], and the client terminates when the handler returns. Keep opt_count <= 5. Equipment matching: an item added with 0x18 has an all-zero option block, so it can only be removed with opt_count=0 and opt_extra=0 (or with the exact nonzero words the client stored). Equipment removal also fails if the tab capacity byte player_info+0x361 > 45; types 0/2 fail if their capacity byte (+0x362/+0x363) > 45. count=0 on a type 0/2 item removes nothing and shows no message. The chat line needs the chat window ([ui+0x59C]) to exist.
specs.references: Matches PySlayer opcode_0x19 (u64 gold, u16 idx, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16, u16) and our server's _build_opcode_19 (15 B, opt_count=0). Memory note 'combat model: 0x19=SELL' agrees. Our server's comments call the loop list 'extra'; it is really option words 0..4 of the item option block, and the trailing u16 is word 5 (the C2S 0x3C encoder in FUN_00469090 builds the same block: u8 n (non-zero words among the first 5), n*u16, then u16 word 5; non-equipment sends u8 0 + u16 0).
open_questions: What option words 0..4 and word 5 mean (sockets/refine/durability?).
Tab names for item types 0 and 2 (u16 stacks up to 999 with a per-slot u32, vs u8 stacks up to 99). Type 1 is equipment, type 3 skill book, type 4 class-change item.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of the individual option words and the +0x0A tail (e.g. refine or durability) inside the 12-byte equipment option blob was not traced to the packet that populates equipment slots.
Whether FUN_00423b70 (consumable remove with negative count) also refuses when the total quantity is short was not fully traced (it is verified for etc items in FUN_00423e70).

specs.name: NpcMonsterSpawn

locations.role: per-entity loop head: new 0x15F0 entity, ctor FUN_00444390, then memset 0 (the memset wipes the CPList vftables the ctor just set)
RosterLookupByIndex(template_index, game_state+0x4E0) -> copies template name/stats, sets +0x11DC
per effect: FUN_00424e20 adds a status effect into entity+0xE84 slots
RegisterLocalPlayer(entity, scene): applies defaults, adds the entity to the scene list, makes it the local player if uid==scene+0x220
FUN_004097b0 + FUN_004095d0: (re)opens the template sprite file (record+0x52) into record+0x678
FUN_00422af0: seeds the per-entity RNG table entity+0x960 (256 ints) from home_x+home_y+index+uid
client-side monster wander AI that uses wander_* / home_* fields when server_controlled==0

specs.grammar:
u8 count
repeat(count) {
  u32 template_index
  u32 uid
  u8 effect_count
  repeat(effect_count) {
    u16 effect_id
    i32 effect_duration_ms
  }
  u8 wander_motion
  u8 wander_rng_cursor
  u32 wander_mode
  u32 wander_timer_ms
  u32 home_x
  u32 home_y
  u32 respawn_tick
  u32 unk_954
  bool unk_8d9
  u8 unk_8cf
  i32 action_state
  u32 action_elapsed_ms
  u8 unk_8bd
  f64 pos_x
  f64 pos_y
  i32 elapsed_e50
  u8 facing
  u8 motion
  u8 motion_8b5
  u8 motion_8b6
  bool unk_8da
  bool unk_8df
  bool unk_8dc
  bool unk_8dd
  bool unk_8de
  u16 cur_hp
  u32 timer_d94
  bool server_controlled
  if(server_controlled != 0) {
    u32 cmd_hold_ms
  }
}
specs.length: 1 + sum over entities of (82 + 6*effect_count + (server_controlled?4:0)). One entity with 0 effects and no hold field = 83 bytes; with 1 effect = 89 bytes

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number of entity blocks. Nothing more is read if it's 0.

fields.name: template_index
fields.meaning: 1-based index into the NPC/monster template list at game_state+0x4E0, which is filled from the map's resources. Must be between 1 and list count (+0x18) or the template doesn't bind (no name, no stats, +0x11DC stays NULL).

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Entity uid. Must not equal the local player's uid (scene+0x220), or RegisterLocalPlayer makes this entity the local player.

fields.name: effect_count
fields.meaning: Number of status-effect entries that follow.

fields.name: effect_id
fields.meaning: Status/skill-effect id. FUN_00424e20 looks up the definition at scene+0xF84 table[id-1]; if it's missing the entry is ignored. Stored in a free slot of entity+0xE84 (21 slots, 0x18 bytes each).

fields.name: effect_duration_ms
fields.meaning: Remaining duration of the effect. Stored at slot+0x0C (entity+0xE90+i*0x18). Ids 0x9C3..0x9F9 are forced to 60000.

fields.name: wander_motion
fields.meaning: Next wander motion for the client-side monster AI (FUN_00417e10 writes 1/3/5/6 here and copies it into +0x8B4). Default 0.

fields.name: wander_rng_cursor
fields.meaning: Index into the per-entity random table +0x960, used by the wander AI. Default 0.

fields.name: wander_mode
fields.meaning: Wander mode/direction chosen by the AI (rand%7, switch in FUN_00417e10/FUN_004158d0). Default 0.

fields.name: wander_timer_ms
fields.meaning: Wander countdown (AI sets 3000..5999 and subtracts 30 per tick). 0 = pick a new wander action.

fields.name: home_x
fields.meaning: Spawn/home X, converted as unsigned to f64. The AI compares distance from home against it, and the respawn logic (FUN_00413920 state 0x16) warps the monster back here. Also part of the RNG seed.

fields.name: home_y
fields.meaning: Spawn/home Y, converted as unsigned to f64.

fields.name: respawn_tick
fields.meaning: While action_state==0x16 (dead), the monster respawns at home with full HP once entity+0xE5C - scene+0xF1C < 0 (FUN_00413920). RegisterLocalPlayer would set 0x7FFFFFFF when +0x15E8 is set, but this read overwrites it. Send 0 for a live mob.

fields.name: unk_954
fields.meaning: Action-related state next to +0x94C/+0x950 (RegisterLocalPlayer clears all three). Meaning unknown; our server sends 32 (copied from 0x07).

fields.name: unk_8d9
fields.meaning: Behaviour flag used by FUN_00413920/FUN_004158d0 (cleared on many state changes). Default 0.

fields.name: unk_8cf
fields.meaning: State byte; RegisterLocalPlayer's default is 8. Meaning unknown.

fields.name: action_state
fields.meaning: Current action/animation state: 8=idle (RegisterLocalPlayer default and respawn value), 4=attack, 0x16=dead waiting for respawn; 9 and 0x13 also appear. Send 8 for a normal idle mob.

fields.name: action_elapsed_ms
fields.meaning: Time spent in the current action state (+30 per tick in FUN_00413920). Default 0.

fields.name: unk_8bd
fields.meaning: State byte; RegisterLocalPlayer's default is 2. Meaning unknown.

fields.name: pos_x
fields.meaning: Current world X.

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: Current world Y.

fields.name: elapsed_e50
fields.meaning: Second elapsed-time counter (+30 per tick while +0x8DF==0). Default 0.

fields.name: facing
fields.meaning: Horizontal facing: 2 and 6 are opposite directions (confusion effects swap 2<->6), 8 = neutral/default. Same field as bits 0-1 of the 0x1B/0x0D state blob.

fields.name: motion
fields.meaning: Motion/stance code (0 idle; AI writes 1,3,4,5,6). Same field as bits 2-4 of the 0x1B blob.

fields.name: motion_8b5
fields.meaning: Motion sub-field (bits 5-8 of the 0x1B blob). Default 0.

fields.name: motion_8b6
fields.meaning: Motion sub-field (bits 9-11 of the 0x1B blob; value 3 and 4 are tested). Default 0.

fields.name: unk_8da
fields.meaning: Flag, default 0.

fields.name: unk_8df
fields.meaning: Flag, default 0; while it's 0, +0xE50 keeps counting.

fields.name: unk_8dc
fields.meaning: Flag, default 0.

fields.name: unk_8dd
fields.meaning: Flag, default 0.

fields.name: unk_8de
fields.meaning: Flag, default 0.

fields.name: cur_hp
fields.meaning: Current HP, zero-extended into the u32 at +0x9C. It overwrites the max-HP default RegisterLocalPlayer copies from +0x110C. 0 = corpse (live-verified: unhittable).

fields.name: timer_d94
fields.meaning: Counter that grows by 30 per tick up to 500 while motion==6 (FUN_00413920). Default 0.

fields.name: server_controlled
fields.meaning: Aggro / server-driven flag (PySlayer comment: 어그로 'aggro'). When nonzero the client wander AI is off (FUN_00417e10 needs it ==0) and the monster follows queued 0x1B commands. Also gates the next field.

fields.name: cmd_hold_ms
fields.meaning: Present only if server_controlled!=0. Initial command hold timer (the same field 0x1B's hold_ms feeds; -30 per tick).

specs.semantics:
Creates one NPC/monster entity per block. For each block the client:
(1) allocates a 0x15F0-byte entity, runs the ctor, then memsets it to 0.
(2) Reads template_index (+0xE60) and uid (+0x84), sets alive/type byte +0x98=4 (template NPC/monster) and clears name[17].
(3) Looks up the template list at game_state+0x4E0 by template_index. On a hit it copies the template name into entity+0 and sets +0x11DC=record (nameplate). It copies record+0x644 (type/class) to +0xE64, +0x660 to +0xE68, +0x63C to +0xE6C, +0x648 (max HP) to +0x110C, +0x650 to +0x119C, +0x658 to +0x1130, +0x654 to +0x1134, +0x680 to +0xDE8, +0x67C to +0xDEC and +0x65C to +0x1140. Float +0x664 goes to f64 +0x11E0. For type 4..7 it sets +0x1150=1..4 and puts record+0x66C in +0x1160/+0x1164/+0x1168/+0x116C. It also copies +0x668 to +0x1154, 10 dwords from +0x250 to +0xDC0, and level byte +0x640 to +0x99.
(4) Reads effect_count and applies each effect via FUN_00424e20.
(5) Calls RegisterLocalPlayer. For type 4 that stamps timeGetTime into +0xE54, applies defaults (0x8B3=8, 0x8BD=2, 0x8CF=8, 0x904=8, HP=max) and adds the entity to the scene list. If uid==scene+0x220 it also becomes scene+0x970 (local player).
(6) Reads the remaining fields, which overwrite those defaults.
(7) Reopens the template sprite file.
(8) Seeds the per-entity RNG table.
The handler never looks for an existing entity with the same uid.
specs.trigger: When a monster/NPC enters the player's view: on map entry for every mob in the map, and on monster respawn.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
template_index must resolve (1..count of game_state+0x4E0 list). If it doesn't, +0x11DC stays NULL. Memory notes report a NULL-deref crash at 0x43C4C2 (nameplate strlen) for alive==4 entities without +0x11DC, and at minimum the body/name won't render.
uid must NOT equal scene+0x220 (the local player uid, 1 on our server), or the monster is registered as the local player.
There is no uid dedup: resending 0x1A for an existing uid seems to add a second entity with the same uid (FUN_004189f0 lookups return the first match). That fits the observed 'snap back to spawn' jitter, and it leaks entities.
Every 0x1A also calls CSpriteControl::OpenFromFile again for the template (record+0x678 is overwritten), which may cost time or memory when spawning in bulk.
The memset after the ctor zeroes the CPList vftables at +0x1350/+0x1360/+0x1370/+0x1588 (client bug; the lists still work because FUN_00459df0 doesn't use the vftable).
cur_hp=0 gives a corpse.
effect entries whose id has no definition are silently dropped.
specs.references:
The field order and widths match windslayer_server.py _build_opcode_1A (line 1494) byte for byte, so the layout is correct. Disagreements about values:
(a) The server sends +0x8B3..+0x8B6 as 127,0,0,1 ('ip'). These are facing/motion bytes; 127 isn't a valid facing, so 8 (or 2/6),0,0,0 is recommended.
(b) The server sends action_state(+0x904)=0; the client's idle is 8.
(c) unk_8cf=1, unk_954=32 and action_elapsed(+0xE00)=501 were copied from 0x07. The client's own defaults are 8, 0 and 0.
(d) The server's 'inner loop = action 0xB3B idle' is really a status-effect entry (FUN_00424e20, skill table scene+0xF84). The live finding that count=0 leaves the body invisible is recorded but not explained statically.
Matches memory project_local_player_spawn.md's 88-byte layout (83 bytes + opcode = 84 with no hold field; 88 includes the optional u32), but that note calls 0x1A the LOCAL player spawn. In fact 0x1A is a generic template (monster/NPC) spawn that becomes local only when uid==scene+0x220, which agrees with reference_combat_render.md.
PySlayer opcode_0x1A.py targets the newer KR layout (different order: second loop, f64 pos early, 6 base-pos u32s, 7 bools) and must NOT be used for EN. The KR Hex-Rays case 0x1A has the same field families.
open_questions: The meanings of unk_954, unk_8cf, unk_8bd, unk_8d9, unk_8da/8dc/8dd/8de and timer_d94 are only partly known (defaults are from RegisterLocalPlayer).
Whether a duplicate uid from a resent 0x1A really leaves two entities (no dedup in the handler or RegisterLocalPlayer was seen, but a dedup elsewhere in the per-frame code wasn't ruled out).
Why effect_count=0 made the body invisible in the live test (the memory note says an effect 0xB3B is needed). Statically the effect list is a status-effect array; the render dependency wasn't traced.

The client-side wander AI (FUN_00417e10) needs type(+0xE64)>2, server_controlled==0, an empty 0x1B queue and +0xE48==0. Why mobs were observed static in-client wasn't resolved (possibly scene+0xF88+0x70 or the caller FUN_0042b260's gates).
blind_open_questions: Meaning of unk_e5c, unk_954, unk_8d9, unk_8cf, motion_e00, unk_8bd, unk_e50, the 5 bools and unk_d94. The widths and order are certain; the names are heuristic.
effect_time: probably remaining duration in ms (60000 is forced for ids 0x9C3..0x9F9), not confirmed.
Whether the Fireway bool reader normalizes non-zero bytes to 1 (send 0/1 to be safe).
RegisterLocalPlayer was only partly read. I did not confirm whether it removes or replaces an existing entity with the same uid; the handler block itself has no such check.

specs.name: EntityActionCommand

locations.role: FUN_004189f0(uid, scene): find entity in scene list; break if not found
GetDataFromPacket(char*,8) into scene+0xEF8 state blob, then bit-decoded into cmd
FUN_00459df0: append the 0x58-byte cmd to the entity+0x1350 command queue
per-tick consumer: pops cmd when entity+0xE48 hits 0 and applies it to entity fields
C2S 0x0D builder that packs the same 8-byte blob from the local player (confirms bit layout)

specs.length: 16 base (uid 4 + hold 4 + blob 8); +4 if action!=0; +16 more if action in {7,9} and sub_b==4; +16 if move_flag!=0. Max 52. Only 4 bytes are consumed if the uid is unknown.

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Target entity uid (remote player or monster). If no entity in the scene+0xC list has it, the handler stops reading.

fields.name: hold_ms
fields.meaning: Command timing. Monsters (+0x98==4): when dequeued it goes into entity+0xE48 and counts down 30 per tick before the next queued command is popped, so it's how long this action lasts. Remote players (+0x98==3): it's a delay before the command applies (0 means 30 ms).

fields.name: state_blob
fields.meaning:
Packed state, read as u32 b0 (bytes 0-3) and u32 b1 (bytes 4-7), little-endian.
b0 bits 0-1 facing: 1->2, 2->6, 0/3->8 (cmd+0x4A -> entity+0x8B3).
b0 bits 2-4 motion (cmd+0x4B -> +0x8B4).
b0 bits 5-8 motion_8b5 (cmd+0x4C -> +0x8B5, players only).
b0 bits 9-11 sub_b (cmd+0x4D -> +0x8B6, players only).
b0 bits 12-15 action (cmd+0x4F -> +0x94C).
b0 bits 16-19 move_flag (cmd+0x4E -> +0x950/+0x8EA, players only).
b0 bits 20-21 facing2: 1->2, 2->6, else 8 (cmd+0x50 -> +0x8D0).
b1 bits 0-11 param12 (cmd+0x44 -> +0x958; the client writes values like 50/250/600).
Other bits are ignored. The 8 raw bytes are copied into scene+0xEF8, which is also the local player's C2S 0x0D scratch buffer.

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: Present only if action!=0. Uid of the action target.

fields.name: target_x
fields.meaning: Present only if action!=0 and sub_b==4 and action is 7 or 9. Target point X (e.g. a ground-targeted skill).

fields.name: target_y
fields.meaning: Target point Y (same condition as target_x).

fields.name: pos_x
fields.meaning: Present only if move_flag!=0. Position X the entity snaps to when the command is applied (non-monster entities only).

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: Position Y (same condition).

specs.semantics:
Queues a movement/action command on an existing entity. The client allocates a zeroed 0x58-byte command, sets entity+0x8D7=1, reads hold_ms and the 8-byte state blob, bit-decodes the blob into the command, and reads the optional target and position fields. It forces cmd+0x04=0 and appends the command to the entity's FIFO at +0x1350 (FUN_00459df0).
FUN_00412100 consumes the queue once per tick for entities with +0x98>2 and uid != local uid (and only while scene+0xF88+0x70==0). When +0xE48 reaches 0 it pops the head.
Monsters (type 4): +0xE48 = hold_ms.
Other entities: if move_flag is set, pos goes to +0x11F8/+0x1288 and cmd+0x40 to +0xDAC.
Then for everyone: +0x8B4 = motion, +0x8B3 = facing.
Players only (type 3): +0x8B5, +0x8B6, +0x8EA/+0x950 = move_flag, +0xD78 = 0, +0x1328/+0x1330 = 0, +0x1338/+0x1340 = target point, +0x8DB, +0x8E8, +0x8D4 and +0x8E7 from unset cmd bytes (0).
Finally for everyone: +0x94C = action, +0xD80 = target_uid, +0x958 = param12, +0x8FF = 0, +0x8D0 = facing2.
This is the server-side echo of another client's C2S 0x0D movement packet (FUN_0042c940 packs the same blob from the same entity fields), and it's also the way to drive monster actions from the server.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#23/#24): a type-3 remote entity advances physics ONLY while entity+0xE48 > 0, i.e. while a node is pending. A single walk node with nothing queued behind it sets +0x8B3 2 but does not move the entity; each new node moves it for ~210 ms using the PREVIOUS node's facing. A relay must therefore STREAM 0x1B continuously - one node per received C2S 0x0D with hold_ms = that packet's logic_elapsed_ms. Measured stop-node latency behind a pending walk: 1.08 s. For an immediate stop use 0x2A.
specs.trigger: The server relays another player's C2S 0x0D movement/action to nearby clients (turning its state into uid + hold + blob + optional target/pos), and sends server-driven monster AI actions (move/attack) for mobs spawned with server_controlled=1.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Unknown uid: only the 4-byte uid is consumed and the rest is ignored (safe).
Commands sent for the LOCAL player's uid are queued but never consumed (FUN_00412100 skips uid==scene+0x220), so they leak memory.
Commands for monsters don't apply pos_x/pos_y directly (type-4 branch only sets +0xE48). Movement must come from motion/facing plus the client's physics, or the position is ignored.
The blob overwrites scene+0xEF8, which the local client reuses for its own 0x0D. The bits the client doesn't recompute (b0 bits 22-31, b1 bits 12-31) will echo back in the next C2S 0x0D.
If you queue many commands with large hold_ms, the backlog stays until the entity is removed.
The client needs entity+0xE48==0 before it pops a command. A monster spawned with server_controlled=1 and a big cmd_hold_ms delays its first command.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C29, world_movement_npc#24): monster motion codes (lo bits 2-4 -> +0x904): 0 -> action 7 then walk 12 (82.5 px/s); 1 -> 4 (melee attack loop); 3 -> jump 10/9/11; 5 -> 1 (attack loop); 6 -> 5 wind-up then 6 dash. With server_controlled = 1 the physics STOPS when the hold expires, EVEN MID-AIR, so a server-driven monster needs a follow-up command before its hold runs out.
specs.references:
C2S 0x0D (FUN_0042c940 @0x42CAAF..) uses the identical blob encoding: +0x8B3->bits0-1 (2->1, 6->2), +0x8B4<<2 (mask 0x1C), +0x8B5<<5 (0x1E0), +0x8B6<<9 (0xE00), +0x94C<<12 (0xF000), +0x950<<16 (0xF0000), +0x8D0->bits20-21, +0x958&0xFFF in the second dword. It likewise sends target uid if +0x94C!=0 and f64 x2 if +0x8B6==4 and action is 7/9. The C2S form carries extra fields (u32 time delta, u16, u32 tick delta, and when move_flag is set u32 +0xD78, f64 x4, bool...) that the S2C form drops.
The captured C2S 0x0D blob '00 02 40 53 00 60 64 75' decodes to facing 8, action 0, move_flag 0 plus garbage high bits, which is consistent.
KR Hex-Rays case 0x1B has the same structure (uid lookup, 0x58 alloc, u32, 8-byte blob, the same conditionals) but DIFFERENT bit widths (KR: 2-5, 6-10, 11-13, 14-17, 18-21, 22-23). Use the EN widths above.
Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py. The memory notes say monster movement is unsolved; this opcode is the likely candidate.
open_questions: Exact meaning of action codes (+0x94C values 5,6,7,9,0xA,0xD,0x10 seen) and motion/sub_b values. They need a trace of FUN_00413920/FUN_004158d0 state machines.

[RESOLVED by live verification world_movement_npc#24, 2026-09-17] Live: a monster under server_controlled = 1 does move from motion + facing plus client-side physics while its hold (+0xE48) is non-zero; walk code 0 gives 82.5 px/s. Physics stops the moment the hold expires, even in mid-air, so continuous commands are required. Original question: "How a monster actually moves under server control: FUN_00412100 doesn't apply pos for type 4. Does motion/facing plus per-frame physics move it, or is there another move opcode? Needs dynamic verification."
Whether hold_ms units are ms (30 subtracted per ~30ms tick is assumed).
The consumer's gate scene+0xF88+0x70==0 (a map/mode flag); when it is nonzero no queued commands are applied.
blind_open_questions: Real-world meaning of the bit groups: +0x8B3 direction codes 2/6/8 (value 4 cannot be carried), +0x8B4/+0x8B5/+0x8B6 action states, skill_kind values, sync_kind values and the 12-bit param +0x958.
Whether sending 0x1B for monster uids really animates and moves them in the EN client (static analysis says the input bits are applied to kind-4 entities; not live-tested).
What [scene+0xF88]+0x70 means (consumer and AI are disabled when it is non-zero).

spec_errata.old: no statement that a single node does not move a type-3 entity
spec_errata.new: type-3 entities simulate only while +0xE48 > 0; 0x1B must be streamed

spec_errata.old: action/motion code meanings were an open question
spec_errata.new: motion codes 0/1/3/5/6 mapped; physics stops on hold expiry

spec_errata.old: how a monster moves under server control
spec_errata.new: motion+facing plus physics while +0xE48 > 0

specs.name: CreateCharacterResult

locations.role: handler block entry; first calls FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) on g_ui_root (window 0x16 = message box, i.e. dismisses the 'Waiting for the server' popup)
result==1: new 0x15F0 entity (0x48B484 + 0x444390), memset, fill from creation-screen state, RegisterLocalPlayer/add-to-scene 0x422120 @0x4527FE, UI FUN_00483430(0x13,1,1) @0x452816
result==2: message box 'The name is already being used.'
result==3: shared message box 'Server process is running... (DB)'
C2S 0x0E CreateCharacter send site that this answers

specs.grammar: u8 result

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1=created OK (client builds the new char-select entity itself from its own creation-screen data), 2=name already in use, 3=server/DB busy, 4=invalid name; 0 or >=5 = nothing (popup just dismissed)

specs.semantics: Reply to the character-creation request. Unconditionally dismisses the message box (UI window 0x16) first. On result 1 NO further packet data is read: the client allocates a 0x15F0 entity and copies everything from its own creation screen (scene=*(0x70EECC)): name <- scene+0x206 (strcpy), appearance words entity+0x122<-scene+0x3AE, +0x128<-+0x3B4, +0x12A<-+0x3B6, +0x12C<-+0x3B8, +0x132<-+0x3BE, +0x134<-+0x3C0 (class), +0x13A<-+0x3C6, +0x136=0. n=scene+0x14 (current entity-list count = number of characters already shown): posX(+0x11F8)=(n+1)*110, posY(+0x1288)=300, uid(+0x84)=30000000+n, alive(+0x98)=3, +0x8D6=1, HP(+0x9C)=100, level(+0x99)=1; adds it to the scene via 0x422120, sets +0x8B4=4, then FUN_00483430(0x13,1,1) (leaves the creation window). Results 2/3/4 show the error dialogs quoted in locations.
specs.trigger: Send after C2S 0x0E CreateCharacter (u16 class@scene+0x3C0, u16@0x3AE, u16@0x3B8, u16@0x3B6, u16@0x3BE, str[17] name@0x206, u16 x4 stats@0x296..0x29C; send site 0x446FE4).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate: result 1 adds a char-select-style entity to whatever scene is current. If sent outside the char-select screen it would inject a bogus entity (uid 30000000+n, alive=3) into the world scene. No max-character check in EN (KR checks 12 slots), so over-creating just keeps placing entities further right. Only 1 byte is read; the KR build reads a 2nd u8 and has a result 5 ('nickname available'). Do not send the KR 2-byte form (the extra byte would be ignored here, but the length changes). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08): the n = scene+0x14 derivation is only safe on a freshly loaded character-select list. After an S2C 0x1F delete the surviving entities keep shifted uids/positions, so a 0x1C create can produce a uid or x that collides with an existing character.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc line 4916) reads u8 result + u8 flag and supports results 1..5; EN reads only result and supports 1..4, with the same meanings for 2/3/4. Our server (windslayer_server.py _handle_create_character ~line 2523) never sends 0x1C: it answers C2S 0x0E by re-sending the full 0x02 login/char-list, which also works. protocol.md's 0x0E layout matches the send site at 0x446FE4. PySlayer has no opcode_0x1C builder.
open_questions: What UI id 0x13 in FUN_00483430(0x13,1,1) is exactly (probably closes the creation window / returns to char select).
Which visual slots scene+0x3B4 and scene+0x3C6 are. They are not sent in C2S 0x0E, and 0x446300 sets them to 4 when class==1.
blind_open_questions: Whether 0x422120 or a later packet increments scene+0x14 (character count) after a successful create; if not, a server may need to resend the character list (0x02) to keep slots consistent.
Exact meaning of UI events 0x16 and 0x13 passed to FUN_00483430 (inferred: dismiss waiting popup / return to char select).

spec_errata.old: no statement about post-delete collisions
spec_errata.new: documented collision hazard after a delete

specs.name: EquipItem

locations.role: loop i<stone_count: GetDataFromPacket u16 -> block[i] = [S+0x224+2i] (no bounds check)
FUN_00404210 item catalog lookup (ESI=scene+0xF84, EAX=item_id); stop if null or itemdef+0x154 != 1
FUN_004189F0(scene, uid) entity lookup; stop if null
FUN_00426680: write item into equip grid entity+0x13C (slot from itemdef+0x1CC kind and +0x1F0), copy block into entity+0x16E; returns previous item id; old block to [S+0x230]
local-player gate: scene+0x220 == uid and bag slot count scene+0x3A9 <= 45
FUN_00423FF0(delta=-1): remove item_id with an identical 12-byte block from bag ids scene+0x3C8 / blocks scene+0x422; stop if not found
if old item != 0: FUN_00423FF0(delta=+1) puts old item and old block in the first empty bag slot (return ignored)
FUN_00465290 refresh inventory window 9; FUN_00441A10 refresh equipment window 7; FUN_0045D0C0/FUN_0045D170 on game_state+0x700 list
current quickslot page (game_state+0x10BC, 8 slots): replace matching item and block with the old item/block; then FUN_00443AC0 + FUN_004411A0 (save QuickSlot/QuickSlotStone to registry)

specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u16 item_id
u8 stone_count
repeat(stone_count) {
  u16 stone_id
}
u16 block_tail

fields.name: uid
fields.dest_or_source: stack [S+0x16C]; used for FUN_004189F0 lookup and compared to scene+0x220 (local player uid)
fields.meaning: Entity (player) whose equipment changes

fields.name: item_id
fields.dest_or_source: stack [S+0xAC]; written into the entity equip grid (+0x13C) by FUN_00426680
fields.meaning: Item catalog id being equipped (must exist in the catalog at scene+0xF84 with Type +0x154 == 1)

fields.name: stone_count
fields.meaning: Number of following u16 option/stone values; the client reads exactly this many

fields.name: stone_id
fields.dest_or_source: option block [S+0x224 + 2*i]; copied to entity+0x16E region
fields.meaning: Socketed stone/option ids (the registry saver names these QuickSlotStone, 5 per item). Only indices 0..4 survive: index 5 is overwritten by block_tail, and index >=6 writes past the 12-byte block.

fields.name: block_tail
fields.dest_or_source: option block +10 = [S+0x22E] (6th u16 of the block)
fields.meaning: Last u16 of the 12-byte item option block (meaning unknown; same trailer as S2C 0x19 and C2S 0x0F)

specs.semantics: Equip-change notice for any entity. The 12-byte item option block is u16[6] = 5 stones + tail, with the wire encoding u8 n, n*u16, u16 tail. The client looks up the item (must be Type 1 equipment) and the entity by uid, and aborts silently if either is missing. It writes item_id into the entity's equip grid at the slot derived from itemdef+0x1CC (kind) and +0x1F0 (alternate grid), stores the block, remembers the previously equipped item and its block, recomposes the sprite and recalculates stats. For remote players that is all. For the local player (uid == scene+0x220, bag slot count scene+0x3A9 <= 45): it removes the bag entry at scene+0x3C8/+0x422 that matches item_id AND the exact 12-byte block, and aborts if there is none. It then puts the previously equipped item (if any) with its block into the first empty bag slot, refreshes the inventory (window 9) and equipment (window 7) windows, and updates the game_state+0x700 lists for items with itemdef+0x1F0. On the current quickslot page, slots holding item_id with the same block are swapped to the old item and old block, and the quickslots are saved to HKCU\Software\Hamelin\WindSlayer\<name>. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C33, item_inventory#03/#05): 0x1D ITSELF removes one matching copy from the bag (this is the root cause of the "item equipped and still in the bag" reports when the option block does not match - and of double removal when the server also sends 0x23). The equip-tab removal COMPACTS the bag (later slots shift down) and the swapped-out item is appended to the first empty slot, i.e. the end of the list after compaction. EN Kind 11 (Wooden Stick, item 179) maps to equip grid index 5 = the Equipment window's Weapon & Shield slot 1.
specs.trigger: Send in response to C2S 0x0F EquipItem. The live capture 'B3 00 00 00 00' is u16 item 179 followed by the same block encoding (u8 0 stones, u16 tail 0), so echo the client's block. Also broadcast to other players so they see the change.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Gates: catalog entry must exist with +0x154==1; entity with uid must exist; the local bag/UI path needs uid==scene+0x220, scene+0x3A9<=45, and an existing bag entry with a byte-identical 12-byte block. If that match fails, the grid and sprite ARE already changed but the bag, windows and quickslots are not, so the item shows both equipped and still in the bag. If the bag is full the old item silently disappears client-side (the add result is ignored). There is no bound on stone_count: the wire stays aligned (exactly n u16 are consumed), but n==6 loses stone 6 to the tail and n>=7 writes past the block into stack [S+0x230..]. Those first 12 bytes get re-zeroed; n>=13 clobbers unrelated locals up to S+0x422, below the cookie at S+0x1304, so no crash is expected. Keep stone_count <= 5. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.
specs.references: Our server's _build_en_opcode_1D_equip (windslayer_server.py ~2171) sends u32 uid | u16 item | u8 0 | u16 0, which matches this grammar; it is sent from _handle_equip_item. That docstring says 0x1D 'does NOT touch the bag (+0xf84)', but +0xF84 is the item CATALOG. For the local player 0x1D DOES remove the item from the bag list at scene+0x3C8 when the block matches, which may double up with the follow-up 0x23. The unused _build_en_opcode_1D (~2143) is wrong for this handler: it sends class as item_id and N=14, which overflows the 12-byte block. The memory note in reference_combat_render.md ('keeps the item IN THE BAG') conflicts with this static reading unless the bag entry's block was non-zero or the local gate failed. KR Hex-Rays 0x1D (doc line 5035) parses a different item struct via sub_40A010, so it is not comparable byte-for-byte. The 5-stone naming comes from FUN_004411A0 'QuickSlotStone%d%d' (inner loop < 5).
open_questions: Meaning of block_tail (6th u16 of the option block): refine level, durability, or a flag?

Exact meaning of itemdef+0x1F0 (selects an alternate equip grid index in FUN_00426680 and skips the block copy there, e.g. costume/cash items) and of the game_state+0x700 lists updated by FUN_0045D0C0/FUN_0045D170.

[RESOLVED by live verification item_inventory#03, 2026-09-17] Live: 0x1D does remove the bag copy when item id AND the 12-byte option block match; the earlier "item stayed in the bag" report was a block mismatch. A server that sends 0x1D and then 0x23 removes TWO copies. Original question: "Why live testing reportedly left the item in the bag after 0x1D: bag block mismatch, or the scene+0x3A9 or uid gate?"
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of the 6 option words (enchant/attribute ids vs values) and whether servers ever sent N>0 with a trailing word, or N=5 + trailing.
Meaning of game_state+0x364 copied into quickslot aux array (+0x11c0) on replacement.
Whether FUN_00441a10 / FUN_0045d0c0 (for def+0x1f0 items, kinds 11/12) start timers or send anything (static callees show no Send/Add, but not fully traced).

spec_errata.new: live-proven not Kind; 0 for ordinary equipment

spec_errata.old: bag removal by 0x1D and the grid index mapping were open/uncertain
spec_errata.new: live-confirmed: 0x1D removes one bag copy, compacts the tab, Kind 11 -> grid index 5

specs.name: UnequipItemToBag
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u16 item_id
u8 option_count
repeat(option_count) { u16 option_value }
u16 option_extra

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: uid of the entity whose equipment changes. If it equals scene+0x220 (local player), the item is also put back into the local equipment bag tab
fields.dest_or_source: stack [base+0x160]; entity lookup; compared to scene+0x220 at 0x454243

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item id of the equipped item to remove (1-based item table scene+0xF84). The def must have def+0x154 == 1 (equipment category) or the whole packet is ignored

fields.name: option_count
fields.meaning: number of option/enchant u16 values that follow. The client's 12-byte item-option record holds 5 option slots (bytes 0..9) plus option_extra (bytes 10..11), so send <= 5. The record is zeroed first, so fewer than 5 leaves zeros. No bounds check: a 6th value lands on bytes 10..11 and is then overwritten by option_extra; values 7+ spill into unused stack locals (no crash, just discarded)

fields.name: option_value
fields.meaning: item option/enchant value i (PySlayer calls these 'enchant'); fills record bytes 2*i

fields.name: option_extra
fields.meaning: trailing u16 of the 12-byte item record (record bytes 10..11); meaning unknown (PySlayer 0x03 sends it unnamed)

specs.semantics: Removes an equipped item from an entity and, for the local player, returns it to the bag. Steps: (1) Look up item_id in the item table; it must exist with def+0x154 == 1, otherwise nothing happens. (2) If the entity is found: FUN_004269a0(entity+0x13C equip id grid [25 u16], entity+0x16E option records [25 x 12 bytes], item_id, &record) finds the slot whose id == item_id AND whose 12-byte record matches exactly (memcmp) and zeroes it. Then FUN_00426d50 rebuilds the body sprite, FUN_0041ace0 recalculates stats, FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recalculates max HP (clamping current HP), and if level != 0 FUN_00427f40(0) does the same for max MP. (3) If uid == scene+0x220 (checked even when the entity lookup failed): for opcode 0x1E, if bag capacity byte scene+0x3A9 <= 45, FUN_00423FF0 (mode EAX=1 'add') puts item_id plus the 12-byte record into the first empty slot of the equipment bag tab (u16 ids at scene+0x3C8, records at scene+0x422; the same arrays the 0x13 pickup path writes). If the item is a cash item (def+0x1F0 != 0), FUN_0045d170(game_state+0x700, item_id) updates the cash-item list. For both 0x1E and 0x24 it then refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290 on game_state+0xD5C) and the equipment window (FUN_00441a10).
specs.trigger: Server confirmation that an item was unequipped (moved from the equipment grid back into the inventory), sent to the owner and to observers so the sprite updates.
specs.gates_and_hazards: DUPLICATION HAZARD: the return value of the removal (FUN_004269a0) is ignored. If item_id or ANY of the 12 record bytes (5 options + option_extra) differ from what was stored at equip time, the equip slot is NOT cleared, but the local player still gets a copy added to the bag. The server must echo exactly the option values it used when equipping (e.g. 0x1D / 0x07). If the bag is full, FUN_00423ff0 silently adds nothing. Equipment-category gate def+0x154 == 1. The local-bag branch needs uid == scene+0x220. option_count > 5 corrupts the record (see field notes). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C10, item_inventory#04): a block mismatch produces a THREE-WAY desync, not just a bag duplicate: (1) the bag gains a duplicate carrying the WIRE block, (2) the equip grid and the Equipment window KEEP the item, and (3) the sprite recompose still drops the item's visual (the character is drawn with an empty hand). Echo exactly the 12 option bytes used at equip time. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C24, trade#07): catalog +0x1F0 == 0 for ORDINARY equipment - the client did send C2S 0x22 for the Wooden Stick (item 179), which the +0x1F0 == 0 gate requires. So +0x1F0 is NOT the gamedef "Kind" column (the comment in windslayer_server.py ~L2223, "Kind at +0x1F0", is wrong); it is the cash / no-trade flag that also greys items out during a trade and routes cash items through the premium lists.
specs.references: Wire layout matches the 0x1D handler at 0x45298C (u32, u16, u8 N, N*u16 into a zeroed 12-byte record, trailing u16) and PySlayer opcode_0x03's item record (u16 id, u8 5, 5*u16 enchant, u16). windslayer_server.py defines _build_en_opcode_1E (line ~2189) but NEVER calls it. Its docstring ('persistent in-place equip merge', u16 skinSelector/class, 14 apparences + weapon) is WRONG: the handler REMOVES the item via 0x4269a0, and sending 14 values would corrupt the record. The 0x1D docstring in the same file ('0x1E is the REMOVE/unequip opcode') is right. reference_combat_model.md's 'combat damage' reading and its '+0x3c8 float-number pool' claim are wrong: scene+0x3C8 is the equipment bag tab's item-id array (confirmed by the 0x13 pickup code FUN_00440e50 at 0x440F70/0x440F99). Newer KR build: case 0x1E/0x24 reads u32 + an item-record helper (sub_40A010).
open_questions: Meaning of option_extra (record bytes 10..11) and of the 5 option values (enchant / refine / socket?) not resolved from tooltip code.
Which C2S request (unequip double-click) the retail server answers with 0x1E was not traced here.
blind_open_questions: Precise meaning of option block word 5 (option_slot5) vs words 0..4 not determined (possibly a refine/socket field).
Exact purpose of the this+0x700 list touched by 0x45D170 (Kind != 0) not identified.

spec_errata.old: duplication hazard listed only the bag duplicate
spec_errata.new: three-way desync: bag duplicate + grid keeps item + sprite drops it

spec_errata.old: itemdef +0x1F0 meaning open (guessed Kind/cash)
spec_errata.new: live-proven not Kind; 0 for ordinary equipment

specs.name: DeleteCharacterResult

locations.role: handler entry; FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) dismisses message box
switch(result-1)<12 via byte table 0x4585D8=[0,1,2,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,4,3] + jump table 0x4585C4=[0x4528A5,0x44D90D,0x4528D6,0x44E372,break]
result==1: if game_state+0x3F8 (selected char entity) != 0 -> FUN_00422B90(scene, entity->uid); game_state+0x3F8=0
result==3: 'You can't delete a character created within 24 hours.'
result==12: 'Invalid password. Please check your password again.'
C2S 0x12 DeleteCharacter send site that this answers

specs.grammar: u8 result

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1=deleted, 2=server/DB busy, 3=created <24h ago (can't delete), 12=wrong password; 4..11, 0 and >12 = silent (popup just dismissed)

specs.semantics: Reply to the character-delete request. Always dismisses the message box (window 0x16) first. Result 1: takes the selected character entity pointer at game_state(0x70EA00)+0x3F8 and, if it is not null, calls FUN_00422B90(scene, entity->uid). That frees the entity from the scene list and, in char-select mode (scene+0xF00==5), shifts entities by x -= 110 and uid -= 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): FUN_00422B90 walks the scene list FROM ITS HEAD and shifts every entity that comes AFTER THE FIRST MATCH IN LIST ORDER. The character-select list is HEAD-INSERTED (the last-loaded character is first), so the characters that actually move are the ones with LOWER slot indices (drawn to the LEFT); higher slots keep their x and uid, a gap is left behind, and slot 0 can end up at x = 0 / uid 29999999. After a delete the client no longer satisfies uid = 30000000+index or x = 110*(index+1). It then clears the selection. Result 2 shows 'Server process is running. Please try again in a few minutes (DB)', result 3 the 24-hour message, and result 12 'Invalid password'.
specs.trigger: Send after C2S 0x12 DeleteCharacter. Send site 0x44AB49: u8 0x12, str[17] name of the selected entity (game_state+0x3F8), str[21] password buffer (or zeros). The client only sends it when the selected entity has +0x15A8==0x214 and +0x904==8, then shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Result 1 is harmless when nothing is selected (null check). The handler deletes whatever is selected on the client, not a name from the packet, so the server must answer the request actually made. KR's success path reads an extra date struct and shows a 1-week message; EN reads nothing more, so do not append data. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C5, login_character#08): after a successful delete the client-side uid/x invariants are broken (see semantics), and a following S2C 0x1C create - which derives uid = 30000000 + n and x = 110*(n+1) from n = scene+0x14 - can COLLIDE with a surviving character. The server should re-send the whole character list (a fresh success S2C 0x02 after a fresh login, never a second 0x02 in the same char-select session, see C6) rather than rely on the client's post-delete layout.
specs.references: KR (PySlayer doc line 5080) has the same u8 result switch, but its success path reads more data. EN reads 1 byte only. Our server does not dispatch C2S 0x12 and never sends 0x1F. The error strings are from strings.tsv (0x6F6680, 0x6F6BBC, 0x6F4E38).
open_questions: Exact source of the 21-byte password field in C2S 0x12 (a UI edit box lookup, window 0x201). This does not affect this S2C spec.
blind_open_questions: Whether FUN_00422b90 also updates scene+0x14 (character count); a 0x02 character-list resend may be needed to keep slot positions consistent.

spec_errata.old: "shifts every later character 110 px left and decrements its uid, keeping the 30000000+index scheme"
spec_errata.new: shifts everything after the first match in LIST order (= lower slots); the uid/x invariants break

spec_errata.old: no statement about post-delete uid/x collisions with 0x1C
spec_errata.new: documented collision hazard between a post-delete list and a following 0x1C

spec_errata.old: trigger described only "send after C2S 0x12"
spec_errata.new: the preceding 0x51/0x80 steps are documented

specs.name: DeathMatchWaitingListStatus
specs.length: 1 byte if waiting_count==0, else 2 bytes (nothing is read if the client is already inside a battlefield map)

locations.role: waiting_count==0 branch: close message box window 0x16
waiting_count==12: countdown this+0x1200=5, SetTimer id 10 / 1000 ms
WM_TIMER id 10 countdown tick; at the end sends C2S 0x3A
probable trigger: C2S 0x39 + u8 battle type (subscribe to battle) from Battlefield list window 0x14
waiting window 0x17b button 3: closes window and sends C2S 0x3B (cancel waiting)

fields.name: waiting_count
fields.meaning: Players currently on the Death Match waiting list (the client shows it out of a hard-coded max of 12). 0 closes the message box and ends reading. Exactly 12 starts the summon countdown.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local frame+0x42; shown as text 'Join(N/12)' on window 0x14 control 9 and 'Standing by\r\n(N/12)' on window 0x17b control 4

fields.name: unk_01
fields.meaning: Read only when waiting_count != 0. The handler never uses it (a spare byte, maybe the max count or a battle type). Send 0.

specs.semantics: Gate: if [[this+0x4D8]+0x70] == 1 (the current map is a battlefield / Death Match map; the same flag blocks the battle-join precheck FUN_00444400), the packet is ignored and nothing is read. Otherwise it reads waiting_count. (a) waiting_count == 0: FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) closes the generic message-box window 0x16. Nothing else is read. (b) waiting_count != 0: reads unk_01. Sets window 0x14 (Battlefield, T key) control 9 to sprintf('%s(%u/%u)', 'Join', count, 12), window 0x17b control 2 to 'Death Match waiting list.' and window 0x17b control 4 to 'Standing by\r\n(count/12)'. If window 0x17b is currently closed (FUN_004837c0 returns 1), it closes message box 0x16 and opens the waiting-list window 0x17b (FUN_00483430(0x17b,3,1)). If count == 12 (list full): sets this+0x1200 = 5, shows a message box '5sec. You will be summoned to the battle field in. ...Strength will be only recovered while you stay still.', calls SetTimer(hwnd=[this+0xE0], id=10, 1000 ms) and closes windows 0x14 and 0x17b. On each tick of timer 10 (FUN_0043e3f0 @0x43E91F) the counter goes down and the message box text is updated. When the counter reaches 1, the client kills the timer, shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' and sends C2S 0x3A (opcode only). So about 5 s after a count of 12 the server gets C2S 0x3A and should summon the player to the battlefield.
specs.trigger: Send to each player on the Death Match waiting list whenever the list size changes, starting with the reply to the subscribe request (probably C2S 0x39 <u8 type>). Send 12 when the match is full to start the client's 5 s countdown. Send 0 to clear or close the waiting state. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x39 (battlefield subscribe) and C2S 0x3A. Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.expected_response: When waiting_count==12: after about 5 s the client sends C2S 0x3A (0-byte body) meaning it is ready to be summoned. Otherwise nothing. Pressing button 3 on waiting window 0x17b sends C2S 0x3B (cancel).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Ignored while [[0x70EED8]+0x70]==1 (already in a battlefield map). The client does not clamp the count: values above 12 just display as 'N/12', and only exactly 12 triggers the countdown. If you send 2 bytes with count 0, the second byte is left unread. The countdown uses this+0x1200 and timer id 10, and sending count 12 again restarts it. Message boxes use shared window 0x16, so count==0 closes whatever dialog is open.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder, and the KR full-packet decomp has no matching main-switch case (its case 0x20 is in an unrelated nested switch). Our server has no 0x20 builder. The UI strings 'Death Match waiting list.', 'Standing by', 'Join' and the countdown string at 0x6F62D0 confirm the naming.
open_questions: Meaning of the unused second byte (unk_01). Nothing in this handler reads it after GetDataFromPacket.
Exact C2S subscribe trigger: 0x44A8BB sends 0x39 + u8 (row type > 4) from the Battlefield list. Not yet confirmed that the server should answer 0x39 with 0x20.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of the second byte (unk_01): it is read only when count != 0 and is never used by the EN client.
Exact meaning of map descriptor +0x70 == 1 (assumed battle/instance map; it also silently blocks room/battlefield/arena joins).
What the 10/1000ms timer does when the countdown reaches 0 (e.g. which C2S or map change follows) was not traced in this pass.

spec_errata.old: the must-reply role was not stated
spec_errata.new: documented as the packet that clears the waiting modal

specs.name: ExpDelta
specs.grammar:
if(scene+0x970 == 0) { stop }
i32 exp_delta

fields.name: exp_delta
fields.meaning: signed experience change added to the local player's total exp (scene+0x278). Positive shows "You've received (+%d) experience points.". Negative is clamped so the total never goes below 0 and shows "Lost (%d) EXP." (prints the negative number). 0 shows no message

specs.semantics: Local-player exp update; ignored entirely if no local player entity is registered (scene+0x970 == 0). delta > 0: FUN_00427cb0(old_total, old_total+delta) checks whether the next cumulative threshold of the exp table 0x6F0EB0 (same data as 0x6F0C28) is crossed. If so it does a client-side LEVEL-UP: opens UI event 0xA2 (FUN_00483430), queues level-up effect 0x24 on the local uid (FUN_0042b580), plays sound 0x24, sets local entity+0x99 = FUN_00440df0(new_total) (can jump several levels), recalculates max HP with full heal (FUN_00427d40(...,1)) and max MP with full refill (FUN_00427f40(1)), and refreshes the stat window (FUN_00442510, 'Lv.%u'). Then it posts the gain message to the chat/system log (FUN_004817d0, color -1). delta < 0: clamps the delta to -total. FUN_00427ce0 checks for a level-down threshold; if one is crossed it sets the level from the new total, recalculates HP/MP (no heal, clamps MP to max) and refreshes the stat window. Then it posts 'Lost (%d) EXP.' (color 0xFFFD4C87). Always: scene+0x278 += delta and FUN_00442aa0 redraws the exp bar ('%u/%u').
specs.trigger: Server grants or removes exp for the local player (monster kill, quest reward, death penalty).
specs.gates_and_hazards: The local player must be registered (scene+0x970 != 0), otherwise the packet is silently dropped and the exp is NOT accumulated. Level-up is computed purely client-side from scene+0x278, so the server's exp total must match the client's starting exp (set by the login/spawn packets) or level-ups will happen at the wrong time or never. Our server also sends 0x22 after a threshold crossing, which plays the level-up effect and sound a second time.

locations.role: CMP opcode,0x7F (0x21 goes to plain message)

specs.references: windslayer_server.py _send_exp sends struct '<i' (4 bytes), which matches. It notes 0x21 'doesn't reliably apply the level', which fits the scene+0x278 baseline dependency above. The newer KR build reads 8-byte (64-bit) exp here, so it is NOT compatible. reference_combat_model.md 'curve @0x6f0eb0' is confirmed.
open_questions: Which login/spawn packet initializes scene+0x278 (total exp) was not traced in this batch.
blind_open_questions: Minor differences between the two exp tables 0x6F0EB0 (crossing check) and 0x6F0C28 (level compute) were not enumerated (first 12 entries identical, arrays not fully equal).

specs.name: SetLevel
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u8 level

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: uid (entity+0x84) of the player (local or remote) whose level is set
fields.dest_or_source: stack [ESP+0x10C] (IAT 0x4A40C8 u32); used as effect target, entity lookup key (FUN_004189f0), and compared to party-frame window +0x134

fields.name: level
fields.meaning: new ABSOLUTE level. 0 = packet ignored after reading

specs.semantics: Both fields are always read. If level == 0 (0x4545B5) nothing else happens. Otherwise: (1) FUN_0042b580(0x24, uid, 0,0,0, 1, 9, 0) queues a deferred event record (type 9, id 0x24, target uid), which is the level-up effect. It runs before the entity lookup, so it is queued even if the uid is unknown. (2) entity = FUN_004189f0(scene, uid). If the entity is missing, jump to step 6. (3) byte entity+0x99 = level; FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 1) recomputes max HP (+0x110C) and sets cur HP (+0x9C) = max (full heal). It does this only when level is 1..99 and class byte +0x110 <= 6; otherwise it writes nothing. Then FUN_00427f40(1) with ESI=entity recomputes max MP (+0x1110) and sets cur MP (+0xA0) = max, again only if level < 100 and class < 7. (4) CSpriteControl::Play_Sound(0x24, entity+0x15A4, entity+0x15A8, gs+0x1044, gs+0x1048, gs+0x104C, gs+0x1050, 0) plays the level-up sound at the entity's screen position. (5) Scan the party-member frames, UI ids 0x75..0x78 (FUN_004830f0). For the first frame whose +0x134 == uid: if max HP != 0, write text 1 = sprintf('%u/%u', +0x9C, +0x110C) and set bar 1 = cur/max. Then, if max MP != 0, write text 2 = '%u/%u' (+0xA0, +0x1110) and set bar 2. If max HP == 0, both HP and MP updates are skipped. (6) FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) always runs when level != 0, whether or not the entity or a party frame was found (0x454694 / 0x454780). It walks a record list filtered by the LOCAL player's level range (+0xDEC/+0xDF0 of each record), class/job and prerequisite ids, which looks like an available-quest list rebuild. The local stat window (FUN_00442510: 'Lv.%u', stat points) is NOT refreshed, the exp counter scene+0x278 is not changed, and no packet is sent back.
specs.trigger: Server-side level-up of any player: broadcast to observers and party members, and send to the owner to apply the new level to the avatar and play the effect.
specs.gates_and_hazards: level == 0 makes the packet a no-op after both fields are consumed (still 5 bytes). The entity must already be spawned for the level/HP/MP to apply; the effect event is queued regardless. The effect and sound play every time, even if the level did not change, so pairing this with a 0x21 exp update that already levels the client plays them twice. Levels > 99 are stored in +0x99, but max HP/MP are not recalculated. Because 0x442510 is not called, the local HUD 'Lv.' label and remaining stat points stay stale until another refresh (e.g. 0x14 or 0x21 paths). The KR build returns early when the entity is missing; EN still runs the FUN_004781c0 refresh. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (login_character#14): besides the stat window, the HUD level label (top-left "LV") is NOT refreshed by 0x22 either.

locations.role: CMP level,0 / JZ 0x44D7AD (break) - after all reads
FUN_0042b580 queue event type 9 id 0x24 on uid
FUN_004189f0 entity lookup; null -> 0x454775 (list refresh only)
FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 1) max HP + full heal
party frame scan UI 0x75..0x78 for +0x134 == uid
matched frame: HP '%u/%u' text+bar, MP text+bar
record list rebuild filtered by local player level/class/prereqs

specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analysts A and B agree on the wire bytes: u32 uid (GetDataFromPacket IAT 0x4A40C8 at 0x454597, dest [ESP+0x118]-12 = [ESP+0x10C]) followed by u8 level (IAT 0x4A4094 at 0x4545AF, dest [ESP+0x59]-12 = [ESP+0x4D]). The only structural difference is that A appended `if(level == 0) { stop }`. The asm shows the level==0 test (CMP byte [ESP+0x4D],0 / JZ 0x44D7AD at 0x4545B5) comes AFTER both reads, and no path in the block reads anything else. The condition therefore gates side effects only, not how many bytes are consumed. A's trailing stop is redundant and misleading, so B's grammar `u32 uid / u8 level` is the correct canonical form, and the gate belongs in gates_and_hazards. On semantics: both correctly say FUN_004781c0 also runs when the entity is missing (JZ 0x454775 at 0x4545F4 falls into the call at 0x454780). B's label 'party list refresh' for FUN_004781c0 is not supported. Its decomp iterates records gated by the local player's level (+0x928 -> +0x99) against per-record min/max, class and prerequisite ids, which is consistent with an available-quest list, not a party list. B's note that 0x427D40 no-ops for level > 99 or class > 6 is confirmed by the FUN_00427d40 decomp. Cross-refs: windslayer_server.py _send_level packs '<IB' (matches). Its docstring's 'refreshes the HP/MP bars' refers only to party frames, and cur HP is full-healed by the flag=1 recalc. PySlayer Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x22 (line 5283) reads u32 + u8 the same way, but returns early when the entity is missing.
open_questions: FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C) exact identity: it looks like an available-quest list rebuild (records filtered by level range, class/job, a prerequisite id checked against 0x55 u16 ids at +0x262, and 3 ids at +0x256), but the owning UI was not traced.
Deferred event type 9 / id 0x24 queued by FUN_0042b580 is assumed to be the level-up visual; the consumer (FUN_00459df0 queue) was not traced.

spec_errata.old: HUD refresh behaviour partially stated
spec_errata.new: HUD LV label is not refreshed

specs.name: InventoryItemRemove (silent)
specs.grammar:
u16 item_id
u16 count
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }
u16 opt_extra

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item id to remove (1-based catalog index)

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number to remove from type-0/type-2 stacks; ignored for equipment (always 1)
fields.dest_or_source: local [frame+0x28] -> FUN_00467140 arg3 (read as a word)

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: How many option words follow (0..5)

fields.name: opt
fields.meaning: Option words 0..opt_count-1 of the 12-byte option block (starts zeroed)

fields.name: opt_extra
fields.meaning: Word 5 of the option block

locations.role: jmp 0x46D968 -> FUN_00465290 inventory UI refresh, return 1

specs.semantics: Same as 0x19 but with no leading gold field and no chat message. Reads item_id, count and the option block (u8 n, n u16 words into words 0.., u16 into word 5). Looks up the item definition (none -> stop, handled). Removes the item with FUN_00467140 using the same type rules as 0x19: type 0 subtract from u16 stacks, type 1 remove the matching equipment slot (option bytes must match), type 2 subtract from u8 stacks. On success refreshes the inventory UI; on failure nothing visible happens.
specs.trigger: Whenever the server takes an item out of the bag without selling it: consumed, used by a quest, destroyed, moved to storage or equipped (our server sends it after the 0x1D equip).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same stack overflow as 0x19: opt_count must be <= 5 (>= 63 corrupts the /GS cookie and kills the client). Equipment is removed only when all 12 option bytes match the stored slot; items granted by 0x18 have zero options, so send opt_count=0 and opt_extra=0. Fails if the tab capacity byte (player_info+0x361/+0x362/+0x363) > 45, if count=0 for stack items, if fewer than count are owned (types 0/2), or if the type is 3 or higher.
specs.references: Our server's _build_opcode_23 (u16 item, u16 count, u8 0, u16 0 = 7 B) has the right format. One correction to its comment: FUN_00404210 does not look up a bag element. It returns the item definition from the global catalog [scene+0xF84] (name at +0, type at +0x154), and is NULL only for item_id 0 or an id past the catalog. Whether the item is actually in the bag is decided later by FUN_00467140 against player_info's tab arrays. The memory note '0x23 didn't remove bag in test' fits the item not being in the matching tab array (or an option mismatch), not a catalog miss.
open_questions: Which C2S requests the original server answered with 0x23 (item use, storage deposit, etc.).
blind_open_questions: Field-level meaning of the option words and tail within the 12-byte blob.

specs.name: UnequipItemRemove
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u16 item_id

specs.semantics: Same handler as 0x1E: removes item_id (with a matching 12-byte option record) from the entity's equip grid +0x13C/+0x16E, rebuilds the sprite, recalculates stats and max HP/MP. For the local player (uid == scene+0x220) it refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290) and the equipment window (FUN_00441a10). Unlike 0x1E it does NOT add the item back to the bag and does NOT update the cash-item list (FUN_0045d170): the opcode check at 0x45424F skips both. So the item simply disappears from the equipment.

specs.gates_and_hazards: Same gates as 0x1E (item def exists with def+0x154 == 1; the removal needs an exact id + 12-byte record match, otherwise nothing changes and there is no error). The window refresh only runs for the local uid. No bag add, so no duplication hazard. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C33, item_inventory#05): removal from the equip tab COMPACTS the list - later slots shift down - so slot indices the server cached before the removal are stale afterwards.

self-use logic: switch on record type rec+0x154 (0 = consumable, 3 = skill, anything else = no-op)
type 0: FUN_00423b70 removes 1 of the id from the bag and checks/stamps the per-slot cooldown; returns 0 -> abort
type 0: FUN_00465290 refreshes the inventory UI, then effect 0x29 on the local uid and sound 0x29
type 3: sets the cast-animation state (scene+0x255=7, scene+0x256=variant 1..11) by id range, plus special cases
type 3: clears the pending-skill word scene+0x258 (unblocks the next C2S 0x15 skill cast)
type 3: FUN_00426cc0 stamps the skill cooldown (local entity +0x29A skill list / +0x7B4 timestamps, rec+0x1EC ms)
adds rec+0x15C to local MP (+0xA0), clamps to +0x1110, refreshes the MP bar (FUN_00443780)
adds rec+0x158 to local HP (+0x9C) when FUN_004258d0(id) is true, clamps to +0x110C, refreshes the HP bar (FUN_00443690)
