S2C 0x5F also clears scene+0x258 (cast rejected / cancel)

specs.grammar: u16 item_or_skill_id

fields.name: item_or_skill_id
fields.meaning: windslayer.hii record id (a consumable item or a skill). The client looks up the record and applies its effect to the LOCAL player. No uid is read.

specs.semantics:
Server confirmation that the LOCAL player used an item or skill. There is no uid, so it always applies to the local player. The client looks up the id in its hii table (FUN_00404210). If there is no record, nothing happens. Otherwise it switches on rec+0x154:
(type 0, consumable) FUN_00423b70(qty=-1, ids=scene+0x63E, counts=scene+0x698, cooldown_ts=scene+0x6F4, id, bag_size=byte scene+0x3AA, cooldown=rec+0x1EC, now=this+0x364, check=1) removes one unit from the client-side bag and stamps the cooldown. If the item is not in the bag or is still cooling down, the handler exits with no effect. On success it refreshes the inventory window, then plays effect 0x29 on the local uid and sound 0x29.
(type 3, skill) Starts the local cast animation by writing scene+0x255=7 and scene+0x256=variant. Those bytes go out on the UDP P2P state as action*10+dir. Variants by id range: 1 = 0x104-0x10E, 0x150-0x15A, 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x200-0x20A, 0x22C-0x236; 2 = 0x10F-0x119, 0x15B-0x165, 0x1B3-0x1BD, 0x1C9-0x1D3, 0x20B-0x215, 0x242-0x24C; 3 = 0x13A-0x144, 0x166-0x170, 0x1DF-0x1E9, 0x216-0x220, 0x237-0x241, 0x7A1-0x7AB; 4 = 0x24D-0x257, 0x76A-0x774, 0x780-0x78A, 0x796-0x7A0, 0x7C2-0x7CC, 0x7D8-0x7E2; 5 = 0x258-0x262, 0x775-0x77F, 0x78B-0x795, 0x7CD-0x7D7, 0x7E3-0x7ED, 0x9FA-0xA04, 0xA3C-0xA46; 6..10 = further families; 11 = 0xB3B-0xB45.
Special skill ids: 0xAD6-0xAD7 and 0xC2C-0xC2D pick the variant from the player's active buff slots. 0xAD8-0xAE2 is a party heal: effect and sound 0x10E on self and on every party member in scene+0x25C..0x26C, and rec+0x158 is added to each member's HP. 0x1F5-0x1FF plays effects 0x54 and 0x37 plus sound 0x54 when mode==0. 0xC2 opens UI message 0x259. 0x876-0x880, 0x881-0x88B and 0x88C call UI helpers FUN_00467fa0, FUN_00467ea0 and FUN_004687f0.
Then for every type-3 id: scene+0x258 (pending skill) = 0, FUN_00426cc0 stamps the skill cooldown, FUN_00441c20(0) and FUN_00443ac0 refresh the quick slots.
(common tail for types 0 and 3) FUN_00443840 refreshes the stats panel. If local entity scene+0x970 exists and [[0x70EED8]+0x70] != 1: MP += rec+0x15C (clamped 0..max) and MP bar refresh; HP += rec+0x158 (clamped 0..max, only if FUN_004258d0(id)=1, i.e. id not in 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x24D-0x257, 0x8C6-0x8D0, 0x8F2-0x8FC, 0x997-0x9A1, 0x9C3-0x9F9, 0xA5D-0xA67, 0xAF9-0xB03, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB25-0xB2F) and HP bar refresh. If rec+0x160 != 0, the HP bar and party HP bars refresh too.
HP/MP deltas come from the client's own hii record: potions have positive values, skill costs are negative. The packet carries no amounts.
Other record types (1/2/4/5/6) do nothing.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C27, combat_skill#03): for id 0x88C, FUN_004687f0 is NOT an unconditional "open the Reinforce UI" - it first checks the distance to a smithy and otherwise shows the modal "Too far for Reinforcement. Go near the smithy."
specs.trigger: Reply to the local player's C2S 0x15 UseItemOrSkill (u16 id [+u16 x,u16 y for 0xA31..0xA3B]) when the use is accepted. Send it for consumables (type 0) and for non-buff skills (type 3). For duration/buff skills, S2C 0x3B with target_uid = caster also runs this same self logic, so use one or the other, not both. To reject a skill cast, send 0x5F.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
1) Unknown id (not in windslayer.hii) or a record type other than 0/3 is silently ignored.
2) Type 0: needs the id in the client-side bag (scene+0x63E) and the per-slot cooldown rec+0x1EC to have elapsed. Otherwise the whole handler aborts with no heal.
3) Type 3: C2S 0x15 skill sends are blocked while scene+0x258 != 0 (set on send at 0x44C248) and while scene+0x255 == 7 (cast animation). If the server never answers a skill cast with 0x25 (or 0x3B for self) or 0x5F, the player can never cast again until a map reload (FUN_0042c360 clears it).
4) CRASH: the type-3 tail at 0x453D98 does LEA on [scene+0x970] with no null check and FUN_00426cc0 reads [+0x29A]. Never send a type-3 id before the local player entity exists (after 0x07 spawn).
5) HP/MP are applied as client-side deltas. If the server also pushes absolute 0x28/0x44, send those AFTER 0x25, or the delta double-applies on top of the absolute value.
6) The HP/MP change is skipped when [[0x70EED8]+0x70] == 1 (probably team/arena room mode, unverified).
7) Plays effects and sounds; no dialogs except id 0xC2 (UI 0x259).
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C27, combat_skill#03): the CAST LOCK scene+0x255 = 7 clears BY ITSELF within 3 s with no TCP packet, so no unlock packet (S2C 0x5F) is needed just to clear the cast animation. The pending-skill gate scene+0x258 is the one that really needs an answer (0x25 / 0x3B / 0x5F), and it is what blocks further casts and equip changes.
specs.references:
PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x25.py sends exactly u16 skill, which matches EN. PySlayer sends opcode_25(300) after consumable use and calls opcode_25(500) 'set_maxhp_and_maxmp', both guesses. project_status.md's '0x25 set max HP/MP' inherits that misnomer. The KR Hex-Rays handler (doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x25/0x3B) reads extra bool/flag fields that EN does NOT read.
Our server: _handle_use_skill (windslayer_server.py:1409) builds the correct EN body (struct '<H') but is dead code: nothing calls it, and inbound 0x25 goes to _handle_attack. _handle_use_item (C2S 0x15, line 1111) sends only 0x28/0x44 absolutes, never 0x25, so the client bag count never decrements and skill casts would stay pending.
reference_combat_model.md says 0x25 feeds the +0x3C8 damage-number pool with a scene+0x220==uid gate. This block has no uid read for 0x25 and no +0x3C8 access; only 0x3B compares a uid with scene+0x220.
open_questions: Exact hii column meanings: rec+0x160 (triggers HP-bar/party refresh), rec+0x1DC (must be >0 for skills to be castable). Record offsets were derived from the loader FUN_004034C0 (0x228-byte records).

Meaning of the mode flag [[0x70EED8]+0x70]: ==1 skips HP/MP deltas and changes party-buff handling (team byte +0x14EB), ==0 selects local/single behaviour in UDP code. Likely room/PvP mode, unverified.
Whether retail sent 0x25 for buff skills too, or only 0x3B to the caster. Sending both would double-apply MP cost and animation.
blind_open_questions: What is [gs+0x4D8]+0x70 == 1 (it suppresses the HP/MP application; likely arena/battle mode, cf. [scene+0xF88]+0x70 used for team checks in FUN_00424e20)?
Meaning of record field +0x160 (only triggers an HP/party HUD refresh).
Whether retail also sent 0x25 for type-3 skills that have a buff duration (0x3B to self already covers that path).

specs.name: QuestAccepted

locations.role: quest-table lookup QuestTable[id-1] (ctx+0xC, vector at +8/+0xC), returns record in EAX or 0
append quest_id to completed-quest list char+0x262 (85 x u16) / count char+0x30C (u8, cap 99)
client-side inventory grant of the quest's Send items (also used by S2C 0x18)
matching C2S 0x16 AcceptQuest send site (u16 quest_id)

specs.grammar: u16 quest_id

fields.name: quest_id
fields.meaning: Quest index into the client's hs/windslayer.hqi quest table (1-based). 0 or unknown id = packet ignored after the read.
fields.dest_or_source: local [esp+0x10]; then written into first empty active slot char+0x256+2*i (char=[ctx+0x18], ctx=game+0xD2C) or into completed list char+0x262

specs.semantics:
Quest-accept result. After reading quest_id the client looks up the quest record (FUN_0040a840). If the record is null, nothing happens (the handler still returns 'handled'). Otherwise:
(a) If record.Money(+0xDE8, i32) >= 0 AND record.Demand_id[0](+0xD0C) == 0 AND record.ReqPro(+0xDF8) == 0 (a quest with no requirements), the quest is NOT put in the active log. FUN_004264a0 adds it to the completed-quest list instead (char+0x262 u16[85] plus count bytes char+0x30C: a new entry gets count 1, an existing one gets count+1 capped at 99, and a full list is shifted left before appending).
(b) Otherwise the quest goes into the first active slot i (0..2) whose u16 id at char+0x256+2i is 0. The client writes the id and clears the ready flag at char+0x25F+i. The progress byte at char+0x25C+i is NOT reset. There is no duplicate check, and if all 3 slots are full nothing is stored and there is no message.
In both cases the client then grants the quest's Send items itself: for i=0..9, stopping at the first zero id at record+0xC94+4i, it calls FUN_00440920(ctx+4, id, 0, count=record+0xD34+4i). That adds the item to the bag and prints "you've received %s. (Count:%u)" (or "You've learned skill(%s)." for type-3 items). Finally it refreshes the quest window (FUN_00478380). Quest record layout (confirmed from hqi loader FUN_00409FE0): +4 name, +0xC94 Send ids[10], +0xCBC Reward ids[20], +0xD0C Demand ids[10], +0xD34 Send_Num[10], +0xD5C Reward_Num[20], +0xDAC Demand_Num[10], +0xDE4 Exp, +0xDE8 Money, +0xDF4 Repeat, +0xDF8 ReqPro, +0xE08 SNPC, +0xE0C ENPC.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x16 AcceptQuest (u16 quest_id, send site 0x477330). The client sends it only after checking that an active slot is free ("You can only take 3 quests at a time...") and that the bag has room for the Send items. The client does not add the quest optimistically; it waits for this packet.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Returns without reading if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null (the sub-handler chain then continues). Hazards: (1) Sending 0x26 twice for the same quest fills two active slots. (2) The client grants the hqi Send items ITSELF, so a server that also sends S2C 0x18 GetItem for those items (0x18's handler at 0x46DEDE calls the same FUN_00440920) duplicates them in the client bag. (3) A no-requirement quest (Money>=0, no Demand, ReqPro==0) goes straight to the completed list, so the server must not expect it to be active. The client's turn-in code (FUN_00477af0) only turns in quests that are in active slots. (4) The client's slot choice is the first empty slot, so the server's slot numbering for 0x59 must copy that rule exactly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, quest_cards_misc#09): one client session exited GRACEFULLY about 2 s after a 0x26 "1a 00" injection followed by a Q keypress (the server logged a clean close with no crash event). It was NOT reproduced in two later sessions with the identical packet, so treat it as an unexplained termination risk rather than a rule; recovery is a restart.
specs.references: PySlayer opcode_26: p16u(random), which agrees on u16 / 2 bytes. Our server's _send_quest_grant packs '<H' quest_id, which matches. Live capture: accepting quest 26 got S2C 0x26 with a 2-byte body, with no desync. Disagreement: reference_gamedef_db.md says 'EN client has NO live quest granted opcode'. That is wrong; this is that opcode. Our _handle_accept_quest also sends 0x18 for each q['send'] item, which likely duplicates the client-side hqi Send grant (PLAUSIBLE; depends on EN hqi Send columns).
open_questions: Whether the EN hqi quest 26 (starter) has ReqPro/Money/Demand set. If all are empty, 0x26 files it straight into the completed list instead of the active log. The live observation 'shown as Accepted' could be either tab.
For no-requirement quests, how the original server delivered Exp/Reward items (0x27 would increment the completion count a second time).
blind_open_questions: Exact correspondence of client quest-def arrays (+0xC94 accept grants x10, +0xCBC rewards x20, +0xD0C demand items x10, counts at +0xA0 offset) to PySlayer gamedef columns 'send'/'reward'/'demand' is inferred from usage, not from the data file loader.
Whether the server should suppress its own 0x18 for accept items is inferred (FUN_00440920 is the same grant routine reached by 0x18 per server comments) - confirm with a live test.

spec_errata.new: unexplained one-off graceful exit recorded

specs.name: QuestCompleted

locations.role: client-side removal of Demand items from bag
refresh NPC quest-dialog list for NPC at ctx+0x1C
matching C2S 0x17 TurnInQuest send site (u16 quest_id)

specs.grammar: u16 quest_id

fields.name: quest_id
fields.meaning: Quest being completed. It must exist in the client's quest table or the packet is a no-op. All rewards come from the client's local hqi record, not from the packet.

specs.semantics:
Quest turn-in result. The client applies all of the completion bookkeeping itself, from its local quest record:
1. Look up the record; if null, return.
2. Clear every active slot whose id == quest_id (id=0, progress byte char+0x25C+i = 0).
3. FUN_004264a0: add quest_id to the completed list char+0x262 (count 1, or count+1 capped at 99).
4. If record.Money (+0xDE8, i32) != 0: gold64 at char+0x228/0x22C += sign-extended Money, and the gold label is refreshed. If Money < 0 the chat shows "Gave %u Gold." (color 0xFFFD4C87); otherwise "You've received %u Gold." (0xFF00C800).
5. For i=0..9 while Demand_id[i] (+0xD0C+4i) != 0: look up the item in the item table at [ctx+4]+0x4D4. If found, call FUN_00467140(type=item+0x154, inv=[ctx+4]+0xD5C, u16 id, 0, u16 count=+0xDAC+4i) to remove it from the bag (types 0/1/2 only). On success, chat "Gave %u item(%s)." and refresh the inventory UI (FUN_00465290).
6. For i=0..19 while Reward_id[i] (+0xCBC+4i) != 0: FUN_00440920(ctx+4, id, 0, count=+0xD5C+4i) grants the item ("you've received %s. (Count:%u)" / skill learned).
7. Refresh the quest window and the NPC quest-dialog list.
EXP (+0xDE4) is NOT applied here; the server must send it separately (S2C 0x21).
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x17 TurnInQuest (u16 quest_id), sent by FUN_00477af0 when talking to the quest's ENPC (+0xE0C). The client checks Money/gold, progress >= ReqPro, Demand items present and reward bag space ("There isn't empty space in the inventory.") before sending.
specs.expected_response: none (server should follow with S2C 0x21 exp if the quest gives exp)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Skipped if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null. An unknown quest_id is a silent no-op. The client does NOT check that the quest was active, so sending 0x27 for a non-active quest still adds gold, removes Demand items, grants Rewards and bumps the completion count. Double-sending doubles rewards. Duplication hazard: the client already adds Money and Reward items and removes Demand items locally. A server that also sends S2C 0x18 GetItem for the rewards (the 0x18 handler calls the same FUN_00440920) duplicates reward items in the client bag. Gold can stay consistent if 0x18 carries an absolute gold total. Gold is not clamped, so negative Money can underflow the u64 if the server skips the gold check. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C21, quest_cards_misc#11): live-confirmed that double-sending re-grants the items and gold and bumps the completion count again; the one exception is a type-3 skill reward that is already learned, which prints nothing the second time. Duplicate 0x27s duplicate items, gold and completion count - not skills.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Our server's _send_quest_complete packs '<H' quest_id, which matches the wire format. However: (a) our server fires it from C2S 0x16 (treated as accept OR turn-in), while the real client sends turn-in as C2S 0x17 (send site 0x477F15), which our _dispatch does not handle, so real NPC turn-ins get no reply; (b) _complete_quest also sends 0x18 per reward item (plus gold_gain), likely duplicating the client-side hqi Reward grant (PLAUSIBLE; depends on EN hqi Reward columns matching the KR gamedef).
open_questions: Whether EN hqi Reward/Money/Demand values match the KR gamedef.sqlite3 rows (item-id drift like 377->179), which determines what the client grants locally.
Whether the original server sent 0x18 inventory syncs after 0x27, or relied solely on the client-side grant.
blind_open_questions: Mapping of def+0xCBC (20 entries) vs def+0xD0C (10 entries) to gamedef 'reward'/'demand' columns is inferred from the helpers used (grant vs negative-count removal) and the chat strings.
Whether the server's 0x18 gold_gain path actually modifies client money (i.e. a true double-credit) was not traced in this pass.

spec_errata.old: double-send behaviour was inferred from the code
spec_errata.new: live-confirmed, with the already-learned-skill exception

specs.name: SetLocalHp
specs.grammar: u16 hp

fields.name: hp
fields.meaning: New ABSOLUTE current HP of the local player (not a delta)
fields.dest_or_source: zero-extended into (*(scene+0x970))+0x9C (local-player entity cur HP, i32). scene = [game_state+0x4CC] = [0x70EECC]

specs.semantics: Reads one u16 (IAT 0x4A4090, stack local [esp+0xE8]). If the local-player entity pointer [scene+0x970] is non-null, writes movzx(hp) to entity+0x9C. Then always calls FUN_00443690 (ESI=game_state): if the local entity exists, sprintf("%d/%d", +0x9C, +0x110C max HP) into HUD text slot 6 (FUN_004838c0(6)); if max HP (+0x110C) != 0 it sets HP globe fill ratio (FUN_004891e0(2, cur/max, 2)) and a HUD state FUN_00489320(2,1, ratio>0.2 ? 3 : 0) (low-HP indicator). No effect, no sound, no reply.
specs.trigger: Whenever the server changes the local player's HP: enter-world / map change right after 0x07 (otherwise player shows 0 HP and is effectively dead), potion use, damage taken, regen.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No uid in packet: always targets the LOCAL player only. If [scene+0x970] is null (before RegisterLocalPlayer) the value is silently dropped. Max representable HP is 65535. Handler does not trigger death at 0; however the entity-update loop (FUN_00413920, action 2/0x11 end) calls FUN_0041a230 when +0x9C < 1, so hp=0 can start client-side death flow later. HUD ratio skipped if max HP (+0x110C, set by 0x07) is 0.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x28.py (setHp, single p16u) matches EN exactly. The newer KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x28) is DIFFERENT: u8 subtype (1=HP,2=MP,3=...) + u16 + i32 max etc. - do not port that. Our server _send_hp (windslayer_server.py:1566) struct '<H' matches; used at enter-world (732), item use (1180), map change (1265). Memory note 'player needs 0x28/0x44 on spawn' consistent.
open_questions: Fireway GetDataFromPacket behaviour on a short packet (len < offset+2) is not visible in the client; server must always send the full 2 bytes.

specs.name: EntityDie
specs.length: 16 (client consumes only 4 if uid not found)
specs.grammar:
u32 uid
if(entity_lookup(uid) == null) {
  stop
}
u32 respawn_tick
u32 respawn_x
u32 respawn_y

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: entity (player or monster) that dies; looked up via FUN_004189f0 in scene list; unknown => stop

fields.name: respawn_tick
fields.meaning: absolute respawn deadline on the client scene clock scene+0xF1C (advanced +0x1E per logic tick in FUN_00417e10, reset to 0 by FUN_0042c360/FUN_00428090). Local player auto-respawns when (int)(respawn_tick - clock) < 0

fields.name: respawn_x
fields.meaning: respawn/home X; converted unsigned->f64

fields.name: respawn_y
fields.meaning: respawn/home Y; converted unsigned->f64

specs.semantics: Starts the death sequence for any entity. After a successful lookup and BEFORE reading the rest, the handler sets entity+0x8E2=0, +0x8E4=0, action +0x904=0x10 (dying), action timer +0xE00=0, and +0x8CF=8. Then reads respawn_tick into +0xE5C and x/y (FILD + 2^32 fixup = unsigned) into f64 +0x1318/+0x1320. The entity update loop (FUN_00413920) plays the death animation in action 0x10, then switches to 0x16 (dead). In 0x16, for TYPE-4 TEMPLATE entities (+0x98 == 4) once (int)(+0xE5C - scene+0xF1C) < 0 the client itself respawns: LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C16, combat_skill#00/#16/#19, world_movement_npc#22) - the LOCAL player is type 3, not type 4, so this branch is NOT the local-player path. That client-side revive also clears the WHOLE buff table, including the 0xB3B render entry a monster needs in order to be drawn, and resets HP to the entity TEMPLATE max (5 for a Pupu), not to the value the server last sent. Details of the revive: posX(+0x11F8)=+0x1318, posY(+0x1288)=+0x1320, action=8 idle, HP=max(+0x110C), MP=max(+0x1110), clears buff arrays. For monsters +0x1318 is also the home position used by the leash check (FUN_00417e10: |posX-homeX|>600 sets return flag +0xDBC). HP is NOT set to 0 by this packet.
specs.trigger: Server-side death of a monster or player (HP reached 0).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unknown uid => no-op. Re-sending for an already dead entity restarts the dying animation (action forced to 0x10). For the local player, respawn_tick=0 (or any value that makes the signed difference negative) causes an immediate client-side respawn at (respawn_x, respawn_y) with full HP/MP as soon as the death animation ends - sending x=y=0 teleports the player to (0,0). A large positive value (e.g. 0x7FFFFFFF) should keep the local player dead until the server respawns it (e.g. via 0x07) - inferred from the signed compare. The server cannot observe scene+0xF1C, so precise timed respawn is not possible. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C16b, combat_skill#19): for the LOCAL player the documented self-respawn does NOT fire, even with respawn_tick = 0 - the player plays the death sequence and stays dead indefinitely (input ignored, no auto-revive after 15 s, HP untouched in memory). HAZARD: a 0x29 aimed at the local player is effectively a permanent death. RECOVERY: the server must revive explicitly (HP via 0x28/0x44 plus a map/spawn sequence, or a fresh 0x07); otherwise only a client restart. Re-derive the revive gate before using 0x29 as a revive path.
specs.references: Our server _build_opcode_29 (windslayer_server.py:1937) sends u32 uid + 3 u32 (named anim/dx/dz, all 0) = 16 bytes: layout correct, field names wrong (they are respawn_tick / respawn_x / respawn_y); used for monster death (works). PySlayer opcode_0x29.py sends only 3 random u32 (12 bytes) - one u32 short for EN. KR Hex-Rays case 0x29 has same structure (uid, then +1388 timer, then two u32) with different struct offsets and action 23. Memory reference_combat_model.md 'death=0x29' consistent.

Behaviour of remote-player entities in action 0x16 depends on room/arena globals (scene+0xF88+0x70, scene+0xF24); not needed for wire format.

Local-player revive gate: with respawn_tick = 0 the documented (int)(+0xE5C - scene+0xF1C) < 0 branch did not fire (combat_skill#19). Is the comparison unsigned, or is there an extra gate (+0x98 == 4, HP == 0, action 0x16 dwell time)? Re-derive before using 0x29 to revive.

Meaning of entity bytes +0x8E2/+0x8E4 and +0x8CF=8 (action/anim set) not resolved.
Monster corpse removal after state 0x16 in online mode (likely requires a separate despawn packet) not traced.

specs.name: RemoteEntityMoveStateSync (keyframe: flush queue + target + position)
specs.length: 16, 17, 33 or 34 bytes: 4 + 8 + 4 + [1 if action nibble is 9 or 10] + [17 if the position block is read]. Nothing is read after the position block, so always sending it gives 33 or 34 bytes.

fields.name: mover_uid
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x1D4]. Passed in EDX to FUN_004189f0, which walks the scene entity list (scene+0xC) and matches entity+0x84. uid 0 or an unknown uid gives null, and the handler stops.
fields.meaning: uid of the entity whose movement/action state is being synced (another player, not the receiver)

fields.name: move_bits
fields.dest_or_source: copied raw into scene(this+0x4CC)+0xEF8..0xEFF. This 8-byte scratch area is the same buffer the C2S 0x0D packer FUN_0042c940 fills. It is decoded into a new 0x58-byte queue node (see sub-fields).
fields.meaning: Same bit packing as the 8 bytes inside C2S 0x0D, so the server can relay them verbatim. Read as move_bits_lo = u32 LE of bytes 0-3 and move_bits_hi = u32 LE of bytes 4-7.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[1:0] horiz_input
fields.dest_or_source: node+0x4A: 1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, 0 or 3 gives 8. Applied later to entity+0x8B3.
fields.meaning: horizontal key/direction state; 8 = neutral. The C2S packer maps 8B3: 2 to 1, 6 to 2, anything else to 0.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[4:2]
fields.meaning: vertical/jump state (a live jump capture had value 3)

fields.name: move_bits_lo[8:5]
fields.meaning: input state byte 8B5 (unknown)

fields.name: move_bits_lo[11:9]
fields.meaning: input state byte 8B6 (a live walk capture had value 1; the C2S packer checks for value 4 on grab)

fields.name: move_bits_lo[15:12] action
fields.meaning: Current action: 0 = none, 1-5 = attacks, 6-10 = grab/throw family, 0xD = death (FUN_00412360 case 0xD sets state 0x10, HP 0 and clears buffs). Values 9 and 10 add the extra u8.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[19:16] reaction
fields.dest_or_source: low nibble of byte scene+0xEFA, stored at node+0x4E. When consumed it goes to entity+0x950 if scene+0xF24 != 0, otherwise to entity+0x8EA.
fields.meaning: Reaction/being-hit state. HAZARD: a nonzero value makes FUN_00412100 copy node+0x10/+0x18 (zeroed by memset) into the entity position, so keep it 0.

fields.name: move_bits_lo[21:20] facing
fields.dest_or_source: node+0x50: 1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, anything else gives 8. Later entity+0x8D0.
fields.meaning: facing direction used for the action

fields.name: move_bits_hi[11:0] action_time
fields.dest_or_source: node+0x44, later entity+0x958. Also used to adjust the node delay when target_uid == local uid.
fields.meaning: action timing/frame value (C2S source entity+0x958)

fields.name: target_uid
fields.dest_or_source: node+0x08, later entity+0xD80. If it equals scene+0x220 (the local uid), the handler zeroes node+0x08, +0x4E, +0x4F and +0x44, sets +0x50 = 8 and entity+0x8E2 = 0.
fields.meaning: Target/victim uid of the action. The C2S 0x0D packer only sends entity+0xD80 when action != 0, so the server should write 0 when there is no action.

fields.name: action_flag
fields.meaning: only present when the action nibble is 9 or 10 (grab/throw). FUN_00412360 case 9 checks it to trigger a buff/effect.

fields.name: pos_x
fields.dest_or_source: written directly to entity+0x11F8, not to the queue node
fields.meaning: mover world X

fields.name: pos_y
fields.meaning: mover world Y

fields.name: airborne
fields.meaning: In-air flag. FUN_00413920 sets it to 1 together with state 10 (jump) and clears it on landing.

specs.semantics:
Server-to-client counterpart of C2S 0x0D: it syncs another entity's input and action state.

After the entity is found, the handler:
- Sets entity+0x8E4 = 1 (it is 0 only for 0x9E) and entity+0x8D7 = 1.
- Mallocs and zeroes a 0x58-byte node and sets node[0] = 0x3DE (990).
- Decodes the 8 bits into the node, zeroes node+0x30/+0x38/+0x08/+0x04, then reads the target, the optional u8 and the optional position block.

Only 0x2A then does these steps:
- Frees every pending node in the entity's move queue (entity+0x1350; head at +0x1354) and sets entity+0xE48 (hold timer) = 0.
- Sets node[0] = 960, or 0 if it was 30 or less.
- If target_uid == local uid, clears the action fields as described above and sets node[0] to 960 minus max(entity+0xDAC, action_time), clamped at 0.

The node is then appended to the queue with FUN_00459df0.

FUN_00412100 consumes the queue each tick, only for entities with state byte +0x98 > 2 whose uid != local uid:
- node[0] is the longest time (in 30 ms steps) the node waits.
- The node applies at once if the entity is idle (904 == 8, 8B3 == 8, 8B4/8B5/8B6 == 0, 950 == 0, 94C == 0).
- Applying it copies the node into entity 8B3/8B4/8B5/8B6/94C/950/D80/958/8FF/8D0 and D78/1328/1330/8DB/8E8/1338/1340/8D4/8E7. The EN 0x2A leaves all of those except the decoded bits, target and 8FF at 0.
specs.trigger: Send to the other players on the same map when a player's C2S 0x0D arrives. This is the correct relay: echoing 0x0D is known to desync. Use 0x2A for an authoritative state (it flushes the queue and carries target and position); use 0x9F/0x9E for buffered updates.
specs.expected_response: none LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#26/#27/#28): 0x2A applies within one sample (<17 ms measured) because it flushes the pending queue and sets +0xE48 = 0, so it is the only "apply now" relay. 0x9E / 0x9F / 0x1B all append BEHIND the pending nodes (0x9E measured 750 ms, 0x9F 1.81 s, 0x1B stop 1.08 s). Use 0x2A for authoritative keyframes and stops, 0x1B for the streamed relay.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- An unknown uid or uid 0 is silently ignored and nothing more is read.
- NEVER send it with mover_uid == the receiver's own uid. The local entity would be found, its position overwritten (a teleport), and nodes queued for the local uid are never consumed (FUN_00412100 skips the local uid), so memory leaks.
- The position block depends on client-only state (mover state 0x10 = dead) and on target_uid == receiver uid. Nothing is read after it, so always appending the 17 bytes should be harmless because trailing bytes are ignored. Omitting it is only safe when target_uid == receiver uid.
- A nonzero reaction nibble (bits 16-19) snaps the remote entity to (0,0) when the node is consumed, because the node x/y at +0x10/+0x18 stay 0.
- Needs a valid scene (this+0x4CC), so send it in-world only.
- Bits 22-31 of lo and 12-31 of hi are ignored. Live C2S captures carry stale garbage there.

locations.role: entity lookup by uid (fastcall EDX=uid, stack=scene)
opcode==0x2A branch: target, optional u8, position block, queue flush
append node to entity move queue +0x1350
per-tick queue consumer that applies node fields to the entity
C2S 0x0D packer that builds the same 8-byte bitfield at scene+0xEF8

specs.references:
- Bit mapping matches the C2S 0x0D packer FUN_0042c940 exactly: 8B3 in bits 0-1, 8B4 in 2-4, 8B5 in 5-8, 8B6 in 9-11, 94C in 12-15, 950 in 16-19, 8D0 in 20-21, 958 in hi bits 0-11.
- Live C2S 0x0D captures decode consistently: walking bits_lo 0x53400200 gives 8B6 = 1; jumping 0x7240000C gives 8B4 = 3; bits_hi & 0xFFF = 0 in both.
- KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc/Windslayers_Full_Packet.c, case 0x2A/0x9E/0x9F) has the same skeleton but a DIFFERENT layout. It adds a u16 before the target uid and a u16 after it, uses wider bitfields (action at bits 14-17, facing at 22-23), adds action 14 to the u8 condition, and uses a state check of 23. Do not port the KR layout.
- windslayer_server.py has no builder. The project memory confirms that echoing 0x0D broke the cipher.
open_questions: Which opcode the original server chose for normal walking versus actions (0x2A, 0x9F or 0x9E). The client semantics suggest 0x2A for authoritative/action states and 0x9F/0x9E for buffered input changes.
C2S 0x0D carries no x/y unless the reaction state is nonzero, so it is unclear where the original server got pos_x/pos_y for 0x2A (server-side simulation, or the last known spawn/position).
Exact meaning of entity bytes 8B5/8B6 and of the 12-bit action_time value.
Whether the (0,0) snap for a nonzero reaction nibble is real in practice or is masked by other state (not verified at runtime).
blind_open_questions: Exact gameplay meaning of 0x2A vs 0x1B. The hit/knockback reading is inferred from the position override and the special case when source == local; the handler itself has no strings.
Meaning of action nibble values 9/10 (which carry action_extra) and of the w1 12-bit parameter (+0x958).
Fireway GetDataFromPacket behaviour when reading past len (throw, clamp or garbage) is not visible in this binary.

spec_errata.old: relative timing of 0x2A vs 0x9E/0x9F/0x1B undocumented
spec_errata.new: 0x2A is instant (queue flush); the others queue behind pending nodes

fields.meaning: current arena team: 0=spectator/none, 1=blue, 2=red ("You are in blue/red team", FUN_00442EE0). Name colors: 1=0xFF5D9DFF, 2=0xFFFF5D5D

fields.meaning: team subscribed for the next round: 0=spectator, 1=blue, 2=red, 3=leave arena (FUN_00442EE0 messages)

fields.meaning: arena kill count (the attacker's +0x14ED is incremented at 0x419E0E)

fields.name: arena_deaths

fields.name: arena_score

specs.length: 1 + sum over players of (320 + 6*buff_count + 4*(number of buffs with id in 0x0A31..0x0A3B) + 2*skill_count). One player with no buffs and no skills = 321 bytes
specs.semantics: The server sends a list of arena players. For each entry the client allocates a new 0x15F0 entity, zeroes it and sets state +0x98=3. It then reads the fields above and, for each buff, calls FUN_00424E20 (buff into a slot; caster uid = own uid). After reading the skill list it calls RegisterLocalPlayer(entity, scene): the entity joins the scene list, and if uid==scene+0x220 it becomes the local player. The team/K/D/score tail is read AFTER registration (RegisterLocalPlayer zeroes those fields, so these values win). The client then sets +0x98 to 3 (in a team) or 1 (spectator), and sets cur HP +0x9C = max HP +0x110C and cur MP +0xA0 = max MP +0x1110, so every entry spawns at full HP/MP computed on the client. There are no position fields: +0x11F8/+0x1288 stay 0. For opcode 0x2B nothing else happens: no scene-state change and no HUD refresh.
specs.trigger: Probably sent to add or sync arena match participants while the client is already in the arena scene (e.g. players joining mid-match), when no HUD/scene transition is wanted. Compare 0x2E (full roster plus transition), 0x2C (add ONE arena player, no count, no K/D/score, handler 0x4503E1) and 0x2D (remove arena player by u32 uid).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- The handler does NOT dedupe uids or clear existing entities. Every entry allocates and appends a new entity, so re-sending a uid that is already present probably creates a duplicate entity.
- skill_count is not bounds-checked: more than 30 overwrites entity fields past +0x2D6 (up to +0x498 at 255).
- More than 21 buffs, or unknown buff ids, are dropped by FUN_00424E20, but their bytes are still consumed.
- An entry whose uid equals the logged-in uid (scene+0x220) replaces the local-player pointer scene+0x970/+0xEE8.
- The name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes.
- Allocation failure would memset NULL (crash), which is not realistic.
- No length checks beyond Fireway's GetDataFromPacket bounds, so a short packet leaves the remaining fields zeroed and desyncs the per-player loop.
LIVE: creates the spectator/roster entity (score, KO, Down shown) but does NOT refresh the roster list window until the next packet that rebuilds it.
specs.references:
- **Agrees:** KR Hex-Rays case 0x2B/0x2E (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c:6192) has the same tail: team byte, state=2*(team!=0)+1, next_team, kills, deaths, u32 score. The KR body is otherwise different: 0x2AD8 struct, 17 appearance parts, 15 equip, 10x3 cash.
- **PySlayer:** opcode_0x2E.py targets that KR layout (and actually writes opcode byte 0x2B), so it is NOT usable for EN.
- **Our server:** its 0x07 builder shares the prefix (name, uid, i32 +0x15D8, u16 +0x12, job1/job2/level/+0x9A/+0x113, 14 appearance, 4 stats, 16x7 equip, 9 words, then counts), which agrees. The EN 0x05 handler is structurally identical up to the tail.
- **Memory notes are wrong in two places:**
  - protocol.md/reference_opcode_atlas.md say the 0x2B handler is 0x4503E1, or that it 'calls 0x4503E1 for the alive-flag write'. 0x4503E1 is the S2C 0x2C handler; block 0x44F762 ends at 0x44FD03 and never reaches it.
  - project_local_player_spawn.md says the registration gate needs alive==4. The asm shows both the ==4 path and the else/switch path reach the uid compare at 0x42219C (only scene+0xF24==0 and uid==scene+0x220 are required).
- **Our server's stale builders:** `_build_enter_world_response` (claims the 0x4503E1 layout, has a u32 flags field instead of bool, extra hp/mp words, no buff/skill lists, 1 trailing byte, pads to 2000) and `_build_pyslayer_enter_world` (KR layout) do not match and are never called.
open_questions: Exact server-side use of 0x2B vs 0x2E: which arena events send which? Semantics are inferred from the arena UI code; no capture exists.
Meaning of the u16 at +0x12 (status_12), the bool at +0x113 (gender?) and the 9-word array at +0x15C.
Unit of buff_remaining (ms is likely from the 60000 default, not verified), and what the ids 0x0A31..0x0A3B that carry 2 extra params are.
Whether sending a uid that already exists in the scene list causes a visible duplicate or is cleaned up elsewhere (e.g. by the 0x2F arena stage load); not traced.
Arena positions: no coordinates are sent. Where arena spawn positions come from (probably movement/sync packets or map spawn points) is not established.

specs.semantics: Single-player spawn for an arena/PvP game room (the arena counterpart of 0x05). Allocates a new 0x15F0-byte entity (operator new + FUN_00444390 ctor), memsets it, sets state byte +0x98=3, then parses the fields above. After the skill list it calls RegisterLocalPlayer(entity, scene) which inserts it into the scene entity list, stamps +0x88/+0x95C with scene clock, computes derived stats (max HP +0x110C / max MP +0x1110) and, if uid==scene+0x220, makes it the local player (scene+0x970 and camera target scene+0xee8). Then reads team (+0x14EB) and overwrites state +0x98 to 3 (playing) or 1 (spectator), reads next_team (+0x14EC), sets cur HP +0x9C = max HP +0x110C and cur MP +0xA0 = +0x1110 (spawns at full HP/MP; no HP on the wire). Finally FUN_00442ee0 (if arena window 0x47E is open: shows 'You are in blue/red team / You subscribed to ...' text for the LOCAL player and team icons 0x7B-0x7D) and FUN_00443280 (rebuilds blue/red roster lists sorted by +0x14F0 score, counts by next_team, prints 'System will balance number of each team members next round.' if counts differ by >1). No reply is sent.
specs.trigger: Server sends to everyone in an arena game room when a player enters that room (client is in arena scene mode 6, set by the 0x2B/0x2E arena player list). Can also spawn the local player's own arena avatar if uid == own uid.
specs.expected_response: none (no Send in block or callees)
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate on scene mode: the entity is created even outside the arena. No duplicate-uid check - sending twice for the same uid creates a second (ghost) entity. skill_count must be <= 30; larger values overwrite entity fields past +0x2D6 (up to +0x498 for 255). Unlike 0x05/0x07 there is no buff loop and no conditional bool after gm_flag; unlike 0x2B/0x2E there are no +0x14ED/+0x14EE/+0x14F0 fields. UI refresh only happens if window 0x47E exists. If fields are short, behaviour of Fireway bounds check is unverified (fields likely stay zero).
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays (PySlayer doc) case 0x2C also allocates an entity and computes state = 2*(team!=0)+1 from a team byte followed by a next-team byte - same semantics, different KR layout. Field order matches the EN 0x05/0x07 per-player block up to the skill list, minus the marriage/GM-hidden conditionals and minus the buff loop. Memory note reference_opcode_atlas says '0x2B calls 0x4503E1 for the alive-flag write' - wrong: 0x4503E1 is the S2C 0x2C handler; 0x2B/0x2E share 0x44F762. windslayer_server.py (~line 798) comment says a 0x2C(map_id=1) experiment went through 0x4507EE->0x4305B0 - that path is actually S2C 0x2D; a 4-byte 0x2C would have created a zero-filled arena entity. Server only consumes C2S 0x2C (room list open), which is a different message.
open_questions: Exact meaning of unk_113 (bool at +0x113) - colour/appearance variant used by FUN_004270f0.
extra_item_id slots 16..24 (+0x15C) assumed cash/costume slots; not verified.
stat_* names follow PySlayer KR order (STR/DEX/INT/TOL); EN UI labels not confirmed.
Whether RegisterLocalPlayer's derived max HP (+0x110C) is sane for a remote arena entity when equipment tables lack the item ids.
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of unk_0012, unk_0113 and the 9 u16 at +0x15C (names are inferred).
stat_str/dex/int/tol names come from PySlayer KR ordering, not verified in EN code.
Whether Fireway GetDataFromPacket bounds-checks against len (short packets) is not visible in the client.

specs.length: Identical to 0x2B: 1 + sum over players of (320 + 6*buff_count + 4*(buffs with id in 0x0A31..0x0A3B) + 2*skill_count); 321 bytes for one bare player
specs.semantics: The wire format and per-player processing are byte-for-byte the same as 0x2B: allocate an entity, apply buffs, RegisterLocalPlayer, then team/K/D/score, state 3 or 1, full HP/MP. After the loop, including when player_count is 0, opcode 0x2E also does the arena scene transition and HUD refresh. It calls FUN_004400C0 with EDI=6, which sets scene+0xF00=6: the same in-game state the 0x07 spawn path sets, and it closes a UI when the previous state was 5. It clears game_state+0x1534 and refreshes the arena scoreboard team/subscription text (only if UI window 0x47E exists) and its score sort. It then refreshes the local HP/MP bar text, points the camera at the local player (or the spectator camera when the local player's team is 0), and refreshes the stat panel, skill/quickslot icons and equipment counters. The existing server comment is correct: only 0x2E, not 0x2B, triggers these transition helpers.
specs.trigger: Send when the client enters an arena/battle match: after the arena stage load (S2C 0x2F, which reads the mode byte scene+0xF70 and loads stage%02u_%02u.hmi), with the full participant list including the receiving player (uid == its login uid). Use 0x2B for later roster additions that need no transition, 0x2C for a single join, and 0x2D for a leave. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C1, pvp_arena#27/#28): 0x2E is step 2 of the MANDATORY room-enter sequence 0x2F -> 0x2E. Until it arrives the client stays on the loading overlay (measured 17 s), so it must follow every 0x2F, carrying the receiving player in the roster.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- Same parse hazards as 0x2B: no uid dedupe (every entry is a new entity), skill_count > 30 overflows entity+0x29A, buffs beyond 21 or with unknown ids are dropped but their bytes are consumed, and names need a NUL within 17 bytes.
- HUD helpers null-check scene+0x970. If the local player is not in the roster (or its uid does not match scene+0x220), the local-player pointer is left as it was: stale or NULL. The team text, HP/MP and stat panel then reflect the old entity or are skipped.
- FUN_00442EE0/FUN_00443280 only act when the arena scoreboard window (UI id 0x47E) exists in g_ui_root+0x5C0.
- The team byte decides spectator camera vs following the local player, and state 1 (spectator) vs 3.
- No positions are sent (entities sit at 0,0 until movement/sync).
- Using 0x2E outside the arena flow (e.g. as a field enter-world reply) was tried in earlier server iterations and did not produce a working field spawn: the client never loaded a map. Field entry is 0x03+0x07.
specs.references:
- **Server comment:** the note that 0x2B/0x2E share handler 0x44F762 and only 0x2E runs the transition helpers matches the asm at 0x44FCB1.
- **Server builders:** `_build_map_enter_packet` is labeled 'Opcode 0x2E (Map/Channel Enter)', but its 47-byte layout (u8 f36, u8 f37, u16, char[16] f38, u16 f48, 5x u8 f5b..f5f, u8 f72, f71, f70, char[17] f4a) is actually S2C 0x2F's handler (0x44FD08 region / decomp line 1707). `_build_enter_world_response` and `_build_pyslayer_enter_world` do not match this grammar. None of the three is called.
- **PySlayer:** opcode_0x2E.py is the KR layout and is incompatible. The KR Hex-Rays tail (team, state 2*(team!=0)+1, next_team, kills, deaths, score) agrees.
- **Memory notes:** the reference_opcode_atlas/protocol.md claim that 0x4503E1 handles 0x2B is wrong: 0x4503E1 is S2C 0x2C (single arena player add, same prefix, tail is only team + next_team).
open_questions: Exact arena flow order on the real server (0x2F, then 0x2E, then 0x2B/0x2C/0x2D/0x37 score updates) is inferred from the client, not from captures.
Whether the client clears old scene entities before 0x2E (e.g. in the 0x2F stage load) or the server must avoid re-sending existing uids.
Meanings of status_12, appearance_flag_113 and unk_15c, and the unit of buff_remaining (as for 0x2B).
What game_state+0x1534 (cleared here and at the end of the 0x07 path) controls.
blind_open_questions: Original server sequencing (0x2F -> 0x2E -> 0x2B?) is inferred from arena strings and fields, not observed
Meaning of unk_flag_12, rank, gender_flag, extra_15c[9]; buff_duration unit
Whether the local-player entity created here (state 1/3, +0x11DC NULL) renders and handles input correctly, or whether a follow-up spawn/position packet is required (position stays 0,0)
Exact behavior of 0x441C20(1), 0x443AC0 and 0x442510 HUD refresh (not traced; no packet reads)

specs.name: RoomGameEnter (arena / play-room / battlefield map load)

locations.role: FUN_00407190 map load; on failure logs 'Could not load MAP. (%s)'
FUN_00422f40: frees every scene entity and clears scene+0x970 (local player ptr)
later use: UDP SendTo(scene+0xF38 ip, room_no+10000) by non-host peers
later use: current_round(F5B) compared to round_count(F36) by host round logic
later use: F37*60 = round time limit in seconds

specs.grammar:
u8 round_count
u8 round_time_min
u16 map_id
str[16] host_ip
u16 room_no
u8 current_round
u8 blue_round_wins
u8 blue_round_losses
u8 red_round_wins
u8 red_round_losses
u8 red_score
u8 blue_score
u8 room_mode
str[17] room_title

fields.name: round_count
fields.meaning: Rounds per game. The host's round logic compares current_round (F5B) with this and resets round/win counters when they match.

fields.name: round_time_min
fields.meaning: Round time limit in minutes. FUN_00458640 does F37*60 minus elapsed seconds for the countdown.

fields.name: map_id
fields.meaning: Arena map code. Loads ./hs/stage%02u_%02u.hmi with (map_id/100, map_id%100). Kept only in a stack local.

fields.name: host_ip
fields.meaning: IP string of the room host, e.g. "127.0.0.1", NUL-padded. Non-host peers later send UDP to this IP on port room_no+10000 (FUN_00423260 @0x4236E8).

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: Room number. Shown as " Room%u" (format "%s%u") in window 0x47E control 0x80. Also the base of the P2P UDP port (room_no+10000) and sent in host packets 0x93/0x95.

fields.name: current_round
fields.meaning: Current round number, 1-based (the host resets it to 1)

fields.name: blue_round_wins
fields.meaning: Rounds won by blue (team 1). Shown as Blue in '%uRound ended. [Blue%d:%dRed]'. On a battlefield, 3 wins makes the final winner.

fields.name: blue_round_losses
fields.meaning: Goes up whenever red wins a round, so it is probably blue's round losses

fields.name: red_round_wins
fields.meaning: Rounds won by red (team 2)

fields.name: red_round_losses
fields.meaning: Goes up whenever blue wins a round, so it is probably red's round losses

fields.name: red_score
fields.meaning: Red team score in the current round (F72 > F71 means red wins). Read BEFORE blue_score.

fields.name: blue_score
fields.meaning: Blue team score in the current round

fields.name: room_mode
fields.meaning: Room type. 0-3 = arena ("Will you exit the arena?"), 4 = play room ("Would you exit from play room?"), 5 or more = battlefield ("You subscribed to leave the battle field?"). The client derives scene+0xF6C (team-mode flag) = 1 when the mode is 2, 3 or 5, otherwise 0.

fields.name: room_title
fields.meaning: Room title, 16 chars plus NUL. Shown in window 0x47E control 0x81.

specs.semantics:
Moves the client into a PvP room game and loads its map. Before reading, the client sets game_state+0x468=0xA5A, scene+0xF08=0, scene+0xF0C=game_state+0x364 (current tick), and scene+0xF73 and +0xF74 (per-team alive counters) = 0. It closes UI windows 0x16, 0x2A, 0x14, 0x478 (room list), 0x17B and 0x236, plus any other open modal. It then reads the 14 fields straight into the scene room block at +0xF36..+0xF74, except map_id, which stays in a stack local.

Next it fills window 0x47E: control 0x80 gets " Room<room_no>" and control 0x81 gets room_title. It fades out (FUN_0043d560: 16 x Sleep(40) unless game_state+0x357 is set), unloads the current map and loads stage<map_id/100>_<map_id%100>.hmi. FUN_0042c450 resets HUD and round state (scene+0x24C = scene+0xF1C, F04 = 0, and so on).

It then sets up the exit-confirmation dialog for the mode:
- mode 4 (play room): window 0x4B text and window 0x47A shown.
- mode <= 3 (arena): windows 0x4D, 0x480 and 0x47E shown, arena exit text.
- mode >= 5 (battlefield): battlefield text, controls 0x7B-0x7D greyed.
Control 0x7E is enabled in every mode.

The map name (map+0x178, cut to 20 chars plus "...") is written to window 4 ctrl 2 and window 0x17 ctrl 2. Finally the client frees every entity in the scene list, including the local player (scene+0x970 = NULL). FUN_00443840 then has nothing to refresh. FUN_00444100 spawns the static map objects and FUN_004400c0 sets scene+0xF00 = 7. This is the same tail as the 0x08 ChangeMap handler, so a server must follow 0x2F with the usual spawn sequence (0x07 local player, HP/MP, other entities).
specs.trigger: Server sends it when a room game starts or when a player joins a running arena, play-room or battlefield game. That comes after room create or join: C2S 0x1B (join: u16 room_no, u8 mode) or the 0x2B create path.
specs.expected_response: The handler sends nothing. Afterwards the arena runs peer-to-peer: non-host clients send UDP packets to host_ip:(room_no+10000) (FUN_00423260), and the host (scene+0xF24 != 0) sends 0x93/0x95 round packets through its CSNSockMan. The captured C2S 0x2F/0x63 zero-byte packets are sent after map loads and are not replies to this packet. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C1, pvp_arena#27/#28): the room map load STALLS at ~99% for as long as it takes S2C 0x2E to arrive (17 s observed). The enter sequence is 0x2F -> 0x2E (roster that includes the receiving player) -> optional 0x2B/0x2C/0x35/0x37; 0x2E is a REQUIRED part of the enter sequence, not an optional roster update. For a field map use 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07 instead.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- No state gate: all 47 bytes are always read.
- DESTRUCTIVE: tears down the world. All scene entities are freed and the local-player pointer is cleared, so the player is invisible or uncontrollable until the server re-sends 0x07 and related packets.
- Never echo the client's 0-byte C2S 0x2F back as S2C 0x2F: the handler would read 47 bytes of garbage, load a random map and open the exit dialogs (this matches the memory note "0x2F must NOT be echoed").
- map_id must name an existing ./hs/stageAA_BB.hmi. On failure the client only logs 'Could not load MAP.' and continues with no map.
- host_ip must be NUL-terminated within 16 bytes, because it becomes the UDP SendTo target.
- room_title must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (it becomes UI text).
- The fade blocks the UI thread about 640 ms.
- If scene+0xF00 was 5 before, FUN_004400c0 also calls FUN_00446300(0x15,0,1,0,1) and sets ui_root+0x5A4=1.
HAZARD (live, pvp_arena#27): after 0x2F the client sits on the loading overlay with 0 entities until 0x2E (or a full 0x08/0x03/0x07 field sequence) arrives. RECOVERY: send 0x2E; otherwise only a restart.
specs.references:
- Our server never sends S2C 0x2F. It only logs and ignores C2S 0x2F ('arena query').
- PySlayer opcode_0x2F.py (newer KR build) sends 31 bytes: u8,u8,u16,str16,u16('Mapcode'),9 x u8. The EN 2008 layout differs after the second u16: 8 x u8 then str[17] room_title, 47 bytes total.
- In EN the FIRST u16 (before the IP) is the map code used for the .hmi path, and the second u16 is the room number/port base. PySlayer sets both to 201, so its comment cannot separate them.
- Consistent with the memory note that 0x2F must not be echoed.
open_questions: F5D/F5F are named blue_round_losses/red_round_losses only from their increment pattern in FUN_00428090 (red win: F5E++ and F5D++; blue win: F5C++ and F5F++). No UI string shows them directly.
The exact meanings of room_mode 0 vs 1 and 2 vs 3 (individual vs team arena variants) are not tied to UI strings. The only evidence is the team flag for 2, 3 and 5.
round_time_min is inferred from F37*60 minus (scene+0xEEC & 0x1FF), treating 0xEEC as an elapsed-seconds counter.
Whether a server-driven arena needs the P2P host (host_ip / room_no+10000 UDP) to be emulated is outside this handler.
blind_open_questions: room_title (scene+0xF4A, 17 bytes): room title or room host's character name? Only use seen: UI control 0x81 of window 0x47E.
f5d/f5f are inferred from increments (red win adds to f5d, blue win adds to f5f) as losses, and f71/f72 as in-round team points; exact UI meaning not confirmed.
Exact room_type numbering (0..3 arena sub-modes, 4 play room, 5 battlefield, 6+?) is not confirmed beyond the dialog branches.
Which C2S (room Start button?) should trigger this packet was not traced.
Fireway GetDataFromPacket behaviour on a short packet (leave target unchanged vs zero) is not visible in the client.
Whether udp_room_ip:10000+room_no is a server-side UDP relay or the room host peer is not proven; C2S 0x2B carries the client's own IP and UDP port 42907, which suggests P2P plus a relay.

spec_errata.new: 0x2E is a required step of the 0x2F enter sequence
