spec_errata.new: stall + recovery documented

specs.name: ArenaCreateFailed_TooManyChannels
specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics:
The payload is empty and nothing is read. The handler calls FUN_00489da0(g_ui_root, text, 3, 3, 0, 0) with text 0x6F74A0: "The number of the arena channels are 
excessive. No more arena can be created.
Please enter to an existing arena, 
or try again in a few minutes."

The message goes into the generic message box (window 0x16). That same box shows "Waiting for the server to response." after a create/join request, so this replaces that text and enables the dismiss button (5th argument 0 instead of 3).
specs.trigger: Reply to an arena room create request, C2S 0x18 (str[17] name, u8, u8, bytes[5] password, u16 mode/map, u8 room_type, sent from window 0x2B), when the server refuses because the arena channel limit is reached.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Purely UI. It needs the UI root and message box window 0x16 to be loaded, which is always the case in-game.
specs.references: The text is in strings.tsv at 0x6F74A0. Not in the KR Hex-Rays extract or in PySlayer's Python (the server_packets import is guarded by try, with no file). Not implemented in windslayer_server.py.
open_questions: Confirm that C2S 0x18 from window 0x2B is the arena create request this answers. It is inferred from FUN_00446300 around 0x449xxx.
blind_open_questions: Which C2S opcode creates an arena room (not traced in this batch).

specs.name: RoomListAddEntry (arena room, or play room if type 4)
specs.grammar:
str[17] room_name
u16 room_no
u8 max_players
u8 cur_players
u8 room_level
u8 room_type
bool has_password

fields.name: room_name
fields.dest_or_source: room+0x00 (a new 0x24-byte struct from malloc, not zeroed)
fields.meaning: room title, NUL-padded. The row format is "%03d %s(%02d/%02d) ..."

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: Room number shown as %03d. The join request C2S 0x1A sends u16 room_no + u8 room_type. It is also copied to scene+0xF48 on join.

fields.name: max_players
fields.meaning: Room capacity: the second number in the row's "(%02d/%02d)". The row printf passes +0x15 first, then +0x14.

fields.name: cur_players
fields.meaning: current player count (first number in the row's "(%02d/%02d)")

fields.name: room_level
fields.meaning: Room level for type 0 rooms, shown as "Lv.%d". The join gate and the enterable counter require local level (entity+0x99) to be between room_level-2 and room_level+1 (the join message clamps to 1..99).

fields.name: room_type
fields.dest_or_source: room+0x17. The handler also sets room+0x18 = 1 for types 1-3 (else 0) and room+0x1C = 1 for types 2-3 (else 0; left unset for type 1).
fields.meaning: 0 = level-restricted "Lv.N" arena room, 1 = "ULMT", 2 = "STD", 3 = "Novice" (novice-only; icon sprite 0x11B), 4 = Play&Chat room (goes to the P-key list instead). Copied to scene+0xF70 on join.

fields.name: has_password
fields.meaning: Room is locked (draws lock sprite 0x7D). On join, if set, the client opens password window 0x4A instead of sending C2S 0x1A.

specs.semantics:
Adds ONE room record. There is no dedupe by room_no: sending the same room twice makes duplicate rows.

If room_type != 4 (arena list, F key, window 0x2A):
1. The record is pushed to the front of the arena room list this+0x440 (head +0x444, count +0x44C).
2. The client reads the current filter label (control 0x15 of window 0x2A) and compares it with the tab labels. It adds the row to window 0x2A (FUN_00489a80) when:
   - the filter is tab 0x16 (All), or
   - the filter is tab 0x17 and room+0x18 == 0 (type 0), or
   - the filter is tab 0x18 and type == 1, or
   - the filter is tab 0x19 and type == 2, or
   - the filter is tab 0x1A and type == 3.
3. It recounts rooms the local player can enter (FUN_00444770). A novice (entity+0x110 == 0) can enter only type 3. Anyone else can enter types other than 3 when room+0x18 is set or their level is within [lvl-2, lvl+1].
4. It writes "%u/%u" (enterable/total) to control 0x14 of window 0x2A and refreshes the list (FUN_00489c50).

If room_type == 4 (Play&Chat room list, P key, window 0x478):
- The record is stored in list this+0x450 (count +0x45C) and added to window 0x478 ONLY IF window 0x478 is the active window (g_ui_root+0x2C == 0x478). Otherwise it is dropped and the struct leaks.
- The client then writes "%u" (count +0x45C) to control 0x14 of window 0x478 and refreshes.
specs.trigger: When a new arena or play room is created (or appears) while players have the room list open: after C2S 0x2C (F-key ARENA list open) or C2S 0x74 (P-key Play&Chat list open). For a full refresh use S2C 0x33 (clears the arena list) / 0x32 (bulk list with the same 24-byte record).
specs.expected_response: none. The user may then join with C2S 0x1A (u16 room_no, u8 room_type), or password window 0x4A if has_password.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- The type != 4 path dereferences the local player scene+0x970 inside FUN_00444770 (reads +0x110/+0x99) for every room in the list. Sending it before the local player exists crashes, so send in-world only.
- The label compares use FUN_0048a050 results without null checks. If window 0x2A or its controls 0x15-0x1A are not loaded, it dereferences null.
- Type 4 entries are silently dropped (and leaked) unless window 0x478 is currently active.
- There is no dedupe or update-by-room_no, so clear with 0x33 before re-sending a list.
- room+0x1C is left uninitialized for type 1, and room+0x21..0x23 are never set. Window 0x478's filter 0x17 reads room+0x22 (== 0x26AF), which is garbage for 0x31-created play rooms.

locations.role: can-local-player-enter check used for the enterable/total counter
add row to UI list window
row renderer: "%03d %s(%02d/%02d) Lv.%d" / ULMT / STD / Novice
join path: C2S 0x1A u16 room_no + u8 room_type, or password window 0x4A

specs.references:
- S2C 0x32 per-entry reads (0x4556A3-0x45576E) use the identical 24-byte record: str[17], u16, u8 x4, bool.
- The S2C 0x33 handler (0x4555E6) clears list this+0x440, resets counter text to "0/0" and has no JMP at its end, so it falls through into the 0x32 handler.
- Window ids are confirmed by FUN_00446300: window 0x2A open sends C2S 0x2C (ARENA, F key) and window 0x478 open sends C2S 0x74 (Play&Chat, P key), matching live captures.
- Our server's _handle_room_query consumes 0x2C without replying. No 0x31 builder exists in windslayer_server.py or PySlayer's Python.
open_questions: Order of max_players versus cur_players. It is inferred from the display "(+0x15/+0x14)", read as (current/max), with no capacity check found to confirm it.
The meaning of room+0x1C (set for types 2 and 3) is not traced.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of local player entity +0x110 (novice/graduated flag) used by the joinable check.
Whether retail sent 0x31 only to clients in the lobby/list windows or to all players.

specs.name: ArenaRoomListAppend

locations.role: adds the row to window 0x2A's UI list

specs.grammar:
u8 room_count
repeat(room_count) {
  str[17] room_name
  u16 room_no
  u8 max_players
  u8 cur_players
  u8 room_level
  u8 room_type
  bool has_password
}

fields.name: room_count
fields.meaning: rows in this packet

fields.name: room_name
fields.meaning: room title (NUL-terminate within 17 bytes)

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: room number (%03d); the key for joins and for 0x34 result 4

fields.name: max_players
fields.meaning: capacity

fields.name: cur_players
fields.meaning: current occupants

fields.name: room_level
fields.meaning: level bracket for type 0 rooms (player level must be in [lvl-2, lvl+1])

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: 0=Lv bracket, 1=ULMT, 2=STD, 3=Novice-only, 4=play room (dropped here)

fields.name: has_password
fields.meaning: locked room (lock icon; joining asks for a password)

specs.semantics: Appends rooms to the existing ARENA room list without clearing it. Rows are parsed, stored, sorted and filtered exactly as described for 0x33: rooms the player can enter go to the head, the others to the tail; the UI row is added only if it passes the current filter combobox; type 4 is dropped. At the end, label control 0x14 of window 0x2A is set to '%u/%u' (enterable/total over the whole list at game+0x440) and FUN_00489c50(0x2A,1) runs. The client does not remove duplicates, so re-sending a room_no creates a second row.
specs.trigger: Server push while the arena list is open, e.g. a newly created room or a continuation after 0x33. No client request maps to it directly.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same null-deref hazard as 0x33: FUN_00444770 reads [[game+0x4CC]+0x970]+0x110 with no null check, once per row and once per stored room. Duplicates are not detected. Type-4 rows leak.
specs.references: Layout identical to PySlayer opcode_0x33. PySlayer has an opcode_0x32 module (not inspected in detail). Our server does not send 0x32.
open_questions: Exact server-side use case (new-room push vs pagination) is not visible in the client
blind_open_questions: When exactly the original server used 0x32 vs 0x33 (paging vs incremental add)

specs.name: ArenaRoomListReset

locations.role: handler block (prologue: clears the list, then falls through into the 0x32 parser at 0x45565E; there is no jmp)
per-room check: can the local player enter this room
row renderer for window 0x2A ('%03d %s(%02d/%02d) Lv.%d' / '... %s' with ULMT/STD/Novice)
C2S 0x2C send when window 0x2A (ARENA list) opens; this is the request that 0x33 answers

specs.grammar:
u8 room_count
repeat(room_count) {
  str[17] room_name
  u16 room_no
  u8 max_players
  u8 cur_players
  u8 room_level
  u8 room_type
  bool has_password
}

fields.name: room_count
fields.meaning: number of rows in this packet (0..255). The loop counter is compared with movzx, so the count is unsigned.

fields.name: room_name
fields.meaning: room title. Exactly 17 bytes are copied and the client adds no terminator, so send at most 16 chars plus a NUL. Printed with %s.

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: room number: shown as %03d, sent back in C2S 0x1A/0x1C, and compared with the requested room number [game+0x4CC]+0xF48 in 0x34 result 4. Join-by-number only accepts 1..128.

fields.name: max_players
fields.meaning: room capacity, the second number of '(cur/max)'. Result 4 of 0x34 copies it into cur_players.

fields.name: cur_players
fields.meaning: current occupants, the first number of '(cur/max)'

fields.name: room_level
fields.meaning: level bracket of a type-0 room. Shown as 'Lv.%d'. The local player (level byte at player+0x99) may enter only if room_level-2 <= level <= room_level+1. The client's join prompt clamps the range to 1..99 ('To enter Lv.%u room, your level must between Lv.%d and Lv.%d.'). Ignored for types 1-3.

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: 0=level-bracket room ('Lv.N'); 1='ULMT'; 2='STD'; 3='Novice' (novice-only room, novice icon sprite 0x11B); 4=play/chat room, which the arena list never stores. Also derives room+0x18 = (type in 1..3) and room+0x1C = (type in 2..3); for type 1, +0x1C is left uninitialized.
fields.dest_or_source: room+0x17 (derived flags at room+0x18 and room+0x1C, set at 0x45572C..0x455750)

fields.name: has_password
fields.meaning: room is locked: draws lock sprite 0x7D (not for Novice rooms). When joining from the list, the client then opens password window 0x4A instead of sending C2S 0x1A.

specs.semantics: Starts a new ARENA room list (window 0x2A). Prologue at 0x4555E6: (1) RemoveHead + free every room in the list at game+0x440 (head +0x444, count +0x44C); (2) if window 0x2A exists, clear its UI rows (FUN_0047d700, no free); (3) set label control 0x14 of window 0x2A to '0/0'; (4) FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1), which clicks message box window 0x16 and dismisses the 'Waiting for the server to response.' popup. It then parses rows exactly like 0x32. Per row: allocate a 0x24-byte room and read the fields. If room_type==4 the row is dropped without being stored or freed (memory leak). Otherwise flag = FUN_00444770(local player, room), meaning the player can enter. Enterable rooms go to the head of the list at game+0x440 (FUN_00459d30), the rest to the tail (FUN_00459df0). The row is added to window 0x2A's UI list (at the head if enterable) only if it passes the current filter: the text of combobox control 0x15 is compared with item controls 0x16=all, 0x17=rooms with +0x18==0 (type 0), 0x18=type 1, 0x19=type 2, 0x1A=type 3. After the loop it counts the enterable rooms in the whole list and sets label 0x14 to sprintf('%u/%u', enterable_count, total_count[game+0x44C]), then FUN_00489c50(0x2A,1) refreshes the scroll. Enterable means: player+0x110==0 (novice, no class change) and type==3; or player+0x110!=0, type!=3, and either type is 1/2 or the level is inside the bracket. Rows the player cannot enter are drawn grey (0xFF999999).
specs.trigger: Send when the player opens the F-key ARENA room list; the client opens window 0x2A itself and sends C2S 0x2C with no payload. Also usable as a full refresh.
specs.gates_and_hazards: CRASH: for every row, and for every stored room in the final count loop, the handler calls FUN_00444770 with ECX=[[game+0x4CC]+0x970] and reads [ECX+0x110] with no null check (the renderer does check it). Sending 0x33 with rooms, or with an already non-empty list, before the local player object exists will access-violate. Send it only in-world. Do not send room_type 4 here (leak, never shown). Name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes, or %s runs into the uninitialized byte +0x11 and room_no. The handler does not open window 0x2A; if the window is not loaded, the UI steps are skipped but data is still stored.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x33.py uses the same byte layout (name17, u16, u8 maxuser, u8 curruser, u8 ??, u8 ??, u8 IsLocked). The two '??' bytes are room_level and room_type; PySlayer sends type 1 (ULMT). PySlayer game_server answers C2S 0x2C code 1 with 0x33. The EN client sends 0x2C with no payload (scout plus live capture), so the code byte PySlayer and our server's _handle_room_query read does not exist in EN. Our server only logs 0x2C and never sends 0x33. Its comment 'answering with 0x33 unprompted opens the arena UI' is not supported by this handler, which never opens a window.
open_questions: Whether dismissing message box 0x16 via FUN_00446300(0x16,0,1,0,1) has side effects when no popup is showing (the server comment says an unprompted 0x33 opened the arena UI)
Use of the derived flag room+0x1C (set for types 2/3) was not traced
Whether the server is expected to split lists above 255 rooms into 0x33 plus 0x32 continuations
blind_open_questions: What the server should send for room_kind values above 4 (the client treats them like kind 0)
Whether an unsolicited 0x33 makes window 0x2a visible (the asm shows no open call, but our server notes claim it does)

specs.name: RoomJoinResult

locations.role: switch on result-1 via jump table 0x4585F4 (8 entries)
C2S 0x1A send (join from arena list: u16 room_no, u8 room_type)
C2S 0x1B join by typed room number (u16 room_no 1..128, u8 type 0 or 4)
C2S 0x1C join with password (u16 [+0xF48], u8 [+0xF70], str[5] password)

specs.grammar:
u8 result
u8 room_type

fields.name: result
fields.meaning:
1=message 'Incorrect password.'; 2='Invalid room #.'; 3=password required: close the wait box and open password window 0x4A (FUN_00489960(0x4A,5) + FUN_00483430(0x4A,4,1)); 4='The room is full
(Please try again in a few minutes.)', and the client finds the row in window 0x2A whose u16 room_no equals the requested [game+0x4CC]+0xF48 and sets cur_players = max_players; 5=accepted: close the wait box and flush the room list (see room_type); 6='Your level is not appropriate.'; 7='Only novice can enter a
[novice-only room].'; 8='A novice can only enter 
[Novice only room].'. 0 or >8: nothing happens.

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: echo of the joined room's type. Read only by result 5: if ==4, the play-room list is flushed (window 0x478 UI rows cleared, label 0x14='0', list at game+0x450 freed); otherwise the arena list is (window 0x2A UI rows cleared, label 0x14='0/0', list at game+0x440 freed). Always present on the wire.

specs.semantics: Server's answer to a room join request (C2S 0x1A / 0x1B / 0x1C, which all show 'Waiting for the server to response.' in message box window 0x16). Both bytes are always read, then the handler switches on result via jump table 0x4585F4 (1->0x455C6A, 2->0x455CA4, 3->0x455CC1, 4->0x455DE6, 5->0x455CF6, 6->0x455C87, 7->0x455E5A, 8->0x455E77). Error results 1,2,4,6,7,8 call FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0), which rewrites the text of the same message box 0x16. Result 3 dismisses the box (FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1)) and opens the password prompt, which later sends C2S 0x1C with the stored room_no/type and the 5-byte password. Result 5 dismisses the box and frees the relevant list data. Actually entering the room is presumably driven by other packets; not traced.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x1A (join a room clicked in the ARENA or Play&Chat list), 0x1B (join by typed room number) or 0x1C (password submit). The client also shows the wait box for C2S 0x18 (create room), so 0x34 may answer that too (unverified). MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x18 / 0x1A / 0x1B / 0x1C. Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.expected_response: After result 3 the client, on user input, sends C2S 0x1C: u16 room_no, u8 room_type, str[5] password
specs.gates_and_hazards: Result 4 always searches window 0x2A (the arena list), even for play rooms. It uses [game+0x4CC]+0xF48, which the client sets on every join attempt. The client checks level/novice rules before sending 0x1A (same strings as results 6-8), so those results matter mainly for 0x1B join by number. Joining by number accepts only 1..128. No crash hazards found (all window lookups are null-checked).
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x34.py ('무투장 입장?', arena enter?) builds a room-LIST payload (count + 24-byte row). That is wrong for EN: the client would read count=1 as result 1 'Incorrect password.' and the name's first byte as room_type. PySlayer's game_server leaves the 0x34 reply to C2S 0x1A commented out. Our server consumes inbound 0x1A as a 'mob query'. In the room context C2S 0x1A is a room join (u16 room_no, u8 room_type); a mob-related C2S 0x1A may exist elsewhere, so check by context. Our server never sends 0x34.
open_questions: Which follow-up S2C packets move the client into the room after result 5
Whether result 5 is also the success reply for C2S 0x18 room creation
Exact meaning of FUN_00489960 mode 5 / FUN_00483430 mode 4 on window 0x4A (assumed: open password input)
blind_open_questions: Confirm that result 5 is the success path and which packets actually move the player into the room afterwards
Exact length and meaning of the password bytes in C2S 0x1C (Add(char*,5) seen at 0x4495E6)

spec_errata.old: the must-reply role was not stated
spec_errata.new: documented as the packet that clears the waiting modal

specs.name: ArenaPlayerTeamUpdate

locations.role: FUN_004189f0(EDX=uid, stack arg=scene): walks scene+0xC list matching entity+0x84; uid 0 returns NULL
JZ 0x455F8D: entity NULL -> both u8 reads skipped, jumps to alive recount
FUN_00428bc0 (ESI=entity): team 0 -> +0x98=1; else if +0x98!=3 refill HP/MP, zero +0x15A0, clear +0xE84 (0x1F8 bytes) and +0x107C (0x90 bytes); then +0x98=3
FUN_00442ee0(game_state): local team/subscription text in window 0x47E (returns if window absent)
FUN_00443280(game_state): arena scoreboard window 0x47E refresh (returns if window absent)
local player scene+0x970 NULL -> break to 0x44D7AD (recount skipped)
FUN_004305b0(game_state,0x27): choose new spectator camera target
zero scene+0xF74/+0xF73 then recount living team members (+0x98==3, team!=0, HP>0)

specs.length: 6 (u32 + u8 + u8); only 4 consumed when the uid is not a scene entity

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Entity uid of the player whose arena team is set; resolved by FUN_004189f0 against scene entity list (+0x84). 0 or unknown -> the two u8 are not read
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x1A4], passed in EDX to FUN_004189f0

fields.name: team
fields.meaning: Current team: 0=spectator, 1=Blue, 2=Red

fields.name: next_team
fields.meaning: Team subscribed for next round: 0=spectator, 1=Blue, 2=Red, 3=leave arena when the round ends (client converts 3 to entity+0x14E9=1 and stores 0)

specs.semantics: Sets a player's current arena team (+0x14EB) and next-round team (+0x14EC). If next_team==3 the client sets the leave flag +0x14E9=1 and stores next_team=0. FUN_00428bc0 applies the state: team 0 -> +0x98=1 (spectator); team!=0 -> if +0x98 was not 3, HP +0x9C=+0x110C, MP +0xA0=+0x1110, +0x15A0=0, buff slots +0xE84 (0x1F8 bytes) and +0x107C (0x90 bytes) zeroed; then +0x98=3. Next it refreshes the local team text ('You are in blue team.', 'You subscribed to enter red team...', 'You subscribed to leave the arena...') and the scoreboard in window 0x47E. If the local player (scene+0x970) is NULL the handler ends here. Otherwise camera follow target scene+0xEE8: if local team!=0 and local+0x15B4!=0x16 -> target=local; else if updated entity team!=0 and (target NULL or target team==0) -> target=entity; else if entity team==0 and entity==target -> FUN_004305b0(game_state,0x27). Finally scene+0xF74 (red alive) and scene+0xF73 (blue alive) are zeroed and recounted over scene entities with +0x98==3, team!=0, HP>0. If the uid is unknown only the u32 is consumed and the handler jumps straight to the recount.
specs.trigger: Server broadcast to arena room members when a player picks/changes team (C2S 0x1D u8 team: 0 spectator, 1 blue, 2 red, 3 leave; 4 also sent at 0x449DDB) or when the server assigns/balances teams.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No map gate in this handler. Unknown uid: 4 bytes consumed, entity untouched, recount still runs. Entity found but local player NULL: break before camera logic and recount. HAZARD: FUN_00428bc0 overwrites +0x98 with 1 or 3 on whatever entity matches, including the local player (normally 4, required by the registration gate); sending it for the local player outside an arena can break local-player state and wipes buffs/refills HP. Leave flag +0x14E9 is never cleared here. UI helpers silently return if window 0x47E is not open.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Analyst A wrote 'u32 uid; if(entity exists){u8 team; u8 next_team} else {stop}', analyst B wrote 'u32 uid; if(entity==null){stop}; u8 team; u8 pending_team'. These are the same wire format in different notation, and both are right: 0x455EA9 reads u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8), 0x455EBD FUN_004189f0 lookup, 0x455EC6 JZ 0x455F8D skips both reads when NULL, 0x455EE2 and 0x455EFF read u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) into entity+0x14EB/+0x14EC, and 0x455F05-0x455F11 convert 3 to leave flag. I used the flat early-exit form. On semantics A is more complete: B implies the recount always runs, but at 0x455F37 a NULL local player (scene+0x970) breaks to 0x44D7AD before the camera logic and recount. That only happens when the entity was found; the NULL-entity path jumps straight to the recount at 0x455F8D. C2S team values checked in FUN_00446300: 0x44B5E3->0x44843D Add(0x1D),Add(1); 0x44B624->0x448461 Add(0x1D),Add(2); 0x44B62B->0x4483EE Add(0x1D),Add(0); 0x449DBF->0x4484AC Add(0x1D),Add(3); 0x449DDB Add(0x1D),Add(4). KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c) has no case 0x35 and PySlayer has no builder. Our server: not implemented.
open_questions: Whether the server ever sends next_team=3 or only echoes the client's C2S 0x1D 3 request; meaning of C2S 0x1D value 4 (0x449DDB, possibly cancel-leave) and how the client would treat next_team=4 if echoed (stored raw).
Meaning of entity+0x15B4 == 0x16 in camera-target logic (treated as not an active combatant).

specs.name: ArenaRoundResult

locations.role: handler entry; [game_state+0x4D8] (CMapControl, also scene+0xF88) +0x70 compared to 1
JNZ 0x44D7AD: not arena map -> break with no reads
'Blue team wins' / 'Red team wins.' / 'Tie!, Restarting the round.'
u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8) reward -> stack [esp+0x114]; added to scene+0x27C and +0x280
FUN_00442c90 record UI ('%u Win/Lose/KO/Down'); recomputes rank scene+0x96C via table 0x6F11D8 and copies it to local entity+0x9A
round advance: if round_result!=0, round_no==scene+0xF36 -> reset F5B=1, F5C..F5F=0; else F5B++
per scene entity: apply next_team (FUN_00428bc0), refill HP/MP, clear buffs
arena-host counterpart computing same fields (cross-check of meanings)

specs.grammar:
if([[game_state+0x4D8]+0x70] != 1) {
  stop
}
u8 round_result
u8 round_no
u8 blue_round_wins
u8 blue_round_losses
u8 red_round_wins
u8 red_round_losses
u32 reward_points
u32 total_downs
u32 total_kos
u32 total_wins
u32 total_losses
specs.length: 26 (6 x u8 + 5 x u32); 0 consumed when not on an arena map

fields.name: round_result
fields.meaning: 1=Blue team wins, 2=Red team wins, other (0)=Tie ('Tie!, Restarting the round.'). 0 also suppresses the final-winner check and the round advance

fields.name: round_no
fields.meaning: Number of the round that just ended (%u in '%uRound ended'); client then increments it, or resets to 1 when it equals max rounds scene+0xF36

fields.name: blue_round_wins
fields.meaning: Rounds won by Blue (Blue%d); >=3 on either side triggers final winner when mode>=5

fields.name: blue_round_losses
fields.meaning: Rounds lost by Blue (host logic increments on red win); not displayed by this handler

fields.name: red_round_wins
fields.meaning: Rounds won by Red (%dRed)

fields.name: red_round_losses
fields.meaning: Rounds lost by Red (host logic increments on blue win); not displayed

fields.name: reward_points
fields.meaning: Local player's round reward. If non-zero: scene+0x27C (reputation) += v, scene+0x280 (Victy) += v; prints '+%uReputation Points, +%uVicty, +%uEXP.' (v three times) and the fame/EXP note
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x114]; added to scene+0x27C and scene+0x280

fields.name: total_downs
fields.meaning: Absolute arena Down count ('%u Down')

fields.name: total_kos
fields.meaning: Absolute arena KO count ('%u KO')

fields.name: total_wins
fields.meaning: Absolute arena Win count ('%u Win')

fields.name: total_losses
fields.meaning: Absolute arena Lose count ('%u Lose')

specs.semantics:
End-of-round result for a team arena. Processed only when CMapControl+0x70==1 (arena map). Reads round_result and the five round counters into scene. If room mode scene+0xF70>=5 prints '%uRound ended. [Blue%d:%dRed]' (round_no, blue_round_wins, red_round_wins). Always prints the winner line. If round_result!=0 and mode>=5 and (blue_round_wins>=3 or red_round_wins>=3): prints 'Final winner: Blue Team.' if blue_round_wins > red_round_wins, else 'Final winner: Red Team.', then FUN_00483430(ui,0x47E,3,1). Then applies the additive reward, overwrites the Down/KO/Win/Lose totals, refreshes the record panel (FUN_00442c90, including rank) and scoreboard (FUN_00443280). If round_result!=0: if round_no==scene+0xF36 then F5B=1 and F5C..F5F=0, else F5B++. Then for every scene entity: if team (+0x14EB) != next_team (+0x14EC), team=next_team and FUN_00428bc0; unconditionally HP +0x9C=+0x110C, MP +0xA0=+0x1110, memset +0xE84 (0x1F8) and +0x107C (0x90). Finally FUN_00442ee0 team status text.
LIVE: shows '<team> team wins' / '+10Reputation Points, +10Victy, +10EXP.' plus a third line 'The same amount of experience point you gained as fame point will be applied when you go back to the field.' - Reputation and Victy apply now, EXP is deferred to the field. specs.semantics:
Applies a timed buff or skill effect to the entity with target_uid and plays its visuals. Steps:
(1) Look up the hii record. Unknown id: stop.
(2) Read uid and find the entity.
(3) If the entity exists and (rec+0x1C8 duration != 0 or id in 0x9CE-0x9D8/0x9E4-0x9F9) and FUN_004257a0(id)==1: read the optional ground x,y for 0xA31..0xA3B. FUN_004257a0 returns 0 for 0x187-0x191, 0x1B3-0x1BD, 0x242-0x24C, 0x78B-0x795, 0x7B7-0x7C1, 0x8BB-0x8C5, 0x981-0x98B, 0x997-0x9A1, 0xA05-0xA0F, 0xA3C-0xA67, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB30-0xB45.
(4) FUN_00424e20 then inserts the buff into the entity's 21-slot table at +0xE84. Slot layout: u16 id; u16 |rec+0x1DC|; u16 rec+0x142; u16 x; u16 y; u32 duration = rec+0x1C8, forced to 60000 for 0x9C3-0x9F9; u32 rec+0x158; u32 source uid = the target itself. Duration comes from the CLIENT's hii record, not the wire. The call returns non-zero for party-type ids (0x8E7-0x912, 0xAE3-0xAF8), which fan out stat updates to party or team members.
(5) If any stat-bonus column (rec+0x1B8..0x1C4) is non-zero, the entity's stats are recomputed (FUN_0041ace0).
(6) If the entity exists, effects and sounds play at its position by id range: 0x124-0x12E effect 0x36/sound 0x36; 0x12F-0x139 effect 0x35/sound 0x36; 0x145-0x14F 0x4A; 0x192-0x19C 0x49; 0x1D4-0x1DE 0x52; 0x8C6-0x8D0 sound 0xB4; 0x8FD-0x907 0xCD; 0x8F2-0x8FC 0xCE; 0x8E7-0x8F1 0xCF; 0x908-0x912 0xD0; 0x913-0x91D sound 0xD1; 0x934-0x93E 0xD3; 0x96B-0x975 0xD8; 0xAE3-0xAED 0x10C; 0xAEE-0xAF8 0x10D; 0xB1A-0xB24 sound 0x112.
(7) If target_uid == local uid, the full 0x25 self-use path runs as well. Otherwise, if step 4 returned non-zero, the stats panel, HP bar and party HP bars refresh; then the handler exits.
specs.trigger: When a duration/buff skill (hii type 3 with rec+0x1C8 > 0) cast via C2S 0x15 succeeds. Send it to the caster (target_uid = caster uid) and, presumably, to every other client in the map so they see the buff. For ground-placed skills 0xA31..0xA3B, append the x,y the caster sent in C2S 0x15.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
1) Unknown id: nothing is read past the id.
2) Unknown target uid (or uid 0): no buff and no visuals, but if uid == local uid the self-use logic still runs.
3) When target_uid is the local player this ALSO does everything 0x25 does: MP/HP cost from rec+0x15C/+0x158, cooldown, cast animation, clearing pending skill scene+0x258. Do NOT additionally send 0x25 to the caster or the cost is double-applied.
4) Local-target type-3 path crashes if the local entity (scene+0x970) is null; see the 0x25 hazard.
5) A full buff table (21 slots, per the grouping rules in FUN_00424e20) silently drops the buff.
6) Party buffs under mode [[0x70EED8]+0x70]==1 dereference scene+0x970 +0x14EB, a null-deref risk if the local entity is missing.
7) PySlayer's KR layout (u16, u8 flag, u32 uid, u16 time, u16 time) will MISPARSE on EN: the flag byte gets absorbed into the uid.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4, combat_skill#08, item_inventory#10/#11): THE CLIENT NEVER EXPIRES A BUFF. In field mode it decrements buff-slot +0xC every tick for type-3 AND type-4 entities, past 0 into negative values; the slot is never removed, stats are never recomputed and the icon merely blinks. The server MUST send S2C 0x43 (remove + stat recompute) or S2C 0x3C (icon only) when a Duration ends. Two more live facts: identical item buffs STACK as separate records and icons (no refresh/replace outside the listed id ranges), and a wire source_uid of 0 is stored as the TARGET's own uid, so the slot +0x14 value is not a literal copy of the wire field. The icon is the item's own icon, drawn bottom-right above the HUD buttons, one per record.
specs.references:
PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x3B.py ('UseBuffSkills') sends u16 skill, u8 0, u32 uid, u16 time, u16 time. That is the newer KR layout and DISAGREES with EN: EN has no flag byte, the duration is taken from the client's hii record (rec+0x1C8, PySlayer's 'Con' column), and the trailing u16 pair exists only for ids 0xA31..0xA3B as ground x,y. PySlayer game_server.py sends it for type-3 skills with Con>0, which matches our type-3 + duration semantics.
The KR Hex-Rays handler (case 0x25/0x3B) is structurally different.
Our server (windslayer_server.py) never sends 0x3B.
reference_combat_model.md groups 0x3B with 0x25 as 'plays a received cast/effect locally', which is correct but incomplete: it is a buff-slot insert plus stat recompute.

Meaning of buff-slot fields copied from rec+0x1DC and rec+0x142, and of rec+0x158 stored at slot +0x10 (buff magnitude?).

specs.length: 6 (u16 + u32); 2 consumed if the id has no item-table entry

fields.name: buff_item_id
fields.meaning: Item-table id (1-based CITEMControl index) of the skill/buff effect to remove. Skills are per-level entries in the item table (e.g. 0x981 Vital Point Strike, 0xA31 Booby Trap, 0xA47 Time Bomb). id 0, out of range or empty -> packet dropped after 2 bytes

specs.semantics: Removes matching buff/debuff slots from an entity without recomputing stats. For i in 0..20 over entity+0xE84 (24-byte slots, u16 id at +0): if slot id == buff_item_id, then (1) if not on an arena map, FUN_004256c0: for ids 0x981-0x98B and 0xA47-0xA51 with a non-zero caster uid at slot+0x14, finds the caster; if caster +0x98>2 and the holder's +0x904 is not 0x10/0x16, applies FUN_00418ac0(holder, caster, 9, ...) and sets holder hit/knockdown fields (+0x8CF/+0x8D0=8, +0x954/+0x958=600, +0x8FF=0, +0xD80=0), which acts as a delayed detonation/strike; (2) if id in 0xA31..0xA3B, queues client event 0xE2 with the slot's u16 pair (+6,+8), likely a trap position; (3) shifts later slots down and zeroes slot 20. For 0x3C processing then ends: no stat recalculation and no HUD refresh.
specs.trigger: Server when a buff/debuff/trap effect on an entity ends and stats do not need recalculation. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4): MANDATORY. The client never expires a buff by itself (it counts slot +0xC down into negative values and leaves the record and icon in place), so every timed buff granted with 0x3B / 0x41 / 0x42 must be terminated by the server: 0x43 when stats or auras must be recomputed, 0x3C when only the icon has to go.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Invalid id -> uid not read, nothing happens. Unknown uid -> nothing happens. After a removal the index still advances, so when two adjacent slots hold the same id the second one (shifted into the current index) is skipped; send again to clear it. The local player's stats and HUD are not recalculated (use 0x43). Do NOT port the KR layout, which has an extra u8.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: The wire formats agree: u16 id, then u32 uid only if the table lookup succeeds (A: 'if(def!=null){u32} else {stop}', B: 'if(def==null){stop}; u32'). The asm confirms both: 0x456660 u16 (IAT 0x4A4090), 0x45667C FUN_00404210, 0x456687 JZ break before the u32 at 0x4566A4 (IAT 0x4A40C8), 0x4566BC lookup, 0x4566C9 JZ break. Naming dispute: B is right that the table is CITEMControl (scene+0xF84 = game_state+0x4D4 set at 0x429D40; its constructor FUN_004031f0 installs CITEMControl::vftable and loads hs\ITMLngKo.lng). A is right that these entries are skills/buffs: items_en.json names 0x981 'Vital Point Strike', 0xA31 'Booby Trap', 0xA47 'Time Bomb', 0x8E7 'Aura of Advance'. So the field is an item-table id whose entries are skill-effect records, and game_system=skill. On FUN_004256c0, B's 'applies hit from caster' is more accurate than A's 'release bind': it calls FUN_00418ac0(holder, caster, 9, ...). KR Hex-Rays case 0x3C/0x43 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 6888) reads u16 + u8 + u32 with 16-byte slots; EN has no u8. Not in PySlayer. Our server: not implemented.

If has_hp: store hp into local entity +0x9C (if [scene+0x970] non-null), refresh HUD HP (FUN_00443690), queue a visual effect entry FUN_0042b580(effect=0x37, uid=[scene+0x220] local uid, 0,0,0, 1, type=10, 0), and play non-positional sound CSpriteControl::Play_Sound(0x37, 0) (IAT 0x4A437C). If has_mp: store mp into +0xA0 and refresh HUD MP (FUN_00443780); no effect/sound for MP. Effect 0x37 is the same id the client uses together with 0x54 for its own heal skills (skill ids 0x1F5..0x1FF in the 0x25/0x3B handler @0x453CAA), i.e. an HP-recover visual. Net result: a 'you were healed' HP/MP set with feedback, local player only.
specs.trigger: Server-side heal / recovery on the local player (heal received, potion, regen with visual). Variant of 0x28/0x44 that adds the recover effect when HP is present.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Local player only (no uid). Effect+sound on the HP branch fire even if [scene+0x970] is null. Each has_hp packet mallocs a 0x20-byte effect entry (FUN_0048b484) and triggers a sound - do not spam per tick. Send bools as 0/1.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x3D reads THREE bools (HP, MP, third stat at +240) and plays no effect - EN has only TWO bools; do not port KR layout. PySlayer has no opcode_0x3D builder. Our server: no 0x3D builder/usage (item use sends plain 0x28/0x44 instead).

specs.name: LocalPlayerDeath (set action 0xD + open death dialog 0x79)
specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics:
The payload is empty; the handler reads nothing after the opcode.

It sets action = 0xD on the local player entity: [[this+0x4CC]+0x970]+0x94C = 0xD. The entity tick FUN_00412360 case 0xD then:
- sets entity+0x904 = 0x10 (dead state), which S2C 0x29 also uses for remote entities
- sets HP entity+0x9C = 0
- sets the revive timer entity+0xE5C = now + entity+0xE58
- clears the buff tables (+0xE84 size 0x1F8, +0x107C size 0x90)
- resets action 94C to 0

It then calls FUN_00483430(g_ui_root, 0x79, 4, 1), which sets ui+0x5A4 = 1 and FUN_00446300 mode 4 shows window 0x79 (skipped if it is already in that state). Any button in window 0x79 sends C2S 0x2E with no payload (FUN_00446300 case 0x79 at 0x44A674). The S2C 0x08 map-change handler closes window 0x79.

The local C2S 0x0D packer will then carry action nibble 0xD, which the server can relay through 0x2A.
specs.trigger: The server decides the receiving player has died (combat is server-driven, HP <= 0).
specs.expected_response: The client sends C2S 0x2E (1 byte, opcode only) when the player clicks a button in the death dialog (window 0x79), most likely return-to-village/revive. The client has a 'Village transfer failed' message box string for a failure reply.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- There is NO null check on the local player pointer scene+0x970. Sending it before the local player is registered (lobby/login/loading) dereferences null and crashes.
- Sending it again re-applies death processing (HP 0, buffs cleared).
- It also needs this+0x4CC (scene) to be valid.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, combat_skill#20/#21): the death dialog (window 0x79) has a SINGLE button ("Revived"); clicking it closes the dialog CLIENT-SIDE immediately and sends C2S 0x2E (0 bytes) without waiting for the server. HAZARD: if the server does not answer, the player is left dead with no UI at all and no way to ask again. RECOVERY: the server must answer C2S 0x2E with the revive/warp sequence (HP via 0x28/0x44 plus 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07, or a fresh spawn).

locations.role: entity action tick; case 0xD = death processing
window 0x79 button handler that sends C2S 0x2E

specs.references:
- The dispatch map lists the KR source file as Packet_handler_4; this opcode is not in the KR main-handler Hex-Rays.
- Our server uses S2C 0x29 (_build_opcode_29 / _send_death) for death, which targets a uid and sets state 0x10 on that entity. 0x3E is the local-player-only variant that also opens the death dialog.
- The client has the string 'Revival in 20 seconds.' (FUN_00458640), shown when the local player is downed in some modes.
open_questions: The exact title/buttons of window 0x79. It is inferred to be the death/return dialog from action 0xD = death, map-change closing it, and every button sending C2S 0x2E.
What C2S 0x2E expects in reply (a village transfer via S2C 0x08/0x03 map change?).
blind_open_questions: What UI window/control id 0x79 is (possibly a death/KO or arena result dialog). It is closed on map change (0x08), and the party HP widgets are 0x75..0x78, so it is not one of them.
Exact meaning of action state 0xD for the local player (knockout vs death animation).

spec_errata.new: single "Revived" button; unanswered 0x2E leaves the player dead with no UI

spec_errata.old: medium
spec_errata.new: high (live-confirmed: HP 0, window 0x79, C2S 0x2E)

fields.meaning: new ABSOLUTE HP; APPLIED ONLY if uid == local uid [scene+0x220] (written to (*(scene+0x970))+0x9C + HUD refresh). For any other entity the value is read and DISCARDED (remote entity +0x9C is NOT updated)

fields.meaning: new ABSOLUTE MP; applied only if uid is the local player (+0xA0 + HUD refresh), otherwise discarded

specs.semantics: Broadcast-style 'entity recovered HP/MP' with visuals. Exact flow: read uid; entity=FUN_004189f0(scene, uid); if null -> stop. Read both bools. (a) if has_hp: read hp; if entity uid == [scene+0x220]: write local +0x9C, FUN_00443690. If has_hp && !has_mp: effect FUN_0042b580(0x37, entity uid, 0,0,0,1,10,0) + positional Play_Sound(0x37, entity+0x15A4, entity+0x15A8, game_state+0x1044..+0x1050, 0) (IAT 0x4A42F8). (b) if has_mp: read mp; if local: write +0xA0, FUN_00443780; effect FUN_0042b580(0x58, uid=[scene+0x220] i.e. the LOCAL player's uid regardless of target - client quirk, identical in the relay copy FUN_00458640), positional Play_Sound(0x58) at the target entity. (c) ALWAYS (entity found, any bool combo incl. both 0): effect FUN_0042b580(0x54, entity uid, ...) + positional Play_Sound(0x54) at the entity. When both bools are set the 0x37 effect is skipped (only 0x58 + 0x54). Effects 0x54+0x37 are exactly what the client plays locally for heal skills 0x1F5..0x1FF (0x453CAA), so 0x40 is a heal/recover visual, not a hurt flinch.
specs.trigger: Server announces that an entity (another player, or the local player) was healed / used a recovery item, so nearby clients show the heal effect; for the local uid it also sets HP/MP.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unknown uid => only 4 bytes consumed, nothing happens. Remote entity HP/MP are NOT changed by this packet (use 0x54/0x14/0x1A for remote bars). Every packet mallocs 1-2 effect entries and plays 1-2 positional sounds - sending it per combat hit caused the observed hitch. MP branch effect always lands on the local player sprite even when target is remote.

specs.name: ItemBuffApply
specs.grammar:
u32 target_uid
u32 source_uid
if(entity_by_uid(target_uid) == null) { stop }
u16 item_id

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the entity that receives the buff; looked up in the scene entity list (entity+0x84). uid 0 or unknown uid ends processing
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [base+0x158]; passed as EDX to FUN_004189f0 (entity lookup)

fields.name: source_uid
fields.meaning: uid of whoever applied the buff. Goes to FUN_00424e20 param_6 and is stored at buff+0x14 (entity+0xe98+slot*0x18). 0 means the target buffed itself: the target's own uid is stored instead, and for item ids 0x9C3..0x9F9 the duration is forced to 60000

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: id of the buff-granting item (1-based index into the item table at scene+0xF84). The item's Duration (def+0x1C8, the tooltip 'Duration:' field) becomes the buff timer. Its stat modifiers are at def+0x1B8..0x1C4
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [base+0x150] -> AX for FUN_00404210 / FUN_00424e20 -> entity+0xE84+slot*0x18

specs.semantics: Adds a timed buff, granted by an item, to an entity. Steps: (1) find the target entity by uid; if it is missing, stop. (2) Read item_id and look up the item definition in scene+0xF84 (FUN_00404210); if it is missing, stop. (3) If def+0x1C8 (Duration) != 0, call FUN_00424e20(scene, entity, duration, 0, 0, source_uid). That writes a 0x18-byte record into the entity's buff array at +0xE84 (21 slots). Some item-id ranges (0x8E7-0x912, 0x9C3-0x9F9, 0xA9F-0xAC9, 0xAE3-0xAF8, 0x1D4-0x1DE, 0xB1A-0xB24) replace a conflicting buff that is already present. Record fields: +0 id, +2 |def+0x1DC|, +0xC duration, +0x10 def+0x158, +0x14 source uid. It then shows buff icons for party members or the local player (FUN_004259c0). If any stat modifier def+0x1B8/0x1BC/0x1C0/0x1C4 is non-zero, stats are recalculated (FUN_0041ace0). (4) For 0x41 nothing else happens. Unlike 0x42, the local character-info stat panel is NOT refreshed.
specs.trigger: Server-side result of using a buff item (scroll, potion or anything else with a Duration) on self or on another entity, so everyone who can see the target shows the buff.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs target_uid to be a spawned entity (the u16 is not even read otherwise). Needs item_id to be a valid 1-based item-table index. The buff is only added if the item's Duration != 0. If all 21 buff slots are full or a stacking rule blocks it, FUN_00424e20 returns 0 without adding anything. No UI dialog. No crash hazard found: the reads are fixed-size. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4, combat_skill#08, item_inventory#10/#11): THE CLIENT NEVER EXPIRES A BUFF. In field mode it decrements buff-slot +0xC every tick for type-3 AND type-4 entities, past 0 into negative values; the slot is never removed, stats are never recomputed and the icon merely blinks. The server MUST send S2C 0x43 (remove + stat recompute) or S2C 0x3C (icon only) when a Duration ends. Two more live facts: identical item buffs STACK as separate records and icons (no refresh/replace outside the listed id ranges), and a wire source_uid of 0 is stored as the TARGET's own uid, so the slot +0x14 value is not a literal copy of the wire field. The icon is the item's own icon, drawn bottom-right above the HUD buttons, one per record.

locations.role: stat recalc FUN_0041ace0 if item has stat mods

specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x42.py builds u32,u32,u16 (10 bytes), which matches the EN layout exactly (no callers). The newer KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c line 7132) reads u32,u32,u16 plus an extra u8, so KR has grown and EN has no trailing u8. Our server never sends 0x41 or 0x42.

Which C2S item-use opcode makes the retail server answer with 0x41 instead of 0x42 was not traced.

locations.role: FUN_00404210 CITEMControl lookup; NULL -> break before uid
FUN_00425af0(scene, entity, 0) with AX=id: returns 0 unless id is an aura (0x8E7-0x912, 0xAE3-0xAF8); otherwise re-evaluates team (arena) or party aura buffs; result in EBX

specs.length: 6 (u16 + u32); 2 consumed if the id has no item-table entry

fields.name: buff_item_id
fields.meaning: Item-table id (1-based CITEMControl index) of the skill/buff effect to remove; its definition's stat fields (+0x1B8..+0x1C4) decide whether stats are recomputed
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x11C]; matched against slot+0; passed in AX to FUN_00425af0

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: Uid of the entity carrying the buff
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x170]; compared with scene+0x220 (local player uid)

specs.semantics: Same slot removal as 0x3C (arena-gated FUN_004256c0, event 0xE2 for 0xA31-0xA3B, compaction). Then: FUN_00425af0(scene, entity, 0) returns 0 at once unless the id is in an aura range (0x8E7-0x912 or 0xAE3-0xAF8). For auras it re-applies team auras (arena map) or party auras (party uids scene+0x25C..+0x26C) to the affected members and returns non-zero when the local player is affected. If the definition has any non-zero stat field at +0x1B8/+0x1BC/+0x1C0/+0x1C4, FUN_0041ace0 recomputes the entity's stats. If target_uid == scene+0x220 (local player) or the aura result was non-zero, it refreshes the stat panel (FUN_00443840), HP/MP gauges (FUN_00443690) and party HP bars (FUN_0043d4e0).
specs.trigger: Server when a stat-affecting or aura buff/debuff on an entity expires or is dispelled. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C4): MANDATORY. The client never expires a buff by itself (it counts slot +0xC down into negative values and leaves the record and icon in place), so every timed buff granted with 0x3B / 0x41 / 0x42 must be terminated by the server: 0x43 when stats or auras must be recomputed, 0x3C when only the icon has to go.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Invalid id -> uid not read, nothing happens. Unknown uid -> nothing. Aura re-evaluation and stat recompute run once the entity is found, even if no slot matched (harmless). Adjacent duplicate slots: only the first is removed per packet. KR layout has an extra u8 after the id; EN does not.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Wire formats agree, and the u16/lookup/u32 evidence is the same as for 0x3C (0x456660, 0x45667C/0x456687, 0x4566A4, 0x4566BC/0x4566C9). The only structural difference is notation. The 0x43 branch starts at 0x4567B0 (cmp [esp+0x43],0x43) and does no further packet reads. Naming follows 0x3C: the table is CITEMControl (B right), and the entries are skill-effect records (A right). On FUN_00425af0, A is correct and B's 'stat recompute' is imprecise: the decomp entry check returns 0 unless AX is in 0x8E7-0x912 or 0xAE3-0xAF8, so it is aura re-application, and the general stat recompute is FUN_0041ace0 at 0x456807, gated on def+0x1B8..+0x1C4. Both analysts correctly state the HUD refresh condition at 0x456818-0x456823 (local uid or EBX!=0). KR Hex-Rays shares case 0x3C/0x43 (branch on opcode 67) but has an extra u8. Not in PySlayer. Our server: not implemented.

Exact meaning of item-def fields +0x1B8..+0x1C4 (likely stat bonus values) and +0x160 (used by FUN_00427d40 inside the aura path).

specs.grammar: str[17] partner_name

fields.name: partner_name
fields.meaning: Name of the other trade party, NUL-terminated inside the 17 bytes
fields.dest_or_source: stack buffer [ESP+0x34] -> strcpy into window 0x4E (trade window) control 0x21 text

specs.semantics: Starts a trade session and resets the trade UI. In order: (1) put partner_name in trade window 0x4E control 0x21; (2) show window 0x4E; (3) set state=1 on controls 2 and 4 (cancel/close buttons) of 0x4E and of 0x291 (final-confirmation window); (4) free every item record in both lists of 0x4E (+0xAC/+0xB0 = my offered items, +0xBC/+0xC0 = partner items) and of 0x291 (FUN_0047d700); (5) set control 3 (confirm button) state=1 on 0x4E and 0x291; (6) clear the partner-confirmed flag [ctx+0x24]=0; (7) set the gold edit box (0x4E ctrl 0x1E) and the partner gold label (0x4E ctrl 0x1F) to the string "0" (0x6F7BEC). Returns 1. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#04): the EN caption of window 0x4E is "TRADE" (the "Exchange" label comes from the KR UILngKo.lng strings). The partner name goes in the RIGHT column header (ctrl 0x21); the left column header carries the local character name (an extra control the earlier docs did not list). Live geometry: the window opens centred at (250,205)-(565,410).
specs.trigger: Server sends to BOTH parties once the target accepts (C2S 0x21 requester_name), each with the other player's name.
specs.expected_response: None immediately. Afterwards the user can offer items (not in this batch), click confirm (window 0x4E button 3 -> C2S 0x23 u64 gold, send site #65 @0x469D05, after an 'You are short of gold.' check against money at [ctx+0x18]+0x228), or cancel (buttons 2/4 -> C2S 0x24 with no payload, send site #66 @0x469D9C; closing the window with param_6==2 is rerouted to the same cancel).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Shared sub1 gate ([ctx+0x8] and UI root non-null). partner_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (unzeroed stack buffer + strcpy). The lists are FREED, not given back to the bag, so a 0x46 sent while the player still has items offered (without a 0x49 first) makes those items vanish from the client's bag view until the server resyncs the inventory. Must be sent before every new trade because it is the only place [ctx+0x24] is reset; otherwise a stale partner-confirmed flag can open the final window too early on the next 0x48.
specs.references: Not implemented in our server or PySlayer. Window ids from the client UI code: 0x70 = request dialog, 0x4E = trade window (C2S 0x23/0x24 handlers in FUN_00469090 case 0x4E), 0x291 = final confirmation window (C2S 0x25 / 0x24 in case 0x291).
open_questions: Exact on-screen roles of controls 2 and 4 (both send cancel 0x24; likely a Cancel button and a close X).

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: Why the trade request failed: 6 = target is already trading (shows "Trading."), 4 = target refuses trades (shows "The player is rejecting trade."). Any other value is read and silently ignored.
fields.dest_or_source: local [ESP+0x1C], used only for the compare

specs.semantics: Failure notice for a trade request. result==6 posts "Trading." (0x6F5088) and result==4 posts "The player is rejecting trade." (0x6F49D8) to the system/chat message queue (FUN_004817d0, colour 0xFFFD4C87). Other values do nothing. No window or trade state changes. Always returns 1.
specs.trigger: Server reply to the requester's C2S 0x20 {u32 target_uid} when the target is busy in another trade (6) or has trades blocked or declined (4).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Shared sub1 gate. The message only shows if the chat window object ([UI+0x59C]) exists. No crash hazards.
specs.references: Not implemented in our server or PySlayer. The requester-side preconditions checked before C2S 0x20 are client-side (manner points, same field) in FUN_00446300 @0x44A398..0x44A4A4.

locations.role: self branch: 0x4E control 3 state=0; my item records (+0xB0 list) +0x18=1
partner branch: FUN_004659d0(gold,0x4E,0x1F) shows %I64u gold; [ctx+0x24]=1; partner records (+0xC0) +0x18=1
0x291 ctrl 0x1D = text of 0x4E gold edit (ctrl 0x1E +0xD1); 0x291 ctrl 0x1E = 0x4E partner gold label (ctrl 0x1F +0x50)
related C2S 0x25 final accept built in window 0x291 button 3

specs.grammar:
u32 confirmer_uid
u64 gold

fields.name: confirmer_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the trade party who just clicked confirm. Compared with the local player's uid [[ctx+0x18]+0x1D8]. That is the same field FUN_00466e30 compares against entity+0x84; offset math suggests it is scene+0x220, the spawn uid used by the 0x07/registration gate.

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Gold the confirming party offers. Shown (formatted with %I64u) in trade window 0x4E control 0x1F only when confirmer_uid is NOT the local player. Ignored in the self branch.

specs.semantics: A party locked in their side of the trade. Self branch (confirmer_uid == my uid): set trade window 0x4E control 3 (confirm button) state=0 and set +0x18=1 (greyed/locked) on each record in my offered-items list (0x4E+0xB0). Gold is ignored. Partner branch: write gold as a decimal string into 0x4E control 0x1F, set the partner-confirmed flag [ctx+0x24]=1, and grey out each record in the partner list (0x4E+0xC0). Then, on either branch: if my confirm button state (0x4E ctrl 3 +0x1C) is 0 AND [ctx+0x24]!=0, both sides are locked. The client then copies every 0x38-byte item record from 0x4E into the final-confirmation window 0x291 (partner +0xC0 -> 0x291 +0xBC/+0xC0 list, mine +0xB0 -> 0x291 +0xAC/+0xB0 list). It sets 0x291 control 0x1D to my gold edit text (0x4E ctrl 0x1E) and 0x291 control 0x1E to the partner gold label (0x4E ctrl 0x1F), shows window 0x291 and hides window 0x4E. Returns 1 on all paths. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#12): the EN caption of window 0x291 is "Comfirming Trade" [sic]; its list headers are "Items to Send" / "Items to Receive" and ctrl 3 is labelled "Trade". The wire behaviour (self echo greys the own list, partner echo opens 0x291 and hides 0x4E) matched the spec exactly.
specs.trigger: On C2S 0x23 {u64 gold} from a party, the server should send 0x48 {that party's uid, gold} to BOTH parties. The self echo is required: the second confirmer's final window only opens on its own echo, because its [ctx+0x24] was set earlier by the partner's 0x48. The first confirmer's final window opens when the partner's 0x48 arrives, because the client already zeroed its button 3 before sending 0x23.
specs.expected_response: When the final window 0x291 opens, OK (button 3) sends C2S 0x25: u64 my_gold (0x291 ctrl 0x1D), u8 my_item_count, repeat(my_item_count){u16 item_id(+0x0) u16 rec_0E u8 opt_count(0..5, count of leading non-zero u16 at +0x2..) repeat(opt_count){u16 opt} u16 rec_0C}, then u64 partner_gold (ctrl 0x1E), u8 partner_item_count, repeat{same record}. Buttons 2/4 send C2S 0x24 (cancel). The server then presumably answers with S2C 0x4A ("Trade completed.") or 0x49.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Shared sub1 gate. confirmer_uid must exactly equal the uid the client registered for its own player, or the self echo is treated as the partner (it would overwrite the partner gold label and set the partner flag). [ctx+0x24] is only cleared by S2C 0x46, so always start trades with 0x46. In the both-confirmed path, if window 0x4E has fewer than 0x1E/0x1F child controls, EDI stays 0 and FUN_004838c0 strcpy's from NULL and crashes (not expected with stock UI data). FUN_00489090 dereferences [0+0x1C] if 0x4E's child list is shorter than 3.
specs.references: Not implemented in our server or PySlayer. NOTE: our server's _dispatch treats C2S 0x25 as 'UseSkill (u16 skill)' and echoes a cast. In this EN client the ONLY C2S 0x25 send site is the trade final-accept in window 0x291 (FUN_00469090 @0x46A99C), so that handler would misfire on a trade accept. 'You are short of gold.' (0x469CAD) checks the 0x23 gold against money at [ctx+0x18]+0x228 (the same u64 that S2C 0x18/0x19 update).
open_questions: What item record fields +0x0C and +0x0E are (likely durability/count, and count/flag). They are only echoed in C2S 0x25 and passed to FUN_00467200 on cancel.
Confirm [ctx+0x18] == scene+0x48 (so +0x1D8 == scene+0x220). Supported by two independent offset pairs (uid and manner points, both delta 0x48) but not proven by a direct write.
blind_open_questions: Whether the server should echo the confirmer's real gold to the confirmer too (the client ignores it on the self branch, so any value works).
The identification [ctx+0x18] == scene+0x48 is inferred from the matching gold fields, not from a direct assignment (the ctx+0x18 initialization was not located).

specs.name: TradeCanceled

locations.role: handler block start (sub1 case 0x49). The block runs to RET 0x10 at 0x0046E53F and makes no GetDataFromPacket call.
FUN_004817d0(ui, "Trade has been canceled." @0x6F501C, colour 0xFFFD4C87): system message
FUN_00483430(0x4E,1,1) calls FUN_00446300(win=0x4E,0,1,0,param_6=1): hides the trade window. param_6 is not 2, so the cancel path that re-enters is skipped, and caseD_2 runs FUN_004835b0 then exits.
FUN_004830f0(0x4E): finds the trade window object. Returns if it is missing or if the list count/head at +0xB0 is 0.
FUN_00459e60(ESI=win+0xAC): pops one 0x38-byte record from the list of items I offered
FUN_00404210(ESI=[[ctx+0x10]+0xF84], EAX=u16 rec+0x0): looks up the item definition
FUN_00467200(ECX=[def+0x154] category, EDX=ctx, stack: rec+0x0 id, rec+0xE u16; EDI=rec+0x2): puts the item back in the local bag
FUN_00465290: refreshes the inventory UI (only when FUN_00467200 returns nonzero)
_free(record). Always runs, whether or not the restore succeeded.

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: The packet has no payload: the handler never reads from the packet, so any trailing bytes are ignored. Steps: (1) Posts the system message "Trade has been canceled." (colour 0xFFFD4C87). (2) Hides trade window 0x4E and final-confirm window 0x291 through FUN_00483430(id,1,1). That becomes FUN_00446300(..., param_6=1), which only hides the windows (FUN_004835b0) and sends nothing. (3) If window 0x4E exists and the list of items I offered (list object at +0xAC, count/head at +0xB0) is not empty, it pops records until the list is empty. Each record is 0x38 bytes, allocated by the self branch of S2C 0x4B. The handler uses rec+0x0 = u16 item_id, rec+0x2 = 12 option bytes and rec+0xE = u16 (count/durability-like). It looks up the item definition through FUN_00404210 in [[ctx+0x10]+0xF84]. If found, FUN_00467200 restores the item by category = def+0x154. Category 0: FUN_00423b70(bag+0x5F6, bag+0x650, bag+0x6AC, id, byte bag+0x362, 0,0,0) with ECX=rec+0xE. Category 1: writes the id into the first zero u16 slot of bag+0x380 (slot count = byte bag+0x361, must be <= 0x2D) and copies the 12 bytes from rec+2 to bag+0x3DA+slot*12; rec+0xE is not used. Category 2: FUN_00423e70(bag+0x760, id, byte bag+0x363) with ESI=bag+0x7BA and EAX=rec+0xE. Here bag = [ctx+0x18]. On success the inventory UI refreshes (FUN_00465290). The record is freed either way. (4) Returns 1. The partner's offered-items list (object at +0xBC, head at +0xC0) is not touched.
specs.trigger: Send to both trade parties when either side cancels (C2S 0x24), and by server policy when a party disconnects or leaves the field mid-trade or when final validation fails.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Shared sub1 gate only. Safe to send with no trade open: the windows are simply hidden and the restore loop is skipped when window 0x4E is missing or its list is empty. The client restores offered items to its bag locally, because it removed them when S2C 0x4B (self branch, FUN_00467140) added them to the trade. The server's inventory model must still treat those items as owned. If the item definition is not found, or category 1 has no free slot (or its slot count is over 0x2D), the record is freed without a restore and the client bag loses the item until the next resync. Hiding the windows does NOT send C2S 0x24, so there is no echo loop.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree the payload is empty (length 0, no fields). A wrote grammar "" and B wrote "stop". This is a difference in notation, not in wire format. The asm from 0x0046E465 to the RET 0x10 at 0x0046E53F has no CALL through any GetDataFromPacket IAT slot (0x4A4090/94/98/C8/CC/D0/D4/B0/118). None of the callees (FUN_004817d0, FUN_00483430, FUN_004830f0, FUN_00459e60, FUN_00404210, FUN_00467200, FUN_00465290) receives the packet pointer (EDI is overwritten at 0x0046E4A1) or the offset (EBP+0x10). The first packet read after this point belongs to the 0x4B block at 0x0046E550. The canonical grammar is "stop", meaning zero bytes are read. Two semantic details were checked in FUN_00467200's asm. (a) Category mapping: A was right and B was wrong. Category 0 goes to FUN_00423b70 (0x004672C9..F2), category 1 to the u16 slot array at +0x380 plus 12 option bytes at +0x3DA (0x00467249..C6), and category 2 to FUN_00423e70 at +0x760 (0x00467223..3F). B's claim that category 1 is equipment and category 2 is stackable does not match that dispatch. (b) The u16 at rec+0xE is the second stack argument (MOV SI,[ESP+0x10] at 0x0046720A). It is used by categories 0 and 2 and ignored by category 1. B mentioned it as a count and A left it out. List offsets: both are consistent. My-items list object is at +0xAC with head/count at +0xB0 (0x0046E4AF/0x0046E4C0). The partner list object is at +0xBC (0x0046E702 in 0x4B) with head at +0xC0 (0x0046E832 in 0x4A). The record size 0x38 is confirmed by PUSH 0x38/FUN_0048b484 at 0x0046E653. A's claim that the windows close without re-sending C2S 0x24 is confirmed: in FUN_00446300, case 0x4E re-enters only when param_6==2, and caseD_2 exits after FUN_004835b0 when param_6==1. Neither PySlayer nor our server implements this opcode. The companion opcode 0x4A ("Trade completed.", u64 money into [ctx+0x18]+0x228 at 0x0046E7FB) is outside this batch.
open_questions: Whether the original server also sent explicit inventory resync packets after 0x49, or relied only on this client-side restore (server policy, not visible in the client).
What exactly the u16 at rec+0xE means (count vs durability) for categories 0 and 2. It comes from the S2C 0x4B payload, which is outside this batch.
Where the partner list at +0xBC/+0xC0 is cleared. It is not cleared in this handler, and the 0x46 block does not visibly clear it either (it may happen inside FUN_0047d700 on window open).

specs.name: TradeCompleted

locations.role: FUN_004659D0 format %I64u gold into window 9 control 0xB
FUN_00467200 add each partner item to local inventory

specs.grammar: u64 gold

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Local player's new absolute gold total after the trade

specs.semantics: Prints "Trade completed." (green 0xFF00C800), overwrites the local gold with the u64 and refreshes the inventory gold label (window 9, control 0xB). Then walks the PARTNER item list of trade window 0x4E (head at window+0xC0); for each struct it looks up the item, calls FUN_00467200(item_id, count) with EDI = struct+2 (12-byte option block) to ADD it to the local inventory (stackables by count; equipment into the first empty bag slot with the options copied), and on success prints "you've received %s. (Count:%u)" and refreshes the inventory UI. Finally closes windows 0x4E and 0x291. The local player's own offered items were already removed from inventory when their 0x4B echo arrived, so nothing is removed here.
specs.trigger: When both players have confirmed and the server commits the trade; send to each participant with that participant's resulting gold.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs ctx+8/ctx+0xC non-null. The client grants the partner's items itself from the 0x4B partner list; the server must NOT also send separate item-add packets for them or they will be duplicated client-side. If the partner list is out of sync (missed 0x4B/0x4C), the client inventory desyncs from the server. Equipment adds silently fail if bag count byte ([ctx+0x18]+0x361) > 0x2D or no empty slot.
specs.references: Gold u64 at [ctx+0x18]+0x228 is the same field used by S2C 0x18 (quest reward, PySlayer opcode_0x18.py writes gold first). Not in PySlayer or our server.
open_questions: Purpose of window 0x291 (likely trade confirm/gold-entry dialog).
blind_open_questions: Exact C2S that leads to 0x4A (0x24 is the likely confirm but was not fully traced).
Identity of window 0x291 and exact effect of FUN_00483430(…,1,1) (assumed close).

specs.name: TradeItemAdded

locations.role: FUN_00467140 remove item(s) from local inventory (self path)
FUN_00489A80(win 0x4E) append to OWN trade list (window+0xAC)
FUN_00459DF0 append to PARTNER trade list (window+0xBC)

specs.grammar:
u16 item_id
u16 count
u32 owner_uid
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }
u16 opt_extra

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item definition id being placed in the trade window

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Quantity offered (stack count; 1 for equipment)
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x1C] -> struct +0x0E; passed as count to FUN_00467140

fields.name: owner_uid
fields.meaning: UID of the player who offered the item. Equal to local player's uid ([ctx+0x18]+0x1D8 == scene+0x220) => own side; otherwise partner side

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: Number of leading option/enchant words that follow (client sender computes it as count of leading non-zero words among the first 5). MUST be <= 5

fields.name: opt
fields.meaning: Option/enchant word i (i=0..opt_count-1)

fields.name: opt_extra
fields.meaning: Sixth option word, always present (option block +0x0A; PySlayer writes a non-enchant value here, exact meaning unconfirmed)

specs.semantics: Trade window item-added notification. All six option words form a 12-byte block (slots opt_count..4 stay zero). If owner_uid == local player's uid: look up item_id in the item DB (null -> silently ignored); call FUN_00467140(item_id, &opts12, count) which REMOVES count of that item from the local inventory (stackables by count; equipment by exact item_id + 12-byte option memcmp in slots +0x380/+0x3DA); on success allocate a 0x38-byte struct {u16 id @0, 6xu16 opts @2, u16 count @0xE} and append it to the OWN list of trade window 0x4E (window+0xAC, head +0xB0, count +0xB8), then FUN_00465290 refreshes the inventory UI. Otherwise (partner's item): if trade window 0x4E exists, append the same struct to the PARTNER list (window+0xBC, head +0xC0); no item-DB validation. These partner structs are what 0x4A later adds to the inventory.
specs.trigger: Server echo of C2S 0x22 (trade add item: u16 item_id, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16 opts, u16 extra; client blocks locally when own list already has 12 entries). Send to BOTH traders: to the offerer with owner_uid = offerer uid (this is what actually removes the item from their inventory client-side) and to the partner with the offerer's uid.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Function-level gate: [ctx+8] (game_state) and [ctx+0xC] (UI root) must be non-null or the packet is unhandled and falls through to SubHandler2. opt_count > 5 overflows the 12-byte stack option buffer (index 5 is overwritten by opt_extra; >=7 corrupts neighbouring locals; >=59 reaches the /GS cookie at frame+0xB0 -> fatal __security_check_cookie crash). Self path: if the option words don't exactly match the inventory copy of an equipment item, removal fails and the item never appears in the trade window (desync). Self path does not require the window to be open for the inventory removal, but FUN_00489A80 silently drops (leaks) the struct if window 0x4E isn't open -> item vanishes from inventory with no trade entry. Partner path requires window 0x4E open. Always returns handled (EAX=1).
specs.references: Not present in PySlayer (no trade opcodes) or windslayer_server.py. The item layout (u16 id, u8 n<=5, n*u16, u16 extra) matches PySlayer opcode_0x03 inventory equipment entries and the EN C2S 0x22 builder at 0x46C62C, with u16 count and u32 owner_uid inserted after the id.
open_questions: Meaning of opt_extra (sixth option word) is unconfirmed.
Whether the server must also validate opt words vs its own DB; client only uses them for its local equipment removal match.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of option_tail (6th blob word) - reinforcement handler 0x8E reads all 6 words fixed-width, so it is part of the option blob, but its semantic (e.g. reinforce level) is unconfirmed.
Stackable (type 0/2) items take a different client path at 0x46C6C0 (count input dialog); the C2S for that path was not traced, but S2C 0x4B format is the same regardless.

specs.name: TradePartnerItemRemoved

locations.role: FUN_0045A000 get node by 0-based index in partner list (window 0x4E +0xBC)
FUN_00459F20 unlink node, then free item struct

specs.grammar: u8 slot_index

fields.name: slot_index
fields.meaning: 0-based index into the PARTNER's offered-item list of trade window 0x4E (insertion order of 0x4B partner adds)

specs.semantics: Removes the slot_index-th entry from the partner-side item list of the trade window (window 0x4E, list container +0xBC) and frees its 0x38-byte struct. Only the partner list is touched; the own list is not affected by this opcode. No message, no inventory change.
specs.trigger: When the trade partner withdraws an item they had offered (inferred; the C2S that causes it was not located).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs ctx+8/ctx+0xC non-null (else unhandled). Silently ignored if window 0x4E isn't open or index >= list length. Index is 0-based and positional, so the server must track the partner's list order exactly as sent via 0x4B.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer or our server.
open_questions: Which C2S opcode (trade-item withdraw) triggers this, and whether the withdrawing player's own list is updated by a different S2C or locally.
blind_open_questions: No client C2S 'remove item from trade' send site was identified in this pass, and no S2C handler here removes from the local own-offer list (+0xAC); unclear whether the protocol supports withdrawing items at all or only uses this for server-side corrections.

specs.name: TradePartnerSlotsFull

system message 0x6F5038 in color 0xFFFD4C87; UI pointer ECX = [ctx+0xC], loaded at 0x46CF73

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: No payload is read. The client shows the system message "There are no more spaces in the other player's item slot." (FUN_004817D0, color 0xFFFD4C87) and returns 1 (handled). No trade or inventory state changes.
specs.trigger: Server rejects a trade add-item request (C2S 0x22) because the trade partner has no room left.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 only runs the handler when [ctx+0x8] != 0 and [ctx+0xC] != 0 (0x46CF5E / 0x46CF76). Otherwise it jumps to 0x46EF76, returns 0 and the opcode goes on to the next sub-handler. The handler reads nothing, so extra bytes cannot desync anything. Harmless to send at any time.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: The two analysts gave the same wire format: zero payload bytes, only the message 0x6F5038 in color 0xFFFD4C87, then return. They differ only in how they wrote it: A left the grammar empty ("") and B wrote "stop". The asm settles it. The block at 0x46E7AA is PUSH 0xFFFD4C87 / PUSH 0x6F5038 / PUSH ECX / CALL 0x4817D0 / MOV EAX,1 / epilogue / RET 0x10. There is no GetDataFromPacket call. The raw binary also confirms that switch index 0x46F000[0x4D-0x18] = 12 goes to jump table 0x46EF90[12] = 0x46E7AA. Both analysts are right about the content. I use "stop" because it states outright that nothing is read, while an empty grammar looks the same as a missing one. The string at 0x6F5038 is used only by SubHandler1. The client already blocks a 13th entry in the player's own trade list ('There are no more spaces in trade slot') at 0x46C5A6 before it sends 0x22 (per analyst B). Neither PySlayer nor our server has this opcode.
open_questions: The client alone cannot tell whether "other player's item slot" means the partner's trade-window slots or the partner's inventory space. This is the server-side condition for sending it.

specs.name: PartyInviteReceived

locations.role: FUN_004838c0: set text of window 0x71 control 1 = inviter_name
window 0x71 click handler: button 3 (Accept) sends C2S 0x28 + str[17] name copied from control 1

specs.grammar: str[17] inviter_name

fields.name: inviter_name
fields.meaning: Name of the character inviting this client to a party. Displayed in the invite dialog and echoed back verbatim in C2S 0x28 on Accept.
fields.dest_or_source: stack buf [esp+0x308] -> window 0x71 control 1 text (ui control +0x50, 0x81-byte field)

specs.semantics: Reads exactly 17 bytes (inviter name), copies it (strcpy up to NUL) into control 1 of UI window 0x71 and opens that window (FUN_00483430 -> FUN_00446300(id=0x71, state=3)). Window 0x71 is the party-invitation dialog: clicking its control 3 (Accept) makes the client build C2S 0x28 = u8 0x28 + str[17] where the 17 bytes are the text of control 1 (the inviter name received here). No entity/party state is changed by this packet itself. No sub-type byte and no gating in the EN client (the KR build reads an extra u8 and checks dialog state before opening). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, party#08): in window 0x71 control 1 is the window CAPTION (it shows the inviter name); the body is static text "wants to party with you." The buttons are "Accept" (ctrl 3, sends C2S 0x28) and "Refuse", which sends NOTHING.
specs.trigger: Server sends to the TARGET player after another player sends C2S 0x27 (u32 target uid, 'Make Party' from the character window 0x50) and the invite is valid (target not already in a party -> else 0x50; level gap <= 10 -> else 0x56).
specs.expected_response: If the user clicks Accept: C2S 0x28 str[17] inviter_name (FUN_00446300 @0x44A64E). No decline packet found in the window-0x71 click case (only button 3 sends).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No client-side gate. inviter_name MUST contain a NUL within the 17 bytes: the 17 raw bytes land in a stack buffer and are strcpy'd into the control; an unterminated name reads past the buffer into stack garbage, and the Accept path strcpy's the control text back into a 17-byte stack local (local_90..local_80) -> stack overflow risk. Max 16 visible chars.
specs.references: PySlayer KR Hex-Rays case 0x4E reads name + an extra u8 (sub_5288E0) and gates on UI state; EN reads ONLY the 17-byte name (asm confirmed: single GetDataFromPacket via 0x4A4098 N=0x11). PySlayer has no builder for 0x4E. Our server: not implemented.
open_questions: [RESOLVED by live verification party#09, 2026-09-17] Live (party#09): the "Refuse" button of window 0x71 sends NO packet at all, so a declined party invite is invisible to the server - it must rely on an invite TTL. Original question: "Whether the dialog has a Decline button that sends anything (not found in case 0x71 of FUN_00446300; likely just closes)."
blind_open_questions: Is the name matched case-sensitively by the server when C2S 0x28 comes back? That is server-side policy and not visible in the client.
Static label text of window 0x71 (e.g. '... invites you') is in UI resources, not strings.tsv, so it was not confirmed.

spec_errata.new: ctrl 1 is the caption; Refuse sends nothing
