spec_errata.new: Refuse sends nothing

specs.name: PartyMemberAdd
specs.length: 29 bytes (str[17] + u32 + 4 x u16). The client reads 0 bytes if all 4 party frames are taken, 25 bytes if hp_max == 0, and all 29 in every other case (the mp_max == 0 stop comes after the last read).

locations.role: Handler entry. Loops over UI window ids 0x75..0x78 (FUN_004830f0 lookup, EDX preserved). Takes the first window that exists and has window+0x134 == 0. If none is free, jumps to 0x44D7AD (0x4568BE) with nothing read.
GetDataFromPacket char buffer (IAT 0x4A4098), N=0x11, dst=[base+0x31C]: member_name
Sets text of frame control 3 to the name (unbounded strcpy into control+0x50)
frame+0x134 = member_uid (written BEFORE any zero check)
Gauge on control 1 = hp_cur/hp_max (FDIVP bytes DE F9: ST1/ST0 = second read / first read). Text on control 1 = sprintf("%u/%u", hp_cur, hp_max) at 0x45698B.
MOV AX,[ESP+0xA8]; TEST AX,AX; JZ 0x44D7AD: if mp_max == 0, stop (the frame is not opened and later steps are skipped)
Gauge on control 2 = mp_cur/mp_max (DE F9). Text on control 2 = "%u/%u" (mp_cur, mp_max) at 0x456A48.
Opens the party frame (window id, state 3, 1)
Stores uid in the first zero slot of scene(handler+0x4CC)+0x25C..+0x26C (5 u32 slots). Skipped if all 5 are used.
FUN_004189f0 looks up the entity by uid. If found, entity+0x13A0 = 1 (party-member flag).

fields.name: member_name
fields.meaning: Party member's character name. Must be NUL-terminated within the 17 bytes, because the control text copy is an unbounded strcpy.
fields.dest_or_source: Stack [base+0x31C], then text of control 3 in the chosen party frame (window 0x75..0x78)

fields.name: member_uid
fields.meaning: Party member's entity uid (same id space as entity+0x84). Must be nonzero, since 0 marks a free frame.
fields.dest_or_source: frame+0x134; first empty slot of scene+0x25C..+0x26C; used to find the entity and set entity+0x13A0 = 1

fields.name: hp_max
fields.meaning: Member's max HP. Divisor of the HP gauge. 0 stops the handler after 25 bytes.
fields.dest_or_source: UI only: second %u in control 1 text; gauge 1 divisor

fields.name: hp_cur
fields.meaning: Member's current HP
fields.dest_or_source: UI only: first %u in control 1 text; gauge 1 numerator

fields.name: mp_max
fields.meaning: Member's max MP. Divisor of the MP gauge. 0 stops the handler before the frame is opened.
fields.dest_or_source: UI only: second %u in control 2 text; gauge 2 divisor

fields.name: mp_cur
fields.meaning: Member's current MP
fields.dest_or_source: UI only: first %u in control 2 text; gauge 2 numerator

specs.semantics:
Adds one member to the party HUD.

1. The client scans UI windows 0x75, 0x76, 0x77 and 0x78 (the 4 party-member frames) for the first one that exists and has +0x134 (bound uid) == 0. If none is free, the packet is ignored and nothing is read.
2. It reads the name and sets it as the text of control 3.
3. It reads the uid and writes it to frame+0x134.
4. It reads hp_max, then hp_cur. If hp_max == 0 it stops. Otherwise it sets control 1 text to "hp_cur/hp_max" and gauge 1 to hp_cur/hp_max.
5. It reads mp_max, then mp_cur. If mp_max == 0 it stops. Otherwise it sets control 2 text and gauge 2 the same way.
6. It opens the frame (FUN_00483430 state 3).
7. It stores the uid in the first zero entry of the 5-entry party uid array at scene+0x25C..+0x26C. If all 5 are used, the uid is not stored.
8. It looks up the entity by uid in the scene entity list (FUN_004189f0). If the entity exists, it sets entity+0x13A0 = 1. That party-member flag gives the entity a longer nameplate draw range.

S2C 0x51 (party member removed) later clears entity+0x13A0, finds the frame by frame+0x134 == uid, closes it and zeroes the uid in the scene array. If the uid equals the local uid at scene+0x220, 0x51 instead closes all 4 frames and clears the whole array.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C51, party#02/#13): the EN party frame renders ONLY the two gauges - the "%u/%u" label text is not drawn in this skin, so values must be read from gauge length or memory. 0x4F does NOT recompute scene+0x96D (party average level); that happens on player REGISTRATION (RegisterLocalPlayer, i.e. a 0x04/0x05/0x07 spawn). The client can hold only 4 remote members: with all four frames bound a 5th 0x4F is silently ignored, so scene+0x26C (the 5th slot of the scene party array) is unreachable through 0x4F.
specs.trigger: When a party forms or a player joins (after the C2S accept): send each member one 0x4F per OTHER member, and send the new member one 0x4F per existing member. Also plausible on map change or re-login to rebuild the HUD.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
GATE: if all 4 frames 0x75..0x78 are bound (+0x134 != 0) or missing, nothing is read. That caps the HUD at 4 other members.

HAZARD 1: frame+0x134 and the name are written BEFORE the hp_max and mp_max checks. With hp_max == 0 or mp_max == 0, the frame stays bound to the uid but is never opened, the uid is not added to the scene party array, and the entity flag is not set. The slot then looks occupied but is invisible. A later 0x51 for that uid may not free it: FUN_00446300 skips the state change when the window is already in the requested state (0x4463FF..0x44640B), and the +0x134 clear sits on that close path (0x446880). Always send nonzero hp_max and mp_max.

HAZARD 2: there is no duplicate-uid check, so sending the same uid twice uses up two frames.

HAZARD 3: there is no check that the uid differs from the local player's uid.

HAZARD 4: the name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes. Otherwise strcpy (FUN_004838c0 at 0x483937) runs past the 17-byte stack buffer.

HAZARD 5: the scene array has 5 slots but only 4 frames exist.
LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C11, party#04): the "always send nonzero hp_max and mp_max" rule also applies to S2C 0x54 and 0x55 - a max of 0 there zeroes the receiver's entity copy and blanks the overhead bar even though the party frame itself is gated.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: The two analysts agree on the free-frame gate, the read order (str[17] name, u32 uid, u16 hp_max, u16 hp_cur, stop if hp_max == 0, u16 mp_max, u16 mp_cur) and every field width. They disagree only on whether the handler also stops when mp_max == 0. Analyst A says it does; Analyst B's grammar leaves that stop out, although B's hazard text mentions it. The asm settles it for A. Right after the mp_cur read at 0x456A1B, the code runs 0x456A1D MOV AX,word ptr [ESP+0xA8]; 0x456A25 TEST AX,AX; 0x456A28 JZ 0x44D7AD, which is the shared no-op break. [ESP+0xA8] holds mp_max: the read at 0x456A04 does LEA ECX,[ESP+0xB4] after three pushes, which gives base+0xA8. That jump skips the MP text and gauge, the frame open (0x456AAE), the scene uid-array insert (0x456AC5..0x456ADE) and the entity+0x13A0 flag (0x456B00). This is the same pattern as the HP check at 0x456960..0x45696B. The Ghidra pseudo-C folds these jumps into its case structure, which probably explains B's omission. Both analysts treat the first u16 of each pair as the max. The asm confirms this: the raw bytes at 0x4569D8 and 0x456A93 are DE F9 (FDIVP ST(1),ST(0), so ST1 = ST1/ST0). The first FILD loads the second read (cur) and the second FILD loads the first read (max), so the gauge is cur/max, and the zero test is on the divisor. B's length note is also wrong: with hp_max == 0 the client has read 17+4+2+2 = 25 bytes, not 23, because both HP reads come before the test. OTHER REFERENCES: KR Hex-Rays case 0x4F has the same read order and both zero checks (per A). KR also flags the local player entity, which EN does not. PySlayer has no 0x4F builder. Our server (windslayer_server.py) has no party packets; one comment near line 1903 notes the 0x75.. widget pool is party-only.
open_questions: Whether the original server sent 0x4F describing the local player to itself. EN never flags the local entity, and there are only 4 frames, which suggests frames hold other members only.

[RESOLVED by live verification party#13, 2026-09-17] Live: it is unreachable through 0x4F - only 4 frames exist, so a 5th member is never stored. The client-side cap is 4 remote members (a party of 5 including self). Original question: "What the 5th scene party-array slot (scene+0x26C) is for, given only 4 frames."

HAZARD 1's detail (a hidden bound frame is never freed by 0x51) rests on the FUN_00446300 same-state early exit at 0x44640B. That exit was seen, but the full close path to 0x446880 was not traced end-to-end.

spec_errata.old: the max = 0 rule was stated for 0x4F only
spec_errata.new: rule extended to 0x54/0x55

spec_errata.old: frame said to show "hp_cur/hp_max" text; 5th scene slot unexplained
spec_errata.new: gauges only; 4-member cap; average level updates on registration, not on 0x4F

spec_errata.old: what the 5th scene party-array slot is for
spec_errata.new: unreachable via 0x4F; cap is 4 remote members

specs.name: PartyMemberRemove

locations.role: local: for each of 5 scene party slots: entity flag 0x13A0=0, slot=0
CMP window_id,3 / JGE - frame-compaction loop is dead code (id >= 0x75 always)
remote: hide the matched frame (clears frame+0x134 via FUN_00446300 case 1)
remote: zero every scene+0x25C..+0x26C slot equal to uid
FUN_00425AF0(scene, scene+0x970 local entity, 1) with AX=0: recompute local player group state
shared tail: FUN_00443840 (HUD stats), FUN_00443690 (HUD HP), FUN_0043D4E0 (refresh party frames HP from entities)

specs.grammar: u32 member_uid

fields.name: member_uid
fields.meaning: uid of the member leaving/removed from the party. If equal to the local player's uid (scene+0x220) the whole party is dissolved client-side.
fields.dest_or_source: [esp+0x6c]; compared to scene+0x220, frame+0x134 of windows 0x75..0x78, scene+0x25C..+0x26C; entity lookup -> +0x13A0 cleared

specs.semantics: Reads one u32 uid. Looks up that entity and clears its party flag (+0x13A0 = 0). If uid == local player uid (scene+0x220): hides all four party frames 0x75..0x78 (hiding a visible frame zeroes its +0x134), and for each nonzero uid in the 5-slot scene party list clears that entity's +0x13A0 and zeroes the slot -> party fully disbanded locally. Otherwise: finds the frame whose +0x134 == uid; if found, hides it (frame compaction code exists but is dead because it compares the window id (0x75..0x78) against 3, so remaining frames are NOT shifted and a gap is left; 0x4F reuses the first free frame); then zeroes any scene party slot equal to uid. Both paths then call FUN_00425AF0(scene, local entity, 1) and refresh HUD stats/HP and party frame HP bars (FUN_00443840, FUN_00443690, FUN_0043D4E0).
specs.trigger: Server sends to all remaining party members with the leaver's uid when a member leaves (C2S 0x29, 'Break Party', no payload) or disconnects; sends to the leaving player with THEIR OWN uid to clear all frames; on disband send each member their own uid.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Unknown uid is harmless (no frame match, no slot match). The local player's own entity +0x13A0 (set to 1 by RegisterLocalPlayer 0x422120) is cleared when the self-uid form is received; KR restores it elsewhere - cosmetic nameplate-range effect only. If the target frame was never shown (0x4F aborted on hp_max/mp_max==0) the hide is skipped and frame+0x134 stays bound (leak). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C51, party#12): live-confirmed that 0x51 does NOT compact the frame array - removing the member bound to frame 1 leaves a gap and the remaining frames stay where they are (0x4F reuses the first free frame). The party-chat gate reads the scene party ARRAY, not the frames.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x51 matches (u32 read, self vs other branch, same dead '<3' compaction loop with frame base 45). PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x51.py builds p16 'Item' with a '??' comment - DISAGREES with the binary (EN reads u32 uid) and is not referenced by PySlayer code. Memory reference_opcode_atlas.md line mentioning dispatch[0x51]=0x4582B3 does not match the jump table: binary index table gives opcode 0x51 -> index 51 -> 0x456B44. Our server: not implemented.
open_questions: Exact effect of FUN_00425AF0 with AX=0 (appears to recompute team/group grouping via entity+0x14EB when scene+0xF88+0x70==1); not needed for the wire format.
blind_open_questions: Whether the server must also send 0x51 for each remaining member to the leaver, or whether one 0x51 with the leaver's own uid is enough. The client local branch clears everything, so one packet suffices client-side.
Exact visual effect of entity+0x13A0 and FUN_00425af0 (probably nameplate color or party marker) was not traced.

spec_errata.new: live-confirmed: no compaction, gap remains

specs.name: PlayerInfoView (remote character info window)

C2S request 0x2A + str[17] name sent when target NOT in scene (Add u8 0x2A @0x44A656, Add(char*,0x11) @0x44A669, Send @0x4484CC)

specs.grammar:
str[17] char_name
i32 manner_points
u8 level
u8 rank
u8 job1
u8 job2
u16 stat_str
u16 stat_dex
u16 stat_int
u16 stat_spr

repeat(equip_count) {

fields.name: char_name
fields.meaning: character name, shown in window 0x72 label 1
fields.dest_or_source: stack local base+0x330 (UI only; not stored on any entity)

fields.name: manner_points
fields.meaning: manner points (same value as entity+0x15D8, which S2C 0x96/0x97 adjust with 'added %d of your manner points'); printed '%d' in label 0x25, red (0xFFFF0000) if <0 else white

fields.name: level
fields.meaning: character level, label 2 'Lv.%u' (entity+0x99 in local path)

fields.name: rank
fields.meaning: PvP/arena rank index into 20-byte name table @0x70BDC8 (0=Trainee, 1..9 Trainee Lv.1-9, 10.. Battler, ... 96 Archangel, 97 Monarch, 98 Windslayer); label 0x24, and stored into window 0x72 +0x134 via FUN_00483270 (entity+0x9A in local path)

fields.name: job1
fields.meaning: base class 0..6 (Novice,Warrior,Monk,Archer,Rogue,Mage,Priest) (entity+0x110 in local path)

fields.name: job2
fields.meaning: job advancement tier 0..2 (entity+0x111); class label 3 text = 15-byte table @0x70C588 at index (job2*7+job1), only if job1<7 && job2<=2

fields.name: stat_str
fields.meaning: stat shown in label 5 '%u' (entity+0xE6 in local path; KR names str)

fields.name: stat_dex
fields.meaning: stat shown in label 6 (entity+0xE8; KR dex)

fields.name: stat_int
fields.meaning: stat shown in label 7 (entity+0xEA; KR int/wisdom)

fields.name: stat_spr
fields.meaning: stat shown in label 8 (entity+0xEC; KR tol, EN create-char calls it spr)

fields.name: equip_count
fields.meaning: number of equipment entries; MUST be <=25 (stack arrays sized for 25)

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item id of entry i (entity+0x13C[i] in local path: slots 0..15 equipment grid, 16..24 the extra/cash u16[9]); 0 = empty, skipped

fields.name: option_count
fields.meaning: number of leading option/enchant words for this entry; keep <=5

fields.name: option
fields.meaning: option/enchant word j of entry i (entity+0x16E block, 6 u16 per slot)

fields.name: option_last
fields.meaning: 6th option word of entry i (always present)

specs.semantics: Opens UI window 0x72 (FUN_00483430(0x72,3,1)) = the other-player character info panel and fills it: label1=name, label 0x25=manner points (red if negative), label2='Lv.%u', label3=class name (if job1<7 && job2<=2), label4 hardcoded ' Not in the Guild' (no guild field on wire), labels 5..8 = four u16 stats, label 0x24 = rank name, window+0x134=rank. Then if window 0x72 exists it is cleared (FUN_0047d700) and for i in 0..24 with item_id[i]!=0 it allocates a 0x38-byte item object {+0 u16 id, +2..+0xD the 6 option words, +0x20 flag=1 if item_template+0x1F0 != 0}, and adds it to window 0x72's item list (FUN_00489A80(...,0) for normal items, FUN_00489C30 for flagged/cash items). Entries are copied by index; the object stores no slot index. Nothing is written to any entity; no uid is carried. Server reply to C2S 0x2A (view info of a player not in the requester's scene).
specs.trigger: Server response to C2S 0x2A str[17] target_name, which the client sends from the player popup window 0x50 control 3 (view info) only when the target uid is not found in the local scene (if it is, the client fills window 0x72 locally from the entity and sends nothing). Send 0x53 instead if the target is offline.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No read gates: all fields always read. HAZARDS: equip_count > 25 overflows stack arrays (u16[25] at base+0x4F4 and 25x12 bytes at base+0xED0) inside the 0x12FC-byte handler frame -> stack corruption/crash. option_count > 5 spills into the trailing word/next entry; >6 on the last entries can run past base+0xFFC. rank >= 99 indexes past the rank table (garbage label text). job1>=7 or job2>=3 leaves the class label stale. Window opens even if items are empty.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays 0x52 is a much larger char-info layout (13x12 + 19x3 words, guild block, etc.) - NOT compatible with EN. PySlayer has no 0x52 builder. Field names cross-checked against the client's local twin at FUN_00446300 0x44A01C which fills the same labels from entity +0x15D8/+0x99/+0x110/+0x111/+0xE6..+0xEC/+0x9A/+0x13C/+0x16E. enter_world_fields.md calls +0x15D8 'money' - wrong, it is manner points (SubHandler3 0x96/0x97 and nameplate red if < -9). windslayer_server.py comments +0xE6..+0xEC as 'equip-appearance/dye ids' - this window prints them as '%u' stats (PySlayer KR: str/dex/int/tol). Not implemented in our server.
open_questions: Exact meaning of the four u16 stats (str/dex/int/spr naming comes from KR PySlayer and EN create-char, not from a label string in this window).
Whether the item list in window 0x72 positions items by entry index or by item kind (item object carries no slot index, so position likely comes from item data or insertion order).
Which option word is which enchant (option[0..4] variable count vs fixed option_last at +0xA) is unresolved.
ResetBuffer for the 0x2A request was not located inside FUN_00446300 (Send path shared at 0x4484C4).
blind_open_questions: Exact stat order: ctrl5..8 match entity +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC. The mapping to Strength/Dexterity/Intelligence/Spirit (string table 0x701760 order) is inferred, not proven.
Meaning of item_extra (record +0x0A / item struct +0x0C): maybe durability, refine level or expiry; not traced.

(format "%s%s" with no space; EN string at 0x6F5128 has no leading space, so include a trailing space in the name only if cosmetic spacing is desired - but the field is fixed 17 bytes) in color 0xFFFD4C87 via FUN_004817d0. No state change. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C49): this text renders in the fading FLOATING NOTICE overlay (right side / bottom right above the HUD buttons), NOT as a line in the chat log.
specs.trigger: Negative reply to a name-targeted lookup, at least C2S 0x2A (view player info) when the target is offline; the positive reply is 0x52.
specs.gates_and_hazards: None. Name must be NUL-terminated within the 17 bytes (sprintf_s %s on the stack buffer; a non-terminated 17-byte name would run into adjacent stack bytes).
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays 0x53 is identical in shape (str[17] + '님은 서버에 없습니다.'). PySlayer opcode_0x53.py is a broken stub (emits opcode byte 0x51 + str[17]). Not in our server.

specs.name: EntityHpUpdate (party member HP)

locations.role: FUN_004189f0 entity lookup by uid (entity+0x84) in scene list
party frames 0x75..0x78 matched by widget+0x134==uid; label 1 '%u/%u' (cur/max), gauge 1 = cur/max

specs.grammar:
u32 uid
u16 max_hp
u16 cur_hp

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: entity uid (matched against entity+0x84 and party widget+0x134)

fields.name: max_hp
fields.meaning: maximum HP
fields.dest_or_source: entity+0x110C (zero-extended u32) if entity in scene

fields.name: cur_hp
fields.meaning: current HP
fields.dest_or_source: entity+0x9C (zero-extended u32) if entity in scene

specs.semantics: If an entity with this uid is in the scene, writes entity+0x110C=max_hp and entity+0x9C=cur_hp. Then, if max_hp != 0, calls FUN_0043d3f0 which scans party member frames (UI windows 0x75..0x78) for one whose +0x134 equals uid and sets its label 1 to "%u/%u" (cur/max) and gauge 1 to cur/max. HP bar only exists for party members (frames registered by S2C 0x4F); for monsters/non-party it only updates the entity HP fields silently. No HUD refresh for the local player, no death handling.
specs.trigger: Server sends to party members when a party member's HP (or max HP) changes. Could also be used to sync a remote entity's HP value.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Entity write skipped if uid not in scene (reads still complete). UI update skipped when max_hp==0 (avoids divide by zero). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C11, party#04): max_hp = 0 is NOT a no-op - the entity write happens FIRST, so it zeroes the receiver's copy of the member's max HP and BLANKS that entity's overhead bar. The "never send max = 0" rule documented for 0x4F must be extended to 0x54 and, by symmetry, to 0x55 (party-vitals-sync). cur>max just overfills the gauge. Does not kill the entity at 0 HP.
specs.references: KR build merges HP/MP into 0x54 with a leading u8 type (1=HP, 2=MP); EN splits HP=0x54, MP=0x55 and has no type byte. Our server _build_opcode_54 (windslayer_server.py ~1930) matches this layout exactly (u32 uid, u16 max, u16 cur) but is no longer sent (hit feedback removed); its docstring's 'floating HP-bar' is the party frame, as reference_combat_model.md already notes.
open_questions: Whether FUN_004189f0's scene list includes the local player (if so 0x54 can also set local entity+0x9C, but no HUD redraw happens here).
blind_open_questions: Monsters spawned via 0x1A appear to be in the list FUN_004189f0 walks (0x1A calls RegisterLocalPlayer, which uses the scene+0x08 list). Direct list insertion was not traced to the byte.

spec_errata.new: max_hp = 0 zeroes the entity copy and blanks the overhead bar

Then finds the first party member frame (windows 0x75..0x78) whose +0x134 == uid (and != 0); if found and max_mp != 0 sets label 2 to "%u/%u" (cur/max) and gauge 2 to cur/max. specs.name: EntitySkillLearned

locations.role: FUN_004189f0 entity lookup; exit if not found (skill id NOT read)
FUN_00404210 item template lookup (itemdb[id-1]); require template+0x154 == 3
FUN_00426b80(scene, entity+0x29A, id, template+0x1DC) picks slot in 30-entry learned-skill list
write u16 id into returned slot
slot chooser: same skill family (id - |level|) with lower level -> replace; same family >= level -> 0; else first empty of 30; full -> 0; level==0 -> 0

specs.length: 6 (server should always send 6; client consumes only 4 if uid is not in scene, harmless since nothing follows)

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: entity uid whose skill list is updated

fields.name: skill_item_id
fields.meaning: item/skill id of a skill record (template Type field +0x154 must be 3; template +0x1DC = skill level within its family, family base = id - level)
fields.dest_or_source: entity+0x29A[k] (u16[30] learned-skill list), k chosen by FUN_00426b80

specs.semantics: Adds or upgrades a learned skill on an entity in the scene: looks up the item template for skill_item_id; if Type (+0x154) == 3 (skill), calls FUN_00426b80 over the entity's 30-entry u16 learned-skill list at +0x29A. If a skill of the same family (id - |template+0x1DC|) is present with a lower id, it is replaced; if the same family is already at >= this id nothing changes; if the family is absent the first empty (0) slot gets the id; if all 30 are full nothing happens. No UI message, no refresh. The same list is filled at spawn by the u8-count u16 loop in 0x07/0x2B, is checked by FUN_00467680 ('You already have learned this skill.'), and is updated for the local player by FUN_00440920 case 3.
specs.trigger: When a player learns or levels a skill, to keep that entity's skill list in sync (likely broadcast to players who can see it, or sent to the learner).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Stops silently if uid not in scene, if the id has no template, if template Type != 3, if template skill level (+0x1DC) == 0, or if the list is full / already at an equal or higher level. Unknown ids are bounds-checked (no crash).
specs.references: PySlayer opcode_0x57.py (KR) sends u8 + u32 + u16 ('About Item/skill') - EN has no leading u8. wsre.py labels 0x57 'QuestLogAdd/Reward' and project_status.md mentions a '0x57 log-add' quest fallback - WRONG for EN. enter_world_fields.md / our 0x07 builder call the +0x29A u16 loop an 'inventory count/extras' - it is the learned-skill list. gamedef note: starter quest item 377 is Type=3, consistent with Type 3 = skill. Not implemented in our server.
open_questions: Which C2S action (skill-book use / trainer learn) makes the original server send 0x57, and whether it goes to the learner, to observers, or both.
Whether the scene list searched by FUN_004189f0 includes the local player (if yes, 0x57 also updates the local skill list without a skill-window refresh).
blind_open_questions: Whether the local player's own entity is in the scene+0x0C list so 0x57 with the local uid also changes the local skill list (likely yes, not verified).
Exact meaning of item template +0x1DC (treated as skill level from the id - |level| family math and FUN_00443e80(this, id, +0x1DC) in the local path).

specs.name: PlayerClassChange

locations.role: FUN_004189f0(scene=[game_state+0x4CC], EDX=uid). Returns 0 right away if uid==0, otherwise walks the list at scene+0x0C (node[0]=next, node[8]=entity) and matches entity+0x84
JZ 0x44D7AD: if the lookup returns null, break (nothing more is read)
CMP byte [entity+0x111],0 then JNZ break (no recompute when non-zero)
FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0): recompute max HP (+0x110C) and clamp cur HP (+0x9C). Returns early if level==0, level>99 or class>=7 (0x427D48..0x427D67)
only if entity+0x99 (level) != 0: FUN_00427f40(0) with ESI=entity, recompute max MP (+0x1110) and clamp cur MP (+0xA0)

FUN_004781c0(game_state+0xD2C): rebuild the LOCAL player's available-quest list. The filter at 0x4782F0 reads [quest+0xC40+(class*3+tier)*4] using the local player (scene+0x970), not the uid in this packet

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: UID of the player whose class changed. Matched against entity+0x84 in the scene list at scene+0x0C. uid 0 or an unknown uid means the handler stops here and ignores the rest of the packet.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x1B0], used only as the lookup key

fields.name: class
fields.meaning: Base class index into the 15-byte name table at 0x70C588, row 0: 0 Novice, 1 Warrior, 2 Monk, 3 Archer, 4 Rogue, 5 Mage, 6 Priest. 0 means no class change yet: FUN_00446300 at 0x4493D2 shows 'You can use [Battlefield] after class change'. The HP and MP recompute functions return early if it is 7 or more.

fields.name: class_tier
fields.meaning: Advancement tier/branch, 0..2. The name index is (tier*7+class)*15 (0x440CAE..0x440CC0). Tier-1 row: 8 Berserker, 9 Fighter, 10 Sniper, 11 Assassin, 12 Elementalist, 13 Bishop. Tier-2 row: 14 Paladin, 15 Counter, 16 BeastMaster, 17 Trapper, 18 Summoner, 19 DarkPriest, 20 empty. The quest filter indexes class*3+tier with no bounds check, so the value must be 2 or less. If 0, the client recomputes stats, HP, MP and the quest list. If not 0, it only stores the two bytes.

specs.length: 6 (4+1+1) when the uid is found; only 4 bytes consumed when it is not. Always send all 6.
specs.semantics: Reads the uid and looks up the entity. If it is not found, processing ends and the last 2 bytes are ignored. Otherwise it stores class at +0x110 and class_tier at +0x111. These are the same fields that 0x02 and 0x07 fill. If class_tier == 0, the client then (1) runs FUN_0041ace0 to recompute derived stats, (2) runs FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) to recompute max HP (+0x110C) and lower cur HP (+0x9C) if it is above the new max, (3) if level (+0x99) != 0, runs FUN_00427f40(0) to recompute max MP (+0x1110) and clamp cur MP (+0xA0), and (4) runs FUN_004781c0 to rebuild the local player's available-quest list. There is no popup, no sound and no reply packet.
specs.trigger: Server sends this when a character's class changes (job advancement). Send it to the player and to clients that have that entity spawned.
specs.expected_response: none (no Add/Send in the block or its callees)
specs.gates_and_hazards: No in-world gate. FUN_004189f0 returns null for uid 0 without touching the scene. For uid != 0 it dereferences scene+0x0C without a null check, so the scene object must exist. An unknown uid is silently ignored. A non-zero class_tier skips all stat/HP/MP/quest recompute, so derived stats stay stale until something else recomputes them. A class of 7 or more makes the HP/MP recompute return early and indexes past the name table. A class_tier above 2 overlaps the next class's quest flags. HP and MP are only clamped down (arg 0). The quest refresh needs the local player object ([+0x928] != 0 check at 0x4781D0). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (login_character#16): 0x58 does NOT redraw the local status window or the HUD class label - they keep the old class name until another FUN_00442510 redraw. For the owner, follow it with a packet that forces a redraw (e.g. the 0x18 job-item path or 0x74).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 @0x45760F), a lookup via FUN_004189f0 @0x457623 with JZ break @0x45762E, then u8 into +0x110 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457647) and u8 into +0x111 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457664), then a recompute gate on +0x111==0 @0x457673. They differ only in how the DSL writes it. A wrote 'if(found){u8 u8} else {stop}'. B wrote 'if(null){stop} u8 u8'. Both put the same bytes in the same order under the same condition, so neither is wrong. I chose A's explicit if/else because it maps directly onto the asm's JZ-to-break. B's field notes are also verified: the Battlefield gate at 0x4493D2 checks +0x110==0, and the quest filter at 0x4782DD..0x4782F0 uses class*3+tier. A's name-table claim is verified by dumping 0x70C588 from the exe, with one correction: the tier-2 row is not aligned with the class indexes (index 14=Paladin sits at class 0). Other references: PySlayer KR Hex-Rays case 0x58 reads u32 plus three u8 and gates on the third. EN reads two u8 and gates on the second, so EN is 6 bytes and must not copy the KR layout. PySlayer has no server builder for 0x58. Our server has no 0x58 builder, but its 0x02/0x07 builders write class/0 into the same two fields.
open_questions: Tier-2 name row at 0x70C588 is shifted by one versus the class index: (2*7+1)=15 is 'Counter' for Warrior, (2*7+0)=14 is 'Paladin' for Novice, and Priest tier 2 is empty. So either class_tier is not a simple sequential tier, or the client string table has an off-by-one. Needs a live check of which (class, tier) pairs the real server used.
Why stats, HP, MP and quests are only recomputed when class_tier == 0 is unclear.
Which C2S request or NPC flow triggers a class change in EN was not traced.

spec_errata.old: UI refresh behaviour unstated
spec_errata.new: no local redraw - follow with one

specs.name: QuestProgressUpdate

locations.role: GetDataFromPacket u8 progress, read directly into char+0x25B+slot
quest completion-condition check (Money vs gold, ReqPro vs progress, Demand items in bag)
chat/system line "[%s] You are ready to complete the quest." color 0xFF00C800

specs.length: 2 (1 if slot >= 4, when the rest is ignored)

fields.name: slot
fields.meaning: 1-based active-quest slot (1..3), the index into char+0x256 u16[3]. Checked with a SIGNED test slot-1 < 3, so 0 is also accepted (hazard). A value of 4 or more ends reading with no UI refresh.

fields.name: progress
fields.meaning: Absolute progress counter for that slot (e.g. kill count), compared against quest record ReqPro (+0xDF8) and shown in the active-quest tab as progress/ReqPro.

specs.semantics: Updates one active quest's progress counter. The byte goes straight into char+0x25B+slot. Then, if that slot's ready flag at char+0x25E+slot is 0 and the quest record for the slot's quest id (u16 at char+0x254+2*slot) exists, the client calls FUN_00426500(ctx+0x10, record, progress, gold64 at char+0x228, bag arrays...). That function returns 1 when all of these hold: (Money >= 0, or gold >= |Money|), (ReqPro == 0, or progress >= ReqPro), and every Demand item (up to 10; types 0 and 2 counted in the bags, type 1 via FUN_00424df0, type 5 skipped) is present in sufficient count. On success the client sets the ready flag to 1 and prints "[<quest name>] You are ready to complete the quest." in green. The message appears once, because the flag suppresses repeats. The quest window is refreshed whenever slot <= 3. The ready flag only controls the message; the turn-in logic re-checks the conditions itself.
specs.trigger: Server sends it whenever a tracked quest counter changes, e.g. a monster kill counted toward ReqPro. It can also be sent with an unchanged value to re-evaluate readiness.
specs.expected_response: none (the player then talks to the ENPC, which sends C2S 0x17 turn-in)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Skipped entirely if ctx+4 or ctx+8 is null. slot=0 passes the signed check and writes progress into char+0x25B, the HIGH byte of active slot 3's quest id (u16 at 0x25A). That corrupts the quest log, and the client then reads a garbage quest id from char+0x254. Only send slot 1..3. Progress is a u8 (max 255). The slot must match the client's own placement: 0x26 fills the first empty slot, and 0x27/0x38 empty the slot.
specs.references: PySlayer opcode_59: p8(random slot) + p8u(unk), which agrees on 2 bytes. Its comment 'v47 - 1 < 5' suggests the newer KR build has 5 slots; EN checks < 3. Our server's _send_quest_progress packs '<BB' slot(1..3), count, which matches. It assigns slots lowest-free in _quest_assign_slot, the same rule as the client.
open_questions: Which game events the original server counted into progress: ReqPro with the NPC field at +0xDFC, possibly a target monster id. Not decidable from this handler.
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of def+0xDF8 (kill count vs generic counter) not confirmed from the quest data loader; FUN_00478380 display of progress not traced.
Whether FUN_00465290 (inventory refresh, also calls FUN_00426500) sets the ready flag on item pickup without any 0x59 was not traced.

spec_errata.source: IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md 1.2.6 (b); roadmap S1-03; quest_cards_misc.md E6/Q-B18. For a u8 slot the client test (int)slot-1 < 3 is exactly slot < 4 (slot 0 still passes).

specs.name: KeyExchangeSeed

locations.role: handler block (primary switch, index table idx 59)
re-init billing/cash object at game_state+0x700 (no packet reads)
MD5 hex of username -> game_state+0xD0A (no packet reads)
C2S build: Add u8 0x01, Add str[41] scene+0x48, Add str[21] scene+0x101
C2S SEND SITE #40: Send(1) login request

specs.grammar: i32 code_key_seed

fields.name: code_key_seed
fields.meaning: Cipher seed for the game connection; passed straight to CSNSocket::SetCodeKey so all following traffic on g_sock_game uses the keyed stream

specs.semantics: First packet on the game server connection. Client installs the key (SetCodeKey), re-initialises the cash/billing sub-object at gs+0x700 (stores game_state, ui root, socket, scene+0xF84, &username), computes MD5(username) as 32 hex chars into gs+0xD0A and sets scene+0x218 = 1 if it differs from the 32-char string at scene+0x131 (else 0; later drives the 'Account transfer' text in 0x02). It then sleeps 1000 ms and sends C2S 0x01 login = str[41] username (scene+0x48) + str[21] password (scene+0x101), 62 bytes after the opcode, which matches the captured 62-byte login.
specs.trigger: Server sends immediately on accepting the TCP connection to 7022 (before any client traffic). At Fireway level it must carry the NoEncode flag and be encoded with EncodebyArray since no key exists yet (per our server/memory).
specs.expected_response: C2S 0x01 login: str[41] username, str[21] password (62 bytes), sent ~1 s later, encrypted with the new key. Server should answer with S2C 0x02.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate other than the global [gs+0x408]!=0 drop. Any 0x5A received mid-session re-keys the cipher (desync unless the server re-keys identically), blocks the network thread 1 s inside the receive critical section, and re-sends login (our server ignores mid-flow 0x01).
specs.references: Our GameServer._handle_fireway sends 0x5A + <i seed with NoEncode+EncodebyArray - matches. protocol.md matches (MD5, Sleep 1000, login send). PySlayer KR 0x5A handler is the same idea but the KR login it triggers carries many more fields (id + 3 more strings + 4 bytes); EN sends only username[41]+password[21].
open_questions: Origin of the 32-char string at scene+0x131 compared against MD5(username) (probably launcher/command-line supplied) was not traced; it only affects the account-transfer UI text in 0x02.
blind_open_questions: What populates scene+0x131 (the 32-char hash compared against MD5(username)); it only affects the ID-transfer UI in 0x02.
Whether SetCodeKey changes the per-packet cipher in this Fireway build (memory notes say only the static table is live).

specs.name: PlayerRoomBalloonSet

locations.role: FUN_004189f0 entity lookup by uid (uid 0 means null)
TEST ESI,ESI then JZ 0x44D7AD: break if not found
GetDataFromPacket u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) into entity+0xE1 (room type), read unconditionally
GetDataFromPacket char buffer N=0x11 (IAT 0x4A4098) into entity+0xD0 (room title), read unconditionally
cross-check: the 0x04/0x07 spawn record reads u16 +0xE2 and, only if non-zero, u8 +0xE1 and char[17] +0xD0

render: if +0xE2==0x81 draw sprite 0x168 (no title). Else if +0xE2!=0: type==4 draws sprite 0x19C and a coloured title, otherwise sprite 0x87 and a title. Draw_Text(+0xD0) at 0x431945. Gated by [game_state+0x4D8]+0x70==0 and g_ui_root+0x40!=0

click on a player with +0xE2!=0: open dialog 0x133. 0x81 shows 'Enter the cash shop?'. Otherwise sprintf '[%s] %s' with the title: type<4 'Enter the arena?', ==4 'Would you enter the play room?', >4 'Will you subscribe to join the battle?'. Stores room no in dlg+0x134 and type in dlg+0x40

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: UID of the player whose room balloon is being set. uid 0 or an unknown uid means nothing more is read.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x1B4], used only as the lookup key

fields.name: room_no
fields.meaning: Room number the player is in. 0 = none (no balloon, not clickable). 0x81 = cash-shop marker (the same value S2C 0x75 writes): draws sprite 0x168 with no title and the click prompt is 'Enter the cash shop?'. Any other non-zero value draws a room balloon, and clicking it opens join dialog 0x133 carrying this number.

fields.name: room_type
fields.meaning: Room kind. Below 4 = arena ('Enter the arena?', sprite 0x87). 4 = play/chat room ('Would you enter the play room?', sprite 0x19C, coloured title). Above 4 = battle ('Will you subscribe to join the battle?', sprite 0x87). Read even when room_no == 0.

fields.name: room_title
fields.meaning: Room title drawn in the balloon and used in the '[%s] %s' join prompt. Exactly 17 raw bytes with no NUL forced, followed directly in memory by +0xE1/+0xE2. Send at most 16 characters, NUL-padded. Read even when room_no == 0.

specs.length: 24 (4+2+1+17) when the uid is found; only 4 bytes consumed when it is not. Always send all 24.
specs.semantics: Looks up the player by uid. If not found, processing ends. Otherwise it overwrites the player's room info: u16 room number (+0xE2), u8 room type (+0xE1) and a 17-byte title (+0xD0). All three are read unconditionally, unlike the spawn record, which skips type and title when the room number is 0. With room_no != 0 the client draws a room balloon over that player, and clicking the player offers to join that room (dialog 0x133 gets the room number and type). Send room_no=0 to clear the balloon. There is no UI refresh, no sound and no reply.
specs.trigger: Broadcast to clients in the same field when a player creates, enters or leaves an arena room, play room or battle room, so others see or lose the balloon and can click to join. 0x07 can carry the same state at spawn.
specs.expected_response: none directly. If a viewer confirms dialog 0x133, the client sends a join request (not traced here).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No in-world gate. Scene must exist when uid != 0 (FUN_004189f0 dereferences scene+0x0C). An unknown uid is silently ignored. The title is used as a C string (sprintf_s '[%s] %s' at 0x44C968, Draw_Text at 0x431945); if all 17 bytes are non-NUL it runs into the room_type/room_no bytes, so always NUL-terminate. The balloon only draws when [game_state+0x4D8]+0x70 == 0 and g_ui_root+0x40 != 0. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C40, pvp_arena#25): a 0x5B carrying the RECEIVER'S OWN uid does draw the balloon over the local player (verified with a "Duel Room" balloon above the local character, cleared again by 0x5C). The server must therefore decide deliberately whether the room owner gets their own balloon.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts give the same wire format: u32 uid (IAT 0x4A40C8 @0x4576D8), lookup FUN_004189f0 @0x4576EC with TEST/JZ break @0x4576F3/0x4576F5, then u16 into +0xE2 (IAT 0x4A4090 @0x45770F), u8 into +0xE1 (IAT 0x4A4094 @0x457729) and char[0x11] into +0xD0 (IAT 0x4A4098, PUSH 0x11 @0x45773C, call @0x457745), then JMP break. There is no condition between the three reads. They differ only in how the DSL writes it: A 'if(found){...} else {stop}' versus B 'if(null){stop} ...'. Both put the same 24 bytes in the same order, so neither is wrong. I chose A's explicit if/else form. B's extra facts are verified: S2C 0x75 writes +0xE2=0x81 at 0x457FD3; type/title are read unconditionally here but only when +0xE2 != 0 in the spawn record (0x44F03C JZ 0x44F07C); and the render gates at 0x4317B3..0x4317CD. A's render and click details are verified at 0x4317DA..0x4318F2 and 0x44C8C5..0x44C9AE. Other references: memory note project_local_player_spawn.md calls +0xE2 'marriage'; the binary shows it is the room number/balloon, though that note's read order matches. Not present in PySlayer server_packets or the KR Hex-Rays excerpt. Our server has no builder.

The C2S join request sent after confirming dialog 0x133 was not traced.

[RESOLVED by live verification pvp_arena#25, 2026-09-17] Live: yes - 0x5B for the receiver's own uid draws the balloon above the local player and 0x5C removes it, so sending it to the owner is a deliberate server choice, not a no-op. specs.name: ForcedDisconnect

locations.role: WM_TIMER id 7 -> PostMessageA(hwnd, WM_CLOSE) -> game_state+0x408=1 (client exits)

specs.grammar: u8 reason

fields.name: reason
fields.meaning: Kick reason. 1='Disconnected due to unusual game play.' 2='Disconnected due to unusual\r\ninput delay.' 3='Identified as an macro tool user,\r\nDisconnecting.' 99='Transferring to server failed.' Any other value='Connection to Server got disconnected'.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [base+0x4A] (zeroed first), passed in EAX to FUN_0044d4b0

specs.semantics: Reads a u8 reason. Calls FUN_0044d4b0 with ESI=game_state. If game_state+0x408==0 (window not already closing) and game_state+0x1528==0 (no disconnect already handled), it sets +0x1528=1 and shows the reason text in a modal message box (FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0)). It then starts SetTimer(hwnd@game_state+0xE0, id 7, 5000 ms). When timer 7 fires, the window proc posts WM_CLOSE and the client shuts down. The client does not close the socket itself here; the 5-second timer closes the whole game.
specs.trigger: Server-initiated kick: anti-cheat or speed-hack detection (1), input-lag detection (2), macro detection (3), failed server transfer (99), or a generic disconnect (other).
specs.expected_response: Nothing is sent. The client shows the dialog and closes itself about 5 s later.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Ignored if game_state+0x408!=0 (client closing) or +0x1528!=0 (after 0x17 or an earlier disconnect notice). Only the first notice is shown. Because the game exits, don't send this for a soft error. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, quest_cards_misc#17): live-verified for reasons 1, 0x63 and 7 - the modal appears and the process is GONE within 8 s WITHOUT the user clicking OK. RECOVERY: none, the client must be restarted. A preceding S2C 0x17 suppresses both the dialog and the exit.
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x5D: reads u8 then sub_47F8B0(), the same structure. Reason strings come from FUN_0044d4b0 in the EN binary. Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py.
open_questions: What dialog style 3,3 means in FUN_00489da0 (OK-only is assumed) wasn't checked; it doesn't affect the wire format.
blind_open_questions: What the WM_TIMER id 7 handler does (probably closes the client or returns to login). Not traced in this pass.

spec_errata.new: live: process gone within 8 s without clicking OK; recovery = restart

specs.name: SkillRequestUnlock

locations.role: skill-use path: only sends C2S 0x15 <skill_id> when scene+0x258 == 0, then sets scene+0x258 = skill_id
equip path: C2S 0x0F equip only allowed when scene+0x258 == 0
S2C 0x25/0x3B skill-result handler also clears scene+0x258

specs.semantics: No payload. Clears the scene's pending-skill word (scene+0x258). The client sets that word to the skill id when it sends C2S 0x15 for a skill (FUN_0044c090). While it is non-zero, the client refuses to send another skill request and silently blocks equip/unequip (FUN_0044c2c0 / FUN_0046cad0; 'You can't equip or unequip while attacking.'). The 0x25/0x3B skill-effect handler also clears it. 0x5F releases the lock WITHOUT any effect, so it is effectively a 'skill request rejected/cancelled' reply.
specs.trigger: Send in reply to a C2S 0x15 skill request that the server rejects or will not animate (cooldown, invalid target, not enough MP, etc.). Otherwise the client stays locked until some 0x25/0x3B arrives or a map-change reset runs (FUN_0042c360 also zeroes it).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No gate. It dereferences [game_state+0x4CC] (scene) without a null check, so do not send it before the scene exists. It has no visual effect and is a no-op if no skill is pending.
specs.references: Our server's _handle_use_item (C2S 0x15) ignores non-consumable ids and sends nothing, so casting a skill there leaves scene+0x258 set: the client can't cast again and can't equip until a map change. Sending 0x5F in that branch would fix it. Not in PySlayer. The 0x25/0x3B handler at 0x453D89 clears the same word.
open_questions: Whether the original server also used 0x5F for other kinds of cancel (e.g. interrupted cast) is unknown; the client-side effect is the same either way.
blind_open_questions: Whether any UI message is expected to accompany the rejection (none in this handler).

specs.name: FriendPresenceUpdate

locations.role: friend lookup by name in CMessenger+0x08 list (strcmp)
friend/mentor list UI refresh (window 0x176); sorts entries with status!=1 before status==1
append system line to main chat (green 0xFF00C800)

specs.length: 23 (21 if the friend isn't found or the uid doesn't match; the client stops reading)

fields.name: friend_uid
fields.meaning: Friend's character uid. It must equal the uid given for this friend in S2C 0x0B/0x0C (entry+0x18), or the packet is ignored.

fields.name: friend_name
fields.meaning: Friend's name, used as the lookup key into the friend list (CMessenger+0x08).

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Channel number the friend is on. Shown as 'Channel %d' when presence==4.

fields.name: presence
fields.meaning: 0 = online on the same channel as you ('<%s> has logged in. (Friend)'). 1 = offline (no message; list sorts it last). 4 = online on another channel ('<%s> has logged in.(Friend, Channel %d)'). Other values are stored with no message. The 0x07 mentor block (0x0044E5C5..0x0044E5E1) sets 1 for offline, 0 for same channel and 4 for another channel.

specs.semantics: Updates one friend's online state. The client finds the friend-list entry by name (FUN_00472180 over CMessenger+0x08). If there is no entry, or entry+0x18 != friend_uid, it stops (returns 1, nothing changes). Otherwise it reads the channel into entry+0x14 and the presence into entry+0x20. presence 4 prints green '<name> has logged in.(Friend, Channel N)' to main chat. presence 0 prints '<name> has logged in. (Friend)'. Any other value prints nothing. In all matched cases it then calls FUN_00470270 to redraw the messenger friend list and the (online/total) counter.
specs.trigger: Server sends it to every online player who has this character in their friend list when the character logs in, logs out (presence=1), or changes channel.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub3 gate: CMessenger+0x68/+0x70 must be non-null. There is no chat-room (+0xCC) gate. The friend list must already be filled by S2C 0x0B (or 0x0C add), with the same name and uid, or this packet has no effect. Send only after S2C 0x07 has initialised the messenger. friend_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (the local isn't pre-zeroed; the name is passed to strcmp and sprintf_s with a 0x80 buffer).
specs.references: Not in PySlayer. Not in windslayer_server.py. The friend entry layout matches the 0x0B list handler in the same function: str[17] name, u8 +0x14 channel, u32 +0x18 uid, u8 +0x20 status.

Values 2 and 3 print no chat line. Original question: "Presence values 2 and 3 (and others) are stored but have no visible meaning here. Other UI code may render them (e.g. a busy state)."

Offline (status 1) prints no 'logged out' notice; confirm that is intended.

spec_errata.new: icon mapping recorded live

specs.name: MessengerChatRoomMessage

locations.role: handler block (sub3 jump-table case 0x61). CMP [EBX+0xCC],0 / JZ 0x471FF6 happens before any read; 0x471FF6 returns 1 and reads nothing
GetDataFromPacket char buffer N=0x11 (PUSH 0x11 at 0x471343) into esp0+0x20: sender_name
memset: zeroes esp0+0x100 and esp0+0x101..0x13C (61 bytes) before the text read
GetDataFromPacket char buffer, N = MOVZX byte esp0+0x12 (0x47137D, pushed at 0x47138B), into esp0+0x100: message. This is the last read
inline strcmp of sender_name vs own name CMessenger+0x7C picks the colour (equal 0xFFC766A6, else 0xFF3277CC)
appends a text line to messenger chat-room window 0x177, split into 30-byte chunks (29 if a Hangul lead byte would be cut)
C2S 0x35 room-chat sender {u8 len, bytes[len]}; no local echo
S2C 0x0F (result==1) reads u32 into CMessenger+0xCC (room id), the gate for this packet
FUN_0046f860 (called from the S2C 0x03 handler at 0x44E52F) clears +0xCC and sets +0x74 = g_sock_game

specs.length: 18 + msg_len when in a room (keep msg_len <= 58); 0 bytes consumed when CMessenger+0xCC == 0

fields.name: sender_name
fields.meaning: Name of the room member who spoke, NUL-padded. Compared byte-wise with your own name (CMessenger+0x7C) to pick the colour of the "%s : " header line.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local esp0+0x20 (17 bytes, NOT pre-zeroed)

fields.name: msg_len
fields.meaning: Number of message bytes that follow. It is the N of the raw char-buffer read.

fields.name: message
fields.meaning: Chat text, with no terminator on the wire. It lands in a buffer whose first 61 bytes were zeroed first, so a text of up to 58 bytes is terminated by that zero fill.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local esp0+0x100 (esp0+0x100..0x13C zeroed; next local at esp0+0x140)

specs.semantics: A line of text in the Messenger 1:1 / group chat room. It is processed only while CMessenger+0xCC (the room id set by S2C 0x0F result 1, cleared on every S2C 0x03) is non-zero. Otherwise the handler returns 1 without reading anything. When processed, the client reads sender_name[17], msg_len and message[msg_len]. It then builds "%s : " from sender_name and appends it to chat-room window 0x177 via FUN_00472430. That line is colour 0xFFC766A6 if sender_name equals your own name (+0x7C), else 0xFF3277CC. Next it builds "  %s" from the message and appends it in 0xFFC8C8C8. The handler returns 1. The sender (FUN_00470120) only transmits C2S 0x35 and never appends the text locally, so the server must relay this packet to the sender as well as to the other room members.
specs.trigger: Server relay of C2S 0x35 {u8 len, bytes[len]}. FUN_00470120 sends that only when CMessenger+0x74 != 0, the text is non-NULL, +0xCC != 0 and ENGINE Curse_Engine_Clean passes. Send it to every member of the room, the sender included.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub3 entry gate: CMessenger+0x68 and +0x70 must be non-zero, or sub3 returns 0 (unclaimed). Room gate: +0xCC != 0, otherwise the packet is silently ignored with nothing consumed. The reads use CMessenger+0x74 (g_sock_game, set by FUN_0046f860 from S2C 0x03) as the CSNSocket this pointer. CRASH HAZARD 1: the message line is built with _sprintf_s(buf, 0x3D, "  %s", message), which needs strlen(message) <= 58. A longer string (a msg_len of 59..255 with no NUL inside, or a msg_len >= 61, which is unterminated inside the 61 zeroed bytes) makes _sprintf_s call the CRT invalid-parameter handler, and by default the process terminates. CRASH HAZARD 2: msg_len up to 255 writes esp0+0x100..0x1FE. That stays below the stack cookie at esp0+0x244, so there is no cookie failure, but it makes the strlen unbounded. CRASH HAZARD 3: sender_name must contain a NUL within its 17 bytes, since the local is not pre-zeroed and feeds "%s : " into the same 61-byte buffer. Rule for the server: 1..58 text bytes with no embedded NUL, and a name of at most 16 chars plus NUL.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: There is no real wire-format disagreement. Analyst A gave str[17] sender_name, u8 msg_len, bytes[msg_len] message, gated on CMessenger+0xCC != 0 with else stop. Analyst B gave the same three reads under the same gate but wrote the text as str[msg_len]. The structural-signature tool did not recognise that variable-length str, so it reported B as 'str[17] u8' only. The asm proves the layout both analysts described. At 0x47132D, CMP [EBX+0xCC],0 / JZ 0x471FF6 returns 1 before any read. At 0x471343/0x47134A, PUSH 0x11 then call [0x4A4098] reads 17 bytes into esp0+0x20. At 0x47135E, call [0x4A4094] reads a u8 into esp0+0x12. At 0x47137D/0x47138B/0x471397, MOVZX ECX,[esp0+0x12] is pushed as N for call [0x4A4098] into esp0+0x100, and no further GetDataFromPacket follows before the RET at 0x471476. A's bytes[msg_len] is the correct canonical DSL, because str[N] denotes fixed-width NUL-padded text and this field is variable-length with no terminator on the wire. B was also right to leave the sender echo as an open question, and it is now resolved: FUN_00470120 (C2S 0x35 at 0x470163: Add u8 0x35, Add u8 len, Add(text, len), Send) never appends locally, so the server must echo. On buffer size, B's 61-byte figure is the zeroed span (esp0+0x100..0x13C) and A's 64 bytes is the slot up to the next local at esp0+0x140; both agree the text must be <= 58 bytes. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x61.py (KR) builds pstr(name,17)+p8(len)+pstr(chat,len), which agrees. Its 'About normal chat?' comment is wrong: in EN this is the Messenger chat-room line (window 0x177). windslayer_server.py does not implement it.
open_questions: Fireway.dll GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) behaviour when N exceeds the remaining packet length is not visible in the exe (bounds check vs over-read).
Whether the room id in +0xCC must match anything on this packet: the packet carries no room id, so the client assumes a single active room.

specs.name: MessengerChatRoomMemberLeft

locations.role: remove matched node from window 0x177 member list (list object at window+0xBC)
append '<name>has logged out..' to chat-room window 0x177 (color 0xFF00A2A2)
C2S 0x36 leave-room sender (no payload); clears local member list and +0xCC

fields.name: member_name
fields.meaning: Name of the room member who left.
fields.dest_or_source: local [esp+0x20] (pre-zeroed); strcmp against each name string in window 0x177 list (+0xC0 head, node+8 = char*)

specs.semantics: A member left the current Messenger chat room. Only processed while CMessenger+0xCC != 0. Otherwise nothing is read and it returns 1. The client finds window 0x177. If it exists, it walks the member-name list at window+0xBC (head at +0xC0) and removes and frees the first node whose string equals member_name. Whether or not a match or the window was found, it prints '<member_name>has logged out..' (no space; literal string at 0x6F4BF8) into the chat-room window in colour 0xFF00A2A2. The member-list widget isn't explicitly redrawn here.
specs.trigger: Server sends it to the remaining room members when a member sends C2S 0x36 (leave chat room) or disconnects.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub3 gate: CMessenger+0x68/+0x70 non-null. Ignored unless in a messenger room (+0xCC != 0). member_name is read into a pre-zeroed buffer, but 17 non-NUL bytes still overrun into adjacent stack locals during strcmp/sprintf, so always NUL-terminate.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer server_packets. Not in windslayer_server.py. The companion join packet S2C 0x0F (result 1: u32 room_id -> +0xCC, u8 count, str[17] x count) fills the same window 0x177 list.
open_questions: Whether the server also sends 0x62 to the leaving player is unknown. The leaving client already cleared +0xCC in FUN_00472790, so it would ignore it anyway.
blind_open_questions: Which C2S makes the server broadcast this (closing the room window) was not traced; FUN_004701a0 sends C2S 0x37 {u8} and is a candidate.

specs.name: BattlefieldQueueCounts

locations.role: FUN_004838c0 set text: UI window 0x14 control 9
FUN_004838c0 set text: UI window 0x14 control 4
UI window 0x14 is the Battlefield window: opening it sends C2S 0x38

specs.grammar:
u16 player_count
u8 join_count

fields.name: player_count
fields.meaning: Number shown as '<N> Players' in control 4 of the Battlefield window (UI id 0x14). Likely the number of players in or waiting for the battlefield.

fields.name: join_count
fields.meaning: Death Match join-queue fill, shown on the Join button (control 9) as 'Join(<n>/12)'. The 12 is hard-coded. S2C 0x20 formats the same button the same way.

specs.semantics: Updates two text labels in the Battlefield window (UI id 0x14): control 9 gets 'Join(join_count/12)' and control 4 gets 'player_count Players'. There is no gate on game mode (unlike S2C 0x20, which checks [game_state+0x4D8]+0x70 != 1). The labels update even if the window is closed; FUN_004838c0 returns 0 if the window or control is missing. Nothing is stored in game state.
specs.trigger: Send when the Battlefield / Death Match queue counts change, and plausibly in reply to C2S 0x38 (opening the Battlefield window with the T key) so the window shows current counts.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Fireway readers bounds-check. On a short packet GetDataFromPacket leaves the destination and offset unchanged, calls CSNSockMyListener::OnError (0x4788E0), which only logs 'Error occured in Fireway (0x15/0x16)', and returns. So a short or empty 0x63 does not desync or crash, but the labels are formatted from stale stack data in the OnReceive frame (garbage text). Always send all 3 bytes. Keep join_count at 12 or below to match the /12 display. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (quest_cards_misc#06): an EMPTY S2C 0x63 (the old baseline's misroute of the client's C2S 0x63) leaves the Battlefield window's Death Match label showing garbage ("60276 Players"); only control 4 is visibly corrupted. Never answer C2S 0x63 with an empty 0x63.
specs.references: Our server (windslayer_server.py:607-608) answers C2S 0x63 with an EMPTY S2C 0x63 (b''). That triggers two Fireway short-read errors and writes garbage 'Join(?/12)' / '? Players' text into the Battlefield window; send u16+u8 (e.g. 00 00 00) or nothing instead. The same 'Join' string (0x6F6368) and 'Join(%u/12)' format are used by S2C 0x20 ('Death Match waiting list.'). Not in PySlayer server_packets or the KR Hex-Rays excerpt.
open_questions: Is S2C 0x63 the intended reply to C2S 0x63 (sent after map load on socket [game_state+0xDD0]) or to C2S 0x38 (Battlefield window open)? Static analysis shows no request/response link.
Exact meaning of player_count (queue population vs players currently inside the battlefield) is not confirmed by any other reference.
blind_open_questions: Which exact server event originally sent S2C 0x63 (reply to C2S 0x38 vs periodic broadcast) cannot be determined statically.
Whether total_players counts battlefield participants or all online players.

spec_errata.new: empty 0x63 corrupts the Battlefield label

fields.meaning: Item id in misc bank slot i (0 = empty)

fields.name: misc[i].quantity
fields.meaning: Stack count for misc slot i. It is a single byte, unlike the consumable tab.

fields.name: bank_gold
fields.meaning: Gold stored in the bank. It is shown as decimal ('%I64u') in control 10 of the bank window 0x1A7.

specs.length: 14 + sum over equip entries of (5 + 2*option_count) + 4*consume_count + 3*misc_count. An empty bank is 14 bytes: 01..03 caps, 00, 00, 00, u64.
specs.semantics: Replaces the whole client-side bank (warehouse) state. First it zeroes [game_state+0x4cc]+0x980..+0xE77 (0x4F8 bytes). Then it reads 3 tab capacities and 3 slot-ordered lists: Equipment is item u16 plus a 12-byte record of up to 5 option u16 and a trailing u16. Consumable is item u16 plus u16 qty. Misc is item u16 plus u8 qty. Last it reads the bank gold u64. FUN_00465110 (reached with ESI=this+0xD5C; that object's +0x18 points to the same block +0x48, so offsets 0x938..0xE28 in the callees match 0x980..0xE70 here) sets the gold text in window 0x1A7, resets the tab-button states and rebuilds the visible grid (FUN_00465C70). Unused slots stay zero, i.e. empty. Nothing is sent back.
specs.trigger: Server-initiated. The bank window (0x1A7) opens from local data only: bank NPC -> password dialog -> C2S 0x51 -> S2C 0x80(1,0x1A7), and no request for contents is sent. So a server should send 0x65 before the player can open the bank (e.g. at enter-world or right before 0x80 for 0x1A7). It should also send it whenever the full bank state needs to be resynced. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C32, shop_storage#03): a 0x65 sent AT ANY TIME BEFORE S2C 0x80 {1, 0x1A7} is enough - the bank window draws the block when it opens. The extra post-open 0x65 that design F3 / section 1.5 asks for is OPTIONAL; it is harmless but it resets the tab selection to Equipment.
specs.gates_and_hazards: There is no gate; it always runs. It has no bounds checks. (1) Any list count > 60 writes past its 60-entry array: equip_count > 60 runs item ids into the record area and records past +0xCCC. Near 255 it writes past the 0x4F8-byte block into the rest of the scene/player object, which corrupts the heap. (2) option_count > 5 spills into equip_attr_last (count 6 gets overwritten by the trailing read) and into the next slot's record. For slot 59 it spills into the consumable array. Keep option_count <= 5 and every list count <= 60. (3) Capacities > 60 only affect drawing. The client's own +5 extension stops at 60. (4) Any 0x65 wipes everything, so partial updates must resend the full state.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder (server_packets has no opcode_0x65.py). The KR Hex-Rays 0x65 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c:7745) is a reworked layout: it reads the u64 FIRST, then 3 u8, then 3 lists of 48-byte records via sub_40A010, with a 0x57F8 memset. So KR does NOT carry over to EN. The EN equipment-entry encoding (u16 item, u8 n, n*u16, u16) is the same as the player-inventory equipment list in the EN 0x03 handler (+0x3C8/+0x422/+0x42C) and as PySlayer opcode_0x03 'Equipment' (p16 item, p8 5, 5*p16 enchant, p16). windslayer_server.py has no 0x65 builder, and memory notes do not mention it.
open_questions: Meaning of equip_attr_last (record +10). Worn equipment in 0x07 carries 6 fixed u16, and this looks like the 6th, but its meaning (durability/grade/upgrade?) was not traced through tooltip FUN_00484140.
Real default bank capacities (the extension item adds 5 up to 60). The initial value is unknown, and PySlayer uses 35 for the player inventory.

[RESOLVED by live verification shop_storage#03, 2026-09-17] Live: any 0x65 sent before the 0x80 {1, 0x1A7} bank-open reply is enough - the window renders from the stored block when it opens. A post-open 0x65 is optional and merely resets the tab to Equipment. Original question: "When the original server sent 0x65 (at login/enter-world vs. right before the 0x80 bank-open reply) is not provable statically. The client never requests it."
Deposit/withdraw deltas are handled elsewhere (e.g. SubHandler1 0x46CF40 reads a u64 into bank gold at +0xE70). Those opcodes are outside this batch.
blind_open_questions: Tab names are inferred (tab1 has per-item option lists = equipment; tab2 u16 qty; tab3 u8 qty). The exact UI labels were not confirmed from strings.
Meaning of the tab-1 per-entry trailing u16 (grid item +0x0C; possibly durability/period/refine). It is not sent back in C2S 0x3D.
Which C2S or NPC action opens window 0x1A7 and should trigger this packet was not traced (S2C 0x80 with window_id 0x1A7 is one candidate).

spec_errata.new: any 0x65 before 0x80 {1,0x1A7} suffices

specs.grammar:
u64 gold
u16 item_id
u16 qty
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }
u16 item_ext

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: player's new gold balance (always applied, even if the item move fails)

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item definition id being moved into the bank

fields.name: qty
fields.meaning: quantity moved. Type 0: 1..999; type 2: 1..99; type 1 (equipment): must be >=1 (0 would take the bank remove path), actual count ignored

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: number of leading option u16s (<=5)

fields.name: opt
fields.meaning: option slot i of the 12-byte option blob

fields.name: item_ext
fields.meaning: slot 5 of the option blob (always present)

specs.semantics: Confirms moving an item from the inventory into the Bank (window 0x1A7, 'There are no empty space in Bank.'). Sets gold, looks up the item definition and branches on its type (itemdef+0x154): 0 = u16-stack item (bank tab at char+0xC84 ids / +0xCFC counts), 1 = equipment (bank ids char+0x93C, 12-byte blobs char+0x9B4; identified by an exact 12-byte opts+ext match), 2 = u8-stack item (bank ids char+0xD74 / u8 counts +0xDEC). It adds +qty to the bank, then removes qty from the matching inventory tab (inventory: equip char+0x380/+0x3DA, type0 +0x5F6/+0x650, type2 +0x760/+0x7BA). If both succeed it rebuilds the Bank and inventory windows.
specs.trigger: Server sends after a bank-deposit request. Best candidate is C2S 0x13 (u16 item_id, u16 qty, u8 n, n*u16 opt, u16 item_ext), sent from FUN_00469090 when the drag source is inventory window 9 (after an 'exceeded the amount you have' check).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No window/NPC gate in the handler. Silent no-op (gold still applied) if item id is unknown, the type is >2, a bank tab capacity byte (char+0x938/939/93A, unlocked slots) is >60, an inventory capacity byte (char+0x361/362/363) is >45, the qty is out of range, or there is no free bank slot / not enough in inventory. The bank is mutated BEFORE the inventory; if the inventory removal fails the bank change stays but no refresh happens (desync). opt_count must be <=5 (stack overflow hazard).
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Not in windslayer_server.py. Wire layout is byte-identical to our documented S2C 0x19 SellResult (u64 gold, u16 item, u16 count, u8 n, n*u16, u16 trailer).
open_questions: Why gold is carried: likely a bank fee or unchanged balance; check against real server behaviour.
Confirm that C2S 0x13 is the request that 0x66 answers (drop-target context in FUN_00469090 not fully traced).
Meaning of item_ext / opt slots.
blind_open_questions: Which C2S opcode requests a bank deposit, and does the u64 reflect a deposit fee?
Meaning of attr_tail.
The 'bank' name rests on offset correlation with the Bank slot-extension strings. The wire grammar does not depend on it.

type 2: bank cap char+0x93A<=60; FUN_00427940(item,-qty); jumps to 0x0046D883 -> FUN_00423e70(char+0x760,item,cap) EAX=+qty

specs.grammar:
u16 item_id
u16 qty
u8 opt_count
repeat(opt_count) { u16 opt }

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: item definition id being taken out of the bank

fields.name: qty
fields.meaning: quantity withdrawn. Type 0: 1..999; type 2: 1..99; ignored for equipment (fixed -1/+1)

fields.name: opt_count
fields.meaning: number of leading option u16s (<=5)

fields.name: opt
fields.meaning: option slot i of the 12-byte option blob

fields.name: item_ext
fields.meaning: slot 5 of the option blob (always present)

specs.semantics: Mirror of 0x66 with no gold field: moves an item from the Bank back to the inventory. Item type 0/2: bank -= qty then inventory += qty; type 1 (equipment): remove the bank slot whose id and 12-byte opts+ext blob match exactly, then add it to inventory equipment. On success it rebuilds the Bank window (0x1A7) and inventory window (9).
specs.trigger: Server sends after a bank-withdraw request; C2S 0x14 is the likely request (at least for equipment), but this was not fully traced.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same silent-failure conditions as 0x66: unknown id, type>2, bank capacity byte >60, inventory capacity byte >45, qty out of range, item not in bank, or inventory full. Bank is mutated before inventory, so a failed inventory add loses the item client-side without a refresh. For equipment, opts beyond opt_count are zero on the client side, so the stored blob must have zeros there to match. opt_count must be <=5.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. Not in windslayer_server.py. Same item-tail encoding as 0x66/0x88/0x89 and our documented 0x19 SellResult, minus the leading u64 gold.
open_questions: Confirm that C2S 0x14 is the request and whether stack-item withdrawal uses a different C2S layout that includes qty.
Meaning of item_ext / opt slots.
blind_open_questions: Which C2S opcode requests a bank withdraw?
Meaning of attr_tail.
The 'bank' name is inferred from offset correlation (see 0x66). The grammar itself is certain.

specs.name: StorageGoldUpdate (gold deposit/withdraw result, variant A)
specs.grammar:
u64 amount
u64 storage_gold
u64 gold

fields.name: amount
fields.meaning: Probably the amount moved. The client reads it and never uses it.

fields.name: storage_gold
fields.meaning: Gold now in storage. Its label is shown in window 0x1A7, child 10; the same field is shown by FUN_00465110 and checked by the withdraw dialog 0x1AB.

fields.name: gold
fields.meaning: Gold now carried in the inventory. Its label is inventory window 9, child 11.

locations.role: FUN_004659d0(storage_gold, win 0x1A7, child 10): sprintf %I64u then set label
C2S 0x3F withdraw-gold sender (u8 0x3F + Add(u64) amount); checks amount against player_info+0xE28
C2S 0x3E deposit-gold sender (u8 0x3E + u64 amount); checks amount against player_info+0x228

specs.semantics: Reads 3 u64 values with no branches. The first one is thrown away. The second is stored as storage gold at player_info+0xE28 and the third as inventory gold at player_info+0x228. Both are then written as decimal text (%I64u) into UI labels: storage window 0x1A7 child 10 and inventory window 9 child 11. A label only changes if its window exists (FUN_004838c0 walks the UI window list); the stored values are updated either way. Returns 1 (handled). 0x68 and 0x69 run the exact same code, so the client cannot tell them apart.
specs.trigger: Most likely the server's reply to C2S 0x3E (deposit gold: u64 amount from gold dialog 0x1AA, checked against inventory gold) or C2S 0x3F (withdraw gold: u64 amount from dialog 0x1AB, checked against storage gold). Send the new totals for both purses.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 first returns 0 (unhandled, nothing read) if [ctx+8]==0 or [ctx+0xC]==0; normally both are set while in-world. No other checks. Offset grep found no other code writing player_info+0xE28, so this packet may be the only way to set storage gold.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer (server_packets/__init__.py imports opcode_0x68 but the file doesn't exist). Our server has no builder. Window 0x1A7 is called storage because NPC function id 0x1A7 opens window 0x1A7 (FUN_004447d0), and it has item tabs 7/8/9 plus gold dialogs 0x1AA/0x1AB.
open_questions: Which of 0x68/0x69 the original server used for deposit vs withdraw; the client handles both the same way.
Whether the first u64 is really the amount moved (the client ignores it).
Whether another packet sets storage gold when storage opens (e.g. a block copy that an offset grep would miss). If not, send 0x68/0x69 when storage opens.
blind_open_questions: Whether 0x68 = deposit result and 0x69 = withdraw result (or the reverse) is not determinable from the client; wire and behaviour are identical.
Semantic of the discarded first u64 (transfer amount vs. account key) is unconfirmed.
Window id 0x1A7 is inferred to be the storage/warehouse window from the deposit/withdraw dialog code (0x1A9/0x1AB) in FUN_00469090; no UI string was directly tied to it.

fields.name: mileage_balance
fields.meaning: Mileage balance; window 0x1CF control 0x68.

fields.name: box_count
fields.meaning: Number of cash item box records (bought or received, not yet moved out). JZ at 0x461C5B then signed JLE at 0x461C61 skip the loop when <= 0; JL at 0x461CB0.

fields.meaning: Record +0x00: unique cash item serial (box lookups by item_id+serial in FUN_0045e6f0).

fields.name: item_id

specs.semantics: Enter the cash shop. (1) game_state+0x1534 = 0 (clears the wait/fade flag FUN_0043d560 sets). (2) Free box list mall+0x28; read cash -> +0x588, mileage -> +0x58C, box_count, then box_count 28-byte records into +0x28. (3) Rebuild snapshot lists: +0x48 = deep copy of +0x28, +0x58 = deep copy of owned list +0x04 (filled by 0x6F). (4) mall+0x5B8 = 0; FUN_0045af00 initializes the shop UI. (5) FUN_0045c470 swaps the world scene for ./hs/preview99_01.hmi ('Could not load Preview MAP.' on failure), creates a 0x15F0 preview avatar from the local character's appearance (alive byte=3, HP=100, uid=char+0x1D8, fixed position constants), calls RegisterLocalPlayer and sets [game_state+0x4CC](scene)+0xF00 = 4 (opening window 0x15 first if it was 5). (6) Opens windows 0x1CF, 0x1FB, 0x1FC, 0x1FD, and 0x3F3 only the first time (mall+0x5B4). (7) If byte mall+0x00 != 0 shows 'Thank you for your first purchase of wind cash. 500 mileage has reserved...' and clears it. (8) FUN_0045e260. Returns 1.
specs.trigger: Reply to the client's request to enter the cash shop (the 'Enter the cash shop?' dialog 0x133 for type 0x81 in FUN_0044c4b0, confirmed in FUN_00446300 at 0x446CF8, which re-dispatches as id 3 / control 1). The C2S request opcode was not traced.
specs.expected_response: none directly; the client then uses the shop C2S commands in FUN_0045f2e0 (0x43, 0x45, 0x48, 0x49, 0x4B, 0x51, 0x70, 0x71, ...)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only the SubHandler4 entry gate ([mall+0x14], [mall+0x18] non-NULL). No other pre-read gate. HAZARD: unconditionally unloads the current world map, loads the preview map and registers a preview avatar as local player; sending it outside the shop flow pulls the client out of the world. The server must restore the world with the normal map-change sequence on exit. Send 0x6F first, because list +0x04 is snapshotted here. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (section 4, premium_cash#13/#30): live - the mall renders fully, but NO exit control works from inside it (three attempts produced 0 packets), so the client cannot leave on its own and C2S 0x42 could not even be produced. RECOVERY: the server must push the world back with the map-enter sequence (S2C 0x08 -> 0x03 -> 0x07); otherwise the client must be restarted.
open_questions: Which C2S opcode requests shop entry and which one requests exit (a 0-byte C2S 0x46 sent from the shop UI at 0x463D7C, guarded by mall+0x5AC, is an unverified candidate).
Where byte mall+0x00 (first-purchase flag) is set.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A and B agree exactly on the read sequence: u32 at 0x461C25 into +0x588, u32 at 0x461C3B into +0x58C, i32 at 0x461C4F, then a loop of single 28-byte reads (PUSH 0x1c at 0x461C8F, call at 0x461C96). The only difference is the record tail: A has u8 origin + u8 unk_1b, B has u16 unk_1a. The wire bytes are identical, but the client reads +0x1A as a single byte (CMP byte ptr [ECX+0x1a],DL at 0x45FB4F on box records found by FUN_0045e6f0 in list +0x28; CMP byte ptr [EDX+0x1a],3 at 0x462322). No reader of +0x1B exists, so A's layout is the precise one. On a minor semantic detail B was right and A was not: the +0xF00 = 4 write in FUN_0045c470 (0x45C6CB/0x45C6E2) goes to [game_state+0x4CC], which is the scene, not the character. Winner for the grammar: A. PySlayer has no opcode_0x6A.py. Our server does not implement 0x6A, but the comment on its disabled 0x6F sender (windslayer_server.py ~L789) actually describes this block. Strings: 0x6F5840 'Enter the cash shop?', 0x6F7F70 './hs/preview99_01.hmi', 0x6F4610 first-purchase message.

spec_errata.new: no exit control works - the server must restore the world

specs.name: CashShopExit

locations.role: handler block start (block 0x462027-0x462062 contains no GetDataFromPacket)
UI root: find window 3, walk to control 6, set control state (+0x18) = 3

specs.grammar: stop
specs.semantics: No payload is read (the 'stop' is at the start: the handler has no read calls, so any trailing bytes are ignored). (1) FUN_00463a10 writes the cash shop wish list (vector mall+0x20C, first u32 of each entry, up to 12) to the registry under the character name at [game_state+0x4CC]+0x206 as Wish0..Wish11 (zeroing them first). (2) FUN_00489320(3,6,3) on the UI root sets window 3 / control 6 to state 3. FUN_00483470 makes the same call when restoring the HUD, so this probably re-enables the HUD cash shop button. (3) FUN_00465290 rebuilds the inventory UI. Returns 1. It does not unload the preview map or restore the world scene.
specs.trigger: Server acknowledgement that the player left the cash shop (inferred from the wish-list save and the HUD control reset).
specs.gates_and_hazards:
Only the SubHandler4 entry gate ([mall+0x14], [mall+0x18] non-NULL). FUN_00463a10 skips the registry save if game_state or scene is NULL. Harmless outside the shop apart from the registry write and the HUD control state. The world map must be restored separately with the normal map-change packets.
LIVE: writes the Wish0 registry value (e.g. 4235) and leaves the client on the black preview screen - it does not return to the world by itself; follow with a full map load.
open_questions: Exact identity of window 3 / control 6 (probably the HUD cash shop button).
Which C2S exit request precedes 0x6B.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree that the block reads nothing. A wrote 'stop' and B an empty grammar, which mean the same thing. The asm block 0x462027-0x462062 is PUSH EBX / CALL 0x463A10 / PUSH 3,6,3 / CALL 0x489320 / CALL 0x465290 / MOV EAX,1 / return, with no IAT GetDataFromPacket call. 'stop' is kept as the canonical DSL form. On semantics A is more precise: FUN_00489320 walks the UI root window list for id 3, steps to control 6 and stores param_4=3 in the control's +0x18 state, not a 'simulated activation'. FUN_00465290 is the inventory window builder (bag +0x380 etc.), not a generic HUD refresh. Winner: tie on grammar, A on details. PySlayer has no opcode_0x6B.py. Our server: not implemented.

spec_errata.new: LIVE: writes the Wish0 registry value (e.g. 4235) and leaves the client on the black preview screen - it does not return

}
