fields.meaning: 1 = purchase OK. 0x0E = popup "You are short of cash.". Any other value = popup "You failed to buy the item.\r\n\r\nPlease try again in a few minutes.". Nothing more is read on failure.

fields.name: cash_balance
fields.meaning: New absolute cash balance
fields.dest_or_source: cash-shop manager (game_state+0x700) +0x588; shown in UI label 0x67

fields.name: mileage_balance
fields.meaning: New absolute mileage balance. If it is higher than the old value (unsigned compare), the client shows "50% bonus mileage has been deposited."
fields.dest_or_source: local, then mgr+0x58C; shown in UI label 0x68

fields.name: item_serial
fields.meaning: Unique id of the bought cash item (record +0x00). Later 0x6E, 0x72 and 0x73 and C2S 0x45 find the record by this value. The next nine fields all come from ONE 28-byte buffer read at 0x462318.

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Item template id (record +0x04). Ids 0x75C..0x761 (1884-1889, equipment/consumable/etc/storage slot expansions) are applied right away (+5 slots, up to 45 for inventory or 60 for bank) and are not stored.

fields.name: item_kind
fields.meaning: Record kind: 1 = counted item (quantity goes down on use, record removed at 0); 2 = duration/period item (expire_time is valid). Matches item def +0x1F6. The client only reads the low byte.

fields.name: unk_07
fields.meaning: Unused by the client (probably the high byte of a u16 kind, or padding). Send 0.

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: Count of the item (shown in the box window; decremented by use)

fields.name: expire_time
fields.meaning: Win32 SYSTEMTIME expiry for duration items: u16 wYear, wMonth, wDayOfWeek, wDay, wHour, wMinute, wSecond, wMilliseconds. A year below 1900 means no expiry (FUN_0045a9f0). Send zeros for counted items.

fields.name: origin
fields.meaning: Source flag. 3 = event reward, which shows "Congratulation.\r\n\r\nYou received an event item.."

fields.name: unk_1b
fields.meaning: Unused by this handler; send 0

specs.semantics:
Result of a cash-shop purchase. On success the client sets cash and mileage to the absolute values sent and redraws their labels. It shows the bonus-mileage popup if mileage went up. It reads one 28-byte cash item record. If record.item_id is a slot-expansion ticket (0x75C..0x761), the client applies it (+5 slots, with a popup) and frees the record. Otherwise it adds the record to the cash item box list (mgr+0x28), with no check for duplicate serials. Both paths then rebuild box window 0x1FC (FUN_0045b280) and inventory-side window 0x1FD (FUN_0045b360), and redraw the labels. On failure the client only shows a popup.
LIVE: the generic failure message has a second line 'Please try again in a few minutes.'; slot-extension success grows the bag from 35 to 40 slots.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x43 'C' (buy): u8 opcode, bool pay_with_mileage, u8 count, then count x u16 item_id; sent from cash shop windows 0x1F7/0x1F8/0x1FF. The server probably sends one 0x6C per bought item, since each packet carries only one record.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 returns 0 without reading if mgr+0x14 or mgr+0x18 is NULL (cash-shop manager not initialized). A repeated serial makes duplicate box entries. Result 0x0E and other non-1 values read nothing after the result byte.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer (doc/server_to_client/README.md only lists 0x6C among Packet_handler_4 opcodes). Not in windslayer_server.py. Our server's 0x80 'CashShopBalance' does not write mgr+0x588/+0x58C: in the corpus only FUN_0045ae40 (reset) and sub4 opcodes 0x6C/0x6E/0x70/0x71 write those fields. Record layout agrees with the 0x6F list parser (FUN_0045e8e0(item_id@+4, qty@+8, serial@+0); kind==2 && year!=0 -> expiry popup FUN_0045ebb0) and with FUN_00464380.
open_questions: Does the server send one 0x6C per item for multi-item (cart) purchases, or use another opcode such as 0x6D (u8 count + 0x7E-byte entries) for carts?
Exact meaning of record bytes +0x07 and +0x1B; is item_kind really a u16 whose high byte is unused?
Is the mileage sent here the balance after a 50% bonus? The client only compares it with the old value.
blind_open_questions: Exact C2S request that produces 0x6C (0x43 cart buy is the best candidate; a multi-item cart may expect several 0x6C or a different reply).
Meaning of record bytes +0x07 and +0x1B, and origin values other than 0 (purchased) and 3 (event), e.g. gift.
Whether item_kind (+0x06) equals the template field +0x1F6 checked in 0x72 (both use value 2 for period items).

specs.name: GiftInboxList

locations.role: GetDataFromPacket char buffer, N=0x7E (126) per gift record (IAT 0x4A4098)
FUN_00459df0: append record to CPList at ctx+0x5F4
post-loop: find UI window id 3, 6th control, set control+0x18=0
consumer: shows head gift in dialog window 0x3EF (reads rec+0x00, +0x11, +0x6C)
FUN_0045e260 call at end of S2C 0x6A handler (only packet-driven trigger of the popup)
dialog 0x3EF button-2 handler: C2S 0x4B reply, pops head gift, shows next

specs.grammar:
u8 gift_count
repeat(gift_count) {
  str[17] sender_name
  str[91] message
  u16 item_id
  bytes[16] unk_6e
}

fields.name: gift_count
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x13]; loop count (unsigned; 0 skips the loop but the HUD step still runs)
fields.meaning: number of 126-byte gift records that follow

fields.name: sender_name
fields.dest_or_source: record+0x00 (heap block new(0x7E) appended to CPList ctx+0x5F4, ctx=game_state+0x700). FUN_004838c0(6) at 0x45E39A strcpy's it into dialog 0x3EF control 6 (+0x50)
fields.meaning: name of the character who sent the gift. It is sent back as the recipient name in the C2S 0x4B reply.

fields.name: message
fields.dest_or_source: record+0x11; FUN_0048a060(4) at 0x45E3DB strcpy's it into dialog 0x3EF control 4 (+0xD1)
fields.meaning: gift message text (91 bytes, same size as the message field in C2S 0x4B)

fields.name: item_id
fields.dest_or_source: record+0x6C; read at 0x45E2BF/0x45E361, looked up in the item table ([ctx+0x1C], index id-1); the item name goes to dialog control 1; the id goes to window+0x134 via FUN_00483270
fields.meaning: gifted item id (for example 3327..3332 = WS Gift Card 1000..50000)

fields.name: unk_6e
fields.dest_or_source: record+0x6E..+0x7D; stored but no reader found in the EN client
fields.meaning: unknown trailing 16 bytes (possibly a serial or timestamp); send zeros

specs.semantics: Adds pending received gifts to a client-side queue. For each record the client allocates 126 bytes (operator new, NOT zeroed), reads exactly 126 raw bytes into it and appends it to the CPList at cash-shop ctx+0x5F4 (ctx = game_state+0x700). The list is only cleared by FUN_0045B0F0 (session reset). After the loop, even when gift_count==0, it walks UI root ([ctx+0x18]) window list +0x5C0 for the window with id 3, sets UI+0x5F0 to that window, steps 5 nodes along its control list +0x8C and sets control+0x18 = 0 on the 6th control. +0x18 is the button state (0 = normal/enabled, 3 = disabled, per FUN_00489c50), so this enables a HUD gift icon. S2C 0x78 in SubHandler3 does the same with control 8. No popup comes from 0x6D itself. The gift dialog (window 0x3EF) is opened by FUN_0045E260, which runs at the end of the S2C 0x6A handler (cash shop list) and again after the user confirms a gift dialog. FUN_0045E260 takes the head record, looks up item_id and shows the dialog only if itemdef+0x1F0 != 0 or item_id is in 0xCFF..0xD04. Dialog contents: control 1 = item name, control 6 = sender_name, control 4 = message, control 8 = empty reply box (string at 0x6F2118).
specs.trigger: Send when the player has pending cash-shop gifts from other players, e.g. on entering the world or right after another player's C2S 0x4B gift. For the popup to appear, send it before S2C 0x6A (cash shop list).
specs.expected_response: None directly. When the dialog's button 2 is pressed, the sender name passes FUN_0043df40 and the reply text is non-empty, the client sends C2S 0x4B: u16 9999, str[17] sender_name, str[91] reply_text (send site #51 @0x46098E). It then pops and frees the head gift and shows the next one. With empty text it only pops.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 runs only when [ctx+0x14] (game_state ptr) and [ctx+0x18] (UI root) are non-null; otherwise it returns 0 and the opcode goes unhandled. Records are allocated with new and not memset: a short packet leaves heap garbage. sender_name and message are later copied with unbounded strcpy (loops at 0x483937 / 0x48A0E0), so both MUST be NUL-terminated inside their fields (name <=16 chars, message <=90 chars) or the copy overruns the 126-byte block and the controls. Queue-stall hazard: if the head record's item_id is not in the item table, or itemdef+0x1F0==0 and item_id is outside 3327..3332, the dialog never opens. Only the dialog pops the queue, so every later gift is blocked. Button 2 aborts without popping if sender_name fails FUN_0043df40 (empty, contains a space or a forbidden word such as 'gamemaster'/'yahoo'), so the gift cannot be dismissed. If UI window 3 or its 6th control is missing, the HUD step returns early (harmless). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C20, chat_mail_gm#11, chat_mail_gm#09): the map-change sequence RESETS the Gift HUD button (window 3 control 6) back to disabled even though the queue itself survives S2C 0x03. To relight the button after a map change or an 0x2F resync, send this packet again with count = 0 - that runs the HUD step without adding queue entries (records are append-only and would otherwise duplicate).
specs.references: No PySlayer builder or parser for 0x6D (its doc only lists 0x6D under Packet_handler_4). Not in windslayer_server.py. The 126-byte layout matches S2C 0x78 (SubHandler3 @0x471A42: u8 count + 126-byte records into another list, enabling HUD window 3 control 8). The sender/message sizes (17/91) match both C2S 0x4B send sites (#51 @0x46098E with u16 9999; #55 @0x461064 with a real item id), so C2S 0x4B is 'send gift/note to player' and this record is its received side with item_id moved to +0x6C. Item names from server/data/en/items_en.json: 3327..3332 = WS Gift Card 1000/3000/5000/10000/30000/50000.
open_questions: Meaning of record bytes +0x6E..+0x7D (16 bytes): no reader found in the EN client (the list is only touched by FUN_00459df0, FUN_0045B0F0, FUN_0045E260 and FUN_00459f90).
Meaning of itemdef+0x1F0 (the flag that lets non-gift-card items open the dialog); probably a 'giftable cash item' flag.
Which UI element window id 3 / control #6 is (probably the HUD gift/present icon), and whether clicking it asks the server to open the cash shop (which would lead to 0x6A and the popup). Not traced.
Whether the server should resend 0x6D after gifts are consumed: the client never removes records except through the dialog or a session reset, so resending duplicates them.
blind_open_questions: Meaning of record bytes +0x6E..+0x7D (16 bytes) - no reader found; 16 chars would fit a 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' date but this is unverified.
Identity of UI window id 3 and its child #6, and whether [ctrl+0x18]=0 means enabled/normal (0x6B sets 3).
Whether a server-sent record with item_id 9999 (the client's own 'reply' marker) is intended to be displayable; with no item def it would block the queue head.

fields.name: item_serial

specs.name: CashItemOwnedList

locations.role: dispatcher: gate [mall+0x14]/[mall+0x18] non-NULL, index table 0x4630AC + jump table 0x463060 -> 0x4618EC
handler block start: frees lists mall+0x04 and mall+0x38
pre-read gate + purge of cash items from the bag at char+0x380 (ids) / +0x3DA (12-byte attrs); CMP AL,0x2d / JBE at 0x4243D1, returns 0 when byte char+0x361 > 45
pre-read gate + purge of the bag at char+0x5F6 / u16 counts +0x650; returns 0 when byte char+0x362 > 45
pre-read gate + purge of the bag at char+0x760 / u8 counts +0x7BA; returns 0 when byte char+0x363 > 45
JZ 0x46302A on helper failure = return 1 with nothing read (same at 0x461999, 0x4619C7)
ungated purge of cash items from the fixed 45-slot bag char+0x7E8 (u8 counts +0x842)
GetDataFromPacket(char*,0x1C) IAT 0x4A4098 -> 28-byte cash item record into a fresh heap node
period item with a date: prints '[%s] will expire in %d day(s).' / remaining-time line to chat instead of bag insert
insert into a bag by item template +0x154 (0 -> +0x5F6 bag, 1 -> +0x380 bag, 5 -> +0x7E8 bag with serial array +0x870)
rebuild window-5 list of active period items (iterates mall+0x04 records with +0x06==2 and year!=0)

specs.grammar:
if(char_bag_slots_0x361 <= 45 && char_bag_slots_0x362 <= 45 && char_bag_slots_0x363 <= 45) {
  i32 count
  repeat(count) {
    bool is_equipped
    u32 serial
    u16 item_id
    u8 limit_type
    u8 unk_07
    u16 quantity
    u16 expire_year
    u16 expire_month
    u16 expire_day_of_week
    u16 expire_day
    u16 expire_hour
    u16 expire_minute
    u16 expire_second
    u16 expire_milliseconds
    u8 origin
    u8 unk_1b
  }
} else {
  stop
}
specs.length: 4 + 29*max(count,0) when the client-state gate passes (always true in normal play: bag slot bytes never exceed 45); 0 bytes consumed if the gate fails

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number of records. Signed: JLE at 0x461AE8 skips the loop when <= 0; loop index compared with JL at 0x461BA0.

fields.name: is_equipped
fields.meaning: 1 byte. Non-zero: record is appended to mall+0x38 only (worn cash items; no bag insert). Zero: appended to mall+0x04 (owned, not worn) and put into a bag. Confirmed by S2C 0x1D at 0x452C58 calling FUN_0045d0c0 (moves the record with matching item_id from +0x04 to +0x38) and 0x452C95 / 0x4542A3 (0x1D, 0x1E/0x24) calling FUN_0045d170 (reverse).

fields.name: serial
fields.meaning: Record +0x00: unique cash item serial. Passed as arg 4 to FUN_0045e8e0 (stored in char+0x870[slot] for category-5 items); matched by FUN_00464380 and by the box lookup FUN_0045e6f0 (item_id, serial).

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Record +0x04: item template id (1-based index into item table at mall+0x1C).

fields.name: limit_type
fields.meaning: Record +0x06: 1 = count-limited (FUN_00464380 at 0x4643D0 subtracts uses from quantity; shop UI 0x45FBA5); 2 = period item (expiry SYSTEMTIME used; 0x461B67, 0x441C9D, 0x45BAD1); other = no special handling.

fields.name: unk_07
fields.meaning: Record +0x07: no reader found (padding). Send 0.

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: Record +0x08: count / remaining uses. Passed as the add amount to FUN_0045e8e0; a value of 0 makes every insertion helper (0x4246D0, 0x4248A0, 0x4247A0) return 0, so the item is not placed in a bag. For category 5 the low byte becomes the u8 stack count. (LIVE C13: for stat-reset items this is BOTH the icon stack count and the number of points the client lets the player redistribute - send 5 for a "Reset 5 Stat Points" record.)

fields.name: expire_year
fields.meaning: Record +0x0A: SYSTEMTIME.wYear. If is_equipped==0 && limit_type==2 && expire_year!=0 (0x461B67/0x461B6D) the client only prints remaining time and does NOT insert into a bag. FUN_0045a9f0 treats year < 1900 as no date.

fields.name: expire_month
fields.meaning: Record +0x0C: SYSTEMTIME.wMonth

fields.name: expire_day_of_week
fields.meaning: Record +0x0E: SYSTEMTIME.wDayOfWeek (unused by FUN_0045a9f0)

fields.name: expire_day
fields.meaning: Record +0x10: SYSTEMTIME.wDay

fields.name: expire_hour
fields.meaning: Record +0x12: SYSTEMTIME.wHour

fields.name: expire_minute
fields.meaning: Record +0x14: SYSTEMTIME.wMinute

fields.name: expire_second
fields.meaning: Record +0x16: SYSTEMTIME.wSecond

fields.name: expire_milliseconds
fields.meaning: Record +0x18: SYSTEMTIME.wMilliseconds (unused)

fields.name: origin
fields.meaning: Record +0x1A, read as a BYTE by the client: 0 = bought with cash (shop UI 0x45FB4F computes a refund/price value only when this byte is 0); 3 = event reward (0x6C handler 0x462322 shows 'Congratulation... You received an event item'). Other values: no refund value.

fields.name: unk_1b
fields.meaning: Record +0x1B: no reader found (padding). Send 0.

specs.semantics: Full rebuild of the character's owned (out-of-box) cash items. Order: (1) free every node of lists mall+0x04 and mall+0x38 (mall = game_state+0x700). (2) For bags char+0x380 (slots byte +0x361), +0x5F6 (slots +0x362), +0x760 (slots +0x363) call purge helpers that first check the slot byte <= 45 (else the handler returns 1 immediately, nothing read) and then remove and compact every item whose template +0x1F0 != 0 (cash item). (3) Purge the fixed 45-slot bag +0x7E8 the same way. (4) Read i32 count; per record: alloc 28 zeroed bytes, read bool is_equipped, read the 28-byte record raw. is_equipped != 0 -> push to +0x38 only. Else push to +0x04, then if limit_type==2 and expire_year!=0 -> FUN_0045ebb0 chat expiry notice (no bag insert), otherwise FUN_0045e8e0(mall, item_id, quantity, serial) inserts into a bag by template category (0, 1, 5; others ignored; silent failure when full or quantity 0). (5) FUN_00465290 rebuilds the inventory UI; FUN_00441c20(1) rebuilds the window-5 period-item list. Returns 1.
specs.trigger: Server sends the complete owned cash item set whenever it must be synced (likely after world entry once the base inventory exists, and before 0x6A, which snapshots list +0x04 into +0x58). The requesting C2S opcode was not identified.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 returns 0 (unhandled) if [mall+0x14] or [mall+0x18] is NULL. The two lists are freed before the gate, so a failed gate still wipes them. Every 0x6F deletes all cash items (template+0x1F0 != 0) from the bags, including ones delivered by 0x07, so it must always carry the full set; count=0 means 'no cash items'. Worn items (is_equipped=1) are only tracked, not inserted. quantity=0 silently skips bag insertion. No bound on count; each record is heap-allocated. Always send exactly 4 + 29*count bytes. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C13, premium_cash#21): the stat-reset ALLOWANCE the client enforces is this record's u16 quantity at +0x08 - NOT the item definition's Cash_V. A "Reset 5 Stat Points" record must therefore be sent with quantity = 5 or the player can restore only one point. The same field also drives the stack count drawn on the Premiums icon, so for these items quantity is both stack size and allowance.
open_questions: Which C2S request (if any) the original server answered with 0x6F, and exact timing relative to 0x07/0x6A.
Meaning of origin values other than 0 and 3; unk_07 and unk_1b have no reader in the cash-shop code (assumed padding).
UI label of the fixed 45-slot category-5 bag at char+0x7E8.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the read order (i32 count at 0x461AD5, then per record bool at 0x461B28 and a single 28-byte blob at 0x461B3E) and on total size. They differ on two points. (1) Gate: A wraps the body in a client-state if/else-stop; B only mentions the gate in hazards. The asm proves the gate is a real branch in the read path: the helpers at 0x4243D0/0x4245D0/0x4244E0 begin with CMP AL,0x2d / JBE (AL = byte [char+0x361/0x362/0x363]) and otherwise XOR EAX,EAX / RET 0xc; the handler tests the result (JZ 0x46302A at 0x46196B/0x461999/0x4619C7) and 0x46302A is MOV EAX,1 / return, before the first GetDataFromPacket. A is correct. (2) Record tail: A uses u8 origin + u8 unk_1b; B uses u16 unk_1a. The wire bytes are identical, because the record is read as one 28-byte blob (PUSH 0x1c at 0x461B3B). But the client reads +0x1A as a single byte (CMP byte ptr [ECX+0x1a],DL with DL=0 at 0x45FB4F in FUN_0045f2e0; CMP byte ptr [EDX+0x1a],3 at 0x462322 in the 0x6C handler), and nothing reads +0x1B, so A's split is the precise layout. On semantics, A's 'is_equipped' reading of the bool is confirmed by FUN_0045d0c0/FUN_0045d170 being called from the 0x1D and 0x1E/0x24 handlers to move records between lists +0x04 and +0x38; B's claim that +0x38 has no other reader is wrong. B's point that quantity=0 blocks bag insertion is correct and is included. Overall winner: A. Other refs: PySlayer has no opcode_0x6F.py. Our server (windslayer_server.py ~L789-823) has a disabled 0x6F sender that sends 28 zero bytes, which would parse as count=0 (wipe all cash items) plus 24 ignored bytes. Its comment about rep movsd, [+0x5B8]=0, FUN_0045AF00 and FUN_0045C470 describes the 0x6A block (0x461D37-0x461F2F), not 0x6F.

spec_errata.old: allowance assumed to come from the item def (Cash_V)
spec_errata.new: allowance is the record u16 quantity at +0x08

spec_errata.old: quantity documented as a stack count only
spec_errata.new: also the stat-reset allowance

specs.name: CashMileageBalance

u32 cash_balance

u8 first_purchase_bonus

fields.name: cash_balance
fields.meaning: Absolute cash balance shown in the cash shop

fields.name: mileage_balance
fields.meaning: Absolute mileage balance

fields.name: first_purchase_bonus

specs.semantics: Sets the cash shop's cash and mileage values, optionally shows the first-purchase popup, and redraws both labels. It also clears mgr+0x5AC. That flag is set when the player clicks button 5 ('charge cash') in the cash shop window 0x1CF. While it is set, button 0xA8 (refresh) sends C2S 0x46 'F' (FUN_00463d70). In the corpus this is the only packet that sets both balances without any other side effect.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x46 'F' (no payload, the refresh after charging). Also usable whenever the server wants to push the balances, for example when the cash shop opens.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same SubHandler4 gate. No other preconditions; reads a fixed 9 bytes.

specs.semantics: Broadcast that a character used a cash item. For any visible character the client updates appearance: for the three random hair/dye items it applies the server-chosen hair_code to hair slot 4; for other items FUN_00427430 applies the change set in the item def (switch on def+0x1F4: 0 generic slot, 1 hair style, 2 hair color, 0x0E special), and items with no appearance effect do nothing here. It then plays effect 0x140 and sound 0x140 on the character. If the character is the local player, the client also closes the 'Waiting for the server' message box and reads item_serial. It looks up the item def: for a duration item it reads the 16-byte expiry and calls FUN_00464380 with it, then refreshes window 5; otherwise it calls FUN_00464380 with NULL. FUN_00464380 finds the record by serial in list mgr+4. A kind-1 record loses one from quantity and is removed at 0. A kind-2 record gets the expiry copied in. Either way FUN_0045e8e0 updates the character inventory and windows 0x1FD etc. are rebuilt. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C36, premium_cash#10): the window-5 "period item" list prints the record's ABSOLUTE expiry SYSTEMTIME as "<month>month <day>day HH:MM" - it is not a remaining-day count. Item 3323 also settles the record-length question: the client def +0x1F6 == 2 == gamedef Cash_T, so the 26-byte (duration) form is the correct length for it.
specs.trigger: Likely the reply to C2S 0x48 'H' (u16 item_id) sent from confirm window 0x3F4. FUN_00463d90 opens that window when the player uses a generic cash item from the inventory, and it shows the 'Waiting for the server to response.' box that this packet closes. Send it to the user and to nearby players (the same full body works for all; other clients stop reading early and ignore extra bytes). MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x48 (use cash item). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same SubHandler4 gate. If the uid is not in the scene, only 4 bytes are read (nothing is applied). For other players reading stops after item_id/hair_code. For the local player, if item_id has no item def, reading stops after the serial. The expiry is read only when def+0x1F6 == 2, so the server must use the same item-def table as the client; a mismatch makes the server send or omit 16 bytes the client does not expect (trailing bytes are harmless, missing bytes are read out of bounds). An unknown serial is ignored, but the inventory UI is still refreshed.

JZ break when lookup returned NULL (name NOT read)
redundant recheck entity+0x84 == uid, JNZ break
inline strcpy loop entity+0x00 -> scene+0x206 (local character name)
FUN_00442510(this=game_state) refresh local character-info window (runs only if scene+0x970 != 0)
related S2C 0x73 rename result (SubHandler4): u8 result; if 1 -> u32 + 'Your character name has successively changed.' else 'The name is already being used.'

specs.length: 21 (4 + 17); only 4 bytes consumed when uid is 0 or not a loaded entity

fields.name: uid
fields.meaning: Entity uid (entity+0x84) of the character whose name changed. uid 0 or a uid not present in the current scene entity list ends the handler without reading the name.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local (block-relative [esp+0x1A0]); used for FUN_004189F0 lookup and compared to scene+0x220

fields.name: new_name
fields.meaning: New character name, exactly 17 raw bytes, NUL-padded; must contain a NUL within the 17 bytes (max 16 chars) because for the local player it is copied with an unbounded strcpy.
fields.dest_or_source: read directly into entity+0x00 (name[17]); if uid == scene+0x220 also copied to scene+0x206

specs.semantics: Reads u32 uid and looks the entity up in the current scene's entity list (FUN_004189F0 walks scene+0xC nodes, matching node->entity+0x84 against EDX=uid; uid 0 returns NULL immediately). If not found, the handler breaks to 0x44D7AD without reading anything else. Otherwise it reads 17 bytes straight over the entity's name buffer (entity+0x00), so the name changes in place. If uid equals the local player uid (scene+0x220), it copies the name (inline strcpy loop) to scene+0x206 and calls FUN_00442510, which rebuilds the character-info panel labels (Lv.%u, stats, stat buttons) when scene+0x970 (local player entity) is non-null. No chat line, popup or sound in the EN build.
specs.trigger: Server broadcast to clients that have the renamed character loaded (including the renamer) after a successful rename. The requester separately receives S2C 0x73 (u8 result; result==1 is followed by a u32 and shows 'Your character name has successively changed.'; otherwise 'The name is already being used.').
specs.gates_and_hazards: Global OnReceive gate: every packet is dropped while [game_state+0x408] != 0 (0x44D5F5). Unknown uid or uid 0 -> silently ignored; the 17 name bytes are left unconsumed (harmless as the handler ends). new_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes: the local-player copy to scene+0x206 is an unbounded byte loop that would run past entity+0x11 into following entity fields and overflow the scene name buffer. Only entity+0x00 is written; a cached nameplate record (entity+0x11DC) is not touched here, so whether the overhead name re-renders immediately is unverified. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C45, premium_cash#05): the server must NEVER send the short (4-byte) form. A 0x74 whose 17 name bytes are missing is read out of bounds by the client - live it did no visible harm, but the read is unbounded. Always send all 21 bytes, and only for a uid the receiver has loaded. (Test-tooling note: encoding this packet needs "__assume__": {"entity_with_uid_exists": true}, otherwise the client-state condition defaults to false and only 4 bytes are produced.)
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: There is no real wire-format dispute. Analyst A gave 'u32 uid; if(entity exists){ str[17] new_name }' and Analyst B gave the same plus an explicit 'else { stop }'. Both describe identical byte behavior and both are correct; B's form is adopted only because it states the early-exit path explicitly. Evidence from the asm: at 0x457F0B a u32 is read via IAT 0x4A40C8 into [esp+0x1A0] (pushes: len EDI, &offset [esp+0x10], pkt EBX, dst lea [esp+0x1AC] after three pushes = [esp+0x1A0]); 0x457F17 loads EDX=uid and 0x457F1F calls FUN_004189F0, which takes EDX as the key, returns NULL for uid 0 or no match and never writes EDX (RET 4); 0x457F2A JZ 0x44D7AD skips the rest; 0x457F32/0x457F38 re-check entity+0x84==uid; 0x457F4B/0x457F4D push N=0x11 and dst=EAX (the entity pointer, i.e. entity+0x00) before the char-buffer read at 0x457F4E (IAT 0x4A4098); 0x457F61 compares uid with [scene+0x220] and JNZ breaks; 0x457F77..0x457F83 is an inline strcpy to scene+0x206; 0x457F87 calls FUN_00442510. A's related 0x73 claim is confirmed at 0x46278F..0x46282C (u8 result via 0x4A4094; ==1 then u32 via 0x4A40C8 and the success string 0x6F46CC; else string 0x6F4DFC). KR Hex-Rays case 0x74 (u8 subtype + uid + name + rename chat line) does not match EN. PySlayer has no opcode_0x73/0x74 builder; our windslayer_server.py has no 0x74 references.
open_questions: Whether nameplates for remote players re-read entity+0x00 each frame or use a cached record at entity+0x11DC (decides whether other players see the new name right away without a respawn).
Meaning of the u32 that follows result==1 in S2C 0x73 (passed to FUN_00464380); outside this batch.

specs.length: 4 if uid is 0 or unknown to the client; 12 for a non-local entity; 18 when target_uid is the local player

fields.name: target_uid
fields.meaning: uid (entity+0x84) of the character whose base stats changed. FUN_004189f0 returns NULL for uid 0 or a uid not in the scene list -> handler returns 1 and reads nothing more
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x20] (used for lookup and party-window match)

fields.meaning: key (record +0x00) of the premium-inventory record to consume (vector object at ctx+0x04, begin ctx+0x08, end ctx+0x0C). Read only when the entity is the local player

fields.name: consume_count
fields.meaning: quantity to consume; FUN_00464380 uses only the low 16 bits (BP). Record type byte +6 == 1: qty +8 decremented if qty >= count, record freed at 0; type 2: not decremented. Normally 1

specs.semantics: Result/broadcast of a stat redistribution (stat-reset cash item). Looks up the entity by uid; if absent, stops. Overwrites the four base stats +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC (bonus fields untouched). If level +0x99 != 0, FUN_00427f40(0) recomputes max MP +0x1110 and clamps cur MP +0xA0. Scans party windows 0x75..0x78 for the first one whose +0x134 == uid and, if max MP != 0, updates its '%u/%u' MP text (element 2) and gauge. FUN_00427d40(scene, entity, 0) recomputes max HP +0x110C and clamps cur HP +0x9C; if max HP != 0, FUN_0043d3f0 updates the party HP display. FUN_0041ace0 recomputes derived combat stats (in a special mode scene+0xF6C != 0 it overwrites all four stats with 55 and level with 49). Queues effect {0xA, 0x140, uid} on client+0x430 and plays sound 0x140 at the entity. If the entity is the local player: closes modal window 0x16, reads cash_item_serial and consume_count, consumes that premium item (FUN_00464380 also refreshes inventory/quickslot UI) and refreshes the stat window (FUN_00442510). Returns 1 on every path.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x4A sent from the stat redistribution window: u8 0x4A, u16 (low 16 bits of window+0x134), then 4x u8 = (low byte of current stat +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC) minus the window's per-stat value; the client then shows 'Waiting for the server to response.'. Send the 18-byte form to the requester; the 12-byte form (uid + 4 stats) can be broadcast to other clients that have the entity spawned. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x4A (stat reset). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 does not parse unless ctx+0x14 and ctx+0x18 are non-null. uid 0 or unknown uid: only 4 bytes read, no effect. For the local player, if the trailing 6 bytes are missing GetDataFromPacket leaves stale stack values (serial = entity pointer, count = low word of client pointer); FUN_00464380 then most likely matches nothing but still refreshes the UI; always send the 18-byte form to the owner. FUN_00464380 does not stop at the first type-1 match that leaves qty > 0 (keeps scanning) and calls FUN_0045e8e0 with -count even when qty < count. Stats are absolute; values inconsistent with level make the client-side remaining-points count negative. Max HP/MP recompute requires level 1..99 and class +0x110 <= 6. Effect/sound 0x140 plays for every recipient. No dialog shown. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C15, premium_cash#09): the client draws free points as total(level) - sum(stats) with NO clamp, so a 0x76 whose stats sum above the level total paints a NEGATIVE "Stat Point" value (observed -7). The server must keep sum(stats) <= total(level) when answering C2S 0x4A.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire format (u32 uid; stop if entity not found; 4x u16 into +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEA/+0xEC; if local player, u32 serial + u16 count). The structural-signature difference is only notation (A nested the rest inside if/else-stop, B used an early stop); the bytes are identical. The asm confirms it: u32 via [0x4A40C8] at 0x462856 -> [esp+0x20]; FUN_004189f0 at 0x46286A and JZ 0x46302A (return 1) at 0x462875; four CALL ESI with ESI=[0x4A4090] at 0x462899/0x4628B2/0x4628CB/0x4628E4 into EDI+0xE6/E8/EA/EC; local gate CMP ECX,[EAX+0x1D8] / JNZ 0x46302A at 0x462A5E; u32 [0x4A40C8] at 0x462A8D -> [esp+0x24] and u16 [0x4A4090] at 0x462AA1 -> [esp+0x14], both passed to FUN_00464380 at 0x462AB4. On the side details, A was right that FUN_00427d40 recomputes max HP (it writes +0x110C and clamps +0x9C), where B only said 'derived stats'. A was also right that the trigger is C2S 0x4A (Add u8 0x4A at 0x460BCA, send at 0x460C50). B's guess of C2S 0x72 is wrong: 0x72 is the stone extraction request at 0x46C066. B was right, and A missed, that FUN_0041ace0 forces the stats to 0x37 and the level to 0x31 when scene+0xF6C != 0 (decomp lines 590-600). Other checks: not in PySlayer (no opcode_0x76) and not in our server. The stat offsets match the u16 stats our 0x07 spawn builder writes. C2S/S2C pairing offset of 0x2C (0x4A->0x76, 0x72->0x9C).
open_questions: Stat names for +0xE6/+0xE8/+0xEC are inferred from stat-name table order; only +0xEA (INT -> MP formula) is behaviorally confirmed.
Which S2C packet fills the premium-inventory vector at ctx+0x04 (A said 0x6A/0x79, B said 0x6F) was not re-verified.
Whether C2S 0x4A's u16 (window+0x134) is an item code or a truncated cash-item serial is unresolved; the server reply's u32 serial must match the record key regardless.
Whether the original server broadcast the 12-byte form to others cannot be proven statically (the non-local path exists).

specs.name: SendMessageItemResult

locations.role: clear text of window 0x3FD elements 7 (recipient) and 9 (message)
C2S trigger: send site #55, opcode 0x4B from message window 0x3FD
cash item use dispatcher: items 0x766/0xCF8 open window 0x3FD

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = message delivered; any other value = failure

fields.name: cash_item_serial
fields.meaning: key (+0x00) of the premium-inventory record to consume (count fixed at 1 by the client)

specs.semantics: Result of using a 'send message to a player' cash item. Always first dismisses message box window 0x16 (the waiting modal). If result == 1: clears window 0x3FD text element 7 (recipient name) and element 9 (message body), closes window 0x3FD, reads cash_item_serial and consumes one of that premium item (inventory/quickslot refresh), then shows modal 'You successfully sent the message.'. Otherwise shows modal 'Failed to send the message .' and reads nothing more. Delivery of the message to the recipient is not part of this packet. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C14, social_friend#34): with cash_item_serial = 0 the success modal "You successfully sent the message." is still shown but NO item is consumed - serial 0 behaves as "no item". The server must always echo the real serial of the consumed record.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x4B: u16 item_ref, char[17] recipient name (window 0x3FD element 7, validated by FUN_0043df40), char[91] message (element 9). Window 0x3FD is opened by using cash items 0x766 or 0xCF8. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x4B (send note / message item). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 exits without parsing if ctx+0x14 or ctx+0x18 is null. result must be exactly 1 for success. On success with a missing u32 the serial is stale stack data (harmless, no match expected). Serial not found in the premium list -> nothing consumed, UI still refreshed. Live (C14): serial 0 (or any unmatched serial) leaves the item in the player's premium list while the success popup claims the message was sent - a silent client/server divergence. Live 2026-09-25 (livetest bug 4): the consume-by-serial the success calls (2009 FUN_0046df70 from 0x46C094, 2008 FUN_00464380) finds the serial but only acts on a record whose limit_type (+6) is 1 (count-limited: quantity - 1, removed at 0) or 2 (period item); a limit_type 0 record is found and left alone, so the S2C 0x6F that put the Note in the cash bag must carry limit_type 1.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer; not implemented in our server. String refs 0x6F6C58 / 0x6F6BF4 are used only by this handler.
open_questions: How the recipient receives the message (which S2C opcode) is outside this handler.
Exact in-game name of cash items 0x766/0xCF8 not resolved.
Confirm from the binary that cash_item_serial == 0 is a deliberate "no item" sentinel rather than a lookup that simply never matches (live: the modal shows, nothing is consumed).
blind_open_questions: Which C2S opcode sends the message request (no Add of 0x77 exists in the client)
Whether window 0x3FD is a megaphone/server-wide shout or a letter UI

specs.name: MemoList

locations.role: GetDataFromPacket u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) -> count at [ESP+0x12]; JBE 0x471AA3 skips loop when 0
GetDataFromPacket char buffer (IAT 0x4A4098) N=0x7E into the malloc'd record (one 126-byte read)
FUN_00459df0 appends record ptr to messenger list +0x34 (head +0x38, tail +0x3C, count +0x40)
UI window id 3 -> 8th control (+0x8C list, index 7) -> [ctrl+0x18]=0 (shows memo HUD button)
FUN_00470640: for each record in messenger+0x38 list, FUN_00489a80(0x3FE, record) adds record ptr to window 0x3FE item list +0xAC; count label '%u' from messenger+0x40
window 0x3FE controls 0x0C/0x0D: Draw_Text(record+0x00) = sender name (jump table 0x481670)
window 0x3FE controls 0x0E/0x0F: sprintf '%u/%u/%u %u:%u' from u16 record+0x6E,+0x70,+0x74,+0x76,+0x78 (+0x72 skipped)
row select in window 0x3FE: strncpy(messenger+0xA4, record+0x00, 0x11) = reply-target name
on confirm of 'All the messages will be deleted...' (dialog 0x16 result 0x64): C2S 0x44 (0 bytes), window 3 control 8 state 3, close 0x3FE, FUN_0046fc40 clears list

specs.grammar:
u8 count
repeat(count) {
  str[17] sender_name
  str[93] text
  u16 year
  u16 month
  u16 day_of_week
  u16 day
  u16 hour
  u16 minute
  u16 second
  u16 millisecond
}

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number of 126-byte memo records that follow (0..255; unsigned JBE / movzx loop bound).

fields.name: sender_name
fields.meaning: Record +0x00..+0x10. Sender character name; drawn as a C string by window 0x3FE controls 0x0C/0x0D (0x47E4E6) and strncpy'd (17 bytes) to messenger+0xA4 as the reply target on row select (0x4732C2). Must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (<=16 chars). Part of the single 126-byte read at 0x471A80.

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Record +0x11..+0x6D. Memo body, drawn with CIME::DrawMultiText (controls 0x10/0x11, 0x47F304). NUL-terminate within 93 bytes (<=92 chars).

fields.name: year
fields.meaning: Record +0x6E. First %u of '%u/%u/%u %u:%u' (SYSTEMTIME.wYear position).

fields.name: month
fields.meaning: Record +0x70. Second %u (wMonth).

fields.name: day_of_week
fields.meaning: Record +0x72. Not displayed (renderer skips it); SYSTEMTIME.wDayOfWeek position.

fields.name: day
fields.meaning: Record +0x74. Third %u (wDay).

fields.name: hour
fields.meaning: Record +0x76. Fourth %u (wHour).

fields.name: minute
fields.meaning: Record +0x78. Fifth %u (wMinute).

fields.name: second
fields.meaning: Record +0x7A. Not referenced by any renderer found (wSecond position).

fields.name: millisecond
fields.meaning: Record +0x7C. Not referenced (wMilliseconds position).

specs.semantics: Delivers stored memos (offline messages). The handler reads a u8 count, then for each record mallocs 0x7E bytes, reads exactly 126 bytes into it with one GetDataFromPacket(char*, 0x7E) call, and appends the pointer to the messenger memo list (messenger+0x34; FUN_00459df0 keeps head +0x38, tail +0x3C, count +0x40). The list is NOT cleared first, and the memo window is not redrawn here. After the loop (also when count==0) it finds UI window id 3 in the UI root list (messenger+0x70 -> +0x5C0), sets it as current (+0x5F0), walks to its 8th control (+0x8C list, index 7) and sets control+0x18 = 0, which shows/enables the HUD memo button. When that is used, FUN_00470640 opens window 0x3FE, adds every record pointer to the window's item list (+0xAC) and shows the count. The window renderer FUN_0047db10 then draws record+0x00 as the sender name, record+0x11 as the multi-line body, and u16s at +0x6E/+0x70/+0x74/+0x76/+0x78 as 'Y/M/D h:m'. The 16 bytes at +0x6E..+0x7D match a Win32 SYSTEMTIME exactly: wDayOfWeek at +0x72 is skipped, and wSecond/wMilliseconds are unused. Selecting a row copies 17 bytes of the name into messenger+0xA4 (reply target). Closing the window asks 'All the messages will be deleted when closing the window. Will you continue?'. On OK the client sends C2S 0x44 (no body), sets window 3 control 8 to state 3, closes 0x3FE and frees the list.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 gate: messenger+0x68/+0x70 must be non-null, otherwise the packet is dropped. The records accumulate: they are cleared only by the messenger reset on S2C 0x03 (FUN_0046f860 -> FUN_0046fc40) or by the C2S 0x44 confirm path, so resending the full list without a reset duplicates memos. count==0 still lights the window-3 control-8 memo button, so skip 0x78 entirely when there are no memos. sender_name must contain a NUL within its 17 bytes, or both Draw_Text and the strncpy to +0xA4 run on into the body. text must contain a NUL within its 93 bytes, or DrawMultiText runs into the date bytes. A truncated packet leaves the malloc'd (non-zeroed) record partly uninitialized. If window 3 or its 8th control is missing, the UI step is silently skipped. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C20, chat_mail_gm#11, chat_mail_gm#09): the map-change sequence RESETS the Msg HUD button (window 3 control 8) back to disabled even though the queue itself survives S2C 0x03. To relight the button after a map change or an 0x2F resync, send this packet again with count = 0 - that runs the HUD step without adding queue entries (records are append-only and would otherwise duplicate).
specs.trigger: Server sends when the player has stored memos, typically after login/world entry (after S2C 0x03, which resets the list), and presumably with count=1 when a new memo arrives (append-only behaviour supports this). FUN_00483470 (world-entry UI setup) also checks the list count at +0x40 before touching window 3.
specs.expected_response: None directly. Later, when the user confirms deleting memos on closing window 0x3FE, the client sends C2S 0x44 with 0 bytes (send site 0x47295F).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree on the wire at the call sites: u8 count at 0x471A50 (IAT 0x4A4094), then a loop (JL back-edge 0x471AA1) of malloc(0x7E) plus ONE GetDataFromPacket char-buffer read with N=0x7E (PUSH 0x7e at 0x471A7D, IAT 0x4A4098 at 0x471A80). The byte count 1+126*count is therefore identical. They disagree only on the 126-byte record: B gave an opaque str[126] 'text', A gave name[17] + text[93] + 8 u16. A is correct. FUN_00470640 (0x4706A6) passes each list record pointer (node+8) in EDX to FUN_00489a80, which appends it to window 0x3FE's item list at +0xAC (0x489ABB/0x489ACA). The window-0x3FE renderer in FUN_0047db10 fetches items from that same +0xAC list via FUN_00459fd0 and splits the record by control (jump table 0x481670 = {0x47E4E6, 0x47E4E6, 0x47E54F, 0x47E54F} for controls 0x0C..0x0F). Controls 0x0C/0x0D draw record+0x00 as a string (Draw_Text, PUSH EAX at 0x47E3F3). Controls 0x0E/0x0F do movzx word [EAX+0x78], [EAX+0x76], [EAX+0x74], [EAX+0x70], [EAX+0x6E] into sprintf '%u/%u/%u %u:%u' (0x47E584..0x47E5A7). Controls 0x10/0x11 do ADD EAX,0x11 then DrawMultiText (0x47F304/0x47F31D). FUN_00472900 strncpy's exactly 0x11 bytes from record+0 into messenger+0xA4 (0x4732B8..0x4732C2). So the record is a 17-byte name, a body at +0x11 running to +0x6D (93 bytes), and a 16-byte SYSTEMTIME at +0x6E, which fits the 0x7E size exactly. B's 'displayed as a single string' is wrong: +0 is drawn only up to the name's NUL, and the body and date come from fixed offsets. B's other observations (0x44 send on confirm, window 3 control 8 indicator, FUN_00483470 count check) are consistent with the code. Cross-refs: no PySlayer builder exists (opcode_0x78 import present, file missing). The opcode atlas lists 0x78 under Packet_handler_3 with no format. Our server has no builder. B notes the sibling S2C 0x6D (SubHandler4 0x462E42) has the same u8 + repeat 126-byte shape, but its record sub-layout was not re-verified here.
open_questions: The date field names are inferred from the SYSTEMTIME-shaped layout. The client prints +0x6E/+0x70/+0x74 as the first three numbers, so year/month/day is the natural order, but the server's original fill convention is unverified. +0x72, +0x7A and +0x7C are never read.
Which C2S action creates a memo server-side (the send-memo request) was not identified in this batch.
The initial visibility of window 3 control 8 before any 0x78 comes from UI resources, not from code seen here.
Is 0x6D (same wire shape, list +0x5F4, window 3 control 6) a different message category with the same record layout? Not verified in this adjudication.

spec_errata.new: send count = 0 after each map change/resync to relight it

specs.name: CashBoxItemAdd

locations.role: handler block start: alloc 28 zeroed bytes
push_back to cash item box list mall+0x28
rebuild box window 0x1FC list (item_id, quantity, serial)

specs.grammar:
u32 serial
u16 item_id
u8 limit_type
u8 unk_07
u16 quantity
u16 expire_year
u16 expire_month
u16 expire_day_of_week
u16 expire_day
u16 expire_hour
u16 expire_minute
u16 expire_second
u16 expire_milliseconds
u8 origin
u8 unk_1b

fields.name: serial
fields.meaning: Record +0x00: unique cash item serial (box lookup key with item_id, FUN_0045e6f0).

fields.name: item_id
fields.meaning: Record +0x04: item template id.

fields.name: limit_type
fields.meaning: Record +0x06: 1 = count-limited, 2 = period item.

fields.name: unk_07
fields.meaning: Record +0x07: padding, send 0.

fields.name: quantity
fields.meaning: Record +0x08: count shown in box window 0x1FC.

fields.name: expire_year..expire_milliseconds
fields.meaning: Record +0x0A..+0x19: expiry; year < 1900 = none.

fields.name: origin
fields.meaning: Record +0x1A (byte-read at 0x45FB4F): 0 = purchased with cash (refund value shown), 3 = event reward.

fields.name: unk_1b
fields.meaning: Record +0x1B: padding, send 0.

specs.semantics: Adds one record to the cash item box: allocates a zeroed 28-byte node, copies the payload raw, appends it to list mall+0x28 (no duplicate check), then FUN_0045b280 rebuilds box window 0x1FC and FUN_0045b360 rebuilds shop panel 0x1FD. Balances and bags are not touched. Returns 1.
specs.trigger: A new item lands in the player's cash item box outside a purchase reply (e.g. a received gift, or an item moved back to the box). Purchases use 0x6C, which carries balances plus the same record. Request not traced.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Only the SubHandler4 entry gate. No dedup: the same serial sent twice shows twice. Safe outside the shop (list + window rebuild only), but the shop windows are only meaningful after 0x6A. Always send exactly 28 bytes.
open_questions: Which C2S action (e.g. box moves 0x48/0x4B, gift receipt) the server should answer with 0x79.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts agree that the handler performs exactly one 28-byte raw read (PUSH 0x1c at 0x462092, call through IAT 0x4A4098 at 0x462099), so the wire length (28) is not in dispute. They differ only on the tail: A has u8 origin + u8 unk_1b, B has u16 unk_1a. The client reads record +0x1A as a single byte: CMP byte ptr [ECX+0x1a],DL (DL=0) at 0x45FB4F on box-list records returned by FUN_0045e6f0 (which scans vector mall+0x2C, i.e. this list +0x28), and CMP byte ptr [EDX+0x1a],3 at 0x462322 on the same record type in 0x6C. Nothing reads +0x1B. A's layout is correct. The same 28-byte record layout is read by 0x6A, 0x6C and 0x6F. PySlayer has no opcode_0x79.py. Our server: not implemented.

specs.name: MentorRegisterResult

locations.role: handler block (sub3 jump-table case 0x7A); no room gate
GetDataFromPacket char buffer N=0x11 (IAT 0x4A4098) into esp0+0x20: mentor_name
SUB EAX,0x65 / JZ 0x471742 (novice error); SUB 1 / JZ 0x4716F2 (not found); fall through = success
result 0x65: sprintf_s "<%s>%s" name + 'is a novice. Only a class-upgraded player can become a mentor.', colour 0xFFFD4C87, return 1 with no further read
result 0x66: sprintf_s "<%s>%s" name + 'can not be found.', colour 0xFFFD4C87, return 1 with no further read
success: operator new(0x28), zero it, copy the 17 name bytes to node+0x00..0x10
success only: GetDataFromPacket u32 (IAT 0x4A40C8) into node+0x18: mentor_uid
node+0x14 = result; if result==0x64 then node+0x14 = CMessenger+0x90 (own channel) and node+0x20 = 0, else node+0x20 = 4; node+0x24 = 1
FUN_00459df0 appends the node to the mentor list at CMessenger+0x14
C2S 0x5C {str[17] mentor_name} request this answers; refuses your own name locally ('You can't register yourself.')

mentor login notice helper (called from the S2C 0x7D handler at 0x471927): same encoding, 0x64 = same channel (status 0), 0x66 = offline (status 1), else channel N (status 4); matches the head entry by +0x18 uid
S2C 0x03 handler mentor sub-block (after the u32 gate): name[17], u8 channel (0x66 = offline), same node layout

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 0x65 = error, target is a novice ('<name>is a novice. Only a class-upgraded player can become a mentor.'). 0x66 = error, not found ('<name>can not be found.'). 0x64 = success, mentor online on YOUR channel: the node channel is taken from CMessenger+0x90 and status is 0. Any other value = success, with the value stored as the mentor's channel number and status 4 (online on another channel).
fields.dest_or_source: stack esp0+0x13; on success -> node+0x14 (replaced by CMessenger+0x90 if 0x64)

fields.name: mentor_name
fields.meaning: Mentor character name, NUL-padded. Printed via "<%s>%s" into a 0x80 buffer. On success its 17 bytes are copied into the node.

fields.name: mentor_uid
fields.meaning: Mentor's character uid. Present only on success. Later S2C 0x7D mentor status updates (FUN_00470780) match on node+0x18.

specs.semantics: The client first reads result (u8) and mentor_name[17]. For result 0x65 or 0x66 it prints a red (0xFFFD4C87) main-chat line built from "<%s>%s" with the name and the error text, returns 1 and reads nothing else. For any other result it does the following in order. It prints the green (0xFF00C800) line '<name>is registered as your mentor.' and allocates a zeroed 0x28-byte node. It copies the 17 name bytes to node+0x00 and reads the u32 mentor_uid into node+0x18. It sets node+0x14 = result. If result == 0x64 it overwrites node+0x14 with CMessenger+0x90 (own channel) and sets status node+0x20 = 0; otherwise it sets status = 4. It sets node+0x24 = 1, appends the node to the mentor list at CMessenger+0x14 (FUN_00459df0) and refreshes the messenger UI (FUN_00470270). There is no duplicate check.
specs.trigger: Server reply to C2S 0x5C {str[17] mentor_name}, sent by FUN_0046ff70 from the name-entry dialog. The client blocks registering yourself, and FUN_00472900 only lets a novice register ('Only a novice can register a mentor.'). Send 0x65 if the target has not class-upgraded, 0x66 if they don't exist or are offline, and 0x64 or the channel number on success.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub3 entry gate: CMessenger+0x68 and +0x70 must be non-zero. No chat-room gate. Reads use CMessenger+0x74 (g_sock_game), which FUN_0046f860 sets from the S2C 0x03 handler, so send this only after S2C 0x03. mentor_name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes: the local is not pre-zeroed and is formatted into a 0x80-byte buffer with _sprintf_s, where an overrun triggers the CRT invalid-parameter handler. Success appends a new node every time with no duplicate check, so don't send success twice, or after S2C 0x03 already delivered a mentor. FUN_00470780 only inspects the list head. On a same-channel success, send 0x64 rather than the numeric channel: a numeric value equal to your own channel is still stored with status 4 ('other channel'). This differs from the 0x03 block, which compares against the own channel. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#17): the 22-byte success form (result 0x64 + str[17] name + u32 mentor_uid) is accepted live - the grammar is right; the wsproto encoder dropped mentor_uid because of a hex-literal comparison bug.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: The two analysts agree on every read and its order. The structural difference is only that B spells out the terminating branch. A gave 'u8 result; str[17] mentor_name; if(result != 0x65 && result != 0x66) { u32 mentor_uid }' and B gave the same with an explicit 'else { stop }'. The asm confirms both paths. At 0x4715CD, call [0x4A4094] reads the u8 into esp0+0x13. At 0x4715DC/0x4715E3, PUSH 0x11 then call [0x4A4098] reads 17 bytes into esp0+0x20. At 0x4715E9..0x4715FA, MOVZX result, SUB 0x65 JZ 0x471742, SUB 1 JZ 0x4716F2. Both error blocks (0x4716F2..0x47173F and 0x471742..0x47178F) contain only _sprintf_s, FUN_004817d0 and RET 0x10, with no GetDataFromPacket. The success fall-through does its single extra read at 0x471690 (call [0x4A40C8], u32 into node+0x18). So B's explicit form, with 'else { stop }', is the canonical grammar and A's is equivalent. One side point: A said the matching mentor sub-block lives in S2C 0x07 at 0x44E5BA and that the client needs 0x07 first. That is wrong. 0x44E5BA is inside the S2C 0x03 handler (asm marker for 0x03 precedes it; FUN_0046f860 is called there at 0x44E52F and sets +0x74/+0x90 and clears +0xCC), as B said. windslayer_server.py _build_pyslayer_opcode_03 emits that mentor gate u32 = 0, which confirms it. Node layout, colours and status values (0x64 -> own channel, status 0; other -> status 4) were verified at 0x4716A1..0x4716C7 and match FUN_00470780 (S2C 0x7D). There is no PySlayer builder for 0x7A, and it is not implemented in windslayer_server.py.
open_questions: Server-side rule for when 0x65 applies (the class-upgrade check happens on the server) is not visible in the client.
Whether a channel value of 0 or a value >= 0x67 is ever used in practice. The client accepts any non-0x65/0x66 value as success.

CMessenger+0x90 is copied from byte [[CMessenger+0x6C]+0x1CF] in FUN_0046f860. Its identity as the local channel number comes from its use as the 'same channel' value (0x7A, FUN_00470780), not from a direct write of the channel.

spec_errata.old: no live byte-count confirmation
spec_errata.new: success with result 0x64 = 22 B (live)

specs.name: MenteeLoggedIn

locations.role: search mentee list (messenger+0x28 head) for record with +0x18 == uid
not found: malloc(0x28) new record, flag=0
call FUN_00470880(flag): status/channel fixup, append if new, UI refresh
green system chat line via FUN_004817d0

specs.grammar:
u32 mentee_uid
u8 channel
str[17] mentee_name

fields.name: mentee_uid
fields.meaning: Unique id of the mentee character. Used as lookup key into the messenger mentee list; written to rec+0x18.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Channel the mentee logged into. 100 (0x64) = same channel as the local player: the client replaces it with its own channel (messenger+0x90), sets status rec+0x20=0 and prints '<%s> has logged in. (Menti)'. Any other value: stored as-is, status rec+0x20=4 (online on another channel), prints '<%s> has logged in.(Menti, Channel %d)' with this value.

fields.name: mentee_name
fields.meaning: Mentee character name, NUL-padded, exactly 17 bytes. Shown in the chat line and the messenger window.

specs.semantics: Mentee came online. Handler is in the CMessenger sub-dispatcher (this = *(game_state+0x4e4)). Looks up mentee_uid in the mentee CPList (messenger+0x24, head +0x28, count +0x30). If found, the existing 0x28-byte record is zeroed in place and refilled (not re-added); otherwise a new 0x28-byte record is malloc'd. Reads channel -> rec+0x14 and name -> rec+0x00, sets rec+0x18=uid, then FUN_00470880: rec+0x24=2 (relation type mentee), channel==100 -> rec+0x14=own channel (messenger+0x90) and rec+0x20=0, else rec+0x20=4; appends to the mentee list only if newly allocated; calls FUN_00470270 (redraw messenger window 0x176; mentor tab count '(%u)' = mentor count + mentee count). Finally prints a green (0xFF00C800) system chat line: '<name> has logged in.(Menti, Channel N)' if status==4 else '<name> has logged in. (Menti)'.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 runs only if messenger+0x68 != 0 and messenger+0x70 (UI root) != 0; otherwise it returns 0, SubHandler4/5 do not claim 0x7B and the packet is silently dropped. messenger+0x74 (the CSNSocket used for reads) and messenger+0x90 (own channel) are set by the messenger reset FUN_0046f860, which is called from the S2C 0x03 handler at 0x44E52F; send only after 0x03. Channel value 102 (0x66) has NO special meaning here (unlike 0x7D/0x03) and would show as 'Channel 102'. Zeroing an existing record is safe (same uid).
specs.trigger: Server sends to a mentor when one of their mentees logs in (or changes channel).
specs.references: No PySlayer builder (opcode_0x7B import is in server_packets/__init__.py try/except but the file does not exist). Strings '<%s> has logged in.(Menti, Channel %d)' @0x6F5DBC and '<%s> has logged in. (Menti)' @0x6F5EA8 ('Menti' = mentee). Record layout matches 0x7E and the 0x03 mentor sub-block (0x44E55C..0x44E608: name[17]@+0, channel@+0x14, uid@+0x18, status@+0x20, type@+0x24). Our server does not send it (windslayer_server.py only handles C2S 0x7E portal).
open_questions: Whether the server ever sends 0x7B for a mentee already in the list (channel change) or only on login; both are handled.
Exact server rule for channel==100 vs real channel number (client treats 100 as 'same channel as me').
blind_open_questions: Where CMessenger+0x90 (own channel, used for the value 100) is filled was not traced.
Not confirmed whether the original server also sent 0x7B when a mentee changed channel.

specs.name: MenteeRemove

locations.role: FUN_00459f20 unlink node from mentee list (messenger+0x24) then _free(record)

specs.grammar: u32 mentee_uid

fields.name: mentee_uid
fields.meaning: Unique id of the mentee to drop from the local mentee list.
fields.dest_or_source: local [ESP+0x14] -> arg 2 of FUN_004722e0, compared with record +0x18

specs.semantics: Walks the mentee list (messenger+0x28 head); every record whose +0x18 == mentee_uid is unlinked (FUN_00459f20 on list messenger+0x24) and freed. Then refreshes the messenger window (FUN_00470270). No chat message. Unknown uid -> only the refresh happens. Because mentee records never get the 'offline' status from 0x7B/0x7E, this is most likely the 'mentee logged out' notification (mentees appear only while online) or the relationship being dissolved.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same SubHandler3 gate as 0x7B (messenger+0x68 and +0x70 non-null, else dropped). Send only after S2C 0x03 (messenger reset sets messenger+0x74). Safe for unknown uid.
specs.trigger: Server sends to a mentor when a mentee logs out or the mentor/mentee link is removed.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder. No UI string. Not implemented in our server.
open_questions: Whether 0x7C means 'mentee logged out' or 'mentee relationship removed' server-side; the client just deletes the entry either way.
blind_open_questions: Whether the original server used 0x7C for mentee logout, for relationship dissolution, or for both. The client handles both the same way.

specs.name: MentorStatus

locations.role: gate: first record of mentor list (messenger+0x18 head) must have +0x18 == mentor_uid

specs.grammar:
u32 mentor_uid
u8 channel_or_state

fields.name: mentor_uid
fields.meaning: Unique id of the local player's mentor. Must equal the uid of the (single) mentor record, else the packet is ignored.
fields.dest_or_source: local [ESP+0x1c] -> arg 1 of FUN_00470780, compared with mentor record +0x18

fields.name: channel_or_state
fields.meaning: 100 (0x64): mentor online on the same channel -> record status +0x20=0, +0x14=own channel (messenger+0x90), chat '<%s> has logged in.(Mentor)'. 102 (0x66): mentor offline -> status +0x20=1, no chat message, channel byte untouched. Any other value = channel number the mentor is on -> status +0x20=4, +0x14=value, chat '<%s> has logged in.(Mentor, Channel %d)'.
fields.dest_or_source: low byte of local [ESP+0x14] -> arg 2 of FUN_00470780 (only BL used) -> mentor record +0x14 / +0x20

specs.semantics: Updates the online state of the player's mentor. FUN_00470780 checks the head of the mentor CPList (messenger+0x14, head +0x18) exists and its record uid (+0x18) == mentor_uid; if not, nothing happens. Otherwise sets status/channel as described and, for 100 and channel values, prints a green (0xFF00C800) system chat line. It does NOT call the messenger window refresh (FUN_00470270), so the list display updates on the next refresh.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 gate (messenger+0x68/+0x70 non-null). Requires a mentor record to already exist: it is created only by S2C 0x03 (mentor sub-block when the mentor uid read at 0x44E54C is non-zero) or by S2C 0x7A (mentor registered). Our server's 0x03 sends mentor gate = 0, so 0x7D would be ignored until that changes. Only the FIRST mentor record is checked.
specs.trigger: Server sends to a mentee when their mentor logs in (channel/100) or logs out (102).
specs.references: Strings '<%s> has logged in.(Mentor, Channel %d)' @0x6F5D6C and '<%s> has logged in.(Mentor)' @0x6F5DE4. Offline sentinel 0x66 matches the 0x03 mentor sub-block (0x44E5BD: channel 0x66 -> status 1). PySlayer opcode_0x03 carries a 'Mentor name' field but has no 0x7D builder. Not in our server.
open_questions: Whether values other than 100/102 are ever sent for same-channel login (client treats any value other than 100/102 as a channel number).
blind_open_questions: Not checked whether the original server ever sent status 101 here. In S2C 0x7A, 101 is the 'is a novice' error. Here 101 would be treated as channel 101.

specs.name: MenteeList

locations.role: rec+0x24=2; channel==100 -> own channel & status 0, else status 4
FUN_00470270 messenger window refresh (inside the loop, once per entry)

fields.name: count
fields.meaning: Number of mentee entries that follow.

fields.name: channel
fields.meaning: Per entry. 100 (0x64) = same channel as the local player (client substitutes messenger+0x90 and sets status rec+0x20=0); anything else = channel number, status rec+0x20=4. No offline sentinel is handled here.

fields.name: mentee_name
fields.meaning: Per entry. Mentee character name, NUL-padded, 17 bytes.

fields.name: mentee_uid
fields.meaning: Per entry. Mentee unique id (key used by 0x7B/0x7C).

specs.semantics: Bulk-adds mentees to the messenger mentee CPList (messenger+0x24). NOTE the per-entry field order differs from 0x7B: channel, name, uid. For each entry a zeroed 0x28-byte record is filled, rec+0x24=2 (type mentee), status set per channel rule, appended (no duplicate check, list NOT cleared first), and the messenger window is refreshed after each append. No chat messages.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 gate (messenger+0x68/+0x70 non-null). The mentee list is cleared only by the messenger reset FUN_0046f860 -> FUN_0046fb70 called from the S2C 0x03 handler (0x44E52F); resending 0x7E without an intervening 0x03 duplicates entries. Send after 0x03. count must match the data present.
specs.trigger: Server sends to a mentor after entering the game (after S2C 0x03) with the currently online mentees.
specs.references: Not to be confused with C2S 0x7E (portal use, 4-byte portal code, handled by our server at windslayer_server.py:627 and PySlayer parse_0x7E.py). No PySlayer S2C builder. Same 0x28-byte relation record as friends (0x0B, type 0) and mentor (0x03/0x7A, type 1).
open_questions: Whether the real server included offline mentees (client would show channel 102 as a channel, so probably only online mentees are sent).
blind_open_questions: Whether offline mentees were ever sent in this list. The client cannot mark them offline (102 is not handled here), so the list is probably online-only.

specs.name: ExpDeltaFromMenti

fields.name: exp_delta
fields.meaning: signed exp change for the local player (same processing as 0x21: level-up/down, message, scene+0x278 += delta)

fields.name: menti_id
fields.meaning: id of the mentee (apprentice) the exp bonus came from. Matched against record+0x18 of the entries in the mentor/menti list (game_state+0x4E4 manager, list head +0x28; records are filled by SubHandler3 e.g. S2C 0x0B: name[17]@+0, u8@+0x14, u32@+0x18, u8@+0x20). The found record's name (+0) goes into the message. Read ONLY when exp_delta > 0

specs.semantics: Same as 0x21 (ignored if no local player; level-up/down; scene+0x278 += delta; exp bar refresh), but when delta > 0 it also reads menti_id and searches the mentor manager list. If a record with +0x18 == menti_id is found, it posts "You've received (+%d) experience points.(Menti[%s])" with that record's name. If not found, NO message is shown but the exp is still added. For delta <= 0 the u32 is not read and the 0x21 behaviour applies (the 'Lost (%d) EXP.' message for negative values).
specs.trigger: Server grants the mentor a bonus share of exp earned by one of their mentees ('Menti').
specs.gates_and_hazards: Same local-player gate and exp-baseline hazard as 0x21. Sending menti_id with delta <= 0 is harmless (trailing bytes are ignored). The name lookup needs the mentor list to have been filled first (SubHandler3 0x0B-family packets); otherwise the message is skipped.

locations.role: walk mentor list [game_state+0x4E4]+0x28 for record+0x18 == menti_id

specs.references: Strings: 0x6F5E00 "You've received (+%d) experience points.(Menti[%s])", plus the mentor/menti login strings used by SubHandler3 0x4708C0 / 0x470780. The newer KR build shares a case with 0x21 but uses 64-bit exp and a different extra read order, so it is NOT compatible. Not in windslayer_server.py or PySlayer.
open_questions: Whether menti_id is the mentee's in-world uid or a DB character id: it is compared to the u32 at record+0x18 filled by SubHandler3 0x0B, whose source was not traced further.
Exact list-object layout (manager+4 list vs head at +0x28) not verified; only the compare offsets are certain.
blind_open_questions: Numeric identity of mentee_id (character db id vs uid) - only known as record+0x18 of the [this+0x4E4]+0x28 list; the S2C packet that fills that list was not traced here.

specs.name: SecondPasswordResult

locations.role: target==0x1F9: call FUN_0045E0D0(this+0x700), the cash-shop purchase continuation
other target: FUN_00483430(g_ui_root, target, 3, 1) -> ui_root+0x5A4=1; FUN_00446300(target,0,3,0,1) opens that window
result!=1: FUN_00489DA0 message box 'Invalid password.\r\n\r\nPlease check your password again.' (0x6F6BBC)
opens the password dialog 0x201 and stores the target window id at dialog+0x134 (via FUN_00483270). It refuses with 'no SS# in this ID...' when [game_state+0x4cc]+0x218==0.
matching C2S request 0x51: Add u8 0x51, Add(char*,0x15) password, Add(ulong) dialog+0x134 target window id
after a verified 0x1F9: checks the selected cash item price (+0x1FC) against the cash balance (+0x588) and opens the purchase confirm window 0x1F9, or shows 'You are short of cash.'

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: Second-password (SS#) check result. 1 = accepted. Any other value shows the 'Invalid password' message box and reading stops.

fields.name: target_window_id
fields.meaning: UI window id to continue into. Echo back the u32 the client sent in C2S 0x51. Known values: 0x1A7 = Bank/warehouse window, 0x1F9 = cash-shop purchase confirmation (special-cased), 0x235 = a third protected window (unidentified). Any other id is opened with FUN_00446300(id,0,3,0,1).

specs.length: 5 when result==1; 1 otherwise (anything after is ignored)
specs.semantics: Reply to the secondary-password (SS#) dialog. Flow: a protected action (bank NPC -> 0x1A7, cash-shop buy -> 0x1F9, or 0x235) opens dialog 0x201 with the target id stored at dialog+0x134. The user types the password. The client sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id} and closes the dialog. On S2C 0x80: if result != 1, it shows the 'Invalid password. Please check your password again.' box. If result == 1 and target == 0x1F9 (505), it calls FUN_0045E0D0: the selected cash item (this+0x700+0x5BC) is re-checked against the cash balance (+0x588). It then opens purchase confirm window 0x1F9 (mode 4) and sets its fields, or shows 'You are short of cash.'. If result == 1 and target is anything else, ui_root+0x5A4 = 1 and window <target> is opened with mode 3; for 0x1A7 that is the bank window, drawn from the data sent in 0x65. Nothing is sent back directly. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C7, login_character#07): target_window_id 0x235 is the CHARACTER-DELETE confirmation window. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F.
specs.trigger: Send in reply to C2S 0x51 (the password dialog submit). Echo the client's target_window_id. Send result=1 when the password matches the account's secondary password/SS#, and anything else to reject.
specs.expected_response: none directly. With target 0x1F9 the user then confirms the purchase in window 0x1F9, which triggers the cash-shop buy request (not traced here). With 0x1A7 the bank opens using the existing 0x65 data. CHARACTER-DELETE SEQUENCE (live-verified, C7, login_character#07) - all four steps are required: (1) the player presses Delete on window 0x12; FUN_00464480 opens password dialog 0x201 with owner 0x235. (2) The dialog's OK sends C2S 0x51 {str[21] password, u32 target_window_id = 0x235}. (3) The server MUST answer S2C 0x80 {result 1, target_window_id 0x235} (any other result shows "Invalid password"); without that answer the flow stops silently at 0x51 and deletion is impossible. (4) Confirm window 0x235 opens; its OK (control 2) sends C2S 0x12 {str[17] name, str[21] password}, which the server answers with S2C 0x1F. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C32, shop_storage#03): for target 0x1A7 the bank window renders from whatever S2C 0x65 last delivered, so the 0x65 must precede this packet; no post-open 0x65 is required.
specs.gates_and_hazards: There is no state gate in the handler. The password dialog itself only opens if [game_state+0x4cc]+0x218 != 0 (set by the 0x5A handler when the account's SS# field at +0x131 differs from the default at this+0xD0A); otherwise the client shows 'no SS# in this ID...'. Sending an arbitrary target id makes the client try to open that window (FUN_00446300) and sets ui_root+0x5A4=1. Sending 0x80 unsolicited with a real window id pops that window open. Target 0x1F9 with no cash item selected (+0x5BC == 0) does nothing.
specs.references: windslayer_server.py has _build_opcode_80(value, flag=1) = u8 flag + u32 value (byte layout correct) and _send_cash_balance(), but labels it 'CashShopBalance' and fills the u32 with the winnie balance (999999). That meaning is WRONG: the u32 is a UI window id, not a balance. The function is also never called. It should instead reply to C2S 0x51 (which is not in _dispatch) by echoing the target window id. PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x80.py sends p8(1)+p32u(0x4CF) (same layout, a KR window id, comment 'About Cash??'). The KR Hex-Rays 0x80 (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c:7975) likewise reads u8==1 then a u32 and switches on window-like ids (0, 15/24/34, 79, 80, 153, 176...), which confirms the window-id meaning, though the KR id set differs from EN.
open_questions: [RESOLVED by live verification login_character#07, 2026-09-17] Live: window 0x235 is the character-delete confirmation window. Dialog 0x201 is opened with owner 0x235 by the Delete button, its OK sends C2S 0x51 {password, 0x235}, and the OK of window 0x235 (control 2) sends C2S 0x12. Original question: "Identity of window 0x235, the third caller of the password dialog (FUN_00446300 line ~1236; related path sends C2S 0x12 with a 17-byte name when mode 2)."
Which account field the original server compared the password against (the client dialog is labelled around an 'SS#'; the C2S 0x51 field is 21 bytes). Is it the same width as the login password?
Whether the original server ever sent result values other than 0/1 (the client treats every non-1 value the same).
blind_open_questions: Which C2S opcode carries the password this packet answers (not found among the scouted send sites checked: 0x49/0x51 room joins, 0x65/0x66 ID-transfer dialog 0x290)?
Full list of EN window ids that are legitimately gated by this check (0x1F9 is certain; 0x1A7 storage is a guess).
Whether FUN_00446300 is a guaranteed no-op for an unknown window id (only its entry checks were read).

spec_errata.new: 0x235 identified as the character-delete confirm window

spec_errata.old: expected_response did not mention the delete chain
spec_errata.new: the delete chain is written into expected_response

spec_errata.old: identity of window 0x235 unknown
spec_errata.new: 0x235 = character-delete confirm window
