spec_errata.new: 0x65 must simply precede the 0x80 bank open

specs.name: VillageTransferResult

locations.role: handler block entry (primary switch case 0x81); no popup dismissal or state gate
GetDataFromPacket u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) -> result at [esp+0x7A] (LEA [ESP+0x86] taken after 3 pushes)
result==1: GetDataFromPacket u64 (IAT 0x4A4118) written directly into [game_state+0x4CC]+0x270 = scene+0x270 (gold)
FUN_004659D0(gold_lo, gold_hi, 9, 0xB): sprintf %I64u, then set the text of UI window 9 control 0xB
result!=1: FUN_00489DA0 message box 'Village transfer failed / Please try again in a few minutes.', then JMP 0x44D7AD with no more reads

probable request: C2S 0x5D = Add u8 0x5D, Add u8 [dlg+0x40] (village index), Add u16 cost (low 16 bits of [dlg+0x134]), Send(1). Sent from dialog 0x237 only if client gold (scene+0x270) >= cost; otherwise shows 'You are short of gold.'

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = village transfer accepted and a gold value follows. Any other value shows the 'Village transfer failed' dialog and nothing more is read.

fields.name: gold
fields.dest_or_source: scene(*0x70EECC)+0x270, read directly into it. This is the same u64 gold field that S2C 0x03 fills and that the client's 'You are short of gold' check at 0x44AD6A reads.
fields.meaning: The player's new ABSOLUTE gold total after the transfer fee, not a delta. It is shown as a %I64u string in UI window 9 control 0xB. Only present when result==1.

specs.semantics: Result of a paid village (town) teleport. If result==1, the client overwrites its u64 gold at scene+0x270 with the value from the packet, updates the gold text in UI window 9 control 0xB and plays sound 0x29. This handler does NOT change the map or the player's position, so the actual move has to come from the normal map-change packets. If result!=1, the client shows a 'Village transfer failed. Please try again in a few minutes.' message box and reads nothing more. Both paths then break to 0x44D7AD.
specs.trigger: Server reply to the village-transfer request, most likely C2S 0x5D (u8 village_index, u16 cost), which the dialog-0x237 confirm button sends at 0x44ADBA. The server can also send it at any time to set absolute gold and play the coin sound.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No preconditions: gold is written even when the player is not in the world. On failure, do NOT add the u64, because the client reads only 1 byte and any extra bytes would just be ignored. On success the u64 is required; a 1-byte packet with result==1 would make GetDataFromPacket read past the end of the buffer. Gold is an absolute value, so sending a delta would corrupt both the displayed gold and the client-side 'short of gold' check.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts found the same reads in the same order: a u8 result at 0x452908 (IAT 0x4A4094), CMP [esp+0x7A],1 / JNZ 0x45296F at 0x45290E, and, only when result==1, a u64 at 0x452931 (IAT 0x4A4118) written straight into [ESI+0x4CC]+0x270 (scene+0x270, gold). Their only difference was the grammar text. Analyst A wrote an explicit 'else { stop }'; analyst B left the else branch out. On the wire the two are identical, and both are right. The failure path at 0x45296F only pushes the message-box arguments, calls FUN_00489DA0 and jumps to the shared break at 0x44D7AD with no GetDataFromPacket call, and the success path also ends at 0x45296A with JMP 0x44D7AD. I use A's explicit form because it records that the failure packet is exactly 1 byte. Both analysts also agree on: the FUN_004659D0 %I64u formatting into window 9 control 0xB (the sprintf of "%I64u" is confirmed at 0x4659ED), Play_Sound(0x29,0) at 0x452964, and the length (9 bytes on success, 1 on failure). B's extra lead also checks out: at 0x44ADBA in FUN_00446300 the client Adds u8 0x5D, u8 [dlg+0x40] and u16 (MOVZX SI of [dlg+0x134]), then calls Send(1), after a u64 gold >= cost check at 0x44AD6A..0x44AD7A. That makes C2S 0x5D the likely request. Other references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x81 has the same wire shape (u8 result, u64 gold on 1, UI control 7, sound 0x23, 'village move failed' text). PySlayer has no opcode_0x81 file, and our server (windslayer_server.py) has no 0x81 or 0x5D handling.
open_questions: Is C2S 0x5D (u8 village_index, u16 cost) the request that gets 0x81 back? The send site at 0x44ADBA is certain, but the pairing is inferred from the dialog flow and the gold check, not seen in a capture.
Which packets did the original server send after 0x81 to actually warp the player? Probably the usual 0x08/0x03/0x07/0x0A/0x28/0x44/0x1A map-change sequence.

specs.name: ItemStallOpenResult
specs.grammar: u8 result

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = the stall opened. 9 = 'Invalid information transaction... This violation will be recored...' warning box. Any other value = 'Item stall opening failed. Closed the stall and try again later.' box.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [ESP+0xc]; checked against 1 at 0x46D0DB and 9 at 0x46D102

specs.semantics: Reply to the seller's C2S 0x5E (open item stall). Note that the client already sets ctx+0x20 (selling) = 1 and ctx+0x1c (setup) = 0 right after it sends 0x5E (0x46B63B). ctx here means the window-mode controller at game_state+0xD5C, which is EBX in the handler. result==1 calls FUN_00466f20 (ESI=ctx). That sets ctx+0x20=1 and ctx+0x1c=0, calls FUN_00489320(0x259,0x19,3) to change the state of stall-window control 0x19 (the Open/Start button), disables child controls #25 and #26 (child+0x18=0), then calls FUN_00489320(0x259,0x1c,3) and (0x259,0x1d,3). This switches window 0x259 into selling mode. result==9 shows message box 0x6F6058 through FUN_00489da0(msg,3,3,0,0) and sets ctx+0x1c=1. Any other result shows message box 0x6F6470 and sets ctx+0x1c=1. On both failure paths ctx+0x20 (selling) stays 1, so the next Close click sends C2S 0x60 and needs S2C 0x84 to close the window. Reads exactly 1 byte and returns 1 (handled).
specs.trigger: Send it to the seller as the reply to C2S 0x5E (u8 item_count, str[25] shop_name, per item: u16,u16,u32,u8 n,u16*n,u16), which the client sends from 0x46B546..0x46B635 when the stall window's Start button (control 0x19) is clicked. On success the server should also send S2C 0x85 to the other players on the map.
specs.expected_response: None. The client sends nothing back.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Sub-handler entry gate: ctx+8 != 0 and ctx+0xc (UI root) != 0, or the function returns 0 and the packet goes on down the sub-handler chain. On failure (result != 1) ctx+0x20 stays 1, so the Close button does not close locally and sends C2S 0x60 instead. The server MUST answer that 0x60 with 0x84 result=1, or the player is stuck in the stall window (FUN_00465fe0 refuses to switch modes while ctx+0x20 != 0 and the mode is 0x259). Result 9 is the 'cheat' wording. Use it only for real tampering. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18/#19): CLIENT-SIDE ITEM DUPLICATION HAZARD. S2C 0x83 result == 1 (and S2C 0x82 with result != 1) sets ctx+0x1C = 1 WHATEVER the current window mode, so outside a real stall this latches the stall SETUP flag. FUN_004665e0's 0x259 branch then returns the listed items into the bag whenever ANY later 0x87 buyer window is closed, without checking whose list it is (observed Blue Mushroom 5 -> 15). S2C 0x84 with no window open does NOT clear the flag. SERVER RULE: send 0x83 only in reply to C2S 0x5F and 0x82 only in reply to C2S 0x5E. The old "inert outside mode 0x259" claim (design 6.1) is WRONG. RECOVERY for a client that has already duplicated: relog (the server must resync the inventory).

On send it sets ctx+0x1c=0. result==1 calls FUN_00483430(0x259,1,1) on the UI root (ctx+0xc), which sets ui+0x5a4=1 and calls FUN_00446300(0x259,0,1,0,1) to close window 0x259. fields.meaning: Sprite index of the stall signboard. It is the first argument of CSpriteControl::DrawSprite (DAT_0070e70c) at 0x431760. Read only when the entity exists and its stall flag was 0 (stop path otherwise).

fields.name: stall_title
fields.meaning: Stall title drawn above the sign by CIME::Draw_Text. Exactly 25 raw bytes are copied with no forced terminator. Put a NUL inside the 25 bytes (at most 24 chars), because entity+0x150E (the sprite id) follows directly. Read only on the same path as sign_sprite_id.

specs.semantics: Opens the stall sign on another player. The client reads u32 owner_uid and resolves it with FUN_004189f0. If no entity is found (or the uid is 0), or the entity's stall flag byte +0x14F4 is already nonzero, the handler jumps to 0x46EF5A and returns 1 (handled) with nothing else read or changed. Otherwise it first sets entity+0x14F4 = 1 (0x46CFDD), then reads u16 into entity+0x150E and 25 raw bytes into entity+0x14F5, and returns 1. The per-frame routine FUN_004316b0 draws the signboard sprite and title for entities with alive state 3 (remote players) and the flag set, while scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6. FUN_0044c4b0 makes the sign clickable: if no other stall or trade window is busy, clicking sends C2S 0x61 with u32 owner_uid to request the stall contents. FUN_00466e30 also checks the flag when placing a new stall, so a stall can't be opened too close to another open one. Trailing extra bytes are harmless because the offset is sub1's by-value argument copy.
specs.trigger: Broadcast to players in view on the seller's map when a stall opens successfully (after C2S 0x5E and S2C 0x82 result=1). Players who arrive later learn about open stalls from the stall sub-block of the S2C 0x04/0x07 player data, or from a 0x85 sent after that player's spawn.
specs.expected_response: None. Clicking the sign later makes the client send C2S 0x61 (u32 owner_uid).
specs.gates_and_hazards: sub1 entry gate: [ctx+0x08] and [ctx+0x0C] must both be non-null (ctx = main handler this+0xD5C). Otherwise sub1 returns 0 and the opcode falls through the rest of the chain unhandled. The owner entity must already be spawned (0x04/0x07). If the flag is already 1, the new sprite and title are silently ignored and only the uid is consumed, so to change them send 0x86 (clears the flag) and then 0x85 again. The flag is set before the u16/str reads, so a truncated packet would still leave the flag set with stale sprite/title data (how the Fireway read bounds-check behaves on a short packet was not verified). An unterminated 25-byte title makes Draw_Text run into the sprite-id bytes. The sign is never drawn for the local player (alive==4). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C48, shop_storage#09/#11, trade#16): with shop_open = 1 the client draws the stall TITLE but NO signboard sprite for sign ids 0, 1 or 0x168 on the S2C 0x04 vendor path (id 1 produced only a brief flash), so 0x168 is NOT a valid sign-sprite id. CONFLICT: on the S2C 0x05 ghost path sign sprite id 1 DID render a real sign plus an owner glow (trade#16), so the valid id set - and what distinguishes the two paths - is still unknown. Also live: an all-zero appearance block yields an INVISIBLE body (nameplate only).
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts derived the same wire layout: u32 owner_uid, then on the found-and-flag-clear path u16 sign sprite and a 25-byte title, with nothing further read on the other path. A wrote the condition inverted with a bare stop, B wrote if/else with stop. The two grammars mean the same thing, so the grammar dispute is only notation, and I re-verified it from the asm. 0x46CFAA calls IAT 0x4A40C8 (u32) into [ESP+0x18]. 0x46CFB8 calls FUN_004189f0, which only walks the entity list and returns NULL for uid 0, so it reads no packet bytes. 0x46CFC3 JZ and 0x46CFD2 JNZ (flag at +0x14F4) both go to 0x46EF5A, which is MOV EAX,1 and return. 0x46CFDD sets the flag. 0x46CFEE calls IAT 0x4A4090 (u16) into +0x150E. 0x46D004 PUSH 0x19 then 0x46D00A calls IAT 0x4A4098 into +0x14F5. The two analysts differed on one cross-reference. A said the same stall block is in the S2C 0x1A spawn at 0x44F6A1. That is wrong. 0x44F6A1 is inside the handler whose marker says S2C 0x04|0x07 (asm line 1813 of OnReceive_MainTcpHandler; it loops per player and has CMP opcode,7 at 0x44F6FE). No other code in the main handler reads +0x14F4, and 0x1A is the monster/NPC spawn. B was right that it belongs to the 0x04/0x07 player block. The 0x04/0x07 block matches windslayer_server.py _build_en_opcode_07 (lines ~2293/2395), which always writes bool 0 there. A's renderer details (FUN_004316b0: scene+0xF00 in {4,5,6}, alive==3, DrawSprite(+0x150E), Draw_Text(+0x14F5, x+5, y-0x8C)) and the C2S 0x61 u32 uid send at 0x44CA2F were confirmed in the asm. PySlayer has no 0x85 builder, and our server doesn't implement it.
open_questions: Which sign_sprite_id values are valid (indices into sprite control DAT_0070e70c) is unknown. C2S 0x5E carries no sprite choice, so the server has to pick one.
Whether the original server also sent 0x85 to the seller for their own entity is unknown. It would only set the flag on the local entity, and alive==4 entities are never drawn.
The S2C 0x87 reply to the C2S 0x61 view-stall request was not re-verified here (it was only claimed by analyst A).
How a truncated 0x85 behaves (Fireway GetDataFromPacket bounds-check) was not verified. The flag is already set before the u16 read.

UNRESOLVED (shop_storage#11 vs trade#16): sign_sprite_id 0, 1 and 0x168 drew no signboard on the S2C 0x04 vendor path, yet id 1 drew a sign plus an owner glow on a 0x05 ghost. Find the valid sprite id set and what distinguishes the two paths before relying on any id.

specs.semantics: Reply to viewing another player's item stall. Gate: if the local player's own stall is open/pending (stall ctx+0x20 or ctx+0x1c set and ctx+0==0x259) the client reads NOTHING and shows 'Open stall is opened. Close the Open stall and try again.'. On result==1 and item_count>0 the client opens the stall window 0x259 in buyer mode (FUN_00466390(0), sets ctx+0=0x259), stores owner_uid at ctx+4, writes the 25-byte stall name into control 0x1f, then for each item builds a 0x38-byte entry {item_id, 12-byte option blob, qty, price} and appends it to the window list. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C31, shop_storage#13): result == 6 shows "Open stall is opened. Close the Open stall and try again." (the same box as the local own-stall gate), and result != 1 - as well as result == 1 with item_count == 0 - shows "The shop is closed or adjusting." LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C50, trade#17, shop_storage#12): the EN caption of window 0x259 is "Pedding" [sic] and its controls are Name / Goods (rows drawn as "icon, qty, <price> Gold each") / Purchase / Close.
specs.trigger: Server sends in response to C2S 0x61 (u32 target_uid), which the client sends when the player clicks another player whose entity+0x14f4 stall flag was set by S2C 0x85.
specs.expected_response: none automatically; the user may then buy via C2S 0x62 (u32 owner_uid, u16 item_id, u16 qty, u8 n, n*u16 opt, u16 item_ext), answered by S2C 0x88 (buyer) and 0x89 (seller)
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 entry requires ctx+8 and ctx+0xC non-null. Own-stall gate reads nothing. opt_count is unbounded: values >=11 overwrite the already-read price local, and >=69 reach the stack cookie at S+0xBC (process abort); send opt_count<=5. stall_name gets no forced NUL if all 25 bytes are non-zero (bytes after it on the stack are not zeroed). The list is not explicitly cleared in this block (FUN_00466390 path is assumed to reset the window). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C8, shop_storage#18): if a stray S2C 0x83/0x82 has latched ctx+0x1C, closing THIS buyer window copies its listed items into the local bag (client-side duplication). Only send 0x87 in reply to C2S 0x61, and never leave ctx+0x1C latched.
specs.references: No PySlayer builder (server_packets has no 0x87). Not implemented in windslayer_server.py. The per-item layout exactly mirrors the client's own C2S 0x5E stall-open builder at 0x0046B546..0x0046B618 (u16 id, u16 qty, ulong price, u8 n, n*u16, u16 entry+0x0C), which independently confirms field order.

The "no own stall -> only gold changes" expectation holds only while no 0x87 has been received since login. specs.name: CardDeckList

locations.role: call site of SubHandler5 in the unclaimed-opcode chain (ECX = game_state+0xDC4)
handler-object init, run from the S2C 0x02 login-response handler @0x44DF8F: [+0]=game_state, [+4]=g_ui_root, [+8]=item table [scene+0xF84], [+0xC]=g_sock_game, [+0x10]=charinfo=scene+0x48

fields.name: deck_count
fields.dest_or_source: read straight into charinfo+0xE30 (= *(0x70EECC)+0x78... i.e. scene+0xE78; charinfo pointer cached at 0x70F7D4)
fields.meaning: number of cards registered in the Card Deck (dictionary). Also the loop count.

fields.name: card_item_id
fields.meaning: item id (1-based index into the item table) of the i-th registered card

specs.semantics: Replaces the whole local Card Deck list. The u8 count is read directly into charinfo+0xE30, then deck_count u16 item ids are read directly into charinfo+0xE32.. (no bounds check). Then FUN_0045a160: finds dialog id 8 (Card Deck window) and clears its list (FUN_0047d700), adds one 0x38-byte list entry per id (the loop stops early at the first id == 0), picks page/scroll state, and if the item table's u16 total-card count at [itemtable+0x24] is non-zero, formats "%u / %u (%u%%)" = deck_count / total / percent into control 0x29 (FUN_004838c0). The stored list is also what the client checks before registering a card (FUN_0045a3c0 says "This card is already registered ." if the id is already in the list, so it sends no C2S 0x64 for it). No reply is sent. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C22, quest_cards_misc#13/#14): [itemtable+0x24] - the "%u / %u (%u%%)" label's TOTAL - is 880 in the EN client, not 64. In the decoded EN hii (4248 items) exactly 880 entries have CardNpc != 0, while only 64 have CardSpr != 0, so +0x24 counts CardNpc != 0 entries. The label reads n / 880 with floor(n*100/880)%, so 1 or 2 registered cards both show 0%. Before any 0x8A/0x8B the label shows the untouched template text "000/000 (000%)".
specs.trigger: Server-pushed; no C2S request in the EN client asks for it. Send after a successful login (S2C 0x02 success), and before or at world entry, so the deck window and the duplicate check have data. The 0x8B result-2 text "Failed to receive dictionary information. Please log in again." suggests the original server sent this list at login.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Ignored (no bytes consumed) until the handler object is initialized by a successful S2C 0x02 login response: SubHandler5 checks [0x70F7C4]!=0 and [0x70F7C8]!=0. CAPACITY HAZARD: ids are written in place with no bounds check. charinfo+0xE98 holds an i32 field (compared with 100/30 at 0x469189, updated by SubHandler3), so at most 51 entries fit (0xE32..0xE97). Keep deck_count <= 50/51. At about 133 or more entries the writes reach the item-table pointer at scene+0xF84 (charinfo+0xF3C), which other code dereferences. An id of 0 ends the UI list early (the count label still shows deck_count). Ids should be real item ids (category 2 card items); unknown ids just produce empty list entries.
specs.references: PySlayer: no opcode_0x8A.py exists (server_packets/__init__.py only has a try/except import stub); the KR Hex-Rays doc has no card-deck strings. Our server (windslayer_server.py): no builder and never sends 0x8A. The opcode atlas lists 0x8A only as a SubHandler5 route. The format comes from asm alone and matches the decomp.
open_questions: Exact deck capacity: 51 slots fit before the i32 at charinfo+0xE98, but the design limit could be 50 (the struct may have 2 alignment bytes). No explicit constant was found.
Is charinfo+0xE30 zeroed on login or character load? If not, a missing 0x8A may leave stale data from an earlier session.

Does dialog 8 (Card Deck window) always exist when 0x8A arrives? If it does not, FUN_0045a160 adds entries to whatever dialog ui_root+0x5F0 points at. Probably harmless because the UI is built at startup, but this was not verified.

[RESOLVED by live verification quest_cards_misc#13, 2026-09-17] Live: [itemtable+0x24] = 880 in EN, which is exactly the number of decoded EN items with CardNpc != 0 (only 64 have CardSpr != 0). It is the card-dictionary total, not the count of registrable Monster Card items. Original question: "What the item table's u16 at +0x24 is: presumably the total number of collectible cards, loaded from client data."
blind_open_questions: True capacity of the deck array inside char_data (scene+0x48) is not bounded by the client; the <=51 safe limit is inferred from a heuristic scan of scene-relative field accesses, not proven.
Exact server timing for sending the list (login vs. after 0x07) is not determined from the client; nothing requests it.

fields.name: new_deck_count
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x12]; on success written to charinfo+0xE30 (deck count). Also used as the 1-based slot: the id goes to charinfo+0xE30+2*new_deck_count = entry index new_deck_count-1

specs.semantics: Reply to C2S 0x64 (card register). Before reading anything, the handler calls FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) on ui_root, which closes the 'Waiting for the server to response.' message box (dialog 0x16). It then reads result. result==1: reads new_deck_count (u8) and card_item_id (u16). It looks up the item record (itemtable[card_item_id-1]); if there is none, it stops silently. Otherwise it calls FUN_00467140(category=[rec+0x154], inventory object game_state+0xD5C, id, 0, qty 1) to take one of that item out of the client's own inventory (category 0 = equip, 1 = consumable, 2 = etc; other categories fail). If the client does not hold the item, it stops silently and the deck is NOT updated. On success it writes charinfo+0xE30 = new_deck_count and u16 charinfo+0xE32+2*(new_deck_count-1) = card_item_id, rebuilds the deck list and the 'n / total (pct%)' label (FUN_0045a160), prints "Registered <item name> in the Card Deck." to the chat log (colour 0xFFFFFFFF; the name is the null-terminated string at item record +0), and refreshes the inventory window (FUN_00465290). result 2, 6 or anything else: shows the matching message box; no more bytes are read. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C22, quest_cards_misc#13/#14): [itemtable+0x24] - the "%u / %u (%u%%)" label's TOTAL - is 880 in the EN client, not 64. In the decoded EN hii (4248 items) exactly 880 entries have CardNpc != 0, while only 64 have CardSpr != 0, so +0x24 counts CardNpc != 0 entries. The label reads n / 880 with floor(n*100/880)%, so 1 or 2 registered cards both show 0%. Before any 0x8A/0x8B the label shows the untouched template text "000/000 (000%)".
specs.trigger: Send in reply to C2S 0x64 [u16 card_item_id]. The client sends 0x64 when the player confirms dialog 0x292 (button 2) after choosing to register a card item. The item must be category 2 with the card flag [rec+0x14C] set, and not already in the 0x8A deck list. After sending, the client shows 'Waiting for the server to response.' and waits for this packet. MUST-REPLY (live-verified section 4): this is the packet that closes the "Waiting for the server to response." modal left by C2S 0x64 (card register). Without it the client stays behind that box (dialog 0x16 has no OK button except on the 0x64 path).
specs.expected_response: none (the client consumes the card item locally on success)
specs.gates_and_hazards: Ignored (no bytes read) before the handler object is initialized by a successful S2C 0x02 login response. The waiting box is dismissed for every result. On success the client removes one card from its own inventory, so the server must NOT also send an inventory-removal packet (the card would be removed twice), but it must update its own inventory and deck records. If the client has no such item, nothing is registered client-side and no message appears, so client and server go out of sync. new_deck_count must be >= 1: with 0 the u16 id is written over charinfo+0xE30/0xE31, corrupting the count. Keep new_deck_count <= 50/51 (no bounds check; an i32 field sits at charinfo+0xE98). If new_deck_count is not old_count+1, the client's list gains gaps (a 0 id ends the UI list early) or overwrites existing entries. Category-1 items fail when inv+0x361 > 45. The chat string buffer is 64 bytes (sprintf_s).
specs.references: PySlayer: no opcode_0x8B.py and no parse for C2S 0x64 (only a try/except import stub in server_packets/__init__.py). Our server: _dispatch has no C2S 0x64 branch and there is no 0x8B builder. The UI strings (strings.tsv 0x6F5190, 0x6F517C, 0x6F5FAC, 0x6F7F50, 0x6F5FF0) confirm this is the card-deck/dictionary system. No live capture exists.
open_questions: Values other than 1/2/6 all show the generic failure text; whether the original server used other codes (e.g. 3/4/5) with separate meanings is unknown.
Whether the original server sent new_deck_count = old+1 or reused the slot some other way cannot be told from the client. Appending (old+1) is the only safe choice.
Whether a separate inventory-sync packet is needed if the card stack was not in the client's inventory is untested.
blind_open_questions: FUN_00483430(0x16,1,1) at the top of the handler is inferred to close the 'Waiting for the server to response.' modal (window 0x16) - not fully traced through FUN_00446300.
Whether the server should also send a fresh 0x8A after registration is not required by the client (0x8B updates the list itself).

Please create a character in the game and than try again.'; 2 = transfer applied (reads new_id); 3 = 'same ID as present. please put new ID.'; 4 = 'Identical as Id presents. fields.dest_or_source: stack buffer frame+0x70C (not pre-zeroed); sprintf_s(frame+0xC10, 0x40, '%s%s', new_id, 'Applying') -> FUN_004838c0 window 0x12 control 7

specs.semantics: Result of an account ID-transfer request made from the character-select / ID-transfer window 0x12 ('Application for a transfer ID from ID without SS#...'). Each result code opens a message box (window 0x16) with the fixed English text listed under the result field. Case 2 also reads a 33-byte ID string, sets window 0x12 control 7 to new_id followed by 'Applying', sets control 5 to state 3 (disabled) and shows 'Successfully completed ID transfer.\r\n log in with new ID \r\n transfer ID same way as before.' Case 7 sets controls 5, 6 and 7 of window 0x12 to state 3. Values above 8 do nothing and read nothing more.
specs.trigger: Reply to the client's ID-transfer request from window 0x12 (character select). The request opcode was not identified in this batch. For a private server this is legacy Yahoo-ID migration and can be left unused.
specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate. new_id MUST contain a NUL within its 33 bytes: the stack buffer is not cleared, and sprintf_s into a 64-byte buffer with '%s%s' + 'Applying' will hit the CRT invalid-parameter handler (likely a crash) if the combined string is 64 bytes or longer. Keep new_id at 32 characters or fewer. Results above 8 are silently ignored.
specs.references: No PySlayer or KR equivalent (the dispatch map lists kr_source_file n/a, since the Yahoo ID transfer existed only in EN/2008). Jump table 0x458614 = [0x457AE6, 0x457B03, 0x457A60, 0x457B20, 0x457B3D, 0x457B5A, 0x457B77, 0x457B94, 0x457BE4], checked against the raw binary. S2C 0x02 (0x44DE85) carries the matching status byte (this+0x1546: 1 = '<id>Applying' with str[33], 2 = 'requesting ID transfer.', otherwise 'Account transfer possible'). Our server does not implement it.
open_questions: Which C2S opcode sends the ID-transfer request that this answers. Not traced in this batch; it would be in FUN_00446300's window 0x12 / 0x290 handling.
Exact visual meaning of control state 3 set by FUN_00489320 (probably disabled or greyed out).
blind_open_questions: Which of C2S 0x65 or 0x66 produces which result codes was not traced; the pairing with 0x8C is inferred from the shared UI (window 0x12 controls 5/6/7 and the 'Applying' label).

specs.name: CraftResult (Concoction / Mineral Refining result)

locations.role: handler block entry (sub1 switch: opcode-0x18 via index table 0x46F000 / jump table 0x46EF90)
GetDataFromPacket u16 (IAT 0x4A4090) -> [ESP+0x1C] product_item_id; LAST read of the block
FUN_00404210 item-table lookup ([[ctx+0x10]+0xF84], id-1); null -> JZ 0x46EF5A return (busy flag not cleared)
result==1: FUN_00467140 removes each of 8 recipe materials (rec+0x202 ids, rec+0x212 counts)
matching C2S 0x67 send (u8 0x67, u16 [window+0x134]) that this answers

specs.grammar:
u8 result
u16 product_item_id

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = success; 0 = failed (materials consumed client-side); 0x11 = 'Out of empty slot in inventory' + failed (materials consumed); 0x0F = 'Short of material item' (no consume); 0x10 = 'The skill hasn't been learned yet.' (no consume); any other value = plain '<kind>Failed.' (no consume)

fields.name: product_item_id
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [ESP+0x1C]; item-table lookup; FUN_00440920 arg; FUN_00483270(0x28F, id)
fields.meaning: 1-based item-table id of the recipe product (echo of the u16 sent in C2S 0x67). Its record supplies 8 material ids (rec+0x202, u16[8]), 8 material counts (rec+0x212, u16[8]) and craft kind (rec+0x224 u32: 2 = 'Mineral Refining', otherwise 'Concoction'). Must exist in the client item table or the packet is ignored.

specs.semantics:
Final result of a Concoction / Mineral Refining attempt. Reads exactly u8 result + u16 product_item_id, then looks the product up in the item table (FUN_00404210); if absent the handler returns immediately (no UI, [ctx+0x2C] busy flag stays set). result==1: for each of the 8 material entries of the product record whose id resolves, FUN_00467140(category=material rec+0x154, ctx, id, 0, count) removes it: category 0 -> FUN_00423b70 on tab +0x5F6/+0x650/+0x6AC with -count; category 1 (equipment tab +0x380/+0x3DA) -> FUN_00423ff0 with -1 (exactly one instance, count ignored); category 2 -> FUN_00423e70 on tab +0x760/+0x7BA with -count; other categories no-op. Then FUN_00440920(product_item_id,0,1) adds one product ('you've received %s. (Count:%u)'); text = kind + ' Successful.' (e.g. 'Concoction Successful.'). result 0 or 0x11: same material-removal loop, no product; 0x11 prefixes 'Out of empty slot in inventory
 '. result 0x0F / 0x10: prefix 'Short of material item
 ' / 'The skill hasn't been learned yet.
 ', no consumption. Every non-1 result appends kind + 'Failed.' via "%s%s" (no space, e.g. 'ConcoctionFailed.'). All non-early-exit paths: FUN_00465290 inventory refresh, FUN_0048A060 sets text in window 0x28F, FUN_00483430(0x28F,4,1), FUN_00483270(0x28F, product_item_id), FUN_004838C0(control 4, product record), then [ctx+0x2C]=0.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x67 (u16 product_item_id), which FUN_004684d0 sends at 0x468726 when the 5000 ms progress window 0x293 completes for a Concoction/Refining request (reinforcement slots [ctx+0x64]/[ctx+0x66] not both filled). Send exactly once per 0x67.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 only runs when [ctx+0x8] and [ctx+0xC] are non-null. Unknown/zero product_item_id -> silent return without clearing [ctx+0x2C], leaving concoction/refining/reinforcement blocked ('Not allowed during concoction, mineral refining, or reinforcement.'). Client mutates inventory LOCALLY from its own item data (materials removed on results 1, 0 and 0x11; product +1 on result 1); server must apply the identical change and must not send extra add/remove packets for the same craft or inventory double-counts. Equipment-category materials remove only 1 instance each regardless of recipe count.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts read exactly the same wire layout - u8 result at 0x46EA2A (IAT 0x4A4094, out [ESP+0x18]-12 = [ESP+0xC]) and u16 product_item_id at 0x46EA3E (IAT 0x4A4090, out [ESP+0x28]-12 = [ESP+0x1C]) - and no other GetDataFromPacket call exists between 0x46EA44 and the shared exit at 0x46EF5A. The only 'dispute' is A's trailing unconditional 'stop', which is redundant (stop is for terminating a branch); B's plain 'u8 u16' is the canonical form. Wire length 3 on every path; both correct on bytes. Extra detail verified here: the "%s%s" format at 0x4A630C and ' Successful.' (0x6F5958, leading space) / 'Failed.' (0x6F5950, no space) give 'Concoction Successful.' vs 'ConcoctionFailed.'; FUN_00467140 NEGs the count (0x46717A/0x4671E4) and uses -1 for equipment materials (0x4671AF). Not in PySlayer (only a try-import stub for opcode_0x8D) and our server has no 0x8D builder or 0x67 handler (grep of windslayer_server.py finds none).
open_questions: Meaning of item record +0x224 values other than 2 (all non-2 display 'Concoction').
Whether the original server consumed materials on result 0x11 (client does it locally, so server should mirror).
Semantics of FUN_00440920 arg2 (passed 0) - UI/inventory detail, not wire format.

fields.name: equip_option
fields.dest_or_source: zero-initialized stack buffer [ESP+0x34..0x3F]; FUN_004241d0 arg (compared 12 bytes via FUN_00427390 against inv+0x3DA+slot*12)
fields.meaning: The equipment instance's CURRENT 6 option words before reinforcement (echo of the 6 u16 sent in C2S 0x68). Only used to locate the exact inventory slot. Present only when result == 1.

fields.name: new_option_item_id
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [ESP+0x14]; FUN_004241d0 arg; window 0x29B +0x40; its record shown in control 6
fields.meaning: Option value (must be a valid item-table id) written into the first zero word among option[0..4] of the matched slot. If it does not resolve in the item table the client takes the failure path ('ReinforcementFailed.'). Present only when result == 1.

specs.semantics: Result of reinforcing equipment with an elemental stone. Reads u8 result, u16 equip_item_id, u16 stone_item_id; looks up equip_item_id (FUN_00404210) and returns silently if missing (no further reads, [ctx+0x2C] not cleared). If result != 1 -> failure path with no further reads. If result == 1: reads 6 u16 option words then u16 new_option_item_id; if new_option_item_id is not a valid item -> failure path. Otherwise FUN_004241d0 scans equipment-tab slots (count u8 inv+0x361, ids u16 inv+0x380, 12-byte option blocks inv+0x3DA) for id == equip_item_id AND option block == the 12 received bytes, and stores new_option_item_id in the first zero word among option[0..4] (no change if no slot matches or all five are non-zero; success is still shown). Then FUN_00423e70 removes 1 x stone_item_id from the etc tab. Text 'Reinforcement Successful.' ("%s%s" with ' Successful.') into window 0x29B (FUN_0048A060); FUN_00465290 inventory refresh; clears list entries 4 and 5 of window 0x29B (entry+0x18=0); FUN_00483430(0x29B,4,1); window object +0x134 = equip_item_id, +0x40 = new_option_item_id; FUN_004838C0 control 4 = equip record, control 6 = new option record; [ctx+0x2C]=0. Failure path (0x46EEBB): 'This equipment cannot be reinforced.' (result 0x11) or 'ReinforcementFailed.' (no space) into window 0x29B; FUN_00489320(0x29B,5,3) and (0x29B,6,3); FUN_00483430(0x29B,4,1); FUN_00483270(0x29B, equip_item_id); FUN_004838C0 control 4 = equip record; [ctx+0x2C]=0; no inventory change.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x68 (u16 equip_item_id, u16 stone_item_id, 6x u16 option words), sent by FUN_004684d0 at 0x46869D when the 5000 ms progress window 0x293 completes with both the equipment ([ctx+0x66]) and elemental stone ([ctx+0x64]) slots filled. Send exactly once per 0x68.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 requires [ctx+0x8] and [ctx+0xC] non-null. Unknown equip_item_id -> stops after 5 bytes and never clears [ctx+0x2C], leaving crafting/reinforcement UI locked. With result == 1 the packet must carry all 19 bytes; the upper halves of the [ESP+0x10]/[ESP+0x14] dword slots are uninitialized, and a short packet leaves new_option_item_id garbage. The 6 option words must byte-match the client's stored 12-byte block or the option is silently not applied while the stone is still removed (desync). Client consumes exactly 1 stone locally on success only; server must not send an extra stone-removal packet. Trailing option bytes on a result != 1 packet are simply unread.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A's grammar 'if(result == 1 && item_table_has(equip_item_id)) { repeat(6){u16} u16 } else { stop }' and B's grammar 'if(item_db[equip]==null){stop} if(result==1){repeat(6){u16} u16}' produce the identical byte layout on every path; there is no wire disagreement. The asm order shows the item-table gate comes first (lookup at 0x46EC81, JZ 0x46EF5A exit) and only then CMP [ESP+0xC],1 / JNZ 0x46EEBB (0x46EC92/0x46EC97), with the 6-word loop at 0x46ECC0-0x46ECDB and final u16 at 0x46ECEE; the failure block 0x46EEBB..0x46EF5A contains no reads. B's two-step structure mirrors this code order, so it is adopted as canonical (A's combined condition is logically equivalent). Minor text corrections from the binary: format 0x4A630C = "%s%s", ' Successful.' at 0x6F5958 has a leading space and 'Failed.' at 0x6F5950 does not, so success text is 'Reinforcement Successful.' (B's semantics wrote 'ReinforcementSuccessful.') and failure text is 'ReinforcementFailed.' (B's field text wrote 'Reinforcement Failed.'); A had both right. C2S 0x68 layout confirmed at 0x46869D-0x4686E8 (u8 0x68, u16 [EDI+0x66], u16 [EDI+0x64], 6x u16). FUN_004241d0 decomp confirms insertion only into option[0..4]. Not in PySlayer (try-import stub only) nor our server (no 0x8E/0x68 in windslayer_server.py).
open_questions: Whether the original server set new_option_item_id equal to stone_item_id or to a derived id; the client only requires it to exist in the item table.
Meaning of option word index 5 (never written by FUN_004241d0).
Which S2C inventory packet seeds the 12-byte option blocks at inventory +0x3DA, so the server echoes consistent values.
Whether the original server consumed the stone on failure (client does not remove it locally).

specs.name: GatherResult
specs.length: 3 bytes if the tool id has no item def or result != 1; 5 bytes if result == 1 and the tool id has an item def

locations.role: item-def lookup in table [[ctx+0x10]+0xF84]; NULL -> 0x46E9F9 (clear busy flag, return, no more reads)
remove 1 of tool_item_id from the inventory tab chosen by def+0x154 (stdcall RET 0xC). Runs before result is checked.
CMP AL,1 on result; not 1 -> 0x46E9C3 (no more reads)
read u16 reward_item_id (IAT 0x4A4090) into [base+0x0C]; length argument reloaded from [EBP+0x14] because ESI was overwritten at 0x46E93F
add 1 of reward_item_id with no options (ECX = [ctx+0x8]); prints "you've received %s. (Count:%u)" or "You've learned skill(%s)."
refresh inventory window (id 9) and quest item-progress; also called at 0x46E9F4 on both failure paths
result == 0x11 -> "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory." (0x6F7538); otherwise "Failed to obtian item." (0x6F7FEC)
[ctx+0x28] = 0 (clear gather busy flag); the success path does the same at 0x46E9A0
sets busy flag [ctx+0x28] = 1 and the start time [ctx+0x5C], and opens progress window 0x295 ('Herb Gathering' / 'Item Mining')
related C2S 0x69 send once 5000 ms (float 0x4A67AC) have passed: u32 [win0x295+0x11C] node key, u16 [win0x295+0x134] tool item id

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = success (reward_item_id follows); 0x11 = inventory full; any other value = generic failure ('Failed to obtian item.')

fields.name: tool_item_id
fields.meaning: The gathering tool used. It should echo the u16 from C2S 0x69: 0x8A7..0x8AA are garden shovels (Herb Gathering), 0x8AB..0x8AE are shovels (Mining). The client removes 1 of it whenever the id has an item def, even if the gather failed.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [base+0x18]; FUN_00404210 lookup, then FUN_00467140(id, NULL, 1)

fields.name: reward_item_id
fields.meaning: Item granted on success (count 1, no options). Read only when the tool's item def exists and result == 1.

specs.semantics: Result of a Mining or Herb Gathering action. The client reads result (u8) and tool_item_id (u16), then looks up the tool's item def with FUN_00404210. If there is no def (id 0 or out of range included), it only clears the gather busy flag [ctx+0x28] and returns: no message, no inventory refresh, no more reads. Otherwise it always removes 1 of tool_item_id from the local inventory (FUN_00467140, tab chosen by def+0x154) before it looks at result. If result == 1: it reads reward_item_id, adds 1 of it via FUN_00440920 (chat message "you've received %s. (Count:%u)", or "You've learned skill(%s)." for skill-book items), refreshes the inventory/quest UI (FUN_00465290), clears [ctx+0x28] and returns. If result == 0x11: message "There isn't empty space \r\nin the inventory.". Any other result: message "Failed to obtian item.". Both failure paths then refresh the inventory UI and clear [ctx+0x28].
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x69. FUN_004684D0 sends 0x69 once the 5000 ms progress bar of window 0x295 finishes. The window is opened by FUN_00467B00 when the player uses a garden shovel (0x8A7..0x8AA) on a herb node or a shovel (0x8AB..0x8AE) on a mineral node. 0x69 carries u32 node key (roster index, stored in window+0x11C at 0x467D4B) and u16 tool item id (stored in window+0x134 at 0x467D3F).
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler1 gate: [ctx+0x8] != 0 and [ctx+0xC] != 0, otherwise the packet goes unhandled. While [ctx+0x28] != 0, FUN_00467B00 returns at once (0x467B1E), so no new gather can start until 0x8F clears it. A UI event for window 0x295 in FUN_00446300 also clears it ([game_state+0xD84] = 0 at 0x446A2A). The client removes the tool on failure too (any result, as long as the def exists), so the server must also remove it on failure, or resend the tool, or the inventories drift apart. Send reward_item_id only when result == 1. On any other path the packet is 3 bytes, and extra bytes are ignored anyway. A tool_item_id with no item def skips the removal, the messages and the UI refresh; only the flag is cleared.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: A's grammar was 'u8 result; u16 tool_item_id; if(item_def != null && result == 1) { u16 reward_item_id }'. B's was the same reads nested as if(def exists) { if(result == 1) { u16 } else stop } else stop. Both describe the same bytes in the same order, and the asm agrees with both. Reads: 0x46E91D u8 (IAT 0x4A4094) into [base+0x1C]; 0x46E931 u16 (0x4A4090) into [base+0x18]; 0x46E945 FUN_00404210 then JZ 0x46E9F9, which only clears [EBX+0x28] and returns; 0x46E963 FUN_00467140 removes the item unconditionally (stdcall RET 0xC, so the later [ESP+0x1C] still points at result); 0x46E96C CMP AL,1 / JNZ 0x46E9C3; 0x46E981 is the only other read, u16 (0x4A4090) into [base+0x0C]. None of the callees (FUN_00404210, FUN_00467140, FUN_00440920, FUN_00465290) receive the packet pointer or offset, so there are no hidden reads. B's nested form is kept because it follows the branch order in the code. On meaning, A was right that the u16 is the tool: FUN_00467B00 takes the used item id in [EBP+0x10], accepts only 0x8A7..0x8AA (garden shovel, Herb Gathering: entity+0x644 == 2, skill 0x56, map check 0x138) or 0x8AB..0x8AE (shovel, Mining: entity+0x644 == 1, skill 0x52, map check 0x139), stores it in window 0x295 +0x134 (FUN_00483270 at 0x467D3F), and FUN_004684D0 sends that same value as the u16 of C2S 0x69 (0x468584 / 0x4685A7). That settles B's tool-or-material question, and it covers both gathering types, so the name GatherResult is used rather than ItemMiningResult. The 5 s timer is confirmed: float 0x4A67AC = 5000.0. Other strings: 0x6F7FEC, 0x6F7538; 'Mining' 0x6F5F24, 'Item ' 0x6F5F3C, 'Herb Gathering' 0x6F5F2C. FUN_00440920 is the same add-item helper used by other reward packets (for example the S2C 0x18 quest reward). Neither PySlayer nor our server has this opcode.
open_questions: Result codes other than 1 and 0x11 all show the same generic failure message. The client does not show which codes the original server actually used.
The client does not check that tool_item_id in 0x8F matches the id sent in C2S 0x69. It removes whatever id the server sends, so the server should echo the tool id it received.

Not confirmed whether the programmatic close of window 0x295 in FUN_004684D0 (FUN_00483430 at 0x4685CB) reaches the FUN_00446300 path that clears [game_state+0xD84]. If it does not, a missing 0x8F leaves gathering blocked until the player closes the window by hand or the flag is otherwise reset.

specs.name: ChatLineOrange

locations.role: handler block start; memset 88-byte buffer frame+0x788
FUN_00445f00(this, text, 0xFFFF8000) appends a line to the chat log
chat-log append: splits text into 88-byte (87 at a Hangul boundary) lines on chat window 0x0B

specs.grammar:
u8 text_len
str[text_len] text

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: Number of raw text bytes that follow (no terminator required). Keep it at 87 or less.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local frame+0x7B, used as the byte count for the char read

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Chat line text shown as-is in ORANGE (ARGB 0xFFFF8000). No sender field, so the server must pre-format it, e.g. 'Name : message'.
fields.dest_or_source: 88-byte zeroed stack buffer frame+0x788 -> FUN_00445f00 -> chat window 0x0B line list

specs.semantics: Zeroes an 88-byte buffer, reads a u8 length and then exactly that many raw bytes, and appends the text to the chat log (UI window 0x0B) in orange (0xFFFF8000) through FUN_00445f00. That function measures the string with strlen, splits it into 88-byte lines, and wakes up the chat box if it has been idle more than 3000 ms. There is no sender, uid or channel field: this is a pre-formatted colored chat/notice line.
specs.trigger: Server wants to print an orange line in the chat log (system notice, or possibly party/guild chat relay).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate. text_len is not bounds-checked against the 88-byte stack buffer: text_len > 88 overflows the stack (corrupts other locals in OnReceive's frame), and text_len == 88 leaves no NUL, so strlen runs past the buffer into stack garbage. Use text_len <= 87. An embedded NUL truncates the displayed text. text_len = 0 reads nothing and adds no line (strlen 0).
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x90.py builds 0x90 + p8(len) + raw text (no NUL), which matches. The KR Hex-Rays (Windslayers_Full_Packet.c case 0x90) uses the same color -32768 (0xFFFF8000) with a 156-byte buffer in KR versus 88 in EN. Our server has no 0x90 builder. The only 0xFFFF8000 literal in the client is this handler, so the color does not reveal which chat channel it belongs to.
open_questions: Which chat channel the original server used orange 0x90 for (party chat relay versus GM/system notice). The C2S party chat (0x6A, text pre-formatted 'Name : msg' by the client) has no local echo, so 0x90 is a plausible relay, but that is not proven.
How Fireway GetDataFromPacket(char*,N) behaves when offset+N exceeds the packet length (whether it clamps or reads past the end).
blind_open_questions: Intended use (GM notice vs. system message) is not provable from the handler; only the color differs from 0x91.

specs.name: ChatLineGreen

locations.role: handler block start; memset 88-byte buffer frame+0x838
FUN_00445f00(this, text, 0xFF8EE085) appends a line to the chat log
same color used for the local echo of '/f ' friend (messenger) chat

specs.grammar:
u8 text_len
str[text_len] text

fields.name: text_len
fields.meaning: Number of raw text bytes that follow (no terminator required). Keep it at 87 or less.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local frame+0x87, used as the byte count for the char read

fields.name: text
fields.meaning: Chat line text shown as-is in LIGHT GREEN (ARGB 0xFF8EE085). No sender field, so pre-format it, e.g. 'Name : message'.
fields.dest_or_source: 88-byte zeroed stack buffer frame+0x838 -> FUN_00445f00 -> chat window 0x0B line list

specs.semantics: Same as 0x90 except for the color: zeroes an 88-byte buffer, reads a u8 length and that many raw bytes, and appends the text to the chat log (window 0x0B) in light green 0xFF8EE085 through FUN_00445f00 (strlen, split into 88-byte lines, wake the chat box). The client uses this exact color for its own echo of '/f ' friend chat (FUN_00444a90 case 'k', which formats '%s : %s' with the player name), so 0x91 is most likely the incoming friend/messenger-style chat line. It also works as a generic green console/notice line.
specs.trigger: Server wants to print a light-green line in the chat log (friend chat relay, or a console/system message as PySlayer does).
specs.gates_and_hazards: No state gate. Same overflow hazard as 0x90: text_len > 88 smashes the stack, and text_len == 88 has no NUL terminator. Use text_len <= 87. An embedded NUL truncates the text. text_len = 0 adds nothing.
specs.references: PySlayer server_packets/opcode_0x91.py = 0x91 + p8(len) + raw text. PySlayer plugin/custom_cmd.py uses it for console replies ('Dump done!', '[Console Message] CharX...'), which confirms it works on KR. The KR Hex-Rays case 0x91 uses color -7413627 = 0xFF8EE085 with a 156-byte buffer in KR versus 88 in EN. Our server has no 0x91 builder; its chat broadcast uses a different opcode.
open_questions: Whether the original server used 0x91 specifically for friend-chat relay. The C2S friend chat (0x6B) goes out on the messenger socket ([this+0x4E4]+0x74), not on the game socket where this handler reads.

specs.name: PartySkillHpEffect

locations.role: FUN_00404210: 1-based lookup of skill_id in the skill table [[this+0x4CC]+0xF84]; null -> abort
loop over the 5 party-member uid slots scene+0x25C..+0x26C
member cur HP (+0x9C) += skill.hp_delta (+0x158), clamped to [0, max HP +0x110C]
FUN_0043d3f0(uid, max_hp u16, cur_hp u16) updates the party-member HP frame (windows 0x75..0x78)
FUN_004258d0(skill_id) gate for the local-player branch
local player (scene+0x970) cur HP += hp_delta, clamped; FUN_00443690 refreshes the HUD HP

specs.grammar: u16 skill_id

fields.name: skill_id
fields.meaning: Skill definition id (the same table and ids as C2S 0x15 use-skill and the quick slots). The HP amount is NOT on the wire: the client uses skill_record+0x158 (signed i32 HP delta) from its own data table.
fields.dest_or_source: stack local frame+0xB0; index (1-based) into the vector at [[0x70EECC]+0xF84]

specs.semantics: Applies a skill's HP effect to the whole party on the client. Steps: 1) record = skill_table[skill_id-1] (vector begin +8, end +0xC). If it is out of range or null (including skill_id 0), stop. 2) For each of the 5 u32 party uid slots at scene+0x25C, +0x260, +0x264, +0x268, +0x26C that is non-zero and matches an entity in the scene list (FUN_004189f0): spawn effect event 0x10E on that uid (FUN_0042b580(0x10E, uid, 0,0,0,1,0xA,0)), play sound 0x10E (non-positional), entity+0x9C (cur HP, i32) += record+0x158, clamp to entity+0x110C (max HP) and to >= 0. If the low 16 bits of max HP are non-zero, call FUN_0043d3f0(uid, (u16)max, (u16)cur) to update that member's party HP bar ('%u/%u' plus gauge) on party frame windows 0x75..0x78. 3) If the local player entity scene+0x970 exists, record+0x158 != 0 and FUN_004258d0(skill_id) returns 1: spawn effect 0x10E on the local uid, play sound 0x10E positioned at the local entity (+0x15A4/+0x15A8) relative to the camera (this+0x1044..0x1050), local cur HP += delta clamped to [0, max], and FUN_00443690 refreshes the HUD HP text '%d/%d' and gauge. FUN_004258d0 returns 0 (skips the self-heal) for these skill_id ranges: 0x187-0x191, 0x1BE-0x1C8, 0x24D-0x257, 0x8C6-0x8D0, 0x8F2-0x8FC, 0x997-0x9A1, 0x9C3-0x9F9 (five consecutive 11-id blocks), 0xA5D-0xA67, 0xAF9-0xB03, 0xB0F-0xB19, 0xB25-0xB2F.
specs.trigger: After a party member casts a party-wide HP skill (e.g. a group heal), send to every party member's client so each one applies the heal locally.
specs.gates_and_hazards: The client changes HP locally from its own skill table, so the server must apply the same delta (record+0x158) to its HP state or the HP bars will drift. Use explicit HP packets such as 0x54/0x28 to resync if needed. If the party slot list contains the local player's own uid (RegisterLocalPlayer compares the slots against the local uid, so self can be in the list), the local player may be healed twice: once in the loop, and again in step 3 for skills not excluded by FUN_004258d0. Unknown or zero skill_id does nothing. Out of party (all slots 0) only step 3 applies. Every call allocates an effect event (FUN_0042b580) per target and plays sound 0x10E. Avoid sending in bursts (the earlier lag was traced to per-hit effect events from 0x40).
specs.references: Our server has no 0x92 builder; windslayer_server.py only mentions '0x92->0x10e' in a comment about hard-coded sounds, which matches Play_Sound 0x10E here. The KR Hex-Rays case 0x92 differs: it parses a larger struct through sub_40A010 (12 locals, skill id in the third field) and uses effect/sound 0x70, but the loop over 5 party slots (KR offsets 592..612) and the local-player branch have the same structure. The EN wire format is only a u16, confirmed by the single GetDataFromPacket(ushort&) at 0x457CFB. The skill table identification rests on the quick-slot code (FUN_0043d8b0 -> FUN_00404210 on the same table -> FUN_0044c090 sending C2S 0x15 with record +0x154 type, +0x158 HP, +0x15C MP cost) and on the matching FUN_004258d0 gate in the 0x41/0x42 handler (0x453EEE).
open_questions: Whether scene+0x25C..+0x26C (the party uid slots) includes the local player's own uid in practice, which would double-apply the heal for skills FUN_004258d0 does not exclude.
Exact skill names for the excluded id ranges in FUN_004258d0 (11-id blocks = one skill per level range). They could be cross-checked against gamedef.sqlite3.
Whether record+0x158 is really 'HP delta' for every skill type. It is signed: negative values are HP costs (see the 'Not enough HP.' check in FUN_0044c090).
blind_open_questions: Whether scene+0x25C..0x26C (5 slots) includes the local player's own uid or only the other members. The party frames are only windows 0x75..0x78, i.e. 4.
What the FUN_004258d0 excluded ranges correspond to (probably skill families whose heal does not include the caster).

spec_errata.old: medium
spec_errata.new: high (live: +52 HP applied exactly once with the burst effect)

specs.name: CashItemExpired

locations.role: FUN_00459c90: get element idx of vector ctx+0x04
FUN_00464570: erase element idx from vector ctx+0x04
FUN_004817d0: add chat-log system line, color 0xFFFDF34C
FUN_00441c20(1): rebuild inventory window from cash-item vector

specs.grammar: u32 item_serial

fields.name: item_serial
fields.dest_or_source: stack local [esp+0x28]; compared with u32 at +0x00 of each 28-byte record in the vector at ctx+0x04 (ctx = game_state+0x700)
fields.meaning: unique serial of the time-limited cash item that expired (the record's +0x00 u32, as delivered by S2C 0x6F)

specs.semantics: Removes an expired premium (cash) item. The client walks the pointer vector at ctx+0x04 (begin ctx+0x08, end ctx+0x0C) from index 0. For each element whose u32 at +0x00 equals item_serial it: erases the element from the vector; looks up the item definition by the u16 item_id at element+0x04 (item table [ctx+0x1C], index id-1); if found, prints "[<item name>] is expired." to the chat log in color 0xFFFDF34C; frees the 28-byte record; and calls FUN_00441c20(1) on game_state to rebuild the inventory display. The loop then goes on to the end of the vector. No reply is sent.
specs.trigger: Send when a time-limited cash item (e.g. 'EXP 50% 7 Days') in the player's cash-item list reaches its expiry time.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Needs [ctx+0x14] and [ctx+0x18] non-null (SubHandler4 entry). No match (or an empty vector) is a silent no-op. After erasing index i the loop increments i, so the element shifted into slot i is skipped; this only matters for duplicate serials (use unique serials). The chat line needs the chat window ([UI+0x59C] != 0); an unknown item_id still removes and frees the record, just with no message. Only records that 0x6F put into the ctx+0x04 list (its per-record bool == 0) can be expired. Records in the ctx+0x38 list (bool != 0) are not searched.
specs.references: Not in PySlayer (listed only as a Packet_handler_4 opcode) and not in windslayer_server.py. Record layout cross-checked against the S2C 0x6F handler (0x4618EC): i32 count, then per record bool + 28 raw bytes; bool==0 -> vector ctx+0x04, where +0x00 u32 is passed as the key and +0x04 u16 is the item id (FUN_0045e8e0 args at 0x461B7E). Items such as 3321..3326 'EXP 50%/100% 60/30/7 Days' are the kind of time-limited items this applies to.
open_questions: Exact meaning of the remaining fields of the 28-byte cash-item record (+0x06 u8, +0x08 u16, +0x0A u16) belongs to the S2C 0x6F spec; not needed for 0x93's wire format.
blind_open_questions: Exact meaning of the 0x6F record +0x00 u32 (DB serial vs slot key) - named serial by role only.
What FUN_00441c20(1) refreshes exactly (large UI routine, 2019 bytes).

specs.name: ComplimentResult

locations.role: switch(result-1) via jump table 0x472164 (7 entries: 1->0x471B8D, 2->0x471C58, 3/4->0x471FF6 no-op, 5->0x471C89, 6->0x471BF6, 7->0x471C27)
FUN_00489da0 notice dialog '<%s> has been complimented'

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1=success; 2=character doesn't exist; 5=target already got enough compliments today; 6=you can't compliment the same player twice; 7=you can compliment only once a day; 0,3,4,>7 = silently ignored

fields.name: target_name
fields.meaning: name of the player who was complimented (shown as '<%s> has been complimented'); NUL-terminate within 17 bytes (it is fed to sprintf_s %s)

specs.semantics: Reply to the local player's compliment (manner-point +) request. Only UI: a modal notice dialog (FUN_00489da0(text,3,3,0,0)). result 1: reads 17-byte name and shows '<name> has been complimented'. result 2: 'The character doesn't exist. fields.meaning: name of the player who gave the compliment, shown in '<%s> added %d of your manner points.'; NUL-terminate within 17 bytes

specs.semantics: Manner-point increase broadcast after a compliment. Every receiving client looks the uid up in the scene entity list; if not found the packet is ignored entirely. If found, entity.manner(+0x15D8) += delta. If the uid is the local player's session uid (scene+0x220), the client additionally reads the 17-byte complimenter name, adds delta to the local character's manner points (scene+0xEE0), refreshes the manner number in window 0x1B (red when negative), and prints a green system chat line '<name> added N of your manner points.'. Manner points gate chat/whisper/trade/item stall/play rooms client-side (strings 0x6F3DB0, 0x6F40F4, 0x6F4130, 0x6F416C, 0x6F41A8).
specs.trigger: Server sends after a successful C2S 0x6D compliment: to the complimented player (with complimenter_name) and optionally to nearby clients so their copy of entity+0x15D8 updates. Pair with 0x94 result 1 to the complimenter.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 in-world gate. The local update ONLY happens if the local player's own entity (spawned via 0x1A with uid == scene+0x220) is present in the scene entity list; otherwise nothing is read/applied. The name is read conditionally on client state, so a server cannot know whether it is consumed - put it last and always include it. Name must be NUL-terminated within 17 bytes (sprintf_s %s). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C42, social_friend#25): the 25-byte form (u32 uid + i32 delta + str[17] complimenter name) is accepted for target_uid == local uid and renders the green line - the grammar is right; the wsproto encoder was emitting only 8 bytes. manner_delta is confirmed to be a SIGNED DELTA, not an absolute value.
specs.references: No PySlayer implementation. Not in windslayer_server.py. entity+0x15D8 cross-checked: S2C 0x1A reads i32 into entity+0x15D8 right after uid (0x44F01C); FUN_00446300 shows 'The player is prohibited to trade due to his/her low manner point.' from it. local_char base = scene+0x48 inferred from FUN_00442c00 reading scene+0xEE0 (0xEE0-0xE98 = 0x220-0x1D8 = 0x48).
open_questions: Whether the retail server broadcast 0x96 to bystanders or used 0x97 for them is unknown.
The mapping [subhandler_obj+0x6C] == scene+0x48 is inferred from offset consistency, not from a direct write.
blind_open_questions: entity+0x15D8 is inferred to be the per-entity manner-point copy (only used here and in 0x97 within this batch); not cross-checked against the 0x1A spawn layout.
Whether the original server sent 0x96 only to the target or broadcast it to the whole map.

specs.semantics: sub_type 8: prints 'In channel %u.' to the chat/system log. sub_type 9: client-side item grant - looks up the item definition; if the id is invalid nothing happens. Depending on itemdef+0x154: type 0 (consumable) is merged/stacked (max 999/slot) into the consumable tab; type 1 (equipment) inserts a single item into the first empty equip slot with zeroed 12-byte attributes (only if equip capacity scene+0x3A9 <= 45); type 2 (etc) is stacked (max 99/slot) into the etc tab; other type values abort. If the add returns success it refreshes the inventory window and logs "you've received <item name>. (Count:<count>)" in white. Any sub_type other than 8/9 is a no-op after the first byte.
specs.trigger: Server-initiated notice (EN subset of the KR 0x99 GM/admin-notice family): 8 when telling the player which channel they are on, 9 when the server grants an item (quest reward / GM give / event) and wants the client to add it to its inventory.
specs.gates_and_hazards: Inventory is modified client-side only with no ack: if the tab is full (or count==0, or capacity byte > 45) the add fails silently (no message) and server/client inventories diverge; server must mirror the same stacking rules (999 consumable, 99 etc, equip 1-per-slot, 1 item per packet for equip). Invalid item_id (0 or beyond table) -> silently ignored. Unknown sub_types are safe no-ops (trailing bytes ignored).
specs.references: KR Hex-Rays case 0x99 is a larger switch (5, 8, 9, 0x13 Superman mode, 0x14 Supermode, 0x2C kick, 0x2D ...); KR sub 8 is identical (u8 channel), KR sub 9 reads a bigger item struct (sub_40A010) - EN reads just u16 id + u16 count. PySlayer opcode_0x99.py only builds sub 0x13/0x14 (+u8), which the EN client ignores. Our server's tab mapping (+0x3a9 equip, +0x3aa consume, +0x3ab other) and items.json type (0 consumable, 1 equip, 2 etc) agree with the add routines. Our server: not implemented.

specs.name: ElementalStoneExtractResult

locations.role: FUN_00424260(ci+0x380, ci+0x3DA, equip_item_id, &record, stone_id, byte ci+0x361), ci=[ctx+0x24]
FUN_00427390 12-byte compare of stored record vs packet record
IDIV EBX (count of non-empty sockets) on the stone_id==0 random path: divide by zero if all 5 empty
modal 'Elemental stone extraction failed. \r\n\r\nPlease try again in a few minutes.'
C2S trigger: send site #69, opcode 0x72 from extraction window 0x473

fields.name: result
fields.meaning: 1 = extraction succeeded; any other value = failure modal and stop

fields.name: equip_item_id
fields.meaning: item id of the equipment; matched against u16 array ci+0x380[i] for i < byte ci+0x361

fields.name: socket_stone[0..4]
fields.meaning: stone ids currently in sockets 0..4 of that equipment (words 0-4 of its 12-byte record, BEFORE extraction); read in a 5-iteration loop

fields.name: socket_extra
fields.meaning: 6th word of the 12-byte record (not a stone socket; only used for the exact 12-byte identity compare)

fields.name: stone_id
fields.meaning: stone id to remove from sockets 0..4. 0 = client removes socket index rand() % (number of non-empty sockets)

fields.name: cash_item_serial
fields.meaning: key (record +0x00) of the premium-inventory record (extraction tool) to consume, count 1

specs.semantics: Result of an elemental stone extraction. On result == 1: builds a 12-byte record from the 6 u16 words and calls FUN_00424260. That picks the FIRST slot i < byte ci+0x361 whose u16 id at ci+0x380[i] == equip_item_id AND whose 12-byte record at ci+0x3DA+i*12 is byte-identical to the packet record. If stone_id != 0, it zeroes the first of sockets 0..4 equal to stone_id (not found: no change). If stone_id == 0, it zeroes socket index rand() % count_nonzero; that is a filled socket only while stones are packed from socket 0. If the removed value is nonzero, the remaining stones are shifted toward socket 0. The removed stone id is returned but discarded; the stone is NOT added to the inventory by this packet. Then FUN_00465290 rebuilds the inventory UI, cash_item_serial is consumed (count 1) and the modal 'Extracted elemental stone.' is shown. Otherwise the modal 'Elemental stone extraction failed. \r\n\r\nPlease try again in a few minutes.' is shown and nothing more is read. Returns 1.
specs.trigger: Reply to C2S 0x72 sent from extraction window 0x473 (FUN_00469090 at 0x46C066..0x46C0B8): u8 0x72, u16 tool item id (window slot; tools 0xF70 and 0xD6D require a selected stone, else 'Select the elemental stone to extract.'), u16 equipment item id ([win+0x66], else 'Place your equipment'), u16 selected stone id, 6x u16 from equipment record +2. The server can echo equip id and the 6 words byte-exact, and must replace stone 0 with the stone it actually removed.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler4 does not parse unless ctx+0x14 and ctx+0x18 are non-null. result must be exactly 1. CRASH: stone_id == 0 while the matched slot's sockets 0..4 are all empty -> IDIV by zero at 0x42430D. DESYNC: stone_id == 0 lets the client pick a random socket on its own; always send the real nonzero id. If equip_item_id plus the 6 words do not exactly match the client's stored record (or the slot index >= byte ci+0x361), no socket changes, but the tool is still consumed and the success modal still shows. The extracted stone must be delivered by a separate item-add packet.
specs.references: ADJUDICATION: Both analysts gave the same wire format: u8 result; if result == 1 then u16 equip id, six u16 record words, u16 stone id, u32 cash serial; else stop. The signature difference is only notation (A listed six u16 lines, B wrote repeat(6)). Neither exactly matches the code's shape, which is a 5-iteration loop plus one separate read; the grammar above mirrors that, and the bytes are identical. VA evidence: u8 [0x4A4094] at 0x462CEA -> [esp+0x13] with CMP 1 / JNZ 0x462E11; u16 at 0x462D09 -> [esp+0x1c]; loop counter [esp+0x14]=5 at 0x462D2B with u16 read at 0x462D41, ADD ptr 2, SUB/JNZ at 0x462D4C/0x462D51; separate u16 at 0x462D69 -> [esp+0x3a]; u16 at 0x462D7D -> [esp+0x24]; FUN_00424260 at 0x462DA6; u32 [0x4A40C8] at 0x462DCB -> [esp+0x28]; FUN_00464380(ctx, serial, 1, 0) at 0x462DDB. A's divide-by-zero crash is confirmed (the EBX count at 0x4242CB..0x424304, then IDIV EBX at 0x42430D). One correction to both: the random path zeroes index rand()%count, not a guaranteed non-empty socket, and shifting is skipped when the zeroed value was 0 (TEST AX,AX at 0x42435E). The C2S 0x72 layout both cited is confirmed at 0x46C066..0x46C0B8. For game_system, A's 'item' was chosen because the main effect is changing equipment sockets; B's 'premium_cash' also fits, since a cash tool is consumed. Not in PySlayer or our server. The record layout matches the FUN_00465290 12-byte copy from ci+0x3DA+i*12.
open_questions: Meaning of socket_extra (record word 5) is unconfirmed; it is only used in the identity compare.
Which S2C packet delivers the extracted stone into the inventory is unknown.
Behaviour of tools other than 0xF70/0xD6D (which allow stone 0 = random) was not enumerated.

specs.semantics: Result of buying extra friend-list slots. result 1: stores the new capacity byte, overwrites local gold and refreshes its display, shows the (mistranslated) notice 'You added him/her on your friend list. Hope you make many good friends.', and updates the friend window counter '(friend_count/capacity)' (window 0x13 control 0x176; count is [+0xD0], maintained by the friend list code). Any other result: notice 'You failed to added him/her on your friend list.'.
specs.trigger: Send in response to C2S 0x73 (no payload; FUN_00472900 @0x47369C, window 0x47B button 2). Client pre-checks: gold >= 50,000 (0xC350) else 'You are short of gold.'; capacity [+0xD1] < 50 (0x32) else 'You can't add more friends to your friend list.'. The add-friend flow says 'Can't be add. Visit Frenaiga.' when count >= capacity, so this is the Frenaiga NPC slot-expansion service.
specs.gates_and_hazards: SubHandler3 in-world gate. Gold is absolute (send post-deduction balance). Capacity >= 50 blocks further client requests. Sending result 1 without the 9 trailing bytes leaves capacity/gold unchanged or garbage. LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C44, social_friend#30): the success form is exactly 10 bytes (u8 result + u8 friend_capacity + u64 gold) - the campaign test plan was one byte short. Live: capacity 25 and an absolute gold of 50000 were applied, and the friend-window header switched from "(2/20)" to "(2/25)" even while the Mento tab was selected.
specs.references: No PySlayer implementation. Not in windslayer_server.py. Capacity byte +0xD1 cross-checked with S2C 0x0B (friend list: u8 capacity into +0xD1, u8 count, per-entry str[17] name, u8, u32, u8) and FUN_00470270 which sets +0xD0 (count) and prints the same '(%u/%u)'.

The EN success text is a mistranslation; naming as 'friend list expansion' is based on the C2S 0x73 gates, not on a string.
blind_open_questions: Is 0x9D really a friend-slot expansion purchase, or the result of adding a specific friend? The EN message says the latter; the fields and 50,000-gold gate say the former.
How much the capacity grows per purchase and the exact price (the client only checks gold >= 50,000).
The payload of C2S 0x73 (send site #85, reached with PUSH EDI then Send) looked like no Add calls after the opcode on that path, but this was not fully verified.

specs.name: RemoteEntityMoveStateQueued (short delay, clears flag 8E4)

fields.name: mover_uid
fields.dest_or_source: stack [esp+0x1D4]; matched against entity+0x84 through FUN_004189f0
fields.meaning: uid of the entity being synced

fields.name: move_bits
fields.dest_or_source: scene+0xEF8..0xEFF, decoded into a queue node exactly as in 0x2A
fields.meaning: Same 8-byte bitfield as C2S 0x0D / S2C 0x2A: lo[1:0] horizontal input (1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, else 8), lo[4:2] 8B4, lo[8:5] 8B5, lo[11:9] 8B6, lo[15:12] action 94C, lo[19:16] reaction 950, lo[21:20] facing (1 gives 2, 2 gives 6, else 8), hi[11:0] 958.

specs.semantics:
Uses the same handler block as 0x2A.

It sets:
- entity+0x8E4 = 0 (the SETNZ on opcode != 0x9E)
- entity+0x8D7 = 1

It builds a queue node from the bits with node+0x08 (target) = 0 and node+0x52 = 0. The node's delay is set to node[0] = 0x1E (30 ms, about one tick), and the node is appended to the entity move queue (+0x1350). LIVE-VERIFIED CORRECTION (C3, world_movement_npc#29 - CONTRADICTED and now corrected): 0x9E is NOT an immediate stop. The 30 ms is the node's OWN hold, counted only after every node already queued ahead of it has finished, so the real latency is the remaining hold of the queue (measured 750 ms behind one pending walk node); the queue drains at about 2x speed while >= 2 nodes are queued. entity+0x8E4 = 0 is written AT RECEIPT, not on dequeue. For 'stop now' use 0x2A (it flushes the queue and carries a position) or relay the stop as the next 0x1B. The queue is NOT flushed, entity+0xE48 is not reset, and no position is read. FUN_00412100 applies the node on the next ticks, which sets 94C/D80/958/8FF/8D0 etc. on the entity.
specs.trigger: Relay a buffered movement/input change for another entity when it should apply almost immediately. The exact use by the original server is unknown.
specs.gates_and_hazards:
- An unknown uid or uid 0 is ignored after 4 bytes.
- Do not send it for the receiver's own uid: FUN_00412100 never consumes the local uid's queue, so nodes leak.
- A nonzero reaction nibble (bits 16-19) makes the consumer copy the zeroed node x/y into the entity, snapping it to (0,0).
- Clearing entity+0x8E4 changes interpolation checks in FUN_00413920/FUN_004158d0/FUN_00416380.
specs.references:
- KR Hex-Rays groups 0x9E with 0x2A/0x9F and likewise sets the delay to a global (dword_6375BC) for 0x9E, but its bitfield layout differs.
- Not implemented in windslayer_server.py or in PySlayer's Python.
open_questions: When the original server used 0x9E instead of 0x9F (for example stop/idle transitions, since it clears flag 8E4).
blind_open_questions: Gameplay meaning of 0x9E vs 0x9F (both have no source uid; they differ in delay 30 vs 990 and in the +0x8E4 flag).

spec_errata.old: 0x9E applies within about one tick (immediate stop)
spec_errata.new: 0x9E queues behind pending nodes; measured 750 ms; use 0x2A for an immediate stop

specs.semantics: Starts a new Play&Chat room list (window 0x478). There is no type check, no can-enter check and no filter, so rows appear in reverse arrival order. Afterwards label 0x14 = sprintf('%u', count[game+0x45C]) and FUN_00489c50(0x478,1).
