c2s.summary:
The 86-site list is incomplete. 3 of the missed items are gameplay packets the server must handle: 0x42CE94 (0x0D movement), 0x42F76B (0x7E portal) and 0x42F904 (0x2B world-entry).

Method: a raw scan of .text in WindSlayer.exe for the bytes 08 41 4A 00 finds exactly 90 references to the Send IAT slot 0x4A4108: 89 `CALL [0x4A4108]` and 1 `JMP [0x4A4108]`. Nothing loads Send into a register, so no Send call is hidden behind a register or vtable. The corpus asm agrees (89 CALL + 1 JMP).

**Missed direct Send sites (3):** 0x42CE94 (0x0D), 0x42F76B (0x7E) and 0x42F904 (0x2B). All three are in corpus/c2s_send_sites_scout.json (89 entries) but were dropped from the 86-site list. The scout also got the 0x2B opcode wrong (None) because its u8 Adds go through `CALL ESI`.

**Missed tail call (1):** 0x470018 in FUN_0046ffe0 sends C2S 0x32 (messenger/friend window) on g_sock_game via its copy at [obj+0x74]. It has no SEND SITE marker.

**Missed UDP SendTo (5 sites):** all on g_sock_map [0x70E6FC], which CreateSockets makes as a UDP socket bound to 42907, not a TCP map socket.
- 0x44E002: after S2C 0x02 login success, broadcasts u8 0x11 + u32 account id to 255.255.255.255:42907.
- FUN_00423260, called every tick:
  - 0x423787 and 0x4237FD (register calls through EBP): loopback datagrams to 127.0.0.1:42907 on normal field maps.
  - 0x4236F5: u8 0x03 to the IP and port+10000 that S2C 0x2F supplies, on arena/team maps.
  - 0x423759: host-mode unicast to each entity; likely dead because scene+0xF24 is never set nonzero.
- Fireway's SendTo adds the same 8-byte header and encoding (SetHeader + CEncMsg::EncodebyArray) as Send.

**Missed WinINet traffic:** FUN_00476660 does an HTTP GET auto-patch from windslayer.globalgamecdn.com. It only runs if S2C 0x01 returns a u16 version that is not 3 and below 60001; it ends by launching YG_WSLauncher.exe. ShellExecuteA opens 6 browser URLs; none of that touches the server.

**Checked, no misses:**
- **Version socket:** no Send or SendTo ever uses g_sock_version [0x70E6F8]. The C2S 0x01 login at 0x44D8BF goes on g_sock_game.
- **Raw winsock:** the exe imports nothing from ws2_32/wsock32 and loads no networking DLL at runtime.
- **Other DLLs:** only Fireway.dll imports WS2_32. Its send() is called only from CSNSocket::SendBuffer and sendto() only from the two SendTo exports. It never calls its own Add/Send exports, so there's no hidden heartbeat.
- **Listener callbacks:** the CSNSockMyListener callbacks don't send anything.
- **Wrappers:** every function that calls Add also calls Send or SendTo, and no caller adds bytes before calling a Send-containing function. FUN_0043e2e0 and FUN_0043e3f0 have no direct callers but are reached through vtable 0x6F7F00/0x6F7F0C; both are already in the list.

**Sockets of listed sites:** all listed sites resolve to g_sock_game (directly or through UI-object copies at +0x14, +0x20, +0x74, 0x720 (object at +0x700) and 0xDD0 (object at +0xDC4)), except 0x418294, 0x41AC20, 0x428244, 0x4284D3, 0x4285DE and 0x428884. Those send on child sockets of a CSNSockMan at scene+0xF98, which is only ever written as 0, so they're likely dead code rather than game-server C2S.

**Open questions:** I didn't prove that the map-mode flag [[mainwnd+0x4D8]+0x70]==1 means arena. I inferred it from team-id logic and from 0x7E being allowed only when the flag is 0. I also didn't confirm which messenger action 0x32 performs.

s2c.summary:
Completeness audit of every receive and parse path in WindSlayer.exe (EN 2008). Static analysis only: the corpus plus capstone/pefile passes over WindSlayer.exe and Fireway.dll. Nothing was run or modified.

RECEIVE ENTRY POINTS (complete list):
(1) The client has exactly one listener class, CSNSockMyListener. RTTI in the exe has only .?AVCSNSocketListener@@ and .?AVCSNSockMyListener@@. Its vtable is at 0x6F8408, and the only code that writes that vtable pointer is at 0x440191, 0x44027C and 0x4787FA. Slots:
- [0] 0x478810, [1] 0x40B5E0, [2] 0x478820: stubs that return 0. Slot 1 is Fireway's raw-recv callback; its data is thrown away.
- [3] 0x478830: TCP. Fireway's TCPPacketManager calls vt+0xC with (sid, pkt, len). The client drops sid and calls OnReceive_MainTcpHandler(pkt, len).
- [4] 0x478850: UDP. Fireway's recvfrom goes through UDPBufferManager and UDPPacketManager to vt+0x10 with (pkt, len, from_ip_str, from_port). The client calls FUN_00458640 with ECX=pkt and stack args (owner, len, ip, port).
- [5] 0x478880: disconnect dialog. [6] 0x4788E0: "Error occured in Fireway (%u), WSA(%d)" log. [7]: destructor.
So the version socket (7011) and the game socket (7022) share one dispatcher and one opcode space. Nothing on the client side tells them apart.
(2) g_sock_map (0x70E6FC) is a UDP socket, not a TCP map socket. It is created with Create(0xA79B, 2, true, true) and Fireway calls socket(AF_INET, 2, 0), then binds 0.0.0.0:42907. Every datagram goes to FUN_00458640 and can never reach the TCP dispatcher. This contradicts the note in windslayer_server.py (~line 841) that fake UDP 0x11 packets caused TCP-style UI popups: UDP 0x11 only stores the sender's IP.
(3) WinINet HTTP updater: FUN_00475970 and FUN_00476660, with the text list parsed by FUN_0040AC70. It is started by S2C 0x01.
Nothing else receives data: no ws2_32 imports in the exe, no other CSNSocket objects (the constructor IAT slot 0x4A40E4 is used only in CreateSockets), no named pipes and no WM_COPYDATA. Scene+0xF98 (CSNSockMan*) and scene+0xF24 (P2P-host flag) are only ever written with 0 (full-.text scan: 0x440301 and 0x411FC3), so the P2P-host and child-socket code is dead.

GETDATAFROMPACKET AUDIT: I scanned all 9 GDP import slots (0x4A4090/94/98/B0/C8/CC/D0/D4/4118) as both call and mov-reg references across all of .text. Every hit is in one of 8 functions:
- OnReceive_MainTcpHandler: 455
- SubHandler1: 68, SubHandler2: 4, SubHandler3: 57, SubHandler4: 45, SubHandler5: 4
- ParseChannelList 0x4404D0: 6. This is a helper of S2C 0x01 (call at 0x44D734).
- FUN_00458640: 20. This is the UDP dispatcher and the only GDP site outside the TCP tree.
No hit falls outside a corpus function body. The only direct calls to the two dispatchers are the rel32 calls at 0x47883D and 0x478867.

FIREWAY BEHAVIOUR THAT AFFECTS GRAMMARS:
- On a short packet, GetDataFromPacket leaves both the output and the offset unchanged, calls listener vt[6] (log only) with error 0x10..0x19 and the first byte, and returns 1. A truncated field keeps whatever was in memory; the client does not disconnect.
- UDP header (GetUDPHeader 0x10003A00) uses the same 8-byte framing as TCP: u32 with length in bits 0-10, bit 11 = DecodebyArray, seq in bits 12-19. Differences from TCP: a datagram whose seq equals the last seen seq is dropped (error 0x130, log only). TCP instead requires a strictly increasing seq (wraps after 0xFF) and closes the connection otherwise. UDP does not check the length bounds.

SERVER-RELEVANT CONCLUSIONS:
(a) S2C 0x01 is the version-server reply; I verified its full grammar in asm, including ParseChannelList. The current _build_version_body matches it.
(b) In EN 2008, battle-map UDP state (0x07/0x08/0x09 plus the HP/MP opcodes 0x06/0x0C/0x0E/0x0B/0x0D/0x0F/0x0A/0x10) is sent to the client at UDP 42907. Since P2P-host code is dead, the sender must be a relay whose address comes from TCP S2C 0x2F: str[16] at scene+0xF38 and u16 at scene+0xF48. The client says hello with UDP 0x03 to that IP at port u16+10000. On non-battle maps the client only loops 0x04 and 0x03 back to 127.0.0.1:42907, so the server must not send UDP there.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- The relay role is inferred, not confirmed by a capture.
- Meaning of entity +0x1114..+0x1128.
- Whether the relay should leave the receiving player's own uid out of the 0x07/0x08/0x09 records (the client applies records to state>=3 entities, including the local player at 4).
- In UDP 0x0A, the 0x58 effect is tagged with the local player's uid (scene+0x220), not the target's. Possibly a client bug.
- scene+0xEEC..0xEF7 is used as a scratch area by both the UDP sender FUN_00423260 and the receiver.
- The G_UpdateList.h token layout is fragile and only approximate.

Confidence: high for the entry-point map, the GDP audit and the UDP grammars (every GDP call checked in asm against stack offsets). Medium for bitfield meanings and relay semantics.

missed_items.what: UDP framing rules for any server-side UDP sender. g_sock_map is created with header and encode flags on (+0x13B5=1, +0x13B6=1), so each datagram is: u32 hdr (bits 0-10 = total length including the 8-byte header; bit 11 (0x800) set -> CEncMsg::DecodebyArray, clear -> plaintext; bits 12-19 = seq) + 4 more header bytes + payload. The payload handed to the dispatcher is hdr+8 with length (hdr&0x7FF)-8; the actual datagram size is not used. Seq rule: if last >= 0xFF, last is reset to -1; a datagram whose seq EQUALS last is dropped (SetLastError 0x130 -> listener vt[6] log only). A lower seq is accepted, unlike TCP's GetHeader (0x10003810), which requires seq > last and otherwise closes the socket with error 0x12D. Datagrams the client loops back to itself also advance 'last', because the socket keeps a single counter.

FIREWAY UDP FRAMING (verified in Fireway.dll asm):
Socket setup:
- Create(port, type, encrypt->+0x13B5, udp_header->+0x13B6) @0x10005500. The game calls Create(42907, 2, 1, 1) @0x4402DB.
- Init zeroes send seq +0x13A8 and recv last_seq +0x13AC.

Receive path:
1. Socket thread window, WSAAsyncSelect 0x401 FD_READ -> ioctlsocket FIONREAD -> recvfrom (0x10004755) -> inet_ntoa/ntohs.
2. UDPBufferManager 0x10004180: memcpy into a zeroed 0xFEE-byte stack buffer (no bound check).
3. GetUDPHeader 0x10003A00:
   - size = hdr & 0x7FF.
   - If last_seq >= 0xFF, last_seq = -1.
   - seq = (hdr >> 12) & 0xFF. seq == last_seq -> drop (0x130); else last_seq = seq.
   - If hdr & 0x800: need encrypt && !NoEncode, then DecodebyArray; a bad checksum drops (0x12F). If the socket is not encrypting, drop (0x133).
   - Bit 11 clear -> plaintext accepted.
4. UDPPacketManager(hdr+8, size-8, ip, port) -> listener vtable+0x10.

Header and cipher:
- Header = u32 [size(11 bits) | 0x800 encoded | seq << 12 | 0 in bits 20-31], then u32 checksum.
- By-array cipher: XOR key T[(seq+15)&0xFF]; checksum = (T[seq] + sum(plain & 0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF, with T = Fireway 0x1000B138 dword table low bytes. Matches cencmsg.encode_by_array/decode_by_array.

Send path (SendTo 0x10003C60 / 0x10003DF0): SetHeader 0x10002150 pre-increments seq (1..255, 0) and sets size = payload+8 and bit 11 when encrypting; EncodebyArray; sendto of size bytes.

Differences from TCP GetHeader:
- TCP requires 8 < size <= 0x7FF and a strictly increasing seq, and closes the socket on errors.
- UDP only drops an exact repeat of the last seq, with no size check and no close.
- Every drop calls SetLastError, which only logs via listener slot 6.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Scene input bytes +0x254..+0x257 are read only by the UDP sender FUN_00423260. In field mode the client sends 0x04 and then 0x03 to 127.0.0.1:42907 (itself) every tick, so local-player input is applied through this UDP loopback. Anything that blocks the loopback or steals seqs affects movement.
2. The recv seq dedupe is per socket, so server datagrams can collide with the client's own loopback seqs.
3. The host flag scene+0xF24 is written only as 0 (0x411FC3, confirmed by a disp32 byte scan), so all in-client room-host code (peer address capture in FUN_00423850, snapshot unicast 0x423759) is dead in EN. An arena host must be external at host_ip:room_no+10000.
4. The server source names bit 0x800 NO_ENCODE_FLAG; in Fireway that bit means ENCODED.
5. Prior critic claims verified: 0x03 = u32, u8, u8 via FUN_00423850; 0x11 = u32 (unused), with the source IP copied to scene+0x224 and port forced to 42907.

HOW A DATAGRAM REACHES IT
1. Fireway FD_READ handler: ioctlsocket(FIONREAD), then recvfrom at 0x10004755.
2. The source is turned into inet_ntoa string + ntohs port.
3. UDPBufferManager 0x10004180. The header flag +0x13B6 is 1 (Create arg4), so it memsets a 0xFEE stack buffer and memcpys the datagram in with no size check.
4. GetUDPHeader 0x10003A00:
   - len = h0&0x7FF.
   - Seq = (h0>>12)&0xFF. If it equals the previous seq it is dropped (error 0x130). The previous seq is reset to -1 when >= 0xFF, starts at 0 from Init 0x10002A60, and is updated before decryption.
   - If h0&0x800: requires +0x13B5=1 and +0x13B4=0, then runs DecodebyArray 0x10006BC0 (XOR K[(seq+15)&0xFF]; checksum h4 = K[seq]+sum(b&0x5F)+K[(seq+37)&0xFF]+seq, masked 0x0FFFFFFF; errors 0x12F/0x133).
   - Returns buf+8.
5. UDPPacketManager 0x100022E0 calls listener vtable[4] 0x478850, which calls FUN_00458640 with ECX=payload and stack (owner=game_state 0x70EA00, len=(h0&0x7FF)-8, from_ip_str, from_port).
   - The UDP listener is a separate CSNSockMyListener instance at [0x70E704] (0x44027A), same vtable 0x6F8408.
   - Errors go to vtable[6] 0x4788E0, which only logs 'Error occured in Fireway (%u), WSA(%d)'.

GENERAL RULES
- One message per datagram.
- The Fireway header is not in any grammar.
- Plaintext (bit 11 clear, h4 ignored) is accepted.
- The static table equals cencmsg._STATIC_TABLE. encode_by_array output was cross-checked.

DISPATCHER ENTRY
- If [game_state+0x408] != 0, return immediately without locking. The only nonzero write is WM_CLOSE in window proc FUN_0043e3f0 at 0x43E450, so this is a shutdown flag. The corpus label 'g_game_state_inworld_flag' is misleading.
- Otherwise EnterCriticalSection(game_state+0x368), the same critical section as the main window proc at 0x43E466.
- u8 opcode at offset 0 via GetDataFromPacket, with ECX=g_sock_game as the reader object; this only affects which listener logs short reads.
- Opcodes are indexed with op-3 into the byte table 0x459BF8 (15 entries), then jump table 0x459BD8.

EVERY OPCODE ACCEPTED (anything else, including 0x05, goes to the default exit 0x459BB5 = no-op)
- 0x03 -> 0x4586D4. No gate. u32 uid, u8, u8 -> FUN_00423850.
- 0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09 -> 0x458743.
  - Map object [game_state+0x4D8] is dereferenced without a null check.
  - If map+0x70 == 1 (arena), 0x04 is dropped and 0x07/0x08/0x09 continue. Otherwise only 0x04 continues.
  - Then bytes[4] are read into scene+0xEEC, and the datagram continues only if (hdr>>18) == map+0x1B8.
- 0x06, 0x0C, 0x0E -> 0x4595B9. Requires map non-null and map+0x70 == 1.
- 0x0A -> 0x459856. Same gate.
- 0x0B, 0x0D, 0x0F -> 0x4596B5. Same gate.
- 0x10 -> 0x4597B1. Same gate.
- 0x11 -> 0x459B45. Requires scene non-null and scene+0x220 != 0.

CORRECTIONS / NEW FACTS VS THE PRIOR CRITIC
- 0x03 is not a 'peer hello'. It sets a remote entity's input/command digits (+0x8B3..+0x8B6), +0x88 and +0x15DC.
- The ip:port learning in FUN_00423850 is gated on scene+0xF24. A raw displacement scan found that field is only ever written 0 (0x411FC3), so that code is dead in EN. The same holds for host unicast at 0x423759.
- 0x11's u32 is read but never used or compared.
- UDP dedupe rejects only a seq EQUAL to the previous one, unlike TCP GetHeader's strictly-increasing rule. Seq state is shared across all sources, including the client's own per-tick loopback datagrams to 127.0.0.1:42907.

SERVER HAZARDS
- Header length must be >= 9. With 0x800 set and length < 8, DecodebyArray's loop bound wraps and crashes the client.
- Keep datagrams <= 2047 bytes; anything over 4078 overflows the client's stack buffer.
- Use a rolling seq.

UDP-RECV-B: All four opcodes share one handler block, 0x458743..0x4595B4 in FUN_00458640, and one wire grammar: a u32 header (sent as 4 raw bytes) followed by count x 8-byte records. Every width and bit mask was checked in the asm, the switch tables were decoded from the binary, and the sender FUN_00423260 was cross-checked. Its FPU uses chop mode, so the positions are TRUNCATED halves, not rounded as the decompiler shows.

Main findings:
(1) Map-mode gate: 0x04 is accepted only when [[0x70EED8]+0x70] != 1; 0x07/0x08/0x09 only when it == 1. There is no NULL check here, unlike cases 0x06/0x0A.
(2) Header bits: timer = bits 0-8, count = bits 9-17, map_code = bits 18-31. The map code must equal [[0x70EED8]+0x1B8] or the records are ignored.
(3) Record bits: rec_lo = x/2 (bits 0-11), y/2 (12-22), facing (23: 0->2, 1->6), action-1 (24-29), attack_phase (30-31). rec_hi = anim_toggle (bit 0), uid (bits 1-25), bits 26-31 ignored.
(4) In normal fields the CLIENT SENDS 0x04 TO ITSELF (127.0.0.1:42907 @0x423787) every tick. This loopback is the path from local simulation to render (+0x1598..+0x15B4). A server should not send 0x04. It must keep entity uids below 2^25 and coordinates within X 0..8190, Y 0..4094, or entities render frozen or wrapped.
(5) 0x07/0x08/0x09 come from the arena HOST (phase scene+0xF04 = 0/1/2). The EN client never becomes host (F24 is only ever 0), so a private server emulating arena rooms must send these to each client's UDP source address (learned from the client's 0x03 hellos to host_ip:room_no+10000).

UDP framing, verified in Fireway.dll: the same 8-byte header as TCP (size | 0x800 | seq<<12, then checksum), with an EncodebyArray static-table body. Plaintext (0x800 clear) is also accepted. The payload length comes from the header. Seq rule: one last_seq per socket, starting at 0. A datagram is dropped only if its seq equals last_seq (the reset to -1 happens after 255). last_seq is updated before the checksum check. The source address is never validated.

Short reads do not advance the offset, re-apply the stale record, and call the game socket listener's OnError, which only logs.

UDP-SEND: Every UDP send in the client is accounted for; there are only 4 SendTo call sites.

**How the sites were found**
- A raw scan of the whole image for the IAT addresses (any byte form: CALL [imm], MOV reg,[imm], JMP [imm]) finds 0x4A410C (SendTo by IP string) only at 0x4236F7, 0x42371C and 0x42377B. Those are the direct call at 0x4236F5 and the EBP loads that feed CALL EBP at 0x423759, 0x423787 and 0x4237FD.
- 0x4A40DC (SendTo by numeric IP) appears only at 0x44E004 (call 0x44E002). SetBroadCast (0x4A40E0) appears only at 0x44DFC4.
- NoEncode is not imported, so every UDP datagram is encoded.
- FUN_0046ffe0 / Send (0x4A4108) is TCP only: Fireway Send rejects sockets whose type is not 1.

**Framing (verified in Fireway.dll)**
- Create at 0x4402DB is called as (42907, 2=UDP, encode=1, header=1).
- SendTo (0x10003C60 / 0x10003DF0) sends one datagram of payload+8 bytes:
  - SetHeader 0x10002150 builds dword0 = (len+8)&0x7FF | 0x800 | seq<<12, with bits 20-31 = 0.
  - seq is a per-socket counter at +0x13A8. It is reset to 0 in Init/Initial_Socket, incremented before each send, and wraps 255->0.
  - EncodebyArray 0x10006B20 computes dword1 = (T[seq] + sum(plain&0x5F) + T[(seq+0x25)&0xFF] + seq) & 0x0FFFFFFF, and XORs every payload byte with T[(seq+0x0F)&0xFF]. This matches cencmsg.encode_by_array exactly.
  - The client's TCP Send uses the same SetHeader/EncodebyArray code.
  - Argument 3 of SendTo = 1 clears the buffer after the send.
- Add fails (and drops that field) once the buffer would exceed 0x7F7 bytes.

**Tick timing**
- FUN_00423260 runs once per FrameMove.
- FUN_0040db20 calls vtable+0x18 = FUN_0042b260 at most once every 30 ms, inside CS game_state+0x368. OnReceive and the UDP receive path take the same lock, so there are no buffer races.
- FUN_0042b260 returns unless scene+0xF00 is 4, 5 or 6.

**Map mode and host flag**
- mode = [scene+0xF88]+0x70. scene+0xF88 is the same map object as game_state+0x4D8. The value is the .hmi XML 'mode' attribute; values >1 are stored minus 2.
- Host flag scene+0xF24 is only ever written 0 (ctor at 0x411FC3; checked by a capstone .text scan). Every host branch is therefore dead in EN 2008: the 0x423759 unicast with opcodes 0x04/0x07/0x08/0x09.

**Reachable traffic**
- (1) 0x11 + u32 account_id, broadcast once to 255.255.255.255:42907 after S2C 0x02 success.
- (2) Map mode 0: every tick, 0x04 world snapshot then 0x03 input, both to 127.0.0.1:42907. This is self-loopback, including at character select.
- (3) Map mode !=0: 0x03 input to host_ip(scene+0xF38) : room_no(scene+0xF48)+10000.
  - Sent every tick while the local entity has +0x98==3, or until the first 0x07/0x08/0x09 arrives (scene+0xF08==0).
  - Otherwise sent as a keep-alive when more than 9000 ms have passed.

**Snapshot bitfields**
- Confirmed against the receiver FUN_00458640.
- header: timer 9 bits | count 9 bits | map_code 14 bits (AA*100+BB).
- rec_a: x/2 12 bits | y/2 11 bits | facing 1 bit | action_code 6 bits | 2 event flags.
- rec_b: anim toggle 1 bit | uid 25 bits | 6 stale bits.
- Constants read from the binary: 0.5 at 0x6F8AE0, 0.001 at 0x6F8A90.

**Implications for the server**
- Never bind UDP 42907 on the client PC.
- To support arena maps (mode 1), the server must itself act as the UDP room host on host_ip:(room_no+10000). It receives the 0x03 inputs and returns 0x07/0x08/0x09 snapshots (map_code must match) to the client's source address.

**Open items**
- How the original service hosted rooms (relay vs server-side host).
- Which of direction codes 2/6 means left.
- Exact meaning of the entity+0x8D1/+0x8D9/+0x8E0 flags and of the scene+0x257 status classes.
